title: Segfault in-game ~88s in on Zelda OoT (0400486024DEC000), looks like NvProg object read as guest NVNprogram

body:
### What happened

Since the late latch (`60284e79`, `1015aedf`: `nvn_link_latch.h`, the drain into it in `nvn_link_drain.h`), Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave on its tactics battle maps sometimes locks to 30 fps on a 60 Hz link while the GPU needs only about 10 ms a frame. Every lock starts at a drain into the latch, lasts until the frames fall back, and comes again at the next drain into the latch. With `DM_PRESENT_LATCH=0` the same kind of battle map holds 60 fps for 6000 frames. It happens every time a drain enters the latch on this game.

It is not a constant 30 fps. In play, the Metal HUD moves between a steady 60, a steady 30 and values in between. The log shows the same thing: some 300-frame windows are all 16.7 ms, some are all 33.3 ms, and windows that cross a change are mixed (frames 1200-1500 below: p50 16.73 ms, p95 32.91 ms).

The game's frame work at 60 fps is about 15.9 ms of a 16.7 ms tick, so its presents come late after the callback that woke its acquire. `docs/reference/frame-rate.md` lists "games that present long after their acquire returns" as not checked. Instead of falling back to the queue's one-tick slack, the frames settle into a steady two ticks each.

**Latch on** (default). Excerpts from the log, in order:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frame latency 1 (window)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: the callback that woke the acquire waits briefly for its present and takes it (DM_PRESENT_LATCH)
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 600: frame time p50 16.67 / p95 17.88 / max 67.31 ms (300 frames); frame work p50 15.90 / p95 17.23 / max 66.54 ms (300 frames); NVN submit+present p50 3.80 / p95 4.54 / max 50.11 ms (300 frames); GPU p50 9.63 / p95 11.22 / max 21.54 ms (300 frames);
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frames stood in the present queue while the game kept up, the acquire waited 1 more tick (16.6 ms) to let them out (drain #2, frame 634)
[dm] [longframe] frame 635 (11.88 s) whole frame 33.5 ms, submit+present 3.9 ms, GPU 9.6 ms; new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0, 0.0 ms in all; ...
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: from the callback to its targetTimestamp over 300 ticks: min 15.92 ms, mean 16.51 ms (late latch: 246 presents taken, 0 timeouts, entered by 1 drains, the next needs 2 s of early frames)
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 900: frame time p50 33.29 / p95 33.85 / max 34.51 ms (300 frames); frame work p50 32.41 / p95 32.97 / max 33.65 ms (300 frames); NVN submit+present p50 4.74 / p95 5.32 / max 6.04 ms (300 frames); GPU p50 10.13 / p95 10.55 / max 10.69 ms (300 frames);
[dm] [nvn] on-screen up to frame 900: 300 frames, dropped 251 (discarded 0), p99 33.34 ms
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: from the callback to its targetTimestamp over 300 ticks: min 16.57 ms, mean 16.64 ms (late latch: 546 presents taken, 0 timeouts, entered by 1 drains, the next needs 2 s of early frames)
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 1200: frame time p50 33.34 / p95 33.89 / max 34.25 ms (300 frames); frame work p50 32.43 / p95 32.96 / max 33.34 ms (300 frames); NVN submit+present p50 5.04 / p95 5.54 / max 5.96 ms (300 frames); GPU p50 10.17 / p95 10.29 / max 10.37 ms (300 frames);
[dm] [nvn] on-screen up to frame 1200: 300 frames, dropped 300 (discarded 0), p99 33.34 ms
[dm] [nvn] power up to frame 1200: CPU energy 1.38 W, 46.0 mJ per frame (30.0 fps); CPU 64% (100 = one core), ...
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frames stood in the present queue while the game kept up, the acquire waited 1 more tick (16.7 ms) to let them out (drain #3, frame 1453)
[dm] [longframe] frame 1454 (34.97 s) whole frame 33.2 ms, submit+present 4.5 ms, GPU 10.3 ms; ...
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: from the callback to its targetTimestamp over 300 ticks: min 8.28 ms, mean 16.07 ms (late latch: 601 presents taken, 1 timeouts, entered by 2 drains, the next needs 4 s of early frames)
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 1500: frame time p50 16.73 / p95 32.91 / max 34.11 ms (300 frames); ...
```

Frames 300-600 run at 60. From drain #2 at frame 634 (the first drain into the latch) every frame is 33.3 ms, with GPU p50 10.1 ms and submit+present 4.7-5.0 ms, while the latch keeps taking presents. The frames go back to 16.7 ms around frame 1350, then drain #3 enters the latch again at frame 1453 and the 33 ms frames come back.

**Latch off** (`DM_PRESENT_LATCH=0`, same kind of battle map, 6000 frames, otherwise the same settings):

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: each callback takes the frame already queued (DM_PRESENT_LATCH)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frames stood in the present queue while the game kept up, the acquire waited 1 more tick (16.7 ms) to let them out (drain #1, frame 166)
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 600: frame time p50 16.67 / p95 17.52 / max 55.64 ms (300 frames); frame work p50 15.91 / p95 16.84 / max 54.78 ms (300 frames); NVN submit+present p50 3.74 / p95 4.51 / max 38.38 ms (300 frames); GPU p50 10.13 / p95 11.23 / max 21.72 ms (300 frames);
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frames stood in the present queue while the game kept up, the acquire waited 1 more tick (16.6 ms) to let them out (drain #2, frame 1723)
```

All 20 `timing up to frame` lines (300 to 6000) read frame time p50 16.64-16.68 ms, p95 under 17.7 ms, GPU p50 9.9-11.3 ms. `on-screen` dropped 0 in most windows (7, 3, 1 and 3 in four of them). Both plain drains left it at 60.

**Other games on the same Mac and host, latch on:** Fire Emblem Engage, Ocarina of Time, Pokopia and Super Mario Galaxy 2 entered the latch and stayed at 60 fps. In Super Mario Galaxy 2, 300 presents per 300 ticks, and present to screen went from about 46 ms down to 22-30 ms. So the latch works as intended there. This looks specific to a game whose frame work is close to a whole tick. Those runs were short (title screens and early gameplay), except for Super Mario Galaxy 2, which was played.

### What you expected

After a drain into the latch, a game whose presents come late falls back to the queue's slack (or the latch backs off), and the game stays at 60 fps instead of a steady two ticks per frame.

### Game, title ID and version

Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave, 04007EF01F8AE000, update 2.0.0 (v131072), DLC mounted

### nxnative commit

`ae7c1023`, plus local changes that do not touch `nvn_link_latch.h`, `nvn_link_drain.h` or the display-link and present code in `nvn_mtl.m`

### Shader chain version

850f0ff42604 (upstream's 648a020c093b plus a local change in `shader_split.py`)

### How it was built and run

Mac, the host from a terminal (--platform mac)

### Device and OS

Mac Studio M5 Max, macOS 27.2.1. A 3440x1440 screen at a fixed 120 Hz (macOS shows `120.00Hz`). At the 60 fps target the host runs the 60 Hz link on it (`present tick 60 Hz`, period 16.67 ms), and the log reports `frame latency 1 (window)`. The 30 fps stretches are two ticks of that 60 Hz link, not of the screen's 120 Hz.

### Settings and environment overrides

```
DM_FPS_TARGET=60
DM_FULLSCREEN=1
DM_GFX_SCALE=0
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx
DM_LANG=zh-Hans
DM_METAL_HUD=1
DM_SCREEN_MATCH=0
```

The game renders at 3440x1440. With `DM_PRESENT_LATCH=0` added, it holds 60 fps.

### Logs

The excerpts above are from the host's log of each run. The latch-on run's full log was overwritten by the next run, so only the lines quoted above are left from it. I can attach the full latch-off log, or a new latch-on log, if that helps.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: Mac: the late latch locks Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave to 30 fps on the 60 Hz link with the GPU at 10 ms

### Summary
We are porting the Qt launcher to Linux. Linux can run every pre-processing stage but cannot compile Metal. We want maintainers to confirm the handoff below before we build on it.

### What Linux can run
Extraction (`nx_extract` rebuilt for linux-x64), the rewriter, the shader split, profiles and tables, RomFS filling. It stops at the shader libraries.

### What Linux cannot run
`xcrun metal`/`metallib`, `metal-tt`, `make -C dm/host`, `xcodegen`, `sips`, `plutil`, `PlistBuddy`, and `xcodebuild`/`actool`/`codesign`.

### Proposed handoff
A `<id>_build` work folder plus a small `handoff.json` (pin, engine id, chain, profile digest). On a Mac, unmodified `dmsh_build.py` and then `dm/ios/tools/build_ipa.sh` consume it, with `--prepare-xcode` when the user wants a signed device build.

### Ask
1. Is this the split you would accept for a Linux port?
2. Would you take a Linux-rebuilt `dmsh_xlate`/`spirv-cross`, whose `dmsh_chain.lock` fingerprints necessarily change?

Pin: 5fc927d5ed2d4ba0c950a69bf27578ddd5714945

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Nothing is changed upstream. This asks about a boundary, not a patch.

- The plan is a `docs/linux-port` note in our fork (LNPANDY/NX2Apple): stage table, one decision, handoff contract.
- Reason for stopping at the Metal step: `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock` records the macOS and iPhoneOS Metal compilers, `ios_metal.py` compiles MSL with `xcrun -sdk iphoneos`, and `gen_build.py` gets the host's MSL from `make -C dm/host` + `host_msl.py`, which also calls `xcrun`.
- Apple ships Metal tooling for macOS and Windows only; the Windows port already replaces `build_ipa.sh` with `build_app.py`.
- `--prepare-xcode` itself is Mac-only (`xcodegen`, `sips`, `plutil`, `PlistBuddy`, and `gen_build.py`), so it stays the Mac half of the handoff.
- Related: #538 (Linux/aarch64 request, closed without an answer) and #244 (Windows port).

</details>
title: Linux launcher port: a `_build` handoff that stops before the Metal step

body:
The pipeline prebuild tool (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD=tool`, invoked by `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` for `--platform mac` builds) spends roughly 28–33% of its time with all worker threads idle while Metal serializes pipeline archives. Splitting compilation across two processes cuts prebuild wall time by 20–26% in a quick prototype, though one unexplained Metal abort occurred in 51 two-process runs.

### Background

The prebuild tool compiles the base pipeline for every known shader pair (vertex + pixel shader from the game profile's `shader_pairs.tsv` and `pso_pairs.tsv`) into a Metal 4 pipeline archive, then exits. Worker threads compile these base pipelines in parallel (18 workers on the M5 Pro below; by default matching how many compiles Metal's compiler runs at once), and every 2,000 base pipelines the newly compiled batch is serialized to a new `.mtl4a` file.

Because #2513 hit a `SIGSEGV` in Metal's `MultiLevelAirntBinaryCache::getElementAtDestination` when compilation overlapped with archive serialization (on an M4 Pro running macOS 27.2), `ser_begin` in `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` now drains in-flight compiles and blocks all new compiles in the process until serialization completes.

### Baseline measurements

Measured on an M5 Pro (18 cores, macOS 26.7.3), `main` `c22f30a3`, one run each:

- **Tears of the Kingdom (24,175 pairs):** All 18 workers were blocked for **64.5 s of 195 s (~33%)** while building shader-pair base pipelines. The 12 archive writes took 2–7 s each; draining in-flight compiles before each write took only 0.07–0.17 s.
- **Pokémon Scarlet (24,487 pairs):** All 18 workers were blocked for **38.8 s of 140 s (~28%)**.
- **CPU usage during writes:** `dmhost` uses no CPU while a single `MTLCompilerService` thread uses one core.
- **Other work:** The rest of the tool's run (the prewarm list's pipelines) adds 0.2–7 s.

### Two-process prototype

As a proof of concept (gated behind `DM_PSO_PREBUILD_PROCS=2`), I split prebuilding across two processes:

- Each process has its own Metal device, compilers, serializers, and 18 workers (36 total).
- Both processes claim groups of shader pairs from a shared counter.
- The `ser_begin` serialization hold is unchanged, so an archive write only blocks compiles in its own process.
- Each process writes `.mtl4a` files into its own subfolder of the archive; once both processes exit, the tool moves the files into the archive under the next sequence numbers.

Wall time to build the shader pairs' base pipelines (measured by the tool from before starting the two processes until both exit; best of 3; one-process and two-process runs alternating; each from an empty archive):

| Workload | One process | Two processes | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Tears of the Kingdom (`main` `c22f30a3`) | 186.8 s | 139.0 s\* | −47.8 s (−25.6%) |
| Tears of the Kingdom (`main` `4cc27d10`) | 213.6 s | 165.8 s | −47.8 s (−22.4%) |
| Pokémon Scarlet (`main` `c22f30a3`) | 140.4 s | 112.6 s | −27.8 s (−19.8%) |

\*Best of the 2 runs that completed; the other hit the Metal abort described below.

Between `c22f30a3` and `4cc27d10`, Tears of the Kingdom's shader libraries were rebuilt with the shader translator from `4cc27d10`. Pokémon Scarlet was not benchmarked on `4cc27d10`.

- **Output equivalence:** One-process and two-process runs build the same base pipelines with 0 failures, and a one-process run over a two-process archive finds every pair already present.
- **Other configurations tried (not faster):** 3 or 4 processes; 2 processes with 12–14 workers each.
- **Memory overhead:** A prebuild process peaks at 0.5–0.8 GB resident and a compiler service at up to 0.6 GB; the second process adds one prebuild process and two compiler services.

### Open issue: 1/51 Metal abort

In 1 of 51 two-process runs (46 Tears of the Kingdom, 5 Pokémon Scarlet) — specifically a Tears of the Kingdom run on `c22f30a3` — one process aborted inside Metal:

- **Error:** `Render Pipeline Descriptor Validation: vertexFunction must not be nil` under `newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor`, called from `arch_capture_try`.
- **Not #2513:** Neither process was serializing at the time (the aborted process's last archive write had finished 10.6 s earlier).
- **Result:** The surviving process finished the remaining pairs; the tool logged the lost process, skipped writing the completion stamp (`prebuilt.tsv`), and exited with status 0, leaving 948 missing base pipelines to be built on the next run.
- **Reproducibility:** Did not occur in any of the 30 subsequent two-process runs on `4cc27d10`, nor in 14 one-process runs (11 on `c22f30a3`, 3 on `4cc27d10`). The cause is unknown.

### Not tested

- **macOS 27.2**, where the #2513 crash was originally observed
- **`--prebake` mode**, which writes the archives shipped inside a Mac app bundle alongside each archive's `.mtl4-json` Metal pipelines script
- **Other Macs**

### Question

Is this worth pursuing, or is the current wait acceptable for a build step? If it's of interest, I can share the patch (one file, ~170 lines, disabled unless `DM_PSO_PREBUILD_PROCS` is set).
title: Pipeline prebuild: workers wait ~30% of the time on archive writes

## What is missing

PR #3241 adds a profile for Alien: Isolation (`010075D00E8BA000`). The game keeps its shaders in `resources/nvn_shader_cache`, a container (magic `NVNC`) of 3,225 whole GLSLC outputs, and nothing in `shader_split.py` reads it. A build from the NSPs therefore stops at the GLSLC capture step:

```
[RED] captured only 6 run-time shaders, the profile needs 2818
```

The script sees 6 GLSL sources and `glslcCompile` in `main` and expects run-time capture only. For the PR I cut the container by hand into `glslc_capture/<FNV-1a of the output>.glslc` files beside the RomFS, which is where the split reads them, and built the tables from those. So the profile cannot be rebuilt from a raw dump yet.

What I found in the file (`resources/nvn_shader_cache`, 30,503,584 bytes):

- Header, 16 bytes: `NVNC`, u32 version = 1, u32 count = 3,225, u32 blob size = 30,297,168.
- 3,225 records of 64 bytes: u32 offset at +0x38 and u32 size at +0x3c. Two 64-bit values at +0x00 and +0x20 (probably the key) are not decoded here.
- The blob: the entries back to back, offsets counted from its start; `16 + 3,225 x 64 + blob size` equals the file size exactly.
- Every entry is a GLSLC output (magic `0x19866891`, its u32 at +0x44 equals the entry size). All 3,225 parse with `shader_split.glslc_shaders`. Stages: 3,218 pixel, 3,219 vertex, 6 compute, 9 domain, 9 hull, 2 geometry.

Not checked: whether the game also loads this file as a shader cache at run time.

## What you propose

A reader in `shader_split.py` that recognises `NVNC` and hands its entries to `glslc_shaders`, as for the other containers, so that these games need no capture step for them; or, if you prefer, a documented pre-step. You know the code better than I do, so please take it whichever way fits. Below is the small script I used, as a working prototype of the extraction only. On this game it produces exactly the 3,225 files the PR's tables were built from (same names, same bytes).

One more thing the capture step contributes: the six run-time shaders. A Mac boot of 30 s captures all six, and the tables in the PR include them.

<details>
<summary>nvnc_cut.py (48 lines)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut a Switch `nvn_shader_cache` (magic NVNC) into one `<FNV-1a>.glslc` file per entry.

Usage: nvnc_cut.py <nvn_shader_cache> <output folder>

Alien: Isolation (010075D00E8BA000) keeps its shaders in /resources/nvn_shader_cache. Each entry is a whole GLSLC output, which
shader_split.py reads from <dir>/<FNV-1a of the output>.glslc (the glslc_capture folder beside the RomFS).

Layout, as found in that file:
  header, 16 bytes: b"NVNC", u32 version (1), u32 count, u32 blob size
  count records of 64 bytes: u32 offset at +0x38 and u32 size at +0x3c (the rest, probably a key, is not used here)
  blob: the entries back to back, offsets counted from the start of the blob
"""
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def fnv1a64(data: bytes) -> int:
    h = 0xcbf29ce484222325
    for b in data:
        h = ((h ^ b) * 0x100000001b3) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def main(src: str, out: str) -> None:
    data = Path(src).read_bytes()
    if data[:4] != b'NVNC' or len(data) < 16:
        sys.exit('not an NVNC cache')
    magic, version, count, blob_size = struct.unpack_from('<4sIII', data, 0)
    if version != 1:
        sys.exit(f'NVNC version {version}: only version 1 is known')
    blob = 16 + 64 * count
    if blob + blob_size != len(data):
        sys.exit('the sizes in the header do not add up to the file size')
    out_dir = Path(out)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(count):
        offset, size = struct.unpack_from('<II', data, 16 + 64 * i + 0x38)
        entry = data[blob + offset:blob + offset + size]
        (out_dir / f'{fnv1a64(entry):016x}.glslc').write_bytes(entry)
    print(f'{count} entries cut into {out_dir}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])
```

</details>

## Platforms

Mac (tested), and Android through Peanuts Native, which builds its packs from the same split.
title: A reader for Alien: Isolation's NVNC shader cache (resources/nvn_shader_cache)

## Summary

On iPhone 17 Pro Max, TOTK reaches gameplay after successful manifest prewarm, but I recorded two different in-game crash signatures on the same IPA: an uncaught `std::bad_alloc`, and then a null-destination `memmove` from `pkg_edges_take` with prediction disabled.

Related background: #2965. The library-input ownership/unmap fix in `8c94bd1e5312cfc74f49afff6c3d1e2326ec66b9` is included in this build. These runs fail **after** prewarm; I am not assuming either a shared root cause with #2965 or completely independent causes. This is a new report, not a request to reopen that issue.

## Environment

- iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 27.2.1; TOTK 1.4.3 (`0100F2C0115B6000`).
- Commit `3a2a62f705ed09bf71de3e286d0803560bbb8a4a`, shader chain `4dbd705d26e9` (both logs confirm).
- B-route shaders, packaged with `--shader-files` and separate RomFS.
- Both runs: `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`; MTLDevice pipelines/hybrid off confirmed in the logs.
- `DM_NVN_PREFETCH=0` in both runs. Only the second adds `DM_NVN_PREDICT=0`. The attached env files show these explicitly.

## Logs

[Two complete crash-session app logs and their env files](https://gist.github.com/hexart/6a92bb0e0d8d9b9cd7172f456f384394). App-container UUIDs in paths are redacted; crash addresses and diagnostic data are preserved. This is an unlisted gist accessible to anyone with the link. No saves, game files, user manifest, Jetsam or other-app reports are attached.

All times below are **2026-11-23, UTC+8 (Asia/Shanghai)**.

### 1. Around 12:43–12:48: uncaught bad_alloc

File: `20261123-1248-prefetch-off-bad-alloc.log`.

- Startup lists: bundled **4,092** + user **10,447** lines. Prewarm completes: **8,468 shaders / 5,113 render pipelines / 82 compute pipelines**, **49.226 s**.
- Gameplay is reached. Last logged long frame: **11,116 at elapsed 307.93 s**, including startup/prewarm; last save timestamp **12:48:37**.
- Ends with `libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::bad_alloc` and `CRASH sig=6`.
- Host workqueue stack ends in `_pthread_wqthread`, but much of it is `<redacted>`. Aligned `operator new[]` symbols occur in the register-memory peek, **not an identified failing allocation stack**; the allocation caller, requested size and alignment remain unknown.
- No `mmap failed` or `NSMallocException` messages.
- Crash census: footprint **2.11 GiB**, virtual regions **449.93 GiB**, 16,186 regions; largest free gap printed **0.00 GB**. Most recent periodic process-limit headroom sample was **1,283 MB**, not a measurement at the failure itself.

### 2. Around 14:51–15:12: prediction off, SIGSEGV in texture edge snapshot

File: `20261123-1512-predict-off-pkg-edges-segv.log` (the complete session was in `log.prev.txt` after a subsequent launch; that new launch's short log is deliberately not attached).

- Both boot env lines are present. Later: `DM_NVN_PREDICT=0: no parallel precompile prediction`.
- No submission-binds `shader prefetch:` or `parallel precompile:` messages throughout this session. Periodic statistics show zero predictions and background builds.
- Startup lists: bundled **4,092** + user **10,845** lines; **14,061** deduplicated prewarm rows. Completes **8,595 shaders / 5,382 render pipelines / 84 compute pipelines** in **1.6837 s**.
- First save timestamp **14:51:04**, last save **15:11:10**. Last long frame: **55,987 at elapsed 1,258.36 s** (about 21 minutes). This includes two graphics suspend/resume sequences with audio interruptions, so it is not 21 minutes of uninterrupted gameplay. The completed crash log's modification time was **15:12:00**.
- Ends with:
  ```text
  CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=_platform_memmove+0xa8 lr=pkg_edges_take+0x16c
  x0=0 x1=0x713f330040 x2=0x2fe0
  bt: tex_mtl_resolve+0x1240 tex_mtl+0x64 treg_tex+0x20
      tex_by_id_ref+0x2c0 encode_args_full+0x3e14 encode_args+0x154
      draw_+0x39ac draw+0x88 mtl_exec+0x1d68 nq_worker+0x664 ...
  ```
  The dump identifies the source region with a **256×256 texture, format 0x87**. `x2` is the copy count at the fault, not an established allocation-request size.
- No `bad_alloc`, `NSMallocException` or `mmap failed` messages in this session.
- Crash census: footprint **2.28 GiB**, virtual regions **449.97 GiB**, 17,975 regions; largest gap printed **0.01 GB**. Last periodic sample (frame 55,800) reports process-limit headroom **1,026 MB**, GPU allocated **2,086 MB**, system free **124 MB**, and zero memory-pressure warn/critical events. These precede the crash and are not allocator-failure measurements; system free memory is not process headroom.

I checked the device's system crash-log root and `Retired`: no corresponding DmIOS `.ips` was available for either run.

## Source finding / possible defensive handling (not tested)

[`pkg_edges_take`, same build, lines 3465–3475](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/3a2a62f705ed09bf71de3e286d0803560bbb8a4a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L3465-L3475) assigns either buffer-backed storage or `malloc(pk->edge_n[i])` to `pk->edge[i]`, then calls `memcpy` without checking the destination. The second log's null destination and return address make this a concrete path to review. They strongly suggest a null edge-snapshot destination, but do **not** prove whether malloc failed versus object state/concurrency, or why an allocation would fail.

Could this optional snapshot path fail conservatively: clear any partially built snapshots **and their lengths**, abandon the edge-only-write optimization, and let the normal conservative re-upload decision apply? [`pkg_edges_clean`, lines 3501–3508](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/3a2a62f705ed09bf71de3e286d0803560bbb8a4a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L3501-L3508) already returns false when both edge lengths are zero. Merely skipping `memcpy` while keeping nonzero `edge_n` would still leave a later null `memcmp` risk. This is an **unimplemented, untested defensive suggestion for maintainer review**, not a proven fix or an explanation of underlying allocation pressure.

For the first signature, preserving raw PCs and image identities even for `<redacted>` frames, and capturing the failing allocation's requested size/alignment, would be more useful than guessing its caller from nearby shader activity.

## Interpretation limits

- This is **not an equal-input controlled A/B**: user lists were 10,447 vs 10,845 lines, routes/interruption history are not established identical, and the 49.226 s vs 1.684 s prewarm reflects different cache conditions. The longer second session does not establish that disabling prediction extended survival.
- Disabling program prefetch plus this configuration's prediction path was verified, but was insufficient to prevent an in-game crash. This does not exclude all shader/PSO paths, retained-cache growth or allocation pressure; the observed exceptions differ.
- In both censuses tag 31 is **385 GiB of GUARD reservations**, not evidence of shader leakage or a 450 GiB guest allocation (guest is 5 GiB). Untagged regions total about 50.8 GiB, with provenance unresolved. The printed gap sizes are rounded; `0.00 GB` does not mean zero bytes. Neither census alone proves VA exhaustion, and low footprint/headroom samples do not identify the failing allocator.
title: TOTK on iPhone: in-game crashes after prewarm (bad_alloc and null destination in pkg_edges_take)

body:
### What happened

Gameplay (new game, the station after the intro) runs at about 25–38 fps on an M2 Max, fullscreen. The log's timing lines put it on the GPU (GPU p50 26–42 ms, submit+present 4–7 ms, thermal nominal). The game already renders 960x540 and DLSS → MetalFX temporal takes it to 1920x1080, so resolution is not the cost.

A 90 s Metal System Trace (Instruments, attached to `dmhost`, 2,958 frames, about 33 fps) shows the GPU is not saturated:

- GPU at its Maximum performance state 94 % of the time, thermal state Nominal throughout.
- GPU busy (any channel, union of intervals) only **64 %** of the window: per frame, busy p50 **21.1 ms** (p90 31.8) against a first-to-last span p50 **29.6 ms** (p90 41.5).
- About 400 GPU intervals per frame across ~20 command buffers: 140 fragment, 43 compute, 140 vertex. 323,356 of the 417,952 fragment intervals (77 %, about 110 a frame) last under 10 µs.
- Idle time: 31.9 s of the 89 s. **20.8 s of it is inside one command buffer** (gaps between consecutive encoders: 9.1 s in gaps under 100 µs, 9.5 s in gaps of 100 µs–2 ms), about 7 ms a frame. 8.8 s is in gaps of 5 ms or more between command buffers, about 3 ms a frame.
- MetalFX temporal costs 0.63 ms a frame, the Metal HUD 0.09 ms.

This matches [Draw passes that wait for each other again while images share memory](docs/reference/frame-rate.md) (many small idle gaps between render encoders of one command buffer), and the log says `draw-pass entry barriers full 17147 / saved 0` with the default `DM_NVN_BARRIER=full`.

So I tried `DM_NVN_BARRIER=game` (player env.txt, no rebuild). It took effect (`draw-pass entry barriers full 2155 / saved 1271`), but about 30 s in, at frame 1,593, a command buffer failed with a GPU page fault:

```
[RED] command buffer error details fence=10342: ... Code=2 "Caused GPU Address Fault Error (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)" ...
[RED] state of the failed submission fence=10342: frame 1593; since the last submission: passes +5, first texture uploads +0, re-uploads +0, serial table changes +38; deferred-release queue 140
[RED] zero GPU addresses in failed command buffer #1: 0 (none) (0 in the run)
```

After it, every later submission was ignored (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored`, 489 execution errors) and the host exited with 70. The two runs before it with the default barriers (about 40 min and about 10 min, the second one with the trace) had no execution error at all. The GPU returned to idle after the exit (not the #2664 hang).

My guess is that PRAGMATA's sparse pools and its deferred releases need the full order that `game` drops (pages remapped or memory released while a later pass that the full barrier used to hold back still reads it), but I have not traced which pass faulted.

### What you expected

With `DM_NVN_BARRIER=game` (or a profile `draw_barriers game`), the game keeps running and the in-buffer gaps shrink, as on Ocarina of Time. If `game` cannot be safe here, a barrier that waits only where PRAGMATA's pages or releases change could recover part of the ~7 ms a frame.

### What happened

This update and patch for Doom 2016 v1.4 was built on these commits that have not yet been merged upstream: 

https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/851

# Depth snapshots by rectangle: copy only what changed (DOOM 2016: about 98.6% less shadow-map copying)

## Problem

DOOM (2016) caches its shadows in one 4096x4096 Depth16 atlas (ser 29 in my logs). Its shader `d46395f1b700b798` samples that atlas while drawing into it, after a game barrier each time. The same-pass depth sampling rule (`fb_depth_snap`) then takes a fresh snapshot, and every snapshot copies the **whole level: 32 MB**.

In a GPU profile from an iPhone 15 Pro (A17 Pro), each copy appears as a gap of about 1.65–2.2 ms before the next shadow pass. There were 8–22 copies per frame in combat, so **8–32 ms of GPU time per frame** went to copies. In the heaviest sampled frame, that was more than the actual rendering.

## Change

Each snapshot cache entry now remembers the texture it was copied from, plus the rectangles written to that texture since the copy. When the next snapshot is needed, only those rectangles are copied into the existing snapshot texture. If nothing was written, nothing is copied and the pass is not ended.

Writes are tracked as follows:

- **Draws** that write depth or stencil to the attachment add their viewport ∩ scissor (+8 px margin) (`dsr_draw_note`, after `fb_prepare`).
- **Scissored depth clear triangles** (`clear_ds_tri`) add their scissor.
- **Anything not bounded by a rectangle** makes the next snapshot a whole copy, as before. This covers:
  - a main pass whose depth load action isn't Load (a clear or don't-care load);
  - any pass opened through `enc_r_begin` (geometry, tessellation, transform feedback, internal passes);
  - a blit into the texture (`enc_b_copy_texture`, `enc_b_copy_buffer_texture[_opt]`, and the direct copy in the MetalFX ordering path);
  - a clear still waiting (`R.clear_d` / `R.clear_s` / lazy clears);
  - mesh-task draws;
  - layer-writing vertex shaders;
  - a replaced source texture (its base pointer changed) or a re-keyed or reshaped cache entry.

The change is controlled by `DM_DEPTH_SNAP_RECT` (1/0). It defaults on for DOOM (0100416004C00000) only, and a launcher toggle ("Fast shadow copies") is shown for DOOM. With it off, behaviour is unchanged. A log line reports progress: `depth snapshots by rectangle so far: N (… by rectangles, … with nothing to copy, … whole); copied X MB where whole copies would have been Y MB`.

## Results (iPhone 15 Pro, DOOM 1.4, 75% 3D resolution)

| | Before (whole copies) | After (rectangles) |
|---|---|---|
| Snapshot data copied | 32 MB each | 8.8 GB over ~20,000 snapshots (whole copies would have been 640 GB) |
| GPU time per frame, p50, gameplay | 45–56 ms | 21–29 ms |
| Frames dropped per 300, gameplay | 174–241 | mostly 0–24 |
| Frame time p50, gameplay | 52–62 ms | ~33 ms (holds the 30 fps cap) |

Shadows render correctly with it on. Only the first snapshot of the session was a whole copy.

Caveats on the comparison: the "after" session started with the phone cooler (thermal state 0 rising to 2; "before" was at 2 from launch). The texture upload mode also differed between the two runs, and the "after" run used the slower one. The GPU-time halving is far larger than either difference.

## Notes

- Built and tested on the engine shipped with NX2Apple v1.5.0 (nxnative `99224562` plus its patches). The patch applies there with offsets only. It may need a small rebase onto current `main`.
- Only DOOM has been tested. The mechanism is general (any `fb_depth_snap` user benefits when its writes are rectangle-bounded). A game-profile key, or default-on after wider testing, may suit the project better than the program-ID check.

[depth-snapshot-rects.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35244976/depth-snapshot-rects.patch)

Feature Request: Per-Game Controller Face Button Remapping (A/B and X/Y)

Summary

Add options to independently swap the A/B buttons and X/Y buttons for all supported controllers.

Description

It would be useful to have the ability to swap the A/B and X/Y face buttons independently, allowing users to configure controller layouts to their preference.

For example, Xbox controllers use a different physical button arrangement than Nintendo controllers. Being able to swap A/B would allow Xbox users to match the traditional Nintendo button layout.

Requested Features

1. Independent Button Swapping

Provide two separate options:

* Swap A and B
* Swap X and Y

Each option should be independently configurable, allowing users to:

* Leave both pairs unchanged.
* Swap A/B only.
* Swap X/Y only.
* Swap both pairs.

2. Settings Window

Ideally, provide these options in the NxNative settings window under Controller Settings.

3. Per-Game Configuration Through env.txt

Also provide the ability to configure these options through each game’s env.txt file.

For example:

DM_SWAP_AB=1
DM_SWAP_XY=0

Where:

* 0 = Original button mapping.
* 1 = Swap the corresponding button pair.

Both options should default to 0 if not specified.

4. Controller Compatibility

The remapping should work with all supported controllers, including:

* Xbox controllers
* PlayStation controllers
* Nintendo Switch controllers
* Other supported gamepads

Expected Behavior

* Remapping should occur at the controller input layer.
* All games should receive the correctly remapped button inputs.
* The settings should be independent for each game.
* Changing the mapping for one game should not affect other games.
* The configuration should work without requiring a separate launcher.

Rationale

Different controllers use different physical face-button arrangements. Providing independent A/B and X/Y swapping would make NxNative more flexible and allow users to choose their preferred button layout.

This would also eliminate the need for external controller-remapping software or modifications to individual game files.

Thank you for considering this feature.
title: Feature Request: Per-Game Controller Face Button Remapping (A/B and X/Y)

body:
### What is missing

I play full screen on a TV (second display) while using the Mac on the main monitor. As soon as I click anything on the main monitor, the controller stops driving the game, until I click the game window again. With `DM_FOCUS_KEEP=1` the game keeps running and presenting out of focus, so only the controller is missing.

Two things stop it:
1. `NSWindowDidResignKeyNotification` → `input_release()` sets `g_input_on = 0` and calls `pads_release()`, and every controller path then returns early on `!g_input_on` (`front_mac.m`). This goes back to #128, which releases input on focus loss so nothing stays pressed.
2. `GCController.shouldMonitorBackgroundEvents` is never set, so GameController stops delivering controller events once another app is active.

The same request reached NX2Apple (LNPANDY/NX2Apple#1169, from a MacBook user with the game on an external display), and it was closed there with a pointer to this repository, as it is engine code.

### What you propose

An opt-in switch, off by default, for example `DM_PAD_BACKGROUND=1`:
- set `GCController.shouldMonitorBackgroundEvents = YES` (macOS 11.3+);
- when the window resigns key, release the keyboard and mouse as today, but keep the controllers on (controller paths gated separately from `g_input_on`);
- minimizing the window still releases everything, as today.

#128's concern is input staying pressed after focus loss. With background events on, a controller's button-up still arrives while another app is active, so nothing should stick.

I tested the idea on a Mac Studio with a DualSense in a build from NX2Apple: a small injected library that sets `shouldMonitorBackgroundEvents` and keeps the game's focus-loss handlers from releasing the controllers. The controller keeps driving the game while another app is active and everything works flawlessly. Happy to send a small PR if the switch is welcome.

### Platforms

Mac
title: Mac: opt-in switch to keep controller input when the game window loses focus

## What happened

The 3D scene is black in battle while the battle UI renders normally. This reproduces in New Game and when loading a save.

## Environment

- Game: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (Asian release), title ID `0100B8A026F14000`, update 1.0.1 (`v65536`)
- NX2Apple 1.5.0, packaged nxnative engine `99224562186a`, shader chain `df1800562702`
- Apple M5 Max, macOS 27.2.1
- Build target: This Mac

## Reproduction

Build this game for Mac, start New Game, and enter a battle. The 3D background is black; timeline and menus remain visible. It also happens with an existing save.

## Frame diagnosis

A frame-2100 target capture shows the 3D scene in intermediate target serial 40212. Pass 73274, using fragment shader `8201e29be86bacaf_b` and vertex shader `315fd0e69cae491f_b`, reads scene 40212, bloom 40213, and 3D LUT 257, then writes target 40226 entirely black. Later passes propagate that black image; the UI is drawn afterwards.

The 32×32×32 LUT contains nonzero RGB at 32761/32768 texels. The exposure buffer starts with floats `1.2, 1.2, 1, 1`; `fp_c3[156].w` is about 0.94. The log reports zero shader keys missing from the map and no `[RED]` lines.

## Checks already tried

- MetalFX upscaling off
- `DM_PROF_RENDER_COND=on`
- `DM_PROF_TEX_FLUSH_UPLOAD=on`
- `DM_PROF_TEX_DIRTY_UPLOAD=on`
- `DM_PSO_MTL4=0` (MTLDevice pipeline path)

The scene remained black in every test. All temporary diagnostic overrides have been removed.

The regional profile records an older Mac battle rendering correctly, but says that was not rerun on the current consolidated profile. Could this color grading pass or 3D LUT sampling be a current-chain regression? The exact cause remains unconfirmed.

No game files, keys, saves, or captured textures are attached. I can provide redacted diagnostics if useful.

body:
## What happened

1. The iPhone app had cloud saves on (a folder in iCloud Drive) and was in step with the cloud. Another device later sent a newer save with more progress.
2. The IPA was reinstalled. The cloud-save folder came back as not chosen, because the old bookmark no longer resolved for the new install (`CloudSaves.m`: "A re-signed build gets a bookmark the system will not resolve for it").
3. The folder was chosen again in the launcher and Play was pressed.
4. **The cloud save was replaced by the older save still on the iPhone. No dialog was shown.**

## Likely cause

After the folder is chosen again, iCloud on the iPhone may not have listed the folder's contents yet. Neither `<title>/save.dmsync` nor its `.save.dmsync.icloud` placeholder is visible.

- `front_save_sync_fetch` (`dm/ios/Sources/SaveSync.m`) takes "neither file exists" as **no save in the cloud** and returns `0`.
- `ss_decide` (`dm/host/save_sync.c`): `if (!*remote) return *local ? SS_PUSH : SS_KEEP;`. With nothing in the cloud, this device's save is sent. The decision ignores that `<save>.sync` still holds a `base`, which proves this device synced a save to that folder before.
- `save_sync_report` therefore says `cloud=0 conflict=0`. The launcher passes `ask` and shows no dialog. The mount logs "is not in the cloud yet: it goes to the cloud", and `send_save` writes the old save over the path. iCloud then uploads it over the newer server copy.

The #2180 / 07d6ea46 protection ("ask when both changed") does not cover this, because the cloud side looks *empty*, not *changed*. No backup of the cloud's save is kept either, because the host never saw it.

## Expected

"No save in the cloud" while this device has a sync base should not count as an empty cloud. The save may only be unlisted (a folder chosen again, a reinstall), or it may have been removed. The player should be asked before this device's save is sent. A send during the game should never go over a cloud save the start could not see.

## Related

- #2180 / 07d6ea46: ask when both saves changed (does not cover a cloud that looks empty)
- #1785: never replace a cloud save that was not compared
- #1148: the cloud-saves folder picker / bookmark resolution on iOS
- #882: LiveContainer folder picker
title: iOS cloud saves: after a reinstall and choosing the folder again, an older local save silently replaces the cloud's (iCloud had not listed the file yet)

- base size 56.87 GB, update 59.93 GB
- no DLC in the package

## Engine and graphics API

- **NVN** (markers in `main`, `sdk`, `subsdk0`)
- **Wwise** audio (marker in `main`)
- modules: `main`, `rtld`, `sdk`, `subsdk0` (C/libc), `subsdk1` (C/libc)

## Survey and what happened

`survey.md` is attached (generated by `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py 0400DDB020648000.nup --platform mac-app --survey-only`, nxnative `e2c6d93`, chain `df1800562702`, Apple M5 Max / macOS 26.6.2).

**Build ID lookup:** `no profile registers its main build` — `main` is `afd670b6ba27b9e68d268e601bf91acd`, and there is no profile for `0400DDB020648000` at all, so this went straight to the survey path.

**How far it got:** the survey completed. No build was attempted beyond the provisional profile, so I have no gameplay log to attach — I stopped there rather than reporting a crash that says nothing about the port.

### What the survey names as open, and what I could confirm

1. **SDK 20_5_3.** The survey warns SDK 20 differs from the SDK 16 sizes the host was converted to. Worth noting: Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (`04003F40232DE000`) is **SDK 20.5.15** and plays, so SDK 20 itself is not the blocker — but the NVN object sizes still need checking per `docs/reference/nvn-objects.md`.

2. **No BNSH / BAHS at the top level.** The RomFS is 150 files / 59.83 GB, and 59.57 GB of it is `archive/emporium` (118 files). The survey says the shaders "are inside compressed or other containers or in main, and must be located first". This is the part I do not know how to approach: `archive/emporium` is a Red Engine container, not a Nintendo one, so locating the shader blobs means reversing that container format first. Any pointer here would be the most useful thing in this report.

3. **`nn::ro` at run time.** The RomFS holds 1 `.nro` and 1 `.nrr`; registered NROs have to be collected and rewritten beside the other modules.

### What is *not* a problem

The imports are covered. `main` imports 544 symbols and **all 544 are new** (none shared with the game the host was brought up on), but the host's 1,356 HLE hooks contain every one of them — `present in new game sdk exports: 1038` of 1356. Broken down by area: `C/libc` 219, `other C++` 74, `nn::os` 71, `nn::hid` 41, `nn::fs` 26, `nn::codec` 18, `nn::audio` 17, `nn::vi` 13, `nn::account` 12, `nn::oe` 12, `nn::ro` 8, `nn::nifm` 7, `nn::ssl` 6, `nn::time` 5, `nn::socket` 3, plus a few singletons, and `nvn` 1. So the symbol layer is not what would stop a port.

### Provisional profile the guess produced

```
modules      main sdk
mem_reserve  0x140000000
mem_alias    0x118000000
mem_stack    0x10000000
app_pool     0x240000000
sys_resource 0x4000000
```

The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource and `main` never sets a heap, so the game maps its own memory: 5 GB block with a 4.375 GB alias region. That is a guess from the files, not measured.

## What I am asking

Mainly: **is this reachable, and where would you start?** Concretely —

- Is the `archive/emporium` container something you have seen (or would want a helper for), or is shader location here a dead end for now?
- Is the SDK 20 NVN-object check a "walk the list in `nvn-objects.md`" job, or did you find a shortcut when Hyrule Warriors (SDK 20.5.15) was brought up?
- If a profile for this is out of scope for now, say so and I will leave it — I would rather ask than spend a week on the container and get nowhere.

I am happy to run experiments and send back what they show. I will not attach game files, keys or anything extracted from the game; the survey was generated on my machine and contains only module metadata, sizes, symbol names and counts.

## Environment

- nxnative `e2c6d93`, shader chain `df1800562702`
- Apple M5 Max, 64 GB, macOS 26.6.2
- package: `.nup`, update v262144

body:
### What happened

SUPER BOMBERMAN R 2 (provisional profile from the NSP script) aborts when leaving the title screen (pressing Start), exit 134:

```
[dm] [RED] sf: the game connects to service friend:u itself, which the host does not serve
[dm] game called nn::diag abort: Result 0xe15, call site sdk+0x8d97c
[dm] bt: sdk+0x8d97c sdk+0x345718 sdk+0x344f88 sdk+0x341b60 sdk+0x341d28 main+0x15e834c main+0x22b2c80 ...
[dm] FATAL game aborted
```

### Game, title ID and version
SUPER BOMBERMAN R 2, 0100B87017D94000, 1.0.0 (main build 6B48A9447073EA2F), NintendoSDK nnSdk-14_3_0-Release

### nxnative commit / shader chain
806fabe1 / shader chain 26e1a5f38264

### Device and OS
Mac17,8 (Apple M5 Pro), macOS 27.2.1

### How it was built and run
NX Play (`nxplay <NSP folder>`, which runs `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`); reproduced on the Mac running the host from a terminal (`start_mac.sh`). Xbox Wireless Controller.

### Settings and environment overrides
None (NX Play defaults).

### Cause

Mapping the backtrace to the sdk's dynamic symbols:

| Address | Symbol |
|---|---|
| sdk+0x341d28 | `nn::friends::EnsureBlockedUserListAvailable(AsyncContext*)` |
| sdk+0x341b60 | `nn::friends::EnsureBlockedUserListAvailable(AsyncContext*, const account::Uid&)` |
| sdk+0x344f88 | `nn::friends::detail::ShimLibraryGlobal::Initialize()` |
| sdk+0x345718 | return address in `nn::friends::detail::ipc::Initialize()` |

`hle_friends.c` / `hle_offline.c` cut the `Uid` forms of most friends calls, but not the blocked-user list availability calls, nor several no-`Uid` (preselected user) forms. Comparing this game's `nn::friends` imports with the host hooks (`nso_syms.host_hooks`), the unhooked ones that matter are:

**Open `friend:u` directly (abort 0xe15 without a cut):**
- `EnsureBlockedUserListAvailable` (both forms), `CheckBlockedUserListAvailability` (both forms)
- `EnsureFriendListAvailable(AsyncContext*)`, `CheckFriendListAvailability(bool*)`
- `DeclareOpenOnlinePlaySession()`, `DeclareCloseOnlinePlaySession()`
- `GetProfileList(AsyncContext*, Profile*, const NetworkServiceAccountId*, int)`
- `UpdateFriendInfo(Friend*, const NetworkServiceAccountId*, int)`

**Forward to already-hooked `Uid` forms (cut for consistency):** `NotificationQueue::Initialize()`, `Friend::Update`. `UserPresence::Initialize()` only stores the current user and returns success; it is accepted like its `Uid` form.

**Run on objects whose constructors are cut:** `AsyncContext::Cancel`, `NotificationQueue::Clear`, `NotificationQueue::Finalize` lock the object's mutex, which the cut constructors never initialise.

The remaining unhooked imports are local getters/setters, except `Friend::GetProfileImage` and `Profile::GetProfileImageUrl`, which open the service but need a valid `Friend` / `Profile`, which the cut lists never produce (not cut here).

### Fix (tested locally)

Cut them the same way as their existing `Uid` counterparts: `Ensure*` fails at once, `Check*Availability` reports unavailable with success, `UserPresence::Initialize()` is accepted, the rest fail or do nothing.

```diff
diff --git a/dm/host/hle_friends.c b/dm/host/hle_friends.c
index 59dfd782..36bd4043 100644
--- a/dm/host/hle_friends.c
+++ b/dm/host/hle_friends.c
@@ -69,3 +69,24 @@ HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends29DeclareCloseOnlinePlaySessionERKNS_7account3UidE", "o
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends12UserPresence10InitializeERKNS_7account3UidE", "presence accepted, not published (cut)", Result, h_fr_UpInit, void *self, const void *uid) { (void)self; (void)uid; return RES_OK; }
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends12UserPresence14SetDescriptionEPKc", "presence accepted, not published (cut)", Result, h_fr_UpDesc, void *self, const char *s) { (void)self; (void)s; return RES_OK; }
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends12UserPresence6CommitEv", "presence accepted, not published (cut)", Result, h_fr_UpCommit, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_OK; }
+// The forms without a Uid (the preselected user) and the blocked-user list: the SDK's own opens the friends service and aborts with 0xe15 when it cannot
+// (SUPER BOMBERMAN R 2 1.0.0 calls EnsureBlockedUserListAvailable(ctx) at the title screen). Cut the same way as the Uid forms above and in hle_offline.c
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends12AsyncContext6CancelEv", "async context has nothing to cancel (cut)", Result, h_fr_AcCancel, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_OK; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends12UserPresence10InitializeEv", "presence accepted, not published (cut)", Result, h_fr_UpInitNoUid, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_OK; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends28DeclareOpenOnlinePlaySessionEv", "online play session unavailable (cut)", Result, h_fr_OpenSessionNoUid, void) { return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends29DeclareCloseOnlinePlaySessionEv", "online play session unavailable (cut)", Result, h_fr_CloseSessionNoUid, void) { return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends14GetProfileListEPNS0_12AsyncContextEPNS0_7ProfileEPKNS_7account23NetworkServiceAccountIdEi", "profile query fails (cut)",
+          Result, h_fr_GetProfileListNoUid, void *ctx, void *out, const void *ids, int n) { (void)ctx; (void)out; (void)ids; (void)n; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends16UpdateFriendInfoEPNS0_6FriendEPKNS_7account23NetworkServiceAccountIdEi", "friend info update fails (cut)",
+          Result, h_fr_UpdateFriendInfoNoUid, void *f, const void *ids, int n) { (void)f; (void)ids; (void)n; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends6Friend6UpdateEv", "friend info update fails (cut)", Result, h_fr_FriendUpdate, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends17NotificationQueue10InitializeEv", "notification queue init fails (cut)", Result, h_fr_NqInitNoUid, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends17NotificationQueue5ClearEv", "notification queue has no session (cut)", Result, h_fr_NqClear, void *self) { (void)self; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends17NotificationQueue8FinalizeEv", "notification queue has no session to close (cut)", void, h_fr_NqFini, void *self) { (void)self; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends25EnsureFriendListAvailableEPNS0_12AsyncContextE", "friend list (cut): the request fails at once", Result, h_fr_ListEnsureNoUid, void *ctx) { (void)ctx; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends27CheckFriendListAvailabilityEPb", "friend list unavailable (cut)", Result, h_fr_ListAvailNoUid, uint8_t *out) { *out = 0; return RES_OK; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends30EnsureBlockedUserListAvailableEPNS0_12AsyncContextE", "blocked user list (cut): the request fails at once", Result, h_fr_BlockedEnsureNoUid, void *ctx) { (void)ctx; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends30EnsureBlockedUserListAvailableEPNS0_12AsyncContextERKNS_7account3UidE", "blocked user list (cut): the request fails at once",
+          Result, h_fr_BlockedEnsure, void *ctx, const void *uid) { (void)ctx; (void)uid; return RES_FAIL; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends32CheckBlockedUserListAvailabilityEPb", "blocked user list unavailable (cut)", Result, h_fr_BlockedAvailNoUid, uint8_t *out) { *out = 0; return RES_OK; }
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn7friends32CheckBlockedUserListAvailabilityEPbRKNS_7account3UidE", "blocked user list unavailable (cut)", Result, h_fr_BlockedAvail, uint8_t *out, const void *uid) { (void)uid; *out = 0; return RES_OK; }
```

With this host the game runs on the Mac: title screen, main menu, Story (World 1 gameplay) and Battle Offline vs 3 COMs, 60 fps, no `[RED]` lines and no abort. Any game calling the direct forms listed above aborts with the same 0xe15, so this is a general fix; I did not add a game profile or note. Not done: `regress.py`, checks in `t_friends.c`, and the docs below.

Suggested `docs/reference/services.md` entry:

> ### SDK 14's friends calls without a `Uid`, and the blocked-user list availability
> - **Symptom:** `[RED] sf: the game connects to service friend:u itself`, then an `nn::diag` abort with Result 0xe15 in `friends::detail::ipc::Initialize` under `friends::EnsureBlockedUserListAvailable` (`sdk+0x341d28`) when leaving the title screen.
> - **Cause:** the no-`Uid` forms and both blocked-user-list availability forms were not taken over.
> - **Fix:** cut as the `Uid` forms are (`hle_friends.c`).
> - **Found on:** SUPER BOMBERMAN R 2 (`0100B87017D94000`, 1.0.0, SDK 14.3).

Open: the immediate `RES_FAIL` from `Ensure*` matches `EnsureFriendListAvailable`'s `Uid` form, but another game could turn it into an error applet (as Dark Souls Remastered did with `GetBlockedUserList`); only this game was tested.

Suggested label: `mac`.

body:
Ocarina of Time: MetalFX produces a dark image after initially rendering with correct colors

Description

When using MetalFX spatial upscaling with Ocarina of Time, the game sometimes renders with noticeably dark or incorrect brightness.

Interestingly, the first run with MetalFX enabled appeared to have correct colors and lighting. Subsequent launches produced a dark image, even though the same MetalFX settings were being used.

The problem also occurs when launching the generated game application directly from Finder, without the separate NXNative Launcher application running.

Environment

  • Platform: macOS

  • Game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

  • NXNative build commit: 806fabe19829

  • Shader chain: 82cb7bb335cc

  • Game profile: 0400486024DEC000

  • Internal rendering resolution: 1920×1080

  • Output resolution: 2560×1440

Configuration

DM_UPSCALER=metalfx
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off
DM_SHARPEN=0.25
DM_RENDER_SCALE=1.00
DM_FIXED_RESOLUTION=1
DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=0
DM_FIXED_SCALE=1.00

Expected behavior

MetalFX should produce an image with brightness, lighting, and colors consistent with the game's original upscaler.

Actual behavior

The image becomes noticeably darker when MetalFX is enabled.

The first MetalFX run appeared correctly colored, but subsequent launches produced the dark image. Disabling MetalFX and using the game's original upscaler does not exhibit the same dark-image behavior.

Diagnostic findings

The MetalFX-enabled log confirms that NXNative recognizes Ocarina of Time's special upscaler color format:

upscaler fa3033d05c0a41d6_b: square-rooted input, linear output (the shader squares): squared into linear, then MetalFX in HDR mode

MetalFX initializes successfully:

upscaler: MetalFX spatial scaler (HDR) 1920x1080 format 115 → 2560x1440 format 115

The first dispatch also confirms that the square-rooted input correction is applied:

upscaler: first dispatch of fa3033d05c0a41d6_b drawn by MetalFX, 1920x1080 at 0,0 of 1920x1080 (format 92, copied) → 2560x1440 at 0,0 of 2560x1440 (format 92, drawn back), squared from its square roots

The source code in dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m contains the OOT-specific UP_COLOR_ROOT detection and COPY_T2T_SQUARE correction. The log indicates this path is being activated.

Comparison of MetalFX ON and OFF logs

The two logs were compared:

  • 0400486024DEC000.log — MetalFX OFF

  • 0400486024DEC000.prev.log — MetalFX ON

Both logs contain exactly the same counts of unrelated graphics errors:

Error | MetalFX OFF | MetalFX ON -- | -- | -- Missing integer-output shader entry points | 14,574 | 14,574 Task/mesh pipeline failures | 1 | 1 Total RED graphics errors | 14,586 | 14,586

This suggests those existing errors are not specific to the MetalFX configuration.

Additional observations

  • The problem occurs when launching directly from Finder.

  • The separate NXNative Launcher application does not need to be running for the issue to occur.

  • The environment file correctly specifies DM_UPSCALER=metalfx.

  • The MetalFX initialization and OOT-specific color correction messages appear in the MetalFX-enabled log.

  • The first MetalFX launch appeared correct, while later launches were dark.

Request

Could the MetalFX texture input/output handling or HDR color processing be investigated?

In particular, it would be useful to determine why the OOT-specific square-root correction is reported as active, yet the resulting image can still appear dark, and why the first MetalFX launch appeared correct while subsequent launches did not.

I have not established the root cause yet, so this report is intended to document the reproducible behavior and diagnostic evidence rather than assume a specific implementation bug.

[Save.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35220450/Save.zip) [0400486024DEC000.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35220458/0400486024DEC000.log) [0400486024DEC000.prev.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35220459/0400486024DEC000.prev.log)
title: Ocarina of Time: MetalFX produces a dark image after initially rendering with correct colors

body:
### What happened

On my M1 Pro, Ocarina of Time hangs the GPU (GPU restart, page faults, then the host exits) shortly after loading Kokiri Forest, on a build that includes 32fe34ef ("chain/mesh: keep subgroup helpers out of line", PR #3069). I traced it to `mesh_subgroup_noinline` in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_rewrite.py`.

**Cause.** In the foliage mesh shaders, SPIRV-Cross's lane prefix-sum helper (`_87`) calls the shuffle helper (`_97`). With both marked `noinline`, the M1's compiler gets the outer helper wrong: its outputs are never written. The vertex indices built from it go out of range. These meshes spill their stage arrays to device memory (`dm_scr`), so the writes land outside their slice, and that's the hang or page fault.

- Spilled, hang: `bc9d26e29a45e6b6`, `65a079a285d693a0`, `eb021183bf9b0092`
- Not spilled, flicker only: `e6df2f14035e7be7`

**Offline repro.** I put the real `_87` and `_97` of `eb021183bf9b0092` in a 32-thread compute kernel, built with the build's flags, and ran it through the runtime compiler on the M1 Pro. I compared it against the fully inlined version over 40 random trials, counting only trials where all 32 lanes call:

| Variant | Wrong outputs |
|---|---|
| `_87` and `_97` out of line (as shipped) | 640 (never written) |
| `_97` inlined, `_87` out of line | 0 |
| `_87` inlined, `_97` out of line | 0 |
| a lone out-of-line shuffle | 0 |

So it's an out-of-line SIMD-group helper calling another out-of-line one. One level is fine.

**What I tried in game** (hand-patched libraries through `DM_MSL_DIR`):
- **Every helper inlined in the 44 affected mesh libraries:** the hangs went away, but `ac2f3feb11427426` then crashed MTLCompilerService (`XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED`, as in #2825), and that took the concurrent compiles down with it.
- **Callee inlined, callers out of line:** correct in the harness, but the game hung the GPU, so I dropped it.
- **Callers inlined, shuffle out of line for `ac2f3feb11427426`, the rest fully inlined:** 56,703 frames, 0 GPU errors, 0 compiler failures, and the foliage draws correctly.

### Proposed fix

Keep only the leaves out of line: a subgroup helper that calls another subgroup helper stays inline. Both spellings are matched, so the pass stays idempotent on sources that were already rewritten.

On the 44 affected libraries:
- **30 change:** the two callers are inlined, and the shuffle stays out of line.
- **14 are unchanged:** they have a single helper.
- **`ac2f3feb11427426`:** the output is byte-identical to the variant I played with.

All 15 mesh pipelines I have recorded compile in parallel on the M1 with 0 failures. I added a case for the nested helpers to `test_dmsh_raw_noinline.py`, and all its tests pass.

**Not checked yet:** any GPU other than the M1 Pro. In particular, I don't know whether inlining the callers brings back the #2825 SIGBUS on `g14s` at the 26.6 minimum; your offline matrix would show it.

If it helps, I can open a PR with the change and the test.

The original reports in #2777 predate 32fe34e, so this can't explain them. Unchecked indexes into spilled stage memory turn any wrong index into a hang, though.

### What happened

Packing a Mac app from an unpacked game folder (base + update v262144) stops at the shader split's table check, every time. Pack, file check and rewrite pass.

```
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 040041E0212AE000's:
shader_map.tsv: 94 row(s) only in the profile, 94 only in the split
  profile: ps_objects.bin	0	pixel	0dbd6d97785bcb50	/objects/_mattest2.w3d#SHN@0x1f30#var0
  split:   vs_objects.bin	0	vertex	0fb048039a4d2fc8	/objects/_clock.w3d#SHN@0xcd0#var0
```

This looks like the same cause as #2927 and #2950: since 8d62601, a duplicate key takes its first copy's label. Fast Fusion's `shader_map.tsv` was last changed in b16693b3 (2026-11-14), before 8d62601, and none of the later profile refreshes included it.

The two tables hold the same 2,976 shaders, with the same keys, stages and packages. Only two duplicate keys changed their representative, from `blocker_full.w3d` to `_clock.w3d`, which sorts first:

```
ps_objects.bin	pixel	f50c22cdf793173f	profile: /objects/blocker_full.w3d#SHN@0x28b0#var0
                                        	split:   /objects/_clock.w3d#SHN@0xcd0#var0
vs_objects.bin	vertex	0fb048039a4d2fc8	profile: /objects/blocker_full.w3d#SHN@0x28b0#var0
                                        	split:   /objects/_clock.w3d#SHN@0xcd0#var0
```

Ignoring the index column, these 4 rows are the whole difference. The new first rows shift the indices of 47 rows each in `ps_objects.bin` and `vs_objects.bin`, which gives the 94/94 count. `_clock.w3d` is in the update's RomFS as well as the base's, so this is not a difference between game files. The split's `shader_facts.tsv`, `shader_pairs.tsv` and `pso_pairs.tsv` are byte-identical to the profile's.

Workaround, verified: copying the split's `shader_map.tsv` (`<work folder>/shader/pkg.partial/tables/`) into `dm/games/040041E0212AE000/`, as docs/reference/packing.md describes for a splitter change. After that, all 8 stages pass and the app plays on the Mac with no black screen (a 9-minute session).

### What you expected

The split matches the profile's tables and packing continues. A refresh of `dm/games/040041E0212AE000/shader_map.tsv` from a split at current main would fix it.

### Game, title ID and version

Fast Fusion, 040041E0212AE000, base + update v262144 (no DLC), as an unpacked game folder (exefs + romfs)

### nxnative commit

99224562 (NX2Apple 1.5.0's engine, `99224562186a8fdb7e97afb872319a21941ec317-ebcbf51f244f`). The profile's `shader_map.tsv` on main is unchanged as of 2026-11-21.

### Shader chain version

df1800562702

### How it was built and run

The NSP script failed before anything ran (`--platform mac-app`, run as the NX2Apple GUI runs it)

### Device and OS

Apple M5 (Mac17,3), macOS 27.2.1

### Settings and environment overrides

none

### Logs

Script failure. The run used `--progress json`; below is an excerpt of its `say` and `stage_end` events written as console lines, with paths shortened. The build stops before the app runs, so there is no host log.

```
[14:24:14] game profile: 040041E0212AE000
[14:24:14] Mac app: the Mac shaders and the Mac host, packed into a Mac app; no iOS shaders, Xcode project or IPA
[14:24:15] base: base

✓ [3/8] rewrite (0:06): main, sdk
✗ [4/8] shader split (0:21)
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 040041E0212AE000's:
shader_map.tsv: 94 row(s) only in the profile, 94 only in the split
  profile: ps_objects.bin	0	pixel	0dbd6d97785bcb50	/objects/_mattest2.w3d#SHN@0x1f30#var0
  split:   vs_objects.bin	0	vertex	0fb048039a4d2fc8	/objects/_clock.w3d#SHN@0xcd0#var0
Either these game files are not the versions the profile registers, or shader_split.py now reads them differently and the profile's tables were not split again (the split's tables: <work folder>/shader/pkg.partial/tables)
```

# Shader scan fails with `NameError` because `FZLC` and `RDHS` constants are undefined

## Description

When building Fast Fusion for macOS using NxNative Launcher, the shader scanning stage fails to read 3,329 files because `shader_split.py` references the `FZLC` constant without defining it.

The build reports:

```text
3329 file(s) could not be read, their shaders are left out
(first: audio/00_01.adpcm: NameError: name 'FZLC' is not defined)
```

The shader scanner reports that the profile's tables hold every file's shaders, but the individual files are skipped because of the Python exception.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS
- Game: Fast Fusion
- Build target: mac-app
- Source: `seedds/nxnative`
- Affected file: `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`

## Findings

The current `shader_split.py` contains references to both `FZLC` and `RDHS`, but neither constant is defined.

The references are located around:

```python
if head[:4] == FZLC:
    found += fzlc_shaders(path, '/' + rel)
```

And:

```python
if tail == RDHS:
    found += rdhs_shaders(path, '/' + rel)
```

The expected definitions are:

```python
FZLC = b'FZLC'
RDHS = b'RDHS'
```

These constants are missing from the current source file.

## Previous workaround

I previously encountered this exact problem and locally corrected it by adding:

```python
FZLC = b'FZLC'
RDHS = b'RDHS'
```

to the constants section of `shader_split.py`.

That allowed the shader scanning stage to proceed past the missing-constant errors.

However, after attempting another build, the same `FZLC` error returned. The definitions are once again missing from the source file.

## Expected behavior

The shader scanner should define all format signatures used by its file-d

## Input

`The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time [0400486024dec000][v131072].nup` — 25,622,267,860 bytes (matches the profile README's "25.6 GB").

## Repro

```
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<nup>" --platform mac-app -o "<out>.app" --work-dir <work>
```

Fails at step `[3/6] shader split` — on **both** revisions below, with byte-identical output:

- `b989137` — the commit that added this profile (checked out detached)
- `e689cb7` — main at the time of writing

## Error

```
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 0400486024DEC000's:
shader_map.tsv: 3,023 row(s) only in the profile, 3,022 only in the split
  profile: vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	ce0eba6c3584814d	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc
  split:   vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	4c35081101443a7f	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b85a8
```

## Analysis

- The profile's tables were added wholesale in `b989137` (114,669 insertions, new directory).
- Checking out exactly `b989137` and splitting the same NUP reproduces the same 3,023/3,022 mismatch, so later split changes (c931e58/9f834e4/760c7fe) are not the cause.
- NUP version (v131072) and size (25.6 GB) match the profile README.
- This suggests the committed tables were generated with a tree (or game dump) that differs from what was committed — i.e. anyone following the README with a correct dump should hit this.

body: ### What happened Playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, 0400486024DEC000, update v131072), built as a Mac app. M2 Max MacBook Pro, 96 GB, macOS 26.7.3, 2560x1440 on a 144 Hz display. bf1e4edd renders this game correctly at a locked 60 fps and has never faulted across a week of play. On 72e81a32 it drew magenta light leaks over whole scenes and occasional white-outs. On current main (d2fd78b4) the picture is worse and the GPU dies. What it looks like: geometry, textures, character models and the HUD all draw correctly, and over the top of them sit uniform, grid-aligned squares of fully saturated colour (green, yellow, white, red, cyan), plus a magenta wash pooling around every light source. The squares being identical in size and grid-aligned suggests a tiled lighting or bloom accumulation pass. Performance looks normal while this happens: 52 fps, GPU 17.4 ms, no pipeline stalls in the log. Screenshot attached. After a few minutes the GPU faults. macOS filed seven gpuEvent reports for dmhost at 20:06:45, then WindowServer died at 20:07:34 with a userspace watchdog timeout, which restarts the login session. An earlier run faulted the same way at 19:10. It happened both times I launched, within about five minutes each. The gpuEvent reports say: "restart_reason_desc" : "BIF0 page fault" "bif0_fault" : { "is_read" : true, "level" : 2, "requestor" : 174, "address" : 681160867840 } "guilty_dm" : 1 "command_buffer_trace_id" : 81198719934 So the GPU read an unmapped address (0x9E985A0000) and the driver restarted it. That would also account for the corruption: a read of unmapped memory returns whatever is there, and garbage landing in a light accumulation buffer looks exactly like those blocks. Guessing at a culprit, two commits in this range touch residency, which is what keeps memory mapped while the GPU is still reading it: c4f12d24 (nvn/residency: retire upload staging off Metal feedback) and bbacc45c (nvn/residency: retain placed texture parents). Ruled out: mods (reproduced with DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY removed from env.txt entirely; the same 24 overlays are fine on bf1e4edd), stale build artifacts (the build log shows the shader cache invalidated by hash and all 42,847 recompiled from scratch, the pipeline archive rebuilt, the rewrite step rerun), and local changes (the only one is an unrelated getenv for stick gain in dm/host/pad_hid.h). Attached: gpu-reports.zip with all eight gpuEvent reports and the WindowServer crash, plus the output of scripts/bug_report.py. ### What you expected The game renders as it does on bf1e4edd, and macOS does not panic. ### Game, title ID and version The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, update v131072 ### nxnative commit d2fd78b4 ### Shader chain version df1800562702 ### How it was built and run Mac app (--platform mac-app) ### Device and OS MacBook Pro, M2 Max, 96 GB. macOS 26.7.3. 2560x1440 on a 144 Hz display. ### Settings and environment overrides env.txt during the failing runs contained only: DM_HID_MAP=A=2,B=1,X=4,Y=3,L=5,R=6,ZL=7,ZR=8,MINUS=9,PLUS=10,LS=11,RS=12 DM_HID_GAIN=1.8 DM_HID_DEAD=0.2 DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY was removed entirely for the no-mods test, and the corruption and panic happened anyway. Normally that line carries 24 overlay paths, all of which work correctly on bf1e4edd. No settings were changed in the app between the working bf1e4edd build and the failing one. Render scale and upscaler are at their defaults. ### Logs [gpu-reports.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35191980/gpu-reports.zip) [nxnative-report-0400486024DEC000-2026-11-20.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35192057/nxnative-report-0400486024DEC000-2026-11-20.zip) ### No game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

## Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072): white screen at the Temple of Time → Chamber of Sages transition on iPhone; the 4 GB alias region runs out

**Symptom:** after the Master Sword, as Ganondorf walks into the light, the screen stays one flat color (229,229,229 across the whole picture) while the game keeps running at full speed (`frame step … 1.000 of real time`, a constant 68 draws a frame). No `[RED]` or `CRASH` line. The `[mem]` high-water mark stops at **+3.75 GB of the 4.00 GB** alias region (`mem_alias 0x100000000`).

**Reproduced on the Mac** with `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0x100000000`: the same flat screen, the same +3.75 GB.

| Alias region | Result | High mark |
|---|---|---|
| 4 GB (the profile's) | white screen, Mac and iPhone 18 Pro | +3.75 GB |
| 64 GB (the Mac's default) | passes | +5.51 GB at the scene |
| 8 GB | passes, Mac and iPhone 18 Pro | +7.76 GB, 2.50 GB mapped |

**Fix tested:** `mem_reserve 0x420000000`, `mem_alias 0x200000000` (heap unchanged at 8 GB). Branch: `dag294-alt/nxnative`, `oot-alias-8gb` (`b1144e08`, on `bee218d9`).

On an iPhone 18 Pro (iOS 27.2.1, built with `--prepare-xcode`, free Apple ID), iOS accepts the 16.5 GB block (17 sparse guest files). Through the transition into the Chamber of Sages and about 27 minutes of play: `0.999 of real time`, 0 dropped frames in the last window, thermal 2, footprint 4.86 GB, headroom to the memory limit 3.3 GB.

**Notes:**
- The high mark rises with churn (2.50 GB mapped against +7.76 GB), as in "An alias high-water mark near the top is not exhaustion". The 4 GB failure looks like a request no hole fit at this transition. 8 GB passes this scene and about 27 minutes after it; I have not shown it is enough for the whole game, and you may prefer another size or fix.
- The profile's values are the same in every version through `130ef293`. The README says they came "as Donkey Kong Bananza" and that the game was "Mac only so far".
- SDK 22.2.8: the node-area cut applies (`AddressRegionManager node area 1 GB → 62 MB`, implementation 7 of 9). The 2 MB alignment rule matches nothing, which I take to be expected for SDK 20 and later.
- On the iPhone, one `[RED] queue 6: an event wait has held it 8.0 s` near frame 8,100, right after a 296 MB 12288x12288 texture and about 1 GB of upload staging swaps, likely the transition's load. It resolved and play went on. It is not in the 4 GB runs, which never got that far.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: the slot-7 texture type mismatches for `9b310b3349825e9a` and `09ab31c69af710c9`.

**Build:** `bee218d9`, shader chain `66eab9c9a6b4`.

**Logs:** https://gist.github.com/dag294-alt/b936c70c3a4db94e2140b7a5883807e8
- `oot-mac-bee218d9-4GB-white.log`: Mac, `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0x100000000`, white screen
- `oot-white-screen.txt`: iPhone 18 Pro, the profile's 4 GB, white screen
- `oot-8gb-pass.txt`: iPhone 18 Pro, 8 GB, through the transition

Every launch, in-game (village outskirts / forest path after New Game), most nearby surfaces show only their smallest mip levels: large blocky "mosaic" patches on ground and walls, rocks and debris that look faceted (no normal-map detail), Leon's model as a dark blurred shape. pool stand-ins up to frame 6438: 5060 made (2461 of them a level cut down, 4418 in a sparse pool; 10 of a sparse pool not made: a page unmapped), 1360 gave way to their texture, 2899 held now ... the dummy 10 times

body:
**Correction (2026-11-20):** an earlier version of this issue called this a loop that left the writing thread stuck. It isn't. Frames keep coming in every affected run, and each write completes. The detector's "loop" was repeated single faults on the same page. This is fault churn, not a livelock.

### What happens

`nvn_dirty` write-protects pool pages after it uploads textures from them, and re-protects a page after each re-upload. In Ocarina of Time, six game worker threads clear the same object (pc `sdk+0x168f6c`, lr `sdk+0x164824`, in the game's texture-compaction path) about every 100 ms. The 16 KB host page is re-protected between those writes, so every write faults once. `nvn_dirty` then unprotects the page and marks it written. Each write gets through, but the page cycles between protected and writable continuously.

Counts, from runs of about 14 minutes on a Kokiri Forest route:
- write faults: about 270,000;
- frames ≥ 45 ms: 23.3 a minute.

Both are with the pager and guest files off. Castle Town shows the same pattern at lower counts.

It happens with any guest-memory mode (pager on or off, guest files on or off). Seen on a host built from main 0def324d (2026-11-15) plus test carries.

### What you expected

A page that a game thread keeps writing isn't re-protected after every upload, so the writes don't each take a fault.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072

### Device and OS

MacBook Air M2, 16 GB, macOS 27.0

### A fix being tested

"Write-pending" pages: a page unprotected for a write stays writable, and every reader treats it as changed, until a whole frame passes since that write. Then it is protected again with a fresh generation. No millisecond constants.

First results, one run each:
- write faults ×0.22 (Kokiri 270k → 61k, Castle Town 19.6k → 4.7k);
- re-uploads 0 → 7;
- pacing at Kokiri unchanged (23.3 → 22.3 frames ≥ 45 ms a minute).

So it's an efficiency change, not a correctness fix. More runs, with guest files on, are in progress.

Also on `on_fault`: it no longer claims a fault on a page its state calls unprotected while the kernel still has it read-only.
title: nvn_dirty: a page written every ~100 ms by several threads is re-protected after each upload, so every write faults (Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000)

### What happened

Building The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening v131072 (1.1.0) from base XCI + update NSP with the NX Play front end (`--platform mac-app`) fails every time at the shader split, the same gate class as #3027:

```
  split:   ps_main.bin	0	pixel	f98d9cbfcb3cacb3	main#BNSH@0x1c36000#var0
Either these game files are not the versions the profile registers, or shader_split.py now reads them differently and the profile's tables were not split again
```

The game files are exactly the versions the profile registers (update 1.1.0 / v131072, no DLC), so this is the splitter-output-changed case of docs/reference/packing.md. The committed `shader_map.tsv` was last touched by `8950f2ea` (Nov 16); since then the duplicate/representative selection and shader reader changes (incl. `5df3dbe8`, PR #2943) landed, and #3010 (`c075ab2`, the fix for #3027, already in this checkout) refreshed only Ocarina of Time's map. Link's Awakening is not among the refreshed profiles listed in docs/reference/packing.md.

I can reproduce identically from the terminal; the GUI hides the gate message, so the build shows only "build failed".

### What you expected

The split matches the profile's registered tables and the build proceeds to the shader build, as it did when the profile was last split.

The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening, 01006BB00C6F0000, 1.1.0 (v131072), no DLC

**Cause:** the same as Ocarina of Time in #3034 / c075ab26. The BAHS record-slot reader from 5df3dbe8 (PR #2943) drops two candidates outside their file's record entry slots, which Raiders' profile still lists:

| package | index | stage | key | source |
