| `vs_other.bin` | 81 | vertex | `22fff9012db5acaa` | `/Lib/agl/agl_resource.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.debug.sarc.zs/agl_common.sharcb#BAHS@0x27ea4` |
| `vs_other.bin` | 402 | vertex | `16d1e80284e796bd` | `/Lib/agl/agl_resource.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.debug.sarc.zs/agl_technique_pfx.sharcb#BAHS@0x10eda4` |

5df3dbe8 refreshed Mario Kart World's and Donkey Kong Bananza's tables but not Raiders'. (`22fff9012db5acaa` is the shader from the "Optional stage byte in short NVN2 control sections" entry in `docs/reference/shaders.md`, #2916.)

**Checked against the split of my game files**
- The split: 27,190 shaders, no red lines. `shader_pairs.tsv`, `shader_facts.tsv` and `pso_pairs.tsv` are byte-identical to the profile's
- `shader_map.tsv`: the profile's rows minus those two, with the later `vs_other.bin` indices decremented, equal the split's data rows exactly (27,190 rows). Profile indices were contiguous; no other Raiders table references either key
- Attached: that refreshed `shader_map.tsv` (the profile's comment lines kept)

**Result with the refreshed map:** the build completes (shader build, pipeline archive, signed Mac app), and about 28 minutes of play ran with 0 `[RED]` lines and 0 `is not in the shader map` lines, so neither key was asked for. Mostly 59-60 fps; no GPU fault (#1289); clean exit.

**Suggested change:** refresh `dm/games/0400380020056000/shader_map.tsv` as c075ab26 did for Ocarina of Time, and add Raiders to the "Payload outside the control section" entry in `docs/reference/shaders.md`.

**Not checked:** an iPhone or iPad build, other Raiders versions.

body:
### What happened

Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072) at 120 fps, Castle Town market, 1080p, `DM_FPS_TARGET=120`, headless: in 5 of 10 runs the frame step went to hold 2 in the route's first seconds and stayed there for most of the route (29.4–54.6 % of frames at 120) while the GPU sat at 640–810 MHz and 4.5–5.9 W. In the runs that get out, the same stretch runs at hold 1 at 1250–1420 MHz.

### Why (measured, logs with `DM_LOAD_LOG=1`)

1. **The load.** In 35 of 35 runs one or two probes back to hold 1 fail between presents 2364 and 2859, the first seconds of the route: frame cost 1.10–1.37 ticks, GPU 0.94–1.14 ticks at hold 1 after the grace. Those probes are right to fail. The GPU work of a frame there (GPU ms × MHz) is 12–17 Mcycles; after the load the market costs 9–10.
2. **The reading at hold 2 does not follow the load.** At hold 2 macOS sets the GPU clock so the GPU is about 78 % busy: 700–880 MHz and 74–80 % busy in every run. The market reads 12.8 ms a frame there and the fountain 13.0 ms, while their GPU work differs by 25 % (9.1–9.8 against 11.5–11.7 Mcycles; n=4 stays of 23–33 s). So the GPU time at hold 2 is about 1.55 ticks whatever the scene costs.
3. **The ratio never expires.** `nvn_fgpu_learn` keeps the largest ratio the failed probes gave, and with `FSTEP_GPU_FAILS` (2) of them `nvn_fgpu_slow` asks whether `cur` over the ratio fits kmin. Learned in the load, the ratio (about 1.2) set against a reading pinned near 1.55 never lets a probe start again. In one run (n=1) with nothing else holding the run, the ratio alone kept hold 2 for 22 s after a hitch: 1.49 / 1.22 = 1.22 ticks against the 1 that fits, at 760 MHz.

Main's rules alone do the same in a simulation with t_fstep's harness (main `8a06d2550`, `nvn_fstep.h` unchanged since `c22f30a3f`): GPU 0.83 at hold 1, a load where hold 1 costs 1.25, 1.55 at hold 2 during and after it. Two probes fail in the load, the ratio is 1.24 (n 2), and in the 4,900 frames after the load no probe starts. With the hold-2 reading falling to 1.15 after the load, one probe starts and holds.

### What fixed it here

On our build the frame step gets the GPU work of a frame once a second at the longer hold (GPU ms per frame × the IOReport "GPU Stats" clock), keeps the largest work a probe failed from, and drops the failed probes' ratios for that kmin when the 3-second mean falls 15 % under it. With no clock reading nothing changes. Market at 120, n=10 each, same build otherwise:

| | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| runs trapped at hold 2 (under 60 % held) | 5 of 10 (7 of 19 with older runs) | 0 of 10 |
| longest stay at hold 2 | up to 31.4 s | 6.1–10.1 s |
| ratio dropped | – | 10 of 10, presents 2785–2850, 10.7–11.3 against 12.9–13.7 Mcycles |

At 60 fps nothing changed (98.3, 98.2, 98.2 % against 98.2, 98.2, 98.2 %, n=3). The fountain at 120 stays mostly at hold 2, where it belongs: at hold 1 it needs the top clock (1609–1620 MHz, 86 % busy) and still misses.

Ageing the ratio by time instead breaks 12 of t_fstep's cases (Kokiri Forest, Hyrule Field: a scene that really does not fit hold 1 gets probed again and again). GPU time alone cannot tell that scene from this one; GPU work can.

### Question

Main has no GPU clock reading on the host. Would you take one (IOReport "GPU Stats", read once a second, Mac only) for the frame step, or do you prefer another signal for "the load the probes failed in has ended"? With your answer I can open a PR with this rule on main and its t_fstep cases (the trap clears when the work falls, stays without a clock, stays when the work does not fall).

### Setup

Tested on a MacBook Pro (Mac17,7), Apple M5 Max (18-core CPU, 32-core GPU), 36 GB, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131), Xcode 27.2, headless, built on `c22f30a3f` with our Ocarina of Time 120 fps patches (not on main). Our build also has a second gate of its own that learns from failed probes in GPU time and traps the same way; it held 4 of the 5 trapped runs, and the n=1 run above is the one where main's ratio alone held. Ocarina of Time build fails due to stale shader_map.tsv entry

Summary

Building The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000) failed because the shader table generated by the current shader splitter did not match the existing game profile's shader_map.tsv.

The difference was caused by one stale vertex shader entry in the profile. The current splitter rejects that entry, resulting in subsequent vertex shader indices being shifted by one.

Original build error

split shader tables differ from game profile 0400486024DEC000's:
shader_map.tsv: 3,023 row(s) only in the profile, 3,022 only in the split

Profile-only:
vs_shader.bin  28 vertex ce0eba6c3584814d
/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc

Fresh split:
vs_shader.bin  28 vertex 4c35081101443a7f
/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b85a8

Investigation

Comparing the existing profile tables against the freshly generated tables showed:

Table | Profile rows | Fresh split rows | Result -- | -- | -- | -- shader_map.tsv | 42,849 | 42,848 | Different shader_facts.tsv | 4,125 | 4,125 | Identical shader_pairs.tsv | 28,178 | 28,178 | Identical pso_pairs.tsv | 6,471 | 6,471 | Identical

The profile contained an additional vertex shader entry:

vs_shader.bin 28 vertex ce0eba6c3584814d
...AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc

This entry was absent from the fresh split.

The next valid vertex shader was present in both tables, but its index differed:

Profile:    vertex 29  4c35081101443a7f  @0x1b85a8
Fresh split: vertex 28  4c35081101443a7f  @0x1b85a8

Subsequent vertex shader indices were similarly shifted by one. The other shader types and the remaining tables matched.

Suspected cause

This appears consistent with the BAHS descriptor validation change introduced by commit 5df3dbe8 (packing/shaders: reject stray BAHS descriptors (PR #2943)).

The existing Ocarina profile appears to retain a BAHS descriptor that the updated splitter correctly rejects as a stray descriptor.

Workaround

I backed up the original profile table and replaced only:

dm/games/0400486024DEC000/shader_map.tsv

with the freshly generated shader_map.tsv.

The replacement was verified using cmp and SHA256:

0e79b9ecba5cba530cffc07cf70aff6bfb72e2a1b7a4b8c98ba06f6921670970

The other three profile tables were left unchanged.

Expected behavior

The build should either:

  1. Recognize and automatically refresh stale generated shader tables when the splitter's output changes, or

  2. Clearly identify that the profile's generated tables need to be regenerated and provide a supported refresh procedure.

Ideally, existing registered game profiles should not require manual table replacement after a legitimate shader splitter correction.

Environment

  • Game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

  • Title ID: 0400486024DEC000

  • Platform: macOS

  • Repository: seedds/nxnative

  • Relevant splitter change: 5df3dbe8

Note: The workaround corrected the table mismatch. A subsequent full build has not yet been confirmed, so this report does not claim that all build issues are resolved.
title: Ocarina of Time build fails due to stale shader_map.tsv entry

body:
**Setup**
- MacBook Pro, Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131)
- NX2Apple 1.4.0 (`/Applications/NX2Apple.app`), engine `ccd834e06a3938834bb5579e2ccc6a0ad13d3970`, shader chain `e047be1b6829` (the log says "commit not recorded")
- Built as a Mac app from the base game NSP, `--platform mac-app`
- Launcher choices: `DM_LANG=pt`, `DM_FULLSCREEN=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`. Everything else default (`DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE` off, bilinear). Pipeline prewarm finished: 18290 shaders, 11034 render pipelines, 0 skipped.
- Played by hand with a controller, 1 player, Grand Prix, Propeller Cup (Copa Hélice), track "Céus Gelados" (game language is Portuguese), lap 1/3, Funky Kong.

**What I see**
On this track, whose sky is a blue gradient with big pink/peach clouds, parts of the sky are drawn as hard, stair-stepped blocks instead of a smooth gradient:
- a peach/orange vertical band in the sky with a staircase edge on its right side and a vertical bar next to it;
- the large pink-white cloud on the right has a jagged, pixelated outline (steps of roughly 15-30 px on a 1000 px wide frame, so about 1.5-3% of the screen width each);
- a few loose peach bars floating on their own in the blue.

These shapes **flicker from frame to frame** (they are not static). The rest of the scene is correct: kart, track, items, HUD and the objects at the horizon are all smooth. Later in the lap (inside the ice-cream parlour building, and further on) the sky looks fine again, so it is limited to part of the lap.

Screenshot attached (red arrows point at the stepped band and the jagged edge). I also have a 20 s screen recording; I can attach it or cut a shorter clip if useful.

**Expected**
A smooth gradient sky with soft cloud edges, like on the Switch.

**Frame rate / stability**
Not related to speed: frame p50 about 16.6 ms, GPU about 8.7 ms at frame 3900, 0 dropped on-screen frames in the periodic report. No crash.

**What the log says**
Full log: `0100152000022000.log` (6239 lines, about 105,900 frames) and `0100152000022000.prev.log`. There is no `[RED]` line about shaders or pipelines, and no pipeline compile during the race. The only one-time renderer notices that look relevant, all printed early and identical in the previous session's log:

```
[nvn-mtl] new-texture zeroing: pixel format 134 not cleared (compressed / unsupported)
[nvn-mtl] render target in a compressed texture: view format 0x2f drawn into a 32x32-block shadow (Metal format 123) and copied back after the pass (first case pass 201)
[nvn-mtl] same-pass feedback sampling: shader 72f0bae5b9472e9a_b renders level 1 of a view of levels 0+5; it samples a view of the levels below (mip-chain pass)
[nvn-mtl] cube binding fallback: texture ID 6221 has a 2D descriptor; zero cube bound (the shader may leave this input unused)    (frame ~3900; texture ID 5264 in the previous session)
[nvn-mtl] [RED] texture ID 1112 not registered     (frame 4, once)
```

**My guess (not confirmed)**
I cannot tie any of these lines to the exact moment of the glitch, because the log has no per-frame timestamps for them. My suspicion is the "render target in a compressed texture" path: the game renders into a block-compressed texture, the emulator draws into a 32x32-block shadow texture and copies it back, and a sky/cloud layer could end up sampled at block resolution, which would give exactly this staircase look. The flicker would then be the shadow copy-back racing with, or lagging behind, the pass that samples it. The cube-map fallback (zero cube bound) is a second candidate, but it is logged around frame 3900, which looks like the menu/load, so I think it is less likely.

Art of Rally (#679) reports the same "render into a compressed-format render target" situation, so it may be the same root cause.

**What I can do next**
Tell me which of these you would like and I will run it and attach the output:
- `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP` / `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` / `DM_NVN_SHOT` for a lap, to see which pass produces the sky;
- a run with `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0` to rule out the present snapshot ring;
- a run with a different value for `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE`.

Related: #1186 (Mario Kart World, "one sky artifact", also a sky/cloud problem with blinking clouds).
title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (0100152000022000) on MacBook Pro M3 Pro: "Céus Gelados" (Propeller Cup) sky shows stair-stepped blocks that flicker

## macOS build fails in `nvn_mtl.m` due to missing screenshot and display-link latch implementation

### Description

Building Fast Fusion for macOS using NxNative currently fails during Objective-C compilation of:

`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`

The shader-processing stages complete, and the build reaches the macOS host compilation stage. Compilation then stops with **13 errors** in `nvn_mtl.m`.

The errors appear to involve two separate areas of the Metal presentation implementation:

1. Screenshot capture references a missing `present_shot` function and an undeclared `ev_val` variable.
2. The display-link callback contains references to latch-related variables and state that are not declared or initialized in the current implementation.

### Build environment

- Platform: macOS native app
- Game: Fast Fusion
- Source repository: `seedds/nxnative`
- File failing to compile: `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`
- Compiler: Apple Clang via Xcode
- Build target: `mac-app`

### Compiler errors

**1. Screenshot capture — lines 18897 and 18899**

```text
error: call to undeclared function 'present_shot'
error: use of undeclared identifier 'ev_val'
```

Both screenshot-capture paths call:

```objc
present_shot(src, path, crop, ev_val, &shot_ready);
```

However, `present_shot` is not declared or defined where these calls are compiled, and `ev_val` is not available in that scope.

This affects both the configured screenshot-frame capture and the queued screenshot capture.

**2. Display-link hold tolerance — line 19080**

```text
error: use of undeclared identifier 'tol'
```

The callback uses:

```objc
update.targetPresentationTimestamp < g_link_hold_until - tol
```

but `tol` is not declared in the current callback scope.

**3. Display-link latch state — lines 19103–19104**

```text
error: use of undeclared identifier 'latch'
error: use of undeclared identifier 'wk_cb'
error: use of undeclared identifier 'wk_room'
```

The callback contains:

```objc
const int k = !latch || hold_ticks >= 2 ? -1 :
    it.t_in >= wk_cb[0] ? 0 :
    it.t_in >= wk_cb[1] ? 1 : -1;

link_drain_note(
    cb,
    cb - it.t_in,
    ticket > first,
    k < 0 || wk_cb[k] < 0 ? -1 : it.t_in - wk_cb[k],
    k < 0 ? 0 : wk_room[k]
);
```

The variables `latch`, `wk_cb`, and `wk_room` are not declared or initialized in the current callback implementation.

The `link_drain_note()` function already accepts the five arguments shown above, and `link_latch_on()` is present in the file. This suggests that portions of the display-link latch implementation are present, but the corresponding callback state and logic may be missing or incomplete.

### Additional context

The display-link callback currently contains newer presentation logic, including:

- `hold_ticks` calculation based on the frame period.
- Ocarina of Time fast-forward handling through `fg_take_or_hold()`.
- External producer synchronization through `ext_wait()`.
- Snapshot and submission commit waits.

These existing behaviors should be preserved when correcting the callback.

The latch-related code appears to be associated with the earlier display-link latch implementation introduced in commit `60284e79`:

`gfx/nvn: the display-link callback latches the present of the acquire it woke (#2648, PR #2757)`

That implementation included callback wake tracking, latch state, the `wk_cb` and `wk_room` timing arrays, and coordination between the display-link callback and `mtl_link_wait_ticks()`.

The current file appears to contain only portions of that implementation. Simply declaring the missing variables may not be sufficient; the corresponding synchronization and latch behavior may also need to be restored or adapted to the newer presentation code.

### Requested fix

Please review and correct the affected portions of `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`:

1. Restore or update the screenshot-capture implementation so that `present_shot` and its event/synchronization argument are correctly defined and available.
2. Restore or correctly define the display-link hold tolerance.
3. Restore or adapt the complete display-link latch callback state and wake-tracking logic, including `latch`, `wk_cb`, and `wk_room`.
4. Verify that the latch implementation remains compatible with the newer `hold_ticks` and Ocarina of Time fast-forward logic.
5. Confirm that the macOS Metal backend compiles successfully after the changes.

### Build result

The latest build stops at:

```text
make: *** [gen/040041E0212AE000/obj/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m.o] Error 1
```

The compiler reports:

```text
68 warnings and 13 errors generated.
```

The 13 errors listed above are the current compilation blockers. The warnings are primarily Metal command-encoder type compatibility warnings and deprecated PVRTC usage; they are not the errors stopping this build.

### Attachments

- `mac_host_build.log` — complete compiler output from the failed macOS build.

[mac_host_build.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35127904/mac_host_build.log)
title: macOS build fails in nvn_mtl.m due to missing screenshot and display-link latch implementation

## Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, NUP v131072) build fails at shader split on main: the rewritten BAHS reader finds the AglShader BAHS program at a different offset, tables differ from the profile

### Build

- nxnative `main` @ `130ef293` (cloned fresh via nx-native-wrapper `bin/setup`), macOS 27.2.1, M1 Max.
- Game: retail NUP `0400486024DEC000` update v131072 (the same container that built fine on Nov 17 at `8d62601f`).
- `nxplay --rebuild --mac-app`.

### What happens

Step 3/6 shader split stops the build:

```
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 0400486024DEC000's:
shader_map.tsv: 3,023 row(s) only in the profile, 3,022 only in the split
  profile: vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	ce0eba6c3584814d	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc
  split:   vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	4c35081101443a7f	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b85a8
```

Everything else matches (3,022/3,023 rows identical except this one program).

### Reading

`dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` was rewritten in this window (+477/−74, PR #2861's RAGE WAD reader and the validated binary-array helper `bahs_binary_records`). The AglShader.sharcb BAHS program that used to be found at `0x1b41cc` is now found at `0x1b85a8` (different bytes → different hash). Either the new validated reader picks the wrong candidate for this sarc, or it is more correct and the OOT profile's committed tables just need a re-split with the new reader. The profile folder (`dm/games/0400486024DEC000/`) has no changes in this window, so its tables predate the reader rewrite.

The previous build (`8d62601f`, Nov 17) split and built this exact NUP fine.

### Ask

Regenerate the profile tables with the new reader (if `0x1b85a8` is the correct program) or fix the candidate selection for AglShader.sarc — and either way, a note whether existing OOT builds on disk keep playing while the split is broken (mine does — the Nov 17 app still runs).

body: ### What happened All UI text (menus, subtitles, objectives, button hints) misses parts of its letters: thin strokes are dropped here and there. It shows at the game's native 1280x720 as well as scaled to fullscreen. ### Cause The text fragment shader `bfd75fb65cc56ac0` samples the glyph atlas (1024x1024, swizzle RRRR) through a combined handle with sampler ID 0. The game never registers sampler 0 (`[RED] sampler ID 0 not registered`). `nvn_mtl.m` treats ID 0 as no sampler and binds `dummy_samp()`, whose `MTLSamplerDescriptor` defaults to nearest filtering, so texels of the atlas are skipped. On the console the GPU reads sampler pool entry 0, and the text is smooth there. ### Confirmation Setting `minFilter` and `magFilter` to `MTLSamplerMinMagFilterLinear` in `dummy_samp()` makes every glyph render complete. ### Fix Bind for sampler ID 0 what the console's pool entry 0 holds. Linear min/mag filtering gives the correct result for this game; whether it is right for every game depends on what the NVN driver writes at entry 0, which I could not check. ### Screenshots Before: After, with a linear dummy sampler: ### Game, title ID and version The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition, 01003D100E9C6000, 4.04d (v589824), no DLC; provisional profile ### nxnative commit cd0cf744 ### Shader chain version 4922414e9fdc ### How it was built and run Mac app (--platform mac-app) ### Device and OS MacBook Pro 14-inch M2 Pro (Mac14,9), macOS 27.2.1 ### Settings and environment overrides `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_BARRIER=full` (for the separate exposure issue, #3048)

body: ### What happened Every sunlit surface clips to white; shaded areas look right. The in-game gamma setting does not help. It happens on every run. ### Cause The eye adaptation runs three compute dispatches in one encoder: - `3ef5601ed7a5dc03` clears a 1024-byte storage buffer (a 256-bin luminance histogram) - `c03b77306aeca1c0` fills it from the 640x360 luminance target - `f71bce7ec8fe07b7` reduces it to the 1x1 RGBA32F average luminance The game sets no barrier between the clear and the fill (only one, bits `0x21`, before the reduce). With `MTLDispatchTypeConcurrent` the two run together, the histogram loses counts, and the reduce writes NaN. The adaptation pass (`3e0d60078cb88e46`: prev + (cur - prev) * speed) then keeps NaN in every following frame. The exposure pass (`8b80c7a2c2d6d5ea`) clamps the luminance with max/min, which returns the lower bound for NaN, so the exposure stays at its maximum. ### Confirmation - The 1x1 average and adapted luminance targets read NaN on most frames. - With `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_BARRIER=full` they hold finite values (about 1.4-1.6), the scene renders correctly, and the frame rate is unchanged (60 fps). ### Fix Order a dispatch after an earlier one in the same encoder when their storage-buffer ranges overlap (write after write, read after write), even without a game barrier. Workaround until then: `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_BARRIER=full` in the game's `env.txt`. The same five shader keys are in the registered profile `0100A0800E9C4000` (4.04b), so it is probably affected too (not tested). The same game also has a separate UI text issue: #3049. ### Screenshots Before: After, with `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_BARRIER=full`: ### Game, title ID and version The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition, 01003D100E9C6000, 4.04d (v589824), no DLC; provisional profile ### nxnative commit cd0cf744 ### Shader chain version 4922414e9fdc ### How it was built and run Mac app (--platform mac-app) ### Device and OS MacBook Pro 14-inch M2 Pro (Mac14,9), macOS 27.2.1 ### Settings and environment overrides none

body:
The profile registers only **1.4.0 (v393216)**, so building from a dump whose newest update is **1.5.1 (v524288)** derives a profile — and the derived profile loses the one cut this game needs to get past its first dispatch. The result is a **blank window on both Mac and iPad**: the app opens, audio runs, the game never draws.

### The warning

    v524288 is not a version game profile 010038B015560000 registers (v393216 1.4.0):
      packing v524288 from a profile derived from it
    [RED] main: no function patch carries the registered builds' fixes to this build
          (1.4.0 (3cfd4578…) has 2 cuts), and the game may stop where they were needed

The missing cut is the profile's **job-pool lost wake-up**; its own note says the signal went to a worker that never ran and the game hung forever on a boot dispatch in 4 of 6 Mac runs, so a blank window is the expected failure when it is absent.

### The cuts are the same on 1.5.1, at the same offsets

`main` of v524288 is build `ace351a145c07a51f8e239666640a0d8`. Searching its text for `ldr x0,[x0]` + `b` + `ldr x0,[x0]` + `b` where both branches target one address gives **exactly one site: 0x1254c**, branching to `0x655b20` (`SignalEvent`) — the same offset as 1.4.0's, with only the branch encoding differing:

    (0x12554, '000040f9', '000400f9')  ldr x0,[x0] → str x0,[x0,#8]     (identical to 1.4.0's cut)
    (0x12558, '720d1914', 'fdffff17')  b SignalEvent → b 0x1254c          (1.4.0 had '36fc1814' here)

### With those two cuts in `CUTS`

- `rewrite_main.log`: `cuts 2`, and the "no function patch carries the fixes" warning is gone;
- **Mac: 60 fps** (p50 16.70 ms, p95 16.99), no red lines, and the frame capture writes again (the unpatched build logged the screenshot request but never produced a file);
- **iPad mini: 60 fps** (p50 16.70, p95 17.59), no red lines.

### Ask

Could 1.5.1's build be registered in `dm/games/010038B015560000/patches.py` (the two CUTS entries above, keyed by `ace351a145c07a51f8e239666640a0d8`)? Alternatively a `MATCH_CUTS` rule would cover future updates — the profile's `BINDING` row says this patch is `now: build`, `goal: game`, and the site is easy to recognise.

I'm running it from a local `DM_GAMES_DIR` overlay meanwhile (upstream profile + that one entry). Related: #2275 is the CRI Mana movie streaking on this same version — that one still stands; this is only the boot hang.

Dump: `v-final_fantasy_tactics_the_ivalice_chronicles.nsp` (base) + `…_v524288.nsp` (1.5.1), no 1.4.0 update available here.
title: FINAL FANTASY TACTICS (010038B015560000, 1.5.1 v524288): derived profile loses the job-pool wake-up cut — blank window on Mac and iPad, and the two cuts for 1.5.1's main

### What happens, and when

Hogwarts Legacy (v1.0.5) is finally booting and playable in-game. Overall performance and texture streaming are very smooth—a noticeable improvement over the latest Astris build.

However, I encountered two new in-game issues:

Low-Fidelity Voice / Dialogue Audio:
Background music, sound effects (SFX), and ambient audio all play normally.

Only spoken dialogue/voice lines sound very low-fidelity, quiet, and heavily compressed/muffled (similar to old 32-bit console audio).

Particle Effects Glitch:
General graphics and textures load smoothly without issues.

However, particle effects exhibit severe visual glitches. Specifically, right after casting the Revelio spell, intense flickering/flashing lights appear across the screen, making it very harsh on the eyes. (Note: This same particle flicker also occurs on Astris, likely related to how the game handles certain Unreal Engine effects).

I have attached a short screen recording demonstrating both the voice audio quality and the Revelio flickering glitch. Thank you.

title: Hogwarts Legacy v1.0.5 - Low-fidelity voice audio & particle glitch

body:
The profile's `shader_map.tsv` no longer matches what `shader_split.py` produces, so the build stops in `prepare`. This is **not** a dump/version mismatch: the game data is exactly the build the profile registers. It looks like a table refresh is due after the GLSLC-reading changes.

### The failure

```
$ python scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<dump>" --work-dir <tree> --mac-app -o <app>
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 010069401ADB8000's:
shader_map.tsv: 1,366 row(s) only in the profile, 1,366 only in the split
  profile: ps_main.bin	0	pixel	0967121f0f0b1aaf	main#GLSLC@0x113e2d0
  split:   ps_main.bin	0	pixel	0335ab33d0ca2cc2	main#GLSLC@0x113ba58
Either these game files are not the versions the profile registers, or shader_split.py now reads them differently and the profile's tables were not split again
```

### The game files are the registered ones

`game.tsv` says `main=c841ffe2717ff03a13990480c51da73f`, and the dump's `extract/v262144/ExeFS/main` has exactly that module ID:

```
profile: build v262144 1.05 main=c841ffe2717ff03a13990480c51da73f sdk=12f161039300861f1054371f0e36b8c9
module:  moduleid c841ffe2717ff03a13990480c51da73f091c04fa000000000000000000000000
```

### What differs is only where the shaders are located

Comparing the profile's `shader_map.tsv` with the tables from the current split (both 1,726 data rows):

- **the hash sets are identical: 1,726 of 1,726 shaders are the same shader** (same decoded bytes);
- **1,366 rows differ**, by the per-file index and the source address:
  ```
  profile  ps_main.bin  0  ...  0967121f0f0b1aaf  main#GLSLC@0x113e2d0
  split    ps_main.bin  0  ...  0335ab33d0ca2cc2  main#GLSLC@0x113ba58
  profile  ps_main.bin  1  ...  2620d9bd8ee4561a  main#GLSLC@0x113f488
  split    ps_main.bin  1  ...  f11f275b5bb503e7  main#GLSLC@0x113cc08
  profile  ps_main.bin  2  ...  7dde4cf3d984fd24  main#GLSLC@0x11407c0
  split    ps_main.bin  2  ...  0967121f0f0b1aaf  main#GLSLC@0x113e2d0   (the profile's row 0 hash)
  ```
- 1,462 of the 1,726 rows keep an identical source string; 264 get a different one.

The same shader set at renumbered indexes and different `main#GLSLC@` offsets reads like the split now locates one-stage GLSLC outputs from a different reference point than when the table was written.

### When it started

I built this title successfully on **2026-11-11**. In between, the split's GLSLC reading changed, most directly:

- `0c83e685` (2026-11-13) packing/shader_split: read a one-stage GLSLC output by its section header first
- `bc36ee25` (2026-11-16) NVBC-wrapped CIVBSF records, `eb2e27f8`, `72047f1a`, plus the newer `9f834e41` / `c931e584` / `e0c30043` archive readers

### Workaround I'm using

A local overlay (`DM_GAMES_DIR` pointed at it) holding the upstream profile with the tables from **the current split** copied over it, `game.tsv`/`bf_want.tsv` untouched. With that, the build is clean:

What happened
During normal play the picture froze while a cutscene was playing and the game stopped responding to input. The audio kept running and the host's internal frame counter kept advancing, so this looks like a movie-output/presentation stall rather than a host crash or a frame-rate problem. I closed the app manually because the screen would not update; the launcher then logged the host exited with 0 (a clean, user-initiated quit — not a crash).
The freeze happened late in a long session, around in-game frame 178543 / t≈2979 s (about 50 minutes in), in a section where an AV1 video was being decoded for a cutscene.
What I found in the runtime log
Immediately before the frames bunched up, the AV1/VideoToolbox decoder started refusing packets:
[dm] [codec] AV1 decoder 1: 2560x1440, input format 3, output format 2 (VideoToolbox on the host)
[dm] [codec] image pool 2560x1440 format 2, tiling or mode 2, 1 picture(s): the host keeps the decoded pictures
[dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 0 pictures waiting for a released buffer and 12 packets to decode
[dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 0 pictures waiting for a released buffer and 12 packets to decode
[dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 0 pictures waiting for a released buffer and 12 packets to decode
[dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 0 pictures waiting for a released buffer and 12 packets to decode
[dm] [movie] AV1: VideoToolbox decoding 2560x1440, profile 0 level 12
[dm] [movie] nn::codec decoder 0x7a055e2400: first picture 2560x1440 into buffer 0
result 3603 / "a packet refused with 0 pictures waiting for a released buffer and 12 packets to decode" repeated 4 times. Right after that, whole frames stretched to 23–38 ms for a long run:
[dm] [longframe] frame 178543 (2979.37 s) whole frame 28.0 ms, submit+present 2.8 ms, GPU 6.1 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 178636 (2980.93 s) whole frame 31.8 ms, submit+present 1.0 ms, GPU 0.7 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 178761 (2983.02 s) whole frame 37.9 ms, submit+present 0.2 ms, GPU 0.7 ms
Across the session the movie threads stayed pinned even after the cutscene, one thread occupying most of a core:
[dm] [nvn] threads up to frame 186000: CPU by guest priority <=44 1131 ms/s; top:
  0x102e 'MovieVideoHandler'   priority 44  740 ms/s,
  0x1028 'MediaExtractorWorker' priority 44  223 ms/s,
  0x1025 'MovieEventHandler'   priority 34  141 ms/s
Other detail worth noting: the display path reported a standing-frame drain during the same stretch, while audio callbacks showed zero underruns and GPU submit time stayed ~0.2–0.7 ms — i.e. the GPU and audio were fine, the stall was on the movie/picture path:
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frames stood in the present queue while the game kept up, the acquire waited 1 more tick (16.7 ms) to let them out (drain #9, frame 178760)
[dm] audio #0 device callbacks 620000: 240–240 frames each, 4.0 blocks queued on average at callback; in these 2000, 0 underruns, 0.0 ms zero-padded
The overall frame statistics near the end still read 60 fps (frame time p50 16.67 ms), which is consistent with the guest frame loop advancing while the visible picture stayed stuck on a movie frame.
Possible relation to existing reports
Two reports look related, but neither is the same case, so I am opening a new one:
- #2407 ("Ocarina of Time ... an in-game AV1 cutscene stops after the first picture on iOS, and the Mac build plays it") — same AV1/VideoToolbox path and the same nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603) line, but reported on iOS; here it is the Mac host that freezes. It would be useful to know whether the Mac-side difference noted in #2407 applies here too.
- #2990 ("Super Mario Sunshine freezes entering the M graffiti: movie-output notifications lost after EOS (Mac)") — same symptom (frozen picture, audio and frame loop keep running) but an AVC EOS/notification path, not AV1.
I am reporting the observation only; I have not diagnosed or patched the host.

Moved from LNPANDY/NX2Apple#645, which was closed on 2026-11-19 as engine-side (maintainer: engine issues belong in nxnative, not NX2Apple).

## Setup

- Game: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (UE 5.6), title ID `0100B8A026F14000`
- Device: iPhone 14 Plus, iOS 27.0.1, Apple A15 GPU (no native BC texture support)
- Built with: NX2Apple v1.1.0 (also reproduced on v0.4.8); installed via the NX2Apple shell IPA + LiveContainer, game data in the shell app's `Documents/games/` folder
- `DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1` (`bc_cpu 1` in the log) — CPU decoding of BC textures is active

## What happens

The game launches and runs at ~60 fps, geometry is intact, host UI (buttons, fps counter, menu text) is clean — but the whole 3D scene renders with wrong colors plus streaking noise. Screenshot from #645 (same run as the log below):

![IMG_0392 — whole 3D scene with wrong colors and streaking noise on an A15 iPhone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f9a9b3a-145c-482d-bcfd-287a7151bc5f)

Log (run 2026-11-04 11:06 CST, v0.4.8):

```
boot: DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1
[dm]   more stdalloc_cap 0 key_skip 0+0 bc_cpu 1 ue_pool 0 enc_thread 0
[dm] [nvn-mtl] BC textures: this GPU has no BC support, decoding them on the CPU (profile tex_bc_cpu)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] Metal device Apple A15 GPU
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 900: frame time p50 16.73 / p95 17.25 / max 17.93 ms
```

No crash, no FATAL, and no texture-decode warning or error anywhere in the full log. Full log excerpt: [log-excerpt.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34355088/log-excerpt.txt)

## Retest on v1.1.0 (2026-11-06)

Rebuilt with v1.1.0 at the maintainer's request and retested: wrong colors and streaking unchanged from v0.4.8. (Full v1.1.0 log excerpt: [log_3-excerpt.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34454779/log_3-excerpt.txt); the v1.1.0 run also ended after ~2.5 min with memory at 2984 MB and 87 MB headroom — that looks like iOS killing the app for memory, and v0.4.8 showed the same texture-streaming surge to ~2585 MB, so I am not reporting the memory climb as a v1.1.0 regression, only as context.)

## Why this looks like a decoder bug, not a setup problem

- Same device, same BC CPU decode path: Mario Wonder renders with correct texture colors (about 3.5 min of play) — so the CPU decode path works in principle; FFRS fails per-game.
- Not a resolution / present / upscale problem: `DM_OPMODE=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`; the log shows no decode warnings.
- Release-note checks of NX2Apple v1.2.2, v1.2.3 and v1.4.0 list no BC texture-decode fix for this.

## Question

Is BC CPU decoding expected to produce correct colors for this game on A15, or is there a known gap in the CPU decoder for the BC formats this game uses? Happy to provide the full logs and the screenshot from #645, and to retest on a current engine build if that helps.
title: BC CPU decode on A15 iPhone: whole-scene wrong colors + streaking (FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE)

### What happened

The Mac build of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time v131072 stops at step 3/5, shader split, with exit code 1. The split reports 3,023 rows only in the profile and 3,022 only in the generated shader map.

Reproduction command using the documented build entry point

```sh
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "/path/to/The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time.nup" --platform mac
```

The NUP contains the base game, update v131072 and no DLC. Extraction and rewriting succeed before shader validation stops the build.

Confirmed from the generated tables and a read-only check of the affected archive in the dump

- The registered shader map contains 42,848 keys. The generated map contains 42,847. Exactly one registered key is absent, and there are no added keys.
- The absent key is `ce0eba6c3584814d`, recorded as vertex shader `vs_shader.bin`, index 28, at `/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc`.
- All 3,022 changed rows for keys present on both sides differ only in package index. Their shader keys, stages, package names and source labels are unchanged.
- The data rows in shader_facts.tsv, shader_pairs.tsv and pso_pairs.tsv match exactly.
- I decompressed ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs using the dump's zstd dictionary and inspected AglShader.sharcb. The current BAHS reader selects 5,893 records from 5,894 scan candidates. Temporarily disabling only the binary-record-array filter in memory exposes exactly the descriptor at 0x1b41cc, with key ce0eba6c3584814d, that the new reader rejects.

Commit `5df3dbe8` (PR #2943, reject stray BAHS descriptors) added the validated binary-record-array filtering. It refreshed the Bananza and Mario Kart World maps, while the Ocarina of Time map still includes this rejected candidate. The omitted entry shifts 3,022 indices, which accounts for the complete table mismatch.

The Ocarina shader map appears to need regeneration with the corrected BAHS reader. Please retain the validated record filtering when refreshing it.

Validation covers the existing failed split tables and the affected archive reader. A refreshed full build and gameplay were not tested. The investigation made no source or app changes.

The registered v131072 profile should match the current validated BAHS split, allowing the build to proceed to shader compilation.

### What happened

I originally reported these issues in LNPANDY/NX2Apple#1371. The NX2Apple maintainer requested that engine-related problems be reported directly to nxnative.

I am experiencing three performance-related issues with Resident Evil 4 Gold Edition (Switch 2) on an Apple M5 Pro MacBook Pro.

1. Significant runtime pipeline compilation stalls

The game is generally capable of running at approximately 60 FPS, but occasional severe frame-time spikes cause noticeable freezes.

The attached runtime log contains several examples:

Frame

GPU time

Pipeline compilation

These stalls appear strongly associated with runtime pipeline compilation rather than ordinary GPU rendering load.

For example, frame 1469 took approximately 2.15 seconds, with 2.11 seconds spent compiling 28 new pipelines, while the reported GPU time was only 10.4 ms.

The same log records a lengthy pipeline prebuild phase:

60,723 shader pairs processed

15,764 pipeline bases built

43,559 already archived

1,400 left to be handled by draws

0 failures

Total prebuild time: approximately 1099.8 seconds

Despite this substantial prebuild phase, severe compilation-related stalls still occur during gameplay.

I understand that some runtime compilation may be unavoidable, but I would appreciate an investigation into whether pipeline caching, prebuilding, or asynchronous compilation could reduce these stalls.

2. Noticeable FPS degradation after extended gameplay

During a longer gameplay session, the game initially ran relatively smoothly, but performance noticeably degraded after approximately 30 minutes of continuous play.

I have not established whether this is caused by thermal throttling, memory/resource accumulation, GPU synchronization, or another bottleneck.

Importantly, the attached runtime log captures only approximately 3 minutes and 20 seconds of frame execution, excluding the long startup preparation. It demonstrates intermittent pipeline compilation stalls but does not independently establish the sustained FPS degradation observed in my longer session.

I am reporting the longer-session slowdown as an additional observation rather than claiming that the attached log proves its cause.

3. High CPU temperatures during cinematic cutscenes

During normal gameplay, the monitored CPU temperature is usually around 60°C.

However, during certain cinematic cutscenes, CPU temperature rises significantly, reaching approximately 90°C.

The MacBook Pro's fans do not noticeably increase their speed during these temperature spikes.

I understand that a CPU temperature of 90°C does not necessarily indicate a hardware fault or thermal throttling.

However, the significant temperature difference between normal gameplay and cutscenes seems worth investigating.

Possible areas to examine include CPU-side graphics work, video decoding, synchronization overhead, and shader/pipeline processing during cinematic sequences.

I have not confirmed whether the cutscene temperature spikes are related to the extended-session FPS degradation.



### What you expected

I would expect:

More consistent frame pacing during gameplay, with fewer severe stalls from runtime pipeline compilation.

Stable performance during extended gameplay sessions without substantial degradation after approximately 30 minutes.

More predictable CPU workload and thermal behavior during cinematic cutscenes.

Where technically feasible, additional rendering-resolution, frame-rate, or quality controls to help balance performance and image quality.

In particular, I would appreciate clarification on whether the observed runtime pipeline stalls are expected with the current RE4 profile or whether improvements to pipeline prebuilding and caching are planned.

### What happened

The Mac build stops at step 3/5, shader split, with exit code 1 on commit `a4c82979`. The split reports 417 rows only in the profile and 417 only in its generated shader map.

Reproduction command using the documented native build entry point

```sh
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "/path/to/Sonic Frontiers Definitive Edition.nup" --platform mac
```

The NUP contains update v65536 and no DLC. The script accepts the update as the whole game, reuses the 26.4 GB extraction, rewrites main and sdk, and then fails the shader table comparison.

Confirmed by read-only analysis of the same NUP, extracted modules and generated tables

- main Build-ID is `38151dd9103a9d4b9e2479a8e2b04e59` and sdk Build-ID is `31945f745022d0232d2562252641b3d3`. Both match the registered v65536 profile.
- Reading main and sdk from the NUP verifies their stored SHA-256 hashes. Their payloads are identical to the extracted files. The main NSO also passes decompression and its enabled segment-integrity checks.
- The profile and split contain the same 4,958 shader keys. Zero keys are missing or added. shader_facts.tsv, shader_pairs.tsv and pso_pairs.tsv have identical data rows.
- All 417 changed map rows belong to main. 387 differ only in package index. The other 30 differ in package index and source label.
- The Needle reader finds 1,586 records in main, representing 1,554 unique keys. 30 keys have duplicate copies. The duplicate control/code pairs pass same_shader.
- Applying the previous last-occurrence selection in memory reproduces every main row in the registered shader map exactly. Applying the current first-occurrence selection reproduces every main row in the failed split exactly.

The cause is the change in `8d62601f` from the last-wins dictionary comprehension for main to `uniq_keys(found)`, which keeps the first occurrence. For example, key `6d6f5b99bd7cfcce` occurs at both `main#NEEDLE@0x29c2b44` and `main#NEEDLE@0x2a814fc`. The registered row uses the latter. Choosing the earlier copies changes the sort order and shifts further package indices.

The split log also contains 1,586 no-code-area diagnostics from the raw scanner. Every diagnostic offset corresponds to a control section already decoded by the Needle reader. All registered shader keys remain present.

Related to the duplicate source-selection regression reported for Bananza in #2921.

Validation was limited to the NUP/module checks, comparison of generated tables, and in-memory replay of duplicate selection. A corrected full shader build and gameplay were not tested. Source code and app files were left unchanged.

### What you expected

The registered v65536 dump should pass shader table validation and proceed to shader compilation. Equivalent duplicate shader records should retain source selection compatible with the registered map.

Sonic Frontiers Definitive Edition, 0400921025B32000, v65536 (1.0.0), no DLC

a4c82979

### What happened

[nxnative-report-010090C022978001-2026-11-19.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35068525/nxnative-report-010090C022978001-2026-11-19.zip)

This is the **native** Switch release from 8 October 2026 (title ID `010090C022978000`, a multi-program application: program 0 is the launcher `MareLauncher`, programs 1–5 the games), not the Cloud Version. I packed program 1 (Kingdom Hearts Final Mix) on its own with `--program 1`.

KH1 mounts the launcher's RomFS by program index (`fs::MountRom("rom0", 0, …)`). With the launcher's RomFS extracted (`nx_extract … --app 010090C022978000 --romfs-image`) and placed at `<build>/extract/v0/romfs_programs/0.img`, the app packs it and both mounts work (thank you for the `romfs_programs` support):

```
[dm] fs mount rom: → …/Kingdom Hearts 1 Final Mix.app/Contents/Resources/romfs.img (read-only)
[dm] fs mount rom0: → …/Kingdom Hearts 1 Final Mix.app/Contents/Resources/romfs_programs/0.img (read-only)
```

The game then runs: steady 60 fps, the loading-screen music plays, saves commit, and it keeps drawing (frame 300: 19,907 draws; later about 3 draws a frame). But the picture is solid magenta, exactly (255, 0, 255), from the first frame, in the window and in `DM_CTL` `shot` captures.

Three Vulkan commands are not implemented, and the game calls each of them in its first frame:

```
[dm] UNIMPL vkCmdClearAttachments (x0=0x7c3ade8f80 x1=0x1 x2=0x171e11580)
[dm] [vk] [RED] dynamic state 4 not implemented (the imports have no matching set function)
[dm] UNIMPL vkCmdSetBlendConstants (x0=0x7c3ade8f80 x1=0x171e113a8 x2=0xff)
[dm] UNIMPL vkCmdResolveImage (x0=0x7c3ade8f80 x1=0x7c3acab1e0 x2=0x6)
[dm] [vk] frame 1: draws 3, passes 2, submits 9, copies 8 (since the last record, 1 frames); pipelines so far 3, buffer memory 10.0 MB
```

My guess, not checked: if the game renders into a multisampled target and resolves it with `vkCmdResolveImage`, the image it presents is never written. Pure magenta is also what an all-zero ASTC block decodes to, so the other possibility is an ASTC texture (a full-screen loading image) whose contents never arrive. `dynamic state 4` is blend constants, which goes with the missing `vkCmdSetBlendConstants`.

On engine `b2d46b86` (2026-11-07) the same program also showed solid magenta (it then needed `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY` with the launcher's files to get past start-up); the `LOAD_OP_DONT_CARE` change (ced36121) didn't change it.

### What you expected

The KH1 loading screen and title screen.

Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX (native release), application `010090C022978000`, program 1 (`010090C022978001`), v0 (no update), US. SDK `nnSdk-20_5_24-Release`. body:
**Request:** local wireless (`nn::ldn`) between devices running nxnative, so games' "Wireless Play" / local multiplayer modes work across nearby phones.

**Today:** `dm/host/hle_offline.c` cuts the whole service: `nn::ldn::Initialize`, `CreateNetwork`, `Connect` and the rest return failure, and `Scan` finds 0 networks. In Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (0100152000022000) Wireless Play therefore never sees or hosts a room.

**Idea:** carry LDN over the ordinary Wi-Fi network the devices share, the way ldn_mitm does on Switch homebrew: a host advertises its `NetworkInfo` (plus the game's advertise data) over UDP broadcast on the LAN, stations scan by listening for those broadcasts, and once connected the game's own sockets run over the real LAN IPs, with `GetIpv4Address` / `GetNetworkInfo` answering from that LAN session. nxnative-to-nxnative only; no interop with real consoles needed.

**Setup:** iPhone 16 Pro Max, iOS 26, IPA built from `main` (c22f30a) with handheld.txt, run in GameCase. The game itself runs fine (BotW and MK8 both play; see #2444).

I know this is a large feature and may be out of scope; filing it so it is tracked. Happy to test builds on two iPhones (or an iPhone and a Mac) if it ever lands.
title: Feature request: local wireless (nn::ldn) over LAN, e.g. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Wireless Play

body:
### Game

**It Takes Two** (Hazelight Studios / EA) — Nintendo Switch (eShop)

- Title ID (base): `010092A0172E4000`
- Availability: NSP base + update + DLC packages exist on common archive sites
- Genre: linear co-op action-adventure

### Why it is a good fit

It Takes Two is one of the most-requested *local* co-op titles, and the two-player
experience is entirely split-screen couch co-op — exactly what the engine's new
multi-controller support (per #10, each controller gets its own player slot on
macOS and iOS) was built for. A working profile would showcase the new input
stack end to end with a mainstream game.

### Current status

- No profile exists under `dm/games/010092A0172E4000/`
- #10 confirmed controller infrastructure only; the maintainer explicitly noted
  the game itself still needs a profile and recorded gameplay validation
- Not listed in the companion app's GAMES.md either

### Offer

I own the game and have the dumps staged, and would be glad to:

- run the build pipeline against my dump and report logs/crash reports
- test on Apple Silicon (M5 Max, large display, MetalFX path) with two
  DualSense/Pro controllers for split-screen validation
- iterate on any profile knobs (version pinning, patches) you want probed

### Environment

- Hardware: Apple M5 Max (Mac)
- Engine channel: upcoming 1.5.0 stable (pin `94a09447`)

Thanks for considering — happy Chinese-community users would love a couch co-op flagship to demo.
title: Game profile request: It Takes Two (010092A0172E4000) — local split-screen co-op showcase for the new multi-controller support

### What happened

Packing v131072 with `--platform mac-app` on a clean checkout of `ac3fc4d7` stops at the shader map check.

```text
[04:29:55] ✗ [3/6] shader split (2:20)
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 0400486024DEC000's:
shader_map.tsv: 3,023 row(s) only in the profile, 3,022 only in the split
  profile: vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	ce0eba6c3584814d	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b41cc
  split:   vs_shader.bin	28	vertex	4c35081101443a7f	/Shader/ApplicationPackage.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.release.sarc.zs/AglShader.sharcb#BAHS@0x1b85a8
```

After #2943 the splitter finds all 5,893 binary records in `AglShader.sharcb`. The old scan also read `0x1b41cc` inside a fragment record as a vertex descriptor. Removing that entry at `vs_shader.bin` index 28 and decrementing later indices reproduces every data row in the new map. All 42,847 retained shader records are byte-identical. The data rows in `shader_facts.tsv`, `shader_pairs.tsv` and `pso_pairs.tsv` also match.

### What you expected

Packing v131072 should pass the shader map check. I can submit the regenerated map as a one-file PR.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, v131072, no DLC. The build IDs of `main`, `subsdk0` and `sdk` match `game.tsv`.

### nxnative commit

`ac3fc4d7`

### Shader chain version

`03a3ac831bfb`

### How it was built and run

The NSP script failed before anything ran

### Device and OS

Mac mini M4 Pro, macOS 27.2.1

### Settings and environment overrides

None. Build options: `--platform mac-app --no-seen-shaders --gpu g16s -l ru`.

`build.log` is the full console output from the failing pack. `split.log` is the output of the independent split.

title: Grand Theft Auto: III – The Definitive Edition (v1.0.8) Pipeline archive & Shader unreadable

body: ### Which step failed Pipeline prebuild or Pipeline archive ### The message The game builds and boots, and both the main menu and cutscenes render properly. However, once actual gameplay begins, the 3D world and character graphics are completely missing (blank/black screen). Only the 2D HUD elements (minimap, health/armor bars, weapon/ammo icons, etc.) are visible on screen. Additional Build Context: I noticed two warnings/errors during the build process that are likely causing this missing 3D rendering issue: Shader Split: The status reported 6,233 shaders, 30135 file(s) unreadable, suggesting that a huge portion of the game's shaders failed to be extracted or read properly. Pipeline Archive: The step failed with the message "Failed, the app is packed without one". body:
### What is missing

[Cartouche](https://github.com/cartouche-app/Cartouche) is an iOS front end for nxnative: it installs and starts the IPAs players build from their own games, often with Cartouche Builder on their Mac, which runs your NSP script as docs/frontends.md describes. It never downloads or ships a game. Earlier I sent #1315 (the guest memory in files) and the iPhone runs in #1184.

After each session, Cartouche reads the summary lines nxnative writes in the game's log, on the iPhone and, in its console in Cartouche Builder, on the Mac: the `[nvn]` timing, on-screen and power lines, `[longframe]`, `pipeline prepare`, the memory and thermal lines, `CRASH sig=`, `GPU access revoked` and `[RED] boot:`. Cartouche Builder also reads the Mac launcher's last line, and sends how each build ended, with its commit and stage. Unless the player turns it off, the numbers go to the project's server: never a log line, a path or an account. We sum up what is about nxnative on a page redone every Thursday: **[nxnative's games on players' iPhones and Macs](https://github.com/cartouche-app/Cartouche/blob/nxnative-measurements/README.md)**.

From November 10 to 17 it covers 1,390 sessions from 107 installs and 279 hours, by game, by model and by commit: frame rate, frame times, stutters and shader stalls, pipeline prepare, memory peak, heat and how sessions ended; then the crashes several installs share, devices, the games played on players' Macs, and the builds on players' Macs by commit, the IPAs and the Mac apps apart. Every line and every figure sums up at least three installs, or three Macs, and nothing names an install or a session. Sessions on GPUs your check refuses, those whose game process ran without Increased Memory Limit (Cartouche's doing) and those of modified builds are counted apart, so they don't read as yours.

What stands out this week:

- **Builds on players' Macs:** from November 11 to 17, Cartouche Builder built 215 IPAs of 55 games on 49 Macs, from 99 of your commits, in a median of 25 minutes, and 129 builds failed, counting a game of a Mac once for each commit, as its last try ended. The steps they failed at most were the shader split (23, on 11 Macs), the iOS app build (21, on 11 Macs: `786715256f37` and `ccd834e06a39` built nothing on November 11 and 12, with Xcode 27.2), iOS shaders (13, on 8 Macs) and IPA pack (10, on 4 Macs). The page has them by commit, with the regressions apart.
- **Shader split since `8d62601f`:** on November 16 and 17, 8 Macs failed at it, against 3 in the four days before, and on 3 of them the game had built before; on the page, `8d62601f375f` built 7 games and failed 6, all there. As far as we can read, that commit makes `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` keep the first copy of a shader that `main` carries several times (`uniq_keys`) where it kept the last, so the tables of profiles split before no longer match and the build stops with "the split shader tables differ from game profile". Its parent, `24e007be`, still builds Mario Kart World v0 for us. `5df3dbe8` changed Mario Kart World's v0 map on November 18, with a full v0 resplit still open, and `uniq_keys` is still there: I can send a bug report with the log once our builds have tried it.
- **Your app for the Mac:** Cartouche Builder now builds it next to the IPA and starts it. From November 15 to 17, it built 37 Mac apps of 22 games on 13 Macs, and 12 Macs played 10 games 58 times (5.6 hours), Ocarina of Time on 5 of them and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on 3. 35 of those ended with the game quitting, none as a crash or with the GPU revoked; the other 23 (9 Macs), most under a minute, left no launcher line we know.
- **Minecraft Dungeons II:** 12 sessions on 3 installs and 3 models, all ended with SIGABRT at start.
- **Super Mario Galaxy:** 15 sessions and 11 hours on 7 installs, and no `[nvn]` timing, on-screen or power line in any of their logs. Is that expected for this game, or do they stay on a black screen?
- **Mario Kart World** (20 installs): 30.6 fps for its 60, 108 stutters a minute, a quarter of them waiting for shaders, and 4.9 s of shader stall a minute. **Ocarina of Time**, which you follow in #1789 (26 installs, 243 sessions): 30.0 fps for its 30, 24.2 in its slowest 5%; 95 sessions reached the serious thermal state, 19 most likely ran out of memory, and its peak is 5,950 MiB.
- **MetalFX:** its present pass took 2.7 ms of GPU time on iPhones (21 installs) against 0.5 ms for the bilinear one (81 installs), as your launcher warns, and no more crashes: 8% of sessions ended in one with it (253 sessions) and without (1,137).

Since Cartouche's version of November 13, sessions name their commit (`DMCommit`): 364 of the 1,110 that count this week. Players build from many commits (16 for Ocarina of Time alone), so only one line by game and commit reaches three installs yet.

All of this comes from log lines, which docs/frontends.md calls diagnostics, not an interface, adding that events a program can read would be its next piece. Until then, a reworded line drops a measurement without a sound, and a game that writes no summary line, as Super Mario Galaxy above, can't be told from one on a black screen.

### What you propose

Events like the NSP script's `--progress json`, one JSON object per line, in a file beside the log or at a path the front end gives in the environment:

- the start of a session: title ID, game version, `DMCommit`, shader chain, the settings in effect;
- a summary every few minutes and at the end: frames, frame-time percentiles, stutters and those that waited for shaders, shader stall, pipeline prepare, memory peak, thermal state;
- how it ended: quit, crash with its signal, GPU access revoked, boot failure.

The names and fields are yours to choose. We would read the events of the builds that write them, and the log of the others; meanwhile we follow your `Front-ends:` lines.

And about the measurements, if they help:

1. Which form suits you: that page, a weekly post in your Discussions, or a TSV like your `validated.tsv`?
2. Which fields you would add or drop. We read each build's shader chain (`DMChain`) but don't send it yet.
3. `[nvn] power` times each 300 frames by the clock, so a stretch in which the game was suspended (left behind Cartouche's console, or Cartouche in the background) comes out at a few fps; we now leave out a stretch with a frame of a second or more. Is the line meant to count that time?

If this is noise for you, say so and we won't post more.

### Platforms

iPhone, iPad, Mac
title: Front ends: session events, and players' measurements by game, model and commit

## What happens

Building **Pokémon Legends: Arceus** (`01001F5010DFA000`, base v0 + update **v262144 / 1.1.1**) from current main stops at the shader split:

```
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 01001F5010DFA000's:
shader_map.tsv: 36 row(s) only in the profile, 36 only in the split
  profile: vs_main.bin	0	vertex	5c116cabc36aeae3	main#BNSH@0x4020000#var2
  split:   ps_main.bin	0	pixel	0f1f2c66d3f64aa1	main#BNSH@0x4020000#var0
```

## Environment

- macOS 26.7.1, Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal toolchain 32023.922.4
- nxnative **main `42d02fa8`** (includes the command-memory fix `0e409ed8`)
- `python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<folder>" -k prod.keys --platform mac-app`
- The modules' build IDs match the profile's `build` row (`main=aee8f150…`, `subsdk1=4dd097b4…`, `sdk=b39add63…`), so the game files are the registered version; the script prints no "derived profile" notice.
- Extraction: 19,101 files / 6.0 GB, rewrite `main, subsdk1, sdk` OK.

The same game files and command built fine on **`f644af4b` (Nov 14)**: 12,851 shaders, no table mismatch. The splitter changed between that commit and `42d02fa8` (shader chain `d254f45e8002` → `cf3be507e0eb`). Commits touching `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` in that range: `72047f1a`, `bee218d9`, `049f8e0e`, `b32d0bf3`, `b6baa5d2`, `eb2e27f8`, `bc36ee25`, `25b9d2fe`, `b4b1c8d7`, `8d62601f`, `31b537f1`.

## It is only the label columns, not the shaders

Comparing the two `shader_map.tsv` byte for byte, as a map keyed on column 4 (the shader key):

- both files have **12,852 data rows** and **exactly the same 12,852 keys**;
- the sets of names (`vs_main.bin` / `ps_main.bin`), stages (`vertex` / `pixel`) and keys are identical;
- all 36 differing rows differ **only in the index column (3rd) and the `#varN` label of the source column (5th)**.

Examples:

| key | profile | split |
|---|---|---|
| `5c116cabc36aeae3` | `vs_main.bin 0 vertex main#BNSH@0x4020000#var2` | `vs_main.bin 0 vertex main#BNSH@0x4020000#var0` |
| `0f1f2c66d3f64aa1` | `ps_main.bin 0 pixel main#BNSH@0x4020000#var3` | `ps_main.bin 0 pixel main#BNSH@0x4020000#var0` |
| `84e5cbd33db320a7` | `vs_main.bin 4 vertex main#BNSH@0x4028000#var13` | `vs_main.bin 7 vertex main#BNSH@0x4028000#var2` |
| `9e4aba4d6c75c3a8` | `ps_main.bin 3 pixel main#BNSH@0x4028000#var14` | `ps_main.bin 9 pixel main#BNSH@0x4028000#var14` |

`shader_pairs.tsv`, `shader_facts.tsv` and `pso_manifest.tsv` do **not** differ, so the drift is confined to `shader_map.tsv`'s index/`#varN` columns of the variations at `main#BNSH@0x4020000` and `@0x4028000`.

## Workaround used

Copying the split's own table over the profile's lets the build proceed, and the result works:

```
cp <build>/shader/pkg.partial/tables/shader_map.tsv dm/games/01001F5010DFA000/shader_map.tsv
```

then the split is reused/converges and the build compiles 12,851 of 12,851 shaders. The app boots and plays (this is the build that confirmed the `0e409ed8` command-memory fix in #2717).

## Request

Please re-split and refresh `dm/games/01001F5010DFA000/shader_map.tsv` from the current splitter (and check whether the index/`#varN` columns feed anything else, so the refresh is complete). Until then, anyone rebuilding Arceus from main hits this stop, since the comparison is on whole rows rather than keys.
title: Pokémon Legends: Arceus: the profile's shader_map.tsv is out of date with the splitter (36 rows differ in index/#varN only)

body:
### What happened

Just Dance 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 compiled for Mac on macOS 27.2.1 crash at start due to a to a crash in opus decoding 
(JD 2019 doesn't have this issue)

[dm] FATAL Opus decoder 0x7fdd1070a0 was not initialized by the host

After many try and with the help of AI, I've been able to make all these version to run correctly (they also need IPK v5 decoding, cf #2976 , #2954) with the following change in hle_codec.c

remplace : 
`HLE_FORCE_ALIAS("_ZN2nn5codec19HardwareOpusDecoder10InitializeEiiPvm", "_ZN2nn5codec11OpusDecoder10InitializeEiiPvm", OPUS_WHY); `
by this (after the declaration of opus_fn)
```
HLE_FORCE(
    "_ZN2nn5codec19HardwareOpusDecoder10InitializeEiiPvm",
    "hwopus service; register the C view of the software OpusDecoder",
    int, h_codec_HwOpusClassInit,
    void *hw, int rate, int ch, void *buf, size_t size) {
    int (*f)(void *, int, int, void *, size_t) =
        opus_fn("_ZN2nn5codec11OpusDecoder10InitializeEiiPvm");
    int result = f(hw, rate, ch, buf, size);
    if (result == 0) {
        void *hw_type = (char *)hw + 8;
        if (!objmap_get(hw_type))
            objmap_put(hw_type, hw_type);
    }
    return result;
}
```

and in h_codec_HwOpusFini, replace 
`void *s = objmap_del(hw); if (s) { f(s); free(s); }`
by
```
void *s = objmap_del(hw);
if (s) {
    f(s);
    if (s != hw)
        free(s);
}
```

I don't submit it as a PR as I totaly don't understand what could be the impact for others game.
The problem might need to be fixed in another way

Here is the explaination given by AI

## Fix HardwareOpusDecoder state mapping and cleanup

### Problem

The host replaces the hardware Opus decoder with the SDK's software `OpusDecoder`, since the hardware `hwopus` service is not available in the emulator environment.

The C++ `HardwareOpusDecoder::Initialize` entry point was not correctly registering the initialized decoder in the `objmap` used by the other HLE codec handlers.

While investigating a crash in Just Dance 2020, the logs showed that the pointer received by `Initialize` differed by 8 bytes from the pointer later used by the channel-count handler. Since `objmap` uses exact pointer addresses as keys, the subsequent lookup failed, even though initialization had succeeded. This resulted in the decoder being reported as not initialized and the game aborting.

### Changes

**1. Add an explicit HLE wrapper for `HardwareOpusDecoder::Initialize`**

Instead of relying on the previous direct alias, the wrapper explicitly calls the SDK's software `OpusDecoder::Initialize` implementation and preserves its return value.

After successful initialization, it registers the adjusted decoder pointer (`hw + 8`) in `objmap`, using the pointer itself as the mapped value.

This ensures that subsequent codec handlers can resolve the decoder state using the address they actually receive.

**2. Make finalization aware of in-place decoder state**

The finalization handler now distinguishes between two cases:

- When the mapped state pointer is the same as the decoder pointer, the software decoder state resides in the existing game-owned decoder object. It must be finalized but not freed.
- When the mapped state pointer is different, it represents separately allocated host-side state. It must be finalized and then freed.

Previously, the finalization path unconditionally freed the mapped pointer, which is unsafe when the state is stored in-place.

### Result

The decoder state is now correctly resolved after C++ initialization, and finalization respects the ownership of the underlying memory.

This fixes the observed Just Dance 2020 crash in the hardware Opus decoder path without changing the actual Opus decoding implementation.

The change is limited to decoder state registration and lifecycle management.

### Game & Environment
- **Game:** Tetris Effect: Connected (`0100DE501433A000`), version 2.0.2.2 (`v1310720`)
- **Modules:** `main=8838095f4f659f63cb45a00e62dfb887`, `subsdk0=a8cb97803f7f442a3b6cce1c7cd4ee4a`, `sdk=357efc198e728cb5d55265aff304f03c` (SDK 13.3.2)
- **nxnative:** `c379a903` (main) / `dfebf54549a7`, shader chain `9b791ad68066`
- **Platform:** Apple M4 Mac (`mac-app`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`)

### Original Problem
The game boots with the logo spinning in the bottom right, then crashes to desktop with `sig=11 addr=0 pc=main+0xb64bec lr=main+0xb64bdc` (`x20=0`) on `GameThread`:

```
[dm] ro::RegisterModuleInfo: refused an NRR that registers only online SDKs (1 hashes), as before NROs were loaded; the game plays offline
...
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=main+0xb64bec lr=main+0xb64bdc sp=0x7ec91a61d0
x0=0x3ad4 x1=0x7ec91a61d0 x2=0x7bde818000 x3=0x107753c50 x4=0x7bde81a340 x5=0
...
[dm] bt: main+0x2742aec main+0x2742768 main+0x2741670 main+0x2a36fc4 main+0x30821a8 ...
```

Because the host refuses `nro/EOSSDK-Switch-Shipping.nro`, `EOS_Platform_Create` (`main+0x410600`) stays a stub returning `0`, so `OnlineSubsystemRedpointEOS` does not register `"RedpointEOS"`. The Actor `BeginPlay` at `main+0xb64b18` (called from `AActor::DispatchBeginPlay` at `main+0x2742aec`) calls `IOnlineSubsystem::Get("RedpointEOS")` at `main+0xb64b88` and dereferences `x20` at `main+0xb64bec` (`ldr x8, [x20]`) without checking for null.

### Workaround Patch (in fork)
Added the profile and `patches.py` workaround (`eos_null_guard`, branching to `main+0xb64c3c` when `x0 == 0` at `main+0xb64b8c`) on branch `game/tetris-effect-connected` in the fork:
- Commit: https://github.com/hibimono-create/nxnative/commit/4c518512
- Branch: https://github.com/hibimono-create/nxnative/tree/game/tetris-effect-connected

### Current Status & Remaining Issue
With `eos_null_guard`, the game boots past the spinning logo and **single player is playable** on Mac.

However, selecting **Multiplayer** from the main screen navigates to the multiplayer main screen, where the game does not hang but **user input does nothing** (cannot select anything or go back to the main screen), requiring the user to quit the game. Static inspection of `main` also shows additional unchecked `GetOnlineSubsystem("RedpointEOS")` call sites (e.g. `main+0xb64fe8`, `main+0xb652d8`, `main+0xb691e0`).
title: Tetris Effect: Connected (0100DE501433A000): RedpointEOS null-pointer crash on boot and multiplayer input lock

body:
Follow-up to #2912. When Mario Kart World submits a frame, the game thread copies the whole batch of commands before replay can start. In the original M3 Max race test, the first batch took 0.85–1.1 ms to copy while the GPU was idle. [Arthur's submission-streaming commit](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/c6f491a240710efde6dabd52e8ed2b239f2915e2) lets replay start on the first finished command node while the rest are copied.

The original in-run A/B switched the change on and off every 300 frames in the uncapped race on an M3 Max. Median docked frame time went from 11.9–13.2 ms to 11.2–12.3 ms, a 0.7–1.4 ms drop in five of six pairs, with one tie. Handheld median frame time went from 9.7–11.0 ms to 8.9–9.9 ms and fell in all seven pairs. GPU time was unchanged. Both versions held 59.8 fps at the 60 fps cap. These figures come from the original branch.

Please put the change in a standalone PR against current main and repeat the same race with streaming on and off. Check that submissions still run in order and that textures and programs stay alive until replay finishes. The original queue tests passed with streaming both ways. The gameplay comparison on current main is still open.
title: nvn: retest submission streaming in Mario Kart World

body:
## Proposal

Would you accept an opt-in observation gate for hit telemetry on macOS? It would reuse the existing offline OBS rewrite. A reader could see each collision notification as it happens, including hits that leave the victim's percentage unchanged. Default builds would omit the gate.

- Pin the Super Smash Bros. Ultimate 13.0.5 profile (title ID `01006A800016E000`) to nxnative's 16-byte build key `21450c647b8c5940ed5b68218ea128fd`. The notification implementation starts at `main+0x67a7b0`. Its first word is `d10303ff` (`sub sp, sp, #0xc0`). The exported thunk and direct in-game callers both lead there. Enable the gate only for the matching build and word.
- Give the callback a read-only view of the saved arguments, including `s0` for damage, and the incoming guest link register for diagnosing callers. The OBS trampoline already saves SIMD state internally. The consumer also needs a registration path safe to call from its reader thread, for example by publishing the callback pointer with release/acquire operations. The gated rewrite would require a host that knows the assigned ID and callback ABI.
- The consumer would check the rewritten site and gate registration before attaching. Its callback copies arguments into a preallocated ring. The reader thread drains the ring. The callback does no I/O, allocation, locking, game calls or guest writes.

## Local results

A scratch macOS host based on `b06f4e0e` used the existing OBS trampoline. The hook reported all 33 independently counted Training contacts. A reader sampling every presented frame detected 27 separate percent rises. The six misses were jabs at 999% or with Fixed Damage on. The run drained 40 notifications in all with zero ring drops. The reader kept the callback disabled on an ungated build. Full-match frame-time cost remains unmeasured.

Is this a use of OBS you'd accept? If so, would you prefer a versioned read-only callback view or a small accessor for the saved registers on top of the existing OBS interface?

## Suggested implementation

1. **Profile and rewrite.** In `dm/games/01006A800016E000/patches.py`, add the opt-in entry for the pinned `main` above. Use the existing `site_obs` path in `dm/tools/patch_nso.py` to relocate the original instruction and resume at `main+0x67a7b4`. Reuse the opt-in build configuration and cache invalidation conventions. An ordinary build should emit the same image and gate table it does today. A wrong build or word must never produce the Smash gate.
2. **Host.** Reserve a gate ID in `dm/host/dm.h` and dispatch it in `dm/host/hle.c`. Expose a read-only, versioned callback view, or an accessor accepted by the maintainer, valid only for the duration of dispatch. Preserve existing OBS callers and their register-editing behavior. Publish a callback installed by the reader thread safely before the dispatch thread can load and invoke it. Require matching host support before using gated modules.
3. **Register view.** `w1` is the raw attacking object ID, `w2` is the victim object ID, and the low 32 bits of `v0` are the float damage argument. Retain raw `w3` and `w4` for diagnostics without assigning meanings to them. The layout in `dm/host/entry.S` distinguishes the incoming guest link register saved by the trampoline from the trampoline's return address in `regs[30]`. Keep offsets into that private save frame inside nxnative.
4. **Scope.** The game-specific part is an address and fingerprint in the Smash profile. The host-side read-only view and safe publication can be reused by other observers. Player ownership, hit classification, persistence and display belong in the consumer.

## Acceptance checks

- Rewriter tests cover opt-in, default and wrong-build cases and a mismatched original instruction. Inspect the output to verify that the opt-in uses one OBS gate and that its trampoline executes the displaced instruction and resumes at the following instruction.
- Host tests cover attaching from another thread, reading the expected integer and SIMD arguments and the incoming link register, dispatch with no observer, and rejection of an unsupported gate or interface. Cover guest register preservation in the read-only path and existing OBS compatibility.
- Run one macOS Training comparison with a gated and default build. Include an ordinary hit, a flat-percent hit and a multi-hit move. For performance, repeat the same longer workload with the gate absent, present without an observer, and present with an observer. Report frame-time median and tail, missed frames and ring drops. The earlier spike counted hits and drops.

🤖 Written by @dtcristo's agent (GPT-6.2 Sol)
title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate: opt-in OBS gate for hit telemetry
