## Summary
In Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072) on a 16 GB Mac, GPU memory held in the residency set grows by about 25 MB a minute at its low points while the game's own memory stays flat. After about 40 minutes, an area load pushed the footprint to 14.5 GB and the memory watchdog ended the session (`DM_MEM_CAP_GB=14`):
```
[RED] memory watchdog: resident 14506 MB over the limit of 14 GB (frame 71700), exiting
```

## Setup
- Base M4 Mac mini (10-core GPU, 16 GB), macOS 27.2.1, fullscreen at 2560x1440 @ 120 Hz.
- 30 fps cap, dynamic resolution off.
- Host built from main 72047f1a plus a few open PRs (#2226, #1662, #1436, #1751, #2530) and local switches (`DM_NVN_FAMILY_NOCOMPRESS=0`, `DM_PRESENT_QUEUE=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=2`, encode thread on).
- A 40-minute session of normal play across several areas.

## Data
Low and high points per window of about 7,200 frames (4 min), from the periodic `memory up to frame` and `residency set up to frame` lines:

| frames | resident | GPU allocated | residency set min | serial objects min |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7.2k–14k | 10.6 / 11.5 GB | 5.8 / 6.7 GB | 7.1k | 4.1k |
| 28.8k–36k | 11.0 / 12.7 | 6.0 / 7.8 | 7.0k | 4.2k |
| 43k–50k | 11.2 / 13.1 | 6.4 / 8.3 | 7.4k | 5.1k |
| 57.6k–64.8k | 11.6 / 12.8 | 6.8 / 8.1 | 8.5k | 6.0k |
| 64.8k–71.7k | 11.6 / 14.5 | 6.8 / 9.2 | 8.2k | 6.1k |

- **GPU allocated minus the residency set's MB stayed at 1,336–1,358 MB in every window.** All of the GPU growth is objects in the set. Its MB at the low points went from about 4.45 to 5.47 GB.
- **Serial objects** (`g_by_serial`) grew 4.1k → 6.5k, together with the set's object count.
- **The game's own memory looks flat.** The heap is 6.2 GB, and the alias region has stayed mapped at about 2.5 GB since frame 900. So the game doesn't seem to hold more textures over time; the host keeps more of them alive.
- **Host side (resident − GPU allocated)** was flat at 4.6–5.0 GB until frame 65k, then rose about 0.5 GB in the last 5 minutes. That part is unexplained.
- **Bounded or not growing:** the ghost table (512), the view cache, recycled heaps waiting (0–254 MB), stand-in heaps, memory pools (4.3k–5.2k), shared textures (floor 256 → 338), and CPU-written textures (flat after frame 13k).
- **Churn over the session:** 69,007 render targets released (235 GB in total), 86,926 first uploads, 44,999 re-uploads. `aglTextureDataMgr::Compaction` runs throughout.

## A suspect (not confirmed)
`own_tex_end_locked` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_owner.m:281` on c22f30a3). When a *copy* of a texture object is finalized while the object the texture was initialized in still has its magic and serial, the serial stays live and that object is not checked again.

If the game then frees, moves or overwrites that original object without a Finalize, the serial stays live for good. That keeps:
- its `g_by_serial` texture (and spare),
- its `g_tex_live` and image-description entries,
- its sharing-table entry (`alias_take_over` spares what a live serial holds),
- and its descriptors' views.

A memory pool's Finalize would end it, but this game's pools live for the whole session.

This fits "serial objects grow while the game's memory is flat", together with the game's texture-compaction thread moving texture data. But we can't show from this log that the game takes this path.

## Next
We're adding a periodic diagnostic that counts serials whose own object no longer holds them, plus malloc and owner-table sizes. We'll post the result from the next long session. If someone who knows the owner tables can say whether a moved or freed texture object without a Finalize is expected from this engine, that would help confirm or rule out the suspect.

The full log (2.3 MB) is available on request.
title: Ocarina of Time: residency set grows about 25 MB/min until the memory watchdog ends a 16 GB session after about 40 min

Build: cheemu/kid-with-sword-remake branch `L` at `e2869c41` (L6.4–L6.6), built with `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios --romfs separate`, the README's build settings. The only local change is a two-line launcher label (the build's version under the Play button); no engine changes. Dump: 0400486024DEC000 v131072.

Logs (bundle id and container paths replaced): https://gist.github.com/DocStream-Oficial/8a4804d27396e27ca792ba14feadfeef

## 1. iPhone 17 Pro Max (12 GB, iOS 27.2): guest memory grows ~3 GB in 10 minutes, then SIGSEGV

- Two sessions, render scale 0.80 and 0.75, frame generation off. In both, `[mem] alias region mapped … GB` keeps rising during normal play: 4.0 GB after loading the world, 5.5 GB at 8 min, 6.75 GB at 11 min (`alias region mapped up to +7.75 GB (alias region 8.00 GB)`).
- The last ~60 s before the crash are a continuous run of 50–400 ms frames on the submit thread (GPU 13–20 ms), with guest-file page-ins; the guest file grew 9.5 → 9.8 GB.
- Then six `alias region mapped 7.00 GB (application pool 9.00 GB)` in a row, `[RED] BufferInitialize: pool has no storage (pool 0x0 flags 0 offset 0 size 0x3d0)` and `CRASH sig=11 addr=0x4 pc=h_nvnMemoryPoolGetFlags+0` (log `iphone17pm_L6.6_80pct_crash_sig11.log`; the 0.75 run is `iphone17pm_L6.6_75pct_alias_growth.log`).
- Same phone on L6.1 (`ab41a33a`/`e72f779a`): 30 minutes at 0.65 with frame generation, the alias region stays at 3.25 GB, 0.2 % dropped frames (`iphone17pm_L6.1_65pct_reference_30min.log`). So something between L6.1 and L6.6 lets the mapped guest memory grow; we did not bisect it.

## 2. iPad Pro 11" M4 (8 GB, iPadOS 27.3): ~6 GB wired, the system kills or thrashes the game

- After 10–15 minutes, especially after a boss or in heavy areas, JetsamEvents show 43–55 MB free and 5.9–6.3 GB wired, with the game the largest process at 4.2–4.4 GB; iPadOS kills hundreds of processes and, at the end, the game (`ipadM4_8GB_L6.6_65pct_killed.log`). Another run did not die but thrashed: 3–7 s freezes every few seconds, each reading 400–680 MB of guest file back (`ipadM4_8GB_L6.6_thrash.log`).
- `DM_CTL restop` in the world: residency set 3,736 MB — shared buffers 3,343 / 1,938 MB, textures 1,001 / 1,129 MB, heaps 116 / 388 MB, private buffers 17 / 279 MB. The largest shared buffers are whole mid-sized pools: 305, 244, 201, 88, 75, 64 MB (`ipadM4_8GB_L6.6_restop.log`).
- Render scale barely changes it: Metal allocation 5.9–6.2 GB at 0.50, 0.65 and 0.75 (matches the profile's note that on Apple GPUs this game's cost hardly follows resolution).
- What we tried locally and reverted: chunking pools of 64 MB or more on iOS (`BIG_MIN` as a runtime threshold). It does not help this game: those pools get `one buffer of the whole pool (raw global memory's pool table)` anyway, and the chunks plus per-upload buffers caused residency churn (2,840 additions / 3.4 GB in 300 frames, 3.3 s of residency commits) and far more hitches. Mentioned only so nobody repeats it.

Workarounds we use meanwhile: L6.1 on the iPhone; on the 8 GB iPad 0.50–0.65 without frame generation, ≥20 GB free storage, and restarting the game every ~15 minutes.

Happy to run any build or switch you want measured on both devices.
title: Ocarina of Time (kid-with-sword-remake L6.6) on iOS: guest memory grows until a crash, and 8 GB devices run out of system memory

body:
### What happened

On an iPhone 17 Pro Max, Tears of the Kingdom 1.4.3 starts, shows the pipeline-prewarm progress screen, and aborts every time around 16000–18000 of 26456. This started after a period of normal play (the list in `Documents/pso_user.tsv` had grown). Rebuilding the IPA on a current shader chain and sideloading it again does not fix it, because that file stays in the app container.

The IPA was packed with `--romfs separate --shader-files` (needed so the shader library is not a single image over AltServer's ~2 GiB limit). The iOS shader step finished 28,669/28,669; this is not a hole in the pack. RomFS (`Documents/romfs.img`) is present. The device still had ~53.8 GB free. The abort is not Jetsam: physical footprint at crash was only ~0.82 GB of 11.42 GB RAM.

Turning **Metal 4 pipelines** and **Pipeline prebuild** off in the settings screen does not avoid the crash. Startup still always prewarms the known pipeline lists: bundled `pso_manifest.tsv` (4,092 lines) plus `Documents/pso_user.tsv` (26,381 lines from earlier play on this phone), 26,456 lines in total. Those two toggles only change how pipelines are compiled / whether a one-time stand-in prebuild runs; they do not skip this list prewarm. The on-screen counter is that prewarm, not a walk of the 28,669-library pack.

A launch with both toggles off (`DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`) still printed `pipeline prepare: 7052 of 26456 lines done after 0.5 s, the progress screen shows`, then 257 unique `[RED] failed to load shader … mmap failed` on individual files under `DmIOS.app/msl/b-5ea15f2c8240/*.metallib` (spot-checked files exist in the IPA), then:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=6
```

during `__warm_prepare_block_invoke` → `warm_task` → `pso_build_ex` → `pso_build_dev`. Address space at crash: 449.93 GB in 11,824 regions, largest free 0.00 GB.

With Metal 4 left on, a later launch died in the same prewarm with `NSMallocException`: `attempt to allocate object of class 'AGXG18PFamilyVertexProgram' failed`, plus `std::bad_alloc`, and the same VA picture (12,250 regions, largest free 0.00 GB, footprint 0.84 GB). There were also earlier `MTLCompilerService` `EXC_CRASH` / `SIGABRT` aborts under `buildSpecializedFunctionRequest` / LLVM `emitError` on this device; those look closer to #2474 and the Mac prewarm compiler crashes, but they are not required to hit the mmap/VA abort.

Workaround that does work: `Documents/env.txt` containing `DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off`. That skips both `pso_manifest.tsv` and `pso_user.tsv` at start, and the game then reaches in-game (pipelines built when first drawn). There is no settings-screen control for this.

### What you expected

Startup should either complete the prewarm or degrade (skip a pipeline, unmap unused metallibs) instead of aborting once `pso_user.tsv` has grown. The settings toggles that look related to pipelines should either skip this list prewarm, or a documented in-app setting should exist for `DM_PSO_MANIFEST`. Updating the IPA should not keep tripping over a play-history list that no longer matches a new shader chain, or at least should not mmap every loose `--shader-files` metallib until iOS virtual address space is gone.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, 0100F2C0115B6000, 1.4.3 (v720896)

### nxnative commit

82c354b

### Shader chain version

5ea15f2c8240

### How it was built and run

iPhone or iPad, unsigned IPA from build_ipa_from_nsp.py

Packed with `--romfs separate --shader-files` and installed with Sideloadly.

### Device and OS

iPhone 17 Pro Max (iPhone18,2, Apple A19 Pro), 11.42 GB RAM, 512 GB, iOS 27.2.1 (24B156)

### Settings and environment overrides

Failing runs:
- Settings screen: Metal 4 pipelines off, Pipeline prebuild off (`DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`). No `Documents/env.txt`.
- Also reproduced with Metal 4 pipelines on and Pipeline prebuild off (`DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`).

Working workaround:
- `Documents/env.txt`:
  ```
  DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off
  ```

### Logs

Excerpts from `log.prev.txt` / `log.txt` in the app container (a launch with both toggles off). Full logs on request; nothing attached contains game files.

```
pipeline prepare: 7052 of 26456 lines done after 0.5 s, the progress screen shows
[RED] failed to load shader … mmap failed
… (257 unique metallib paths under msl/b-5ea15f2c8240/)
[dm] CRASH sig=6
```

Address space at crash: 449.93 GB in 11,824 regions, largest free 0.00 GB, physical footprint 0.82 GB of 11.42 GB RAM, ~53.8 GB disk free. Backtrace in the host abort: `__warm_prepare_block_invoke` → `warm_task` → `pso_build_ex` → `pso_build_dev`.

I used an assistant to pull the device logs and summarize the numbers; the logs and the `DM_PSO_MANIFEST=off` workaround were checked on the device.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: Tears of the Kingdom (0100F2C0115B6000) on iPhone 17 Pro Max: startup prewarm of a large pso_user.tsv exhausts virtual address space with --shader-files

body:
## What happened

Nine Sols crashes with `sig=11` inside the game's own code every time its movie player stops. It boots, plays the opening movie at a locked 60 fps, and dies at the movie → gameplay handoff. **3 runs, 3 crashes, always the same PC.**

Skipping the intro does not avoid it: a second, shorter movie (473 packets) stops the same way and crashes at the same instruction.

## What you expected

The movie ends and gameplay starts.

## Game, title ID and version

Nine Sols, `0100D810170D0000`, update v65536 (display 1.1), no DLC. There is no profile for this title in `dm/games/`, so it runs on the **provisional profile** the survey generated (`profile_guess.py`).

## nxnative commit

`1db4bcb28b59`

## Shader chain version

`5ea15f2c8240`

## How it was built and run

iPhone or iPad, unsigned IPA from `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios` (RomFS bundled, `--icon`), signed and run in LiveContainer. `unzip -t` on the IPA: no errors. `stubs=0` at boot.

## Device and OS

iPad Pro M4 (iPad16,3), 8 GB, iPadOS 26 or later — the log takes the iOS 27 `deviceMotionBody` path. `Metal device Apple M4 GPU`.

## Settings and environment overrides

None. No `Documents/env.txt`, settings screen at defaults.

## Logs

`log.txt` and `log.prev.txt` (both crashing runs) plus `bug_report.py`'s `report.md`:

https://gist.github.com/ShubhxYT/ffa7e8f77887bca2ceefb1efd0e58c7a

Nothing there contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

## What the logs show

All three runs fault at the same instruction reading a null:

```
log.txt      L523  [dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0  pc=main+0x7959f0 lr=main+0x7959ac
log.prev.txt L889  [dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0  pc=main+0x7959f0 lr=main+0x7959ac
earlier run        [dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0  pc=main+0x7959f0 lr=main+0x7959ac
```

Run after skipping the intro (shorter movie, 66 s in):

```
[dm] [movie] Flush
[dm] [movie] Stop
[dm] [movie] decoder 0x70fc40ed50 destroyed: 473 packets in, 465 frames out; decoded 473 packets, average 3.84 ms per packet, longest 23.35 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 2979 (66.34 s) whole frame 61.7 ms, submit+present 0.1 ms, GPU 0.5 ms
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=main+0x7959f0 lr=main+0x7959ac sp=0x171f163f0
x0=0 x1=0x2 x2=0x8 x3=0x206 x4=0 x5=0x1244a5d94
```

Run with the full opening movie (169 s in):

```
[dm] [movie] decoder 0x70fc9dfe20 destroyed: 3375 packets in, 3375 frames out; decoded 3375 packets, average 4.27 ms per packet, longest 28.85 ms
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=main+0x7959f0 lr=main+0x7959ac sp=0x16fe523f0
```

Decoder configuration in both: `type 2 output 4 mode 1`, VP8 through `libvpx v1.17.0`, 1920×1080.

It is not memory, and nothing was missing by name:

- `[mem] guest memory: memory pool 3.21 GB and the host's margin 1.60 GB (half the pool), room to the memory limit 7.96 GB, DM_GUEST_FILE unset: anonymous`
- `on-screen up to frame 9300: 300 frames, dropped 0 … footprint 1232 MiB`
- `headroom to the system memory limit 7199 MB`
- `stubs=0`, and no `[RED]` line anywhere in either run
- steady `frame time p50 16.67 ms` / `p99 16.67 ms`

This looks like [Video decoded off the caller's thread](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/movies.md#video-decoded-off-the-callers-thread) in shape — a crash right after `[movie] Stop` and `decoder … destroyed` — but not in character: that entry's residual failure is 2 in 12 runs, while this is 3 for 3 at the same PC with the same null register. So it reads more like a deterministic state or return-value mismatch at teardown than the residual race.

## One observation that may narrow it

The same title ran on macOS for 10,662 s (639,900 frames) with **zero `[movie]` lines** in the log — the movie library was never entered at all. On iOS it is entered immediately and the crash follows. If that Mac session simply never triggered a cutscene, the observation means nothing; if the Mac path avoided `movie::Decoder` entirely, that difference may be the whole bug.

## What I can capture next

Happy to rerun with `DM_MOVIE_TRACE=1`, with `DM_PROBE` around the caller of `main+0x7959f0`, with a Mac build from the same commit against the same point, or with `--prepare-xcode` for a non-LiveContainer install — whichever would help most.

## No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

body:
### What is missing

Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072) draws its 3D at 1920x1080 docked even with Dynamic resolution off, while its output is 2560x1440. There is no switch to raise it: `DM_GFX_SCALE` is already at tier 0 (the top), `DM_RENDER_SCALE` needs a render-scale stub this game does not have, and `DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION` only goes down.

The size is data, not code. A one-float change to a RomFS file, served through `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY`, renders the 3D at native 2560x1440 with no rebuild and no host change, and holds 60 fps on an M4 Max.

### Where the size comes from

`Pack/Bootup.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.pack.zs` (zstd with dictionary ID 4 from `Pack/ZsDic.pack.zs`, a SARC) holds `System/GameGraphics/ModelSceneExtensionParam/Default.game__gfx__ModelSceneExtensionParam.bgyml` (BYML v7, 3,672 bytes). Its `ResolutionParam` and `DynamicResolutionParam` are hash-keyed maps:

| `ResolutionParam` entry | BaseResolution / FinalImageResolution | `ResolutionLevelPaletteType` | Level 0 scale | 3D size at level 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#d30fdb96`, `#eeb1db9f` (docked) | 2560x1440 | `0x2ebeca77` | 0.75 | 1920x1080 |
| `#0b46e9da` (handheld) | 1920x1080 | `0x90e0a495` | 0.75 | 1440x810 |

- Palette `0x2ebeca77`: 10 levels, 0.75, 0.71112, 0.66667, 0.62223, 0.58334, 0.53334, 0.5, 0.4445, 0.37223, 0.33334; `LoadThreshold` 95, `ReduceCounterMax` 2, `IncreaseCounterMax` 30.
- Palette `0x90e0a495`: the first 8 of those; `LoadThreshold` 108, `ReduceCounterMax` 3, `IncreaseCounterMax` 30.

The game's draw size is level scale × BaseResolution, which matches the sizes in the game note and in #1653 (1920x1080 docked, 1440x810 handheld). With the profile's dynamic-resolution stub returning level 0 (Dynamic resolution off), level 0's `ResolutionReduceScale` alone sets the 3D size. `gsys/ModelSceneConfigParam/Main…bgyml`'s `BaseResoWidth/Height` (1280x720) is not the size the game draws at.

### What was changed

Only `DynamicResolutionLevelParamList.0.ResolutionReduceScale`, 0.75 → 1.0, in both palettes. It is an inline float, so the member keeps its size: the SARC was patched in place and recompressed with the same dictionary (dictionary ID written in the frame), then placed at `<overlay>/Pack/Bootup.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.pack.zs` with `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY=<overlay>` in the Mac app's `env.txt`. BaseResolution, FinalImageResolution and the other levels are unchanged, so the output stays 2560x1440 and the game's upscaler (NDSR) runs 2560x1440 → 2560x1440.

### Measurements

Mac app from the v131072 NUP, main `e4b0d9b7`, chain `a9bfaeb9fa8c`, Apple M4 Max (64 GB), docked. `scripts/bench.py`, route `field-still` (a save in a Goron City room, standing still, window 85-265 s), one run per variant, `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP=every:1800`:

| Variant | Most frequent pass target | fps | frame p50 / p99 | GPU p50 / p95 | dropped | over budget | red lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 1920x1080 (183), 960x540, 480x270 | 59.5 | 16.66 / 17.41 ms | 7.11 / 7.66 ms | 17 | 52 | 1 |
| overlay, level 0 = 1.0 | **2560x1440** (217), 1280x720, 640x360 | 59.7 | 16.66 / 17.29 ms | 8.76 / 9.39 ms | 6 | 16 | 1 |

- The one red line is the same in both runs and not new: `stage 5 cb3 has no uniform buffer bound: shader a039399e6336de1b_b`.
- The half and quarter buffers follow the base (960x540 → 1280x720, 480x270 → 640x360).
- Screenshots at 200 s show visibly finer detail at 1440p (the grate, Link's hair, the Goron's face). No artefacts were seen.
- Played afterwards with the launcher's defaults and with `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx` + `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`. Both looked clearly better than stock; MetalFX was preferred by eye. Likely reasons: NDSR is tuned to reconstruct from a smaller input, and the display is larger than 2560x1440.

Not tested: outdoor areas (Hyrule Field, Kokiri Forest), cutscenes, long sessions, memory on 16 GB Macs (the render targets grow by 1.78×), the iPhone, handheld mode, MetalFX's GPU cost at this size, raising BaseResolution or FinalImageResolution for 4K.

### What you propose

For the dev to consider; nothing here is a pull request.

1. A launcher choice for this game, for example "Native resolution", that puts level 0 at 1.0. Either serve the patched member from the profile as a RomFS overlay built from the game's own file at pack time (no game data in the repository), or have the host answer the scale where the game reads `ResolutionReduceScale` / the level function returns. The dynamic-resolution stub in `patches.py` already sits at the level function.
2. Off by default until it has been checked outdoors and on smaller Macs. With Dynamic resolution on, the levels below 0 would still start from the new top.
3. Possibly general: other games on this engine (`game__gfx__ModelSceneExtensionParam`, Tears of the Kingdom's layout; #2290's comment describes TOTK's `ResolutionParam`) may cap their 3D the same way. A tool that reads `ResolutionParam` and the level palettes from the RomFS would show which titles draw below their output.
4. Related: #2290 (host-side internal resolution for every NVN game) would give more than 1× of the output. This data change gives at most 1×, but needs no host or chain change.

### Platforms

Mac (tested). iPhone and iPad not tested.
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072): native 2560x1440 3D docked from one RomFS value (ResolutionReduceScale level 0 0.75 → 1.0), 60 fps on an M4 Max

body:
**PRAGMATA (0400C76024710000) was listed as not tested on iOS. It runs.** With the alias region overridden it gets past the startup fault we reported to ourselves for weeks, and then reaches a steady ~30 fps with judder from present pacing. Below is everything measured, on an iPhone with an A20 Pro (12 GB RAM, iOS 27.2), build `b3fe7770`, package v196608, DLC `0400c76024711001`.

## 1. The startup crash was the alias region, exactly as README.md says

What we saw before any tuning:

```
fs RomFS image ...: 7 entries
CRASH sig=11 addr=0x10 pc=main+0x788f0
```

Identical with an update-only extract and with the complete package, so it was never missing files. The RomFS layout was right all along (`natives/NSW2/`, `runtime.args`, `re_chunk_000.pak` + 2 patches).

The 7-entry mount plus an immediate `sig=11` at the same PC reads as: the game asks for its 32 GB mapping, the 4.38 GB iPhone alias region refuses it, and the next instruction dereferences the null it got back. README.md already says the game reaches alias +38.41 GB and that the iPhone layout is not enough — the crash is that sentence happening.

**Fix, one env line, no code change:**

```
DM_ALIAS_SIZE=42949672960
```

That is 40 GB of alias region instead of the platform's 4.38 GB on iOS. With it the game boots, mounts the RomFS, plays the opening, and runs for tens of thousands of frames. It has not crashed once in five separate sessions.

If iOS is meant to run this title at all, the profile probably wants this in its own notes — or the iOS default alias region wants to be sized from the profile's declared reach rather than the platform default. Either way, `DM_ALIAS_SIZE` is the workaround and it works.

## 2. It then runs at ~30 fps, GPU-bound

Console mode, 60 Hz display link, no pipeline archive:

```
frame time p50 29.91 / p95 34.68 / max 179.45 ms
GPU p50 28.82 / p95 33.11 / max 44.75 ms
NVN submit+present p50 8.51 ms
footprint 2.8–3.3 GB, thermal 2
```

The GPU sits at 29 ms against the 33.3 ms a locked 30 would need. That is a Switch 2 title on a phone and it is not unreasonable — but it means every heavier scene falls off the edge rather than degrading gracefully.

## 3. What we tried, and what each one did (measured, not guessed)

| key | expectation | measured result |
|---|---|---|
| `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` | lock 30 | **no effect** — no `frame step` lines at all; this engine paces itself |
| `DM_RENDER_SCALE=0.75` | −44 % GPU | **no effect** — GPU p50 unchanged at 27.5–31 ms; accepted as a key but the profile has no render-scale stub |
| `DM_PRESENT_HZ=30` | steady 30 Hz presents | **worse** — `old frames dropped by merging 293–1,099 per 300 ticks`; the game presents at 60 |
| `DM_OPMODE=0` | fewer pixels | **worse** — GPU p50 rose from 28.8 to 34.4 ms; handheld gives a power-saving guest profile, so it is slower, not cheaper |

## 4. The judder we cannot tune away

What the player reports: normal motion, then roughly half a second of too-fast motion, at intervals. The display-link counters show the mechanism:

```
display link up to tick N: ticks 300, presents 301, empty ticks 13–33
old frames dropped by merging 0–1
submission ahead of target display p50 32.9–33.2 ms, min −25.3 ms
frame time p50 28–30 ms, p95 45–58 ms
```

The game delivers frames unevenly — anywhere from ~20 to ~58 ms — while the host takes the newest queued frame each 60 Hz tick. A late frame leaves an empty tick; an early one lands on back-to-back ticks. Average frame rate is fine; the *cadence* is not, and that is what reads as lurching.

Pipelines are not involved: `new pipelines 0` on every long frame, and `pipeline prepare: the prewarm lists hold nothing to build` — the profile ships no manifest, so there is nothing to prebuild even if we wanted to.

Related: #2432 (shader library size), #2664 (compute loop after exit), #2624 (4x depth-only passes). None of them is the boot fault below — this is the iOS side of the title, which README.md lists as untested.

## Questions

1. Should the iOS alias region be derived from the profile's declared reach? `DM_ALIAS_SIZE` works, but requiring a guess at 40 GB to launch a supported title seems like a gap worth closing in the profile.
2. Is the present pacing judder a known iOS characteristic, or is there a setting that makes the link take the *oldest* queued frame instead of the newest (`DM_PRESENT_FIFO=0` looked like it, but we did not want to stack another variable before reporting)?
3. Would a prewarm manifest for this profile be possible? There is nothing to capture for `DM_PSO_PREBUILD_OUT` today.

Happy to run any experiment you want on the device — it is a spare phone with exactly one title installed, so a broken build costs nothing but a reinstall.
title: PRAGMATA (0400C76024710000) on iOS: runs with DM_ALIAS_SIZE=40G, then judder from present pacing, not pipelines

# Bug: `pack_app.py` fails with `NameError: name 'romfs_rows' is not defined`

## Summary

The macOS app packaging script fails during the GameData packaging step because `romfs_rows` is referenced without ever being initialized.

This appears to be a regression introduced by commit `52ca101d0a565f5202377a06376c4a3adbd82927` (November 16, 2026), which added support for packing additional program RomFS files for Switch 2 Edition NUP packages.

## Environment

- Platform: macOS
- Script: `dm/mac/pack_app.py`
- Repository: nxnative
- Affected commit: `52ca101d`
- Game being packaged: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
- Package type: Switch 2 Edition NUP

## Error

The packaging process completes the following steps:

```text
step: launcher and host (clones of the game files)
step: shader libraries
step: pipeline archive
```

It then fails with:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "dm/mac/pack_app.py", line 563, in <module>
    pack(parse(sys.argv[1:]))
  File "dm/mac/pack_app.py", line 489, in pack
    place('GameData', rtop, 'game files', romfs_rows,
          lambda d: copy([romfs], d, clone['romfs']))
NameError: name 'romfs_rows' is not defined
```

## Cause

The November 16 change modified the packaging logic and introduced the `sib` and `trees['programs']` variables to support additional program RomFS files.

However, the main RomFS packaging code still references `romfs_rows`:

```python
rtop = 'romfs.img' if romfs.is_file() else 'romfs'
place('GameData', rtop, 'game files', romfs_rows,
      lambda d: copy([romfs], d, clone['romfs']))
```

The variable is also referenced later:

```python
if romfs.is_file():
    note(romfs, [str(romfs), *romfs_rows[0][1:]],
         bundled('GameData', rtop))
```

There is no assignment to `romfs_rows` anywhere in the function.

The previous implementation passed `inventory(romfs)` directly to `place()`. The November 16 change appears to have omitted the corresponding assignment when the packaging logic was updated.

## Suggested Fix

Initialize `romfs_rows` using the existing `inventory()` function before its first use:

```python
romfs_rows = inventory(romfs)
rtop = 'romfs.img' if romfs.is_file() else 'romfs'
place('GameData', rtop, 'game files', romfs_rows,
      lambda d: copy([romfs], d, clone['romfs']))
```

This also restores the metadata required by the later `note()` call.

## Verification

Adding the single initialization line:

```python
romfs_rows = inventory(romfs)
```

resolves the `NameError` at the source level.

The local change passes:

```text
git diff --check
```

The change does not modify the existing shader packaging, pipeline archive, or additional-program RomFS handling.

## Expected Behavior

The macOS packaging process should complete the GameData step and continue through app signing and final app bundle creation without raising a `NameError` for `romfs_rows`.

## Actual Behavior

Packaging terminates with a NameError after the shader libraries and pipeline archive have been processed.
title: Bug: pack_app.py fails with NameError: name 'romfs_rows' is not defined

## Symptom
Fate/hollow ataraxia REMASTERED (010070E022546000), display version 1.0.2, can return to the title with Continue after Save & Title, but entering Entrance shows empty slots. This is separate from the OpenGL bring-up in #2818 / #2819.

Tested on the macOS host at 1db4bcb2, using an externally generated provisional profile. Main build ID: 6c16aa06a25504cee9cf0f4f7b5e615c. The analogous symptom was reported on iPhone, but the instrumentation and A/B below were performed on Mac only.

## Reproduction
1. Use a writable COPY of an existing save directory, with cloud sync disabled for the isolated test.
2. Load/play, then select Save & Title; confirm the title's Continue state.
3. Enter Entrance and confirm the transition: the slots appear empty.
4. Start a fresh process from a copy of the committed save taken BEFORE entering Entrance: slots still appear empty.

## File-level evidence
Temporary instrumentation recorded the actual filesystem APIs, their results, offsets, byte counts, and snapshots of the save write buffers. It was not just a path-resolution trace.

- Save & Title: CreateFile on an existing file returns EEXIST, OpenFile mode 7 succeeds, SetFileSize(0) is followed by complete writes, CloseFile and a successful atomic Commit. The final observed write is 8,849 bytes to udat_rel.bin.
- That write buffer and the committed file are byte-identical (SHA-256 797e3f94c847e9ac5abb102ebebedff4c2730c352e4d39771b38d6afb2caa87a).
- In this specific Entrance transition window there is no ReadFile of the save; the game rewrites and commits another 8,849-byte serialization. The file is not left empty. This observation is not a promise that every Entrance path performs no reads.
- A fresh process from the pre-Entrance snapshot completely reads back the same 8,849 bytes (same hash), yet still shows empty slots. This rules out a lost host write and shows that the Entrance rewrite is not necessary to reproduce the hidden slots.

## Slot-filter evidence (this main build only)
The slot population path setHollowSlotInfo checks a cached hollow/check_savedata_version boolean. The config getter defaults to true when no config value is available. In the inspected process the smash::fw::config::Config object's handle at +0x30 is NULL.

At main+0xdf879c the code searches the Thumbnail description at +0x80 for a space; at +0xdf87ac it calls atoi on that position; at +0xdf87b0 it compares the result with 0x1b6 (438). A lower value skips adding that entry to the valid-slot list when the check is enabled. One persisted description is "119 2 2", so that parsed value is 2. The serialized record also contains a timestamp, completion percentage and a screenshot name; these are not absent just because the UI is empty.

Controlled A/B: restart from a COPY of the SAME pre-Entrance committed save. In the diagnostic host only, set the cached check false at main+0x7efd448 and its initialization flag at main+0x7efd450. Two slots then display date, completion, play time and COPY/DELETE; selecting a slot restores Continue. No save-version number was edited. These offsets are observations for the exact build above, NOT a proposed unconditional host patch.

## What is still open
- Why is the local configuration unavailable in this port? Trace Config::load -> purchase::createConfigFile -> Util::readAll2, including the resolved path, mount and returned bytes.
- What is the intended check value for this release, and why is the description's parsed value below the threshold? The parsed integer should not yet be assumed to be a documented SavedataVersion field.
- Fix the configuration loading / underlying host behavior if incorrect, instead of disabling a general integrity check or fabricating a version of 438.
- Validate an eventual fix on Mac (cold restart and Save & Title -> Entrance -> slot load) and independently on iPhone.

## Scope / safety
No production fix is deployed. The temporary I/O audit and runtime bypass are not proposed for merging into hle_fs.c. Original saves were not changed; all experiments used isolated copies. No ROMs, decrypted game files, save contents or personal paths are attached.

The earlier hypothesis that the slots require a game-operated cloud service was not supported by this experiment. A missing timestamp path alone also does not prove a failed read: the observed timestamp operation was DeleteFile. A path resolver's success label is not an OpenFile or ReadFile result.
title: Fate/hollow ataraxia 1.0.2: persisted saves hidden in Entrance by version filter

body: ### What happened Packing Breath of the Wild (base + 1.9.0) as a Mac app stops at the shader split, every time, since 8d62601: the split shader tables differ from game profile 01007EF00011E000's: shader_map.tsv: 11 row(s) only in the profile, 11 only in the split profile: vs_main.bin 0 vertex 21fe759b8114941c main#BNSH@0x1d7a000#var2 split: vs_main.bin 0 vertex 21fe759b8114941c main#BNSH@0x1d7a000#var0 The same game files packed fine with f43284e (2026-11-13). The keys are identical; only the labels differ. Cause: 8d62601 ("nvn/raytracing: run Welcome Tour's native ray modules on Metal") changed the main scan in dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py from results.append(('main', {skey(c, k): (w, s, c, k) for w, s, c, k in found}, var_pairs(found), {})) # last duplicate wins to results.append(('main', uniq_keys(found), var_pairs(found), {})) # setdefault: first duplicate wins BotW's main BNSH at 0x1d7a000 holds some shaders in more than one variation, so those 11 keys are now labelled with the first variation (#var0) instead of the one dm/games/01007EF00011E000/shader_map.tsv registers (#var2 etc.). ### What happened

Building **Hello Kitty Island Adventure** stops at the rewrite step, every time:

```
[RED] main: Unity internal calls (3178): targetFrameRate at 0xb151f38, [RED] vSyncCount getter at 0x1c4d170 not read
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../dm/tools/patch_nso.py", line 1426, in <module>
    assert tgt, f'jump table {ins.address:x}'
AssertionError: jump table 478a7b4
```

Command: `build_ipa_from_nsp.py <input folder> -k prod.keys --platform mac-app`. It is the same assertion on the experimental engine (pin 94a09447, line 1641) at the same address, and on the same game's 3.0.0 update it moves to `4a521d4`, so it is not one bad package.

**The `br x18` at `0x478a7b4` is not a jump table but an IL2CPP virtual-method thunk**, which the engine already describes in `docs/reference/rewriter.md` under *Unframed pointer tail calls followed by zero trap padding*. Disassembly of `main` (`0x478a770..0x478a7c0`):

```
0x478a770  120c40f9  ldr  x18, [x0, #0x18]
0x478a77c            str / ldr / ldp / stp / mov   <- 17 instructions moving stack arguments
0x478a7b4  40021fd6  br   x18
0x478a7b8  1f2003d5  nop
0x478a7bc  1f2003d5  nop
```

The only difference from the documented form is the padding. This compiler pads with `nop` (`0x1f2003d5`); `tail_call_padded` accepts only `udf #0` (`0x00000000`):

```python
if j + 1 >= len(insl) or any(p.mnemonic != 'udf' or p.op_str != '#0' for p in insl[j + 1:]): return False
```

So the test fails, control falls through to the offset-table forms, and the assertion fires. `tail_call_at_end` cannot take it either: the `br` is not the last decoded instruction (`at_end=False`).

**One-line fix**, accept `nop` as padding too:

```diff
-    if j + 1 >= len(insl) or any(p.mnemonic != 'udf' or p.op_str != '#0' for p in insl[j + 1:]): return False
+    if j + 1 >= len(insl) or any(not ((p.mnemonic == 'udf' and p.op_str == '#0') or p.mnemonic == 'nop')
+                                 for p in insl[j + 1:]): return False
```

Nothing else changes, and the rule is not loosened: `nop` does nothing, exactly like `udf #0`, and every other condition stays as written (contiguous decoding, only `mov` / `ldr` / `ldrh` / `ldp` / `add` / `str` / `stp`, no writes to `sp` / `fp` / `lr` / `x29` / `x30` including the 32-bit aliases and writeback, the last write of `x18` a plain pointer load). The only thing that differs is the padding the compiler chose.

Checked on that instruction list on its own: `tail_call_padded(insl, 17)` returns `False` before the change and `True` after it. The *Unframed pointer tail calls followed by zero trap padding* entry in `docs/reference/rewriter.md` would then want "zero trap padding" widened to "padding that does nothing (`udf #0` or `nop`)".

Current `main` still tests only `udf #0` (`dm/tools/patch_nso.py`, `tail_call_padded`), so this case looks uncovered today.

No game files, keys or extracted data are attached or quoted; the disassembly above is one 20-instruction window of address arithmetic.

### What you expected

The thunk at `0x478a7b4` is taken as an indirect tail call and the rewrite carries on. With the one-line change it does: the rewrite log finishes with `br_call: 8`, and the rest of the build passes (heap check, address ranges, 12,087 shaders, the Mac host). The app starts and reaches the main menu at a steady 30 fps (frame time p50 33.34 ms, no drops in 300 frames, saves written), so the package itself is fine, only this padding form is missing from the rule.

### Game, title ID and version

Hello Kitty Island Adventure, 010027901C89C000, 2.17.2 (v1310720), no DLC. The same game's 3.0.0 (v1441792) hits the same assertion at 0x4a521d4.

ccd834e06a39 (the engine NX2Apple 1.4.0 ships). The experimental engine 94a0944755 fails the same way.

d24f05cf9d78 (stable engine), 19d183a2b462 (experimental)

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

Mac18,5, Apple M6, macOS 27.2.1

none (the command above was run as listed, no env.txt and no DM_* variables)

### Logs

`<title ID>_build/logs/rewrite_main.log`, whole. The `[DIAG]` lines and the trailing `main {... br_call: 8 ...}` line come from the run with the one-line change plus a temporary print of the rejected window; the unpatched run stops at the assertion quoted above, and its console output ends with `[RED] patch_nso.py exit code 1 on main`.

**Symptom.** Over Ocarina of Time's opening movie (the night sky, then the title screen over the field), small green and grey vertical-striped blocks appear, with faint vertical banding over large parts of the picture. The blocks move from frame to frame. Screenshots are in the first comment.

**Setup.** 16 GB M2 MacBook Air, macOS 27.0. Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072). Host: main 44d67fbe plus a few open PRs (#2889, #2484, #2495, #2771, #2545, #2635, #2901). Cold start, no input, to frame 4500, warm pipeline archive. Handheld 1440x810, cap 30, `DM_NDVE_ENGINE=1 DM_GUEST_FILE=1 DM_RT_PRESENT=1 DM_FRAME_WG=1 DM_PRESENT_LINK=0`.

**What the log shows in this run**
1. During the background prewarm, Apple's shader compiler service died: `XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED`, 9 times.
2. Two compute pipelines were never created (`d15370a382630d4e_b`, `e6be82d835fbe4d3_b`), so their dispatches are skipped.
3. When the movie starts, the NDVE engine reports:
   `[RED] NDVE engine: a dispatch out of the network's order at 9442573ee4ace011_b after 3 of the network's dispatches were skipped; the engine is off from now on`
4. The game's own network then runs with those dispatches still missing. That fits the blocks: part of the network's output is never written.

The AV1 decode itself looks healthy (1920x1080, ~59 pictures a second).

**Open (untested, not bisected)**
- Is the compiler-service crash the trigger, or does the grid also show when every pipeline builds?
- Two host gaps either way: a compute pipeline that fails on an XPC interruption isn't retried later, and once the NDVE engine turns off, the game's network runs with dispatches missing.
- Related: #2900 (the same compiler crash poisoning the pipeline archive).

We aren't working on a fix right now; we can attach the run log on request.

body:
## Summary

The Continuous integration section of `docs/development.md` says the supported CI toolchain is Xcode 27.1. Both workflows that select Xcode explicitly select 27.2, and the README, compiler helper and Metal lock agree with the workflows. The developer guide therefore gives conflicting toolchain information.

## Runtime or environment

Verified by reading a fresh checkout of `main` at commit `f3e53afe42c36ccc53883dfec94d22f27cf2348c`. The repository has no published releases. This is a documentation comparison; no game build or Xcode 27.1 execution was performed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the checkout above, read `docs/development.md:166-172` under Continuous integration.
2. Compare `.github/workflows/tests.yml:21-25` and `.github/workflows/lint-c.yml:31-32`.
3. Compare `README.md:44,58,60`, `dm/gfx/tools/own_compilers.py:13` and `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock:5-6`.

These inspection steps were performed. No game, title ID, device run, environment override or gameplay log is applicable to this documentation-only report; no game files or keys are attached.

## Expected behavior

The developer guide's description of the supported CI Xcode version agrees with the explicitly selected workflow toolchain and the project's current build requirements.

## Actual behavior

The guide says:

```text
docs/development.md:166 All five macOS jobs, including the sanitizer job, run with the toolchain the
docs/development.md:167 project supports: Xcode 27.1 on GitHub's `xcode-27` image, named by path in
```

The workflow selections are:

```text
.github/workflows/tests.yml:25   DEVELOPER_DIR: /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
.github/workflows/lint-c.yml:32   DEVELOPER_DIR: /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app/Contents/Developer
```

The lock records `Apple metal version 32023.922 (metalfe-32023.922.4)` for both SDKs. The compiler helper names Xcode 27.2, compares each present Metal compiler's version string against that lock, and reports an error for a mismatch unless the explicit override is enabled (`own_compilers.py:41-52,70-74`). Thus a different compiler is rejected by the default gate. A developer installing 27.1 after reading the guide could hit that gate; this consequence is an inference, not a locally executed build failure.

## Evidence

- Expected source: [workflow selection](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/f3e53afe42c36ccc53883dfec94d22f27cf2348c/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L21-L25), the C lint selection quoted above, and the README build requirements at the listed lines.
- Failure source: [developer guide](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/f3e53afe42c36ccc53883dfec94d22f27cf2348c/docs/development.md#L166-L172) still names the previous version.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

The evidence is the checked-out documentation, workflows, helper and lock. Runtime reproduction was not run; the complete documentation defect follows directly from the conflicting version declarations for the same CI toolchain. The compiler-gate consequence is separately qualified above.

## Restoration check

Read the same guide paragraph and workflow selections again: the guide must name the same supported Xcode version as the workflows, README and helper. Preserve the existing compiler lock and default version check; accepting an unsupported compiler would not restore the documentation contract.

## References

- https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1043 — the open CI scheduling change already includes the 27.1-to-27.2 wording correction, but that correction is absent from current main; no scheduling change is needed to close this documentation report.
- https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/421 — historical introduction of the supported-toolchain CI setup; the guide still describes its previous version.
- https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/782 — concerns compiler compatibility and a proposed newer-compiler policy, whereas this report concerns the guide disagreeing with the currently selected toolchain.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The directly verified defect is conflicting documentation wording. No build failure caused by following this paragraph was executed or observed, so this report does not claim consequential runtime impact.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The current README and explicit workflow selections consistently name Xcode 27.2; a reader can use those sources to resolve the contradiction without changing code or weakening the compiler gate.
title: fix(docs): CI guide still names Xcode 27.1 while workflows select 27.2

body:
Splatoon Raiders (`0400380020056000`, update v65536 from a NUP, no DLC) stopped building on the Mac after 8d62601f ("nvn/raytracing: run Welcome Tour's native ray modules on Metal"). That commit causes two separate failures. Both have small fixes, given below.

## 1. Shader split: the profile's `shader_map.tsv` no longer matches

```
✗ [4/6] shader split (0:51)
[RED] the split shader tables differ from game profile 0400380020056000's:
shader_map.tsv: 36 row(s) only in the profile, 36 only in the split
  profile: vs_main.bin    0    vertex    827f495b663a3c57    main#BNSH@0x4c98000#var2
  split:   vs_main.bin    0    vertex    827f495b663a3c57    main#BNSH@0x4c98000#var0
```

**Cause:** 8d62601f changed how `main` merges its keys in `shader_split.py`:

```diff
-        results.append(('main', {skey(c, k): (w, s, c, k) for w, s, c, k in found}, var_pairs(found), {}))
+        results.append(('main', uniq_keys(found), var_pairs(found), {}))
```

The dict comprehension kept the **last** copy of a repeated key. `uniq_keys` keeps the **first** copy, as every RomFS file already did, and it also checks that the copies match. Splatoon Raiders' `main` BNSHs (`@0x4c98000`, `@0x4c9f000`) repeat 22 of their 40 keys. The key set is unchanged, but column 5 now names an earlier variation for those 22 (`#var2` → `#var0`, `#var28` → `#var0` and so on). Because rows are ordered by source, 14 more `ps_main.bin` / `vs_main.bin` rows change only their `index`: 36 rows in all. The profile's tables were last split on 2026-11-10 (5d61592f), before this change.

**Fix:** register the new split's `shader_map.tsv` in the profile, as 5d61592f did. The diff is exactly the 36 `ps_main.bin` / `vs_main.bin` rows plus the column-5 header line from 90b7cefd. `shader_facts.tsv`, `shader_pairs.tsv` and `pso_pairs.tsv` from the new split are byte-identical to the profile's. With the re-registered table, the split passes (27,192 shaders).

**Other games:** any profile whose `main` repeats a shader key is probably affected the same way. I did not check any other profile.

## 2. Mac shaders: `IndexError` in `dmsh_build.py` `job_for`

With the split fixed, the Mac shader build stops after about 1,655 of 27,192 shaders:

```
  File "dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py", line 991, in translate
    for k in miss: jobs[k], c1s[k] = job_for(k, loc[k][0], rec_of(k)[1], wb)
  File "dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py", line 417, in job_for
    if dmsh_ampere.is_nvn2(rec[ci:]) and rec[ci + 0x56] == 8:
                                         ~~~^^^^^^^^^^^
IndexError: index out of range
[RED] own_compilers.py exit code 1
```

**Cause:** the stage-8 RT check that 8d62601f added reads control byte `0x56`. `dmsh_ampere.is_nvn2` accepts any section of at least `0x48` bytes, so a record whose NVN2 control section is shorter than `0x57` bytes goes out of range. `shader_split.py` already guards this byte (`len(ctl) > 0x56`, in `nvn2_stage` and `same_shader`).

**Fix:**

```diff
-    if dmsh_ampere.is_nvn2(rec[ci:]) and rec[ci + 0x56] == 8:
+    if dmsh_ampere.is_nvn2(rec[ci:]) and len(rec) > ci + 0x56 and rec[ci + 0x56] == 8:
```

This changes the chain version, so `dmsh_chain.h` needs regenerating (`dmsh_chain.py --header`).

**Which record:** exactly one of the 27,192: key `22fff9012db5acaa` (`vs_other.bin` index 81, `/Lib/agl/agl_resource.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.debug.sarc.zs/agl_common.sharcb#BAHS@0x27ea4`), an agl BAHS vertex shader whose NVN2 control section is `0x50` bytes; every other one is at least `0xe0`. It has been in the profile since c8521eeb. `ci` is correct: in every record it equals `0x38` + the code length, which `shader_split.py` also checks when it writes the package. So the guard is the fix, not a mask over a wrong `ci`.

A rebuild with the guard is in progress and has gone past the earlier failure point without a traceback. I'll add a comment when it finishes.

## Environment

- nxnative `b2e52b37` (main), Mac-only build (`nxplay --rebuild --build-only`)
- macOS on Apple silicon

body:
**Ocarina of Time on an M2 MacBook Air: occasional GPU hangs (vertex-stage firmware lockup) since main moved past 0def324d.**

Setup: 16 GB M2 MacBook Air (10-core GPU), macOS 27.0, Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072), handheld 1440x810, cap 30, guest files on, `DM_RT_PRESENT=1 DM_FRAME_WG=1`. Our build: main 44d67fbe plus a few open PRs (#2889, #2484, #2495, #2771, #2545, #2635, #2901), scripted Kokiri walk loop to frame 45,000 (~25 min).

**Symptom**
- About once per 25-minute run, a command buffer fails:
  `[RED] command buffer error … MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=1 "Caused GPU Hang Error (00000003:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)"`.
- Usually the game recovers (one frame lost, a visible hitch). Twice in quick succession, Metal stops accepting work and the host aborts in `front_gpu_lost`; that happened in 1 of 6 runs.
- macOS writes one `gpuEvent-dmhost` report per hang in /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports. All 8 are identical: "firmware-detected lockup", signature 577, with the tiler/vertex stage busy and fragment and compute idle.

**Numbers** (run logs over three days, same Mac, same route family)

| Build | Frames | Hangs |
|---|---|---|
| main 44d67fbe + the PRs above | ~121k | 9 (in 5 of 6 runs) |
| main 0def324d + carries (incl. #2484/#2495, #2771, and #2889 on its own ~39k frames) | ~700k | 0 |
| main b06f4e0e | ~154k | 0 |

The PRs in our build were run for hundreds of thousands of frames on the 0def324d base without a hang, and #2889 only changes fragment shaders, while the lockup is in the vertex stage. So the change looks to be in main's range **0def324d..44d67fbe** (108 commits). Candidates by reading, not tested:
- 6dad3406: MSL 3.2 for every shader (a BAR.SYNC now kept in object/mesh shaders);
- d7877c50 (#2308): mesh-stage memory in a leased slice;
- 69e7b11b, c8c58e6c: vertex pulling;
- 44d67fbe (#2847): arena rollover.

Each failed command buffer is a whole frame, and the rarest shaders in it differ from hang to hang, so no single shader stands out.

We haven't bisected; it's rare enough to live with on our side. If it helps, we can attach a `gpuEvent-dmhost` report and a run log, or run a build someone wants checked.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**What happens**

Mario Kart World 1.8.0 (v917504) packed from a NUP (`MKW.nup`, the whole game as one base package) with `--platform mac-app`, from `8d62601f`. The title menu shows `version: ?`. An emulator shows `1.8` from the same file.

**Why**

- The NUP's package carries an icon (0x0003), a display version label `v1.8.0` (0x0004), the name `Mario Kart World` (0x0005) and the code header, but **no NACP (0x0002)**. So `extract/v0/` gets `icon.jpg` and no `control.nacp`.
- 1.8.0's main (`d00e4f399e411d0613aa8d26b1c02fef`) is not a build the profile registers, so the script packs it from a derived profile, and `derive_profile` finds no `known` display version for it.
- `disp = nacp.version(control.nacp) or known or '?'` gives the derived row `build v0 ? main=d00e4f39… subsdk0=… subsdk1=… sdk=…`. `GetDisplayVersion` (`hle_sdk16.c`) then answers `?`, and the game shows it.

This is the same path as the Super Mario Bros. Wonder 1.2.1 "Ver. ?" case noted in `derive_profile`, except that the profile there registered the build.

**Proposed fix**

If there is no NACP and no version on record for the build, use the NUP's own display version label, but only when it reads as a version number. `pack_nup.py`'s header rightly says the labels are typed by whoever packed the NUP (HWAoI's name label is "HWAoI"), so a label that isn't shaped like a version is still ignored, and a NACP or a registered build row still wins:

- `scripts/pack_nup.py`: `T_VERSION = 4`. When a package has no NACP, `control()` writes `display_version.txt` beside the ExeFS from the label, if it matches `v?\d+(\.\d+){0,2}` (so `v1.8.0` becomes `1.8.0`, and `HWAoI` or `v1.8.0 beta` give nothing). The file is removed again when a NACP is present.
- `dm/tools/nacp.py`: `label_version(folder)` reads it back.
- `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`: `derive_profile` uses `nacp.version(control.nacp) or known or nacp.label_version(d) or '?'`. The Mac app / IPA version (`app_version`) and the survey's `dv` fall back to it in the same way.
- Tests: `test_nsp_nup.py` (label parsing; NACP wins; a non-version label is ignored) and `test_nsp_alias.py` (the label comes after the control data and the profile's row). `test_nsp_nup`, `test_nsp_alias`, `test_nsp_aarch64`, `test_nsp_incremental`, `test_lint_python` and `test_docs` pass.

The patch (148 lines including the tests) is below.

**Result**

After the rebuild, the derived row is `build v0 1.8.0 …`, the app version is 1.8.0, and the menu shows the version correctly. The rebuild reused the extract, the rewrite and the shaders. The only stage that ran again was the shader split, because the derived `game.tsv` changed.

**Also seen on 1.8.0 (M4 Max, 240 Hz)**

The frame-step stub matched 1.8.0 by fingerprint (`frame step cap 0 → 60 fps at present 1`, no `skipped` line). In one full race, every 30 s window after loading was `held 1 / 2 / 3 vsyncs 1800 / 0 / 0`, with game time 0.999–1.000 of real time and 0–2 frames dropped per 300 on screen.

+    p = Path(folder) / 'display_version.txt'

body:
**Symptom.** On current main, Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072) can abort about 4 s after launch, at frame 0, every time, once its pipeline archive holds a bad flush period. Metal asserts inside the archive lookup during the prewarm:

```
mtk_build → AGX ArchivePipelineFactory::lookupRenderPipeline
→ -[MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor validateWithDevice:]: meshFunction must not be nil
```

Seen on a 16 GB M2 MacBook Air, macOS 27.0, on main 44d67fbe and later. A build before eed7c429 is not affected.

**What happens.**
1. Apple's shader compiler service (MTLCompilerService) crashes (SIGBUS in AGX's LLVM backend) while compiling one of the game's mesh shaders, `ac2f3feb11427426_b` (Foliage). It crashes on that shader on every start, alone and from both its metallib and its MSL source, so every cold or partly cold start hits it. The crash itself is older: it shows in runs from before eed7c429, and earlier builds survived it.
2. Every compile in flight then fails with `XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED` (Metal error domain `AGXMetalG14G`, code 2).
3. Since eed7c429, a capture failure hands the period over (`arch_cap_failed` → `arch_flush_from`), and `arch_write_file` serializes it. Pipelines captured in that period while the service was dying are written with their functions missing. In the first case the log line was "capturing a render pipeline failed after 1225 in its flush period", and the file was `00000-1225`.
4. The next launch looks those pipelines up, and Metal asserts instead of returning an error.

A second form: the service can die while only plain compute compiles are running. No capture fails then, so the period (42 task/mesh pipelines in our case) is written at the next normal hand-over, also broken.

**Evidence.** The same archive played without that one period file (to frame 1233, no crash), and aborted with that file alone. The repro is the shader above with any object shader, compiled under one second.

**Workaround.** Delete the pipeline archive, or just the newest period file written after a "capturing … failed" line. The next start rebuilds it, but can poison it again while the compiler crash remains.

**Fix in progress.** When a compile fails because the compiler service died, mark the current period crashed and don't write it, at every compile site (render and compute, background, task/mesh prewarm, geometry mesh, specializations), with `t_pso_archive` checks. We'll open the PR shortly. Separately, we're reducing the shader that crashes the compiler, to see whether the translator can avoid the pattern; so far it needs a single-byte store into a threadgroup `uint` array through a `uchar*` cast.

## What happened

Ocarina of Time built from the `cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake` fork's **FF10** (tag `ff10`, `f3e79949`) hits a **GPU hang** on an iPhone Duo after a few minutes of normal play. iOS recovers once or twice, then revokes the process's GPU access and the game stops:

```
Caused GPU Hang Error (00000003:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)
Discarded (victim of GPU error/recovery) (00000005:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim)
Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors) (00000004:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored)
[RED] GPU access revoked: the display command buffer was ignored
FATAL GPU access revoked
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 -[DmRecTable forwardingTargetForSelector:]+0 gpu_lost_check+0x50 __present_now_block_invoke ...
```

The fork's issues are turned off, so I'm reporting it here; FF10 starts from nxnative main of 2026-11-14, so this may be on main as well (not tested on main itself).

## Two runs

| | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Played before the stop | ~8.7 min (frame 31,210) | ~3.8 min (frame 13,581) |
| Hangs before the stop | first one recovered at ~frame 15,600, fatal one at 31,210 | first one fatal |
| Settings | 60 fps, render scale 0.65, Wide view on, pipeline prebuild off | 60 fps, render scale 0.65, Wide view **off**, pipeline prebuild **on** |
| GPU p50 around the stop | 14-16 ms | ~13 ms |
| Frames dropped | 15.2 % | 0.65 % |
| Thermal state | 0-1 (never 2) | 0-1 (never 2) |
| Footprint peak | 5.65 GB | 3.2 GB |

Run 2 had headroom (steady 60 fps, GPU ~13 ms of 16.7, cool phone) and still hung, so it doesn't look like load or heat.

Shaders in the failed command buffers in **both** runs (from `game shaders by failed/ran over`):

kencalx's [NX18](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18) fork added two diagnostics for freezes on the iPhone. I'd like to bring them upstream, but together they come to about 1,090 changed lines, so I'm asking first.

1. **Freeze detector** (`DM_STALL_LOG`; [d96b25db](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/d96b25db6), [91cceea6](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/91cceea67)). When presents stop while the app is in focus, it writes a red line and a dump of the host's state. That covers the threads, the GPU queue and what each wait is waiting on. The dump holds off behind the on-screen keyboard's text box. This adds a new `dm/host/stall.c` with `t_stall` and `t_stall_dump`, and touches `crash.c`, `hle_thread.c` and the iOS gamepad code. About 650 lines.
2. **Ten-second wait lines** ([f608c3f7](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/f608c3f75), [37dddff2](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/37dddff2e)). A wait with no time limit logs a line once it passes 10 s: SyncWait's fast wake, upload, present, encode and copy. So a freeze names the wait it's stuck in. About 400 lines, and it builds on part 1.

Related: #1550 (GPU hang watchdog) and my #2098 (a residency commit that does not return freezes the game). As far as I can tell, NX18's detector complements #1550 rather than duplicating it. #1550 watches GPU completions, and this watches presents and host waits.

Would you take these as two PRs in that order? The work is kencalx's, and I'd credit them as co-author.

kencalx's [NX18](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18) fork can build from an NX archive made by NXConvert. An NX archive can hold a game's NCAs already decrypted, so a build from one needs no `prod.keys`. A `.nx` file, or a folder that holds one, is packed like a NUP. NX18 also adds `nx_extract --plain`, which reads decrypted NCAs through a checked in-memory header.

The whole change is about 5,900 lines across ten NX18 commits, starting at [ec91d25a](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/ec91d25ae) and running through 4543c1d0. That includes 64 small fixture archives, `scripts/pack_nx.py` (about 1,000 lines) and a C# change to `nx_extract`. Since `nx_extract` is now committed as a NativeAOT binary (641636e21), the `--plain` part would need you to rebuild that binary.

Is this something you'd want? If it is, I'll split it into three PRs, each under 1,000 lines:

1. `pack_nx.py` with its tests
2. `nx_extract --plain`, for you to rebuild the binary
3. The build-script wiring

The work is kencalx's. I'd port it with them credited as co-author.

## What NX18 found

[NX18](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18), a fork of this repository by kencalx, ran into the problem that `nvn_link_drain.h` fixes on the Mac ("A frame standing in the present queue after a late frame", `docs/reference/frame-rate.md`) on the iPhone, where the drain is off by default because it hasn't been measured there.

NX18 solved it differently. Its `present_trim` drops a frame that has stood in the display link's queue for K link ticks (K = 60 by default on iOS, scaled to the link's rate), instead of having the acquire wait the standing ticks out. Their numbers, on an iPhone 18 Pro Max, with game enqueue to target display p50 before and after:

- 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim: about 43 ms to about 28.5 ms, 3 frames dropped in 55 s, 60 fps held, no audio underruns ([afac2cab](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/afac2cab9))
- Super Mario Odyssey (Ultrawide on): 40 to 49.5 ms to 25.3 to 29 ms, 6 trims in about 2 minutes, frame interval p99 17.2 to 18.8 ms against 17.1 to 18.6 ms without ([ce221c00](https://github.com/kencalx/NX18/commit/ce221c009ad98edce421a4b1815826dc6a7d2287))
- Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, NieR:Automata, Persona 4 Golden and Persona 5 Royal improved similarly, and none of the seven games got worse (per-game commits in NX18 on Nov 11, 2026)

These are NX18's measurements. I haven't reproduced them.

## The question

Main already has one fix for this symptom, so I'm asking before writing a PR (CONTRIBUTING, "a second implementation of an existing path"):

1. Turn on main's drain on iOS and measure it against NX18's numbers. This keeps one mechanism, but nobody has measured the drain on the phone yet.
2. Port NX18's trim for iOS only. It's measured there, but it drops frames, which the drain was written to avoid.

I can do either one, including the iPhone measurements on an iPhone Duo. Which would you rather have?

Credit: the diagnosis and the measurements above are kencalx's work in NX18.

---

Following [PR #556](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/556), the macOS host was upgraded from `-O1` to `-O2` in [c4ffb9d](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/c4ffb9df262677658c3282e9d25a782ec54c2604), resulting in measurable performance improvements.

However, the potential benefits of `-O3` and link-time optimization (LTO) over the new `-O2` baseline haven't been evaluated independently yet.

**Suggested evaluation:**

Benchmark the following configurations against the current `-O2` baseline:

- `-O3`: more aggressive compiler optimizations, including additional loop and vectorization optimizations.
- `-O2 -flto=full`: full link-time optimization, allowing optimizations across translation units.
- `-O3 -flto=full`: combining both approaches.
- Optionally, `-flto=thin` as an alternative to full LTO.

Ideally, the benchmarks would cover CPU-intensive gameplay scenes, particularly those with high draw-call counts, and compare host CPU time, frame times, and executable size.

The original PR demonstrated improvements when comparing `-O1` against `-O3` with LTO, but these measurements don't establish whether either optimization provides additional benefits over `-O2`.

**LTO compatibility:**

As discussed in PR #556, full LTO caused a `SIGBUS` crash in `dm_bigstack_enter` when running Breath of the Wild. A potential fix using `.alt_entry` was included in the PR.

Any further LTO evaluation should include regression testing of the big-stack implementation before considering it for the default build.

If benchmarks demonstrate reproducible performance improvements without regressions, enabling the corresponding optimizations could be a worthwhile follow-up to the existing `-O2` change.
title: dmhost: Evaluate -O3 and LTO performance improvements for the macOS host

Following the switch to NativeAOT in [641636e](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/641636e217313a691438e0f1d259b9062d309c44), it would be worth enabling additional compiler optimizations for the C# tools, particularly the shader translator (`dmsh_xlate`), which can be invoked thousands of times during shader compilation.

The existing build already uses the Release configuration, but NativeAOT's default optimization policy balances execution speed and binary size rather than prioritizing performance.

**Suggested optimizations:**
- Set `OptimizationPreference=Speed` to prioritize execution speed during NativeAOT compilation.
- Consider `UseSizeOptimizedLinq=false` to enable LINQ throughput optimizations that NativeAOT normally disables to reduce binary size.
- Evaluate other suitable compiler and trimming options, provided they preserve functionality and compatibility.
- Benchmark shader translation throughput and startup latency before and after the changes.

The original [PR #545](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/545) already included some of these optimizations, alongside performance benchmarks.

Since the tools are distributed as precompiled native executables, any improvements would directly benefit users without introducing additional dependencies. A modest increase in binary size may be a worthwhile trade-off, particularly for the shader translator.

Reference: [Microsoft — Optimizing Native AOT deployments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/native-aot/optimizing)
title: dmsh_xlate/nx_extract: Enable speed-oriented NativeAOT compiler optimizations

body:
Following the introduction of NativeAOT builds in [641636e](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/641636e217313a691438e0f1d259b9062d309c44), it would be worth updating the two C# tools (`dmsh_xlate` and `nx_extract`) from .NET 10 to the recently released .NET 11.

.NET 11 is now generally available and is also the default version provided by Homebrew (`dotnet` and `dotnet-sdk`). [It includes additional runtime and NativeAOT performance improvements](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/performance-improvements-in-net-11/).

**Suggested changes:**
- Update both projects and the vendored Ryujinx dependencies to target `net11.0`.
- Update the .NET SDK version used in CI and the build documentation.
- Rebuild the committed NativeAOT executables and update their fingerprints and shader translation chain metadata as required.
- Verify that the rebuilt tools produce identical outputs and retain compatibility with supported macOS versions.

Since the executables are already self-contained, this would not introduce any new .NET runtime requirement for end users.

The original [PR #545](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/545) also included the .NET 11 upgrade, although this part wasn't included in the upstream implementation.
title: dmsh_xlate/nx_extract: Upgrade to .NET 11

body:
## What is missing

On a Switch a game that loses focus stays in memory, so progress since its last save point waits there. On an iPhone the system can end the app any time once it is in the background, and everything since the game's own last save point is lost. Games that save only at story beats or areas lose the most (FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Pokemon: Let's Go, Pikachu!, found on an iPhone 17).

## What I propose (and have working)

The host asks the game to run **its own** save when the app leaves the foreground; no save format is touched.

- Host: a new observation gate `OBS_SAVE_POINT` (`dm/host/dm.h`). A game profile's `patches.py` places it at a point in the game's frame loop where its save may run; the host's callback writes 1 into a register and a small stub in the profile calls the game's save routine before that frame. `dm_focus_set` asks once per in-focus to out-of-focus change (resign active, switcher, Control Center, Mac window losing focus); `DM_SAVE_ON_LEAVE=0` turns it off. The iOS front end waits up to 1.5 s for the save before the cloud-save flush. A launcher toggle ("Save when leaving the game") shows where the profile declares the `SAVE_ON_LEAVE` capability.
- Per game, found by reverse engineering: the game's save entry plus a per-frame point. Resonance: autosave entry `main+0x428e21c` called from the GameThread loop, only with a game loaded (at the title the save object holds empty data and a save there overwrote slot 0). Let's Go, Pikachu! 1.0.2: save routine `main+0x1cdc80`, called before the world step in the per-frame update `main+0x13d9d0`.

## Checked

- Resonance (Mac): title 0 commits; field 1 commit; resign then background completes the save; Continue loaded a field, a battle and a cutscene save. iPhone: the app closed in a boat scene came back at the dock.
- Let's Go, Pikachu! (Mac, headless, copy of a real save): focus loss in the overworld, in a wild encounter and at boot each gives exactly one save commit, and the resulting save loads (Continue resumes in the overworld).
- Not checked: Pikachu on a phone, trainer battles, a fresh install with no save (a blank save may be written at the title), other builds of these games.

## Questions

1. Is this direction wanted, or would you prefer the save found by code pattern (a function-matched rule, as other profile patches do) so it survives game updates?
2. Per-game patches are keyed to one build ID. Is that acceptable for this kind of hook?
3. Should the host guard generically (for example skip while a save is already in progress), or leave guards to each profile?

If it is welcome I would send the host part and the Resonance profile as one PR off current `main`, and Pikachu's after a phone check.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Save when the player leaves the game (iPhone ends backgrounded apps): host hook plus per-game profile patch

body:
### What is missing

On an iPhone with a 120 Hz screen (A20 Pro, "Duo" below), Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072) does not hold 60 fps on a heavy route; it holds 40 (25 ms, three refreshes) when the frame step can count ticks of 1/120 s (a separate PR). nxnative has no frame generation, so the screen shows 40 or 30 pictures a second even where it could show 60.

Apple's MetalFX frame interpolator (`MTL4FXFrameInterpolator`) makes one frame half-way between two pictures and takes no phase (Xcode 27.2 headers: `deltaTime` is the input spacing; no output timestamp). So it can double 30 to 60, but it cannot make 40 → 60, which needs frames at 1/3 and 2/3 of an interval.

### What you propose

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an issue first for a change of this size: about 3,300 added lines in 20 files (counted with shared files whole), with two generators. Before opening PRs I would like to know whether and how you want it.

#### What we built (in our fork, default off)

1. **2x, `DM_FRAMEGEN=2x`:** MetalFX's frame interpolator after each present snapshot, the generated frame shown on the present's first tick and its own picture half an interval later, on the display link. Motion found from the two pictures (`dm/gfx/msl/fgmv.metal`), the still HUD kept from the present, back-off while frames drop, `DM_FRAMEGEN_SCALE`. **Ported from the iPhone fork kid-with-sword-remake (cheemu21, MIT)**, commits `7979a465` and `c73064ee`; the PR would carry that attribution and the MIT notice.
2. **1.5x, `DM_FRAMEGEN=1.5x`:** our own generator, since the MetalFX interpolator has no phase: bidirectional block motion with a second vector per tile, occlusion-weighted warp, HUD copied back. One generated frame per 25 ms present, at 2/3 and 1/3 in turn, shown 16.7 ms apart on the 120 Hz link while game time steps evenly. `DM_FRAMEGEN_30` (on with 1.5x) gives 33.3 ms presents one frame half-way, so 30 is shown as 60 too (the thermal cap). `DM_FRAMEGEN_Q` (on) chooses vectors per pixel at block edges and refines to sub-pixel. 16.7 ms presents are shown as drawn.
3. **A player's choice:** a launcher row "Frame generation: Off / When frames drop" for a game whose frame step takes ticks of 1/120 s, switched while the game runs (`dm_framegen_live` / `dm_framegen_set`) from the iOS in-game menu and a Mac Performance menu.

It touches `nvn_mtl.m` (present snapshots, the present path, a new `fgmv.metal` host library), the frame step only through the present times it reads, and the front ends for the menu rows. It depends on the 40 fps / ticks-of-1/120-s change for 1.5x.

#### Measurements so far (single runs, our fork)

| What | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5x at 40 real, battery, cold start, water route | iPhone Duo (A20 Pro, iOS 27.2), earlier base, scale 0.33 + `DM_FRAMEGEN_SCALE=0.5` | until 356 s about 60 shown a second (minutes 2-3: 59.9; 4-5: 59.0 / 58.3), 99.2 % of shown intervals at 16.7 ms, real 40; then thermal state serious, engine cap 40 → 30, and (before `DM_FRAMEGEN_30` existed) 30 shown / 30 real for the rest |
| 1.5x at 40 real, headless, 180 s | M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, our fork | frame time 25.00 ms p50 / 25.12 p95, 1,800 of 1,800 generated per 30 s window, generator GPU p50 2.9-7.0 ms a frame (0.5 scale) |
| Cost at a steady 60 with 1.5x enabled (no frame generated) | M3 Max, headless, `DM_AB` on/off, four runs | copy + luma 0.09-0.13 ms GPU p50 a present; game GPU p50 13.84 / 13.83 ms, frame p95 17.67 / 17.81 ms, game time 1.000 |
| Quality lever `DM_FRAMEGEN_Q` | real 25 ms camera-pan fixture from a Duo snapshot dump, M3 Max at 0.5 scale | PSNR 31.27 → 31.98 dB, SSIM 0.860 → 0.877, bad pixels 1.41 → 1.24 %, at +0.4-0.5 ms GPU |
| Quality, unit test `t_fg15` | M3 Max, synthetic ground truth (frames n and n+3 → n+1, n+2) | 48 checks, **2 failing: the whole-picture PSNR targets, 27.8 and 27.4 dB against 30 dB**. Not lowered; they fail the same on every base since the generator was written |
| `DM_FRAMEGEN_Q` cost on the device | Duo, A/B in one run | inconclusive: generation ran only in the first phases (hold 3), later phases bypassed it |

Player impression on the Duo (in-game counter, not a measurement): almost always 60 fps, with visible artefacts at fast camera movement; `DM_FRAMEGEN_Q` came from that.

#### Known limits

- Quality: the two whole-picture PSNR checks fail; fast pans still show artefacts at block edges and disocclusions; no perceptual study.
- At a 40 ↔ 30 change game time jumps once and up to two frames show 25 ms.
- 2x keeps its start choice; a ring of 2 of `DM_PRESENT_SNAP`'s own refuses 1.5x while the game runs.
- Only Ocarina of Time has the frame-step stub in ticks of 1/120 s that 1.5x needs; other games could use 2x.
- No Mac windowed or fullscreen play test of the Mac menu entry; device runs are from an earlier base than current main.

#### Questions

1. Is frame generation in scope for nxnative at all (it adds frames the game did not draw, with artefacts)?
2. If yes: one generator (ours, with phases, also for 2x) or both (Apple's interpolator for 2x, ours for 1.5x)?
3. Split proposal: (a) the snapshot/present hooks with 2x, (b) 1.5x and 30 → 60 on top, (c) the player's choice and menus. Each on current main, each with its tests and a device run.
4. What quality bar would you want before merging (the PSNR targets in `t_fg15`, a perceptual check, player reports)?

Credit: the 2x path is ported from cheemu21's kid-with-sword-remake fork of nxnative (MIT, same copyright notice as nxnative).

### Platforms

Mac, iPhone
title: Frame generation on the display link: 2x (MetalFX interpolator) and 1.5x (40 → 60, own generator) — scope before a PR?
