body:
## What happens

Pokémon Friends (`010008C01E742000`, update 1.1.5, Unity 2022.3.62f1, SDK 19.3.11; no profile in the repository yet), packed with the NSP script on main ad1ee5bf, renders its 3D blurry. The heap check sets `app_pool 0x40000000`: "no heap set and the alias region used up to +4.26 GB of 4.38 GB in the heap check: a 1 GB pool, so StandardAllocator's region leaves the game room for its own".

## Why

`hle_svc.c` reports `app_pool` as `GetInfo(TotalMemorySize)`, which Unity hands to the game as `SystemInfo.systemMemorySize`. On a new save, the game calls `UnityEngine.SystemInfo::GetPhysicalMemoryMB()` (`main+0x39731d4`, through the internal call at `main+0x492eab0`) and, at 2048 MB or less (`cmp w0, #0x800` / `b.gt`, `main+0x39731d8`), stores graphics quality 1 (Low). The main camera's target is then half the screen and the 3D renders at 672x378. On hardware the application pool is 3285 MiB, so the game never takes this path. The level is saved: a save made with the small pool stays Low after the pool changes, until the player raises it in the game's options.

## Measured

On the Mac (M5 Max), main ad1ee5bf, docked, a fresh save each time, the same scene after the first-boot screens; the render targets are from `DM_CTL` `texlist 1` (targets with render-target flags):

| `app_pool` | render targets in the scene |
|---|---|
| `0x40000000` (the heap check's guess) | 672x378 ×23, 1344x756 ×21, 1920x1080 ×4 |
| `0x88000000` (2176 MB) | 1920x1080 ×45 |

Frame time 16.7 ms in both, no red line. On an iPhone 17 Pro, the game has been played with `0x88000000` since 2026-11-06. The hardware pool, `0xCD500000`, ran out of the alias region there after the name entry (main of 2026-11-06: a 16 MB allocation failed, `CRASH addr=0` at `main+0xa48fd0`).

## Thoughts

The 1 GB rule keeps the alias region free for the Unity games it lists, and this game needs that on the phone too, but a game that sizes itself by `GetPhysicalMemoryMB` goes to its lowest setting under it. In this case a pool just above the game's 2 GB threshold kept both. Two things the guesser could do: look for the `UnityEngine.SystemInfo::GetPhysicalMemoryMB()` internal-call name in `main` (IL2CPP keeps it as a string) and say so in the survey, or start the rule above 2 GB. LEGO Voyagers (`01005B901F8EE000`, no profile in the repository either) has the same name in its `main`; what it does with the value was not checked. Advance Wars 1+2: Re-Boot Camp already needed 2 GB for another reason (`docs/reference/memory.md`, "Sizing the pool and alias region for virtual address memory"). Which of these fits, or whether it belongs in a profile, is your call.

Nothing here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: profile_guess: the 1 GB pool makes Pokémon Friends pick its Low graphics (3D at 672x378)

body:
In `pso_predict_rest_` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:12968` on `e6a358f5`), each candidate that has no made base goes through `hybrid_get`. That calls `pso_build_ex` to make the pulling stand-in on the submit thread. When the pulling base is in the archive, this is a synchronous MTL4 archive lookup. Most of these lookups are cheap. While base compiles run in the background, though, a few take tens to hundreds of ms, and the whole frame waits. Related to #2438 but a separate cost. That issue was about how often the walk runs and is fixed by 53cbb993. This one is the latency of a single walk. 960d203e does not cover it: the walk admits no builds, because every candidate is served by `hybrid_get`.

**Measured** (Ocarina of Time, `e6a358f5` plus two local patches that do not touch this path: rumble tuning, plus one log line in `pso_get_`'s hybrid branch; Mac M4 Max, macOS 26.7.1, 13.5 min session, bundled archive `applegpu_g16s.mtl4a` 4180 MB):

```
[longframe] frame 33454 (586.84 s) whole frame 332.4 ms, submit+present 315.3 ms, GPU 12.2 ms; new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0, 273.2 ms in all; texture uploads 0 first + 0 re-uploads, 0.0 MB / 0.0 ms; draws with a hybrid pipeline 11
[nvn] pipelines up to frame 33600: on the submit thread pipelines 273.3 ms, shader libraries 0.0 ms, predictions 2 / 273.3 ms (builds admitted 0); all threads: archive lookups found 10 / 311.0 ms, found none 10 / 0.2 ms, specializations 29 / 0.3 ms, bases compiled 10 / 1559.5 ms; draws with a hybrid pipeline 51 (19 pulling pipelines made, 0 misses with no pulling base ready); background builds kicked 10, done 10, made by the draw 0, in flight 0
```

- Both predictions in that window took 273 ms and admitted no builds. The window also had 10 archive lookups totalling 311 ms and 10 background base compiles totalling 1.56 s.
- The same pattern showed up on `5a4e23a2` (2026-11-15, 11.6 min): a single mid-game stall of 165 ms, in a window with `predictions 2 / 102.3 ms`, `archive lookups 4 / 136.3 ms` and `bases compiled 5 / 753 ms`.
- A local log line in `pso_get_`'s own `hybrid_get` branch (draw blocked > 50 ms) never fired in either session. The slow lookups come from the walk's call site, not from the draw's.
- Outside these windows, archive lookups are fast: same p95 frame time as before (16.82 ms) and 0.24 % empty display ticks.

**Hypothesis:** a lookup in the MTL4 archive is serialized behind a background base compile on the same compiler, so a lookup that usually takes under 1 ms waits for that compile to finish. I have not confirmed this with a trace.

**Possible directions** (your call):
1. In the walk, skip candidates with no stand-in in `g_pso_hy` and hand them to the background queue. The walk only needs to know whether a draw would wait. It does not need the stand-in made there.
2. Or time-box the walk: stop calling `hybrid_get` once the walk's own time passes a few ms in the current submission.

**Observability (minor):** `g_hy_ns` (`nvn_mtl.m:10594`) is accumulated but never printed. Adding it to the pipelines line and to `[longframe]` would have made the first case (a 366 ms frame that `[longframe]` reported as "0.6 ms in all" on `5a4e23a2`) visible without patching.
title: Ocarina of Time: 270 ms+ mid-game stalls from synchronous archive lookups in `hybrid_get` inside the prediction walk while bases compile in the background

body:
Ocarina of Time — played from inside Ganon's Castle to the ending, on an M5 MacBook Air

## Environment

- Hardware: MacBook Air `Mac17,3`, Apple M5, GPU `applegpu_g17g` (the same GPU as the report in #1566), 24 GB unified memory
- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)
- Game: `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, text set to `zh-Hans`
- Build: a Mac `.app` built from the engine at `92aa1222`, shader chain `d7576061facd`, built 2026-11-10 11:08 — before `0662f9d8a` (2026-11-11 07:11) and before the movie-player cut of #2456, so nothing below is a statement about current `main`
- Session: 279.6 minutes, frames up to 584,242, `the host exited with 0`, log 58,531 lines
- Settings: fullscreen off, `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, dynamic resolution off, shader prebuild on

## Progress and stability

From inside Ganon's Castle, through the final battle, the ending and the staff roll: the game can be finished on this engine. No crash, no abort, no progression blocker in 4 h 39 min. The ending and the credits played.

The profile's README says `Not played yet: the Deku Tree dungeon, combat, later areas`. This is one run that covers the end of those on one machine, on a build a week old. It is not a verification of the areas in between, and I have not retested on current `main`.

## What the endgame showed

### Every empowered sword hit flashes the screen white

Matches #2508 exactly, including the precondition: it starts once the Master Sword is empowered, and from then on each hit puts a large white flash over the screen instead of the intended effect. The ground at the forest entrance and in the Temple of Time's sword chamber flickers with bright patches too.

This build predates `0662f9d8a`, so this is a sighting consistent with the diagnosis in #2508, not a new one. What it adds is a machine and a GPU that report does not cover (M4 Max there, `g17g` M5 here), so the flash is not tied to one GPU family.

### Music and voice drop out in the final battle; the ending played almost silently

In the battle the background music and the dialogue voice stop and come back. Through the ending it was silent apart from a line or two of sound now and then. #1566 reports the shorter version of this ("sound drops for a few seconds now and then") on the same GPU.

What this log shows:

- `renderer 0 rendered 3336000 frames, 3151450 of them not silent` — a nonzero mix in 94.5% of frames over 16,680 s, and in the last forty minutes almost every minute is 100%
- the device path is clean: 1,668 statistics lines all read `device callbacks 2000: 240–241 frames each, 4.0 blocks queued on average at callback; in these 2000, 0 underruns, 0.0 ms zero-padded`, except 6 lines with 29 underruns in total, in six clusters (64, 74, 142, 152, 160 and 270 minutes), each a few milliseconds of zero padding
- one device opened once: `audio #0`, 48 kHz, 2 channels, no switch during the session; `OpenAudioRenderer rate 48000 samples per frame 240 ... submixes 11 ... sinks 2`, `DeviceSink inputs 6`
- 20 `[codec]`/`[movie]` lines, all 1920x1080 AV1 through VideoToolbox, `AV1 decoder 1` for every movie; decoders start at lines 17696, 19846, 21555, 22998, 23976 and again at 58461. The first four log `end of stream` after 1,980 / 2,368 / 18,699 / 7,343 pictures; the one started at 23976 and the one at 58461 never do, and the process exits with 0 about 70 lines after the last `first picture`

**One caveat about those counters, which is why this is not filed as a separate audio bug.** `rendered N frames, M of them not silent` is the renderer's final mix. Effects and ambience are resident and always playing, so they hold the sum nonzero while a music or a voice bus is dead. The counter cannot tell "the music stopped" from "the music is playing", and it cannot rule the mix in or out for a scene like this — the same conclusion #1661 reaches from the other side.

Both known causes of sound loss in this game are newer than this build: the movie-player cut in #2456, where the picture falls one more frame behind every frame so the sound ends first, and `0662f9d8a` for the NaN colours. I cannot separate them from what I heard. `DM_AUDIO_DUMP` (the PCM the game appends, before the device) and `DM_AUDREN_TRACE` would settle it in one sitting; neither was set in this session.

### Memory over 4 h 39 min

Resident memory: 5,660 MB at frame 300, 9,788 MB by frame 13,500, then 11.5 to 15.5 GB for the rest of the recorded window, 14,868 MB at frame 364,500. GPU allocated: 3,621 MB, 13,220 MB, and 19,291 MB late in the session. No OOM, no Jetsam, no crash on a 24 GB machine. #2088, the closest report in shape (about 4 hours, M4 Pro, 48 GB), ends at a 13.9 GB footprint.

## Performance

- frames up to 584,242 in 279.6 minutes
- 12,875 frames (2.2%) took more than 33 ms; 60 took more than 1 s
- the endgame sits at frame time p50 16.68 ms (last window, frame 584,100); GPU time on the long frames near the end is 11–12 ms
- the long stalls line up with the app losing focus: the session has 184 focus transitions, and the worst frame (frame 214687, 2,120 s long, at 7,542 s into the session) carries `new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0`, which is the app in the background rather than the renderer

## What I did not test

- no retest on current `main`, so there is no fixed / not fixed comparison here
- `DM_AUDIO_DUMP`, `DM_AUDREN_TRACE` and `DM_NVN_BLEND_ZERO=0` were not set
- one machine, one build, one run; the areas before Ganon's Castle were played on earlier builds and are not part of this log

Log kept (58,531 lines, 14.5 MB) and available on request — every line quoted above is verbatim from it.

### What happened

Fate/hollow ataraxia REMASTERED (an OpenGL ES game, like Balatro) boots to its title screen but **crashes the moment a new game starts** (SIGSEGV jumping to address 0), and after that is worked around the scene draw is **completely black**.

Traced to two independent causes in the GL layer, both from how this game builds its GL calls:

1. **Vendor-suffixed entry points get a null pointer.** The Switch binary resolves old-style extension names through `eglGetProcAddress` (`glGenFramebuffersEXT`, `glBindRenderbufferEXT`, `glCheckFramebufferStatusEXT` …). `gl_lookup()` in `dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m` matches `swhle` table names exactly, so the suffixed names return NULL and the game calls through a null function pointer:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=0 lr=main+0x3bab70c
```

(the blr to 0 follows `eglGetProcAddress("glGenFramebuffersEXT")` returning 0). The same crash class hits any GL ES 2 game that prefers `*_EXT` names on a core-3.0 host. A glad-style loader in the same game also asks `eglGetProcAddress` for **EGL** names (`eglGetCurrentDisplay`), which the lookup only tried for `gl`-prefixed names — and that hook did not exist at all.

2. **A sampler uniform named `texture` does not translate.** The game's built shader code declares `uniform sampler2D texture;` — legal desktop GLSL 1.x, but the translation to MSL goes through GLSL 310 where `texture` is a built-in function, so 16 of the game's 78 runtime-captured scene fragments fail with `'texture' : redefinition` and the scenes they draw come out black. Only the 2 title-screen shaders translate.

### What you expected

New Game enters the first scene and renders.

### Game, title ID and version

Fate/hollow ataraxia REMASTERED, 010070E022546000, update v131072 (1.0.2), cartridge .xci (base + update in one dump). No official profile: provisional from survey.

### nxnative commit

f4b7e77 (main). The fixes that make it playable are in the PR filed alongside this issue — three small pieces: retry the lookup on the bare stem after stripping a vendor suffix (EXT/ARB/OES/NV/…), record display/context/draw-surface in `eglMakeCurrent` and answer `eglGetCurrentDisplay` / `eglGetCurrentContext` / `eglGetCurrentDrawSurface`, and rename a `texture`-named sampler uniform in `gl_shaders.py` before the MSL compile (the tsv keeps the game's name and the lookup keys are the sources' hashes, so the rename is invisible to the game).

### Shader chain version

Not the NVN chain: an OpenGL game, `gl_shaders.py` translates a runtime capture (78 shaders captured by booting on the Mac; 75 translate with the fix — the 2 that fail want a sampler slot above 15).

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <fate-ha folder> -k prod.keys --platform mac` for the Mac host, then `--platform ios --prepare-xcode` for the iPhone project; run on the Mac as a windowed dmhost of `patched_v131072` (`DM_WINDOW=1 DM_AUDIO=1`).

### Device and OS

Mac mini (Apple silicon), macOS 27.2.1 arm64; the iOS target also compiles at this commit.

### Settings and environment overrides

`DM_LANG=zh-Hans` (the game ships ja / en-US / zh-Hans); shaders captured once with `DM_GL_CAPTURE`; the rest default.

### Logs

The headless shader capture boots die the same way before the fix:

```
[RED] the game stopped after 0 s in the Mac host (exit 139)
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=0 lr=main+0x3bab70c
```

With `DM_GL_MISSES=1` the null pointers are visible one by one before the jump to 0. After the fixes the game plays: title → new game → scenes and cutscene transitions render; 45 minutes of script-driven advancing (2000+ injected taps) with no crash and no missing-shader lines in the log.

- [x] I have no game files to attach (commercial cartridge) but I can test a patch

### What happened

Ocarina of Time starts and plays on an 8 GB iPad Pro M4, but is not playable once in the game. The title, the menus and the opening run (footprint about 1.3 GB, almost no reads from the guest files). From the first gameplay area on:

- the footprint is 3.7–4.5 GB and the guest files hold 5.3–6.0 GB on disk;
- only 0.3–0.9 GB of the guest files' pages stay mapped;
- the process reads 1.5–4 GB per 10 s (30,000–180,000 page-ins per 10 s);
- frames take 0.1–6 s.

iOS never ended the app. Thermal state 0 throughout. The long frames have no pipeline or shader work (`new pipelines 0`). It happened in all four runs, with every setting tried.

My reading, not measured further: the guest's pages (about 6 GB) plus the host's footprint (about 4 GB) do not fit 8 GB of physical memory, so the file pages are evicted and read back.

#### The four runs

| Run | Mode | `DM_FPS_TARGET` | `DM_GFX_SCALE` | Frames | Frames ≥ 100 ms | Worst frame | Footprint peak | Max read per 10 s | Game time / real time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | docked | 60 | 0 | 9,300 | 83, 51.3 s | 6,044 ms | 4.39 GB | 3.02 GB | 0.89 |
| 2 | handheld | 60 | 1 | 3,600 | 74, 31.1 s | 2,920 ms | 4.49 GB | 3.46 GB | 0.65 |
| 3 | handheld | 60 | 2 | 3,900 | 204, 33.6 s | 1,570 ms | 4.08 GB | 4.08 GB | 0.75 |
| 4 | handheld | 30 | 2 | 4,800 | 96, 34.9 s | 5,779 ms | 4.34 GB | 3.13 GB | 0.85 |

Each run goes from boot into the first gameplay area and a few minutes in it. Run 1 started a new game; I did not note which later runs loaded its save.

#### Three observations

1. **The reduced graphics tiers did not lower the footprint.** Peak 4.39 GB at tier 0 docked, 4.49 GB at tier 1 handheld, 4.08–4.34 GB at tier 2 handheld.

2. **At a 60 fps target the frame step sat at 20 fps where 30 fitted (run 3).** Held 1 / 2 / 3 vsyncs: 713 / 180 / 907 frames. A trial at hold 2 reports `cost 0.77, GPU 0.77`, the next trial at hold 1 fails with `3 late frames; cost 5.07, GPU 1.28`, and the step goes `hold 1 → 3`. It looks like #2400 on the Mac. With `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` (run 4) all 1,800 counted frames were held at 2 vsyncs.

3. **In run 4 the GPU time rose to the 30 fps budget.** GPU p50 12–15 ms up to frame 3000, then 21–34 ms from frame 3300 on (p95 32–125 ms), at the same tier and mode. Dynamic resolution was on; I did not check its level.

#### Log lines

Start, every run:

```
[mem] guest memory: memory pool 9.00 GB and the host's margin 4.50 GB (half the pool), room to the memory limit 7.97 GB, DM_GUEST_FILE unset: in files
```

Run 1, in the game:

```
[mem] guest file: 5.67 GB allocated on disk, 1.70 GB dirty in memory (232 ms to count, every 10 s), 0.43 GB given back as holes; process read 10.08 GB, 708674 page-ins, logical writes 7.47 GB; footprint 4.06 GB (internal 0.15, compressed 0.98, peak so far 4.06), file pages mapped (external) 0.45 GB
[mem] guest file: 5.60 GB allocated on disk, 1.86 GB dirty in memory (324 ms to count, every 10 s), 0.87 GB given back as holes; process read 13.10 GB, 812091 page-ins, logical writes 8.28 GB; footprint 3.94 GB (internal 0.09, compressed 1.05, peak so far 4.06), file pages mapped (external) 0.52 GB
[nvn] power up to frame 8700: CPU energy 1.82 W, 179.5 mJ per frame (10.1 fps); CPU 118% (100 = one core), 61% of it on performance cores
[longframe] frame 9047 (723.3 s) whole frame 6043.8 ms, submit+present 4704.2 ms, GPU 57.4 ms; new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0, 0.0 ms in all
```

Run 3, frame step:

```
frame step: hold 2 → 1 vsyncs at present 3355 (trial; cost 0.77, GPU 0.77)
frame step: hold 1 → 3 vsyncs at present 3361 (3 late frames; cost 5.07, GPU 1.28; hold 1 held at 0.15)
frame step: game time 69.15 s in 92.02 s (0.751 of real time); held 1 / 2 / 3 vsyncs 713 / 180 / 907 frames, 452 late, 391 vsyncs paid back, 1600 dropped, 13 up / 10 down (5 probes, 8 failed trials)
```

First start: `pipeline prepare: 14748 lines (11569 shaders, 2691 render pipelines, 324 compute pipelines) in 379.51 s on 9 workers before the first frame`. Later starts: 2.4–2.7 s.

For comparison, the same game on a MacBook Air M5 (32 GB, guest anonymous, commit `94a09447`, handheld, `DM_GFX_SCALE=1`): footprint median 11.5–11.8 GB, 60 fps with short dips.

Possibly related: #2474 (12 GB iPhone, Metal 4 archive path; here `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`), #2772 (guest-file stalls on an iPhone), #2565 (GPU cost on iOS), #2400 (frame step).

### What you expected

A steady 30 fps in handheld mode, or to know that this game is out of reach of 8 GB devices for now. If a setting or a test would help to narrow the memory down (`DM_MEMSTAT`, another guest-file chunk size, anything else), I can run it on this iPad.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), 0400486024DEC000, 1.0 (v131072), no DLC

### nxnative commit

af286190

### Shader chain version

4d84aa6c8a2d

iPhone or iPad, built and run with Xcode. `build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NUP> --prepare-xcode --romfs separate`, Release, Xcode 27.2, entitlements `increased-memory-limit` and `extended-virtual-addressing`. RomFS image (24.44 GB) in `Documents/romfs.img`.

The rest at the defaults the log shows: `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=on`, `DM_UPSCALER=game`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`.

The whole `log.txt` of each of the four runs (the app container's UUID replaced by `<uuid>`, nothing else changed): https://gist.github.com/ocubanox/86a0f6525bd7ed00c74ff3e0f82f6c76

### What is missing

Ocarina of Time on the Mac can swap the game's upscaler for MetalFX spatial (`DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`). MetalFX's temporal scaler would give steadier edges and let the 3D render smaller. It needs motion vectors, depth and jitter, and the game keeps no motion vectors or jitter.

### What you propose

A branch on current main (063fd073) adds `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx-temporal`. The host makes the inputs:

- Camera from the agl scene block, with the decoder from #2591.
- Depth from the scene pass, and camera motion from a reprojection pass.
- Viewport jitter on the scene's draws. No shader changes.
- A reactive mask from depth, through the mask input from #1904.
- RCAS sharpening before the HUD.
- The spatial scaler for any frame that lacks an input.

A third commit makes it the Mac default for Ocarina of Time at 0.67 render scale.

Kokiri Forest route, 2560x1440 output, medians of 3 runs (M1 Max) and 2 runs (M4):

| Mac | Spatial, 1.0 | Temporal, 0.67 |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Max | 51.6 fps | 57.9 fps |
| M4 MacBook Air | 41.4 fps | 48.2 fps |

Fog and water are stable. There are no per-object motion vectors, so Link can leave a faint trail. Tested on Ocarina of Time only.

The diff is about 1,230 lines, about 500 of them tests. Two questions before I open the PR:

1. One PR, or the upscaler first and the default change separately?
2. Is temporal welcome as the Mac default for Ocarina of Time, or should it stay opt-in?

Credits: #2591 (camera decoder and motion kernels), #1904 (reactive mask), and ly05010419/MacNativeGames (MIT, the viewport-jitter approach).

### Platforms

Mac

body:
### What is missing

### In short

On the Mac, a Switch Pro Controller's rumble goes through Core Haptics, which keeps one intensity and one sharpness of the game's two bands. On the pad's linear actuators that feels thin and tight, and raising the gain does not change its character.

A DualShock 4 on the same Mac feels right: `haptics_apple.m` drives it through its own effects report instead.

(#2148 covers the low amplitudes; this is about the route.)

### Game, build, device

- **Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, v131072
- **nxnative:** commit `bee218d9`, shader chain `66eab9c9a6b4`, Mac app (`--platform mac-app`) and the host from a terminal (`--platform mac`)
- **Mac:** MacBook Pro M3 Pro (18 GB), macOS 26.6.2
- **Pad:** Pro Controller (057e:2009) over Bluetooth, paired in System Settings

### Why a direct report can work

The same pad rumbles in Chrome (Gamepad `vibrationActuator`) while GameController has it, so an output report sent beside GameController reaches the pad.

### Scope

I only felt the need on this game, whose rumble is written soft and short for the Switch 2's actuators. On Switch 1 games the Core Haptics route is reported to feel normal on a pad of this kind (#2148, Tears of the Kingdom); I have not compared the two routes on one. So this may matter mostly for Switch 2 titles played with a Switch 1 pad.

### Related

- #2148: weak rumble on this game
- #1433: its author also reports feeling no controller vibration in this game at all

### What you propose

### The route

A route like `ds4_route` for a controller whose productCategory is "Switch Pro Controller": the host sends the pad's rumble report itself (output report 0x10, after subcommand 0x48 01 turned vibration on), with the game's frequency and amplitude for the high and the low band of each side.

### Local patch

I run a local patch that does this, in `dm/host/haptics_apple.m` only (two files attached, the second applies on top of the first):

- **Opening the pad:** `pro_take` / `pro_route` open the first free 057E:2009 HID device that is not GameController's synthetic one and that accepts the subcommand; otherwise the Core Haptics route stays. `DM_RUMBLE_PRO=0` keeps Core Haptics.
- **Encoding:** `pro_encode` uses the frequency and amplitude codes of dekuNukem's rumble_data_table.md, each band capped at 0.85 (`DM_RUMBLE_PRO_MAX`).
- **Sending:** reports padded to 49 bytes over Bluetooth, sent at most every 12 ms on a change and again every 40 ms while a level stays; a neutral report on stop, suspend and release.
- **Optional tuning, off by default:** `DM_RUMBLE_PRO_FREQ=1` (both bands at 160 / 320 Hz), `DM_RUMBLE_PRO_LOW` (share of the high band moved to the low band), `DM_RUMBLE_PRO_CURVE`, `DM_RUMBLE_PRO_HOLD` (ms).
- **Gain:** it also raises the `DM_RUMBLE_GAIN` clamp from 3 to 25, as the patch in #2148 does.

### Checked (by playing only)

The pad rumbles in game, the log has no rumble report error, and it names the new route:

```
haptics: player 1 controller Pro Controller, rumble through the Pro Controller's own report (Bluetooth, resonant frequencies, gain 12.0, cap 0.85, low share 1.00, curve 1.00, hold 100 ms)
```

With the game's own frequencies and gain 3 the texture felt faithful but very soft, which matches #2148 (the game writes 0.02 to 0.07 for the Switch 2's actuators). What felt best on this pad for this game:

```
DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=12 DM_RUMBLE_PRO_FREQ=1 DM_RUMBLE_PRO_LOW=1 DM_RUMBLE_PRO_HOLD=100
```

It is better than the Core Haptics route, but still not what the game's authors wrote for their own actuators.

### Not checked

- USB (64-byte reports)
- Clones that report 057e:2009 (8BitDo in Switch mode, the pads in #2148)
- Two Pro Controllers at once
- A Switch 1 game
- The host tests

The patch was written with an AI assistant and has not been reviewed.

### Side note

With `DM_RUMBLE_GAIN` in `--env-file`, the settings window's Rumble strength is locked (at 300% with gain 3). That may be intended.

### Patch files

No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.

[pro-rumble-v2.patch.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34887364/pro-rumble-v2.patch.txt)
[pro-rumble.patch.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34887363/pro-rumble.patch.txt)

### Platforms

Mac

I have Mortal Kombat 11 1.0.26 (update v1703936, title ID `0100F2200C984000`, SDK 9.3.1, NVN) working on an Apple M2 Mac through NX Play after local host and shader fixes. Menus, fighter selection, matches and story movies were exercised; I subsequently reported the repaired build working. iOS, online play, all modes and full story completion are unverified. The older local runtime lacked tessellation; current upstream implements it, with MK11 coverage pending.

I would like to contribute the profile and the remaining shared fixes. Per CONTRIBUTING.md, I am opening a scope discussion before proposing the larger shader/profile changes as a PR. The local combined patch is broader than a single concern and includes generated profile metadata, so I am separating it for review.

Current upstream already has overlapping changes, including the advancing network clock. Those will not be resubmitted. The first branch, rebased onto current main, contains three small movie fixes:

- Preserve the SDK graphics allocator setter as well as the host callback record: the MP4 extractor otherwise exhausts the SDK bootstrap heap and a 224-byte SampleTable allocation returns null at a story transition.
- Accept native NVN movie texture objects whose movie::Buffer byte capacity is zero, preserving null/invalid-object rejection.
- Reset AAC converter history and reopen Vorbis atomically with Flush, avoiding old-position audio overlap and a decode-before-reset window.

The remaining local work concerns unsigned LDC offsets, computed bindless sampled-texture handles, fragment output classes selected from attachments, compute-written compressed-texture aliases, pending GPU-write tracking, UE3 package parsing, and optional offline compile deduplication. These have now been reconciled with newer upstream shader work in separate focused drafts, as listed below. The final game profile has 76,865 shader-map hashes, 585 observed material facts and recorded prewarm metadata; it contains no shader bytecode or game files.

Focused movie/native-output/allocator tests and documentation checks pass on the current-main movie branch, including ASan/UBSan and system-encoded stereo/5.1 AAC. The reconciled shader fixes have focused translation/GPU checks as detailed below, but no cross-game regression pass is claimed. No automated validation stamp has been invented.

Would a sequence of focused prerequisite PRs followed by the game-profile PR be the preferred approach? I can provide the detailed findings and test limits in each PR. No game files, keys, saves or extracted shader code will be attached.

Submitted separately as drafts, each based on upstream `23790f8d`:

- [#2798](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2798): movie allocator, native texture buffers and decoder flush.
- [#2799](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2799): MK11 profile and gameplay validation route.
- [#2800](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2800): unsigned Maxwell LDC offsets and constant-buffer bounds.
- [#2801](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2801): growing pending-write tracking.
- [#2802](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2802): compute image writes into compressed aliases.
- [#2807](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2807): fragment output classes selected from attachments, preserving upstream unsigned variants.
- [#2808](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2808): wide UE3 chunks, small-window zlib and control-first shader records.

Computed bindless texture sampling is already supported in current upstream and is not resubmitted. The optional older offline-compile optimizations have not been ported; the newer upstream compiler/cache architecture needs separate measurements first.

For owner testing, [codex/mk11-integration](https://github.com/yubismartlabs/nxnative/tree/codex/mk11-integration) combines those fixes and the profile (candidate commit `f5d46131`, shader chain `238c2c3c6acb`, profile inputs `da4c4f927b27`). It is a test branch, not another combined PR. The profile's `VALIDATION.md` specifies the NX Play rebuild and manual route.

Combined checks ran 89 tests with two expected skips. Component GPU checks passed 30 compressed-alias checks and 64 typed-export cases on each of Metal and Metal 4. The standalone Metal compiler is missing locally, so offline library splitting and macOS/iOS compile checks remain unchecked; those GPU fixtures compiled synthetic MSL at runtime. No integrated game build, current-upstream gameplay, five-game regression report, or automated validation stamp is claimed. The owner will build through NX Play. These drafts remain pending that gameplay evidence and shared-fix regression coverage.

body:
### What is missing

Games that use the Switch 2's microphone get none. `hle_audio.c` lists no input device and fails every open, for the older `AudioIn` calls and for SDK 21's input streams (`ListVirtualInputDevices`, `OpenInputStream`). This keeps games from crashing, and the comments there name the cases:

- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072) asks for the state of its two microphone streams, purges them and reads their statistics each update. It opens them only when a virtual input device is listed, so on the host never.
- Star Fox (`0400E88025B1A000`) imports the input stream calls.
- Absolum lists input devices through SDL3's Switch audio driver when its audio starts.

With engine `94a0944755da` on an M3 Max MacBook Pro (macOS 27.0.1), Ocarina plays, and whatever it does with the microphone is out of reach.

### What you propose

An opt-in setting, off by default, that lets the host capture the device's own microphone and offer it to the game as one input device:

- **Capture.** AVAudioEngine's input node on the Mac and on iOS, converted to what the game asks for in `StreamFormat` / `AudioInParameter` (48 kHz mono PCM16 in the calls seen), into a ring the reads drain.
- **Listing.** `ListVirtualInputDevices` and `ListAudioIns` list one device while the setting is on.
- **Streams.** `OpenInputStream` / `OpenAudioIn` succeed, and `Start`, `Read`, `GetInputStreamFilledFrameCount`, the state and the statistics follow the capture.
- **Off, or permission refused.** Everything stays as now: no device and failed opens.
- **Permission.** `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` in the Mac app and in the iOS shell. The system asks the first time a game opens the device, not at start.

Parts it touches: `dm/host/hle_audio.c` (the `AudioIn` and input stream functions), the Mac and iOS front ends (the capture and the permission), and the settings list for the switch.

### Platforms

Mac, iPhone, iPad

### What happened

Played on an iPhone 18 Pro with a free Apple ID (no Increased Memory Limit), with a save carried over from the Mac app through Cloud saves, through Zora's River into Zora's Domain. Two sessions, both ended by me (app sent to background); no crash and no jetsam termination.

- Memory: "room to the memory limit 7.96 GB" / "7.97 GB" at start. Footprint 3.8-4.9 GB during play, peak 4.83 GB.
- First (cold) run: 8,094 of 21,859 frames dropped, p99 up to 750 ms, frame step "game time 75.28 s in 123.37 s (0.610 of real time)", so the game played in slow motion while pipelines were built on first use (no pipeline archive for iOS in this profile).
- Second (warm) run: 171 of 20,945 frames dropped, 69 of 70 report windows at 30 fps, game time 0.99-1.00 of real time after the first loads (0.648 and 0.831 in the first two windows).
- Thermal state 2 for the whole of both runs.
- The first Zora's Domain load took a few seconds, then played normally. The ocarina works with buttons: Zelda's Lullaby opened the waterfall.
- [RED] lines: only "texture type mismatch" on slot 7 (shaders c0aff0eee66cda0f and 09ab31c69af710c9), the same pattern as the known 9b310b3349825e9a.

Install: Sideloadly 0.72 (x86_64 build, under Rosetta) failed with "PackageExtractionFailed (Could not extract archive)" on every retry, for both the default IPA (3.6 GB) and the --shader-files IPA (6.2 GB, 130,497 files, 6.8 GB uncompressed; `unzip -tq` reports no errors). Both need ZIP64. --prepare-xcode and Run (Release) from Xcode installed it without problems.

### What you expected

Steady 30 fps at full game speed after the first start, which the warm run did. The cold first run's slow motion is the open question: whether a pipeline archive or a longer prewarm list for iOS would avoid it. body:
## Summary

Hades II (`0100A00019DE0000`, 1.0.141667, SDK 20) shows save times in the load screen shifted by the host's UTC offset: a save made at 2026-11-16 01:44:03 KST (UTC+9) is shown as Nov 15, 16:44, which is the UTC time. The save file itself stores the correct time.

The cause is the host's `HLE_FORCE` of `mktime` (and `localtime` / `localtime_r`) in `dm/host/hle_time.c`, which follow the host's system time zone. The SDK's own libc does not: its time zone lookup always returns offset 0 and the name `"UTC"`, so on a Switch `mktime` and `localtime` are UTC.

## Evidence

Mac host, macOS time zone Asia/Seoul. Probes on the PLT stubs of `main` (`DM_PROBE=main:5928b4@0,main:5928c4@x2+0,main:5928d4@0,...`) while opening the save select (`DM_KEYS=f700:A`):

1. The save header's time, `0x6af9e153` (1794761043 = 2026-11-15 16:44:03 UTC), goes to `gmtime_r` (stub `main+0x5928d0`, called from `main+0x4301bc`): a UTC `struct tm` {sec 3, min 44, hour 16, mday 15}.
2. That `struct tm` goes to `mktime` (stub `main+0x5928b0`, lr `main+0x430a4c`).
3. `nn::time::ToCalendarTime` (stub `main+0x5928c0`, lr `main+0x430d18`) then receives `0x6af962c3` = 1794728643, which is **32400 s (9 h) less** than the save time. The host's `mktime` read the UTC `tm` as KST.
4. `ToCalendarTime` converts by the host zone, so the screen shows 16:44, the UTC time.

Backtrace of the `gmtime_r` call: `main+0x4705d4 main+0x46d790 main+0x3d48b8 main+0x3d569c main+0x463268 main+0x2a72c0`.

On a Switch the same game code goes through the SDK's own `mktime` and gets the time back unchanged, so `ToCalendarTime` shows the local time.

## The SDK's libc is UTC only

`sdk` defines `mktime`, `localtime`, `localtime_r`, `gmtime_r` and `timegm`. Its time zone helper (the musl-style `__secs_to_zone`, just before `__tm_to_tzname`) is a fixed stub. Hades II 1.0.141667 `sdk` at `+0x5701b0`:

```
str wzr, [x2]        ; isdst = 0
str xzr, [x3]        ; offset = 0
cbz x4, 1f
str xzr, [x4]        ; oppoff = 0
1: adrp x8, ... ; add x8, x8, #0x680   ; zone name -> "UTC" (sdk+0x9b8680)
str x8, [x5]
ret
```

The same stub is in every `sdk` build checked: Hades II v0, v1 and v655360 (SDK 19/20) and Monster Train 2 v720896 (SDK 18.3.5). So `mktime` and `localtime` are UTC on the console, not "converted by the system time zone" as the comment above the hooks in `hle_time.c` says.

## Suggested fix

Keep the three hooks consistent with each other and with the SDK: implement `localtime` / `localtime_r` with `gmtime_r` and `mktime` with `timegm` (rather than deleting the `HLE_FORCE` entries, so that the pass-through entries in `hle_table.c` do not map them to the host's local-time functions for a game whose SDK lacks a definition). Correct the comment. A host test could check that `mktime(gmtime_r(t)) == t` with `TZ=Asia/Seoul`.

Open question: the hooks came in with d1b1708 (Mario Wonder Mac bring-up), with the note that "a game's local timestamps were off by the time zone's offset". I could not test which display that fixed; it would be worth checking that game, since local time on the console comes from `nn::time::ToCalendarTime` (already hooked to the host zone), not from libc.

## Impact

Display only: the save contents and the stored save time are correct. Any game that turns a UTC `tm` back into seconds with `mktime`, or shows `localtime`, shows times off by the host's UTC offset on a host outside UTC.
title: Host mktime/localtime follow the host time zone, but the SDK's libc is UTC: Hades II save times shown in UTC

Memory was stable in the latest run: resident ~12 GB, GPU allocated ~17 GB, no growth after frame ~7000 (32 GB machine).

Engine log, first real error of the latest run: fence=815034, frame 24313, "Caused GPU Hang Error (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)". 28 passes, 294 game shaders, 1 of 819167 command buffers. Every shader in it had already run in more than 5 earlier command buffers (no first-seen shader). 12 hangs in total, then 412x "Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)". Kernel, 13:55:50.505: IOGPUScheduler::signalHardwareError GPURestartSignaled type=1, GPURestartBegin/End, then "Clean slate for app[dmhost] with 1 GPURestarts".

gpuEvent reports (10, all within 13:55:50, process dmhost, macOS 27.2.1 26B131): 6x "BIF0 page fault", 3x "firmware-detected lockup", 1x "MMU interrupt". Page fault read addresses: 0 (x2), 256, 92923110592, 93001327808, 821412495360 (0xBF40000000). Near-null reads suggest an unbound/zeroed pointer or descriptor. # Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets stuck on a black loading screen after sleeping on macOS

**Game:** Animal Crossing: New Horizons  
**Game version:** 3.0.3  
**Platform:** macOS  
**Hardware:** MacBook Pro with Apple M5 Pro, 24 GB RAM

## Environment
- macOS 27.2.1 (Build 26B131)
- Xcode 27.2 (Build 27B52)
- Homebrew 7.0.13 (ARM64)
- Python 3.15.2 (ARM64)
- Build target: `mac-app`

## Description

The game runs and appears playable during the first day. I can go through the initial setup, create my character and island, talk to Tom Nook, and reach the point where the character goes to sleep.

However, immediately after going to sleep, the game gets stuck on a black screen with an infinite loading animation.

**The next-day wake-up animation never appears.**

After restarting the game, the progress is lost and the game starts from the beginning, at the birthday/name setup.

I also checked the expected save directory:

`~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/01006F8002326000/save/`

The directory is empty, and no save files appear to have been created.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Animal Crossing: New Horizons 3.0.3 using nxnative on macOS.
2. Complete the initial character and island setup.
3. Progress through the first day until the character goes to sleep.
4. Observe the game getting stuck on a black loading screen.
5. Restart the game.
6. The game starts from the beginning instead of loading the created island.

## Expected behavior

The game should complete the transition to the next day, show the wake-up animation, and create a persistent save containing the island progress.

## Actual behavior

The game remains on an infinite black loading screen immediately after sleeping. No wake-up animation appears, and the save directory remains empty. After restarting, all progress is lost.

## Additional information

The game runs reasonably well before reaching this point. The issue appears specifically during the first transition after sleeping.

The application log ends with:

`launcher: the host exited with 0`

I can provide the relevant nxnative logs if needed.

Could this be a known limitation or an issue with device save data / save commit handling on macOS?

Related to #2527 (same mechanism on an 8 GB Mac); this is the iPhone side.

**Setup:** Star Fox (0400E88025B1A000), iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro, 8 GB), iOS 27, LiveContainer. IPA built on Windows from main bee218d9 (shader chain 89f570c7e720) plus some local changes that do not touch guest memory. The pipeline archive was already built by an earlier run, so pipelines are not a factor here: 356 bases from the archive, prepare 3.5 s, prebuild 1,483 pairs all archived.

**What the user sees:** a black screen, then about a minute of a very slow, laggy title screen. Once the game is in play it runs acceptably.

**From the log:**
- The guest pool is 9.00 GB with 5.98 GB of room to the memory limit, so `DM_GUEST_FILE` is on (22 files of 1 GB, sparse, in tmp).
- First frame at 19.4 s. The game's own "Out startup" is 5.9 s.
- From 23 s to about 100 s, while the front end's level packages load, there are repeated whole-frame stalls with the GPU near idle, no new pipelines and no texture uploads:
  - frame 714: 9.86 s
  - frame 1179: 6.36 s
  - frame 232: 3.64 s
  - frame 334: 2.51 s
  - frame 215: 2.04 s
  - about ten more over 1 s
- The `[mem] guest file` lines over the same window:
  - 33 s: 0.63 GB allocated on disk, 449,409 page-ins, logical writes 1.73 GB, footprint 0.52 GB
  - 45 s: 2.40 GB allocated on disk, 522,689 page-ins, logical writes 2.85 GB, footprint 0.52 GB
  - by about 3 min: 4.70 GB on disk, footprint peak 2.49 GB
- So the stalls line up with first touches of the pool: about 1.8 GB of new disk blocks allocated in about 12 s.
- Footprint stays around 0.5 GB of the 5.98 GB room during the whole slow phase, and peaks at 2.49 GB for the session.
- Thermal state reaches 1 at 59 s and 2 at 179 s.

**Suggestion:** back only part of the pool with files. For example, keep the first N GB anonymous, with N sized from the room at start minus a margin, and put only the remainder in files, rather than putting the whole pool in files whenever it exceeds the room. On this run the slow phase never needed more than about 2.5 GB of real memory, so it would have stayed off the disk. The S2Arm fix cited in #2527 is the all-or-nothing version of this idea; a split would keep the protection against jetsam for games that really do fill the pool.

A smaller alternative: preallocate, or touch in the background, the first few GB of the guest files during the pre-`nnMain` setup, so the cost moves out of the game's load.

**Question:** the counting pass ("732 ms to count, every 10 s") could also be blocking. Does it run on a thread that can hold up the guest?

## Measured impact
1. The process ends on a failed submission rather than at a gradual residency ceiling: no texture upload or re-upload occurred inside that submission, while the binding table was rewritten 30 times.
2. Signals preceding the failure are already in the log: deferred-release queue depth, serial table changes and ghost-held skipped. #2522 asks for a degradation path; these counters give it a place to trigger before the abort.
3. #2762 reports the same run's ghost-table observation; this issue is limited to the failure-side trigger.

## Ask
1. Consider hooking the degradation path of #2522 to a failed-submission signal, or to a deferred-release queue / serial-table-change threshold, rather than only to an allocation failure.

## Acceptance
1. Same save, same 6-minute heavy main-hub route: no `cb4 has no uniform buffer bound`, no MTL4 queue errors, no `exit 70`.
2. The hook fires before the abort and the session continues at reduced quality.

## Benefit
1. A long session ends as a quality reduction instead of a process restart; detecting the trigger needs no extra memory.

body:
@seedds

Thanks for the work on this. One observation from a single macOS direct run; all numbers below are read from the log of that run.

## Environment
- M2 Air, 8 GB unified memory, macOS, 30 fps, fixed internal resolution.
- Local self-built nxnative bundle (not a release build).
- Env: `DM_NVN_EVICT_TEX=1`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_AT=3000`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_CAPMB=1024`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_EVERY=120`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_IDLE=600`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_KEEP=16`, `DM_NVN_EVICT_LRU=1`, `DM_GUEST_FILE=0`.
- Route: same save, heavy main-hub run (crowds, tavern, shops, cross-region map loads), about 6 minutes.

## What the log shows
1. Every residency sweep reports objects skipped because the ghost ring still holds them: 15, 18 and 27 in successive sweeps. The same sweeps removed 144 MB, 175 MB and 179 MB; cumulative 459 finished textures / 809 MB.
2. At the peak, `restop` reports the residency set holds 5,482 objects / 4,069 MB, of which textures 4,406 / 2,315 MB. The `memory` line at the same frame: resident 8,599 MB, GPU allocated 9,678 MB, residency set 5,274 MB, while Metal's recommended working set is 5,461 MB.
3. At 246.4 s the run died: first `[RED] stage 1 cb4 has no uniform buffer bound`, then 123 lines of `command buffer execution error: The operation couldn't be completed. (MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain error 1.)`, and `launcher: the host exited with 70` (frame 7,161).

## Failed submission counters
```
[RED] state of the failed submission fence=42917: frame 7152; since the last submission: passes +59, first texture uploads +0, re-uploads +0, serial table changes +30; deferred-release queue 365
```
No texture upload and no re-upload happened inside that submission; the binding table was rewritten 30 times within it; 365 objects were sitting in the deferred-release queue.

## Mechanism as read from source
- In `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` the ghost ring is `enum { NGHOST = 512 }`, a fixed size, with no environment override.
- The comment there states a texture stays resident while any serial entry (live or already finalized) holds it, and only leaves when the ring drops that entry.
- Consequence: each sweep has a batch of objects that cannot move merely because an old holder is still in the ring. That matches the "residency only grows" shape we see.

## Ask
1. Make the ghost ring size or its retention window configurable (or shrink it under memory pressure), so already-finalized holders expire earlier.
2. On a scene load (a batch whose destination textures are >= 16), invalidate the finalized holders of that batch once, instead of waiting for the ring to age them out.
3. When a failed submission has both `serial table changes > 0` and a missing binding, print one line saying the table rewrite caused it, so content bugs and lifetime bugs can be told apart.

## Acceptance
Same save, same 6-minute heavy main-hub route: `ghost-held skipped` drops from 15-27 to single digits; `set` peak stays under 3,800 MB; neither `cb4 has no uniform buffer bound` nor MTL4 queue errors appear again.

## Sample
One run. The residency and reclaim figures before the crash are complete; the failed-submission counters are verbatim from the log. More runs are reproducible on request with the same route.

### What happened

Splatoon Raiders runs at 60 fps almost everywhere, but one level — 明泰孜地下遗迹 三层 (the
"Hunt / FloorDungeon" layout in the RomFS) — drops to a steady 14.6–15.1 fps and stays there
for as long as the player is inside it; 298–300 of every 300 frames are dropped. Leaving the
level restores 58–60 fps immediately. It happens every time, in three separate sessions.

It is GPU-bound, not CPU or memory-bound:

  outside the level (300-frame window ending at frame 9,900)   inside (window ending at 11,400)
  frame time p50   16.66 ms                                   66.20 ms
  GPU p50          13.33 ms                                   62.83 ms
  submit+present   5.07 ms                                    5.89 ms  (unchanged)
  draws per frame  1,174                                      1,339    (+165)
  guest CPU        110 %                                      28 %     (waiting on the GPU)
  frames dropped   0 / 300                                    300 / 300

ΔGPU = +49.5 ms over +165 draws ≈ 0.30 ms per extra draw, which matches the documented cost of
this game's ink passes ("The ink map's passes are a large part in inked scenes: 0.32 ms each",
docs/reference/render…), on the 6400×6400 RG8 ink map.

Ruled out: present (window) MetalFX (on in an earlier session, off in both attached logs — same
cost; it measures p50 1.1–2.0 ms over 600 presents); render scale (this game has no render-scale
stub, so the launcher offers only Handheld/Docked, and the numbers above are already Handheld);
memory/residency churn (commits 619 / 20.8 ms, added 409 / 381 MB, removed 397 inside the level,
comparable to 206 MB / 291 MB outside; footprint 11,208 MiB < the 12,124 MB working set);
shader compilation (new pipelines 0 throughout).

Worth noting: the same boss content is documented at 17.7–19.9 ms median on a 16 GB MacBook Air M2
(docked) in dm/games/0400380020056000/README.md, i.e. this M5 renders that level 3.2× slower.

Possible relatives: #1063 (this game's ink stamps on the 6400×6400 RG8 ink map), #1289 (M5 + Metal 4
GPU fault after 4–6 min; on this same machine an earlier session elsewhere died with GPU out of
memory, GPU allocated 16493 MB vs a 12,124 MB working set, after ~4 minutes), #1290 (dynamic
resolution on this game).

> The log lines above are verbatim from the attached logs. The analysis/summary in this field was
> compiled by DeepSeek (AI) from those logs.

### What you expected

That level to hold ~60 fps like the rest of the game (or at least to be playable); it is the
only level so far that behaves like this.

### Game, title ID and version

Splatoon Raiders, 0400380020056000 — built from a dump folder (base/exefs + base/romfs); the dump carries no control data, so the display version is the placeholder (app 1.0). No update and no DLC packed.

### nxnative commit

not recorded — Mac app 1.4.0, engine ccd834e0-4466493482b5, downloaded 2026-11-14

### Shader chain version

d24f05cf9d78

### How it was built and run

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

### Device and OS

Mac17,3 (Apple M5, 16 GB unified memory), macOS 27.2 (26B123)

### Settings and environment overrides

Settings window: 主机模式 = 掌机模式 (Handheld), 游戏自带超分 = MetalFX, 窗口超分 = 标准 (off),
Metal 4 管线 = 开, 着色器预取 = 开, 性能 HUD = 关. Fullscreen.

From the log (launcher env):
  DM_OPMODE=0            (Handheld)
  DM_UPSCALER=metalfx    (the game's own upscaler replaced by MetalFX)
  DM_LANG=zh-Hans
  DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE unset (present upscaling off/bilinear)

No env.txt, no DM_* variables set by hand.

### Logs

[0400380020056000.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34866240/0400380020056000.log)
[0400380020056000.prev.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34866239/0400380020056000.prev.log)
The Mac app on this machine writes its log to <output folder>/log/<title ID>.log
(here: ~/Documents/SwitchGames/Builds/Mac/log/), not to ~/Library/Logs/nxnative/ — so
scripts/bug_report.py finds nothing and produces an empty report.md. The two files attached are

## Summary

On macOS 26+, a Mac app can open a `RemoteImmersiveSpace` on a nearby Apple Vision Pro. The Mac host could use this to show the running game on a virtual screen in the headset, in stereo 3D built from the game's own depth buffer. The Mac stays the machine that runs the game and paces its frames.

Implemented in #2737.

## Proposal

- **Opt-in setting:** `DM_IMMERSIVE=1` ("Apple Vision Pro" in the Mac settings window) opens the immersive space. The Mac window keeps showing the game.
- **Scene:** a SwiftUI `RemoteImmersiveSpace`, added to the AppKit app through `NSHostingSceneRepresentation`. It draws a screen 2.5 m in front of the player, on a thread of its own at the headset's refresh rate, using the head pose from ARKit. Holding the Digital Crown recenters the screen.
- **Stereo from depth, with no per-game data:**
  - While the setting is on, each present is copied into a ring of host textures, together with that frame's scene depth.
  - The scene depth is the depth attachment with the most depth-writing draws in passes that also have a colour attachment. This passes over shadow maps and other offscreen depth buffers.
  - The draws' viewports give the part of the depth buffer the scene covers. Their depth compare gives which side is the far plane.
  - Depth is affine in 1/distance, so the parallax needs no camera constants from the game. The screen plane follows the nearest things in the scene. Each eye searches along the row so that near surfaces cover far ones.
  - HUD overlays stay in front of the scene.
- **Controls:**
  - `DM_IMMERSIVE_3D` scales the depth effect.
  - `DM_IMMERSIVE_SCREEN` sets the screen's size and position.
  - `DM_IMMERSIVE_SHOT` writes both eyes of a frame to a PNG, for testing without a headset.

## Scope and limits

- Mac only. iOS and the visionOS app itself are unchanged.
- NVN games only. Vulkan and GL games give no depth to the tap and show flat (2D) on the headset screen.
- A HUD takes the depth of the scene behind it. It is drawn in front, but its parallax is not its own.

## Validation

- A new `dm/gfx/tests/t_stereo` test (46 checks under Metal validation) covers:
  - picking the scene depth over a decoy and a shadow map
  - both far-plane sides
  - parallax for far, middle and near markers
  - pinned slots left alone
  - a 2D frame staying flat
- The existing present, NVN and clear tests are unchanged.
- Tested on a physical Vision Pro.
- Open: `scripts/regress.py check --games` across the local games.
title: Show games in 3D on Apple Vision Pro from the Mac (RemoteImmersiveSpace)

body:
Not a bug report against nxnative as far as I can tell: data and a few questions. On this Mac I don't get variable refresh in the game on either screen, and the data points to two different reasons. I'd like to know whether others see the same on macOS 27.2.

**Setup:** Apple silicon Mac, macOS 27.2.1, two screens:
- an LG OLED (2019) on HDMI 2.1, direct (no receiver), VRR on at the TV. macOS lists it at 40–120 Hz (`NSScreen` refresh interval 8.33–25.0 ms), Displays › Refresh rate: Variable.
- the built-in ProMotion display, 24–120 Hz (8.33–41.67 ms).

Game: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072), native fullscreen. **Every game number below is measured on our build** (upstream `0f510fd5` plus picked upstream fixes and our own frame-step and pacer patches), not on upstream main.

**How it was measured:**
- Host: each drawable's `presentedTime`. "On the grid" is the share of on-screen intervals within 0.4 ms of a multiple of 8.33 ms.
- TV: its incoming refresh and vertical total, read once a second during each run.
- Two present paths: upstream's 120 Hz display link, and a link-off path on our fork (`DM_PRESENT_VRR`, not upstream) that presents each frame when its GPU work is done, with `presentAfterMinimumDuration`.
- Probe: a 100-line AppKit test outside nxnative. Native fullscreen, a `CAMetalLayer`, one clear per frame, `MTLCommandBuffer.present(_:afterMinimumDuration:)`, 30 s per phase. The loop is at the end.

**1. LG TV over HDMI** (2026-11-15, n=1 per run)

| what | target | runs | TV signal, every sample | on the 120 Hz grid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| game, display link | 60 | 2 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| game, display link | 120 | 3 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| game, link-off path | 60 | 4 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| game, link-off path | 120 | 5 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| game, window | 60 | 1 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| game, `DM_PRESENT_HZ=90`, one per path (link-off: frame step stuck at 15 fps) | 90 | 2 | 119.97 Hz, vtotal 2251 | 100 % |
| probe, 1/60 s | 60 | 1 (1,796 presents) | 119.97 Hz | 100 %, median 16.67 ms |
| probe, 1/48 s | 48 | 1 (1,201 presents) | 119.97 Hz | 100 %, median **25.01 ms** |

- The game runs cover 2560x1440 and 3840x2160, HDR and SDR. At 15 fps a VRR link would have dropped towards the TV's 40 Hz floor; at 60, to 60.
- Unplugging and re-plugging the cable changed nothing (n=1 per path). HDR10 at 4K 120 arrives as it should: 3840x2160 @ 119.97 Hz, 10-bit, BT.2020.
- At 1/48 s macOS held each probe frame to the next 120 Hz tick (3 × 8.33 ms) instead of showing it after 20.8 ms.
- So on this screen the signal never leaves 120 Hz, with or without nxnative (measured).

**2. Built-in ProMotion display** (2026-11-15; game n=3 per row, probe n=1)

| what | target | fps, mean per run | on the 120 Hz grid |
|---|---|---|---|
| game, display link, 3840x2160 render | 120 | 83.9 / 85.9 / 86.2 | 99.8 / 100.0 / 99.8 % |
| game, link-off path, 3840x2160 render | 120 | 60.4 / 101.9 / 60.9 | 99.3 / 99.4 / 98.7 % |
| game, display link | 60 | 59.3 / 59.3 / 59.4 | 99.7 / 99.8 / 99.6 % |
| game, link-off path | 60 | 59.4 / 59.4 / 59.4 | 99.8 / 99.8 / 99.7 % |
| probe, 1/60 s (1,799 presents) | 60 | – | 100 %, median 16.67 ms |
| probe, 1/48 s (1,441 presents) | 48 | – | **0.0 %**, median **20.83 ms** |

- The screen varies: the same probe that sits on the 120 Hz grid over HDMI gets 20.83 ms frames here (measured).
- The game does not: at the 120 target, under load, less than 1 % of intervals fall between 8.7 and 16.3 ms (60–120 fps) on either path. The link-off path held 2 ticks for about 90 % of frames in 2 of 3 runs, and 1 tick for 86 % in the third (measured).
- Read on upstream main (`4258c22a9`), not measured there: the frame step holds each frame for a whole number of 1/120 s ticks (`nvn_fstep.h`), the present follows that hold with `presentAfterMinimumDuration` (`present_itv` in `hle_nvn.c`), and fullscreen on a variable-refresh screen goes through the 120 Hz display link (`link_vrr_120`). #2181 (closed, Breath of the Wild) describes the same starting point: the game's clock moves in whole vsyncs, and frames shown at their own pace need a fractional step the game takes through its own stubs. If I read that right, frames on the grid are how it is meant to work for OoT today, not a fault.

**When the HDMI behaviour changed (inferred):** the TV's own refresh history shows variable rates from this Mac up to 2026-11-10: 39–107 Hz over a 56-minute OoT session, and 42–84 Hz on 11-06. That was on macOS 26.6.2. The Mac updated to 27.2.1 on 2026-11-11, and every session since has read a fixed 59/60/119/120 Hz, with a single 112 Hz reading. Same TV, input, cable and TV settings. Our game build changed in between too, but the probe takes the game out of it. macOS can't be rolled back here, so the update as the cause is inferred, not proven. Not yet reported to Apple.

**Separate, smaller point, screen match:** with `DM_SCREEN_MATCH` at its default, a 60 fps game in fullscreen switches the TV from the variable mode (119.97 Hz, vertical total 2251) to a fixed 120 Hz mode (120.02 Hz, 2250) at start and back at exit. Each switch relocks HDMI: a black flash, and the TV announces game mode and HDR again. With VRR not working it buys nothing here, so I keep `DM_SCREEN_MATCH=0`. Not a request to change the default, just a note for anyone who sees the flash.

**Related:** #347 / #348, PR #1967 and #2181 (ProMotion built-in: frame step, display link in fullscreen, a fractional step) are the background to part 2. #2362 (fixed-rate external screen, a refresh late), PR #1045 and PR #2730 (link choice and pacing) are about something else as far as I can tell: in part 1 the signal itself never leaves 120 Hz.

**Questions:**
1. Does anyone see VRR work over HDMI on macOS 27.2, with nxnative or anything else? A TV of another make would tell whether it is this TV with 27.2.
2. On a ProMotion screen in fullscreen, is the 120 Hz grid the intended behaviour for OoT for now (whole-tick holds, as #2181 describes), or is there a switch for frames at their own pace between 60 and 120 that I've missed?
3. Would a line in the frame-rate docs help ("on macOS 27.2.1 an HDMI VRR screen may stay at a fixed rate; check with ...")?
4. Is the probe a fair reference for "macOS drives VRR on this screen"? It varies on the built-in display and stays on the grid over HDMI, on the same Mac.

**Not known:**
- One TV model, one Mac.
- The game numbers are from our build, not upstream main. The probe numbers involve no nxnative code.

The core of the probe loop:

```swift
layer.maximumDrawableCount = 3; layer.displaySyncEnabled = true
while CACurrentMediaTime() < end {
    guard let d = layer.nextDrawable(), let cb = queue.makeCommandBuffer() else { continue }
    let rp = MTLRenderPassDescriptor()
    rp.colorAttachments[0].texture = d.texture
    rp.colorAttachments[0].loadAction = .clear; rp.colorAttachments[0].storeAction = .store
    cb.makeRenderCommandEncoder(descriptor: rp)?.endEncoding()
    d.addPresentedHandler { dr in record(dr.presentedTime) }
    cb.present(d, afterMinimumDuration: interval)   // 1/60, then 1/48
    cb.commit()
}
```
title: Mac, macOS 27.2.1: no variable refresh in fullscreen. HDMI TV stays at a fixed 120 Hz (also outside nxnative); on the built-in ProMotion display frames stay on the 120 Hz grid

body:
## Summary

- **On a base M2 MacBook Air, current main repeatedly falls into a GPU-bound slow mode after the Kokiri Forest area load.** Frames go from about 32–34 ms to 40–55 ms, with the GPU 95–100 % busy at full clock. The mode switches on and off within a run.
- **It's real, not machine drift.** Old main (7f50222003) and current main, alternated back to back on the same machine in the same hour, spent 11 % and 11 % against 62 % and 71 % of their 250-frame windows in the slow mode.
- **The share of slow windows rises in two steps:**
  - between 26062f9e and 356a7132 (about 10 % → 50 %)
  - between 356a7132 and 0c8a3ac0 (about 50 % → 100 %), where it's one of 04811a63 and 0c8a3ac0, since the host commits in between measure the same as 356a7132

  The first window overlaps the ~0.8 ms step between 26062f9e and 81906931 that was measured on an M4 Pro in [#1789](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/discussions/1789#discussioncomment-19553752) and not yet identified. On this machine it shows up as a mode that takes over much of the run, not a fixed cost.
- **On this hardware it means 60 fps isn't held, and the 30 fps cap isn't held either.** This fits [#2213](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/2213) (M1 Pro) and [#2629](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/2629) (M3 Pro).

**What it points to**

- **Small costs grow on smaller GPUs.** A change that adds well under a millisecond on an M4 Pro can, on a base M2, push enough frames past a vsync to change how a whole run plays. The two steps above look like that: modest on a fast Mac, a large share of slow windows here.
- **The baseline drifted and then came back, more by offset than by removal.** Measured on the fast windows only (250-frame windows under 38 ms, same route positions), against old main:

  | Build | Fast-window p50 vs old main |
  |---|---|
  | 7f50222003 (old main) | 0 |
  | 26062f9e | +1.2 ms |
  | 356a7132 | +3.6 ms |
  | 380ff71a | +4.1 ms |
  | main b06f4e0e | +0.6 ms |

  On main it's back within about 0.6 ms, matching the M4 Pro result in #1789 (main within about 0.2 ms of the build before 26062f9e). Part of that came from changes that removed the cost, such as [#2066](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2066) for the uniform bounds. Part looks like unrelated speed-ups offsetting it: b001c49b's ~1 ms on this machine, for example, is still on main. So there may be a few milliseconds left to gain here beyond old main, as well as the slow mode to fix.
- **Low-end Macs see these effects first.** That makes them a useful early signal rather than an edge case.

## The machine, up front

- **MacBook Air M2**, 8-core CPU, **10-core GPU**, **16 GB** unified memory, fanless, macOS 27.0, on AC power.
- That's the **base** chip, not a Pro or Max. It has about 100 GB/s of memory bandwidth, against 273 GB/s on an M4 Pro.
- It's also the **M2 generation (Apple8 GPU)**. That predates the M3/M4 Dynamic Caching, which sizes registers per shader, and the M4's architecture changes.
- So this is one of the more fragile Macs the project runs on. Costs per frame that barely register on a Pro, Max, M4 or newer chip (memory bandwidth, register pressure, work per draw) can add up to several milliseconds here, or push a frame past a vsync.

## How we measured

- **Route:** `route4_long`, scripted input from the Kokiri Forest save, past the area load, to frame 12000. Input and the guest clock are deterministic (`DM_DETCLOCK`), so frame *f* shows the same scene in every run, and draw counts are checked per run.
- **Settings:** handheld 1440x810, `DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=0`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, 60 fps cap, fullscreen, `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`.
- **Builds:** plain main at each point, each with its own full shader library (42,848 shaders) and host, and a warm pipeline archive. Host-only steps reuse the library of the commit whose shader chain they share.
- **Metric:** the share of 250-frame windows (from frame 1000) averaging 38 ms or more. p50 is reported beside it. Once the mode is common, identical runs spread 5–10 ms, so a point's verdict is its mean share over at least 2 runs.
- **Conditions flagged per run, and runs redone when hit:**
  - other-process load
  - a covered or backgrounded window
  - stall frames (≥ 300 ms with ≥ 70 % in the sync wait)
  - paging and memory footprint
  - GPU clock

## Results

| Build | Commit | Slow share | p50 (ms) | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old main | [7f50222003](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/7f50222003) | ~9 % | 31.4–34.6 | 5 |
| | [79741184](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/79741184) | 0–16 % | 33.6–33.8 | 2 |
| | [26062f9e](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/26062f9e) ([#1860](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1860)) | 9–11 % | 33.8–34.4 | 2 |
| | [356a7132](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/356a7132) ([#1897](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1897)) | ~47 % | 36.9–38.4 | 2 |
| 356a7132 + the host commits after it | c68706f9, 68869cca, [8d5d4f1b](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/8d5d4f1b) ([#1492](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1492)), [81906931](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/81906931) ([#1917](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1917)) | 28–66 % (as 356a7132) | 36.7–38.8 | 1 each |
| | [04811a63](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/04811a63) | *pending* | | |
| | [0c8a3ac0](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/0c8a3ac0) | 100 % | 41.8 | 1 |
| | 380ff71a | 45–100 % | 37.7–47.8 | 3 |
| main | b06f4e0e | 48–98 % | 34–54 | 6+ |

**Crossed control** (one machine, one hour, alternating):

| Order | Build | p50 (ms) | Slow share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7f50222003 | 32.5 | 11 % |
| 2 | main | 34.9 | 62 % |
| 3 | 7f50222003 | 34.6 | 11 % |
| 4 | main | 44.6 | 71 % |

Pending: 04811a63 (splits the second step) and e121931f, a point between 26062f9e and 356a7132 (narrows the first).

**Checked, and not the cause of the slow mode:**
- 26062f9e on its own
- 356a7132
- cfbdd93c
- 81906931: `DM_NVN_FB_DEPTH=0` stays slow
- 8d5d4f1b, c68706f9, 68869cca
- the NDVE engine: title movie only
- the upscaler path: a main run with OoT's upscaler drawn by MetalFX also went slow
- paging and memory footprint: main pages less than old main in steady state
- pipeline compilation during play: warm archives, and the slow windows are GPU-bound, not waiting on the CPU

## Related measurements on this machine

- **[#2574](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2574)** (draws count for occlusion queries only while a later report can see them), on main b06f4e0e: frame p50 −11.7 ms [−24.2, −4.4], GPU p50 −3.8 ms, in-run A/B over 20 clean pairs.
- **Uniform bounds from [#1860](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1860):** in 26062f9e's form, every uniform read guarded with a ternary, the four hottest pixel shaders run 10–31 % slower. As `select()`, the same guard costs nothing (offline, −0.5 %). Main's remaining computed-offset guards, after [#2066](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2066), cost about 0.1–0.3 ms here.
- **[b001c49b](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/b001c49b) ([#1936](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1936))**, resolution families uncompressed: about +1.0–1.1 ms of GPU a frame on this machine (offline). [#2573](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2573) restores compression for OoT.
- **[0662f9d8](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/0662f9d8) ([#2030](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2030))** adds code to the end of every pixel shader with a float4 output. It's after the window above and not yet sized here.
- **First start on main** prebuilds about 34,600 pipeline pairs before the first frame: 45–60 minutes cold on this machine.

## Why it shows on a small Mac and not a large one

- **Headroom hides changes.** At about 13 ms against a 16.7 ms frame, a millisecond more or less doesn't change the frame rate, and 0.3–0.9 ms is close to the run-to-run spread of GPU time.
- **Some costs scale with what the base chips have less of:**
  - **memory bandwidth:** about 100 GB/s here, against 273 on an M4 Pro
  - **registers:** without Dynamic Caching, a shader at its register limit spills
  - **memory:** 16 GB sits much closer to paging than 36–48 GB
- **Frame-rate tiers turn small costs into large ones.** Near the 60→30 or 30→20 step, a small cost pushes some frames past a vsync, and the frame step can hold the game at the lower tier.
- **The two kinds of machine complement each other.** Larger Macs give cleaner GPU-time deltas, with stable clocks and little noise. Smaller Macs show whether a delta changes what a player sees, but need repeated runs, because heat, memory and the slow mode vary between runs.

## Suggestion

Most measurements in [#1789](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/discussions/1789) and in these commits come from M4 Pro, M5 and M6 machines. Where the cost is small there, it can be a frame-rate tier on a base M1/M2. A low-end data point (a base M1/M2 with 16 GB, or an 8 GB machine) for changes on the per-draw or per-shader path, even a short fixed-route run, would catch this kind of drift earlier. Our route and per-run data are available if they help.
