title: DIABLO III Eternal Collection Failed Build

body:
### What happened

**The exact rounding that #1897 brought (356a7132: each block of 8 products summed in a `simdgroup_float8x8`) makes the translated HMMA helper about 3.4 times slower on an M2 Pro. Ocarina of Time's docked upscaler network takes 4.6 ms a dispatch with it and 1.3 ms with the plain half products the helper had before, which is about 3 ms of a 21 to 24 ms frame.** The commit measured +14 % on an M5 Max and says "Not measured in a game", so I think the cost on older GPUs was not known. It happens every frame. Nothing looks wrong; it is only slow.

It is the upscaler row of my [per-pass profile in #1789](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/discussions/1789#discussioncomment-19614165) (4.66 ms for the chain's four dispatches, 18 % of the frame) and of the [numbers I left on #1951](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1951#issuecomment-6879129175). The heaviest of the four is the network level `fa3033d05c0a41d6` (`agl_ndsr_vr_light.pck`): 4.36 ms alone in the game (`DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1`).

#### The kernel alone

A small Metal harness (under Logs) builds the compute pipeline from the kernel's MSL as the build wrote it (`fa3033d05c0a41d6_b.metal`), compiled with the chain's flags (`-O1 -mmacosx-version-min=26.6 -fpreserve-invariance -fwrapv`), sets `dm_border_off` as the host does, and times 240 back-to-back dispatches of the docked grid with placeholder inputs; median of the last 120, no game running. The docked grid is 40x45 threadgroups of 128 threads (1920x1080 to 2560x1440). The kernel is straight-line code (176 helper calls, no loops), so placeholder inputs do the same work: about 5 million 8x8 matrix products a dispatch.

| `dmsh_hmma16816_f16`'s products | GPU ms a dispatch |
|---|---:|
| As on main: float sums, each block rounded per lane | 4.58 |
| The same, one weight pair held instead of 58 | 4.39 |
| The same, no `simdgroup_barrier` in the helper | 4.54 |
| Float sums, one rounding a call (no longer exact) | 3.26 |
| **Plain half multiply-accumulates, as before 356a7132** | **1.33** |
| No products at all (the rest of the kernel) | 0.76 |
| Every operand widened to float | 33.9 |

- The four products of a call cost about 3.8 ms as built and about 0.6 ms as half products.
- It is not register pressure: `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` is 384 in every row (static threadgroup memory 9,728 bytes), and holding one weight pair instead of 58 changes the time by 4 %. Barriers cost nothing measurable.
- A second session repeated the first and fifth rows: 4.72 to 4.77 ms and 1.33 ms. The half-product library that the game then ran also takes 1.33 ms.
- At the handheld grid (30x34, 1440x810 to 1920x1080): 2.55 against 0.77 ms.
- The other two levels my play has built, on the docked grid with placeholder inputs (not their own dispatch sizes): `8df148d58b7cbe8e` 5.11 against 1.43 ms, `d99fbeeb53d38847` 5.09 against 1.45 ms.
- The pipeline also builds slower with the float form: 9.2 to 9.4 s against 1.2 to 1.3 s for this kernel, uncached.

#### By GPU

Your figures from 356a7132 and the [reference entry](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/shaders.md#hmma-rounds-its-f16-accumulator-once-per-8-products) beside mine:

| GPU, what was timed | Float sums | Half products | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| M5 Max, `fa3033d05c0a41d6` isolated | 0.316 ms | 0.276 ms | 1.14 |
| M5 Max, `d99fbeeb53d38847` isolated | 0.446 ms | 0.393 ms | 1.13 |
| M6, a chain of 258 calls, 2,048 threadgroups | 2.56 ms | 1.69 ms | 1.51 |
| **M2 Pro, `fa3033d05c0a41d6`, docked grid** | **4.58 ms** | **1.33 ms** | **3.4** |
| M2 Pro, `fa3033d05c0a41d6`, handheld grid | 2.55 ms | 0.77 ms | 3.3 |
| M2 Pro, `8df148d58b7cbe8e`, docked grid | 5.11 ms | 1.43 ms | 3.6 |
| M2 Pro, `d99fbeeb53d38847`, docked grid | 5.09 ms | 1.45 ms | 3.5 |

#### In the game

The app headless from two test saves, standing still for about two and a half minutes, docked: as built against the same build with the half-product kernel as a loose `fa3033d05c0a41d6_b.metallib` beside the image, nothing else changed.

| Scene | GPU p50 as built | With half products | Saving |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Hyrule Field (child) | 24.15 ms | 21.2 ms | 2.95 ms |
| Kokiri Forest (in front of Link's house) | 21.4 ms | 18.35 ms | 3.05 ms |

- No GPU hang, page fault or crash in any run.
- At full size the screenshots show no dotted rows, blotches or loss of detail beside the as-built ones. What moves between two runs (Navi, clouds, leaves) is larger than any difference the kernel makes, so the pictures neither show nor exclude a small one.
- I then played with it for an evening and kept it.
- Both scenes still run at 30 fps on this Mac. It is 3 ms of the distance to a frame that holds 60.

### What you expected

The exact form where it is cheap, and the half products where it is not.

One library serves every Mac, so the choice has to be made when the pipeline is built. A function constant in `HMMA_BODY`, as `dm_border_off` is, could select the form, set by the host per GPU family, with a setting to force either.

I tried that on this kernel: a `constant bool` at index 217 around the two forms, one library (the diff is under Logs). With the constant unset it takes 4.72 ms and with it set 1.33 ms, the same as the two separate builds, so the constant itself costs nothing. It would be a chain change in `dmsh_rewrite.py` plus the constant in the host's compute specialization. `ndve_engine.metal`'s `hmma()` sums the same way since 356a7132, so the movie network would want the same choice.

What the half form gives up is what the reference entry says: values a few f16 steps off the console's in about half of each HMMA's outputs, as every build before 356a7132 had.

I did not find an exact form that is cheap here. Float sums with a single rounding a call, which is no longer exact, still take 3.26 ms.

Not measured:

- Any other GPU. I have only this M2 Pro (`MTLGPUFamilyApple8`), so I cannot say where the line is: an M1, an M3 and an M4 would tell. #2501 (M1 Pro, the upscaler about 5 ms a frame) may be this; I have not checked it.
- The NDVE movie network on this Mac (#1375 is that network on an M1 Max).
- The picture against the exact kernel's on a frame with nothing moving.
- `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx` since 9e0ddeeb (#1459, #1911), which draws this network with MetalFX. My tree is from before it. This report is about the default (`game`) and about every other HMMA shader; #1334's tensor path is for Apple10 GPUs.

Until the chain has a choice I carry a per-game rewrite in the Ocarina profile (`shader_msl.py`) that gives its three in-play network levels the half products. I am glad to test a branch on this Mac.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072.

### nxnative commit

`e0cf2ac7` plus PR #2532 and local changes. `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_rewrite.py` is main's, byte for byte, and `HMMA_BODY` is the same on today's main (`bee218d9`).

### Shader chain version

`7266ef588d05` (the local tree; plain `e0cf2ac7` is `c030a898168d`).

### How it was built and run

`python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NSP folder> -k <prod.keys> --platform mac-app`; all 42,848 shaders built. The in-game numbers are the host's GPU time p50 from headless runs of the app. The half-product kernel was a loose library in a folder `b-7266ef588d05/` beside the image, which the host reads first, with the title's `pso_archive/` moved aside so it could not hide the changed library. The kernel-alone numbers are the harness below with no game running.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro M2 Pro (19-core GPU, 32 GB), macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2 (Metal compiler 32023.922), `applegpu_g14s`.

### Settings and environment overrides

Docked, Dynamic resolution off, Render scale 1.0, `DM_UPSCALER` at its default. `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1` only in the run that timed the dispatch alone.

### Logs

No GPU hang, page fault or crash in any run. The kernel's MSL is translated from the game's shader, so I am not attaching it: it is `fa3033d05c0a41d6_b.metal` in any Ocarina of Time library. The two diffs below touch only lines that come from `HMMA_BODY`.

<details>
<summary>The half products (the fifth row of the table)</summary>

```diff
-    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f0, am[0], b0, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f1, am[2], b0, c1);
-    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { c0.thread_elements()[i] = half(f0.thread_elements()[i]); c1.thread_elements()[i] = half(f1.thread_elements()[i]); }   // the first block's rounding
-    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f0, am[1], b1, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f1, am[3], b1, c1);
-    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { c0.thread_elements()[i] = half(f0.thread_elements()[i]); c1.thread_elements()[i] = half(f1.thread_elements()[i]); }
+    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c0, am[0], b0, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c1, am[2], b0, c1);
+    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c0, am[1], b1, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c1, am[3], b1, c1);
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>The function-constant prototype (4.72 ms unset, 1.33 ms set)</summary>

```diff
 constant bool dm_border_off [[function_constant(216)]];
 constant bool dm_border_live = !is_function_constant_defined(dm_border_off) || !dm_border_off;
+constant bool dm_hmma_half [[function_constant(217)]];
+constant bool dm_hmma_exact = !is_function_constant_defined(dm_hmma_half) || !dm_hmma_half;
```

```diff
+    if (dm_hmma_exact) {
     simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f0, am[0], b0, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f1, am[2], b0, c1);
     for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { c0.thread_elements()[i] = half(f0.thread_elements()[i]); c1.thread_elements()[i] = half(f1.thread_elements()[i]); }   // the first block's rounding
     simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f0, am[1], b1, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(f1, am[3], b1, c1);
     for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { c0.thread_elements()[i] = half(f0.thread_elements()[i]); c1.thread_elements()[i] = half(f1.thread_elements()[i]); }
+    } else {
+    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c0, am[0], b0, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c1, am[2], b0, c1);
+    simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c0, am[1], b1, c0); simdgroup_multiply_accumulate(c1, am[3], b1, c1);
+    }
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>The harness (bench.swift) and how to run it</summary>

```sh
xcrun -sdk macosx metal -c -O1 -mmacosx-version-min=26.6 -fpreserve-invariance -fwrapv fa3033d05c0a41d6_b.metal -o k.air
xcrun -sdk macosx metallib k.air -o k.metallib
swiftc -O bench.swift -o bench
./bench k.metallib 40 45                        # docked: 1920x1080 to 2560x1440
./bench k.metallib 30 34 1440 810 1920 1080     # handheld
ARG_BASE=1 ./bench d99f.metallib 40 45          # d99fbeeb53d38847 binds a support buffer first
HMMA_HALF=1 ./bench prototype.metallib 40 45    # sets function constant 217 of the prototype
```

```swift
// Throwaway benchmark: builds a compute pipeline from one translated Switch shader library (the NDSR upscaler kernel),
// prints the thread limit the GPU compiler gave it (which falls as the kernel takes more registers on M1 / M2 GPUs),
// and times dispatches of the real grid size with placeholder inputs. Usage: bench <metallib> <groupsX> <groupsY> [inW inH outW outH]
// ARG_BASE=1 in the environment is for a kernel that binds a support buffer first (d99fbeeb53d38847: its reflection lists
// support_buffer at argument 0 and the others one higher); without it that kernel reads unbound memory and the GPU faults.
import Foundation
import Metal

let a = CommandLine.arguments
let gx = Int(a[2])!, gy = Int(a[3])!
let inW = a.count > 4 ? Int(a[4])! : 1920, inH = a.count > 5 ? Int(a[5])! : 1080
let outW = a.count > 6 ? Int(a[6])! : 2560, outH = a.count > 7 ? Int(a[7])! : 1440
let dev = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()!
let lib = try dev.makeLibrary(URL: URL(fileURLWithPath: a[1]))
// The border-colour corrections are specialized off (function constant 216), as the host does for this game.
let cv = MTLFunctionConstantValues(); var off = true; cv.setConstantValue(&off, type: .bool, index: 216)
// HMMA_HALF=1 sets function constant 217, which v_fconst.diff adds to the kernel: the helper then takes plain half products
// instead of the exact float sums (the prototype of one library serving both). Other kernels have no such constant.
if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["HMMA_HALF"] == "1" { var on = true; cv.setConstantValue(&on, type: .bool, index: 217) }
let fn = try lib.makeFunction(name: "main0", constantValues: cv)
let t0 = Date()
let pso = try dev.makeComputePipelineState(function: fn)
print(String(format: "%@: pipeline built in %.2f s; maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup %d, static threadgroup memory %d",
             dev.name, Date().timeIntervalSince(t0), pso.maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup, pso.staticThreadgroupMemoryLength))

// The kernel takes one argument buffer (descriptor set 0): constants, weights, input texture, samplers, output image
// and the border-colour table. Contents are placeholders: the matrix work does not branch on them.
let enc = fn.makeArgumentEncoder(bufferIndex: 0)
let argBuf = dev.makeBuffer(length: enc.encodedLength, options: .storageModeShared)!
enc.setArgumentBuffer(argBuf, offset: 0)
let cbuf = dev.makeBuffer(length: 65536, options: .storageModeShared)!
let sbuf = dev.makeBuffer(length: 65536, options: .storageModeShared)!
let border = dev.makeBuffer(length: 1024, options: .storageModeShared)!
// Weights as small f16 values (0x3400 = 0.25) so the products stay finite.
let w = sbuf.contents().bindMemory(to: UInt16.self, capacity: 32768)
for i in 0..<32768 { w[i] = 0x3400 }
// Texel size where the game keeps a scale pair (constant vector 2); harmless if it means something else.
let c = cbuf.contents().bindMemory(to: Float.self, capacity: 16384)
c[8] = 1.0 / Float(inW); c[9] = 1.0 / Float(inH)
let ti = MTLTextureDescriptor.texture2DDescriptor(pixelFormat: .rgba16Float, width: inW, height: inH, mipmapped: false)
ti.usage = .shaderRead; ti.storageMode = .private
let to = MTLTextureDescriptor.texture2DDescriptor(pixelFormat: .rgba16Float, width: outW, height: outH, mipmapped: false)
to.usage = [.shaderWrite, .shaderRead]; to.storageMode = .private
let tin = dev.makeTexture(descriptor: ti)!, tout = dev.makeTexture(descriptor: to)!
let sd = MTLSamplerDescriptor(); sd.minFilter = .linear; sd.magFilter = .linear; sd.supportArgumentBuffers = true
let smp = dev.makeSamplerState(descriptor: sd)!
// The first argument index of the layout below: 0, or 1 behind a zeroed support buffer (see ARG_BASE above).
let base = Int(ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["ARG_BASE"] ?? "0")!
let support = dev.makeBuffer(length: 65536, options: .storageModeShared)!
if base == 1 { enc.setBuffer(support, offset: 0, index: 0) }
enc.setBuffer(cbuf, offset: 0, index: base); enc.setBuffer(sbuf, offset: 0, index: base + 1)
enc.setTexture(tin, index: base + 2); enc.setSamplerState(smp, index: base + 3)
enc.setTexture(tout, index: base + 4); enc.setSamplerState(smp, index: base + 5)
enc.setBuffer(border, offset: 0, index: base + 6)

let q = dev.makeCommandQueue()!
let lock = NSLock(); var times = [Double]()
let n = 240   // back to back, so the GPU clock is up for the later ones; the median of the last half is reported
var last: MTLCommandBuffer?
for _ in 0..<n {
    let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer()!
    let ce = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder()!
    ce.setComputePipelineState(pso)
    ce.setBuffer(argBuf, offset: 0, index: 0)
    ce.useResource(cbuf, usage: .read); ce.useResource(sbuf, usage: .read); ce.useResource(border, usage: .read); ce.useResource(support, usage: .read)
    ce.useResource(tin, usage: .read); ce.useResource(tout, usage: .write)
    ce.dispatchThreadgroups(MTLSize(width: gx, height: gy, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 128, height: 1, depth: 1))
    ce.endEncoding()
    cb.addCompletedHandler { b in lock.lock(); times.append((b.gpuEndTime - b.gpuStartTime) * 1000); lock.unlock()
        if let e = b.error { print("GPU error:", e.localizedDescription) } }
    cb.commit(); last = cb
}
last!.waitUntilCompleted()
let tail = times.suffix(n / 2).sorted()
print(String(format: "%dx%d groups: GPU ms per dispatch, last %d: min %.3f  p50 %.3f  max %.3f", gx, gy, tail.count, tail.first!, tail[tail.count / 2], tail.last!))
```

</details>

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: HMMA's exact f16 rounding (356a7132) costs about 3 ms a frame on an M2 Pro: Ocarina of Time's upscaler network takes 4.6 ms a dispatch against 1.3 with half products

body:
## What happens

Pokémon Legends: Arceus (`01001F5010DFA000`, base v0 + update **v262144 / 1.1.1**) aborts about **72 s after launch**, at frame ~2114, when the host-lent command-memory cap is reached. Reproduced in two consecutive runs, one frame apart.

## Environment

- MacBook Air **M3** (8-core, fanless), **24 GB**, macOS **26.7.1**
- Xcode **27.2** (27B52), Metal toolchain **32023.922.4**
- nxnative **main `f644af4b`**, profile `01001F5010DFA000`
- Build: `python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<folder>" -k prod.keys --platform mac-app`
  - extraction 19,101 files / 6.0 GB, registered profile (no derived profile)
  - **12,851 of 12,851 shaders** compiled (13:32), pipeline archive `applegpu_g15g` 879 MB (6:36)
  - **zero `[RED]` lines during the whole build**

## Log

```

Multiple build-stage hurdles were encountered and resolved before reaching runtime: ### 1. Title ID & DLC Packaging (`scripts/pack_nup.py`) - **Error**: `[RED] base program ID 0400453019AA8001 is not a base title ID (it must end in 000)` - **Cause**: Switch 2 Edition uses program index `001` (`...8001`) as its base executable. - **Fix**: Updated `pack_nup.py` to allow `app & 0xFFF in (0, 1)` and compute DLC base offsets accordingly. ### 2. NVN2 Control Block Truncation in HCPS (`dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`) - **Error**: `main#SLCT@0x18a01a0 HCPS: truncated control section` - **Cause**: Switch 2 NVN2 shaders have minimum control section headers of 72 bytes (`0x48`, `NVN2_KEY_CTL`), whereas the HCPS splitter strictly expected Maxwell/NVN1 control sections (0x760/0x880 bytes). - **Fix**: Added `nvn2_ctl` validation to use `NVN2_KEY_CTL` (0x48) when parsing NVN2 blocks. ### 3. New Archive Format: `arh2` Headers (`dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`) - **Issue**: Shaders were not being found in `sts.ard` and `common.ard` because Monolith Soft uses a newer **`arh2`** archive table. - **Cause**: Legacy `arh1` used 24-byte records with filename hashes and directory offsets. `arh2` uses 16-byte records: - `u64`: Hash - `u32`: Compressed size (`comp_sz`) - `u32`: Uncompressed size (`raw_sz`) - **Fix**: Added `arh2` parsing in `shader_split.py` (`arh_entries` and `arh_jobs`), successfully extracting and splitting **24,779 shaders**. ### 4. Missing Runtime Shaders (`DM_NVN_SHDUMP`) - On first boot into 3D gameplay, the screen was black and the runtime reported 7 missing shaders: - Vertex: `d0ba4ced4aa25533`, `072668a941597745`, `3b599698f49b275d` - Pixel: `4320c7f2f73529ae`, `ceb8e88f9daf265d`, `f530fece9436e9ad` - Compute: `0e4b92bf11da4a8d` (56 KB compute shader) - Dumped these 7 shaders via `DM_NVN_SHDUMP` and placed them into `extract/v0/glslc_capture/`. ### 5. Compute Shader Driver Constant Bounds Crash (`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py`) - **Error**: `IndexError: index out of range` in `dmsh_build.py` line 426: ```python if stage == 'cs': extra['nvn2_cs'] = [rec[ci + 0xb1], rec[ci + 0xb2], rec[ci + 0xb3], struct.unpack_from('= ci + 0xbc:`. - **Result**: All 24,786 shaders successfully translated to SPIR-V and compiled into Metal binaries (`vs_other.bin`, `ps_other.bin`, `cs_other.bin`). --- ### Current Runtime Symptoms (Persistent Every Time) Even after all 24,786 shaders are compiled and packaged into the Mac app: 1. **In-Engine 3D Gameplay is completely black**: - The game runs at a solid 60.00 FPS (frame interval ~16.5 ms). - Audio, player movement, physics collision, camera rotation, and 2D HUD (radar, player coordinates, target reticles, achievement toasts) function normally. - Pre-rendered `.mp4` video cutscenes display properly. - Any in-engine 3D world rendering (geometry, models, landscape) is 100% black. 2. **2D Textures, Fonts, and UI Elements show comb-like horizontal interlacing**: - Game logo, dialog fonts, and HUD icons show horizontal line shifting/interleaving artifacts, pointing to a block-linear / GOB untiling stride or tile height mismatch in `deswz.metal` / `nvn_deswizzle_gpu.m`. ### What you expected - body:
### What happened

Pokémon Legends: Z-A (`0100F43008C44000`) plays fine at 30 fps, then the host aborts about 77 s in with:

```
FATAL NVN command memory: the game's pool is empty and host-lent segments reached 1024 MB without being reclaimed by the game's blocks
```

The same setup worked the day before I rebuilt. I suspect a regression from `0d103787` ("a lent command memory segment is freed when its list is written over, not when memory over it is granted"). I have not bisected or rebuilt without that commit yet.

### What you expected

## Environment

- Mac app, built from commit `3e628a0d86ec` (shader chain `d254f45e8002`)
- Apple M1 Max, MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,2), macOS 27.2.1
- Game version: [2.0.2 / 1.0.0], built on [date/time] this morning
- Fullscreen, Pro Controller, default settings otherwise (`DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`)
- Previous build (worked): around 11/7

## What happens

- The game boots and plays at a steady 30 fps (frame time p50 33.3 ms, GPU about 17 ms, footprint about 3.9 GB). There is no GPU error and no missing shader.
- The host log keeps printing "the game's command memory ran short, the host lends a segment of 256 KB". The count only goes up:

| Frame | Segments lent so far |
|---|---|
| 603 | 1,024 |
| 1,260 | 2,048 |
| 1,772 | 3,072 |
| 2,180 | 4,096 (1,048,576 KB) |

- The rate rises as the scene gets heavier (draws per frame went from about 500 to about 1,400).
- At 4,096 segments the 1 GB cap (`HOSTSEG_CAP`) is hit and the host aborts. This is frame ~2180, 77 s into the run.

```
[dm] FATAL NVN command memory: the game's pool is empty and host-lent segments reached 1024 MB without being reclaimed by the game's blocks
[dm] CRASH sig=6 ... 
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 ctl_put.cold.1 ctl_chunk_close cmd_alloc+0x1b4 rec+0x24 h_nvnCommandBufferSetRenderTargets+0x80 main+0x18b72ac ...
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

The first segment is lent at frame 0: `command memory: the game's callback did not add enough (need 1400 bytes), using a host-lent segment`.

## Why I think it's 0d103787

Before that commit, `AddCommandMemory` freed lent segments whose guest range the game granted memory over (`hostseg_release`). The commit removed that and frees a segment only when another recording writes records over its guest range (`hostseg_written`). Z-A seems never to meet that condition, so lent segments are never returned. The commit message says no game here lends from its own pool and it was only tested against Splatoon Raiders and `t_nvn`, so Z-A was probably not covered.

I tried `git revert 0d103787` on `3e628a0` and it applies cleanly. I haven't built or tested it yet.

## Not this

- Not the iPhone GPU page-fault freeze (#149, #292): there is no GPU error here.
- Not pipeline or archive related: the pipelines loaded from the archive with 0 compiled.

## Next steps

I can rebuild at the parent of `0d103787` (`fb510cce`), or with the revert, and report back. I can also rerun with `DM_NVN_CMDSTAT=1 DM_NVN_CBLOG=1` for per-frame command-memory numbers if that helps.

3e628a0d86ec

d254f45e8002

Mac, the host from a terminal (--platform mac)

MacBook Pro M1 Max 27.2.1

None

### What happened

The host's periodic counters show the game issuing about twice the work in the same place, while the GPU time per draw does not grow:

| Run (same save, Kakariko) | draws per frame | compute dispatches per 300 frames (no barrier) | attachments load / store per frame | GPU p50 / p95 | dropped per 300 frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before the tomb (frames 2100–3600) | 897–932 | ~10,900–23,000 | 310 / 363 MB | 25.3–26.2 / 28.2–28.9 ms | 0–1 |
| In the tomb (frames 4200–4500) | 1,427–1,725 | 18,405 | 352 / 387 MB | 32.6–35.8 / 41–44 ms | 53–116 |
| After leaving, same session (4800–5100) | 1,062–1,166 | 23,136 | 285 / 334 MB | 29.8–32.3 ms | 9–56 |
| After a restart, Kakariko again (600–1200) | 1,877–2,111 | 41,748 | 455 / 467 MB | 22–37 / 28–43 ms | 10–126 |

From the restart's log: `[RED]` lines 0; pipeline prepare 21,467 lines in 2.2 s, 0–1 bases compiled per 300 frames during play; resident memory ~10.4–11.2 GB, flat; no `thermal` changes. The before/after runs are the `.prev.log` and `.log` of consecutive sessions.

Not established: whether the extra draws come from the game state (the save after the tomb) or from wrong answers to the game's visibility/culling work (indirect-count multi-draws are in use: `indirect-count multi-draw masking`), which would also fit #2226's open ordering question. The shader cache cannot change the draw count, so it is either the save state or what the host answers.

The same draw count and frame time in Kakariko as before visiting the tomb.

body:
A built Mac app leaves one `gpuarchiver-<random>` folder per pipeline archive flush in its user cache folder, and nothing ever removes them. On my Mac Ocarina of Time's app had 4,016 of them, about 285 GB; Tears of the Kingdom's had about 37 GB. Deleting them freed 345.8 GiB in all.

To check your own Mac (quit the games first):

```bash
du -sh "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)"org.nxnative.*/com.apple.gpuarchiver
```

**Where they are.** A built app runs as `org.nxnative.<title ID, lowercase>`, and Metal puts its folders under that bundle ID: `$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)org.nxnative.<title ID>/com.apple.gpuarchiver/gpuarchiver-*`. Each holds an LMDB store (`PersistentState`) and the captured binaries (`air64_v28`, `air64_v29`, `applegpu_g17s`, `descriptor`, `reflection`). `docs/reference/shaders.md` ("Metal's build folders left by pipeline archive flushes") and `scripts/clean_metal_cache.py` only cover the shared folder, `$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)com.apple.gpuarchiver`, which a host with no bundle uses. The app's pile is outside both, and NX2Apple's Play does not clean it either.

**How fast.** Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072), Apple silicon Mac, macOS 27.2, headless replay of a Castle Town market route starting from a save with no `pso_archive/`: every start wrote 6 archive files and left exactly 6 new folders, 560 MB (n=6 starts). A start that writes fewer files leaves fewer folders; a long play session writes one file per timer flush and leaves one folder for each. Three other games I have built show the same, with 21 to 138 folders each.

**Cause.** `ep_new()` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`) makes a new `MTL4PipelineDataSetSerializer` for every flush period (the fix for #294 and the 2,000-capture limit from #1735), and Metal makes a new working folder for each serializer. The host does not remove them on the Mac on purpose, since the shared folder may hold another program's live compiler state, and on iOS it removes earlier runs' folders at start. A bundled Mac host's folder is under its own bundle ID, though, so the iOS reasoning applies to it as well. Measured: one start with `DM_PSO_ARCHIVE=off` (no serializer) wrote no archive file and left no new folder (n=1).

**Do the folders do anything for the next start?** Not that I can measure. Headless starts of a Castle Town market route with the folder emptied against starts that kept the previous run's folders, alternating, n=3 each: first frame 2.22 s emptied against 2.32 s kept, pipeline prewarm 18.2 s against 19.3 s, 98.2 % of frames held in both (means). The host never opens a serializer's folder again after its write; the archive it reads at start is `pso_archive/`.

**Workaround.** With the game closed, delete that game's folder; `com.apple.metal` and `com.apple.metalfe` beside it are Metal's shader caches and can stay:

```bash
rm -rf "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_CACHE_DIR)org.nxnative.0400486024dec000/com.apple.gpuarchiver"
```

**Proposed fix.** On the Mac, when the host runs as a bundle, do what iOS already does: remove the earlier runs' folders at start, before the first capture, from `<bundle ID>/com.apple.gpuarchiver`. Two builds of one game share the bundle ID, so the host takes an exclusive lock beside the folder first and leaves the folders alone when another copy of the app holds it. A host with no bundle keeps today's behaviour (the shared folder, `clean_metal_cache.py`). I have a branch for this and will open a PR.

Not tested: iOS, macOS 26.
title: Mac: Metal's pipeline-archive build folders pile up under the app's bundle ID (org.nxnative.<title ID>/com.apple.gpuarchiver), hundreds of GB, never removed

body:
I'm experiencing noticeable input latency when using a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller over Bluetooth on macOS through NXNative (installed via NX2Apple).

The delay isn't necessarily extremely long, but it's noticeable enough to make gameplay feel less responsive and uncomfortable compared to what I would expect from a wired controller.

This appears to be a longstanding macOS issue specifically affecting the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, rather than a problem with NXNative itself.

I would like to ask whether the NXNative team could investigate a possible software workaround.

In particular, would it be possible to bypass Apple's `GameController.framework` for controller input and use a direct HID-based input backend to communicate with the controller over Bluetooth?

There are already community projects exploring this approach, such as "pro-bridge"(https://github.com/fullstackgabe/pro-bridge), which uses SDL3/HIDAPI to read input directly from the Pro Controller on macOS.

Ideally, a solution would:
- Eliminate or significantly reduce the Bluetooth input latency.
- Preserve all controller features, especially gyroscope input and rumble.
- Ideally support full HD Rumble, including independent motor control.
- Work natively within NXNative, without requiring external hardware or additional adapters.

**Hardware:** MacBook Air M4  
**Controller:** Nintendo Switch Pro Controller  
**Connection:** Bluetooth  
**Software:** NXNative via NX2Apple

I understand that this may require changes to the controller input handling, but it would be a significant improvement for macOS users experiencing this issue.

Is this something the team could investigate, or is there another software-based workaround that could be implemented?
title: Noticeable Bluetooth Input Latency with Nintendo Switch Pro Controller on macOS

### Problem

The build reaches the shader split stage but fails with:

`the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps them in a form shader_split.py does not read`

The survey reports 160 GLSLC compiler-output magics in `main`.

The shader split log finds many control sections, but rejects them with:

`no code area: no data record points at one, and the code builds the address of none right after or right before it; left out`

The resulting shader count is 0.

### What I found

I inspected the rewritten `main.patched.bin` around several control-section offsets reported by `shader_split.log`.

Tested control sections:

- `0x28CC5F0`
- `0x28CD3F8`
- `0x28DCF40`
- `0x28F7F88`

All four samples show the same apparent layout:

- GLSLC magic `91 68 86 19` approximately `0x308` bytes before the control section
- control section begins with `34 12 76 98`
- shader/GPU code appears to begin at `control_offset + 0xE0`

For example, for control section `0x28CC5F0`, the bytes at relative `+0xE0` begin:

`19 79 04 00 00 00 00 00 00 25 00 00 00 22 0E 00`

The same `+0xE0` code layout appears in the other sampled control sections, although the shader lengths/data differ.

This suggests that this game may use a GLSLC layout where the code is stored inline after the control structure rather than being referenced in the way the current shader reader expects.

## CI red on every PR — two environment failures, not the PRs' code

Every recent pull request (mine: #2596–#2599, #2667; also #2595 from another author) fails the same two jobs. Both look like runner-environment changes, not anything the PRs changed.

### 1. `Host unit tests` and `Sanitizers` — `t_save_sync` device-name check

```
both changed: the report says conflict, with the cloud's device
(… cdevice=VirtualMac2,1 … conflict=1 pull=0)
== save sync: 112 checks, 1 failed ==
```

`dm/host/tests/t_save_sync.c` asserts `strstr(line, "cdevice=Mac")` in the conflict report — the test means to check the cloud device is *named*, but GitHub's macOS runners now report their VM model `VirtualMac2,1`, which no longer contains the substring `Mac`. The check is right on real hardware and wrong on the CI image.

### 2. `clang-tidy (ratchet)` — baseline drifted under the runner's LLVM

LLVM 23.1.4 reports new findings in test files none of the PRs touched:

- `dm/gfx/tests/t_vk_swapchain_life.m`: `bugprone-invalid-enum-default-initialization` ×2, `clang-analyzer-core.NullDereference` ×1
- `dm/gfx/tests/t_res_commit.m`, `t_upload_src.m`, `t_wline.m`, `t_zero_depth.m`: `clang-analyzer-nullability.NullablePassedToNonnull` ×1 each
- `dm/gfx/tests/t_wline.m`: `bugprone-command-processor` ×1
- `misc-misplaced-const`: 3 findings vs a baseline of 5 (below, so an improvement the ratchet still flags)

`baseline 211 findings; 7 file/check pairs above it, 1 below it` — every flagged pair is a test file outside the PR diffs. The host files the PRs do touch report 0 findings.

### Suggested fixes (yours to judge — happy to send a small PR if useful)

- `t_save_sync.c`: check the report carries *a* cloud device name (`cdevice=` non-empty) instead of the literal `Mac`, or accept `VirtualMac*` too.
- Lint: refresh the ratchet baseline under the runner's current LLVM (`python3 dm/tools/lint_c.py tidy --update`), or pin the job to the LLVM version the baseline was made with.
title: CI: t_save_sync expects cdevice=Mac (runners report VirtualMac2,1) and the clang-tidy ratchet drifted under LLVM 23.1.4

body:
**Symptom.** In PRAGMATA a compute dispatch can keep running after the game is gone. The host process stays in state E (exiting), `kill -9` does nothing, and the GPU reads 100 % with no game running. A few minutes later WindowServer stops responding, and only a reboot clears it. We had to reboot this way 6 times on 11-06 and 11-07, and once more on 11-13. It is the most serious failure we hit, because it takes the whole Mac down, not just the game.

**Cause, as far as we traced it (11-06, R53 hangar):**
- Three persistent queue kernels, `12a52b68`, `8c48c7ff` and `251426e9` (SDF, 128 groups × 32 threads), poll a shared counter. Each pass is a device-scope atomic and a `seq_cst` device fence.
- When the queue's counters are inconsistent (in one of the two runs, after a page fault made macOS drop the command buffers that held the producers' work), no thread ever leaves its loop.
- The process had already exited (watchdog `_exit(70)`), but command buffers it had committed were still queued (fences 27918–27924), and Metal does not reclaim those. The GPU kept running them.
- Neither run depended on a fault: the 20:15 hang had no page fault and no gpuEvent report. Its submission head and spin kernels were the same as the 20:30 run's, which did fault.

**On main (11-13 21:34).** A host and library built from main 9ccbd6b1a with main's own tools had no loop guard and no GPU watchdog. On this run the game aborted (`nn::diag abort` at main+0x4a9758, signal 6) while GPU work was in flight. The GPU stayed at 100 % with no game running, and the Mac had to be rebooted.

**Why a loop cap alone is not enough.** We tried a per-thread cap of 2^18 passes, the same size #2254 uses. For these kernels that is 4,096 threads × 2^18 ≈ 1.1e9 serialized atomics on one word, roughly 10–30 s per dispatch. With several such dispatches committed behind each other, the GPU still stayed pinned for minutes after the exit.

**What works for us (on every PRAGMATA run since 11-06, no wedge since):**
1. **Every compute loop is capped.** That includes spin, flag-wait and CAS loops, not only loops sized by the data. The cap also reads an abort word every 1,024 passes. Loops containing a barrier get the cap without the abort check, so no thread is left alone at a barrier. The loop cap is bound at compute buffer index 28.
2. **The GPU watchdog raises that abort word before the process exits.** It then waits up to 3 s (`DM_NVN_WATCHDOG_DRAIN_MS`) for the committed work to finish, and logs `drained` or `NOT drained`. Because the word stays raised, work that outlives the process still leaves its loops within 1,024 passes. With the abort raised, the GPU went from 64 % to 0 % in about 10 s in a run where the same kernels hit the cap at a scene change.
3. **Host checks:** a GPU unit test covers this, a 32-thread spin on a flag nobody writes. With the abort raised after 50 ms, the dispatch has to end within 200 ms.

**Possibly the same family in other games:** #432 (Tears of the Kingdom, kernel panic and reboot), #1223 (Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment, WindowServer freezes), #1326 and #1605 (Ocarina of Time GPU hangs), and #2254's Kirby Air Riders particle loop. We have not confirmed that these are the same cause.

**Relation to existing work:**
- #2254 (the 2^18 loop guard, open) covers the first half of item 1. This issue adds the abort word and the drain before exit.
- 797ca451d shows that early returns before a barrier are fine on Apple GPUs. This issue is about loops that never end, not barriers.
- e0cf2ac7 (#2618) makes reads past a bound storage buffer return 0. That may remove some of the inconsistent states that start these loops, but not all of them: the 20:15 run had no fault.

**Not checked:** a fresh repro on current main. We no longer run unguarded hosts, because each repro costs a reboot. Also not checked: whether the cases from other games above are the same.

We can send the abort word and the watchdog drain as a PR on top of #2254, if you'd like that form.

Related to the PRAGMATA bring-up, ccd834e06 (@seedds).

Co-authored with UncraftableXD.
title: PRAGMATA (0400C76024710000): a compute loop that never ends keeps the Mac GPU at 100 % after the process exits, until a reboot

body:
Follow-up to #1806. That issue is the black screen caused by a 28-entry shader map. This one records its root cause and what is still wrong once the map is complete: the main menu does not render and the sky is black in a race.

## Status of the black screen (#1806)

The split found 28 shaders because `shader_split.py` has no reader for Shin'en's `SHN!` containers (Ounce engine). Every `.shdr`, `.w3d`, `.w3p` and `.tex` in the RomFS starts with `SHN!`; only `ndsr/ounce-nvn2-upper_left.ndsr` was read. A reader for it is written and tested locally (`shn_shaders` in `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`, `dm/tools/tests/test_split_shn.py`, an entry in `docs/reference/shaders.md`). **It is not in a PR yet.** With it, the normal `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` run finds **2,976 shaders** (the same count as the full scan in #1806) with no manual scan, and all 26 keys the game asked for at boot are in the map.

Container layout, so it can be checked:

- `SHN!`, u32 header length `0x44`, then three chunks: the data (stored and decoded length at +0x08 / +0x0c, starting at the header's end), the relocations (offset, stored, decoded at +0x18) and the GPU data (offset, stored, decoded at +0x24). A chunk is stored raw when its two lengths are equal, otherwise one LZ4 block.
- Relocations: u32 group count, then per group an i32 target (-1 data, 1 GPU data), a u32 count and that many u32 data offsets of u64 pointers.
- NVN2 control sections (version `0xc9`) are in the data; their code areas are in the GPU data. Each stage has a record `{u64 code offset in the GPU data, u64 control offset in the data}`. In a `.shdr` the code areas are back to back, but in a `.w3d` they sit among vertex buffers, so only the record places them.
- Second cause: `scan_file_in` drops a file before any reader sees it unless it contains a known signature (`shader_split.py`, the long `elif b'BNSH\0\0\0\0' not in d …` line). `SHN!` was not on that list, so the reader alone changed nothing until the list was fixed.

Numbers from the RomFS: 7,053 stages, 2,948 distinct keys (196 vertex, 196 pixel and 65 compute in the 143 `shaders/*.shdr`; the rest in the materials of 402 `.w3d` models, including 46 task and 46 mesh stages, 31 + 31 distinct), 1,420 vertex/pixel pairs. Plus the 28 NDSR shaders.

## What the user reports after the rebuild

Built from a NUP (update `v262144` only, no base game), `--platform mac-app`, provisional profile. The game boots, audio plays, and a race can be completed. But:

- **The main menu does not render**, so what is being selected cannot be seen.
- **In a race the sky is all black.**

I have **not** found the cause of either. I did not capture screenshots or a pass dump (my scripted runs did not give me usable frames; two ended with exit status 138, and I have not established whether that was the game or my tooling). Everything below is from the runtime log and the shader build log, and the links to the menu and the sky are hypotheses.

## Findings from the logs

**1. 62 of 2,976 shaders fail to translate** (`dmsh_build.log`, 2,914 ok). All are task or mesh shaders from the `.w3d` models:

| count | error |
|---|---|
| 30 + 1 | `NotSupportedException: Ampere 923 at 0x1a0: ISBERD mode 34 in a task or mesh shader` |
| 19 + 12 | `NotSupportedException: Ampere 927 at 0xdc0` / `0x34a0: stage output store mode b4 outside a task or mesh shader` |

The `ISBERD` ones look like the known [mesh shaders that read their own outputs back](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/shaders.md#mesh-shaders-that-read-their-own-outputs-back) (that entry names mode `f8`; this is mode `34`). The `mode b4` store error has no entry in `docs/agents/symptoms.md`. At runtime ten of them are asked for and fail with `failed to load shader <key>_b: cannot open …_b.metallib`; all ten are in `objects/collectible.w3d` and `objects/hud_energy.w3d` (collectibles and the energy HUD). A draw of a task/mesh pair without its shaders is skipped.

**2. A compute shader that cannot bind**: `shaders/volumetricfog.shdr` (`cded8d0899ba4a6d`): `reflection conversion failed: B binding cp_t2d_cb196608_10568000 has no resolved slot number`, then `the dispatched program has no compute shader`. That pass is skipped. If it is the fog or atmosphere pass, it is a candidate for the black sky. Not verified. The symptom index has similar entries for NVN2 compute handles (for example "NVN2 compute's separate handles in c[0]").

**3. Other `[RED]` lines in the run** (each seen once or twice):

- `cube texture view of 0 + 1 layers past the 1 faces of texture ID …: read as a 2D array`: a cube view onto a one-face texture; a sky or reflection cubemap would fit, not verified.
- `stage 0 cb1 has no uniform buffer bound: shader eb5ec3e356bf7ad1_b, address 0 size 0 (frame 29)`: a vertex shader from `menu/back_online.w3d`; the first menu-related one. The docs say a slot the game binds empty reads as zero, so it may be harmless.
- `pipeline prebuild: 25 pairs need a library file this app does not carry (first: 02f2100f390d5f08_b.json)`: pulling libraries (`_bp`) missing from the app.
- `NVN unimplemented function called: nvnDlssParametersSetOverlayFullScreen` and `…SetOverlayDebugLayer` (also noted in #1806; probably unrelated).
- The bundled pipeline archive was made for a different depth mode (`near=-w`, run needs `near=0`); the device builds those bases itself.

## Environment

- Apple M4 Max, macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), `main` at `b06f4e0e` plus the local patch above.
- Title `040041E0212AE000`, update `v262144`, main build ID `e76e60ef4fe21decb40223b5de5e6396`, SDK 20_5_13, NVN2, no base game in the NUP.
- Shader chain `d6b05d7481e5`; provisional profile (no profile for this title in the repo).

## Suggested next steps

1. Get the shader reader into a PR (the format above, the prefilter fix, the test), then a real profile for the game.
2. Capture a frame of the menu and of a race sky (`DM_CTL` `shot`, `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`) and see which draws are skipped or sampled black.
3. Decide whether the missing draws are the 62 task/mesh shaders, the `volumetricfog` compute pass, or something else.
4. Translate the `ISBERD mode 34` and `stage output store mode b4` cases, or find what they have in common.

No game files, keys or extracted assets are in this report; the shader keys and file names are identifiers only.
title: Fast Fusion (040041E0212AE000): root cause of the 28-shader map, and a black sky and unreadable menu after it

body:
## What happened

A **third-party BETOP T6 For NS controller**, connected directly to the Mac with a **USB data cable**, has working buttons and right-stick input, but its left stick cannot move the player in Splatoon Raiders.

A standalone diagnostic, which does not require a game or the nxnative host, simultaneously reads:

- The physical device's Nintendo HID input report `0x30`, through a nonexclusive `IOHIDManager` connection.
- Apple's `GCExtendedGamepad.leftThumbstick`.
- `GCController.input.unmappedInput` for the left thumbstick, bypassing system control remapping.

The left stick spans its range in HID packets but remains **exactly `(0, 0)` in both GameController interfaces** during the same movement. This establishes an input-compatibility failure before the game receives the values; it does not establish which driver, firmware or calibration detail causes that conversion failure.

I am reporting the **left-stick input problem** and proposing an optional passive HID stick fallback. This report does not propose changes to motion calibration.

## What I expected

The physical left stick should control movement while the right stick and the game's real motion input remain independently available.

## Device, game and build information

| Field | Observed value |
|---|---|
| Controller | Third-party BETOP T6 For NS; not an original Nintendo controller |
| Connection | USB data cable directly to the Mac; confirmed by the reporter |
| Controller/receiver firmware | Unknown; no wireless receiver was used in this test |
| HID product string | `BETOP T6 FOR NS` |
| Advertised USB VID:PID | `057e:2009` |
| GameController category | `Switch Pro Controller` |
| Mac | Mac Studio, Apple M4 Max, 36 GB RAM (`Mac16,9`) |
| OS | macOS 26.7.3 (`25G342`) |
| Game used for gameplay verification | Splatoon Raiders, `0400380020056000`, update `v65536` |
| Original frontend/build | NX2Apple 1.3.0, Mac app, started from its game library |
| Original game host commit | Not recorded by that binary; its log says `commit not recorded` |
| Original game shader chain | `89f44f9b6bb0` |

## Reproduction without game files

1. Connect one BETOP T6 For NS by USB cable. Disable the controller firmware's gyro-to-stick mapping. No game needs to be running.
2. Save the diagnostic source included below as `betop-input-probe.m` and compile it:

   ```sh
   xcrun clang -mmacosx-version-min=26.6 -fobjc-arc      -framework Foundation -framework GameController -framework IOKit      betop-input-probe.m -o betop-input-probe
   ```

3. Run `./betop-input-probe 18` from an ordinary terminal, outside a sandbox that blocks controller access.
4. Rotate only the left stick through its full range for about 10 seconds, then release it. Leave the right stick untouched.
5. Compare the HID ranges with the mapped and unmapped GameController left-stick readings.

The program sends **no output reports, feature reports or SPI commands**. `HID open=0x0` indicates successful passive access; a permission error or an absence of GameController devices should not be interpreted as this failure.

The left-only capture received **2,254 HID reports**. A separate two-stick capture verified that the right stick does produce changing GameController values, reaching `-1..+1`.

The phase labels in these historical logs are only approximate operation windows: the player started rotating before the initial rest window ended. The empty final phase prints sentinel extrema; it contains no samples and is not a measurement. The decisive evidence is the left-only capture, with changing raw left-stick data and unchanged right-stick data while both GameController left-stick interfaces stay zero. GameController values were polled approximately once a second; HID extrema cover the received reports.

## Proposed compatibility workaround

The local prototype adds an **explicit, default-off** switch:

```ini
DM_PRO_STICKS=left
```

It reuses the existing Pro Controller passive HID reader and `pad_pro.h` stick decoder, rather than changing the game's code or adding a BETOP product-name/game-profile rule.

- `left` substitutes only the left stick. `right` and `both` are additional selections; `0` or unset retains GameController.
- The selected stick bypasses system remapping. The override is explicit because an intentionally unmapped axis can also read zero; the host should not automatically classify every zero axis as broken.
- Buttons, the unselected stick, haptics and Home keep their existing GameController paths. Existing motion handling remains independent.
- A GameController callback reapplies the selected raw stick before publishing input, so pressing a button cannot replace a moving raw stick with the driver's zero value.
- A 60 Hz main-loop poll handles axes for which GameController produces no change callbacks. It publishes only changes, avoiding an idle controller continually taking over `DM_PAD_MERGE` input.
- Packets older than 300 ms are not used for the override. Existing focus and prompt input gates still apply.
- Routing requires one streaming physical Pro-compatible device and one GameController Pro, using its existing player slot. With ambiguous multiple devices it falls back rather than guessing ownership; the existing identical-controller HID path is left in place.
- Disabling motion must not disable the explicitly requested stick reader.
- It uses the existing decoder's dead zone and learned reach. Release the sticks at connection and rotate the selected stick fully once; it does not issue calibration commands to the controller.

The reference patch below is a **stick-only prototype against the stated local baseline**, not a ready-to-merge PR against current upstream. I would appreciate feedback on whether this opt-in approach fits the input architecture before preparing an upstream PR.

## Validation and limits

- The actual patched reader produced left X/Y ranges of **`-32767..32767`** while GameController's left stick stayed zero. The unselected right-stick readings were preserved. Existing raw motion continued delivering samples concurrently; that observation checks stream availability, not motion accuracy or calibration.
- The reporter confirmed in Splatoon Raiders that `DM_PRO_STICKS=left` restores left-stick movement while retaining independent right-stick and real motion aiming, with firmware gyro-to-stick mapping off. This validates input availability, not every aspect of camera behavior.
- The stick-only snapshot's `t_motion_pro_mac`, `t_pad_pro` (55 checks) and `t_pad_hid_mac` passed under ASan/UBSan. They were rerun in isolation for this report, excluding unrelated later workspace changes. The reference patch applies cleanly to the stated baseline.
- Both the local upstream host and the shader-compatible host built. The graphics test suite passed in the earlier stick-only validation, using Python 3.13 and GPU access.
- `regress.py check --games 0400380020056000` reported **ERROR**, not PASS: the existing shader package predates keyed shader records and does not match the newer profile (`ps_other.bin`, shader `0000d6f2ba7af00b`). No shader package was deleted or relabelled to bypass that mismatch.
- `clang-tidy` was unavailable. Those two limitations remain uncompleted checks, not evidence of a passing full regression/lint run.
- Not hardware-tested here: original Nintendo Pro Controllers, another BETOP unit, Bluetooth, other macOS versions, or multiple physical Pros. The additional `right` and `both` selections have synthetic coverage; the left-only path is the gameplay evidence for this report.
- The original failing game binary's exact commit is unknown. The independent reproduction does not depend on that binary, a game build, or any local host patch. No claim is made that the newest upstream revision has been gameplay-tested.

## Related work and requested direction

- https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/296 discusses passive HID motion when GameController exposes unusable motion data. The input field affected here is the stick.
- https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/382 discusses stick shaping/handler queues and a separate direct-HID proposal involving exclusive ownership. This prototype listens nonexclusively and keeps the GameController paths for unselected inputs.

Would an explicit passive-HID stick selection be acceptable upstream, or would you prefer a different extension of the existing controller routing? The reusable evidence here is the standalone HID-versus-GameController reproduction; attribution to a particular Apple or third-party implementation defect remains open.

title: Mac: BETOP T6 For NS left stick stays zero in GameController despite valid HID input

body:
### What is missing

Games on the Switch output 5.1 (the logs show `DeviceSink inputs 6` for TotK, Wonder, MK8, ACNH, OoT). The engine downmixes it to stereo before it reaches CoreAudio, so macOS spatial audio (and head tracking on AirPods Pro / Max) has nothing to spatialize. Control Center's "Spatial Audio" control is not available for the game.

Where the downmix happens (engine `ccd834e0`, built from `ecc41fa`):
- `dm/host/hle_audren.c`, `capture()`: the six DeviceSink mix buffers are summed to stereo (front 1.0, center 0.707, LFE 0.251, back 0.707).
- `dm/host/hle_audio.c`, `device_channels` / `pull_device`: the guest's 6-channel AudioOut is pulled as 2 channels into a stereo AudioUnit on the default output. The device channel count calls answer 2.

### What I propose

Keep the six channels and hand them to macOS as 5.1, so the system spatializer does the rendering (head tracking, personalized profile, the user's Spatial Audio setting). I have a working prototype in a local patch (`DM_AUDIO_SPATIAL=2`, about 370 lines in `hle_audio.c`, `hle_audren.c`, a new `dm_audio_avf.m` and the Makefile). It works on TotK with AirPods Pro 3 on macOS 27.2.1: sound is placed correctly, head tracking works, and the Control Center Spatial Audio panel is active. I can send a PR.

**What the system needs to see** (measured, same 5.1 voice test each time, AirPods Pro 3):

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| Stereo downmix (today) | no spatial |
| 16-bit int PCM, AVAudioEngine, default AUHAL, QuickTime-played 5.1 WAV | everything centered |
| `AUSpatialMixer` inside the app (AmbienceBed, MPEG_5_1_A, head tracking) | positions right, head tracking works, needs about +8 dB, but the system panel shows "Unavailable" and the system spatializer is bypassed |
| **32-bit float interleaved PCM, layout `kAudioChannelLayoutTag_MPEG_5_1_A`, via `AVSampleBufferAudioRenderer` + `AVSampleBufferRenderSynchronizer`** | positions right, head tracking works, **system panel active** |
| E-AC-3 packets via the same renderer | also works, but needs an encoder (ffmpeg); not needed since float PCM works |

The same approach is used by mpv (`ao_avfoundation`) and by beutl (b-editor/beutl PR 3801); also see yukij3/atmos-control. `AVAudioSession` multichannel support is iOS only (unavailable on macOS), so the renderer path is the macOS way.

**Implementation notes (things that bit me):**
- One sample buffer per 5 ms block (240 frames), float32, 6 channels, 48 kHz, presentation time = stream position.
- Anchor the synchronizer **once** at open with `setRate:time:atHostTime:`. `setRate` takes 150 to 200 ms; re-anchoring on every hitch (24 times in the first 10 s of the game loading) made the start unlistenable.
- On a producer hitch, just jump the stream position forward. Do not re-anchor, and do not read the renderer's clock to decide anything.
- Pace the producer to the wall clock.
- A pre-render lead is needed: the system renderer stutters with too little queued ahead. Measured: 250 ms ok, 150 ms ok, 100 ms stutters, 80 ms stutters. Default 150 ms; latency is fine in play (swords, footsteps).
- Gain: the spatializer plays quieter than the stereo downmix, so about +6 dB (hard clip at ±1) was needed.
- Only used when the output is 48 kHz.

**Proposed switch:** off by default. Env var `DM_AUDIO_SPATIAL` (0 = stereo as today, 2 = system spatial renderer), with `DM_AUDIO_SPATIAL_LEAD` (ms, default 150) and `DM_AUDIO_SPATIAL_GAIN` (dB, default +6). Ideally a launcher toggle ("Surround for headphones") that writes it to the per-game `env.txt`. Speakers and non-spatial headphones should keep the stereo path.

**Open points:**
- The fallback internal mixer (mode 1) is kept in my patch; it can be dropped if you prefer one path.
- Tested only on TotK and AirPods Pro 3. Other games and other Bluetooth/wired outputs untested.
- With a call app running (AirPods in call mode) quality drops; this is the system, not the patch.

### Platforms

macOS (Apple Silicon), NX2Apple 1.4.0 / engine from seedds/nxnative.
title: Spatial audio / head tracking for headphones (AirPods): stop downmixing 5.1 to stereo

|---|---|

| Submission ahead of target display | p50 32.9 ms, min 32.7 |

body:
### What happened

**Mac:** MacBook Pro, M3 Pro, 18 GB, macOS 26.6.2, plugged in, Low Power Mode off
**Build:** main `b1e44c1` with `5b0f1372` (PR #2367) cherry-picked, `--platform mac-app`
**Settings:** Docked, Frame rate 30, Dynamic resolution off, Upscaling MetalFX, RomFS overlay with every `ResolutionReduceScale` at 0.675 (flat), Hold frames when late on

**What happens**
- In normal play the frame rate drops at random to 16–17 fps and stays there. It isn't tied to an area.
- Opening and closing the pause menu brings it straight back to 30.

**Log, same session (with 5b0f1372)**
- `timing up to frame 900: frame time p50 66.13 / p95 67.10 ms; GPU p50 46.53 / p95 49.56 ms`
- The pipelines line for that window shows 0 pipelines compiled, 0 archive lookups and 0 hybrid draws.
- When it's fine, the same areas run at GPU p50 18–20 ms (frame p50 33.3 ms). Memory is normal (resident about 11–12.5 GB, footprint stable).
- `power up to frame …: GPU 0.0 ms/s; thermal -1`

**What I tried**
- `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`: still drops (the log confirms "frames are not held longer than the cap's vsyncs (DM_FPS_HOLD)"); frames sit at 66 ms with GPU about 46 ms.
- `5b0f1372` (a frame fits the shorter hold while the hold's mean does): still drops.
- A **60 fps target** with Hold on: it **never gets stuck**. 60 in enclosed areas, about 30 (sometimes a bit lower) in open areas.

**My guess**
At the 30 fps cap the GPU idles about half of each frame, and macOS lowers its clock. The same frame then takes about 46 ms, which spans two 33 ms slots, so the GPU idles again and the clock stays low. The pause menu changes the load and the clock comes back up. With a 60 target the GPU never idles long enough to clock down. Is there a way to keep the GPU's performance state up at a 30 fps cap (a Metal/IOKit performance hint, or treating the cap as a pacing step rather than idle time)?

Happy to run more diagnostics (DM_NVN_GPUPROF, a Metal System Trace) if useful.

### What you expected

A steady 30 fps at the 30 fps cap, as it holds when the GPU isn't clocked down (GPU p50 18–20 ms in the same areas).

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072

### nxnative commit

b1e44c1 + 5b0f1372 (PR #2367) cherry-picked + local PR #1662 mic patch (HLE_FORCE_BIG renamed to HLE_FORCE)

### Shader chain version

b6aa8fd968b7

### How it was built and run

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro M3 Pro (18 GB), macOS 26.7.3

### Settings and environment overrides

Docked, Frame rate 30, Dynamic resolution off, Upscaling MetalFX, Hold frames when late on, DM_TEX_RELEASE=0
DM_MIC=1
DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY=/Users/aideng1607/OoT/res90
MTL_HUD_ALIGNMENT=bottomright
MTL_HUD_ELEMENTS=fps
MTL_HUD_SCALE=0.2
MTL_HUD_OPACITY=0.5

### Logs

[nxnative-report-0400486024DEC000-2026-11-14.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34839275/nxnative-report-0400486024DEC000-2026-11-14.zip)

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

Update: in Handheld mode the same drop (to 17–18 fps) happens but recovers on its own within ~5 s. In Docked it stays at 15–18 fps until the pause menu is opened. It looks like the frame step’s probe back to 30 succeeds when the frame is lighter (handheld) but keeps failing in docked while the GPU is clocked down.
title: Ocarina of Time nxnative fps drop bug

body:
## What happened

Super Mario Sunshine inside Super Mario 3D All-Stars had persistent distorted/crackly, low-fidelity sounding audio during rendered 3D scenes, including Sunshine's own menu. Gameplay remained smooth with normal audio during cutscenes

Disabling Hagi's `ChannelsExtension` in Sunshine's own configuration made the game produce native stereo instead of six-channel PCM. After enabling this change, the audio became smooth.

## Game, build and machine

- Collection: Super Mario 3D All-Stars, `010049900F546000`, update **1.1.4 / v393216**.
- Affected program: Super Mario Sunshine, `010049900F546002`, SDK **9.5.1**.
- Sunshine `main` build ID: `b21e3733e11d6fcf1a8d57ce51bef4a5`.
- Built/run with **NX Play 2.0 (32)** on **Mac mini M4, 16 GB RAM, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131)**.
- The generated launch script records nxnative tree `472e9fe75cd14f9df2665115217590d6d0eba665`, matching commit **8b55ebb364821045ad16fe432166151357bcde10** in the local Git history. The runtime logs themselves say “commit not recorded”; the checkout subsequently updated, so its current HEAD should not be confused with the built host.
- Shader chain: **2afd39090b76**.

## Minimal change that helped

In the game-owned file `rom:/data/database/config/MarioSunshine.config`, change only:

```diff
- "ChannelsExtension" : true
+ "ChannelsExtension" : false
```

The property is under `Hagi.Audio`. The base `rom:/hagi.config` already has this property false; Sunshine's database configuration overrides it to true. Therefore changing only the base configuration would miss this override.

For the local test this was supplied through a single-file RomFS overlay/mod, preserving every other setting in the configuration. The full extracted configuration is **not** attached or proposed for redistribution.

Disassembly of this exact `main` also supports changing the source mode rather than just relabeling six-channel buffers: the `ChannelsExtension` getter at `main+0x13c70` is called at `main+0x199f4`; its result selects mode 4 when enabled versus mode 2 when disabled. The AudioOut initialization around `main+0x1346fc` selects two channels for modes below 3 and six otherwise, and stores that channel count in Hagi's own state before opening AudioOut. No binary patch was applied.

Could the Sunshine profile/build pipeline apply this targeted `Hagi.Audio.ChannelsExtension=false` override automatically for Mac builds, so players do not need to install a mod? A profile-driven transform of the user's own configuration (or an automatically generated per-program override) would avoid shipping extracted game files and could cover both terminal builds and packed Mac apps.
title: Super Mario Sunshine (3D All-Stars, Mac): distorted audio improves with ChannelsExtension=false; stereo confirmed

body: Related to the PRAGMATA bring-up, ccd834e06 (@seedds). ## Summary In PRAGMATA's R53 hangar (st20_100, after the tram ride, "Contact Earth from the Comms Tower"), the lighting washes out in pink, green and white as you enter and again on the stairs. It fades when the camera stays still. On console the hangar is dark blue-grey. No `[RED]` line points at it. The wash starts in the SDF GI. The voxeliser `ef4ad01151918469` reads its surfel colours through a storage buffer bound by address alone (`cp_s3`, `NVN_RB_SBUFQ`). That buffer lies at the base of a 1 GB sparse pool, and when the hangar is entered the game has mapped only its first 0xc0000 bytes. The shader indexes 0x150000 bytes and more. On the Switch the GPU reads 0 past the mapped pages. On the Mac the binding ends at the mapped run, so the shader reads whatever comes after it. Those bytes become hot surfel colours, and the GI bounce spreads them through its volume and into the lighting. This is a class, not one shader: any shader that takes a storage buffer's address from a uniform buffer or the push constants (`NVN_RB_SBUFU` / `NVN_RB_SBUFQ`) and indexes past the pages mapped there. #2509 covers the holes inside such a range. This issue is about the reads past its last mapped page. ## Environment - M4 Pro, macOS 26.6.2. PRAGMATA 0400C76024710000 on our main-based test host (main + #2509 + the PRAGMATA fixes under review), translated library on chain 0d4a65e3c0c5. - Route: the save after the tram ride, then walking into the hangar and up the stairs; 24 shots from 60 s to 129 s, scored by the share of the picture that is washed (saturated, white or green). For scale, a calm hangar shot scores 0.005 or less, and washed shots 0.07 to 0.5. ## What the binding was `DM_NVN_SBUFU_DIAG=ef4ad011` logs every new buffer an SBUFU / SBUFQ slot of that shader resolves to. At frame 3493, its first dispatch in the hangar: ``` F3493 ef4ad01151918469_b aid 8 addr 0xb36000000 lookup len 0x1 -> buffer len 0x400000 off 0x2b0000 | vpool base 0xb36000000 len 0x40000000 nrun 1; pieces from +0: +0:0xc0000@0x7947ab0000 | 1 pool entries hold it: [lo 0xb36000000 hi 0xb360c0000 len 0xc0000] ``` - The slot's address is offset 0 of a 1 GB sparse pool. One run of 0xc0000 bytes is mapped there, so #2509 makes no span: there is no hole. - On `main` the lookup gives the run's own buffer, 0xc0000 bytes, and a read past it runs past the Metal buffer. On our test line, the lookup gave a 4 MB buffer of the physical pool behind the run, at +0x2b0000. So the shader saw 0x150000 bytes, and everything past 0xc0000 was another resource's data. - 83 frames later (F3576) the game maps +0xc0000 for 0xb0000 bytes, and the binding becomes a 0x170000-byte span. - `cp_s2` (aid 7) is in the same state in another sparse pool. How far the shader reads is set by its own records (`cp_s0` cumulative counts, `cp_s1` 60-byte records with the colour base at +52): it reads up to `base + 4 * count`. In the Shelter that is 51,576 bytes, inside its 0x10000-byte run, and the Shelter does not wash. We have not measured the extent in the hangar. The chain from there to the screen was traced with texture dumps across runs (raw dumps at set times, washed against calm): 1. `ef4ad011` (voxeliser) writes the voxel volume. 2. `c08db9c9` packs the voxels. 3. `bfc2118307977103` / `936be3302f47d25f` propagate them into the GI volume (64x32x384 RG11B10). An earlier offline check found `bfc21183`, `c08db9c9` and `41eaf0a7` bit-exact with the Switch's output: they only carry the bad colours on. 4. `845cad29b8a61d04` turns that volume into a packed colour target (960x540 R32Uint). 5. The lighting draw `10e0a286` adds that colour. The colour target's median goes from 0.2 calm to 15 to 180 in the wash, and the lit buffer's from about 1 to 100 to 500. Every other input of the lighting draw is the same washed and calm. ## Results on the route | Arm (same host, same route) | Runs | Worst shot score | |---|---|---| | test host as is | 2 | 0.218, 0.177 (washed: [1]) | | with the binding tail of the PR below | 1 | 0.087 (still washed in that shot: [2]) | | tail + robust access in `ef4ad011`, `41eaf0a7`, `c08db9c9` (local side library) | 3 | 0.013, 0.019, and 0.042 on the tram menu before the hangar (0.004 or less in the hangar; clean: [3]) | | tail + the same robust access + count clamps | 1 | 0.015 (clean) | | robust access without the tail's lengths (the kernels' guards had no length to compare with) | 1 | washed | So the binding tail is part of the fix, not all of it. With it, a shader reads zeros where the Switch does for 4 MB past the last mapped page. The runs only came out clean once the three GI kernels also bounded their reads by the binding's length. It is not yet known whether those reads go further than 4 MB past the run, or whether the guard in `41eaf0a7` or `c08db9c9` is the one that matters. That needs one more split. ## Which games' shaders this reaches We counted the shaders that take a storage buffer by address alone in the translated libraries (reflection kinds `sbuf_ubo` = SBUFU, `sbuf_push` = SBUFQ), and checked in run logs whether the game has sparse pools at all. The change below only touches addresses in sparse pools. | Game | Shaders with an address-only storage buffer | … with a loop and a variable index into it | Examples | Sparse pools at run time | |---|---|---|---|---| | PRAGMATA | **28,967** (SBUFQ; 12,558 fragment, 9,946 vertex, 5,873 compute, 538 mesh) | 13,732 (3,678 compute) | `ef4ad011` (GI voxeliser, the hangar binding), `41eaf0a7` (surfel lighting, writes the same colour buffer), `2ae3de25` / `a3ba2e76` (GI surfel fragment shaders of #2509), `765e6d9d` (mesh) | **yes:** 2.8 million such bindings into sparse pools in a 130 s hangar run (`[span-stats]`); the sampled ones come from 101 shaders, 89 of them with a loop and a variable index | | Orbitals | 15,354 (SBUFU; 10,673 fragment, 2,849 vertex, 1,832 compute) | 5,048 (1,338 compute) | `001dbc179c58e5e1`, `003f854ec6e0f79a`, `006611be1c475e34` | none: no virtual pool in its runs | | Ocarina of Time | 4 (SBUFU, compute) | 4 | `2e8b0151667814d2`, `6d1f16f0e3f269ab`, `ca829b7cc365cd38`, `e28c9a738fbd99fe` | none: one virtual pool, mapped whole onto a physical pool at boot (`MapVirtual: the storage of virtual pool … points at physical pool … + 0`) | | Donkey Kong Bananza | 0 | 0 | | none: one virtual pool mapped whole, as in Ocarina of Time | "A loop and a variable index" is a static count from the MSL (a loop in the shader, and a subscript into the slot that is not a constant). It marks the shaders whose read extent the data can decide, like the voxeliser's. So today only PRAGMATA is affected. The other three either have no such shaders or have no sparse pool to put them in. Games with sparse pools that we have not run (Resident Evil 4 binds into one, `nvn-objects.md`) may be affected. ## Hardware behaviour A virtual (sparse) memory pool's unmapped pages read 0 on the Switch's GPU, and writes to them are dropped. The host already relies on that for the holes inside a span (#2509) and for a buffer address on an unmapped page (the zero dummy, Resident Evil 4's `0ee0c5f004239ce2`). A storage buffer bound by address has no size on the Switch: the shader reads raw addresses as far as it indexes. ## Proposed fix 1. **Host (PR to follow):** a storage buffer bound by address in a sparse pool runs past its last mapped run over zero pages, up to 4 MB (`DM_NVN_SPARSE_SPAN_TAIL_MB`) and at most to the end of the reservation. Pages mapped there read as mapped, a lone run takes a span buffer too, and mapping requests retire span buffers over the tail. This builds on #2509's span buffers and needs it first. 2. **For discussion: robust access for address-only storage buffers in the translator.** A read past the binding's length returns 0, from a per-binding length the host writes for SBUFU / SBUFQ as it binds them. This is what made the hangar clean locally, as a side library over three kernels; a translator pass would cover every shader and would remove the 4 MB limit of item 1. It is a chain change and needs a length table that `main` does not have. We have a working form on our older line (a bind-length table in a spare argument slot) and can bring it as its own PR if you want this direction. Co-authored with UncraftableXD.
title: PRAGMATA (0400C76024710000) washes out in rainbow colours in the R53 hangar: shaders read storage buffers bound by address past the sparse pages the game mapped

body:
**Summary:** on Mario Kart World with 3 players (about 8,000 draws a frame), the replay thread that turns NVN commands into Metal was the bottleneck: 29.7 ms of CPU per frame, 3.71 µs per draw. Four small changes, plus `-O2` on three files and `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`, brought it to 18.1 ms (2.40 µs per draw, 278 → 166 M instructions a frame) with the same picture. These are findings from a local tree (04811a63, 9 Nov); posting them here before any PR, as CONTRIBUTING asks, to see which parts are still relevant on current `main`.

### Setup
MacBook Pro M3 Pro (18 GB), macOS 27.2. Mario Kart World 1.0.0 (0400C3F00006E000), 3 players, 1080p, window. Scripted 345 s runs to a race; medians of the 300-frame windows in the race. Raw times move about 10 % between runs (the scene changes), so µs per draw and instructions per frame are the figures to compare.

| Host | Frame p50 | GPU p50 | Replay CPU | µs / draw | M instr. / frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 04811a63 | 41.1 ms | 30.7 ms | 29.7 ms | 3.71 | 277.6 |
| + the four changes (`-O1`) | 36.1 ms | 29.4 ms | 23.6 ms | 3.17 | 210.8 |
| + `-O2` on the Metal core, `hle_nvn.c` and the address layer | 37.0 ms | 30.4 ms | 23.1 ms | 3.03 | 200.3 |
| + `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1` | **35.1 ms** | 29.6 ms | **18.1 ms** | **2.40** | **165.7** |

Linear fit of replay CPU against draws: 10.2 ms + 2.40 µs × draws before, 7.8 ms + 1.34 µs × draws after. The frame stays at 33 ms because the game runs its own 30 fps mode at 3 players; the GPU (~30 ms) is now level with the replay thread.

### The changes (each behind a switch whose `0` restores the old path, each reviewed by a second reader)
1. **Same-pass feedback check (`fb_prepare`, `fb_tile_plan`, `fb_depth_rule`):** compare a texture slot's serial with the colour attachments before resolving its view, build each shader's slot list once, and read the serial without the lock. Base resolved the view of every texture slot of every draw first.
2. **Submit-side copy (`nq_bytes`, `thr_sys_ns`):** geometric growth and buffer recycling instead of one `realloc` per 4 KB (32 of 181 flatten samples were `realloc`/`memmove`, about 0.5 ms a frame on the game's thread); `thr_sys_ns` with two fewer Mach traps per call. The profile showed the replay thread waiting for work, not for `g_sub_mu`, so the flatten was not moved out of the lock.
3. **Address and encoder lookups:** per-slot address hints, a per-class memo of `conformsToProtocol:` in `enc_is_m4`, `encode_args_` without `g_rmu` for shaders with no texture or sampler bindings, and the last uniform-size block taken again.
4. **Texture ID → Metal texture:** a type cache by class, view type and format cached in the registration.

Not kept: a new epoch rule for texture IDs on sparse-pool mappings. A reviewer built a stale-texture case against it. Measured cost of leaving it: about 5,000 slow-path texture lookups and 46-50 epochs per frame, the largest remaining cost on that thread.

### Build notes
- `-O2` starts and runs. **LTO breaks startup** (no frame with `-O1` + LTO or `-O2` + LTO).
- `-O2` on everything gains nothing over `-O2` on those three files (−4 % per draw).

### Questions
- Which of these paths have changed on `main` since 04811a63? I can rebase the ones still relevant as separate small PRs, one per change, with their measurements.
- Is a per-draw CPU figure on a heavy scene (like the one above) something you would want as a regular benchmark?
title: Replay thread CPU on a heavy scene (Mario Kart World, 3 players, ~8,000 draws): 3.71 → 2.40 µs per draw from four small changes; findings before PRs

body:
**Summary:** on an M3 Pro, with Game Mode out of the picture, macOS still holds the GPU at 470-650 MHz during sustained GPU-bound play while the GPU is 96-99 % busy. IOReport names the state: the GPU power controller's `PWRCTRL` channel reads **SE** instead of **PERF**. It enters SE about 20 s after entering PERF and leaves it only after a GPU idle gap of roughly 200 ms or more. A deliberate ~300 ms pause brings the full clock back in a window, but not in fullscreen. This adds to #349, which traced one cause to Game Mode.

### Setup
- MacBook Pro M3 Pro (18 GB), macOS 27.2.1, on AC power, nominal thermal state.
- nxnative 47607fe0 (11 Nov) with local translator changes. Mario Kart World 1.0.0 (0400C3F00006E000), 3 players split screen, 1080p, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`, `DM_PRESENT_LINK=1`. The game runs its own 30 fps mode at 3 players.
- The host started directly, not from an app bundle (#349 found that such runs never get a Game Mode session). Scripted runs, nobody touching the Mac.

### What the counters show
Read every 250 ms through the private IOReport API (read-only, no sudo): group "GPU Stats", subgroup "GPU Power Controller States", channel `PWRCTRL`; also `GPU_SW` / `GPUPH` performance states and busy time.

| `PWRCTRL` | Requested state (`GPU_SW`) | Clock | GPU busy |
|---|---|---|---|
| PERF | P8 (GPUPH P13) | 1,375 MHz | as needed |
| **SE** | P1-P3 | 470-650 MHz | 96-99 % |

- **Entering SE:** sudden, about 20 s after the controller entered PERF under sustained load (594-604 frames at 30 fps, 1,184-1,211 at 60 fps), even with 6-27 % of the GPU idle just before. So it is not saturation.
- **Leaving SE:** only after the GPU has been idle for a while. A loading screen always does it. A ~300 ms stop of the game thread worked 2 times out of 3; 150 ms never did (about 60 ms of real GPU idle, as 1-2 queued frames finish first).
- **How long PERF lasts** grows with the idle time before it: about 20 s after a 300 ms pause, 50-125 s after a loading screen. It behaves like a budget refilled at rest.
- **Ruled out:** thermal limits (CLTM 0), power (SE was entered at 1.4-1.7 W of GPU power as well as 4.6-5.4 W), user activity (`caffeinate -u` every 5 s changed nothing), window vs. fullscreen vs. borderless for entering SE, MetalFX, the display link.

### An experiment: pause the game when SE is seen
We tried a switch in the acquire path: after 1.5 s of continuous SE, the game thread waits 300 ms (no game lock held there), at most every 8 s.

| Run (3 players, window) | Frame p50 | GPU p50 | Median clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference, 10 races | 42-49 ms | 38-44 ms | 490-650 MHz |
| Pause 300 ms on SE | **33.3 ms** | 23.1 ms | **1,373 MHz** |
| Pause 150 ms | 48.9 ms | 44.4 ms | 519 MHz |
| Pause 300 ms, **fullscreen** | 51.4 ms | 47.0 ms | 472 MHz |

In a window, SE comes back about 20 s after each pause, and the pause is visible (a 0.3 s hitch every ~20 s). In fullscreen the GPU does go idle (95-96 % idle in the next sample) and PERF is reached, but the controller returns to SE as soon as work resumes (< 250 ms). So this is a diagnosis, not a fix to ship.

### Open questions
- What triggers SE, and why it is sticky in fullscreen. A standalone Metal program with ~23 ms of GPU work per frame at 30 fps would tell whether it reproduces without the host, and is the fastest way to try the public levers (`CAMetalDisplayLink` frame rate ranges, `presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration:`, drawable count, the submitting thread's QoS).
- Whether other chips do the same. The M2 Pro data point in #349 did not drop with Game Mode on.

The reader and the switch are small; happy to share them or turn the IOReport reader into a diagnostic line if that is useful.
