### Game, title ID and version

FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, `0100606026F12000`, update v65536 (display version 1.0.1), with the game's own profile.

### What happened

It boots and plays well. From a 6.5-minute session with `DM_FPS_TARGET=60` (the game's own rate is 30):

- **Frame rate:** menus and the first area at a steady 60 fps (GPU 7 to 10 ms). Most of the play after that at 50 to 60 fps, with GPU 15 to 19 ms. One stretch of about 2 minutes (frames 3,300 to 8,400) at about 37 fps: GPU p50 26 ms, so GPU-bound there.
- **Memory:** footprint 1.8 to 3.0 GiB, with at least 3.1 GB left before the system limit. The memory guard stayed normal.
- **Audio:** 0 underruns on both outputs across 76,000 device callbacks.
- **Thermal:** state 2 throughout.
- **Movies:** three VP9 1080p movies through libvpx, all frames out (547, 4,264 and 64 packets), 1 to 4 ms a packet on average.
- **Hitches** (first launch, with no `pso_user.tsv` yet): pipeline builds on first sight, up to 2.7 s once (frame 3048: 60 pipelines and 60 shader libraries) and about 1 s twice (frames 15037 and 16234).

### Buffer-texture churn in the residency set

The same pattern #1061 describes for Mario & Luigi: Brothership (Unreal 4.27). Its fix is not in `main` yet, and this game shows it at a much larger scale. Every 300-frame window in gameplay adds and removes about 79,000 allocations from the residency set, almost all from one line:

```
[dm] [nvn] residency set up to frame 4800: commits 2926 / 235.1 ms, added 79399, 249246 MB (line 4624: 78668, 248509 MB, line 935: 478, 713 MB, ...), removed 79398, 2196 allocations in the set (962 MB)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] memory up to frame 13800: ... finalized textures still referenced 512 (small table, 2393853 put in total) ...
```

In the build's source, line 4624 is the `res_add(mt)` of the `t->d.target == 10` branch in `nvn_mtl.m`, where a buffer texture gets a new view on its pool's buffer. The ghost ring took about 2.4 million puts in 13,800 frames, roughly 175 a frame. Residency commits cost about 235 ms per 300 frames, about 0.8 ms of submit-thread time a frame. That does not explain the GPU-bound stretch, but checking `g_alias` before that branch, as #1061's item 3 does, would likely remove it here too.

### Setup

- **Device:** iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro, 8 GB), installed through LiveContainer, Increased Memory Limit off.
- **Build:** built on Windows with Apple's Metal Developer Tools for Windows (the NXNativeWindows fork), from a merge of `main` at about 2026-11-10. The log has `shader chain 1dd6ab865f17`; the fork's chain differs from upstream's because its toolchain files are hashed in.
- I can share the full log if it helps.
title: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (0100606026F12000, v65536): iPhone 15 Pro Max report, 50 to 60 fps at a 60 target, GPU-bound in heavy scenes; buffer textures churn the residency set as in #1061

I would like to import native save files from an emulator or a console export into a Mac game app. Downloaded ZIPs can have a wrapper folder, so an editable folder preview would help users choose the actual save files without stripping legitimate slot folders automatically.

Mac.

body:
### Game, title ID and version

Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft, `010024601BB16000`, 1.1.4 (update `010024601BB16800` v851968). No DLC.

### Engine and graphics API

Custom engine, OpenGL through EGL (`main` imports EGL and names `glShaderSource`; `subsdk0` is `NintendoSDK_OpenGL`). SDK 20.5.17. Loads 6 NROs at run time through `nn::ro`.

### Build

- nxnative commit `ccd834e`, shader chain `d24f05cf9d78`
- `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <folder> -k prod.keys --platform mac-app`, provisional profile (no profile in `dm/games`)
- MacBook Air M5 (Mac17,3), macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2
- The build itself succeeds: rewrite of main, sdk and 6 NROs; 131 GL shaders translated by `gl_shaders.py`; Mac app packed.

### What happens

The game crashes right after GL initialisation, at the first call through a function pointer that `eglGetProcAddress` left null:

```
[dm] [gl] EGL context: OpenGL 2.0
[dm] vi::SetLayerCrop 0,0 1920x1080
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=0 lr=main+0x1131c sp=0x16f30ec40
[dm] bt: main+0xa298 main+0x5d14 guest_main+0x144 guest_tramp+0x40 _pthread_start+0x88 thread_start+0x8
```

#### 1. GL entry points `hle_gl.m` does not implement

`DM_GL_MISSES=1` lists 8 names the game's loader asks for and gets null for:

```
glCompressedTexImage3D glCompressedTexSubImage3D glGetInternalformativ
glGenSamplers glDeleteSamplers glBindSampler glSamplerParameteri glSamplerParameterfv
```

They are used, not just looked up. With `DM_GL_STUBS=1` the log shows the calls:

```
[gl] [RED] glSamplerParameteri called: not implemented, returns 0 (x0=0 x1=0x2801 x2=0x2600)
[gl] [RED] glSamplerParameterfv called: not implemented, returns 0 (x0=0 x1=0x1004 x2=...)
[gl] [RED] glBindSampler called: not implemented, returns 0 (x0=0x4 x1=0 x2=0x8072)
[gl] [RED] GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB: writes into sRGB attachments are not converted
[gl] [RED] glCompressedTexImage3D called: not implemented, returns 0 (x0=0x8c1a x1=0 x2=0x8e8d)
[gl] [RED] glCompressedTexSubImage3D called: not implemented, returns 0 (x0=0x8c1a x1=0 x2=0)
```

So the game uses sampler objects (min filter, border colour) and BC7 sRGB (`GL_COMPRESSED_SRGB_ALPHA_BPTC_UNORM`) `GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY` textures, and enables `GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB`. The layer already has BC7 / BC7 sRGB formats, 2D arrays and Metal sampler descriptors, so these look like mostly thin additions.

#### 2. Next crash with the stubs: `glUniform4fv` with a null pointer

With `DM_GL_STUBS=1` the game gets further: audio starts, the window opens, all 6 NROs load. Then:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=_platform_memmove+0x1a4 lr=uni_write+0x140
[dm] bt: main+0xe124 nro5+0x6fa68 nro5+0x7b788 nro5+0x9a8d4 nro5+0x7ac8c nro5+0x3b0e8 main+0x5f24 guest_main+0x144 ...
```

The call at `main+0xe120` goes through the pointer the loader stores at GOT `0x9d990`, filled from `eglGetProcAddress("glUniform4fv")` at `main+0x103c0`. The arguments are `(loc, 0x60, *(x25 + 0x78))`: 96 vec4s (a matrix palette, probably) from a pointer that is null here. The game guards the call only with `loc >= 0` (`tbnz w0, #31`), so on the Switch either the location is -1 (the uniform is inactive in that program and the driver drops it) or the pointer is set by then. Root cause not found yet. Candidates: `glGetUniformLocation` returning a location for a uniform the real driver would report inactive, or a value the game should have obtained from one of the stubbed calls above.

### Possible scope

1. Sampler objects (`glGen/Delete/BindSampler`, `glSamplerParameter*`), overriding the bound texture's own sampler state for their unit.
2. `glCompressedTexImage3D` / `glCompressedTexSubImage3D` for 2D arrays (and 3D).
3. `glGetInternalformativ`.
4. Root cause of the null `glUniform4fv` source above.
5. `GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB` conversion.

I may pick this up myself later. Opening this to record the findings in case someone already has the GL side in progress.

No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.

body:
On an iPhone (Duo, iPhone19,4, iOS 26) Ocarina of Time v131072 reaches the Temple of
Time cutscene after the Master Sword is drawn for the first time, from a loaded save,
and stops on a white screen with no HUD. The game is not hung: frames keep advancing
(on-screen windows continue, 300 frames each, 0 dropped), it takes input, and audio
keeps rendering (36,000 device callbacks, 0 underruns, 23,186 non-silent renderer
frames). The movie is frozen on its first picture — which is the cutscene's white
fade-in, hence white rather than black.

The log for every failing run, from the moment the movie opens, with nothing after it:

    [dm] [codec] AV1 decoder 1: 1920x1080, input format 3, output format 3 (VideoToolbox on the host)
    [dm] [codec] image pool 1920x1080 format 3, tiling or mode 1, 1 picture(s): the host keeps the decoded pictures
    [dm] [movie] AV1: VideoToolbox decoding 1920x1080, profile 0 level 9
    [dm] [codec] AV1 decoder 1: first picture 1920x1080 into buffer 0
    [dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 12 pictures waiting for a released buffer
    [dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 12 pictures waiting for a released buffer
    [dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 12 pictures waiting for a released buffer
    [dm] nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603), a packet refused with 12 pictures waiting for a released buffer
    [dm] [nvn-mtl] NDVE engine: first movie frame by the engine (11 dispatches skipped)
    [dm] [nvn-mtl] NDVE engine: first movie frame resampled by the engine

then no further [codec] or [movie] line for the rest of the session, and no [RED] line
anywhere in it.

The asset is two files in the RomFS, AV1 in a Matroska container:

    /Event/Movie/Dm_TimeTemple_0095.webm    51,021,993 bytes
    /Event/Movie/Dm_TimeTemple_0115.webm    14,570,405 bytes

    ffprobe: av1, profile Main, level 9, 1920x1080, yuv420p, 60 fps, no audio track

which matches what the host announces at open (`input format 3, output format 3`,
`profile 0 level 9`). The bitstream is sound: `ffmpeg -v error -i Dm_TimeTemple_0095.webm
-f null -` decodes all 2,955 frames with no error output. I can supply both files if you
want to hand them to a repro directly.

It does not reproduce on the Mac. The same tree built with `--platform mac-app` plays
this cutscene through on an M2 Pro, same save, same profile. And that Mac log is what
rules out two things that look like the bug:

  * The four `busy (result 3603)` refusals with 12 pictures waiting are ordinary
    backpressure, not a deadlock: the Mac log has the same four in the same place, over
    the same `image pool … 1 picture(s)`, and then plays to `end of stream after 5947
    pictures`. It is the same HLE code on both.
  * AV1 decode works on this device and this build: earlier movies with identical
    announced parameters play to `end of stream` on the iPhone too (5,947 and 1,800
    pictures in one session).

Ruled out on the device, each with no difference at all:

  * DM_AV1_DAV1D=1 — dav1d in software instead of the A19's hardware VideoToolbox. The
    log confirms `[movie] AV1: dav1d 1.5.4 decoding (DM_AV1_DAV1D)` and it stalls
    identically, so the decoder is not the variable.
  * DM_NDVE_ENGINE=0 (the game's own movie network instead of the host's kernels)
  * DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0 (no deferred encoding)
  * a full device reboot, and a cold first launch straight after it
  * DM_LAUNCHER=0 (no launcher, no cloud save sync) — the configuration an earlier
    working run used
  * reverting 9d60776 and 47607fe (the linear WriteTexels and packaged-texture-layout
    changes in that day's pull), rebuilt and reinstalled

So the shape of it: the client takes picture one into buffer 0 and presents it, and then
never asks for picture two — on iOS only, with either decoder, while the Mac with the
same code, same pool size and same asset does ask. If the pool's take/release handshake
has an iOS-only path (the native-image route to an NVN texture, a QoS or thread
difference on the client's side of it), that is where I would look first.

Happy to run an instrumented build: I can add a log line to the pool take/release path in
hle_codec_video.c and say which side stops first, if that is easier than telling me from
the outside. DM_MOVIE_TRACE=1 produced no `[movie] [thread] [decoder]` line in the
failing run, so this goes through nn::codec's VideoDecoder directly rather than nn::movie.

Environment: iPhone Duo (iPhone19,4), iOS 26, nxnative 4b616bb54d14, shader chain
2afd39090b76, profile 0400486024DEC000 v131072, separate RomFS (26,247,576,430 bytes),
DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=1, 60 fps target, save at the Temple of Time.
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072): an in-game AV1 cutscene stops after the first picture on iOS, and the Mac build plays it

body:
A proposal from bringing up Minecraft Bedrock (the Vulkan game of #1652): its networking stack needs more from `nn::socket` than the offline-cut stubs provide, and the shape of a fix seems worth a design decision before any code.

**What happens on today's stubs** (every call fails):

1. The WebRTC Signaler builds a socketpair and polls it during boot; with every call returning −1 it `NN_ABORT`s (`fdNone`, physical_socket_server.cc) before `nnMain` even starts. Boot ends there.
2. `nn::socket::detail::EventFd` asks the host for an `AF_EVENTFD` socket, an address family Darwin does not have — the SDK aborts on the unknown family. We emulated it over a pipe (the read end honours the nonblocking flag, translating Horizon's `O_NONBLOCK` 0x80 to Darwin's 0x04 in `Fcntl`; a full pipe on write counts as already-signalled, which is what the SDK's wait wants).
3. Once the calls are real, the NetherNet Network thread retries its outbound connections in a tight loop — a full core of connect attempts. We gate `bind`/`connect` to loopback (anything else returns `ENETDOWN`), which keeps that loop dormant.

With those three, Bedrock boots through the Signaler into the title screen and full gameplay (world creation, 60 fps, audio) — no per-game patches involved.

**The question:** should the host grow an opt-in real-socket mode for this class of game? Sketch: loopback-only by default (`DM_NET=lo` or similar — no outbound traffic, keeping the offline guarantee), full pass-through only behind an explicit opt-in. The alternative is leaving it to downstream forks, which is where our implementation currently lives.

A working version (pass-through with the loopback guard, EventFd over a pipe, real `poll`/`select`) is in 68hctmzzjf-svg/TVPort#2 (`hle_net.c`, `hle_offline.c`) — happy to rework it into a PR here in whatever shape fits the project's design.
title: nn::socket: real loopback sockets and an EventFd — Minecraft Bedrock's WebRTC stack aborts on the offline stubs before nnMain

body:
### What happened

The game drops to 20 fps in places where it could hold 30. There the GPU needs 19–26 ms a frame, which fits 30 fps (33 ms), but the frame step keeps it at 20 (50 ms). With Dynamic resolution off, it was at 20 fps in 50 of 200 ten-second windows.

Two rules in `nvn_fstep_next` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_fstep.h`) cause it:

- **Stepping down is too strict.** Going from 20 to 30 fps needs 30 frames in a row under 28.3 ms, and one slower frame starts the count again. In a scene at 26 ms where some frames take 30 ms, the count rarely gets there.
- **A failed probe can overshoot.** When a try at 60 fps fails, the new frame rate comes from one slow frame, so a single 45 ms frame sends it to 20 fps instead of back to 30.

### What you expected

30 fps where the frame cost fits 30.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, v131072

### nxnative commit

`fd8188c`

**Game**: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072)
**Build**: commit `5aff926f21be`, shader chain `804433846e4b`, iOS app
**Device**: iPhone 19,4 (A20 Pro, 8 GB), 30 fps
**Where**: Hyrule Field, the Death Mountain trail, Kokiri Village and Goron Village — surfaces across the map show wrong or missing materials (bright patches, stretched textures, holes in the ground).

The log carries two task/mesh pipelines that never build:

```
[RED] task / mesh pipeline failed: task - mesh a203347bb7bdbd03_b fragment cd609edc78b467d8_b:
      Fragment input(s) `user(locn5)` mismatching mesh shader output type(s) or not written by mesh shader
[RED] task / mesh pipeline failed: task - mesh 3a6340a04bf09797_b fragment 2a7c48d595feaaeb_b:
      Fragment input(s) `user(locn5)` mismatching mesh shader output type(s) or not written by mesh shader
```

Both are reported once, then the draws that use them are dropped. The fragment stage reads `user(locn5)` but the mesh stage either writes it with another type or does not write it at all, so `newRenderPipelineState` refuses the pair and the surface disappears instead of falling back.

A third line, probably unrelated (the game note calls it harmless):

```
[RED] texture type mismatch: shader 09ab31c69af710c9_b (stage 1) declares slot 7 as Metal type 3,
      texture ID 908 is type 5 (NVN target 4, format 0x3f, Metal format 92); bound as is
```

Everything else is healthy: 30 fps held (p50 33.3 ms), no OOM, no pipeline hang, the rest of the task/mesh set compiles (33 190 pairs prebuilt on the Mac side of this build).

Is the `dlocsig`/`user(locn5)` mapping for passthrough-geometry mesh pipelines meant to insert the missing output, or should the pair fall back to the vertex + passthrough geometry path when the fragment input cannot be satisfied? A fallback would at least restore the geometry while the mapping is fixed.
title: Ocarina of Time (iOS): two task/mesh pipelines never build — fragment reads `user(locn5)` the mesh stage does not write, so map surfaces lose their materials

CONTRIBUTING asks for an issue before a change of more than about 1,000 lines. This is the scope of one such change, ready on the fork as `bymaxmarc/nxnative` branch `pr/hid-imu-samples`, before a pull request is opened.

## The game and what works

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (04008E001F098000, v65536, Switch 2, SDK 22.2.10) on an Apple-silicon Mac (M2 Max, macOS 27.2): with this change and the game's other fixes it goes through the menus and the motion calibration and plays matches with real motion from a right Joy-Con 2 (Bluetooth LE) or a DualSense. The game reads motion only through the SDK's own sensor fusion (`hid::UpdateSensorFusion` → `GetNpadImuSamples`), which talks to the hid service.

## What the change does (host only, `dm/host`)

1. Serves the hid calls the fusion makes (Npad IMU on/off and samples, the six-axis IC information, "newly assigned", the calibration parameter's load / store), with samples stateless like the console's ring.
2. Numbers the host's six-axis handles as the console does (`NpadStyleIndex` in byte 0), so the SDK's own handles are connected.
3. Writes `NpadImuSample` with the acceleration at +0x10 and the angular velocity at +0x1c (they were swapped: the fusion took gravity for a 562 deg/s turn; calibration failed, the paddle spun).
4. Adds fixed sensor noise to the host's own samples and a zero-bias stored calibration for a sensor whose offset is known; learns a GameController's gyro rest offset.
5. Keeps a 128-sample history per live stream and interpolates each 5 ms tick, playing the IMU samples back about one sample interval late (`DM_IMU_DELAY`), instead of repeating the newest sample.
6. Smaller pieces on the same paths: Joy-Cons shown as a pair read their own streams; the Joy-Con 2 clock anchor; `DM_IMU_LOG`.

## Size

About 590 lines of host code (`hle_hid.c` +491 / −38, `motion_fusion.h` +66, `switch2_proto.h`, one line each in `dm.h`, `hle_os.c`, `motion_apple.h`, `pad_switch2_apple.m`), about 940 lines of tests (`t_hid.c`, `t_motion.c`, `t_switch2.c`) and 50 of docs.

## How it is split

- `pr/hid-sw2-services-styles` (about 130 lines, before it): a whole controller shown as a Joy-Con pair when the game supports JoyDual but not full-key; the Joy-Con icon decoration colour; `t_hid` link stubs for main's new `DM_CTL` lines.
- `pr/hid-imu-samples` (this scope).
- `pr/hid-scripted-swing` (about 170 lines, after it): `DM_KEYS` / `DM_CTL` `Swing` and `Lift`, V and B on the Mac keyboard.

Items 1 to 4 cannot ship without 5 without writing an IMU path that never ran in the game: the IMU answer is built on the history (`six_source`, `live_at`), the noise depends on whether a tick holds a sample, and the stored calibration on whether the stream's offset is known. Items 5 and 6 could be cut out only together with that rewrite. If you prefer a different cut (for example the handles and the sample layout first, with the host's flat sensor only), say so and I will rework it.

## What it may reach in other games

The six-axis states (`GetSixAxisSensorStates`) of Switch 1 motion games (Breath of the Wild's aiming, Super Mario Odyssey's shake) now come from the same history and handle numbering, with no playout delay by default; the existing `t_hid` cases for them pass. They were not run in those games.

The pull request is now open: #2385 (after #2384; #2386 follows it). The game profile that relies on all of them: #2387.
title: Scope: Switch 2 sensor fusion (hid IMU calls) and live controller motion for Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, about 1,580 lines

### What

`main` at `ccd834e0` ("Port PRAGMATA …") breaks **every iOS build at link time**:

```
Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:
  "_probe_atrace", referenced from:
      _ctl_main in host__hle_hid.o
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1
```

### Why

`ccd834e0` adds the `atrace ` command to the HID debug console in `dm/host/hle_hid.c` (around line 244), calling `probe_atrace(lo, n)`. That function is defined in `dm/host/probe.c`:

```
dm/host/probe.c:393:void probe_atrace(uint64_t lo, uint64_t n) {
```

but `probe.c` is not among the iOS target's sources, so the iOS link has no definition. It is macOS-only in the iOS project (the file itself is iOS-aware — it guards `mach_vm.h` behind `#if !TARGET_OS_IPHONE` — so it looks like it was never added to the iOS source list rather than being intentionally excluded).

### Reproduce

Any `build_ipa_from_nsp.py <nsp folder> --prepare-xcode` then `xcodebuild` at `ccd834e0`, iOS. I hit it twice, on two different titles:

- Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle (`010067300059A000`, update v589824) — 11,625 iOS shaders compiled, link failed
- building for `--platform mac-app` never ran because the iOS link aborts first when both are asked for

The Mac side is unaffected (the symbol resolves there), and the same two titles built fine for iOS earlier today at `47607fe0`/`b149a1e4`.

### Suggest

Either add `dm/host/probe.c` to the iOS target's sources, or guard the `atrace` branch in `hle_hid.c` with `#if !TARGET_OS_IPHONE`, as the probe itself already does for the mach parts.

I have both dumps here and can test a fix on an iPhone 17 Pro Max and an iPad mini (A20 Pro) as soon as there is one.
title: iOS builds fail at link at ccd834e0: _probe_atrace undefined (dm/host/probe.c is not in the iOS target)

body: ### What is missing Some games require a specific Joy-Con configuration; third-party controllers always appear as Pro Controllers to the game, locking players out of many experiences, including motion games, even if the controller supports motion. For example, in Super Mario Party Jamboree, a DualSense is recognized as a Pro Controller. Selecting an activity that requires Joy-Cons then asks the player to change controllers. In the affected setup, selecting "change" does not provide a controller configuration screen. NXnative already supports native Joy-Con pairing and splitting, automatic player allocation and a controller-joining popup. What is missing is a way to choose how a third-party gamepad is presented to the game and which player uses it. ### What you propose Add a simple, controller-navigable configuration interface: 1. Keep existing automatic assignments and controller behavior as the default. Retain the current joining popup for requests with too few players (can be integrated into one system). 2. When controller types are incompatible, allow selecting Pro Controller, Joy-Con Pair, Joy-Con (L) or Joy-Con (R), restricted to the styles permitted by the game. Allow assigning controllers to each player, including two controllers representing the left and right halves of a Joy-Con Pair. 3. Show which players are ready/not ready and prevent applying an incompatible configuration. Reuse existing input, calibrated motion, rumble and native Joy-Con transport logic. 4. Each physical controller supplies its own motion when two devices form a pair. A one-gamepad pair shares one sensor stream; 5. The configuration menu can be accessed without game request using the topbar on macOS, gear icon on iOS or using the launch menu. A working implementation is available on [this fork's dedicated branch](https://github.com/dandelion711/nxnative/tree/feat/simpleui-prototype), as [one feature commit](https://github.com/dandelion711/nxnative/commit/5ad3487c) (SimpleUI). It is based on upstream `4b616bb` and includes the assignment engine, native macOS/iOS interface, input ownership safeguards, and optional in-game and launch-time access points. +1,656 lines. Successful testing enabled motion games in Super Mario Party Jamboree, motion control in ARMS and Fit Boxing 3 using DualSense and DualShock 4 controllers, that were previously unavailable. (This is something I used extensively in Ryubing but found to be missing in NXnative) Before creating a PR, I'd like to hear some opinions on this and agree on the scope. ### Screenshots Main menu displays the requested number of players and what controller type is assigned to each player. ("Automatic" by default — unmodified assignment rules). The "Not ready" shows what players need adjustment in order to apply: Upon selecting a player, the UI shows what type of controller is permitted. Controller types that aren't permitted are grayed out: When selecting a Joy-Con Pair, the user is asked whether to use one controller to represent the pair or use two physical controller as each Joy-Con: Assigning any controller type to a player asks the player to select a controller. The menu allows to identify each controller via vibration signal and reports whether a controller has already been assigned to a player and whether it has motion support: What else I'd like to eventually include: 1. Controller type auto-assign option: automatically assign each player's controller from "automatic" to the supported type without changing what controller is assigned to who. 2. Configure controllers on the game launch menu (before game start) and an option to save per-game configurations to avoid setting up every time. 3. Allow Keyboard to be represented as a player alongside controller players This could serve as a foundation for later controller-related modifications/tweaks/fixes. ### Platforms macOS and iOS/iPadOS
title: Allow third-party gamepads to be presented as Joy-Con controllers

body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Mac | MacBook Pro `Mac17,8`, Apple M5 Pro (18-core CPU, 20-core GPU), 48 GB |
| macOS | 27.3 (26C5035r) |
| Built-in screen | Liquid Retina XDR, 3456x2234, 120 Hz ProMotion |
| External screen | "Mi Monitor", 2560x1440 native, **fixed rate** (macOS offers 60 / 75 / 100 Hz, no 120 Hz), set to its native 2560x1440 at 60 Hz, no mirroring |
| nxnative | `e2df31ca` (main) plus an unrelated local change (RomFS substitution for three damaged textures in the user's NUP) |
| Shader chain | `2afd39090b76` |
| Game | The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), `0400486024DEC000`, v131072 |
| Build | Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), built with `DMSH_PROCS=0` (see the side note at the end) |

Settings (`env.txt` and launcher): `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`, `DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, `DM_METAL_HUD=1`, `DM_NVN_NDVE_MOVIE_DIRECT=1`; plus the overrides named per run below. Every run is fullscreen (checked with the user).

## Symptom

In fullscreen on the external screen the game stutters visibly in bursts. The same game, same place, same session moved to the built-in screen (also fullscreen) is very smooth. The GPU is not the limit: 10-13 ms of a 16.7 ms frame on both screens.

This looks like the same family as #603 (ProMotion fullscreen late presents), #347 and #822, but on a **fixed-rate external screen**, where the documented workarounds (frame latency 2 for variable-refresh fullscreen, the screen-rate match) do not apply or do not help.

## Measurements

`DM_NVN_TSV` (timing rows only), one run per column, same area of the game each time. "Late present" = `@pres_at_ms - @link_target_ms` of about one refresh (12-21 ms); every other present landed within 4 ms of its target, nothing in between.

| | External, link on, `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY=2` | Built-in (host switches it to fixed 60 Hz), link on, latency 2 | External, **`DM_PRESENT_LINK=0`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frames measured | 6,000 | 7,200 | 29,200 |
| Frames over 25 ms | **19.7%** (1,184) | 0.2% (16) | **0.52%** |
| Presents shown a refresh after the link's target | **54%** | 0% | no link |
| Frame time p50 / p99 | 16.59 / 33.4 ms | 16.66 / 18.4 ms | 16.67 / 19.7 ms |
| GPU p50 | 11.8 ms | 13.0 ms | 10.0 ms |

An earlier session on the external at the default latency 1 (no capture; the log's `on-screen` lines) dropped about 20-35 of every 300 frames, so latency 2 is no better here (19.7% of frames over 25 ms in the capture above).

What the link-on capture on the external shows:

- The link itself is healthy: `@link_gap_ms` p50 16.7 ms (3% of gaps over 25 ms), `@link_lead_ms` about 32 ms, `@wait_ms` and `@drawable_ms` 0. The host hands each frame over in time.
- macOS then shows 54% of presents one refresh after `targetPresentationTimestamp`, in runs (late runs: median 5, max 87 frames; on-time runs: median 4, max 34).
- A late present is followed by a frame over 25 ms 32% of the time (1,051 of 3,261), an on-time one 5% (132 of 2,731). That is the stutter: the host paces the game by the link, and each late present costs the next frame its tick.
- The built-in screen at the same latency shows 100% of presents within 4 ms of target.

## Finding: `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` removes it

With `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` on the same external screen, same settings, fullscreen: 0.52% of frames over 25 ms, p99 19.7 ms, median steady at 16.67 ms. The cost is slightly looser pacing: 0.68% of frames come in under 12 ms (catch-up after a late frame).

#603 found the same on a ProMotion panel with Mario Kart 8 Deluxe; this adds a second display class (a fixed-rate external, so it is not ProMotion-specific), a second game, and a measurement of where the late presents come from. #822 measured that on a fixed-rate screen the link also costs about 20 ms of input lag against `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` (50 ms against 29 ms game call to screen), so there are two reasons to prefer it where a game has headroom.

## Proposal

1. Record the external fixed-rate case in `docs/reference/frame-rate.md` next to the ProMotion entry, with `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` as the known fix (macOS 27.3 here, 26.6.2 in #603, so it is not a single OS build).
2. Let the host decide at run time, so no one needs an env override. It already has the pieces: a fallback to the present thread taking drawables itself (`present pacing mode 1 -> 0`, used when the link goes silent) and the per-present measurement (`presentedTime` against the link's target). If more than about 25% of the presents of a window of some hundred frames land a refresh late while the GPU time is below the frame budget, switch to pacing mode 0 for the rest of the run (or for that screen). A late-present share this large is unmistakable here (54% against 0%).
3. Optionally, make mode 0 the default at 60 fps on fixed-rate screens, given #822's input-lag numbers. That one needs measurements on more setups first.

## Not tested

- `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` on the built-in screen of this Mac (the run ended on the external). ProMotion fullscreen with the link off on this Mac.
- A window (composited) on the external, other monitors, cables or connection types (the connection type of this monitor is unknown), 100 Hz native mode.
- Games that lean on link pacing under load: this game has 4-7 ms of GPU headroom here.
- Input lag with the link off on this setup (only #822's numbers on another Mac).
- Whether the late presents depend on `DM_METAL_HUD=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1` or the MetalFX present upscale (all on; the built-in screen has them on too and does not show it).

The raw per-frame captures (timing rows only, about 19 MB and 31 MB) are available on request.

## Side note: shader build on macOS 27.3

Unrelated to the above: upstream `8b55ebb3` (shader finishing in forked worker processes) crashes the build on this Mac (the pool workers SIGSEGV right after the fork, inside `os_log_preferences_refresh` called from `sqlite3_open` opened by Python's `sqlite3` module; the build ends with `BrokenProcessPool`; I did not trace which call in the worker start opens the database). `DMSH_PROCS=0` builds fine. Say if you want a separate issue with the crash report.
title: Mac: fullscreen on a fixed-rate external screen, display-link presents land a refresh late (54%, 19.7% of frames over 25 ms); DM_PRESENT_LINK=0 fixes it (0.5%)

body:
## The need

Mario Golf: Super Rush (`0100C9C00E25C000`, 4.0.0, #814) has a story mode, Golf Adventure, that is played as a Mii. With the host as it is, the mode cannot start, and with that fixed the player is a body with nothing on its neck:

1. **The mode returns to its save slots at every press.** The console's database is empty, so the game opens the Mii editor to make a Mii (`nn::mii::AppendMii`), the host answers "cancelled", and the game goes back to the slot screen (`mii: AppendMii (the host has no Mii editor: cancelled)` once per press).
2. **The Mii has no head**, as `hle_mii.c` says of the stand-in ("It builds, and draws nothing"). In Mario Kart 8 Deluxe that is a detail of a demo race; here it is the player's character in every scene.

Before offering code I'd like to know whether you want any of this, and in what form, since the present answers ("a console with no Mii of its own", an empty stand-in) are deliberate.

## What I tried

On [`secretlemur28/nxnative@golf-tess`](https://github.com/secretlemur28/nxnative/tree/golf-tess) (`dm/host/hle_mii.c`; commits `d5885d02` for `AppendMii`, `7c10dcd4` and `8d864f34` for the head):

- **`AppendMii` makes a Mii.** It adds one default Mii to the console's database for the run and returns its index, instead of cancelling (`DM_MII_APPEND=0` cancels as before). `GetCount`, `Get` and `GetIndex` then answer for it. Golf shows its own "Select a Mii" screen with that Mii, asks "Play using this Mii?", and the mode starts; the game keeps the CharInfo in its own save.
- **A plain head in the MiiModel stand-in.** The 12 facelines are one ellipsoid (positions as 4 halves, normals as signed 10:10:10:2, texture coordinates as 2 halves: that reading of attributes 1 and 2 drew a lit, skin-coloured head at once), sized so the game's cap sits on it.
- **A drawn face.** The 12 mask shapes are the front of that ellipsoid, and the texture file gets one eye, one eyebrow and one mouth for all 62 / 24 / 37 entries: 64x64 `R8_G8_B8_A8`, block-linear, written with `nvn_swizzle`. From Golf's loader the entry's format byte indexes R8, R8_G8, R8_G8_B8_A8, BC4, BC5, BC7, ASTC 4x4 (`main+0x132c9c`, table `main+0x304b54`), so no compression is needed. An eye's dark part is its blue channel, green its white.

It is not a Mii's own face: every Mii gets the same head and features, there is no nose, hair, hat or nose-line texture, and nothing here comes from the firmware's files. `DM_MII_HEAD=0` leaves the stand-in as it is today.

Result in Golf: the mode starts, plays through its opening, the village and the driving-range lesson, and the character has a head with eyes, eyebrows and a smile under its cap.

## What I have not checked, and what it could change elsewhere

- **Only Golf was run.** Mario Kart 8 Deluxe builds twelve Mii heads for its title screen's demo race from the same stand-in: with a plain head in it those drivers would show generic heads where they show none today. I do not have the game here to look.
- A game that calls `AppendMii` and expects the player to have chosen a Mii gets a default one without being asked.
- The head's size and the mask's texture coordinates were fitted by eye to Golf's cap and camera, not to the real model's proportions.

## Questions

1. Is a default Mii from `AppendMii` acceptable as the default behaviour, or would you rather it be a setting, a per-game profile key, or stay cancelled?
2. Is a host-drawn stand-in head (and face) something you want in the host at all? If so: on by default, or behind a switch or profile key?
3. Would you prefer a different route for games that need real Miis, for example reading the MiiModel system data from files the player supplies from their own console, with the stand-in only as the fallback?

I can cut whichever parts you want into separate PRs (the `AppendMii` change is a few lines; the head and the face are about 120 lines in `hle_mii.c`).
title: Proposal: a Mii for games that need one (AppendMii makes a default Mii; a plain head in the MiiModel stand-in): Mario Golf: Super Rush's Golf Adventure

### What happened

# Mac shader compilation repeatedly crashes with `BrokenProcessPool`; `DMSH_PROCS=0` progresses

## Summary

The default multiprocessing implementation of the Mac shader builder repeatedly fails during shader compilation with `concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool`. Setting `DMSH_PROCS=0` switches to the previous thread-based implementation, which has progressed past the point where the default implementation repeatedly crashes.

## Game

- **Game:** DRAGON BALL: Sparking! ZERO
- **Title ID:** `010035F022078000`
- **Game version:** 2.0.75 (`v262144`)
- **Device:** MacBook Air with Apple M4, 16 GB unified memory
- **Platform:** macOS, native Mac app build

[nxnative-report-010035F022078000-2026-11-11.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34697959/nxnative-report-010035F022078000-2026-11-11.zip)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build the game using `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` with `--platform mac-app`, using the default shader-worker configuration.
2. Shader splitting completes successfully, producing 14,040 shaders.
3. Mac shader compilation fails after approximately 3–4 seconds with `concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool`.
4. Repeat the build with `DMSH_PROCS=0` to use the thread-based implementation.

## Expected behaviour

Mac shader compilation should complete without a worker process terminating unexpectedly.

## Actual behaviour

The default multiprocessing build repeatedly fails at the Mac shader compilation stage. The traceback ends with:

`concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool: A process in the process pool was terminated abruptly while the future was running or pending.`

The failure occurs consistently across three attempts.

With `DMSH_PROCS=0`, shader compilation progressed to 487 / 14,040 shaders (3%) after approximately 23 seconds and was still running at the time of observation.

## Initial investigation

The relevant shader-builder change appears to be commit `8b55ebb3`, which introduced worker processes and documents `DMSH_PROCS=0` as the thread-based fallback.

This makes the multiprocessing implementation a possible cause, but the root cause has not yet been confirmed.

The game profile is derived from the registered 2.0.76 profile for this 2.0.75 build. Shader splitting and extraction complete successfully before the failure.

## Attachments

I will attach the diagnostic ZIP generated by `scripts/bug_report.py`, including the build logs.

Please let me know if additional diagnostics or a reproduction with a different worker count would help isolate the problem.

_No response_

### What happened

An iPad shows the 3D scene magenta for the whole session; a few surfaces are right and the lighting
looks too dark. Same on every launch.

The cause is in the host, not in the game: a GPU copy into a texture of a sparse pool is not
mirrored into that texture's storage, while tex_from_storage() does upload such a texture from its
storage, so every re-upload re-reads the bytes from before the copy.

This build also carries two local edits that are not in any patch (both needed to start the game at
all): the provisional profile gives the game a 5 GB block instead of 66.5 GB (an iPhone cannot
reserve it: FATAL "reserve guest AS" in nn::osInitialize), and FMallocBinned3 slot layout 17
(Unreal 4.24 / 4.25, 4.26's without TryMalloc / TryRealloc) is added to hle_uemalloc.c. Neither
touches textures.

<details><summary>Evidence, and where the two decisions disagree</summary>

Reported from NX2Apple 1.3.0, Densha de GO!! Hashiro Yamanote Line `0100BC501355A000` (update 1.1.1
v131072), iPad Pro 11-inch M4, iPadOS 27.0.1. Game issue with the full log:
LNPANDY/NX2Apple#1182.

- `nvn_mtl.m` `tex_storage_dst()` returns 0 for a sparse pool:
  `… (t->pool->flags & (NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_CPU_NO_ACCESS | NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_VIRTUAL)) …`
- `nvn_mtl.m` `tex_from_storage()` a few hundred lines above does upload a sampled texture in a
  sparse pool from its storage, through the page table (docs/reference/nvn-objects.md, "Sampled
  textures in a sparse pool uploaded through the page table").
- The game fills those textures with `CommandBufferCopyBufferToTexture` (about 10 a frame);
  `TextureWriteTexels` is called 0 times in the whole run.
- `DM_NVN_ZBLOCK=1`: 117 textures, all `NVN_TEXTURE_FLAGS_SPARSE` (0x20), `packaged 0`, 512x512
  ASTC 6x6, 10 levels. Their base levels are all-zero at every re-upload, to the last frame:

```
[zb] upload    ser=112909 format 0x8b 512x512 levels 10 sparse 1 bound from level 1 frame 2279: L0 7396/7396 L1 1849/1849 L2 484/484 L3 0/121
[zb] re-upload ser=112909 ... bound from level 0 frame 3336: L0 7396/7396 L1 1849/1849 L2 0/484 L3 0/121
[zb] re-upload ser=112909 ... bound from level 0 frame 3525: L0 7396/7396 L1 1849/1849 L2 0/484 L3 0/121
```

- `DM_NVN_TEXINFO=512x512` separates two populations of the same shape: 152,300–155,583 of 327,680
  bytes non-zero (the CPU filled the big levels: these draw right) against 2,657–2,705 (mip tail
  only: these stay magenta). A 512x512 ASTC 6x6 tail (L3–L9) is 2,768 bytes, so the levels a copy
  fills are exactly the ones that read zero.
- No `->texture copy into ser=` line is printed for them: `mirror_note` is never reached.
- Not the dirty tracker: `packaged textures: … missed 0 (cumulative)` with `DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK=1`.

Related: #218 (copies into texture storage, Yoshi's Crafted World), #938 (`tex_storage_dst`
excluding GPU-owned storage, for mapped-range invalidation), #1599 ("a texture a GPU copy writes
into is made whole first" — for soft textures, which is the same family and does not cover a sparse
pool).

Two ways out, either is fine:

1. Let `tex_storage_dst()` accept a sparse pool and have `nvn_tex_mirror_b2t` / `nvn_tex_mirror_t2t`
   write through the page table into the mapped physical pages, as `nvn_sparse_copy` reads them.
2. Or stop uploading such a texture from its storage once a copy targeted it (mark it GPU-owned,
   `mtl_tex_gpu_owned`), so the copy lands in the Metal texture and stays.

Either way `sparse_view`'s level clamp should not settle on a level that is mapped but never
written: the log has `sampled from level 1 of 10 (finer levels not mapped)` for textures whose level
0 is mapped-but-zero.

</details>

### What you expected

Textured surfaces, as on the Switch, and normal brightness.

### Game, title ID and version

Densha de GO!! Hashiro Yamanote Line (電車でＧＯ！！ はしろう山手線), 0100BC501355A000, update 1.1.1 (v131072), no DLC

### nxnative commit

daba995ab521 — the engine HEAD this build reports (the fork's engine: NX2Apple pins upstream ab41d6a1 and applies patches/0001–0132; the two local edits for this game are described above)

### Shader chain version

89f44f9b6bb0

Settings: Metal 4 pipelines off, encode thread on, present upscale off, frame rate 30, picture fit.
Documents/env.txt (diagnostics only):
DM_NVN_ZBLOCK=1
DM_NVN_TEXINFO=512x512
DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK=1
DM_NVN_COUNT=1

### Logs

Attached: log.txt — the whole run from the app's Documents (5,400 frames), and
0100BC501355A000_build/logs/dmsh_build.log from the build that made the shader libraries
(5,929 shaders, 5,928 libraries, chain 89f44f9b6bb0). No game files.

body:
### What

Bring-up request for **Frostpunk** (Switch, `0100B1C0249B4000`, display version 1.0.1, update v65536, SDK 20.5.19, NVN). The survey and a provisional build attempt both stop at the same place: the shaders are inside **BitSquid/Stingray bundle containers**, which `shader_split.py` cannot read, so `shader_split` finds no shaders at all.

This is not a request for me to be given a profile — it is a report that the title's container format is unsupported, with the survey and the failing step below, so someone who knows the bundle format can judge whether it is worth a reader.

### The dump

- base `v-frostpunk.nsp` (3.56 GB), update `v-frostpunk_v65536.nsp` (v65536, 0.04 GB), DLC `v-frostpunk_all_expansions_pack_dlc.nsp` (121 KB, licence only, no content)
- modules: main (26.7 / 16.0 / 2.1 MB text/ro/data, 28 MB bss), rtld, sdk
- system resource: 0 MB; SDK components NVN-20_5_19, libz, nnSdk
- engine markers: NVN (main, sdk), "Unreal 4" (main) — but the game data says otherwise (below)
- imports vs host hooks: 1,254 host hooks, 868 present in this game's sdk exports; main imports 349 new symbols, all in areas the host already hooks (libc 182, C++ 60, fs 24, os 14, hid 13, audio 12, mem 8, oe 8, swkbd 6, vi 4, util 3, account 3, socket 2, aoc 2, nvn 2, nifm 2, time 1, ro 1, ec 1, pl 1)

### RomFS: 37 entries, 12 bundle triples, no loose shaders

```
animations.dat/.idx/.str      archives.*        common.*
custom_localizations.*        localizations.*   scenes.*
sequences.*                   sounds.*          templates.*
textures-s3.*                 videos.*          voices.*
```

The `.dat`/`.idx`/`.str` triple is the **BitSquid / Stingray bundle** layout (payload, entry index, string table), and `textures-s3` names the Stingray 3 texture bundle. Frostpunk is 11 bit's engine of that family, so the "Unreal 4" marker in `main` looks like a bundled library rather than the asset engine.

### Where it stops

`build_ipa_from_nsp.py <dump> -k <keys>` → survey OK, provisional profile guessed, then:

```
[5/7] shader split · splitting: 57%, 21/37 files
✗ [5/7] shader split (0:47)
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps
      them in a form shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents)
```

The survey says the same: *"no BNSH / BAHS at the top level: the shaders are inside compressed or other containers or in main, and must be located first."*

### Also flagged by the survey

*"SDK 20, not Mario's 16: NVN object sizes, API version and service layouts differ by SDK (the host was converted from D2R's SDK 12 to SDK 16 sizes); check them one by one."* Even with the shaders located, the NVN struct sizes for SDK 20.5.19 would need checking — Switch 2 titles looked at so far are SDK 19.

### What would unblock it

A reader for the BitSquid bundle triple in `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py` (the same shape as the existing Camelot NARC / Unreal IoStore / RPF6 readers), which would also need the bundle's compression — the survey counted zstd in 8 of the files. I have the dump and can test any reader or profile overlay against it, including on an iPad mini (A20 Pro) and an iPhone, and can run whatever diagnostic you want from the host.

I have not opened a PR because the container format, not the profile, is the work.
title: Frostpunk (0100B1C0249B4000, v65536, SDK 20.5.19): shaders live in BitSquid/Stingray bundle containers, so the split finds none

body:
### What is missing

On the Mac, the mouse is only the touch screen (`front_mac.m`: left button = finger 0) and the keyboard's right stick is Shift + arrow keys, which is all-or-nothing. In third-person shooters such as Red Dead Redemption (`01007820196A6000`), aiming and turning the camera with Shift + arrows is very imprecise, so playing with a keyboard and mouse is not really possible: the game needs a controller.

The keyboard layout is also fixed (WASD, J/K/U/I…). Because it reads key positions (`keyCode`), it already works on AZERTY (ZQSD), but a player cannot move a button to another key.

### What you propose

An optional "mouse as right stick" mode for the Mac front end, off by default so touch-screen games keep working:

- **Mouse movement → right stick**: the pointer is captured while the game window is key (`CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false)` + raw deltas from `NSEvent` `deltaX/deltaY`), and each frame's movement becomes a right-stick deflection, with a sensitivity setting, an optional curve/dead zone, and the stick returning to centre when the mouse stops. Escape or losing focus releases the pointer, as `input_release` already does for held keys.
- **Left click → ZR, right click → ZL** (fire / aim in most shooters), and the middle button or wheel to another button (e.g. R3).
- Settings `DM_MOUSE_STICK=1`, `DM_MOUSE_SENS=<n>`, `DM_MOUSE_BUTTONS=left=ZR,right=ZL,middle=RS`, ideally listed in `launcher.json` so the launch window and front ends can show them. A game profile could turn the mode on by default where it makes sense (shooters), while games that use the touch screen keep the current behaviour.

Related, smaller: a key map setting, e.g. `DM_KEYMAP=A=Space,B=E,ZR=…`, using the same position-based key codes, so a player can rebind the keyboard.

### Platforms

Mac
title: Mac: mouse as the right stick (camera and aiming) with mouse buttons on ZR/ZL, and a keyboard key map

body:
### What happened

On main `8fb5ffeb`, and again on `f75ac06e`, the NSP script's pipeline archive step fails for Bayonetta Origins: Cereza and the Lost Demon, in all three builds I ran, and the Mac app is packed without an archive:

```
pso_offline: 4772 pairs: 4772 bases, 0 left to the device (function constants), left out as the host leaves them: reflection 0, mesh 0, stage inputs 0, library 0, layer 0, primitive ID 0, entry 0 (0.7 s)
pso_offline: 77 compute shaders: 77 compute pipelines, left out: reflection 0, library 0, entry 0, constants 0
pso_offline: applegpu_g14s: metal-tt, 4772 bases, 77 compute pipelines (minutes) ...
pso_offline: applegpu_g14s: batch 1/10: 1000 bases, compiling or checking cache
[RED] pso_offline: metal-tt failed for applegpu_g14s (exit 1): applegpu-nt: error: cannot find private metadata at offset '8' in '…/pso/mac-work/batches.applegpu_g14s/00001/libraries/000c64be106f9a28_bp.metallib'
air-tt: applegpu-nt command failed
air-tt: air-tt command failed
```

The second build (`8fb5ffeb`) had the `pso/mac-work` folder removed first and failed the same way; so did the third, on `f75ac06e` with its new chain `1fa63cf7c7ae` (all 7,661 shaders built again). The app still runs: in a headless run (the bundle's host started directly, `DM_AUDIO=0`, input through `DM_CTL`) the host's own prebuild made the 4,772 bases in the background on the first start (80.4 s, none failed).

**What fails.** The game sets near = 0 (`depth_mode zero`), so every base takes the vertex entry `main0_z`. Of the 4,772 bases in the script, 492 name a specialized vertex function, all of them the `main0_z` entry of a pulling library (246 distinct `<key>_bp`), specialized with `dm_border_off` (constant 216 = true) as `pso_offline.py` does since 511a0a2c. The fragment function of every one of the 4,772 bases is specialized the same way (the game's two cover pixel shaders).

One-pipeline scripts cut from the failing group, each run alone through `xcrun -sdk macosx metal-tt -arch applegpu_g14s -macos-version-min 27.0` (AIR-TT 32023.922):

| Script | Result |
|---|---|
| the group's first base as written: vertex `000c64be106f9a28_bp` `main0_z` specialized, fragment `0ec195a93c4d3496_b` `main0` specialized | fails, `cannot find private metadata at offset '8'` |
| a base whose vertex function declares no constant (`0079d8ba80bda973_bp` `main0_z`), fragment specialized | compiles |
| the first base with its vertex function named unspecialized | fails, `cannot lower module with unresolved function constants` (as the tool's header says) |
| the first base with the vertex function taken from the same library's `main0` entry, same specialization | compiles |
| the first base with the vertex library cut down to `main0_z` alone (`dmsh_side.cut(lib, {'main0'})`), same specialization | compiles |
| the same library with its two functions swapped (`dmsh_side._take` with keep = [1, 0]: `main0_z` first, `main0` second), vertex `main0_z` specialized | compiles |
| that swapped library, vertex `main0` specialized (now the second function) | fails, `cannot find private metadata at offset '8'` |
| the first base of five other libraries as written (`00f8d7ff25b31345`, `013e59a5d89c7323`, `0289a194998883ca`, `03754b2141cedb50`, `04598b27e093203c`, each `_bp` `main0_z` specialized) | all five fail the same way |
| the whole first group without its 100 bases that name a specialized vertex function (900 bases) | compiles, 36 s |

The library reads as well-formed with the layout `dmsh_side.py` reads: two functions, `main0` with `OFFT` (0, 0, 0) and `main0_z` with `OFFT` (34, 8, 17456); the private metadata section is 16 bytes, two 8-byte entries (size 4, `ENDT`). Both functions declare `dm_border_off` (`pso_offline.constants`). So 8 is `main0_z`'s private-metadata offset in its `OFFT`, and an entry is there.

My reading of these runs: this metal-tt fails to specialize a function that is not the first one of its library. The swapped library shows it is the position and not the `main0_z` entry. The runs do not say which of the three things that come with being second is the cause (the function's index, its private-metadata offset or its code offset), and I tried no entry other than `main0` and `main0_z` (`main0_gs`, `main0_l`). It would fit the tool's header, which says specializing a `<key>_bp` function was checked on Ocarina of Time's libraries: that profile sets no `depth_mode`, so its bases take `main0`, the first function. In this game every vertex library has `main0` first and `main0_z` second.

If that reading holds, a game with `depth_mode zero` loses its archive as soon as one of its vertex shaders declares the border constant: one function metal-tt fails fails its group, and a failed group ends the whole step (`sys.exit`), so there is no archive at all, the compute pipelines included.

The comparison with an older main is not a clean before / after: an app built on `3b6b9803` (chain `39417042cfe8`, 2026-11-08, the same AIR-TT 32023.922) got an archive of all 4,772 bases with 0 pairs left to the device, but on that chain the same libraries declared no function constant, so there was nothing to specialize. 511a0a2c is the only commit in between that touches `pso_offline.py`; I did not bisect.

Not checked: any other game (55 of the 159 profiles on main set `depth_mode zero`; whether their vertex shaders declare the constant I have not looked), the iOS architectures, another Metal toolchain.

### What you expected

An archive. Two ways that might give one here, neither tried in the tool:

- leave a pair whose specialized entry is not its library's first function to the device (`rest_pairs.tsv`), as pairs with other constants are: 4,280 of this game's 4,772 bases name an unspecialized vertex function and should stay in the archive (the first group's 900 such bases compile, the last row of the table; the other nine groups and the compute pipelines I have not run);
- hand metal-tt a library in which that entry comes first (the cut and swapped rows of the table). I have not checked whether the host then finds that base, since it matches libraries by content.

I can open a PR for the first one with a test if that is the direction you want.

### Game, title ID and version

Bayonetta Origins: Cereza and the Lost Demon, `0100CF5010FEC000`, base game 1.0.0 (v0). Main has no profile for it yet; the build used the profile I am about to open a PR for (the NSP script's provisional profile plus `depth_mode zero`).

### nxnative commit

`8fb5ffeb` plus that profile's files, uncommitted at build time (the host log says `8fb5ffeb1f09+dirty`); they touch no tool. Then plain `f75ac06e` with the NSP script's provisional profile plus `depth_mode zero`.

### Shader chain version

`5ee7c6407a57` (on `8fb5ffeb`) and `1fa63cf7c7ae` (on `f75ac06e`)

### How it was built and run

`python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NSP folder> -k <prod.keys> --platform mac-app --progress lines`, three times (the second after removing `<title ID>_build/pso/mac-work`, the third on `f75ac06e`). All 7,661 shaders built each time, none failed.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro M2 Pro (19-core GPU, 32 GB), macOS 27.2 (26B123); Metal toolchain 27.2.47.0, `metal-tt -version`: AIR-TT 32023.922; archive architecture `applegpu_g14s`.

### Settings and environment overrides

None for the build. The run that timed the host's prebuild was headless, as said above.

### Logs

The failing lines of `pso_offline_mac.log` are quoted above (the path shortened). The one-pipeline `.mtl4-json` scripts hold no game data (labels, entry names, the constant and unspecialized attachment state); I can attach them. The `.metallib` files they name are built from the game's shaders, so I am not attaching those.

### No game files

- [x] No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.
title: `pso_offline.py`: metal-tt fails on a specialized `main0_z` entry ("cannot find private metadata at offset '8'"): a near = 0 game whose vertex shaders declare `dm_border_off` gets no pipeline archive (511a0a2c)

Borderlands 2 GOTY 1.0.2: Missing projectile visuals, elemental effects and Bink video overlays

Environment

* Game: Borderlands 2 GOTY, version 1.0.2
* Platform: Nintendo Switch version
* Runtime: nxnative
* Tested hosts:
    * macOS — MacBook Pro M1 Pro
    * iOS — iPhone 17
* Graphics backend: NVN / Metal
* Tested frame rate: 30 FPS
* 60 FPS mode: Not tested yet.

Current status

The game launches and is playable on both macOS and iPhone 17 through nxnative.

Performance is very good on both devices at 30 FPS. The 60 FPS mode has not been tested.

A shader parsing compatibility issue was encountered and fixed locally.

Commit: 91c9417b — Fix UE3 shader parsing for Borderlands 2.

The fix allows the second part of certain vertex shaders to be located at either control + 0x30 or control + 0x130.

The shader build completed successfully:

* 57,486 shaders processed
* 57,486 successful
* No shader compilation failures reported in the tested stages.

The original RomFS contents were also verified against the RomFS included in the generated IPA.

Known issues

1. Missing projectile visuals and elemental effects

Several weapon-related visual effects are not rendered:

* Projectile and bullet visuals for affected weapons.
* Fire effects.
* Corrosive effects.
* Slag effects.
* Shock effects.
* Some explosion effects.

The game remains playable, and weapon audio and gameplay logic continue to work.

2. Missing Angel / Lilith video overlays

During gameplay, certain telepathic messages from Angel and Lilith are supposed to display video-like character portraits.

Audio and subtitles play, but the image is missing.

The game contains Bink video files (.bik), and the main executable contains Bink-related implementation symbols and classes.

It is not yet clear whether this is a video decoding issue or a missing rendering integration.

Diagnostics so far

* Missing visual effects have been observed on both macOS and iPhone 17.
* No obvious resource-loading errors were found in the available runtime logs.
* NVN pipeline creation and texture uploads occur during gameplay.
* No direct Bink decoding errors have been identified.
* The original game resources are present in the RomFS image.

Questions

1. Are UE3 Cascade particle systems (ParticleSystem, ParticleEmitter) fully supported?
2. Are there known limitations with particle rendering, dynamic materials or projectile effects?
3. Is Bink video playback supported by the current host/runtime implementation?
4. Could someone help identify the relevant missing UE3 rendering or resource-loading functionality?

Any pointers toward the relevant implementation areas would be appreciated.

The game is already playable on both devices at 30 FPS. The goal is to investigate the missing visual effects and video overlays.
title: Borderlands 2 GOTY 1.0.2 — Playable on macOS/iOS, missing particle effects and Bink overlays

body:
**What happened**

Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072) built from a NUP slowed down progressively on a 16 GB M5 MacBook Air: 30 fps → ~8 fps after 6–10 minutes, with `MapPhysicalMemory ... application pool is full` and the loader thread `OptimizeChangeBanc` pinned. The log's `DM_FSLOG` showed one file, `Tex/Rock_WaterTemple_Gate_M_01_Nrm.bntx.zs` (452972 bytes), read 52,041 times in 599 s, in lockstep with the model `Land_ZoraRiver_ConnectionGate_A_01.bfres.zs`.

The cause: three `.zs` files in the NUP have their first 8–12 KB zeroed, so the zstd frame header and the first block are lost:

- `Tex/CmnTex_Map_Soil_FairyFountain_Floor_D_Nrm.bntx.zs` (216015 bytes)
- `Tex/RBake_Scene_GanonStage_G_2_1_d0_t0.bntx.zs` (1901341 bytes)
- `Tex/Rock_WaterTemple_Gate_M_01_Nrm.bntx.zs` (452972 bytes)

The NUP's per-file SHA-256 passes (the hash was taken over the damaged bytes), `pack_nup.py` packs it without a message, and a second download of the same NUP has the same three files. `docs/reference/packing.md` already says "A damaged file in a NUP or a dump has no hash to fail". Nothing in the build or at run time says which file is bad: the game retries the decode forever instead.

**Suggestion**

When `pack_nup.py` (and the dump path) reads each `.zs`, check that it starts with the zstd magic `28 b5 2f fd` (or a skippable frame `50 2a 4d 18`), and list the file names that do not, as the build already does for other damaged inputs. A file that is zero at the head is cheap to detect: a 16-byte read per `.zs`. I wrote a read-only scanner that does this against a built `romfs.img` and found exactly these three: https://github.com/qq3229311585-jpg/oot2-mac-notes (no game data in it).

**Two things that may help others**

- With the three files replaced by same-size stand-ins (valid zstd frame, same decompressed size; the BNTX's internal texture name must be rewritten to the target's name, and the relocation table `_RLT` must stay valid or the game crashes with a pointer that had the base added twice), the loop is gone: 95 segments / ~17 min at a flat 33.3 ms, `GPU waits so far` flat after updating to a build containing `fd8188c9`, resident memory ~6 GB instead of 12 GB with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`.
- Related, already tracked: #2277 (slow motion after a large scene change), #1821 (purple horizontal line; I see it too, rarely).

**Environment**

Game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), 0400486024DEC000, v131072. Mac app (`--platform mac-app`). MacBook Air, Apple M5, 16 GB, macOS 27.2. ### Outdoor frame pacing in the same session

The run was mostly at 60 fps before the hang, but not GPU-limited: pre-crash GPU time was p50 13.1 ms / p95 18.6 ms, frame time p50 16.7 ms / p95 21.4 ms. At present 3300 (about 55 s) the frame step went `hold 1 -> 2 vsyncs` after three late frames, held 45 frames at 30 fps, then probed back at present 3345 and held at 60 at present 3435 (log: `CPU 93% on performance cores`). The 300-frame window ending at frame 3600 had p95/p99 about 33.4 ms. The 96-100 ms longframes at frames 1344, 3962, 4916 and 5128 coincide with the GPU hangs; frame 1853 was a separate 131.9 ms hitch with 14.3 ms GPU and no new pipelines. The previous run also had 30 fps stretches outdoors (for example, frame 28800: p50 33.27 / p95 50.24 ms), so the frame pacing issue is reproducible separately from the hang.

### What I expected

No GPU hang or GPU-access revocation; the app's 60 fps frame step (or a stable 30 fps) without the 96-100 ms hitches.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, `01007EF00011E000`, 1.9.0 (v1114112).

`7ef83394a9ae` (read from the app's Info.plist). The collector checkout was `79741184`; that is not the build that ran.

- Xcode 27.2 (27B52); Apple metal version 32023.922 (metalfe-32023.922.4)

- Display: 100 Hz; in fullscreen the app switched it to 60 Hz for 60 fps (`front end: screen at 100 Hz switched to 60 Hz for 60 fps in fullscreen`)
- Game Mode is off: `LSSupportsGameMode = false` in Info.plist, and `gamepolicyd` logged `Game mode disabled`
- Drawable 1280x720; output 1920x1080 (later 1920x1048)

### Logs

The full bundle (`report.md`, this run's 266 KiB log and the previous 541 s log) is at `~/nxnative/nxnative-report-01007EF00011E000-2026-11-11.zip`; it is the output of `python3 scripts/bug_report.py "/Applications/The Legend of Zelda - Breath of the Wild.app"` and contains no game files, saves, keys or shader archives. The GitHub CLI here only uploads images and videos, so I could not attach the zip from this terminal; the key `[RED]` lines and the failed shader list are inline above, and I can attach the zip in the web UI or paste more of the log on request.

title: Breath of the Wild (01007EF00011E000, 1.9.0, M4): GPU hang at frame 1344 -> Metal 4 queue dies, GPU access revoked, host exits 70

body:
Environment: MacBook Air M2 (8 GB unified memory, 8-core GPU, 60 Hz), macOS 27.2.1, game 04007EF01F8AE000 (Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave, Switch 2), local build on chain 1d619d0f520b. evict LRU on: EVICT_IDLE=600 / EVERY=120 / AT=3500 / KEEP=16 / CAPMB=512 / LRU=1.

Baseline (DM_GUEST_FILE=0) is healthy: an 86-minute session, locked 30 fps, fp95 mean 33.8 ms, zero faults, exit 0; residency set peaked 4105 MB. The cost is memory: phys_footprint 8.8 GB (compressed 5.1 GB, available 0) by end of session — the reason we wanted the file backing.

With DM_GUEST_FILE=1 (CHUNK=512M) three distinct failures in one afternoon; the common variable is the file backing:

1) Freeze (session under test: hot-save restart, 91.66 s / 2522 frames). The framebuffer froze; user force-quit. Memory fully healthy (footprint 3037 MiB, compressed 162 MiB, guest files 4.38 GB on disk, working as intended), residency set only 3411 MB (far below the 4800–4950 MB crash band we know from guest_file=0). No long-frame buildup (max 698.8 ms), no RED/FATAL lines, and the audio thread kept rendering (28,000 callbacks, 0 underruns) — the submit path wedged while unrelated threads lived. A page-in storm ran through the session: 424,497 page-ins in 91.66 s ≈ 4,640/s, while GPU allocated (ledger) climbed to 9090 MB as the scene rebuilt.

2) Abort at startup: the next launch died 0.3 s after spawn with SIGABRT (abort() called, early main, before the first log line; report dmhost-2026-11-11-173418.ips). The same binary with the same env run manually from a terminal works — the abort only happens on the launcher path, so it also smells like an argv/parent-environment difference, not yet pinned down.

3) GPU reset: the next session ran ~79 s (frame 2150), showed a 147.9 ms frame (submit+present 117.8 ms), and then macOS put up "The GPU stopped running … After a GPU error, macOS stopped running the game's GPU work". The system stayed unresponsive until a forced power-off. Page-ins in those 79 s: 407,584 → 411,800 ≈ 5,200/s.

Working hypothesis: with the guest in unlinked sparse files mapped MAP_SHARED, the no-copy Metal buffers' backing pages page out under pressure. pool_evict_lru (dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m, ~line 1016) holds g_mu while it scans candidates and res_remove()s buffers — touching those swapped-out pages inside the mutex faults and blocks every thread that needs g_mu, including the submit path; sustained pressure escalates to a driver-level reset. For contrast, the S2Arm host uses the same file backing for its 9216 MB pool but has no evict LRU at all, and there the same setup only produces 1.5–2.7 s stalls that recover — the freeze appears only when evict and page-in run concurrently.

Logs and memstat available on request (04007EF01F8AE000.log = the abort session, .prev.log = the GPU-reset session, memstat.tsv = 1 Hz memory samples).

Questions:
- Any known interaction between DM_GUEST_FILE=1 and evict LRU (g_mu hold times, res_remove on file-backed no-copy buffers, pool-table rebuild after evict)?
- Would a mitigation make sense upstream: move the candidate scan out of g_mu, pre-touch before res_remove, or throttle evict while the page-in rate is high?
title: DM_GUEST_FILE=1 + evict LRU on 8 GB MacBook Air M2: framebuffer freeze, abort at startup, and a GPU reset

body:
Findings from a per-shader look at Ocarina of Time's GPU time, Kokiri Forest only, with the tools in https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/2315. The border-emulation part was measured on cut6 (chain cd098f1631bd); main has since made the same change for every shader (#1929, landed as 511a0a2c).

**Device and game.** MacBook Air M2 (10-core GPU, 16 GB), macOS 27.0, Ocarina of Time 0400486024DEC000 v131072, handheld 1440x810 (dynamic resolution off, target 60).

## Method

1. **Map.** `DM_NVN_HILITE` stills give each fragment shader's share of the picture. There were two kinds of run:
   - a scripted walk;
   - six places, each with 8 camera directions plus up and down, from test saves (#2002's `ocarina_test_save.py`).
2. **Rank.** `DM_NVN_GPUPROF` encoder times are joined with `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL` to give each shader's GPU ms.
   - A pass's time is split over its fragment shaders by draw count, so in a shared pass this is a share, not a measurement.
3. **Bench.** fsbench draws one shader full screen, with uniform blocks dumped from the game, together with source variants of the translated MSL. It reports their times, whether each output is bit-exact with the first, and Apple's compiler statistics.
4. **Confirm in game.** `DM_NVN_SHADER_ALT` with `DM_AB=240` draws the variant libraries only in alternate phases of one run:
   - each B phase is compared with its two A neighbours;
   - 3 runs of a 12,000-frame route, with warmed pipelines.

## The shaders

Coverage and ms are the means over the six places; the range is over the places. ms per % is the GPU ms divided by the coverage. Compiler statistics are for main0.

| key (role) | coverage % | GPU ms | Switch 2 regs / instr | Metal regs | spill | Metal instr | ms per % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1e4d2630d24846d0 (main pass, materials) | 9.2 (1.6–26.3) | 0.81 (0.47–1.28) | 91 / 1,760 | 128 | 256 B | 3,112 | 0.088 (a pass share, see below) |
| 19f99e925937b038 (main pass) | 6.5 (0–12.4) | 0.19 | 90 / 1,704 | 128 | 160 B | 2,862 | 0.029 |
| bd75f2962d28d424 (main pass) | 8.3 (walk) | 0.41 (walk) | 90 / 1,696 | 128 | 144 B | 2,839 | 0.049 |
| 087ef21b3a72ad3a (foliage, mesh pass) | 14.9 (8.6–22.2) | 0.22 | | 128 | | | 0.014 |
| 2a712d1a62f11442 (scene) | 8.4 | 0.18 | | 128 | 112 B | 4,330 | 0.021 |
| 9aa7f545bb5abcae (screen-space shadow mask) | an intermediate target: full screen, not visible | 0.46 | | 48 | 0 | 667 | |
| e55bcc53f003046a (depth prepass, alpha test) | 0.8 | 0.27 | | | | | |
| f48e795040c5dc9a (depth prepass and shadow maps, alpha test) | 0.3 | 0.22 | | | | | |

- 10 of the 25 costliest shaders of a main-pass frame are at the 128-register cap, and 8 of those spill. They are the large material shaders. The full-screen and post shaders use 20–48 registers.
- On the Switch 2, the same programs run at 90–91 registers.
- The translation costs 1.67–1.77× the Ampere instruction count, counted in real GPU instructions, not LLVM IR.

## What worked

**Border emulation off (`dm_bs` second sample removed).**
- `dm_bs` makes 11 of 29 texture instructions in 1e4d2630, and 16 of 33 in 19f99e92 and bd75f296.
- The second sample is guarded by a uniform mask test, but it has no side effects, so the compiler if-converts it: both samples always issue.
- This game's samplers use opaque white or opaque black borders, which Metal has itself. No dumped frame (the route at F2400–2402, and 6 places × 49–50 frames) has a border mask bit set.

| | 1e4d2630 | 19f99e92 | bd75f296 | 087ef21b | 9aa7f545 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fsbench, net ms full screen, base → without | 6.87 → 5.23 (−23.9 %) | 4.72 → 2.80 (−40.7 %) | 4.68 → 2.71 (−42.0 %) | 2.06 → 1.41 (−31.6 %) | 0.100 → 0.079 (−20.9 %) |
| output | bit-exact | bit-exact | bit-exact | bit-exact | bit-exact |

- Spill in 1e4d2630 goes from 256 to 208 B. All four stay at 128 registers.
- In game, for the first four shaders only:

| run | GPU p50, B − A | frame mean, B − A |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | −0.49 ms | −0.52 ms |
| 2 | −1.06 ms | −1.06 ms |
| 3 | −0.85 ms | −0.91 ms |

  Each run is 20 phase pairs, and B is lower in all three: about 0.85 ms a frame. 511a0a2c removes the second sample from every shader whose pipeline binds no sampler with a twin; an in-run `DM_NVN_BORDER_KEEP=ab` on main would give the all-shader figure.

## What did not work, or is not overhead

- **`precise::` → `fast::` min/max/clamp**, and dropping the pool-index clamp: identical code from the backend (same statistics), with time changes within noise.
- **Dropping the pool read mark (`dm_pool_mark`):** −12.8 % on 1e4d2630, −2.5 to −3.6 % on the other two. It is not safe: the host makes, over its budget, only the textures a shader has marked as read, so without the marks a needed texture could stay a stand-in.
- **Marking once a SIMD group** when every lane reads the same ID (an atomic for the first lane only) was slower: +4.1 % on 1e4d2630, +2.2 % on 19f99e92.
- **Pool indices as SIMD-group uniform** (`simd_broadcast_first`): −1.0 to +2.5 %, so no gain. It would also need a fact that the index is draw-uniform.
- **NaN scrub of sample coordinates removed:** −4 % at most. It changes behaviour on NaN coordinates, so it was not pursued.
- **9aa7f545's shadow lookups** (8 `sample_compare` on the cascades, 3–9 `gather_compare` on a 12288×12288 atlas) already use Metal's compare samplers natively. Border emulation was its only translation overhead.

## Readings that were corrected

- **1e4d2630 is not overdraw.** Its 264 draws a frame use depth EQUAL with no write after the game's own depth prepass; the MSL has `[[early_fragment_tests]]` and no discard. Each pixel is shaded about once.
- **Lights explain little.** The bench gives about 0.25 ms a light for a full screen, so about 0.02 ms a light at 9 % coverage.
- **Its 0.81 ms is mostly a share of the 699-draw main pass.** Over 60 stills, its ms follows its draw count (R² 0.38), not its coverage (R² 0.01). Its own pixel cost is about 0.6 ms (6.9 ms full screen × 9 %).
- For comparison, 2a712d1a's ms does follow its coverage (R² 0.66): that is what a key that costs per pixel looks like in this data.

## Open leads

- **Read-only storage buffers through `constant`:** −5.5 % on 1e4d2630, +2.4 % on 19f99e92, −2.3 % on bd75f296, bit-exact. It needs a per-buffer fact (read-only, draw-uniform address). Next: an in-run A/B with `DM_NVN_SHADER_ALT`.
- **The pool mark's cost** (≈ −12.8 % on 1e4d2630 if it were free). The remaining options are a function constant that drops the marks while nothing waits to be made, or marking once a draw on the host side.
- **Depth-only alpha test** (e55bcc53, f48e7950).
  - These are prepass and shadow-map draws with the colour mask 0, `discard_fragment`, and a depth write.
  - Their ms follows draws and vertices (R² up to 0.71), not pixels.
  - A depth-only build that keeps only the alpha test may help; not measured yet.
- **Work that coverage cannot see.** Highlight-based coverage misses depth-only draws and intermediate targets (9aa7f545, e55bcc53, f48e7950). Rank those by pass time instead.
- **Register pressure itself.** Removing the overhead above does not bring the material shaders under 128 registers, and front-end flags don't either. They run at minimum occupancy with 91 waits in 1e4d2630.

Related: #1929 (511a0a2c), #2308 (OoT's foliage mesh pass), #1230 (a per-game border-emulation key for Mario Kart World).

No game files or extracted data are attached: only shader key hashes and measurements.
