body:
Players patch Switch games with community ExeFS patches: 60 fps, resolution and quality mods shared as Atmosphère `exefs_patches/<name>/<build ID>.ips` files or IPSwitch `.pchtxt` files, which a Switch with Atmosphère, Ryujinx and the yuzu family all apply. nxnative has no way to take them. Writing the bytes into the NSO by hand skips the rewriter's checks, and a cheat that writes the same code is refused over words the rewriter changed.

Proposal: an NSP script option `--exefs-patches <folder>` (and `DM_EXEFS_PATCHES` for `patch_nso.py`) that writes the patches naming each module's build ID into it after the cuts and before the rewrite scan, so patched words are rewritten like the game's own. Formats as Ryujinx reads them (its parsers, MIT, ported to Python), with stricter errors: a malformed file, a record outside the module, two disagreeing records, or a record over a cut, gate or stub site stops the build with a `[RED]` line. Nothing is fetched and no patch file goes into the repository. Without the option nothing changes.

Scope questions for the maintainer:
- Is a player-supplied patch folder in scope at all, given that a frame-rate patch can change a game's speed and nothing here checks it?
- An NSP script option and env switch only, or should front ends offer it too (the option shows in `--help` and `docs/env_switches.tsv`)?

A PR implementing this (about 430 lines including 19 synthetic tests, no game data) is ready for review if the scope is agreed.
title: Apply community ExeFS patches (IPS, IPS32, .pchtxt) at build time

body:
### What is missing

e09ff955 streams the RomFS into one uncompressed DMROMFS1 image, embedded in the app or copied to the device.
For a large game the image is most of the app's size and of the transfer to the device.
Not every RomFS file is compressed by the game, and some content repeats between files.

### What you propose

This is a second implementation of an existing path, so we are asking before porting it.
Our fork reads the RomFS from a chunk store (b753e01f, 5a625faf, e6497d8e, 1fcbc880, 356bf559):

- Files are cut into content-defined chunks; identical chunks (by SHA-256) are stored once, each a zstd frame with a content checksum, compressed with one trained dictionary per store.
- One file: a 128-byte header, the frames, and an index whose SHA-256 the reader checks on open.
- Random access by offset, with a bounded cache of decompressed chunks (`DM_ROMSTORE_CACHE_MB`, default 16).
- `romstore.py verify` reads every file back through the host's reader and compares it bit for bit.

On `main` it would sit behind the same mount as DMROMFS1, chosen by its magic, with the image the default unless the numbers say otherwise.

### Apple libcompression or vendored zstd

libcompression offers LZ4, zlib, LZMA, LZFSE, Brotli and LZBITMAP (LZRAVEN and LZMESH need OS 27, above the 26 baseline): no zstd and no dictionaries.
Chunks are small, which is why the store trains one dictionary for all of them.
So we vendored zstd 1.5.7 (BSD); the host links only its decoder (`lib/common`, `lib/decompress`), built like libvpx and dav1d, and the compressor runs only in the build tool.
If you would rather not take another vendored library, an LZFSE variant without a dictionary is a smaller change; we would measure it next to zstd.

### Scope and size

About 700 lines of reader, builder and verifier, 290 of tests, and the vendored decoder (about 23,000 lines of upstream zstd).
It has to be redone on e09ff955's image-backed mount, overlays and DLC, which `main` gained after our fork.

### Alternatives considered

- APFS compression of the image: not under our control in an installed app's container.
- One compressed stream for the whole image: no random access.
- Per-file compression: no deduplication, poor ratios on small files.

### Evidence we would bring

For each game we can check, DMROMFS1 against the store, on a Mac and an iPad Air M4:

- Size: image, store, store without the dictionary, and LZFSE instead of zstd. So far we have one title: about 46% of the RomFS size.
- Read speed: cold and warm, sequential and random reads through the host's reader, and boot-to-title time.
- CPU cost: decompression time and the `power` line's CPU energy while a level streams.
- `romstore.py verify` passing on every game measured.

### Questions

1. Would you take a second RomFS format at all, or only one that replaces DMROMFS1?
2. Vendored zstd, or libcompression only?
3. Which games' numbers would decide it?

Platforms: Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: A compressed, deduplicated RomFS store beside DMROMFS1

body:
### What is missing

`hle_account.c` has one fixed user (`k_uid`), its nickname from `DM_NICK`, and `ShowUserSelector` returns that user without asking.
Two people on one device share one save, and a game that lists users or asks who is playing (3D World + Bowser's Fury lists all users) only ever sees one.

### What you propose

Our fork's 31fdd96a, adapted to `main`:

- `DM_USERS` names a tab-separated file, one user per line: Uid (32 hex digits), nickname, profile image path (a JPEG, may be empty), at most 8. Without it nothing changes.
- ListAllUsers, ListQualifiedUsers, GetUserCount, GetUserExistence, GetNickname and LoadProfileImage answer from that list.
- `ShowUserSelector` calls a new hook, `int front_user_select(char out[33])`, on the game thread, blocking as `front_text_input` does: 1 picked, 0 cancelled (the cancel result's value is not yet checked against an SDK), -1 no picker. A weak default returns -1, so front ends without a picker behave as today.
- `MountSaveData` with the preselected user's Uid mounts `DM_SAVE` as now; another user's Uid mounts that user's own folder, created on first mount.

### Saves: the old form carries forward

No existing save moves or changes.
The preselected user stays `k_uid` unless a front end says otherwise, so every existing save still belongs to the user who opens by default.
Other users' saves go beside it, never in it.
Our fork uses `DM_SAVE_ROOT/<uid>/saves/<title ID>/save`, which suits our iOS front end; for nxnative something like `<DM_SAVE>.users/<uid>/` beside `save/` is probably clearer.
Since our change, `main` has gained the device save (`<DM_SAVE>_device`), cloud sync (`DM_SAVE_SYNC`, `<DM_SAVE>-backups`) and save transactions; each user's save would use the same clone-and-commit path.
The device save stays shared, as on the Switch.

### Front ends

`Front-ends:` a new optional hook and an optional `DM_USERS` file; a front end that uses neither sees no change.

### Scope and size

About 190 lines with tests (`t_account`; a `t_fs` case for another user's mount and commit), plus a picker per front end that wants one, plus the save-sync work above.

### Alternatives considered

- One install or one save folder per person: works today, but the game cannot see or switch users.
- A user per controller (as 76545a58 maps controllers to players): games ask for users through the selector, not by controller.

### Questions

1. Is multi-user wanted in nxnative, or should it stay a front-end concern?
2. Which layout for other users' saves?
3. Should cloud sync cover every user or only the preselected one?
4. The user list: `DM_USERS`, the saved choices, or both? Should it show in `launcher.json`?

### Evidence we would bring

Host tests for the list, nickname, picture, selector and another user's mount and commit; an existing save opening unchanged after the update; and a game that lists users and one that shows the selector, played with two users on a Mac and an iPad.

Platforms: Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: Several user accounts: a user list, per-user nickname and picture, the game's user selector, a save per user

body:
### What is missing

Every lock, condition variable and address wait in `hle_thread.c` takes the global mutex G, and a waiter sleeps in `pthread_cond_wait` on G.
Waits on unrelated addresses therefore serialize with each other and with handle waits, events and thread lifecycle.
A game with many job threads can pay for this in hand-over latency and in wakeups of threads that only reacquire G.

### What you propose

ArbitrateLock, ArbitrateUnlock, WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic, SignalProcessWideKey, WaitForAddress and SignalToAddress move off G (our 4519e967, fix 4651bf15):

- Waiters hang in 256 address and 256 condition-key buckets, each an `os_unfair_lock`.
- A waiter parks on a per-thread word with `os_sync_wait_on_address` (macOS 14.4 / iOS 17.4, under the 26 baseline), so a wake reaches one thread.
- The two SVCs that span two addresses take the key bucket, then the lock bucket, so each stays atomic as under Horizon's scheduler lock.
- Kept exact: priority order with arrival order at equal priority, wake-one and wake-all, timeouts (a timeout racing a wake keeps the wake), a signalled condition waiter's lock-stage timeout, SignalToAddress arithmetic, cancellation, the deterministic clock.
- ArbitrateLock spins up to 2 µs (`DM_LOCK_SPIN_NS`) while the word still names the owner; without it two threads trading a short lock convoy.
- Handle waits, events, thread lifecycle and pausing stay under G.

### Scope and size

About 250 changed lines in `hle_thread.c` and a 380-line test, `t_sync` (semantics, lost-wakeup stress, timing, a TSan target).
Our change predates f7345d9a (same-core handoffs), db206a46, 8bdfcb73 and fec8e1f2, so it has to be redone on `main`.
The open part is how a wake through a bucket records the woken thread in the waker's handoff (`note_runnable`) without G.

### Alternatives considered

- A `pthread_cond` per bucket: still wakes through a mutex reacquire, with no per-thread target.
- `__ulock_wait` / `__ulock_wake`: private; `os_sync_wait_on_address` is the public form.

### Measured so far (microbenchmarks only)

`t_sync`, 8 guest threads, same Mac, before -> after: one contended lock 0.49 -> 2.0 M ops/s, four independent locks 4.9 -> 5.3 M, condition ping-pong 0.50 -> 0.83 M hand-overs/s, address semaphore 6.2 -> 9.4 M.
42/42 cases pass before and after; a 180 s stress run and TSan are clean.
These are not game results.

### Evidence we would bring

As fec8e1f2 and PR #1975 did: the old and new hosts in turn on the same route, medians of the 300-frame `power` lines (CPU energy per frame, CPU time, performance-core share, wakeups per second), frame time p50 and p95, and handoff counts.
On a Mac and an iPad Air M4, on games with busy job systems, plus one that shows the spin costs no energy where it does not help.

### Questions

1. Is moving these SVCs off G acceptable, or should G stay the one place that orders thread state?
2. The spin: on by default, per profile, or dropped?
3. Which games would you want measured?

Platforms: Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: Sync SVCs without the global lock: per-address wait buckets and os_sync_wait_on_address parking

body:
### What is missing

#1085 asked for a real internal resolution rather than MetalFX upscaling; #885 gets one for a few games by rewriting each game's sizes, heaps and scripts.
Today a raised resolution needs a render-scale stub per build (Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, Hades II since b84ee29a).
Every other game draws at its own size, and route B's support buffer writes `render_scale = 1.0` into all 73 entries, so the scale code the translated shaders already carry never runs.

### What you propose

A host-side scale S (1, 1.5 or 2), as Ryujinx does it; the game still sees its own sizes and memory.
In our fork (0ace7587, ccdac657, 89a8239d, 714a28ad, 352c3f3c, 8476e8e5, e4dca1f7, 72e4b158):

- The shader build records each texture binding's `render_scale` index and usage flags, and FragCoord use (`dmsh_rscale.py`, checked against the MSL). MSL and metallibs are unchanged; the chain version changes.
- Render targets that pass Ryujinx's eligibility rules are created at S. Viewports, scissors and clears scale per pass; occlusion counts divide by S²; the support buffer carries the real scales.
- Mixed attachments, image bindings, buffer-to-texture copies and CPU writes demote a target to 1x; readbacks go through a 1x copy.
- A 1x pass sampling a scaled texture reads a bilinear 1x copy, so guest-sized kernels (a bloom downsample) keep their footprint.
- At 1x every new path is skipped; below 768 MB of available memory new targets stay at 1x.

### Resolution families and dynamic resolution

c484b13c backs a family with one heap sized for its largest description.
At S that heap is S² larger, and a family has to share one scale: demoting one member demotes the family, or the family stays at 1x.
We met the same need separately (Odyssey re-describes one G-buffer pool about 1,000 times) and would propose building on c484b13c rather than a second heap path.
Dynamic resolution into a sub-rectangle of a fixed target works unchanged, since viewports and normalized coordinates scale with it; re-describing storage per size is the family case.

### Scope and size

About 1,150 lines with tests, plus 85 for a settings row shown for NVN games.
`nvn_mtl.m` has moved about 10,000 lines since our fork point, so this is a fresh port, in steps of a few hundred lines.
NVN only; GL and Vulkan stay at 1x.

### Alternatives considered

- Per-game rewrites (#885, b84ee29a): exact, but per build, and they enlarge guest heaps.
- MetalFX upscaling: cheaper, no new detail.

### Questions

1. Is a host-side internal resolution wanted, given #1085's close?
2. One switch with `DM_RENDER_SCALE` or a separate one (`DM_INTERNAL_RES` in our fork)? Is 1.5 wanted?
3. For a game with a stub: multiply the scales, or take one?
4. Default and memory guard on devices with 8 GB or less?

### Evidence we would bring

- `t_rscale` and `t_rscale_gpu` at 1, 1.5 and 2 under the Metal debug layer, each case against a 1x reference.
- `dmsh_rscale.py` agreement on every library of the games checked.
- Per game and scale, on a Mac and an iPad Air M4: GPU time p50, frame time, the scaled-target memory line, demotions with reasons, and 1x/2x shots of the same frame.

Platforms: Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: Internal resolution for every NVN game: render targets drawn at 1.5x or 2x on the host

All

body:
### What happened

An iPhone build of an Unreal game made from a provisional profile dies at launch, before the game runs any code:

```
[dm] >>> nnosInitialize
[dm] FATAL reserve guest AS
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 mem_init_once+0xc58 … svc_dispatch+0x44 gate_dispatch+0x144 dm_gate+0xe0 sdk+0x14942c guest_main+0x90
```

`profile_guess.py` gives every Unreal main with system resource `mem_reserve 0x1028000000` / `mem_alias 0x1000000000`. Its note calls this the layout "for the bring-up on the Mac" and says an iPhone takes a smaller guest block, as Octopath Traveler 0's profile does. Nothing applies that smaller block to an iPhone build, though. `mem_init_once` on iOS reserves the profile's alias as it is, so it asks for about 64.6 GB in one reservation and fails. Without the extended virtual addressing entitlement, iOS grants about 6 GB.

### Game, title ID and version

Dispatch, `01008BA02525A000`, update v720896, SDK 20.5.15, Unreal with `FMallocBinned3`, 80 MB of system resource. Built for iOS on Windows, with the profile left as `profile_guess` made it. Device: iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro).

### Workaround and result

`DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0xC8000000` in `env.txt` makes the reservation 0xF0000000, which matches the tested Unreal profiles (Octopath Traveler 0, TRIANGLE STRATEGY, Dragon Quest HD-2D and others: `mem_reserve 0xF0000000`, `mem_alias 0xC8000000`). With it the game boots and plays:

- `Unreal's engine region: 62.00 GB asked, 2.81 GB of address space, what the alias region has room for` (ue_region works as intended)
- about 58 fps; 2.5–3.0 GB footprint; alias region mapped up to 1.5 GB of the 3.12 GB
- 5 minutes of play, including handheld ↔ docked switches, with no `[RED]` lines

### Suggested change

Have `profile_guess.py` write `mem_reserve 0xF0000000` / `mem_alias 0xC8000000` for these mains. On the Mac, `mem_init_once` already reserves at least the Switch's 64 GB alias region whatever the profile says (`DM_GAME_MEM_ALIAS > SWITCH_ALIAS ? … : SWITCH_ALIAS`), so the Mac bring-up loses nothing. `test_profile_guess.UnrealMemory` asserts `alias >= 64 GB` and would need to check the iPhone bound instead, for example `reserve <= 6 GB`; its heap check still passes. Minecraft Dungeons II's committed profile (`0100A7C01B792000`) has the same 64 GB values and would hit this on an iPhone too.
title: Provisional Unreal profiles reserve a 64 GB guest block, which an iPhone refuses: FATAL reserve guest AS at launch (Dispatch, 01008BA02525A000)

body:
### What happened
After a large scene change, the GPU time per frame jumps about 3–4× and stays there until the game is restarted. In the meantime the game runs at 5–10 fps and plays in slow motion (game time 0.88 of real time). Restarting and loading the same place brings it back to normal right away, at the same spot.

Seen twice, in two separate sessions:
1. **Leaving the Great Deku Tree after Queen Gohma** (this report's log): the frame before held a steady 30 fps, then went to 7–11 fps.
2. **Walking into the Great Deku Tree** (an earlier session on an older build): GPU 23 → 67 ms, submit+present 10 → 160 ms, 4–5 fps, with a 16 s frame. After a restart, the GPU time inside the Deku Tree was 21–22 ms.

From the log, across the transition (300-frame windows):

| frames up to | frame p50 / p95 | GPU p50 / p95 | submit+present p50 | dropped | footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31200 (before) | 33.3 / 33.5 ms | 24.3 / 26.0 ms | 7.4 ms | 0 | 3.95 GB |
| 31500 (the scene change) | 33.5 / 161.9 ms | 25.7 / 60.9 ms | 7.1 ms | 105 | 6.14 GB |
| 31800 (after) | 143.0 / 175.1 ms | 81.2 / 102.6 ms | 7.5 ms | 298 | 5.99 GB |
| ~40800 (still after, minutes later) | 147.1 / 163.7 ms | 92.5 / 106.4 ms | — | — | — |

Notes from the same log:
- The CPU side stays normal: translation CPU 4–7.5 ms a frame, and `GPU waits so far 0` in the translation detail before and after. It is the GPU's own time per frame that grows.
- The extra GPU time does not follow the draw count, which looks like a per-frame cost that grew:

  | frames up to | draws / frame | GPU p50 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 31500 (before) | 882 | 25.7 ms |
  | 31800 | 1,113 | 81.2 ms |
  | 32100 | 682 | 78.0 ms |
  | 32400–33000 (a screen with almost nothing drawn, probably a menu or loading screen) | 4–5 | **12.2 ms** |
  | 40500 | 386 | 53.8 ms |
  | 40800 | 1,159 | 92.5 ms |

  For comparison, the boot screens took about 0.6 ms of GPU a frame in an earlier session on this Mac (an older build).
- In the scene-change window, the residency set added 4,458 allocations / 3,663 MB (`commits 1520 / 348.5 ms`). The window after it added 1,718 allocations / 545 MB, with 6,842 in the set. GPU allocated stayed at about 7.1–7.4 GB, resident about 6.0–6.1 GB.
- `OptimizeChangeBanc` was the busiest guest thread in the scene-change window (59 ms/s). In the window after, it was no longer at the top.
- Swap was about 3 GB, and the game's footprint about 6 GB. Thermal state stayed normal (`thermal -1`), on AC power.
- No GPU hang or `[RED]` line at the transition.

A similar case was posted in discussion #1789: an M5 (10-core GPU, 16 GB) with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`, where the submit thread waited for the GPU about 4× as often per frame after entering Castle Town Market, and stayed at 15–20 fps until a restart.

### What you expected
The GPU time per frame to return to about 21–25 ms after the scene change, as it is after a restart in the same place.

### Game, title ID and version
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, from a `.nup`. No DLC.

### nxnative commit
`fd8188c9` (as pinned by switch2mac), built as `fd8188c94a53+dirty`. The local changes:
- switch2mac's front end (overlay and settings).
- A local 40 fps frame step: state page +0x38 holds the step's unit, and `DM_FPS_TARGET=40` holds 3 ticks of 1/120 s on a 120 Hz link. It only touches the frame step and present pacing.

The earlier occurrence (2. above) was on `f7a54525` with only switch2mac's front end, at `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, so it is not the 40 fps change.

### Shader chain version
`cb2e91c138e3`

### How it was built and run
switch2mac (`azmasm/switch2mac`) `build --engine nxnative` from the `.nup`, which runs nxnative's `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac-app`. All 42,848 shaders built, with a bundled pipeline archive for `applegpu_g14s`. App and game image on an external USB SSD (10 Gb/s).

### Device and OS
MacBook Pro 14" (Mac14,9), Apple M2 Pro, 10-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 16 GB, macOS 27.2, built-in ProMotion screen.

### Settings and environment overrides
env.txt:
```
DM_FPS_TARGET=40
DM_GUEST_FILE=1
```
Earlier occurrence: `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, `DM_GUEST_FILE=1`.

### Logs
Excerpts above; the full log can be attached if useful.

### No game files
- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: Ocarina of Time: GPU time per frame triples after a big scene change (leaving the Deku Tree) and stays up until restart (M2 Pro 16 GB)

body:
### What happens

Between two Mac builds of Ocarina of Time, **fog, light shafts and the glow around lights stop being drawn**. The geometry, textures and UI are all there; what is missing is the atmosphere.

Seen in two places, from **the same save, at the same in-game time, standing in the same spots**:

- **Great Fairy fountain** (interior, so no day/night cycle): the older build fills the room with mist and a strong bloom around the columns. The newer build draws the same room clear and sharp, with no mist and no glow.
- **Sacred Forest Meadow / Kokiri area**: the older build has visible light shafts from above, haze between the trees and falling leaves. The newer build is dark, with no shafts and no haze.

The player noticed it before any of this was measured, and also reports the newer build feeling less smooth (that part is reported separately in discussion #1789; it is a frame-time tail regression, not this).

### Builds

| | older | newer |
|---|---|---|
| commit | `d8b2b64a` | `ced36121` |
| chain | `39417042cfe8` | `bc8830d4ba5a` |

**Disclosure:** the older build is not plain `d8b2b64a`. It carries four local commits: the opt-in task isolation of #1842 (off by default, not set in these runs) and three for the NDVE movie path (a direct bilinear scale that predates [`c66a36ab`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/c66a36ab)). None of them touches fog, lighting or the scene passes, and none was active in gameplay, but a clean bisect should use plain `d8b2b64a`.

### Setup

- MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), `applegpu_g13s`
- Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), `0400486024DEC000`, v131072, built from a NUP as a Mac app
- `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`, dynamic resolution off, windowed 2560x1440

### What the HUD reads at those spots

| | older | newer |
|---|---|---|
| fountain, GPU / fps | 16.14 ms / 44.72 | 17.58 ms / 34.45 |
| forest, GPU / fps | 21.47 ms / 30.00 | 25.59 ms / 22.16 |

The newer build is **slower** at both spots while drawing less. So this does not look like work being skipped to save time.

(The Metal memory also reads about 3.5 GB lower on the newer build at both spots, but its App memory is lower too and its session was shorter, so that is probably session length and I would not lean on it. It may also be a consequence rather than a cause: effects that never draw never have their textures read, so the pool walk never makes them.)

### What it is not

Each of these was checked and came back negative:

- **Missing shaders.** Both apps ship 42,851 shader-map rows and about 5.4 GB of libraries; the newer image is slightly larger. The build log has no error or warning.
- **Missing pipelines.** Prewarm on the newer build: 16,080 shaders / 6,871 render / 784 compute, against 16,079-16,080 / 6,818-6,831 / 782-784 on the older one. It builds more, not fewer. `shader keys not in the shader map` is 0.
- **Skipped passes.** `@passes` per exterior frame went **up**, 101 to 106.
- **Short uniform bindings** ([`26062f9e`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/26062f9e), [`e45694b7`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/e45694b7)). Those log a line with a running count when they shorten a binding; the log has none.
- **Pool stand-ins** ([`6c676444`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/6c676444)). With `DM_NVN_POOL_FIRST=1`: `4629 made, 798 gave way to their texture, 3717 held; first reads of a texture not made found a stand-in 24 times and the dummy 0 times (0 of them textures of 256 KB or more)`. 24 reads cannot remove the atmosphere from whole scenes.
- **The translation chain.** `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP=every:300` on both builds over comparable routes: 316 distinct fragment shaders and 249 vertex on the older, 297 and 244 on the newer. 47 fragment shaders appear only in the older run and 28 only in the newer, and both sets are a mix of `/Shader`, `/Effect`, `/Layout2Shader` and `/Lib/agl` — **no group of effect shaders is absent from the newer build**. The routes were not identical (11 dumped frames against 19), so this is not airtight, but there is no sign of a whole class of programs going missing.

### Where that leaves it

The same programs run over the same geometry in both builds and the picture differs, which points at **the data those shaders receive — textures or uniforms — rather than at the shaders themselves**. That is the host side, and within it the texture and uniform changes of 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10.

Pass dumps for both builds are available if useful.

No game files or keys are included in this report.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Ocarina of Time (M1 Max): fog, light shafts and glow are no longer drawn between d8b2b64a and ced36121

body:
### What happened

The CRI Mana movies flicker in FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles on an iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro), and so do sprites in the in-engine scenes.

I stepped through a screen recording of the opening movie frame by frame. Two of every three displayed frames are right. Every third frame, the movie picture is replaced by horizontal streaks: each row is a single colour stretched across the whole width, as if every sample of the row read the same texel. The subtitles and the touch overlay stay correct, so only the movie quad is wrong. The per-frame mean brightness of the recording shows the 3-frame period clearly (for example `111 111 86 111 111 86 …`).

There is no `[RED]` line during the movie. Frame time stays at 16.7 ms and GPU time is 2–7 ms, so this is not load-related.

### Game, title ID and version

FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles, `010038B015560000`, update 1.5.1 (v524288), from a profile derived from the registered 1.4.0 one. The 1.4.0 job-pool wake cut was ported to the 1.5.1 `main` (`ace351a1…`, same offsets, only the SignalEvent stub moved), and the game boots and plays.

### Build

An iOS IPA built on Windows with the NXNative for Windows port, host from `main` as of 0d84a3f7 / 6a6a018d, shader chain `b563364ec9dd`.

### What was ruled out

Each change below was tested on the device, and the flicker stayed every time:

| Tried | Result |
|---|---|
| `DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=all` | still flickers |
| `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` | still flickers |
| `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0` | still flickers |
| `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0` (the setting already in use) | flickers |
| Host with argument block patching off (adaff735's path) and the uniform read bound off (all CBSIZE entries 64 KB, no `ub_padded`) | still flickers. The bound's code was never reached in this game, since its log line never printed. |

### What `DM_NVN_TEXINFO=1280x720` shows

- The movie's luma planes are `format=0x1` (R8) 1280x720 textures with `flags=0`, `stride=0` and `size=0xf0000`. They sit in a `CPU_UNCACHED | GPU_CACHED | COMPRESSIBLE` pool (flags 0xa2).
- The game rotates them through 8 storage offsets (`0x27fe400`, `0x29aac00`, `0x2b13200`, `0x2c7b800`, `0x2de3e00`, `0x2f4c400`, `0x30b4a00`, `0x321d000`). Two texture objects are initialized over each storage.
- At first use, each is `swizzled=1 has_layout=0 … storage 983040 bytes non-zero 921600`. That is exactly 1280×720 non-zero bytes, so the data appears to be there.
- During the movie, the stats show 3 first uploads per frame (about 1.3 MB, consistent with Y plus two half-size chroma planes) and about 2,700 residency additions per 300 frames from lines 3431 and 3450. `CriManaDecodeThread` runs at priority 51.

So the textures look complete when the host first reads them. The streak looks like a sampling or binding problem on one frame in three, not missing data. I can't take a GPU frame capture: there's no Mac here.

### What would help

Someone with a Mac reproducing this on the opening movie of a fresh save, which starts within a few seconds of boot, and taking a capture of a streaked frame. I have the screen recording and the full device logs, with and without `DM_NVN_TEXINFO`, and can attach them if useful.

### Separate, smaller finding

0662f9d8's `dm_blend0` helper declares `main0_out& dm_o` without an address space. The Windows Metal front end (32023) rejects it with `reference type must have explicit address space qualifier`, and 201 of this game's 306 pixel shaders failed to build. `thread main0_out& dm_o` builds them all. Apple's own compiler may accept the original; `thread` is valid on both.
title: FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles (010038B015560000, 1.5.1, iPhone): every third frame of CRI Mana movies drawn as horizontal streaks

body:
### What happened

Since 0662f9d ("A NaN or infinite colour under a zero source blend weight adds nothing…"), a Mac build of Ocarina of Time stops at the Mac shaders stage: 22,296 of 42,848 shaders fail to compile in Metal, every time.

```
✓ Mac shaders 20,552 of 42,848 shaders ready (0 from the cache); 22,296 failed
[RED] 22296 shaders that translated in b-cb2e91c138e3 fail in b-7c609af36b0f: a change to the translation chain broke them
```

All failures in `dmsh_build.log` are the same error, on the helper that 0662f9d adds in `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_rewrite.py` (line 522):

```
<stdin>:67:70: error: reference type must have explicit address space qualifier
static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void dm_blend0(main0_out& dm_o, constant dm_blend_state& dm_s)
                                                                     ^
```

`main0_out&` has no address space. A minimal shader with the same signature fails the same way with this Metal compiler, and compiles once the parameter is `thread main0_out& dm_o`:

```metal
static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void dm_blend0(thread main0_out& dm_o, constant dm_blend_state& dm_s)
```

The line is unchanged on main (6a6a018). I have not rebuilt the game with the change.

### What you expected

The shaders compile as on ab41d6a (chain b-cb2e91c138e3, 42,848 of 42,848).

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, update v131072 (NUP).

### nxnative commit

c823c3c (the helper comes from 0662f9d; still present on 6a6a018).

### Shader chain version

b-7c609af36b0f (previous build: b-cb2e91c138e3).

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <game>.nup --platform mac-app --language fr --progress json --allow-damaged` (the NUP has 3 damaged `.bntx.zs` textures, unrelated to this).

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro, M4 Pro (16-core GPU, 24 GB), macOS 26.7.2, Xcode 27.2, Apple metal version 32023.922 (metalfe-32023.922.4).

### Settings and environment overrides

None for the build.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072, Mac): 22,296 shaders fail to compile in Metal since 0662f9d, dm_blend0's `main0_out&` has no address space qualifier

body:
*This report was written by Claude (an AI assistant made by Anthropic), which did the measurements below while working with the account's owner on their own phone. The owner gave permission to publish the findings under this account. No game files are attached.*

## Summary

Ocarina of Time on an iPhone 16 Pro Max (A18 Pro, 8 GB, iOS 27.2) falls into one of two steady states at each launch and stays there until the app is closed. The docs already describe two such states on the Mac ([frame-rate.md, "The GPU idles with the next command buffer already committed"](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/frame-rate.md)). On the phone the state is visible within the first 300-frame window after the save's load frame, before the scene's GPU load is there, and the mark is the CPU's performance state, not the GPU.

Measured on builds made from the `cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake` fork (x9) with local changes, so line numbers and some switches differ from `main`; about 60 scripted launches on one day, 30 fps target, render scale 0.5, Potato preset, standing at the save point and then a scripted route of full camera turns towards Kokiri Forest's village.

## The two states

| | steady | the one that stalls |
|---|---|---|
| CPU power, first window after the load | 0.25-0.7 W | 1.0-1.5 W |
| submit thread's mean clock | 2.0-2.9 GHz | 3.2-3.5 GHz |
| process CPU minus guest threads' CPU | 205-280 ms/s | 415-556 ms/s |
| unnamed threads (Metal / libdispatch), share of a core, standing | 9-11 % | 35-41 % (four threads at 4-14 % each) |
| wakeups out of platform idle | about 70 /s | about 17 /s |
| camera-turn route (65 s) | 25-30 fps, 1-27 frames over 100 ms | 10-20 fps, 180-200 frames over 100 ms |
| time inside residency commits over the route | 0.6-0.7 s | 2.2-4.6 s |

- Guest threads use less CPU time in the second state (the clock is higher); the host-side threads use more, so the surplus is time-based waiting rather than work.
- "Process CPU minus guest-thread CPU" separated every launch. A frame-rate counter that shows it (coloured by the lowest of the last three windows, so a streaming burst does not flip it) lets the player tell which launch they got; I can send that as a small patch if it is wanted.
- In the first window the frames do not overlap yet in either state (the previous frame's last fence is done at each frame's first commit in 300 of 300 frames), so the overlap seen later is a consequence, not the trigger.
- The game makes 6.0 submissions a frame here, one command buffer each.
- How often: 2 of 20 launches when each followed a short standing run, about 40 % when each followed a run with the camera-turn route. Thermal state does not decide it (both states seen at nominal, fair and serious).

## What did not change which state a launch gets

- iOS Game Mode on or off; `DM_RT=0` alone; `DM_FRAME_WG=1`; `DM_QOS_EDGES=0,59`; `DM_NVN_CUT=0`; `DM_NVN_UB_COPY_THREAD=0`; `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`.
- Telling the game it lost focus and got it back, and a real trip to the background and back: a launch in either state stayed in it.
- A limiter on the encode thread that holds a submission's commit until all but k earlier ones have completed: with k = 3 the host-side CPU fell in launches that were already steady, but a launch in the other state stayed there (and at k = 2, or when a frame's commits waited for the whole previous frame, the GPU sat idle, its clock dropped and the frame rate fell to about 21 fps).
- Holding the frame's start until the GPU has finished the previous frame removed the long frames (0 in the route) and cost the frame rate (19 fps standing).
- Wiring file-backed pages before the residency commit (the PR #1971 idea): the buffers were already resident (about 4,000 wired in 0 ms), no change. Flushing upload batches every 32 textures (the PR #2008 idea): the game's uploads here happen inside submissions, so it never took effect.

## Two things that did help

- The game's own lighter resolution preset (`DM_RES_PRESET=1`, 960x540) at a 30 fps target gave the cleanest camera-turn route of the day in a steady launch: 29.8 fps with 1 frame over 100 ms (against 25-29 fps and 1-27 such frames without it).
- Frame generation costs p50 11.7 ms of GPU a generated frame at 1920x1080 on this phone, which does not fit beside a 30 ms frame (the real rate fell to 24 fps), and p50 4.2-4.8 ms at 1280x720 with that preset, where it fits: 30 drawn, 60 shown, 1 present dropped of 1,499 standing.

## Open

What latches the state right after the load is not found. The pattern (same total CPU, higher clock, cores that rarely idle, unnamed system threads busy) looks like the performance controller staying up with something on the Metal side waiting actively, but nothing here proves it. If anyone has a way to name those threads on a phone, or an idea to test, I can run it on this device.
title: Ocarina of Time on an 8 GB iPhone: each launch falls into one of two states, decided in the first seconds after the save loads (measurements)

body:
Building The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072) from a `.nup` stops at the shader regression check:

```
[RED] 001ef25305e1bd7e: translated in b-e1d97965d3f3, translation failed in b-2978804b33f7: integer-input retranslation:
... 1673 more in <work dir>/logs/shader_regressions.log
[RED] 1683 shaders that translated in b-e1d97965d3f3 fail in b-2978804b33f7: a change to the translation chain broke them
```

The text after `integer-input retranslation:` is empty.

## Environment

- MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,3), Apple M1 Pro, 14-core GPU, 16 GB, macOS 26.7.2 (25G332)
- Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal 32023.922
- Repository at `f3ec8fc`, `--platform mac-app`, full shader map (42,848)
- Library from the previous chain: `b-e1d97965d3f3` (12 GB, built from `976fbd5`)
- Library from the new chain: `b-2978804b33f7` (8.9 GB)

## Impact

572 of the 1,683 failing keys are in `dm/games/0400486024DEC000/shader_seen.tsv`, the list the playtests used for the title, the opening, Link's house and Kokiri Forest. `--allow-shader-regressions` would drop shaders those areas draw with.

## Suspect commits

The chain moved across `e45694b` (a uniform read at a fixed offset is bounded once per binding, chain `bc8830d4ba5a`) and `918e9f3` (bounded uniform reads written as `select(0, read, cond)`, chain `eaa843a79149`). The empty message and the "integer-input retranslation" wording point at the second.

## Possibly related

On this Mac the committed native translator's arm64 slice segfaults on `--source-sha`, which is issue #2190 (`pipe2` weak-imported from the 27.2 SDK). Translation itself runs on arm64; only that flag crashes. I built with a wrapper that routes `--source-sha` through the x86_64 slice under Rosetta and ran `tool_lock.py --update-lock`. I can reproduce without the wrapper if that matters.

## Testing

I can run builds, A/Bs or a shader subset against a candidate fix. The full list is in `<work dir>/logs/shader_regressions.log` (1,683 `[RED]` lines) and I can attach it.
title: Ocarina of Time: 1,683 shaders that translated on b-e1d97965d3f3 fail on b-2978804b33f7 (integer-input retranslation)

body:
I would like to agree on the scope of a sampled BUFFER texture ordering fix before opening a large PR, as requested in CONTRIBUTING.md. A locally tested prototype is ready; the production change plus synthetic GPU tests exceeds about 1,000 lines. I am preparing a public source-only version, with #2230 as an explicit dependency rather than duplicating its private-buffer guard.

The two misaligned sampled-buffer snapshot helpers currently read CPU contents while earlier GPU stores or inline updates can still be queued. A CPU memcpy therefore cannot establish the value that a later shader should see. Retaining a table for a whole submission can also reuse an earlier version after a producer changes the source. This is an independently reproduced API-level defect, not a confirmed explanation of any game's visual artifact.

Proposed scope:

- Keep valid aligned buffer-texture carriers separate from their logical source range, including active versus retired mappings.
- Plan per-consumer sampled BUFFER bindings and encode immutable snapshots as ordered GPU copies before the consuming encoder. Preserve the ordinary aligned path without these copies.
- Version cached snapshots by source/range/format and relevant write/mapping generations, retain their allocations through final submission completion, and keep already-issued descriptor tables immutable when background seen IDs arrive.
- Exercise ordinary compute/draw, transform-feedback, geometry and task/mesh consumers. Give unsupported misaligned writable-image bindings a diagnostic and a shape-correct isolated fallback rather than presenting a sampled snapshot as writable storage.

Evidence from the local prototype on Apple M4 Max, macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2, with Metal API validation and both encoder settings:

- 284 ordering checks and 18 geometry checks pass.
- A 71-check public-NVN fixture covers descriptor registration, GPU producers, virtual remapping and an actual in-pass deferred uniform update. Replacing only the ordered GPU copy with the old CPU copy fails seven output checks; setup, completion, remapping and aligned controls still pass.
- A separate control that permits a background pool scan to replace an issued BUFFER table fails two checks; the immutable-table path passes.
- A shape-specific writable fallback control fails two checks; the corrected fallback passes. This is byte/readback proof, not a claim that a Metal abort was reproduced.
- The complete local integration's graphics suite and static checks pass. Its 42,848-shader OOT library is unchanged. Exact public-base synthetic validation is a separate gate and is still being prepared.

Explicitly outside scope: overlapping sampled reads/writes within one operation, GPU-produced descriptor handles resolved on the CPU, and CPU-post counter/report ordering. Native iOS, other games, a whole-game speedup and attribution to OOT floor/glow reports are unvalidated. No shader clamp, draw skip or rendering-resolution change is proposed. The reproductions use generated MSL and literal GPU readback only; no game assets, saves, captures or private logs will be included.

Would you prefer one implementation-and-proof PR stacked on #2230, or a different review boundary? Splitting the tests away from the lifetime/order implementation would make the initial fix harder to verify, but the public NVN fixture and helper-level fixtures can be reviewed as separate commits.
title: Scope proposal: GPU-ordered immutable sampled BUFFER snapshots

body:
Breath of the Wild 1.9.0 on a Mac (Mac app built from main `ced36121` plus local fixes below): with a **Pro Controller 2** over Bluetooth (`DM_SW2=1`), buttons, sticks and rumble work, but motion aiming does nothing at all (in-game *Motion Controls* on, bow aimed with ZR while turning the controller). No other gyro controller was available to compare, so it is not known whether this is specific to the Pro Controller 2 or affects every motion source now (the last confirmation in the game's note is a DualSense, 2026-10-28, #351).

## What was checked

**The controller sends good motion.** `DM_SW2_VERBOSE=1`: raw gyro about 0 at rest and thousands of counts on a turn (e.g. `gyro -4550,94,26`); accelerometer about `-164,-584,4193` lying flat.

**The axes were wrong and are fixed locally.** Held in both hands with its top tipped toward the screen the raw accelerometer read `-73,3227,2597` (+0.79 G on y): the Pro Controller 2's raw frame is the Joy-Con 2 pair's (x right, y forward, z up), not the Pro Controller 1 map `s2_map_pro` borrowed (`{2,-1,-3,-5,4,6}`), which turned that tilt into a ~50 degree roll. Locally `s2_map_pro = {-1,-2,-3,4,5,6}`; `DM_MOTION_LOG` then reads `acc +0.09 -0.61 -0.82 G` held, `-0.14 +0.04 -1.02` flat. Aiming still did not respond after this.

**The game reads live motion from the handle it set up.** `DM_HLECOUNT` over a run: `GetSixAxisSensorHandles` 1 call, `StartSixAxisSensor` 1, `SetGyroscopeZeroDriftMode` 1, `GetSixAxisSensorStates` once per frame (1,450 in 1,450 frames, 16 entries each); no device-type or at-rest query. A local diagnostic in `six_states` (logged under `DM_MOTION_LOG`) shows:

```
[hid] six-axis handles for npad 0, styles 0x1: 1, the first 0
[hid] six-axis read: handle 0 (style bit 0, npad 0, device 0; the npad's styles now 0x1), live, 16 entries: acc -0.48 -0.01 -0.99 G, gyro -0.534 +0.333 +0.196 rev/s, angle -0.066 -0.266 +0.017 rev
```

21 of 22 once-a-second reads after the controller connected were `live`, with values following the movement, while the controller's button (`0x80`) was held.

**Where the game stores it.** `main+0xeb189c` (1.9.0) polls each npad's style (`GetNpadStyleSet`), fetches six-axis handles when the style changes (`main+0xeb1990`), and reads 16 states per handle into its per-npad block (base `+0x58`, stride `0xe98`, states at `+0x290` / `+0x890`; `main+0xeb1a84`). The consumer of those states (what turns them into aiming) was not found.

## Open questions

- Does motion aiming still work in this game with a DualSense (GameController path, `dm_motion_set`)? If not, the regression is in the shared six-axis path since #351, not in the Switch 2 driver.
- What does the game's aiming code read from the stored states (sampling numbers, `delta_ns`, `angle`, `direction`, attributes)? The host repeats the newest sample in all 16 entries with consecutive sampling numbers.

## Local changes (not yet in a PR)

- `pad_switch2_apple.m` / `front_mac.m`: a Switch 2 controller is no longer disconnected as "all players are taken" when *Press a button to join* (`DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN=1`) leaves it without a player until its first press.
- `switch2_proto.h`: the Pro Controller 2's axis map above, with a `t_switch2` check from the recorded samples.
- `hle_hid.c`: `DM_MOTION_LOG` also logs the six-axis handles the game asks for and what each read returns.
title: Breath of the Wild: Pro Controller 2 motion aiming does nothing, though the game reads live six-axis states

body:
Aokana did not switch to touch input when I toggled it on the iPad. At first I thought the game just checked at startup, but that made little sense, so I looked into it.

**Seen on:** the iPad, Aokana - Four Rhythms Across the Blue (`0100990011866000`, Unity 2018.4.22f1 IL2CPP; profile in #1372). Steps:
1. Set Docked in the launcher.
2. Play, then in the in-game menu switch to Handheld and pick Tap.
3. Taps do nothing.

Launched in Handheld, the same game takes taps.

**Reproduces on the Mac** without a device, from a fresh save, headless, with `DM_OPMODE=1 DM_OE_SCRIPT=opmode=0@12 DM_KEYS=20:T0.5x0.5*45/1.5 DM_TOUCH_LOG=1`. The game reads the taps, and `DM_TOUCH_LOG` lists 270 reads with touch points, yet the opening movie plays on. With `DM_OPMODE=0`, the first tap stops it. Starting handheld, docking at 12 s and returning to handheld at 24 s fails the same way.

**Cause:** `touch_read` in `hle_hid.c` numbers docked states from the npad sampling counter, which starts at 65536. Handheld states take `hle_touch.c`'s own count, which starts at 1. Unity's touch reader takes a state only if its sampling number is above the last one it took, docked empty states included; in Aokana's `main` the compare is at `main+0xd2bde0`. After the switch, every handheld state is below the docked numbers and is dropped.

A fix, with a test that fails on main, follows as a PR.
title: Touch does nothing after switching from docked to handheld: docked and handheld touch states are numbered from different counters

body:
## What happened

On an iPhone (Duo, A20 Pro, 8 GB, iOS 27.3), `v23` ran for about 10 minutes of play (frame 17,484) and then aborted right after an in-game save finished:

```
[dm] [nvn] the game sets present interval 3 → 2 (from main+0x4dc1ec)
[dm] save commit #6: .../Documents/save.work swapped atomically into .../Documents/save
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException', reason: '-[NvPkg buffer]: unrecognized selector sent to instance 0x765ade6120'
*** First throw call stack:
()
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type NSException
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8 pc=__pthread_kill+0x8 lr=pthread_kill+0xe4
```

The save itself committed (`save commit #6` before the abort), so no data was lost. The crash is an Objective-C exception — an `NvPkg` received `buffer`, i.e. a serial lookup handed a packaged texture to a caller expecting a buffer/other object.

## Build and machine

- Branch `v23`, commit `262eae40e512`, shader chain `804433846e4b`, profile `0400486024DEC000` (v131072)
- iPhone Duo (`iPhone19,4`), A20 Pro, 8 GB, iOS 27.3
- 30 fps cap; frames just before the abort: `p50 32.7 / p95 42.6 / max 56.5 ms`
- Memory at the time: `resident 5.5 GB, GPU allocated 11.2 GB` (no OOM, no jetsam, no `[RED]` pipeline failure in that window)

## Environment (Documents/env.txt)

```
DM_FPS=30
DM_FPS_HOLD=off
DM_FPS_PAYBACK=on
DM_PRESENT_LINK=1
DM_RENDER_SCALE=0.5
DM_UPSCALER=off
DM_PSO_MTL4=1
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
DM_PSO_PREPARE=1
DM_NVN_TBDR=0
DM_GUEST_FILE=1
DM_GUEST_FILE_MIN_FREE=0
DM_NVN_WINDOW_ALIAS=1
DM_THERMAL_CAP=1
DM_NVN_ALIAS_SWEEP=600
DM_NVN_TEX_RECYCLE=1
DM_NVN_TEX_RECYCLE_MB=256
DM_POOL_ANON_MAX_MB=1024
DM_NVN_RES_EVICT_MB=6500
DM_NVN_GEO_MESH=0
DM_OPMODE=0
```

## What was going on just before

Streaming and compiling in the same second, then the save:

```
[longframe] frame 17478 ... new pipelines 20 ... 160.0 ms in all
[longframe] frame 17482 ... new pipelines 2 + shader libraries 2, 37.0 ms
[nvn-mtl] upload staging blocks: 649 created in total, swapped within a batch 157 times (2184 MB of old blocks swapped out)
[nvn-mtl] texture upgraded to allow format views ser=733774 base format 70 → view format 53 (upgrades=27)
[nvn-mtl] a pool's first GPU write: 5 uncompressed textures taken from its storage are GPU textures from now on
[nvn-mtl] large texture ser=732050 12288x12288x1 format 0x32 target 1 levels 1: 296 MB
```

## Question

Is this the `tex_release 1` path from V23 (release back to level 1) meeting the recycling bin my config enables (`DM_NVN_TEX_RECYCLE=1` + `DM_NVN_ALIAS_SWEEP=600`), or something else in the `NvPkg` lifetime? Is there a switch I should set to avoid it (`DM_TEX_RELEASE`, `DM_NVN_TEX_RECYCLE=0`), or a place to look in `nvn_mtl.m`? Happy to run a build with extra logging or a probe if it helps.

I can attach the full log (`log.prev.txt`, 659 KB) if wanted.
title: Ocarina on iPhone (A20 Pro): '-[NvPkg buffer]: unrecognized selector' aborts the app right after an in-game save (fork v23, commit 262eae40)

body:
### What happened

Since `e45694b7` ("Translator rebuilt (native, static OpenSSL and Brotli)"), the prebuilt translator `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate` segfaults on start (exit 139) on macOS 26.6.2, so no shader build is possible with chain `bc8830d4ba5a`. Every time, still on `origin/main` (`ced36121`, the binary has not changed since `e45694b7`).

```
$ dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate --source-sha
zsh: segmentation fault   (exit 139)
```

lldb:

```
* thread #1, queue = 'com.apple.main-thread', stop reason = signal SIGSEGV
  * frame #0: 0x0000000000000000
    frame #1: 0x0000000100005adc dmsh_xlate`___lldb_unnamed_symbol_100005aa8 + 52
    frame #2: 0x0000000100007848 dmsh_xlate`___lldb_unnamed_symbol_1000077ac + 156
```

### Cause (looks like)

The arm64 slice weak-imports `pipe2` from libSystem and calls it without a null check:

```
$ nm -m -arch arm64 dmsh_xlate | grep weak
  (undefined) weak external _pipe2 (from libSystem)

0x100005ad8  bl  _pipe2        ; symbol stub   <- lr = 0x100005adc
```

`pipe2` does not exist in libSystem on macOS 26.6.2 (`dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "pipe2")` returns NULL), so the stub jumps to 0x0. The binary is built with `sdk 27.2`, `minos 12.0`; I guess a configure-time `HAVE_PIPE2` (the .NET System.Native shim, or one of the newly static libs) picked it up from the macOS 27 SDK. The previous binary (`918e9f34`) has no `pipe2` reference and works.

The README says macOS 26.6 or later is supported, so this breaks every macOS 26 user. Building the translator against a macOS 26 SDK / deployment target (or forcing `HAVE_PIPE2` off) should fix it.

### What you expected

`--source-sha` prints the hash, as `918e9f34`'s binary does (`6b56acf7e489bc22`, `tool_lock.py --check-tools` passes).

### Details

- **Binaries (SHA-256):**
  - broken (`e45694b7`..`ced36121`): `0406b50b2856b1b43c244bb21e7520088a49add2133b1fb89502f23f5e123ada`
  - working (`918e9f34`): `6ea0899e934aa66b485e01bf2df4fbc439a23cc6c65ae1599f925466a4069b39`
- **Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072 (the crash is in the tool, before any game data is read)
- **nxnative commit:** `ced36121` (works on `918e9f34`)
- **Shader chain:** `bc8830d4ba5a` (fails), `eaa843a79149` (works)
- **How it was built:** by hand (`dmsh_build.py`)
- **Device and OS:** Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Xcode 27.2 (27B52)
- **Environment overrides:** none for the tool
title: dmsh_xlate segfaults (jump to 0x0) on macOS 26.6.2 since e45694b7: weak-imported pipe2 is missing

body:
## In short

- **What you see:** I left Ocarina of Time running and fell asleep for about two hours. Afterwards, the Pro Controller did nothing in the game. Reconnecting it did not help. Only quitting the game did.
- **Why:** after the controller dropped and reconnected over Bluetooth, the host read it **twice**, through the raw-HID "twin" path, as player 1 (handheld npad) **and** player 2 (npad No1). OoT wants exactly one player. It opened the controller applet, the host answered, and the game opened it again. This repeated **1,671 times** until I quit.
- **How bad:** the game is stuck without input. You lose anything since the last save. It happened in **two runs in a row** (three reconnects), each time after the controller had been off for a longer while. A short drop of about 20 s reconnected fine. Only **one** Pro Controller is paired with this Mac.

## Seen in two runs

| Run | Controller dropped | Off for (roughly) | On reconnect | Applet loops |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (2026-11-10, afternoon) | after ~1.5 h idle while I was asleep | far longer than 20 min | GameController connects, drops at once → two HID twins, players 1 + 2 | 1,671 (two reconnects, both the same) |
| 2 (2026-11-10, evening), early drop | during play | ~20 s | GameController connects and stays: player 1, all fine | 0 |
| 2, later drop | while I sat in the pause menu ~30 min | ~20–25 min | GameController connects, drops at once → two HID twins, players 1 + 2 | 531 |

So it is not every reconnect. Each time it went wrong, GameController's own connection dropped right after `connected` (in the same moment). Only then did the twin path find **2** IOKit devices for the model.

## What happens

| Step | Log line (shortened) |
|---|---|
| Start of the run: controller read through GameController, all fine | `controller 'Pro Controller' connected: player 1 (npad handheld), with motion (gyro)` |
| Controller idle; it powers off / drops | `controller 'Pro Controller' disconnected: player 1 (npad handheld) is free` |
| Reconnect over Bluetooth: GameController sees it for a moment… | `controller 'Pro Controller' connected: player 1 …` then `disconnected: player 1 … is free` |
| …then the twin path takes **two** IOKit devices for the one controller | `'Pro Controller' (057e:2009) at USB location 0x0: GameController lists 1 of 2 pads of this model: read here` |
| | `controller 'Pro Controller' (HID) connected: player 1 (npad handheld)` |
| | `'Pro Controller' (057e:2009) at USB location 0x69xxxxxx: GameController lists 1 of 2 pads of this model: read here` |
| | `controller 'Pro Controller' (HID) connected: player 2 (npad 1)` |
| The game asks for its one player, over and over | `oe library applet: controller support` → `hid controller applet: 1 to 1 players wanted, 2 connected` → `focus state → 1 (library applet closed)` (×1,671) |

A second reconnect about 17 minutes later went the same way. First the two twins were released (`GameController lists every pad of this model again: read through it`). Then GameController connected and dropped once more. Then the same two twins came back as players 1 and 2.

## Cause / log evidence

- **Two IOKit devices, one controller.** `system_profiler SPBluetoothDataType` lists exactly one Pro Controller (057e:2009). The two twin entries differ like this:
  - **location `0x69xxxxxx`:** its low three bytes are that controller's Bluetooth address (redacted here). Calibration is read normally (`factory calibration: rest 2048 2048 …`).
  - **location `0x0`:** `cannot ask its stick calibration (IOReturn 0x10000003): its sticks measure themselves`.

  So the `0x0` entry looks like a second (or leftover) HID service of the same Bluetooth controller, not a second pad. I did not check this in `ioreg` while it was happening.
- **The twin rule counts it as a second pad.** `hidpad_twins_take` (`dm/host/pad_hid_mac.h`, from #1595 / 1ed28ed0 for #1218) takes "pads of a model GameController lists fewer of" as separate players. With 1 of 2, both IOKit entries became players. a00f03bb ("one Pro Controller is one pad … by its I/O Registry entry") is in this build. It did not catch this case, probably because these are two different registry entries.
- **The applet does not settle "too many".** In `ctrl_support` (`dm/host/hle_hid.c`), only `arg[0] > count` (too few) opens the prompt. With 2 connected and a maximum of 1, the host clamps `info[0]` to 1 and returns. But both npads stay connected (handheld + No1), so OoT asks again on the next frames. On a Switch, the applet would leave just one controller connected. This looks like the "too many" counterpart of #550.

## What was tried

- The controller reconnected a second time while I tried to use it: same result, two players, and the loop went on.
- Quitting the game from the Mac and restarting: works (the host exited with 0).

## Not tried

- A clean restart with the controller already on, to see if the twin path also triggers without a drop.
- `DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN`, USB instead of Bluetooth, unpairing and re-pairing the controller.
- Whether other games that want exactly one player loop the same way.

## Related

- #1722: the same symptom in OoT (one Bluetooth Pro Controller as two players, 2,286 applet loops), but there both twins had the **same** USB location. It was closed and landed as a00f03bb, which is in this build. Here the two twins have **different** locations (`0x0` and `0x69xxxxxx`), and it only happens after a longer disconnect, so this looks like a case a00f03bb does not cover.
- #1218: two identical Pro Controllers over USB count as one (the twin path was added for it)
- #1595 / 1ed28ed0: the twin path; a00f03bb: one Pro Controller is one pad
- #1657: a keyboard receiver becomes player 1 as a raw HID pad since #859
- #550: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe reopened the applet every few frames (the "too few" side)
- #1640: controller applet stand-in waits for presses

## Build

- MacBook Air 15" M4 (Mac16,13), 10-core GPU, 24 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123)
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 0400486024DEC000 v131072, Mac app
- nxnative `main` 629dd752 (shader chain cb2e91c138e3)
- One Nintendo Pro Controller over Bluetooth (057e:2009, firmware shown as 0.0.1)
- Launcher: DM_FPS_TARGET=60, DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=1, DM_OPMODE=0, DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx, DM_UPSCALER=metalfx, DM_FULLSCREEN=1, DM_PSO_MTL4=1, DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1, DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0, DM_FPS_HOLD=off, DM_LANG=de

— Claude (AI agent), for Gesalbter
title: Mac: one Bluetooth Pro Controller comes back as two HID players after it reconnects, and Ocarina of Time reopens the controller applet in a loop (1,671 times), no input

body: ## Symptom Since main's uniform read bound (`26062f9e`, from #1860), Ocarina of Time draws long white streaks from the horses at Lon Lon Ranch and from Link's slingshot. Parts of the slingshot and of the ReDeads' faces also flicker, dropping out for a frame and coming back. With the bound off, all of it is gone. **on main** **with #2219** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae1b8fbb-8c0a-40c6-a9b3-b2f11d6ffb23 ## How it can look - Long white or coloured lines, spikes or stretched polygons from a model to one point of the screen, mostly on animated models: the horses and Epona at Lon Lon Ranch, and Link's slingshot when aimed. - Parts of a model missing for a frame and coming back, like the slingshot's tips or the ReDeads' faces, which looks like flicker. - Possibly more of the white clouds over the ground mist from #1839. There's no `[RED]` line. The quickest check is a build from before `26062f9e`, or with #2219. In the host, this is main's uniform read bound for constant buffers: the zero padding of short bindings (`ub_padded`) and the size table at bank 25 (`DMSH_CBSIZE_BANK`) for reads at computed offsets. The Switch 2's NVN (NVN2) doesn't seem to stop a read at the size passed to `nvnCommandBufferBindUniformBuffer`. ## Setup - MacBook Pro M5 Max, macOS 27.0, `0400486024DEC000` v131072. - My own branch: main from this morning plus some changes of my own. The bound code is main's, unchanged. ## What we tested We ran three variants of the bound in the same places: | Bound | Stretching | Flicker | |---|---|---| | main's, the size the game binds | yes | yes | | the size taken as 4-byte words, at most 64 KB | gone | still on the slingshot and the ReDeads' faces | | none, as before `26062f9e` | gone | gone | Two things pointed at the words idea first. The mesh shaders read up to 16,384 bytes of slots bound with 4,096, and pixel shaders read up to 20,480 of 5,120, which is exactly 4× in both cases. But with the words bound, 5,179 slots across 465 shaders could still read past it at computed offsets, and the flicker stayed. The bound sizes themselves are 16, 64, 256 and 1,024 bytes, which look like plain byte sizes. So it looks like the Switch 2 doesn't stop a uniform read at the size the game binds, and the game relies on that. Switch 1 games like Paper Mario do need the bound, so I'd keep it for them. ## Related - #1839, the white clouds over the ground mist: with the bound on, we saw them too, and turning it off cleared them in our build. That issue was reported before the bound existed, though, so its root cause is the game's own divide by zero, which #2030 fixes. - #2066: the bound's cost in Donkey Kong Bananza, also a Switch 2 game. - #1909: another PR that bounds pixel shader uniform reads. I've opened #PR to turn the bound off for Switch 2 games.
title: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2): vertices streak to the origin and models flicker or drop out with the uniform read bound on (26062f9e)

Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072) on an M1 Pro with 16 GB, macOS 26.6.1. On main 25c2546 the game fell into slow motion after about 80 minutes of a 140-minute session. On 629dd75, a 90-minute session on the same Mac had none.

**Builds** (Mac app from the NUP, all 42,848 shaders built, same shader chain cb2e91c138e3 on both):
- A: main 629dd75 plus #1377, #1379 and a macOS 26 SDK guard
- B: the same on main 25c2546, which adds f02d047, ab41d6a and 25c2546

Settings were the same on both: Handheld, 60 fps target, dynamic resolution off, Metal 4 pipelines off.

**What the player saw on B:** the Forest Temple was fine. Then Link went back to the Temple of Time and became a child again. From there on, Hyrule Field, Kakariko, Kokiri Forest and Death Mountain Trail ran in slow motion. Pausing for a moment brought normal speed back for a while. There was no GPU hang (0 `ErrorHang`) in either session.

**What B's log shows** (`memory up to frame` lines):

| Frame | Resident | GPU allocated | Texture re-uploads | Finalized-texture puts (total) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 121,500 | 9.9 GB | 6.4 GB | 0 | 1,774 |
| 153,000 | 12.2 GB | 8.0 GB | 7 | 2,287 |
| 166,800 | 15.1 GB | 10.0 GB | 5,524 | 7,953,351 |
| 205,500 | 15.2 GB | 10.0 GB | 30,236 | 108,632,926 |
| 234,900 | 14.7 GB | 9.5 GB | 50,848 | 191,419,830 |

- The `finalized textures still referenced` table (512 entries) took under 1 put a frame until frame ~155,700, about 4,900 s in. After that it came in bursts of 6,000 to 24,000 puts a frame, between quieter stretches.
- Texture re-uploads went from 0 to 50,848 over the same stretch.
- Resident memory rose to about 15 GB on this 16 GB Mac.
- Long frames went from a `submit+present` median of about 10–13 ms to 20–98 ms. GPU time stayed at 21–38 ms.
- The 600-frame window median dropped from about 31 fps to 21–25 fps, with minimums of 6–14 fps.

**A over 90 min** for comparison: puts 24,456 in total, re-uploads 16,587, resident 12–14 GB, GPU allocated 7–8 GB, fps p50 30.4.

I haven't tested the three commits one at a time. ab41d6a changes how GPU writes reach textures uploaded from storage, so it looks like the closest fit, but that's a guess. I can build A plus one commit at a time if that helps, but reproducing it takes an hour or more of play.
title: Ocarina of Time on an M1 Pro: slow motion after ~80 min on main 25c2546, finalized-texture table puts jump from <1 to thousands a frame

### What happened

The menus, character selection and pre-race view look sharp. The 3D scene abruptly looks softer or more pixelated when the countdown first shows **3**. With both upscaling settings set to MetalFX, the scene sometimes looks sharper again roughly 10–15 seconds into the race, and the clarity can change again. The apparent recovery is a visual observation and has not been measured. Keeping the outer **Upscaling** set to **MetalFX** and changing **Game’s upscaler** to **Game’s own** leaves the scene visibly soft after the start.

Steps to observe:

1. Start the standalone Mac app in **Docked** mode and **Fullscreen**, with both upscaling settings set to **MetalFX**.
2. Start a race and watch the track and scenery just before and after the countdown first shows **3**. Keep watching during the first 15 seconds.
3. Restart with **Game’s upscaler** set to **Game’s own**, leaving the outer **Upscaling** on **MetalFX**, and compare the same part of the race.

### What you expected

The transition into the countdown should not cause a sudden, visible loss of detail in the race scene.

Mario Kart World, `0400C3F00006E000`, display version **1.8.0**, packaged as a complete application.

body:
Since 641636e2 ("Building no longer needs .NET"), the NSP script stops at once on macOS 26:

```
[RED] the shader translator does not run (exit code -11): …/dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate is the committed native executable; check out the repository again if it is missing or damaged
```

Mac: Apple M3 (10-core GPU), 16 GB, macOS 26.7.2 (25G332), Xcode 27.2 through `DEVELOPER_DIR` (Metal 32023.922). Clean checkout of 73354368; the file is the committed blob (9f265792).

- `dmsh_xlate --source-sha` exits 139 (SIGSEGV). Crash report: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0`, pc 0 (instruction abort), called from `dmsh_xlate +0x5adc` ← `+0x7848` ← `+0x862c` ← `+0x122ec4`.
- `arch -x86_64 dmsh_xlate --source-sha` prints `657232fd201f16a1`, the lock's `xlate_source`.
- The arm64 slice (`LC_BUILD_VERSION` minos 12.0, sdk 27.2) has one weak import, `_pipe2` from libSystem; the x86_64 slice has none. On macOS 26.7.2 libSystem has no `pipe2` (nor `dup3` or `accept4`), so the weak import binds to 0 and the first call jumps there. The runtime's native layer looks configured against the 27.2 SDK, where `pipe2` exists, and calls it without a null check.

Possible fixes: build the arm64 slice against an SDK without `pipe2` (or with its use turned off). Or, if macOS 26 is not meant to be supported, set minos to 27 so the failure is explicit.

Workaround here: building from 30c9b163 (the commit before 641636e2, with the .NET DLLs) works.

Not verified: which function sits at `+0x5adc` (the binary has no symbols).
title: The committed native dmsh_xlate crashes at startup on macOS 26 (arm64): its arm64 slice calls pipe2, weak-imported from the 27.2 SDK and absent on macOS 26

### What happened

command line: `python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py /path/to/game.nup --platform mac-app`:

body:
### What happened

641636e2 (#1853) committed the shader translator and nx_extract as NativeAOT executables (`dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate`, 7.7 MB, universal) and deleted the .NET dlls. `dmsh_chain.lock` now fingerprints that binary plus the translator sources, so the chain version follows the binary.

A fork that changes the translator sources cannot use that binary. Ours does (int8 tensor ops in Program.cs: `imma_tensor`; a flag that pads short uniform bindings; a check on texture-handle queries). Merging origin/main into it:

- the old dlls and `deps.json` are modify/delete conflicts (we edited them, upstream deleted them);
- `dmsh_chain.lock` and `dmsh_chain.h` conflict;
- the committed binary has none of our changes, so taking it silently drops them, and the shaders still build;
- our own build with `native_tools.sh` is not byte-reproducible (the same sources give a different binary each time), so it can never equal upstream's binary or lock, and every merge of main needs a rebuild and a new lock.

We did the merge by hand: kept our sources, built our own binary, updated the lock and header, and compared translator output on a sample of 394 shaders (3,979 library files, 0 differences against the previous build).

### What would make this easier

Any of these would do; we have no preference:

1. A check that says whether the binary matches the sources it fingerprints, and a documented way for a fork to replace it (`tool_lock.py --update-lock` already does the lock half).
2. Keeping the fingerprint on the sources only, so a locally built binary of the same sources gives the same chain.
3. Shipping the binary as a release artifact, not a committed file, so a source change in a fork or a PR does not touch a binary.

### Checked

Main at 976fbd57 merged into a fork with translator changes; the build and tests pass with our own binary. Nothing here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: A forked translator cannot take the committed native binary: every translator source change conflicts and moves the chain

The host doesn't read a controller's battery, so a pad can run flat in the middle of play with no warning. GameController already reports it (`GCController.battery`: level and charging state) for DualShock 4, DualSense, Xbox and Pro Controllers.

1. A short notice over the game when a controller drops to 20 % and to 10 %, styled like the Home hold prompt, gone after a few seconds.

3. A log line with the level at connect and at each of those thresholds, for bug reports.

I did the same for MacNativeGames (ly05010419/MacNativeGames#1225, battery in its HUD box). Would you take a PR along these lines, or do you prefer only some of it?

body:
### What is missing

Nothing blocks play any more, but it took a while to find, so it may help others with an Xbox pad.

On a Mac with an Xbox Wireless Controller, nxnative maps the face buttons by position, as the Switch has them (`dm_pad_face` in `dm/host/pad_apple.h`): the pad's bottom A presses Switch B, the right B presses Switch A, and X and Y are swapped the same way. For someone used to an Xbox pad, the game's A (confirm in the menus) then sits on the button labelled B, and the prompts show A while the pad's A does something else. I looked for a setting in the launcher and in `docs/env_switches.tsv` and found none (`DM_HID_MAP` covers raw HID pads only).

macOS can remap the controller itself, and nxnative follows it. In the macOS settings for the controller, in its button list, set A to B, B to A, X to Y and Y to X, and leave everything else on Standard. I tried this with an Xbox Wireless Controller on macOS 27.0.1, nxnative `04811a6`, Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`): in the game the pad's bottom A is now the game's A, with no change in nxnative. Not checked: the Home button quit prompt ("A quits, B closes") reads GameController's own button names, so with this remap its A would sit on the right button.

### What you propose

Two small things, if you want them:

1. A short tip in `docs/playing.md`, next to the controller notes: a pad's buttons can be swapped in the macOS settings and nxnative follows that.
2. Optionally a per-game switch (for example `DM_PAD_LAYOUT=position|name`, default unchanged), because the macOS remap applies to the controller in every app. It would skip the A/B and X/Y swap in `dm_pad_face` for pads that are not labelled Nintendo. I have not tried a code change.

### Platforms

Mac

Drafted with Claude Code; reviewed by me.
title: Xbox pad: swapping A/B and X/Y works via the macOS controller settings; a docs tip and an optional switch

body:
### Idea

Let phones and other local programs be controllers on the Mac host, one player per sender. `DM_NETPAD=<port>` listens on `127.0.0.1` for small UDP messages and gives each pad a player like a controller. Off by default. macOS cannot make a virtual gamepad without an Apple-restricted entitlement, so this is the way to do it without lowering system security.

### Plan

- `dm/host/netpad.h` (pure parser and state, tested like `input_map.h`) and `netpad_mac.m` (socket).
- Pads take players from `pad_slots.h`, so they work with `DM_KBD_PLAYER=own`, `DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN` and `DM_PAD_MERGE`.
- A Mac-only "Phone controllers" row in `settings.tsv`. Docs in `mac-controllers.md`.

Is a loopback network-pad input welcome? I will adjust to your answer (transport, default, setting).

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Protocol, one datagram per message:

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `P <pad 1-8> <buttons> <lx> <ly> <rx> <ry>` | state. Buttons are the 16 `DM_BTN_*` bits, sticks -32767..32767, +y up |
| `L <pad>` | the pad left |

- Bad messages are ignored whole. A pad silent for 2 s leaves.
- Loopback only. Any local process can send input, so it is opt-in.
- Not covered: rumble, motion, iOS (the code is in `_mac` files).
- Local input only, not networked play (`MULTIPLAYER.md`).
- Tested: new `t_netpad` and `t_netpad_mac`, extended `t_controllers_mac`, `dmhost` builds for two profiles. Not tested: a phone driving a real game.
- The sender is a separate project (a phone web page plus a bridge).
</details>
title: Phones as controllers: network pads on 127.0.0.1 (DM_NETPAD)
Ocarina of Time: rumble too short and soft for controllers with rotating motors (cause + local patch)

body:
### Game, title ID and version

The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, `01009CD0167E2000`, update v131072 (display version 1.7.9b)

### Engine and graphics API

The game's own engine on NVN, with shaders compiled at run time by GLSLC (GLSLC API 17.22, GPU code version 1.16; `main` holds 44 GLSL sources and calls `glslcCompile` in `subsdk0`). SDK 13.3.5. Modules `main`, `subsdk0` (GLSLC), `subsdk1` (NintendoSDK_movie) and `sdk`.

### Survey and what happened

Built with `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` from the game's own dump (a base XCZ and an NSZ update), with its provisional profile, which nobody checked by hand. With no Mac to boot it for the GLSLC capture, the shaders were captured on the iPhone: a capture build was played to the title screen, and its `glslc_capture` folder (43 shaders) was fed back into a second build. It boots and plays well. From a 75-second session:

- **Frame rate:** 60 fps. Frame time p50 16.7 ms; on-screen p99 16.67 ms in most 300-frame windows, with 0 to 4 dropped frames each.
- **GPU:** 5 to 7 ms a frame; the present pass about 1.3 ms.
- **Memory:** footprint 600 to 870 MiB, with about 5.3 GB left before the limit. The guessed pool (`app_pool 0xCD500000`) was enough, and the memory guard stayed normal.
- **Shaders:** none failed to load; the 43 captured shaders covered everything drawn.
- **Audio:** the audio renderer runs on the CPU (manual mode). 0 underruns across 14,000 device callbacks, and one catch-up render.
- **Saves:** 15 commits. One `fs unlink … save.work failed errno=1`; the commits after it went through.
- **Thermal:** state 0 throughout.
- **Hitches** (first launch, with no prewarm list yet): the first frame took 517 ms, and new pipelines gave single frames of 57 to 200 ms.
- **Red lines:** none.

The provisional `game.tsv` (comments and the survey's local paths removed):

```
title_id	01009CD0167E2000
```
