## Game, title ID and version

**OCTOPATH TRAVELER 0, Korean/Chinese regional release**, base title ID `01001300232F4000`, update **1.0.4 (`v262144`)**. Main build ID: `c7c4e3fe091eb9a0adc4df5cbe0c9da9`.

This is a **positive compatibility / bring-up report**, not a crash report or a claim that current upstream main has been tested. Related: #933, which covers the same regional title's **1.0.5**, a different main build (`e3e401c28d9fd3b1f9e033bb7bb31d42`). Please keep the versions distinct.

## Device and observed behavior

- Retained device evidence: **11-inch M1 iPad Pro (`iPad13,4`), iPadOS 27.0.x**. The captured device header says 27.0.1; the in-game HUD says 27.0.
- Simplified Chinese rendering works. The owner reports on **2026-11-10** that they are now playing normally on iPad without problems.
- This goes beyond the initial-settings screen: retained **2026-11-02** evidence includes the actual in-game save screen (level 14, save play-time counter `11:45:46`) and a successful save-complete dialog. This counter is accumulated save play time, **not** a measured uninterrupted test session.
- That iPad save-screen capture shows about **60 FPS** (HUD 59.98). This is one captured scene, **not** a sustained gameplay benchmark or a promise of 60 FPS everywhere.

## Save/load and cloud handoff acceptance

The retained acceptance record documents actual in-game save/load on both Mac and iPad and native iCloud save handoff in both directions:

1. A Mac save at 14:08 was transferred to iPad and loaded there.
2. An iPad save at 14:25 was transferred back and loaded into the Mac game world.
3. The record reports all seven committed save files byte-identical in each handoff, with no manual copying into either runtime during those checks.

For this report, the retained artifacts were checked again, read-only: **all seven returned iPad-to-Mac files match the record's SHA-256 values**, and `SaveData1` in each directional backup matches its recorded SHA-256. The iPad save-screen capture and the Mac world-after-load capture were also inspected. No new game launch, device install, signing or modification of live saves was performed for this report.

## Build provenance and limits

- This is a locally built game using NX2Apple/nxnative, not a verification of the latest NX2Apple release. The historical acceptance record labels its engine version **1.0.0**. The exact source commit of that iPad binary is not retained in the inspected record, so no current-upstream commit is claimed.
- A separate retained Mac runtime log dated 2026-11-09 reports `commit not recorded`, shader chain `89f44f9b6bb0`, profile `01001300232F4000`, a host Unreal allocator, and two add-on contents mounted. These are **Mac log observations**, not an identification of the iPad binary. That Mac run also had cheats enabled and is not presented as a clean vanilla compatibility benchmark.
- Earlier local bring-up on an older fork needed a main-build-bound FMallocBinned3 constructor cut and an allocator row for this 1.0.4 build. The local cut is at `main+0x12e40` (`90310294` -> `1f2003d5`); allocator object `main+0x68022c8`, 26-slot vtable `main+0x5b06f38`. These are historical findings, **not a request to restore fixed-address patches on current main**: current upstream has engine-wide Unreal allocator discovery, as #933 also explains.
- An older fork's ROMFSARC reader needed directory lookups to accept trailing separators such as `Content/Paks/`. Its existing C regression test was compiled and run for this report on a small synthetic archive: **all checks passed**, including root/existing/missing-directory trailing-slash cases. This does not test the current upstream RomFS image reader or independently verify the iPad runtime.
- Earlier build notes recorded 16 compute shader compilation failures involving 3D image atomics. A newer Mac log still contains some shader reflection/load warnings. The owner's successful iPad gameplay is **not proof that every shader path is correct or that those historical failures are resolved**. Full-game completion, all battles/areas, every DLC effect, and sustained frame-time/memory measurements are not claimed.

## Purpose

Please treat this as an additional **1.0.4 regional-build compatibility data point** alongside #933. The owner is reporting successful real iPad play, rather than only booting to settings. It may help the regional profile's tested-build/device notes; maintainers can decide whether it belongs with #933 instead of a separate issue.

## No game files

Nothing attached contains keys, game files, save files, extracted code or shader binaries. Only identifiers, offsets and a description of the locally inspected evidence are included.

body:
### What happened

Two problems, the first blocks the second. Both are on The Hinokami Chronicles **1** (UE 4.26, SDK 10.2.0 base).

**1. The build stops at the shader split with 0 shaders, and the reason is not in `main`.**

```
✗ [8/11] shader split (2:20)
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps them in a form
      shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader
```

`shader_split.log` has the real cause two lines above, as a per-file note:

```
[RED] /APK/Content/Paks/pakchunk0-Switch.pak: the pak cannot be read (no pak footer); its shaders are left out
[RED] /APK/Content/Paks/pakchunk1-Switch.pak: the pak cannot be read (no pak footer); its shaders are left out
```

Both paks carry a **version 9 footer**, whose magic sits **205 bytes** from the end of the file:

```
pakchunk0-Switch.pak  2,394,672,606 bytes   magic at end-205 (0xcd)   footer version 9
pakchunk1-Switch.pak    858,688,066 bytes   magic at end-205 (0xcd)   footer version 9
```

`footer()` / `magic_back` look at end-`0x2c`, end-`0xc8` and end-`0xcc`, and `LEGACY` holds only 4, 8 and 11, so `footer()` raises `no pak footer`. `inline_shaders` propagates it, `unreal_paks` drops both files, `ue_legacy_jobs` then has no folder to scan, and the split reports 0 shaders — even though the IoStore containers beside these paks hold **88,000+ export bundles** whose directory index reads back 97,036 paths (`/APK/Content/...`), and sampling 40 bundles shows 6 contain `LSLG` records. The shaders are inline in the containers, exactly the case `docs/reference/shaders.md` describes for UE 4.27, which is what `inline_in_containers()` already decides for a pak with an empty index.

**2. With the split fixed, the app builds and runs at 30 fps but never leaves engine start-up — the picture stays black forever.**

The game boots, presents, holds 30 fps (presents at 60 Hz, `present tick 60 Hz`), plays no audio and never loads anything:

- `state dump (DM_CTL dump): tick 0 / stage present frame` — still in the pre-game stage after 32 s
- `packaged textures: first uploads 0` — not one NVN texture was ever uploaded
- `64 draws`, GPU time ≈ 1.5 ms: the blit before present and nothing else
- screenshot after screenshot is byte-identical (same md5 over five captures spanning five minutes, `19040` bytes) — a pure black 1280x720 frame
- `same-core handoffs 0, total 0.0 ms`, `handle table use 57 / 4096`, `threads created so far 48`
- the last file open of the whole run happens **0.56 s** after start (`rom:/APK/Content/Paks/pakchunk0-Switch.pak`); after that the only file activity for the remaining 30 s is 11 failed `aoc0..aoc10:/__chunks_N` opens and two `rom:/Title` stats
- threads are alive and idle: `GameThread` 40 ms/s burning `SleepThread` in a UE loop, `FAsyncLoadingThread` parked on its condvar with **wait #1** (it was started and woke once), `RenderThread 2` `wait #75478`, `PoolThread 0..10` `wait #6513`

So the engine reaches its main loop, then no map is ever requested. `World` stays empty and the game never enters a game tick.

### What you expected

For (1): a pak whose footer cannot be read still sits beside IoStore containers, so `inline_shaders` should fall through to `inline_in_containers()` instead of raising, and the split should read the bundles. Failing that, the split reporting 0 shaders should point at the pak that could not be read — that message is one line per file in another log, while the message on screen blames `main` and the RomFS, which sent me looking in the wrong place for a while.

For (2): the game reaching `nnMain`'s loop with textures being created and a map being loaded, as the same engine and SDK do in other titles.

### Game, title ID and version

The Hinokami Chronicles (the first game, not 2), **0100309016E7A000**, base **1.00** (`[XCI][US][0100309016E7A000][1.00][10.2.0].xci`, SDK 10.2.0) with the **1.53** update (`[UPD][US][0100309016E7A800][1.53][16.0.0].nsp`, SDK 16.0.0) and 11 DLC. Built with update and DLC applied; the base alone does not change (2) — the run with the `aoc` directory removed behaves identically.

### nxnative commit

04811a63

### Shader chain version

b-39eb2f781d07

### How it was built and run

Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` driven by a shell script over the xci + update nsp + 11 DLC nsp.

### Device and OS

Mac mini (Mac16,10), Apple M4 (4P + 6E), 16 GB, macOS 27.2.1 (26B131)

### Settings and environment overrides

Built with a provisional profile (`dm/games/0100309016E7A000/game.tsv`), which the pipeline generated and warned about in red, as expected. The runtime tests start the app's own `dmhost` by hand with `DM_ROOT`, `DM_ROMFS`, `DM_MSL_DIR`, `DM_NVN_SHMAP`, `DM_SAVE`, `DM_TEMP`, `DM_AOC_DIR` and nothing else, plus `DM_CTL` for the dump and the screenshots and `DM_FS=1` for the file log.

Tried and ruled out, none of them changes the picture by a byte:

| | |
|---|---|
| DLC mounting (11 `aoc:/__chunks_N` opens fail) | `aoc` directory renamed away: identical |
| video / movie playback | `DM_MOVIE_TRACE=1`: no call at all |
| reads past 4 GB | largest offset read is 2.76 GB |
| same-core wake handoffs | `same-core handoffs 0, total 0.0 ms` |
| splash screen blocking start-up | `DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY` with `UE4CommandLine.txt` = `... -nosplash`: identical |
| the 62 GB engine region crowding the 64 GB alias region (vs 5 GB in the same-engine Pikmin 4 profile) | profile changed to `mem_reserve 0x140000000` / `mem_alias 0x140000000`, rewrite forced, output byte-identical to before; reverted |
| the 48 `shader ... is not in the shader map` lines | all of them arrive late, after the loop is already idle; not the cause |

`-abslog=save:/ue4.log` in the same overlay is ignored: this is a Shipping build with file logging compiled out, so there is no UE-side log to read.

### Logs

Build, first attempt:

```
[13:14:09] [8/11] shader split · checking the inputs …
[13:16:30] ✗ [8/11] shader split (2:20)
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps them in a form
      shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader
```

Same build after the one-line fallback below:

```
[13:23:51] 2 Unreal pak(s) with the shaders inline in the cooked packages …
[13:23:51] ✓ [5/8] shader split (0:13): 56,466 shaders
[13:24:33] [6/8] Mac shaders · compiling: 1%, 827/56,466 shaders, 0 of them cached · ETA 33:49
→ 56,466 shaders compiled, 0 failed (49 minutes)
```

Runtime:

```
[dm] state dump (DM_CTL dump): tick 0 / stage present frame
[dm] handle table use 57 / 4096, threads created so far 48
[dm] same-core handoffs 0, total 0.0 ms
[dm] thread 0x1002 'GameThread' priority 44 core 1 … (SleepThread in a loop, 40 ms/s of CPU)
[dm] thread 0x1031 'FAsyncLoadingThread' priority 44 core 0 mask 0x7 CPU 0.05s svc 2267 waits:condvar … wait #1
[dm] [nvn] packaged textures: first uploads 0, re-uploads on pool content change 0, writes beside a texture only 0; write-protection faults 0, pages unprotected before host writes 6040; missed 0; CPU-written textures alive 0
[dm] 64 draws
[dm] fs open not found: aoc7:/__chunks_8
…
[dm] fs stat not found: rom:/Title
```

### Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| these paks' footer | magic `0x5A6F12E1` at end-`0xcd`, next word `9` — a version 9 (FrozenIndex) footer, for both files |
| what the reader accepts | `magic_back` tries end-`0x2c`, end-`0xc8`, end-`0xcc`; `LEGACY` = {4, 8, 11} |
| containers beside them | `pakchunk0/1-Switch.utoc`, TOC v2, 88,000+ export bundles, no shader library, no `.ushaderbytecode`, no `GlobalShaderCache-` in the pak directories |
| proving the shaders are there | directory index reads 97,036 plain paths `/APK/Content/...`; of 40 sampled export bundles 6 contain `LSLG`; `inline_in_containers()` returns True for both paks |
| shaders found after the fallback | 56,466, all compiled for Metal |
| the picture | 1280x720, five captures over five minutes, identical md5 and identical 19040 bytes |
| file activity | last successful open at 0.56 s; 11 `aocN:/__chunks_N` misses and 2 `rom:/Title` misses afterwards, nothing else |
| GPU | 64 draws, ≈1.5 ms, no textures ever uploaded |

### Suggested fix

For (1), in `dm/gfx/tools/uepak.py`, `inline_shaders` — an unreadable footer is not a reason to treat the pak as absent, because the containers beside it are still there:

```python
def inline_shaders(path, key=None):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        try:
            enc, ioff, isz, _, ver = footer(f)
        except ValueError:
            # A version 9 (FrozenIndex) footer puts the magic 0xcd bytes from the end,
            # which magic_back does not look at. The pak is not absent: it sits beside
            # the IoStore containers, and inline_in_containers() says where its shaders are.
            return inline_in_containers(path)
        ...
```

The fuller fix is to teach `magic_back`/`footer()` about the version 9 layout (magic at end-`0xcd`, index offset and size 8 bytes after the version, `FrozenIndex` block after that); that would also make `unreal_paks` and `pak.read_at` work on these files, which the fallback does not. I did not need it for the split, so I kept the change minimal — it is marked `LOCAL PATCH 2026-11-10` in the file. With it, the same build goes from 0 to 56,466 shaders and the app builds, signs and starts.

For (2) I have no patch, and I would like your read on it. My best hypothesis is the one the survey already flagged: this title is **SDK 10.4 / UE 4.26**, and the host's service layout assumes a much later SDK. The shape of the failure — every thread parked, `FAsyncLoadingThread` woken exactly once, no asset request issued after 0.56 s, `tick 0` — looks like a completion event that is never signalled rather than a rendering problem, which would explain the black frame with the present path otherwise healthy (60 Hz presents, 30 fps held, no crashes, no `UNIMPL` calls).

If that is a known gap I will stop poking at it. If you want the data first, I can run any instrumentation you name on this machine (`scripts/bug_report.py 0100309016E7A000`, an `nn::fs` read-trace, `DM_PROBE` at a given address, `DM_SVC_TRACE`) and paste the output here — the game is on this Mac and reproduces in a 40-second run, every time.
title: shader split reads a version 9 (FrozenIndex) pak footer as "no pak footer": 0 shaders on Hinokami Chronicles 1 (UE 4.26, SDK 10) - and with that fixed the app builds but stays on a black frame, tick 0

body:
Since 0c7e88b9 (#1489), `alias_take_over` records its change as `ser_note(0)`. Sometimes the texture it evicts is the parent of a live sRGB / linear twin's view (`tex_mtl_`'s `srgb_twins` path). That note names no ID of the twin, so nothing sends the twin's IDs back through `tex_mtl_`'s stale-view check. The ID cache keeps the view, so pool tables (patched or built whole) keep its resource ID. Meanwhile the parent leaves the sharing table, and once the submission completes it also leaves the residency set. Line numbers are at 6c676444.

### Reproduction: the twin case in t_pool_notes, with one more walk

`dm/gfx/tests/t_pool_notes.m` already has this case (IDs 7 / 8 / 9). It passes because ID 8 is taken again for another reason. ID 8's first resolution (`tex_put` inside the walk that builds `b15`, after that walk read `g_ser_gen`) left a note, and that note is still in the log when the takeover walk runs. With one walk in between, the case fails:

```diff
     CHECK(v8 && base8 && entry(b15, 8) != dummy_of(b15), "ID 8's serial resolves to a view of the shared texture");
+    table();   // take the note of ID 8's first resolution before the takeover
```

```
FAIL: ID 8's stale view was dropped and its texture made again, and no ID went down the slow path
FAIL: no table is built: the patch gives ID 8 its new texture and ID 9 its own
t_pool_notes: 82 checks, 2 failed
```

In the same run, after the takeover:
- ID 8's serial still resolves to `v8`, and `entry(b16, 8)` is still `v8`'s resource ID.
- Seventeen submissions later, a new table still names `v8` for ID 8.
- By then `base8` is out of the residency set (`g_res_objects`). `v8` was never in it.
- `same_as_whole` still passes, because a table built whole reads ID 8 through the same ID cache and also names `v8`.

### Why

- **The twin.** In `tex_mtl_` (4463-4477), a texture that differs from a shared texture `b` only by the other format of an sRGB / linear pair gets a view `v` of `b`, then `tex_put(serial, v)`. `g_by_serial_held` counts `v`, not `b`.
- **The eviction.** In `alias_take_over` (2586), `serial_table_holds(b)` is false (2597). So once `b`'s own object is finalized and its key has not been looked up for `ALIAS_IDLE` submissions, a texture with another description over that storage evicts it. The twin's lookups don't refresh the key, because they return from the serial table (4434) before the sharing-table lookup (4461). `b` is retired with `defer_obj_release` (2606), and the change is recorded as `ser_note(0)` (2608).
- **Nothing takes the twin's IDs again.** `ser_sync` (6102) clears `view_ser` only for IDs linked to a noted serial, and no ID is linked to serial 0. `pool_gpu` likewise takes again only the IDs of noted serials (9924-9931). So the twin's IDs keep `v` on the fast path (`tex_fast_rid`, 6706).
- **The stale check isn't reached.** The comment above `alias_take_over` (2580-2581) expects `tex_mtl_` to find the view stale (4427-4433) and drop it with a note. That check runs only when `tex_mtl_` is called for the twin's texture object (a render target, copy or clear that names it), or when the ID cache misses for some other reason. A twin that is only sampled through texture IDs never gets there. Before 0c7e88b9, the takeover's bare `g_ser_gen++` started a new ID-cache epoch, so every ID went through `tex_by_id` → `treg_tex` → `tex_mtl_` and the check ran.
- **What the twin reads.** `defer_drain` takes `b` out of the residency set, because `entry_holds(b)` is false. `v` keeps `b` allocated, but `b` is the old private copy that no longer gets the storage's writes, as `alias_take_over`'s own comment says, and it is not resident. tex_by_id's comment at 6469-6471 describes GPU page faults from a table entry with no residency behind it, in a different case.

I haven't seen a visible symptom of this on main. The report comes from reading the code and from the test above. I found it while chasing pale-blue ground patches in my fork, but those most likely came from a path only my fork has, so I'm not tying them to this.

### A fix

Note the twins' serials when their parent is evicted.

As a concept check, I added a scan to `alias_take_over`'s eviction loop. It looks through `g_by_serial` for textures whose `parentTexture` is the evicted one and calls `ser_note(serial)` for each. With the extra walk in place, ID 8's entry stops naming `v8` from the next walk on. The takeover happens inside the `b16` walk itself, so the note reaches the walk after it, and the test's checks for this case would move one walk later. That scan is the full serial-table walk that `g_by_serial_held` replaced, so it isn't the fix itself.

In my fork, I keep a map from each shared texture to the serials that took a twin view of it (up to 8, under `g_smu`):
- `tex_mtl_`'s twin path adds the serial only after checking, under that same lock, that `b` is still the sharing table's entry for its key. Otherwise a takeover on another thread could evict `b` in between and find nothing to note. If the check fails, it drops the view and looks the key up again.
- `alias_take_over` calls `ser_note(serial)` for each listed serial of a texture it evicts. Only those IDs take the slow path, `tex_mtl_` finds the view stale, and the tables are patched for just those IDs.
- A list full of live serials falls back to a bare `g_ser_gen++`. Evictions that already bump with no note (`mtl_alias_drop_pool`, the format-view upgrade) just drop the list.

A simpler option is a bare `g_ser_gen++` in `alias_take_over` whenever an evicted texture has had a twin view made of it. I used that first. It works, but every such takeover then builds every table whole.

My fork's code here differs from main (it has `pool_skip_retired` and a second takeover pass), so this would have to be ported rather than cherry-picked. I can open it as a PR, together with the test change above, if that helps.
title: sRGB / linear twin keeps its view of an evicted parent since #1489: alias_take_over's ser_note(0) never reaches the twin's texture IDs

body:
### What happened

The Hinokami Chronicles 2 (Unreal Engine 4) crashes deterministically about 2 s after launch, at the same instruction, on every build I tried. The Mac app builds, signs and starts (the launcher reports `the host exited with 139`).

The rewrite site for `ldr w8,[x18,#0x20]` reads the **K18 slot**, but the `mrs x18, tpidr_el0` that set x18 five instructions earlier only wrote the **register**. So the load takes whatever the slot held from earlier code (`0x33200` in this thread) and reads `0x33220`, which lies in the `__PAGEZERO` region macOS will not map — no run-time switch can work around it.

### What you expected

The `mrs x18, tpidr_el0` site (site_sysreg_read) to leave its value where the following x18 sites look for it, i.e. in the K18 slot.

### Game, title ID and version

The Hinokami Chronicles 2, 0100AD80208A8000, base 1.70 with the 1.70 update (`[...][1G+1U+8D][US][22.0.0].xci`, SDK 22.0.0); the 8 DLC are not installed on this run (`DM_AOC_OWNED=0` made no difference either).

### nxnative commit

04811a63

### Shader chain version

b-39eb2f781d07

### How it was built and run

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

### Device and OS

Mac mini (Mac16,10), Apple M4, macOS 27.2 (26B123)

### Settings and environment overrides

`--env-file` unset; the run below is the app's own `dmhost` started by hand with `DM_ROOT`, `DM_ROMFS`, `DM_MSL_DIR`, `DM_NVN_SHMAP`, `DM_SAVE`, `DM_TEMP`, `DM_AOC_DIR` and nothing else. Tried and ruled out: `DM_NVN_PREFETCH=0`, `DM_AOC_OWNED=0`, `DM_LANG=en-US`, `DM_AUDIO=0`, and forcing x18's initial slot value to the thread-local region (`pthread_setspecific(g_key18, tlr)`) — the game still ends up with x18 = 0x33200.

### Logs

The crash the host prints (pc is `main+0xffffffffff190a18`, i.e. inside the patch area, confirming the stub is what faults):

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x33220 pc=main+0xffffffffff190a18 lr=main+0x1f2bfe4 sp=0x7ec01d94d0
x0=0x20 x1=0x33200 x2=0x173573930 x3=0x220 x4=0x1 x5=0
...
x18=0x7b95927c20 x19=0x11cc8a028 ...
```

`scripts/bug_report.py 0100AD80208A8000` output is available if you want the full bundle; the interesting part is above and the `[dm] slots:` values in the table below.

### Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| faulting instruction | `0xb8606828` = `ldr w8, [x1, x0]` at the rewritten site with x1 = 0x33200, x0 = 0x20 → `0x33220` |
| ESR / far | `0x92000006` (EL0 data abort, read, translation fault level 2), `far = 0x33220` |
| original code | `main+0x23f5ec0`: `mrs x18, TPIDR_EL0` … `main+0x23f5fb8`: `ldr w8, [x18, x0]`; `cmp w8, #0x102`; `main+0x23f5fc4`: `mov x26, x18`; `bl 0xb49670` |
| thread slots at the crash | `KTLR = 0x7be3b6c000`, `KTLS = 0x7bdf11c420`, **`K18 = 0x33200`** |

`main` has exactly one instruction that writes x18 from a system register: `0xd53bd052` (`mrs x18, tpidr_el0`) at `main+0x23f5ec0`. There is no `mrs x18, tpidrro_el0` and no `msr tpidr_el0, x18` in this module.

`site_sysreg_read` (dm/tools/patch_nso.py) emits

```
stur x16,[sp,#-16]; mrs x18, tpidrro_el0; <slot addr KTLS>; ldr x18,[x18]; ldur x16,[sp,#-16]; b <next>
```

— the value lands in the x18 **register** only. `site_plain` (every other x18 site) starts with `ldr x18, [K18 slot]` and ends with `str x18, [K18 slot]`, so the value the `mrs` produced is dropped and the following site sees the slot as some earlier site left it (here 0x33200; the fault address is what made the port stop, but `mov x26, x18` at `main+0x23f5fc4` would have carried the same stale value).

macOS reserves x18, so a value that only lives in the register cannot survive from one x18 site to the next — this is not specific to this game's logic, it is the one path where the slot and the register disagree.

### Suggested fix

In `site_sysreg_read`, when the destination is x18, write the K18 slot as well:

```python
if N == 18:
    start = here()
    emit(STUR(16, 31, -16)); emit(STUR(17, 31, -24))
    emit(MRS_TPIDRRO(16)); emit_slot_addr(16, 17, kind); emit(LDRX(18, 16))
    emit(MRS_TPIDRRO(17)); emit_slot_addr(17, 16, 'K18'); emit(STRX(18, 17))
    emit(LDUR(17, 31, -24)); emit(LDUR(16, 31, -16))
    emit(B(here(), ins.address + 4))
    return start
```

I have this patch applied locally and rebuilt with it: the module now runs **19 minutes / ~34,000 frames without a crash** (two consecutive 580 s runs, ~30 fps held by the game's own frame cap, p50 33.4 ms, 56,000+ audio callbacks with 0 underruns), and the scripted-input path got through save data creation, the title screen, a cutscene and into an actual battle — where before it faulted 2 s in, every time. Would you take it (or the equivalent) upstream? `msr tpidr_el0, x18` has the same shape in reverse and would need the slot read first — no instance in this module, so I left it alone.
title: x18: a read that targets x18 leaves the K18 slot stale - mrs x18,tpidr_el0 then ldr w8,[x18,#0x20] faults at 0x33220 (The Hinokami Chronicles 2)

body:
### What happened

Building **Red Dead Redemption** (Switch, base XCI + 1.0.7 update NSP) with the NX2Apple 1.3.0 app stops at the shader split, every time:

```
[RED] main control section @0x20ce29c: no code area: no data record points at one, and the code builds the address of none right after or right before it; left out
… (46 of these, 0x20ce29c … 0x234e1f4)
```

The split's log ends with:

```
shaders: 0 (); sources ; compute shader answers 0 rows; variation pairs 0
```

and the run stops with `the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS`.

Extraction and the rewrite both succeed first, so this is not an environment problem:

```
build nx_extract                    OK
提取 v458752                         OK (reused)
改写代码                             OK — main {plain 12362, tpidr_r 13413, …} cuts 0; sdk {plain 12514, …} cuts 5
着色器拆分                           FAILS
```

### What I found about the shaders

The RomFS is **one single `.rpf`** — Rockstar's RAGE archive format — not a tree of Nintendo containers. The extracted image is a 12,071,761,488-byte `DMROMFS1` image whose contents are a single `RPF6` archive:

```
00000000: 444d 524f 4d46 5331 ba60 88cf 0200 0000  DMROMFS1.`......
00000010: 9615 0000 0000 0000 8f00 0000 0000 0000  ................
00000020: 5250 4636 0000 040b 0006 7400 ffff fffd  RPF6......t.....
```

- `DMROMFS1` header: index offset `0x2cf8860ba`, index size `0x1596`, 143 entries.
- The archive proper starts at +0x20 in that image with the magic `RPF6`.

The survey reports the contents by extension:

| extension | files |
|---|---|
| `.rpf` | 134 |
| `.bk2` | 2 (Bink video) |
| `.pkdswitch` | 1 |
| `.pkiswitch` | 1 |

`.pkdswitch` / `.pkiswitch` are RAGE's shader packages (PKSW / PKIS), and the 134 `.rpf` are nested RPF archives. There is **no BNSH, no BAHS, no `.nvnbin`, no NARC, and no `.sp4`** anywhere at the top level — the survey's own "header magic" table comes out empty, which is consistent with nothing in the image being a container any current reader knows.

So `shader_split.py` walks a 12 GB blob, sees no shader magic, and the 46 control sections it does report from `main` are the ones with no code area reachable by a data record — the actual programs are inside the RAGE archive, not in `main`.

**A reader for RPF6 (+ its nested shader packages) does not exist in the engine.** `grep -rn "RPF6" dm scripts` returns nothing; `shader_split.py` mentions only `trpfs`/`.spt`-style paths (`trpfs_jobs`, `trinity_shaders`), which is a different container.

### Why this looks like the Diablo II: Resurrected case (#2013) rather than a config problem

Both games keep every shader in a proprietary volume that the split cannot open, both report `shaders: 0`, and in both cases the control sections surfaced from `main` are a red herring with no code area. The difference is the container: D2R used `build_manifest.psv` + SHAD/BTCD volumes, RDR uses RPF6.

### What I expected

Either the split finds RDR's shaders by reading the RPF6 archive (recursively, since `.rpf` files nest), or the failure names the container it could not read, as the "A file no reader reads" entry in `docs/reference/shaders.md` describes — so the next step is clear instead of one generic line.

### Game, title ID and version

Red Dead Redemption, `01007820196A6000`, display version 1.0.7 (build `v458752`).

Folder contents:
- `Red Dead Redemption [01007820196A6000] [v1.0.4] (1G+1U).xci` — 12,459,116,544 bytes (base)
- `[UPD][01007820196A6800][1.0.6][US][21.0.0].nsp` — 336,014,104 bytes
- `[UPD][01007820196A6800][1.0.7][US][21.2.0].nsp` — 336,014,104 bytes

`nx_extract` notes `leaving out 3 NCAs … that its Application content meta does not list (another title in the package: an update on the cartridge, or a merged NSP)` — expected for this dump, and it does not stop the build.

### nxnative commit

Engine shipped with the NX2Apple app 1.3.0: `c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0-66e8bc624c49`.

### Shader chain version

`89f44f9b6bb0` (`dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h` in that engine).

### How it was built and run

Mac app (NX2Apple 1.3.0, "构建游戏" → "这台 Mac", output folder `~/Downloads/[NS]荒野大镖客 救赎`). The build fails at the split, before anything is produced.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon, arm64), macOS 26.7.3, Xcode 27.2 (iOS SDK 27.2, Metal toolchain present), .NET SDK 10.0.403, Python 3.13.18 bundled.

### Anything else

Survey (`<id>_build/staging/01007820196A6000_survey/survey.md`):

- SDK 15.3.2 (`NintendoSDK_NVN-15_3_2`), NVN + NVN on `main` and `sdk`.
- `main` build ID `37531419da7654ec3f5b586693f7f331`, text/ro/data 20.4 / 6.3 / 8.8 MB, bss 1207.1 MB.
- `sdk` build ID `8618895246b420329b77746b960a66ab`.
- RomFS: 138 files, 11.24 GB — `redemption/territory_swall` 107 files / 0.87 GB, root 25 files / 10.36 GB, `cero` 4 files, `d11extra` 2 files.
- `mem_reserve 0xb0000000`, `app_pool 0xCD500000`; NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource (`IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled` false).

The profile in use is provisional (`profile_guess.py` output, header says "not checked by hand"), and `dm/games/01007820196A6000/` does not exist — expected, since this game is not registered.

Happy to answer questions, run a branch, or test a reader against my copy. I can report back sizes, offsets and header words, but I won't be attaching anything extracted from the game.
title: Red Dead Redemption (01007820196A6000, v458752): "shader split found no shaders" — every shader is inside one RPF6 RAGE archive (the RomFS is a single .rpf)

body:
### What happened

Found and fixed at the root: upstream commit ea0c98df ("Honor NVN queue dependencies and preserve conditional state across continuations").

ea0c98df rewrote submission into per-segment queue nodes. nq_flatten calls nq_end() at every guest OP_SIGNAL_EVENT/WaitEvent, which starts a new Metal command buffer — and that ends the open render pass. BioShock's UE3 signals an event per occlusion query, so the title screen went from 88 to 189 render passes per frame:

This basically halved my FPS in Bioshock Infinite when I rebased


-----

**Title:** NVN signal events split the command buffer, ending the render pass (2x pass count on BioShock Infinite)

**Environment:** macOS 27.2, Apple M1 Max, main = 7ffa63cc.

**Symptom:** a title whose guest command stream signals NVN events inside render passes renders every pass twice. On BioShock Infinite (0100D560102C8000, USA) the title screen goes from 88 to 189 render passes per frame, attachment load 734 MB → 2,582 MB per frame, submit CPU 3.7 ms → 8.4–9.0 ms. Frame rate drops accordingly; nothing looks wrong on screen.

**Cause:** since `ea0c98df` ("Honor NVN queue dependencies…"), `nq_flatten` calls `nq_end(j)` at every `OP_SIGNAL_EVENT` and starts a new `NQ_FENCE` segment. On Metal a new segment is a new command buffer, so the open render pass ends. UE3 signals an event per occlusion query, so this is one pass break per query.

**Bisect** (same save, headless, frame 1500, instructions per draw):
`975bb4c1` 26.0k → `050580df`, `e5f03403`, `bd979ced`, `51ecd693` 27.7–27.9k → `ea0c98df` 43.5k → every later commit 43–49k.

**Why the exact fence isn't needed:** a waiter is ordered by the event value, and `mtl_sub_event`'s post op publishes that value when the submission completes — the behaviour before `ea0c98df`. The mid-pass fence buys nothing and costs a pass load/store plus an encoder per signal.

**Suggested fix** (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_queue.inc`, `nq_flatten`): keep the signal on the current commands node instead of ending the segment:

```c
// before: ... nq_end(j); nq_append(j,NQ_FENCE)->receipt=nq_new(); }
if(h.op==OP_SIGNAL_EVENT) { memcpy(&n->event,a,8); memcpy(&n->mode,a+8,4); memcpy(&n->value,a+12,4); }


### What you expected

_No response_

### Game, title ID and version

Bioshock Infinite

### nxnative commit

ea0c98df

### Shader chain version

094f939bfef9

### How it was built and run

Mac, the host from a terminal (--platform mac)

### Device and OS

Macboook pro M1 Max.

### Settings and environment overrides

N/A

### Logs

bisect (frame 1500, same save, one shader library d5fe9ae8bfba):
  975bb4c1 base    26022 instr/draw  31.33 M/frame  CPU 3.664 ms  1204 draws
  050580df c103    26611            32.17 M        4.618 ms
  c129             27728            33.42 M        3.793 ms
  c136             27770            33.39 M        3.762 ms
  c140             27905            33.74 M        3.871 ms
  51ecd693 c142    27819            33.47 M        3.790 ms
  ea0c98df c143    43517            52.50 M        7.124 ms   <-- regression starts
  c156             43616            52.55 M        7.150 ms
  c180             43584            52.62 M        7.599 ms
  7ffa63cc head    44514            53.60 M        8.407 ms

pass structure @1500:  c142 barriers 27097 load 734 MB | c143 58237 / 2582 MB | head 59005 / 2592 MB | fixed 26626 / 719 MB (CPU 4.722 ms)

One caveat worth stating in the issue: these runs pin the shader library to d5fe9ae8bfba on both sides, so shader compilation isn't a variable — the 094f939bfef9 chain at ea0c98df produces the same pass counts.

body:
### What happened

Investigation and experimental prototype by **Fable 5.2**, using local tests on my M4 Pro MacBook Pro. This report summarizes that investigation and its saved notes; the results have not been independently reproduced outside it. This is a preliminary performance finding, not a validated fix or a ready-to-merge patch.

## Timeline observation

In the Kokiri Forest village route, the local instrumentation reports that the game has submitted the next frame's command recordings before its end-of-frame SyncWait (6 game submits, 37 physical submissions). The queue worker parks them behind an unresolved event in `nvn_queue.inc`. Once the wait opens, one replay worker translates those recordings to Metal, taking about 8–9 ms. In this scene:

- The worker is idle for about 10 ms before that replay.
- GPU work totals about 15.8 ms, while a frame takes about 18.9 ms.
- A roughly 2.9 ms GPU-starvation gap occurs at frame start; the main scene submission reaches the GPU about 8 ms into the frame.

These observations do not imply that event waits can simply be bypassed: early translation can capture uniforms or other memory before the game has finished writing it.

## Experimental result

Fable 5.2 made a scratch prototype (`DM_NQ_PREENC=1`) that encodes past one unresolved event while the worker is idle, retaining commits behind a gate. Gate selection was restricted to a word observed being published from the CPU, with no GPU signal and no queued commands node signaling it, after an earlier attempt blocked unrelated work on a compute-queue wait whose producer had not been submitted.

One 30-second standing-still village sample, about 1,300 draws per frame:

| Metric | Stock host | Prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FPS | 52.8 | 57.6 |
| Median frame | 18.9 ms | 17.34 ms |
| Frame p99 | about 20.8 ms | 18.74 ms |

Fable reported about 36 submissions encoded ahead per frame, a gate held about 10.6 ms, game speed 1.000, no watchdog/early releases in that run, and a screenshot matching the baseline. This is a preliminary single-run result, not a general 9% performance claim.

## Important limitations

- A subsequent run reported 55.9 FPS but triggered early releases. Correct synchronization is therefore not established.
- A 50 ms watchdog can release held work; its correctness is not established.
- The patch also enlarges the allocator pool to 160 and the post ring to 1,024; their contribution has not been isolated.
- Quit logs `[RED] graceful exit not done in 1.5 seconds`.
- Camera movement, transitions, loading screens, cutscenes, long sessions, dynamic resolution and Hold frames on remain unchecked. The wider check batch was interrupted.
- No general regression-suite pass is claimed. The prototype has not replaced the installed app.
- The game copy has three known damaged `.zs` textures and was built with `--allow-damaged`. This is a test-data confound, not something ruled out as a contributor. A clean-copy reproduction is still needed.

Route recorded in the local notes (starts from a copied Kokiri Forest autosave):

```text
35:A~0.2,40:A~0.2,43:A~0.2,48:A~0.2,60:LDown~6,67:ZL~0.3,69:LUp~8
measurement window: 82–112 seconds
```

## Other local comparisons

- Raising the allocator pool from 8 to 48 alone: 52.6–53.3 FPS, no meaningful change from the stock comparison.
- Smaller/unconditional segment commits, pass merging and the encode thread: no useful improvement reported in this spot.
- Standard final upscaling instead of MetalFX: about 54.2 FPS, roughly 0.4 ms improvement.
- Dynamic resolution: 60 FPS at only about 683–763 internal pixels wide; it did not recover in a 75-second still sample.

## Upstream context and questions

At drafting time, main was `a888e6681b3ce4b51a6ef8ea638062ddeae69bfc`, seven commits ahead of the test base, including memory-accounting, prewarm and shader changes. These findings need a fresh baseline there; no current-main reproduction is claimed.

Related work: #1847 (acquire synchronization, translation cost and GPU scheduling), #2073 (cross-frame overlap / optional frame-lag bound), and #1703 / #1245 (queue dependencies needed for correct Ocarina lighting). This report may overlap existing work.

Is this delayed-translation behavior expected given the lifetime and visibility guarantees of event-dependent game memory? Is there an existing issue where these timeline measurements belong? Which recordings or bindings could safely be prepared early while preserving every event dependency?

Before proposing a mergeable change: reproduce on current main, isolate pool-size changes, eliminate forced early releases, compare repeated same-route runs with camera motion and transitions, check visuals/game speed/shutdown, and run appropriate queue/order regressions.

### What you expected

Preserve all event ordering and memory-visibility guarantees while reducing translation-related GPU idle time, if early preparation is safe. I am looking for maintainer guidance on the mechanism and a correct reproduction/validation plan, rather than proposing that event waits be skipped.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), 0400486024DEC000, update v131072

### nxnative commit

04811a634b7f9344e882129b0973dd493369dd62 (stock baseline; separate modified host for prototype)

### Shader chain version

39eb2f781d07; all 42,848 shaders built

### How it was built and run

Mac, the host from a terminal (--platform mac)

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro, M4 Pro (12 CPU / 16 GPU cores), 24 GB RAM; macOS 27.2; Xcode 27.2

### Settings and environment overrides

Docked, full internal resolution, windowed, Italian, game's own upscaler, final MetalFX upscaling. Built using --allow-damaged for three damaged textures (confound disclosed above). Tests use a copied save and a separate host through scripts/bench.py.

Measured baseline/prototype comparison overrides:
```text
DM_DYNAMIC_RESOLUTION=0
DM_OPMODE=1
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx
DM_UPSCALER=game
DM_LANG=it
DM_FULLSCREEN=0
DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0
DM_PSO_MTL4=1
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0
DM_FPS_HOLD=off
DM_WINDOW_TOP=1
```
The benchmark wrapper normally defaults DM_FPS_HOLD=on; the comparisons reported above override it to off. Prototype additionally uses DM_NQ_PREENC=1. Other variant changes are stated in the report.

### Logs

Complete raw run logs are not attached to this preliminary report. The timing results above are transcribed from Fable 5.2's investigation and saved notes, not independently rerun by the reporting assistant. No fresh current-main trace is claimed.

The prototype's known shutdown message is:
```text
[RED] graceful exit not done in 1.5 seconds
```
One subsequent sample triggered early-release guards, so its 55.9 FPS does not demonstrate a correct speedup. The local prototype patch and baseline/prototype screenshots are preserved, but are not attached here. A full reproducible trace on current main remains outstanding.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

```
memory up to frame 300:  resident 5040 MB,  GPU allocated 3215 MB  ... headroom to the system memory limit none
power  up to frame 600:  59.8 fps

title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, Mac 16 GB): GPU memory 3 → 13 GB within a minute and fps drops to ~17 since c68706f9 (fine on 7f502220)

body:
Follow-up to #1860 / 26062f9e (chain 3510ea767778, `TranslationFlags.MetalUniformBounds`).

## What I see

Donkey Kong Bananza `040074A01BF12000` v458752, Freezer Layer (SL500), docked, `DM_RENDER_SCALE=0.6667`. MacBook Air M4 (10-core GPU), macOS 27, on AC power. Same save, same spot, scripted route, about 15,300 draws a frame on the level. The host was built `-O3` + PGO from the same tree both times. The only difference between the two builds is the `MetalUniformBounds` flag in `dmsh_xlate/Program.cs`, with the lock and `dmsh_chain.h` regenerated and every shader and the pipeline archive rebuilt.

| Level, per frame (p50) | With the guard (chain 39eb2f781d07) | Without it (local chain 7c6c9929fed5) |
|---|---|---|
| Frame | 33.3 ms (30 fps) | 18.1 ms (about 55 fps) |
| GPU | 17.5-18.1 ms | 14.6 ms |
| Submit thread translation | 11.9 ms | 9.6 ms |
| Instructions per draw | 13,000 | 10,750 |

The game paces itself at 60 when a frame fits 16.7 ms. With the guard the GPU alone no longer fits, so it drops to interval 2. The map view is GPU-bound either way (about 26 ms of GPU without the guard). Pictures are the same on the level and the map, and no `[RED]` lines appear in either build.

The two other new defaults of that update, `DM_NVN_FAMILY_NOCOMPRESS=0` and `DM_NVN_FB_DEPTH=0`, change nothing here: GPU still 17.5 ms with both off.

## Two separate costs

**1. GPU: every read of c3-c16 goes through the guard.** Bananza's material shaders read many uniform words. NieR's opening flight showed +1.5 % p50 / +6 % p95 in the commit message; here it is about +20 % of GPU time.

**2. CPU: shaders with a `cbsize` binding lost the uniform-only patch path.** `ab_patchable()` lists the binding kinds a uniform-only patch can keep. `NVN_RB_CBSIZE` is not in the list, so it falls to `default: ok = 0`. Every shader with a guarded read, which is nearly all of them now, re-encodes its whole argument block on every draw where only a uniform binding changed. Bananza's long passes rebind one small uniform block per object (12,000 objects, 47 fragment bindings each), the case `encode_args_`'s patch was made for. On top of that comes a 16-byte arena block for the size table at each encode. That accounts for the +2.3 ms of translation and the +2,250 instructions per draw.

## Suggestions

**For the CPU part (host only, no chain change).** Make `NVN_RB_CBSIZE` patchable. The table depends only on the uniform bindings' sizes, which change exactly when a `CBUF` / `UBOP` binding changes. So the patch that rewrites the changed uniform entries can write a fresh size table (or patch the changed words in a copy) and point the `cbsize` slot at it. A cheaper variant: cache the table per stage and reuse its arena block while no size changed (sizes rarely change from draw to draw, only addresses).

**For the GPU part.** Only a few shaders are ever bound short. The host already knows both sides: the bound sizes, and each shader's extent from `cb_extent.tsv` (proven extent or highest fixed-offset read, which `ub_short` already compares). Some options:
- **Two variants of each guarded shader**, guarded and plain. The host picks the plain one when every slot the shader reads is bound at least as long as its extent, which is the case for almost every draw in every game. The guarded one is used only where `ub_short` would fire. That costs a second library per shader, but the host already picks between variants of a shader (the `_bf` readable-tile versions, the `fz` functions), and the plain variant is the pre-#1860 shader.
- **Guard only computed-offset reads**, plus fixed-offset reads past the slot's smallest observed binding. Reads at fixed offsets inside the extent, which the host can check before the draw, need no guard. A draw whose binding is shorter than a fixed-offset read could then take the guarded variant, or get its binding padded with zeros: the reporter found that padding fixed TTYD.
- **At least a switch** (`DM_NVN_UNIFORM_BOUNDS=0` choosing a chain without the guard, or a profile key), so a game known not to read past its bindings can skip it.

I can measure any of these on Bananza, and I'm happy to send a PR for the `ab_patchable` part if that direction is OK.
title: The uniform bounds guard (26062f9e) halves Donkey Kong Bananza's frame rate on an M4: 55 → 30 fps

body:
I ran the translator's Ampere instructions against a real Ampere GPU, a Jetson Orin (sm_87, CUDA 12.6 driver), and compared every output bit for bit. This issue lists what differed and the PRs that fix it. Every PR is now open, so this is the whole series.

## How it was checked

Each of 203 operations is a tiny PTX kernel that the Orin's driver compiles and runs on 1,024 rows of inputs. Those mix signed zeros, denormals, infinities, NaNs, integer limits and rounding ties with random bits. The same machine code then goes through our whole chain (the translator with the build's options, spirv-cross, every MSL rewrite `finish()` makes, the chain's Metal flags) and runs on a Mac's GPU on the same rows. Only the global loads and stores are swapped for shared memory ones, and the Orin's `nvdisasm` checks every swap. #2041 adds this as `test_dmsh_ampere_orin.py`, with the Orin's results as a fixture, so anyone can rerun it on an Apple-silicon Mac without an Orin.

## Where it ends up

| | Bit-exact | Only Metal's own float behaviour | Other differences | Doesn't translate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 81 | 37 | 46 | 39 |
| main + this series | 116 | 56 | 26 | 5 |

Of the 26 left, 9 are fixed by #1800, and 17 are Metal's own approximations of MUFU functions and the divisions built on them. Of the 5 that don't translate, 3 call into the CUDA driver itself (something a game's shader never does) and 2 need 64-bit floats.

## Wrong results

| Instruction | What the Orin does that we didn't | PR |
|---|---|---|
| FSETP / FSET `.NE` | `.NE` is false when an operand is NaN. spirv-cross writes it as MSL's `!=`, which is true then. Maxwell shares the helper. | #2042 |
| SHFL with the lane in a register | The lane is masked to its low 5 bits (lane 2 asking for `0xdaa06cd7` reads lane 23); we returned the thread's own value. Maxwell too. | #2044 |
| I2F `.S64` | One rounding; we rounded the high and low words apart. | #2045 |
| F2FP `.BF16`, `.RELU` | It packs bf16 and clamps negatives to 0; we packed f16 and kept them. | #2046 |
| FMNMX / HMNMX2 with +0 and −0 | `max(+0, −0)` is +0; Metal returns either. | #2047 |
| HADD2 / HMUL2 / HFMA2 `.FTZ` | f16 subnormals are flushed; Metal keeps them. | #2048 |
| HFMA2 / HMUL2 `.RELU` | A NaN result stays NaN; we gave 0. | #2049 |
| FADD / FMUL / FFMA `.RZ` `.RM` `.RP` | The rounding mode is applied; we rounded to nearest. | #2051 |
| HMMA with an f32 accumulator | Products are aligned and truncated in blocks of 8 (the A100 tensor-core model); two thirds of our outputs differed by about 1 ULP. Now bit-exact. | #2061 |
| HMMA with an f16 accumulator outside compute shaders (and m16n8k8) | Each block of 8 is aligned and truncated, then rounded to f16; we summed all 16 with FMAs and rounded once, which is 34 % off on fxd0h's 4.7 million recorded outputs. Now bit-exact. | #2067 |

## Instructions the translator refused

None of these occur in Ocarina of Time's shaders, since its whole build translates. But the compiler emits them for ordinary PTX, so other games may.

| Instruction | PR |
|---|---|
| HFMA2.MMA (0x235, 0x435), which ptxas also uses to load constants | #2049 |
| IDP (`dp4a`, `dp2a`) | #2052 |
| VABSDIFF (`sad`) | #2053 |
| I2I `.SAT` | #2054 |
| PRMT's F4E, B4E, RC8, ECL, ECR and RC16 modes | #2055 |
| IMMA (8-bit integer `mma`) | #2056 |
| PLOP3 on register sign bits (`add.sat`, `sub.sat`) | #2057 |
| MUFU.TANH | #2058 |
| F2I to a signed 64-bit integer | #2059 |
| HMNMX2 `.NAN`, and bf16 half pairs (HFMA2 / HMNMX2 `.BF16_V2`) | #2060 |
| HMMA with bf16 or tf32 sources | #2062 |

## Fixed in other PRs

- **#1800** fixes FMNMX `.NAN`, I2F / I2FP directed roundings (to F32 and F16), F2FP.PACK_AB `.RZ` and the SHFL.UP clamp. I recorded the cases the fixture lacked and checked all of them on the Orin: no regressions, and every fix it lists that the fixture can express matches ([first](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1800#issuecomment-6748851124), [follow-up](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1800#issuecomment-6749596736)).
- **#1412** also translates MUFU.TANH and changes the sin / cos argument reduction. It shows no regressions, but #2058's TANH is closer to the Orin (f16: 3 differing halves against 632), and main's existing reduction is already slightly closer than its own ([comment](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1412#issuecomment-6749881340)).
- **#1334** runs HMMA through Metal 4 `matmul2d` on Apple10 GPUs. It predates #1897, and its tensor body rounds once per 16 products, so 72 % of its outputs match the Orin, against 99.97 % on main. Two `matmul2d` runs, one per block of 8, match as well as main and are still about 13 % faster ([comment](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1334#issuecomment-6749909660)).
- **#1902** makes HFMA2 round once to half. With #2049 it shows no regressions, and its rewrite also covers HFMA2.MMA, but it misses the `.RELU` form ([comment](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1902#issuecomment-6749135591)).

## What isn't fixed, and why

- **NaN bit patterns and f32 denormals.** Metal writes `0x7fc00000` where Ampere writes `0x7fffffff`, and flushes f32 denormals. Matching either would add work to every float instruction in every shader, so the test allows both and reports them.
- **MUFU and the divisions built on it** are Metal's own approximations. They agree within 1 to 2 ULP on normal inputs but aren't bit-exact, so the test reports them without failing.
- **DADD / DMUL** would need software 64-bit floats, since Apple GPUs have none.
- **FCHK and the `CALL.ABS` slow paths** of `div.rn`, `rcp.rn` and `sqrt.rn` call into the CUDA driver, which no game shader does, so they can't be tested this way.
- **The last 0.03 % of f16-accumulator HMMA in compute shaders.** The tensor-core model with a final round to f16 matches every one of fxd0h's 4.7 million recorded outputs, but on the matrix-hardware path it costs 23 to 30 times as much on Ocarina of Time's NDSR upscaler shaders, measured isolated. So compute keeps #1897's method; #2067 applies the model to the per-thread path only.
- **Maxwell's PRMT** isn't implemented at all. I found it along the way; it's outside this series.

## Cost

Every fix applies only to the instructions it's about. Plain round-to-nearest FADD, FMUL and FFMA emit the same MSL as before. Directed rounding exempts NVIDIA's `FMUL.RZ x, 1/(2π)` in front of every sin and cos (about 430,000 in Ocarina of Time), since Metal's sin and cos error dwarfs the argument's rounding. The f32-accumulator HMMA model is heavy, about 1,900 MSL statements, but Ocarina of Time has 2 such HMMAs against 13,267 with an f16 accumulator. The one change on a common instruction is #2047's ±0 rule, 4 to 5 integer operations per FMNMX; I counted it but haven't measured frame time. None of the PRs has a `regress.py` report yet: my only local Switch 2 build comes from an older shader split than main can read.

## Suggested review order

If it helps to take the series in stages, this is where I'd start, by how much each part is likely to matter:

1. **#2041, the test suite.** It catches any future translator change that moves an instruction away from the hardware, including the HMMA paths in #1334 and #1902.
2. **Fixes to instructions game shaders commonly use:** #2049 (HFMA2.MMA, which ptxas also uses to load constants), #2042 (FSETP `.NE`), #2044 (SHFL), #2047 (min / max of ±0), #2048 (f16 `.FTZ`) and #2051 (directed rounding).
3. **Everything else:** #2045, #2046, #2052–#2062 and #2067. These are correct and their cost lands only where the instruction is used, but no game we know of relies on them yet, so they can wait or be dropped if you'd rather keep the series smaller.

## Landing order

Each fix PR carries #2041's commits underneath its own. They all touch the test's `KNOWN` list and the chain header, so later ones need a small rebase; each PR says which entries to take out. A few depend on each other:

- #2049 before #2059 (`f2i_s64`'s program loads a constant with HFMA2.MMA).
- #2061 before #2062.
- With #2048 and #2049 both in, `hfma2_ftz` matches.
- With #1800 in, its nine ops come out of `KNOWN`.

## Verifying

Each PR takes its ops out of `KNOWN`. The test fails if a listed op starts matching or an unlisted one stops matching, so running this on a PR's branch shows exactly what it fixed:

```
DMSH_TEST_XLATE=dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate python3 dm/gfx/tests/test_dmsh_ampere_orin.py
```
title: Ampere instructions checked against a Jetson Orin: what differed from the hardware, and the PRs that fix it

body: Game: Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, title ID 010051F0207B2000, version 1.0.4 (v262144), SDK 20.5.3 Devices: iPad Pro M2 (iPadOS 27.2, LiveContainer) and MacBook Pro M1 (macOS 27.2, mac-app). Same bugs on both. nxnative: commit 7f50222003e4, provisional profile written by the survey What works: the game boots, island Miis render correctly, UI renders, ~30 fps, no crash. Bug 1 – Miis rendered into the UI are blank (iOS and Mac). Every Mii the game draws live into a UI element is missing, while the element's own background renders fine: - "Which Mii do you want to start with?" screen (new game): both starting Miis are missing, only their card backgrounds show. Easiest repro: start a new game. - Mii editor ("From Scratch"): the whole 3D preview is missing, body included. - Some 2D Mii icons in menus are blank while others display. The same screens on ryujinx 1.3.352 with the same dump and update show the Miis correctly (screenshots attached side by side). Island Miis in the 3D world render fine on nxnative, so the Mii models themselves work: the render-to-texture pass for UI Miis seems lost. Possibly related [RED] line: "texture 48×96×1 declares 15 levels, its size holds 7 (format 0x38)". Bug 2 – Street lamps in daylight: a large black, blocky, stair-stepped shape surrounded by a white halo is drawn around street lamps, with occasional flashes. The stair-step pattern looks like a NaN/Inf spreading through a bloom/glow downsample chain. render_cond on: not tested yet Log: no [RED] line when the editor opens. [RED] lines early in the run: - [nvn] SetRenderEnableConditional: the host draws anyway for now - [nvn-mtl] texture 48×96×1 declares 15 levels, its size holds 7 (format 0x38) - [nvn-mtl] color slot 1 holds the same texture as an earlier slot (ser=17119) and this draw writes it (mask 0x8): these writes are lost Attached: iPad log.txt, Mac log, survey.md, screenshots of both bugs (iPad and Mac). [010051F0207B2000.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34593725/010051F0207B2000.log) [log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34593829/log.txt) [survey.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34593969/survey.md)
title: Title: Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream (010051F0207B2000): blank Mii editor preview, black blocks around street lamps

body:
## Environment

- Device: iPhone Duo (`iPhone19,4`), iOS 27.2, Apple A20 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g19p`), 12 GB
- Build: commit `c78d7375bea9`, shader chain `89f44f9b6bb0`, profile `0400E88025B1A000` (Switch 2, `nnSdk-Generic_21_4_4`), RomFS separate (~15 GB in `Documents`)
- `env.txt`: `DM_SHOW_FPS=1`, `DM_THERMAL_CAP=1`
- Installed from Xcode, Release

## Symptom

The game holds 60 fps in flight and combat (13,500 frames, frame p50 16.65 ms, GPU 12.4-13.1 ms, 0-2 dropped per 300), but at scene and area transitions it freezes for 0.5-3.9 s. It reads as stutter during NPC radio dialogue, because those exchanges come with camera cuts that pull a new texture batch, but the voice is incidental: muting the audio does not change it (see below).

## Evidence

Long frames where `submit+present` takes the whole stall and the GPU is idle:

| frame | whole frame | submit+present | GPU | texture uploads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 378 | 3916.8 ms | 3914.5 ms | 10.8 ms | 117 first + 112 re-uploads, 5587.6 MB |
| 3187 | 1643.3 ms | 1641.9 ms | 4.9 ms | 286 first + 56 re-uploads, 4320.2 MB |
| 1365 | 1102.1 ms | 1084.0 ms | 9.3 ms | 181 first + 92 re-uploads, 4888.0 MB |
| 6234 | 663.2 ms | - | - | 15 first + 36 re-uploads, 3071.8 MB |
| 5912 | 552.8 ms | - | - | 27 first + 46 re-uploads, 2235.8 MB |

The lines just before them are package loads, e.g.

```
[game] game-0-package: Unloading ...
[game] game-0-package: Loading ...
[game] game-0-package: Async hi...
```

and the upload counters climb with them:

```
[nvn-mtl] packaged textures: first uploads 2636, re-uploads on pool content change 594, writes beside a texture only
[nvn-mtl] upload staging blocks: 251 created in total, swapped within a batch 133 times (5344 MB of old blocks swapped out)
```

## Audio ruled out

Same build, `DM_AUDIO=0` (silent sink), voice-heavy section:

| | audio on | DM_AUDIO=0 |
|---|---|---|
| slow frames per 1000 | 9.3 (249 of 26,700) | 8.4 (53 of 6,300) |
| frames > 100 ms | 97 | 21 |
| worst frames | 3827, 1740, 1474 ms | 3917, 1643, 1102 ms |
| audio underruns | 32 and 9 per 2000 callbacks | none (silent sink) |

The giant spikes are identical, so they are not the audio output path. (The underruns with audio on are consistent with the same stalls starving the audio thread, i.e. a symptom.)

## Expected

Texture uploads for a package load should not block the submit thread for seconds. Either:

1. upload in bounded chunks across frames, with the draws that need an unready texture held back (the pattern already used for pipeline bases), or
2. keep the upload on a worker while the frame proceeds, so a 5 GB batch costs frames in aggregate rather than one multi-second freeze.

## Reproduction

1. Build `0400E88025B1A000` with `--prepare-xcode`, install, copy RomFS
2. Play until an area transition or a cutscene-heavy radio exchange
3. Watch `[longframe] ... texture uploads N first + M re-uploads, X MB` with `submit+present` at the whole stall

## Notes

- `DM_NVN_DIRECT_UPLOAD` and `DM_NVN_UPLOAD_REUSE` change staging policy only; I have not found a switch that bounds the batch.
- Happy to run A/B builds or capture `DM_NVN_TEXINFO` output for a specific frame if that helps.
title: Star Fox (0400E88025B1A000) on iPhone: multi-GB texture upload bursts block the submit thread for 0.5-3.9 s at package loads

body:
## Environment

- Device: iPhone Duo (`iPhone19,4`), iOS 27.2, Apple A20 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g19p`)
- Build: commit `c78d7375bea9`, shader chain `89f44f9b6bb0`, profile `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072
- Built with `--gpu g19p --prepare-xcode`, installed from Xcode (Personal Team), RomFS separate

## Symptom

With the bundled offline pipeline archive and `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, the app opens the archive, loads its bases, then hangs on a black screen after Play. The log ends after `fs mount savt`, no first frame.

```
[nvn-mtl] pipeline archive bundled with the app: .../DmIOS.app/pso/applegpu_g19p.mtl4a, 479.4 MB, opened in 505.8 ms
[nvn-mtl] pipeline prepare: 12287 lines (9381 shaders, 2093 render pipelines, 813 compute pipelines) in 54.75 s ...
[nvn-mtl] pipeline prepare ... bases 1 compiled, 1836 from the archive, 256 reused; 2093 specializations
[nvn-mtl] compute pipelines so far: 813 from the archive bundled with the app, 0 from this device's archive, 0 built
[nvn-mtl] pipeline archive bundled with the app: holds the bases of every shader pair (3 of 3 probed bases found, 6.1 ms)
```

Eight red lines name the actual blocker, one per vertex key:

```
[RED] pulling library of dd92bf87e78cf5fb_b not usable
      (no library: cannot open .../DmIOS.app/msl/b-89f44f9b6bb0/dd92bf87e78cf5fb_bp.metallib):
      its draws wait for their pipelines
```

`DM_PSO_MTL4=0` in `Documents/env.txt` runs the same build fine (falls back to building bases through the `MTLDevice`), so the game and profile are otherwise sound.

## What I checked

- **Zero `<key>_bp.metallib` anywhere** after a `--gpu` build: `find` over the work folder, `unzip -l` of the IPA, and the built `.app` all return 0. The only iOS shader artefact is the single `msl/b-89f44f9b6bb0.img` plus its `.key`.
- Rebuilding with `pso_mtl4 on` added to the profile (so `ios_wants_pulling()` returns true) compiled the same 42,848 shaders in 49:48 and produced a **2.8 GB** archive instead of 479 MB, but still **zero** `_bp.metallib`. So the profile key changes how many bases are built, not whether the pulling libraries are emitted.
- `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py` writes the pulling library only when both hold:

```
libs = [os.path.join(out, key + '_bp.metallib')] + ([os.path.join(IOSOUT, key + '_bp.metallib')] if IOSOUT else [])
...
if IOSOUT and IOS_PULL: MTL.compile('ios', msl, libs[1])
```

With this packaging the per-shader files never appear next to the linked image, so the host has nothing to open.

- `--shader-files`, which would ship the library as the per-shader files the host looks for, cannot be combined with `--prepare-xcode` (`BuildError: SHADER_FILES / --shader-files shapes the IPA for install tools that cannot copy a large file: it cannot be combined with --prepare-xcode, which Xcode installs`), and Xcode is the only signing route available here.

## Expected

Either:

1. the offline archive step refuses to ship an archive whose pulling libraries the app will not carry (falling back to no archive, as `--gpu none` does), or
2. the iOS shader build emits `<key>_bp.metallib` whenever an archive or `pso_mtl4 on` will make the host read it, including the packaging paths that link the library into one `.img`.

As it stands a `--gpu` archive on this title makes the app unlaunchable, and the failure mode (draws waiting for pipelines) is a hang rather than a fallback to the `MTLDevice` path.

## Reproduction

1. `build_ipa_from_nsp.py <OoT v131072 nup> --work-dir <dir> --romfs separate --gpu g19p --prepare-xcode --team-id <team> --bundle-id <id>`
2. Install with Xcode (Release), copy RomFS, launch, press Play
3. Black screen; the log ends after `fs mount savt` with the `pulling library … not usable` lines above
4. Set `DM_PSO_MTL4=0` in `Documents/env.txt` and relaunch: the same app runs

## Notes

- The archive's `prebuilt.tsv` matches this run (`chain 89f44f9b6bb0`, `depth near=-w`), and `archive.tsv` reports `bases 3222 / rest 0 / compute 4125` for the 479 MB build, so the coverage check itself is passing — it is the libraries the bases are made from that are absent.
- Happy to attach the full log or run a build with any combination of flags you want tested.
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000) iPhone: a --gpu pipeline archive ships bases whose <key>_bp pulling libraries the app does not carry, and hybrid draws wait for them (black screen)

body:
### What happened

Building **Diablo II: Resurrected** (Switch) with the NX2Apple 1.3.0 app (engine `c78d7375…`) stops at the shader split, every time:

```
[RED] main control section @0x1b7fc48: no code area: no data record points at one, and the code builds the address of none right after or right before it; left out
… (10 of these, 0x1b7fc48 … 0x1bca78c)
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the ROMFS: the game keeps them in a format shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader
```

The split's log ends with `shaders: 0 (); sources ; compute shader answers 0 rows; variation pairs 0`.

Two things before the shader problem, in case they matter for the same game:

1. **The DLC stops the build before this.** The Warlock DLC NSP (`0100726014353001`) is a 121 KB licence-only package whose PFS0 table declares 137,152 bytes of files but only 123,840 are there; the data NCA `61f2bb59…` declares 114,688 bytes and 21,760 are present, so `nx_extract --aoc` dies with `ResultFsOutOfRange (2002-3005)` / exit −6 instead of a named "[RED] the NSP is damaged" line. That one is my file's fault (a truncated `.nsz`), but the error comes out as an unhandled LibHac exception.
2. With the DLC left out, the build gets past extraction and the rewrite, then hits the shader split.

### What I found about the shaders

The RomFS is not a tree of resource files: `data/` holds `build_manifest.psv` (29.9 MB, a `|`-separated table `FileId|KeyLayout|Chunk|Archive|CKey|CSize|EKey|ESize|Encoding|Path|Flags`, 127,898 rows) and 17 volume files `00-00000001.data` … `17-00000001.data`. Each row's data is at `EKey[11:16]` (big-endian 40 bits) in `<Chunk:02d>-<Archive:08d>.data`, encoded `n` (raw), `z` (one zlib stream, no BLTE header) or `b:…` (BLTE); the content's md5 is the `CKey` column.

**158 rows are the shaders**, `data:data/hd/shaders/*.bin` (81 MB in total). Each is a `SHAD` container: a chunk list after the `SHAD` header, with `SHDR`, `TXT[`, `SYM[`, `SHMD`, `PRM[` and a `BTCD` chunk whose data starts at `+0x38` (the second `BTCD` of the node, i.e. `tag` at +0x04, `len`/`ver`/`hdr`/`data` at +0x08/+0x0c/+0x10/+0x14; `hdr` 0x24, `data` = rest of the file).

Inside the `BTCD` data the layout is, for graphics:

```
[code area: 0x12345678 header …][control section: 0x34127698, version 1, control +0x20 = 0x880][code area][control section]…
```

i.e. each program is a code area immediately followed by its 0x880-byte control section (no self-length inside the control, which is why `ctl_len()`'s `+0x20` read of `n if 0x760 <= n < 0x880` returns 0 here — `+0x20` is 0, not the section length). Compute programs have no code header: the code area is the file from 0 to the control section, and the control section ends the file (93 of the 158 packages are exactly one 0x880 control section preceded by 2,176 bytes of headerless code — matches `check()`'s `st == 'cs'` case for D2R).

What I counted after resolving the containers and walking the `BTCD` data:

- 8,438 control sections in total, 6,055 distinct `sha256(control[:0x880])[:16]` keys.
- 8,279 graphics code areas (`0x12345678` header, SPH word 0 at code+0x30: 3,656 vertex, 4,623 pixel) and 158 compute control sections.
- Program pairs are adjacent `code+control` units, so a graphics program's vertex/pixel partner is the next unit only where the game stores them together; I did not try to pair them.

I cross-checked the control keys against the shader map shipped in [jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) (`dm/gfx/nvn/shader_map.tsv`, built from D2R 3.3.94012). For the packages the two versions share, 1,423 of the keys I computed are equal to entries there (e.g. `cs_default_c.bin` → `5f420418815f5138`, `vs_2d.bin`/`ps_2d.bin` also match), which pins the container → control-section parse. The rest do not match because my copy is 1.0.0 (build `4de22400c997ed2373f0643e9fe9b079`) and that map was made on 3.3 — not evidence of a parse error.

Two things I did **not** do: I did not add a reader, and I have no way to tell from outside whether the engine's `nvn` host can consume a control section whose `+0x20` is 0 and whose length is implied by the next section (it may need the length synthesised from the following control or the end of the file).

### What I expected

Either the split finds D2R's shaders in the `data/hd/shaders` packages of the RomFS volumes, or the failure names the container so the next step is clear.

### Game, title ID and version

Diablo II: Resurrected, 0100726014352000, 1.0.0.0 (v0, base game only; update/DLC not packed). DLC present in the folder: `Diablo_II_Resurrected_Reign_of_the_Warlock` 0100726014353001 (left out of this build, see above).

### nxnative commit

Engine shipped with the NX2Apple app 1.3.0: `c78d7375bea9c862679ec294a6a69ff3e22e18d0-66e8bc624c49`.

### Shader chain version

`89f44f9b6bb0` (`dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h` in that engine).

### How it was built and run

Mac app (NX2Apple 1.3.0, "Build game" → This Mac). The NSP script fails before anything runs.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro (Apple M1 Pro), macOS 27.2, arm64.

### Anything else

Survey (from `<id>_build/staging/0100726014352000_survey/survey.md`): SDK 11.4.3, modules main/rtld/sdk/subsdk0(NintendoSDK_movie), NVN + FMOD, RomFS 25 files / 7.68 GB, all under `data/`. The survey's own "What it means for a port" already says "no BNSH / BAHS at the top level: the shaders are inside compressed or other containers or in main, and must be located first". `main`'s control sections (the 10 in the log) are the only ones and have no code area reachable by a data record — D2R's graphics shaders live in the volume, not in `main`.

Happy to answer questions or try a branch; I won't be attaching anything extracted from the game.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: Diablo II: Resurrected (0100726014352000): "shader split found no shaders" — the shaders are in the RomFS build-manifest volumes (data/hd/shaders/*.bin, SHAD/BTCD)
