### What happened

Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072, SDK 22.2.8) built with engine `c78d7375` (NX2Apple 1.3.0 / rc9, shader chain `89f44f9b6bb0`) shows a black window with sound from boot. The game itself renders: its 1920x1080 target holds the title correctly. The last pass, the copy of that target into the 2560x1440 swapchain, writes black. The same Mac showed a picture with an earlier build (engine `88c7e03f`, chain `adec7d81d970`). Other users report the same thing on M4 Pro and M5 with this engine (LNPANDY/NX2Apple#836). One user reports that engine `f25fa956` works on an M2 Max (same thread).

### Evidence (frame 3000, title screen)

- `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP=3000`: ser=4292 (1920x1080, fmt 92) holds the full title screen (logo, "New Game", options). Swapchain ser=2 is all zero.
- `DM_NVN_TEXSNAP`: the swapchain is already black at the end of the pass that draws it (pass 8937). Nothing writes it later.
- `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP=3000`, last pass:
  ```
  Y bind_program program=0x769d3dd910 stages=0xff vs=a5b1bd74e47458d7_b fs=29e3c9dd92b8a571_b
  Y update_ub dst=0x7c2a234020 bytes=64
  j 8937 draw-entry vs=a5b1bd74e47458d7_b fs=29e3c9dd92b8a571_b prim=4 count=6 indexed=1
  P 8937 c0 ser=2 fmt=71 2560x1440 ... load
  B 8937 st1 tex reg0 ser=4292 fmt=92 1920x1080
  D 8937 prim=4 vc=6 ... sc=0,0,1920,1080 tgt=2560x1440 vp=0,0,1920,1080
  s 8937 ... cull=2 winding=1
  ```
- The two stages of that program do not fit together. In the chain's MSL:
  - `a5b1bd74e47458d7_b` (VS) writes only `loc0.xy` (a UV). `loc1..loc3` are `dm_pad` (0,0,0,1), with `vs_pad: [1, 2, 3]` in its JSON.
  - `29e3c9dd92b8a571_b` (FS) samples with UVs from `loc2.xy`, and multiplies its output by `loc1.xyz * gl_FragCoord.w` (`out.c0 = (1/w) * loc1 * ...`). With the padded `loc1` every channel is 0, so the output is black.
  - The same FS is also used by the movie draw (vs `8f9728d9b2b88600_b`, program `0x769d3df010`) earlier in the frame. That VS presumably writes `loc1`/`loc2`.
- So either the present program's fragment key is wrong, or `a5b1bd74e47458d7` lost its `loc1`/`loc2` outputs in translation.

### Tried, all still black

`DM_UPSCALER=game|metalfx`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`, `DM_NVN_NDVE_MOVIE_DIRECT=0`, `DM_AV1_DAV1D=1`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_NVN_UB_PARTIAL=0`, and `DM_NVN_UB_DEFER=0 DM_NVN_UBP_RUNNING=0 DM_NVN_UB_LAZY=0 DM_NVN_UB_COPY_THREAD=0` together.

I also tried a host built from `c78d7375` with the program-key lookup back on the NVNprogram's address (`e5f03403` undone in `hle_nvn.c`): still black, same keys. So the program-key change is not the cause.

### Not related

- `nn::codec AV1: busy (result 3603)` lines: the movie decodes and loops.
- Pipelines: prepare and prebuild finished, 0 failed.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072 (one NUP)

### nxnative commit

c78d7375 (NX2Apple 1.3.0-rc9 pin; its fork patches applied)

### Shader chain version

89f44f9b6bb0

### How it was built and run

Mac app (`--platform mac-app`) through NX2Apple 1.3.0-rc9

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro M3 Pro (18-core GPU, applegpu_g15s), macOS 27.2

### Suspects between f25fa956 (reported working) and c78d7375

`04419bc2` (translator: 128-bit raw global loads, occlusion-culled draws skipped), `e5f1adee` (vertex/mesh position invariance), `51ecd693` (output-map write mask; no shader here has `omap` in its reflection), `ea0c98df` (queue dependencies / conditional state).
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000) black screen with sound on c78d7375 / chain 89f44f9b6bb0: the present pass pairs VS a5b1bd74e47458d7 (writes loc0 only) with FS 29e3c9dd92b8a571 (reads loc1/loc2)

body: hey I encountered a visual bug where the ground mist in hyrule fields turn white, according to the analysis light interaction with the mist gets divided by zero. claude ran a deep search and found the cause. a temporary fix worked with the latest shader from the current main ## Symptom Soft white clouds cover the grass and ground for 0.5–2 s at a time when walking back and forth between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field. A 2:32 recording showed six such bursts. It is the ground mist, not the grass. ## Setup - MacBook Pro M4 Pro, 24 GB, macOS 27.0.1, handheld mode, the game's own upscaler. - `0400486024DEC000` v131072. - Mac app from main `1794a35`, with these changes on top: - #1707, #1742, #1752; - #1245's host, with `ea0c98d` reverted; - main's `pso_manifest.tsv`. - Chain `058136f61e9e`. Checked against main `37f076a` (chain `39417042cfe8`) too; see *Main* below. ## Reproduction - A `DM_REC` recording, replayed from a copy of the save with `DM_KEYS=@rec.keys` and `DM_FRAME_DELTA=0`. - It shows the clouds at the same place in every run: about frames 1360–1590 and 2836–3264. ## What the host shows **The first non-finite pixels come from the mist pass.** - Tool: `DM_NVN_MAGSCAN=888c1068ac8f7043:1` (the mist composite). - In the first frame that has non-finite pixels, every earlier scanned colour attachment is clean. - The first pass with any is the mist draw (fragment `5ad65c0eefd09c7f`), in attachment 1: the half-resolution RGBA16F, about 15k pixels. - The composite `888c1068ac8f7043` then carries them into the RG11B10F scene target, about 64k pixels at 1120x630. - The bloom chain turns them into the white clouds. - In `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`'s PNGs, the scene's pure-black pixels lie almost all under the bloom's white areas: 56,262 of 56,370. NaN is assumed to show as black there. **Ruled out:** - **Pipelines built late:** the replay builds them synchronously, and the clouds remain. - **`-fmetal-math-mode=relaxed`:** with only this shader recompiled that way, the NaN remains. - **#1742's `frag_z` line:** reverted in this shader, the NaN remains. - **The fog volumes `128x72x96`:** finite, checked with `texraw` during the burst. - **The light records read from `fp_s4`:** finite. **The shader's own chain to the NaN.** - Method: - Flags were compiled into a replacement `5ad65c0eefd09c7f_b.metallib`, placed in `b-/` over the image. - A binary search then ran over the dependency cone of `out.m_78`, with one replay per step. - Steps, from the output back to the cause: 1. The first non-finite value at top level is `_703`, which comes from `_10184`, the light loop's accumulation. 2. That comes from the light direction `_9728`, computed for light types 2 and 100 as `(sample − light.pos) * rsqrt(d²)`. 3. The light distance `d²` is never 0 or denormal. The sample position `_731 / _733 / _735` itself is non-finite. 4. `_731 = _727 * _631` with **`_727 = 1.0 / _633`**, where **`_633 == 0.0` exactly**: - a flag on `_633 == 0.0` in the else branch lit in 28 of the scanned frames; - a flag on a denormal `_633` lit in none. - What `_633` is (read from the MSL, not measured): - `_633` (`_581`, `_565 = _535 + _384`) is the density-weight sum of the first march loop. - A sample is counted (`_503 = _372 + 1`, so `_629 > 0` and the else branch runs) even when its slab factors (`_515 = clamp(_513) * clamp(_509)`) make its weight `_535` zero. - With every sample weighted 0, the sum stays 0. The reciprocal is then inf, and `inf * 0` sample positions follow. ## Workaround (tested) One line in the MSL (line 901 of chain `058136f61e9e`'s `5ad65c0eefd09c7f_b.metal`): ```diff - float _727 = 1.0 / _633; + float _727 = (_633 == 0.0) ? 0.0 : (1.0 / _633); ``` - It was compiled with `MAC_METAL`'s flags and placed as `/Contents/Resources/msl/b-058136f61e9e/5ad65c0eefd09c7f_b.metallib` over the image. - Replay to frame 3300: **0 non-finite pixels** (MAGSCAN every 10 frames), against millions without it. - The white share in 8 screenshots of the bursts went from 16–59 % to 0 %. - The mist itself still draws. - Play-tested afterwards in normal play with the patch installed: no white clouds on the way between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field. ## Main - `877c7ec` (`dm_zsnap`) and `37f076a` (#1741) change this shader's MSL, but not this line. - I translated only `5ad65c0eefd09c7f` with main `37f076a`'s `dmsh_build.py` (chain `39417042cfe8`). Line 1107 is still `float _727 = 1.0 / _633;`. - #1824 (fetch clamp) changes a `tcb_C.read` that comes after this division (line ~977 here). Reading the code, it does not change `_633`. Not tested. ## Open - The division looks like the game's own: an unguarded reciprocal of the weight sum. The console then computes the same inf / NaN, yet the Switch 2 presumably shows no clouds (not checked against footage of this spot). Where the console loses the NaN is not known. - Candidates: - how NaN is written to the RGBA16F mist target (the mist draw blends: blend mask `0xff`); - the composite's sampling of it; - the RG11B10F scene write. - From the MSL: - The light accumulation (`_10178 = fma(_10174, _10148, _9616)`) is a plain `fma`. `AFmz` emits a select whenever `.FMZ` is set, so that FFMA has no `.FMZ`, and "0 × NaN = 0" there is not the console's escape. - The light type 1 branch compares through `isnan(_9794) || isnan(_9800)`, so the game expects NaN at that point. Types 2 and 100, where the NaN shows here, have no such guard. - Also seen, not followed: one frame at a scene load (F1161) had every pixel of the 1440x810 scene non-finite after the composite.
title: Ocarina of Time (Mac): white clouds over the ground mist on the way between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field. The mist shader `5ad65c0eefd09c7f` divides by its zero density sum, and the bloom spreads the NaN

### What happened

On a 16 GB MacBook Air (M4, `Mac16,13`, macOS 27.0.1), Ocarina of Time v131072 built from `main` at `c78d7375` (which includes `04419bc2`, full resolution with dynamic resolution) stutters badly in Hyrule Field near the castle: frame time p50 33 ms but p95 ~99 ms, max ~143 ms, at a 30 fps target. **Setup:** Mac Studio M3 Ultra, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, Mac app built at commit c78d7375bea9 (shader chain 89f44f9b6bb0), Docked, full resolution (Dynamic resolution off), game's upscaler and MetalFX alike.

**Symptom:** flickering black/dark single-pixel speckles inside fog (Kokiri Forest), at different places every frame. They were also present on the build before 04419bc.

### Bisect
- `DM_NVN_CS_HOIST=0`, `DM_NVN_XV=0`, `DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=all`, `DM_NVN_ZSKIP=0`: speckles remain.
- `DM_NVN_MAGSCAN`: no non-finite pixels in any pass.
- `DM_NVN_SKIP_FS`: `888c1068ac8f7043` (fog composite) → gone; `2ac31180e0534a97` (EftLoc_KokiriForest_MidFog_03) → remain; `5ad65c0eefd09c7f` → gone.
- `DM_NVN_DEPTHOVR=5ad65c0eefd09c7f`: speckles remain, so the attachment depth test is not the cause.

### Raw dump (`DM_NVN_SNAPRAW=1`)
In the 768×432 RGBA16F fog target (c1 of the `5ad65c0e` pass), 2,431 pixels keep exactly the clear value (0,0,0,1) inside fogged areas, single pixels and short 2–4 px axis-aligned runs, all finite. Nothing was written there.

### Mechanism
The fog is drawn twice per frame:
1. Task `efaa4fa6a80ba719`, mesh `3500af98dd8372cb`, fragment `4757b5b373a5406e`: depth only into a 768×432 D32F target (LEQUAL, cleared to 1).
2. Task `efaa4fa6a80ba719`, mesh `066f5daf12e43c71`, fragment `5ad65c0eefd09c7f`: samples that depth texture (reg1, nearest, at FragCoord) and `discard`s when `gl_FragCoord.z > depth` (FTZ compare). So only the front fog layer is shaded.

This relies on both mesh pipelines producing bit-identical depth for the same triangle. On the Mac they occasionally don't.

### Overlay experiments
Patched libraries via `DM_MSL_DIR`, confirmed loaded in the log:
- Both meshes compiled with `-fmetal-math-mode=safe`, no other change: **speckles remain**. Fast-math reassociation alone is not the cause.
- In `3500af98…_b.metal`, `v.position.z = fma(v.position.z, 0.5, v.position.w * 0.5) + v.position.w * 1e-5;` (pre-pass depth pushed back by 1e-5 NDC): **speckles gone**, with `DM_PSO_MTL4` on and off.

### Notes
The position math of the two meshes is the same FFMA sequence, but each mesh writes its vertices through stage memory (threadgroup) before `set_vertex`, so `[[position, invariant]]` cannot tie the two pipelines' computations together. This looks like the same family as "Position invariance across shaders" (foliage pre-pass + EQUAL), but here it survives `-fpreserve-invariance` and safe math. Possible fixes: a depth bias on this pre-pass (per profile), or a general look at whether two mesh pipelines rasterize identical vertices to identical depth on Apple GPUs. Happy to run further tests.

The attached `scripts/bug_report.py` zip was made after the workaround was in place: its `env.txt` and latest log are from a run with the patched pre-pass overlay (`DM_MSL_DIR`), i.e. without speckles.

[nxnative-bugreport-ocarina.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34545776/nxnative-bugreport-ocarina.zip)
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072, Mac M3 Ultra): flickering dark speckles in fog: the fog pass discards pixels whose depth comes out a hair above its own depth pre-pass

body:
# Crash: `-[NvPkg buffer]: unrecognized selector` in `tex_by_id` while encoding a draw

**Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072, standalone update NUP)
**Platform:** Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), ad-hoc signed, 33.5 GB
**Hardware:** MacBook Air M5, 10-core CPU / 8-core GPU, 16 GB, macOS 26.6.2
**Build:** shader chain `dc815e0f38ca`, package archive `applegpu_g17g` (3.2 GB), profile `tex_release 2`
**Frequency:** 2 of 2 sessions, both after several minutes of play

## Symptom

The host aborts with SIGABRT (exit 134). The uncaught exception is identical in both sessions:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException',
    reason: '-[NvPkg buffer]: unrecognized selector sent to instance 0x945c055e0'
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

## Stack

```
abort
  _ZL15_objc_terminatev
  objc_exception_throw
  __forwarding__ / doesNotRecognizeSelector:
  tex_by_id+0x374
  pool_entry+0x194
  pool_gpu+0x308
  encode_args_+0x2514
  encode_args+0xd4
  draw_+0x6de8
  draw+0xc0
  mtl_exec+0xfa0 (x3)
  h_nvnQueueSubmitCommands+0x1e4
  main+0x570358
```

## Cause

`tex_by_id` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`) takes the base texture with `treg_tex(rp)` and then sends `buffer` to it:

```objc
id<MTLTexture> base = treg_tex(rp);
if (!base) { ... return nil; }
v = base;
...
if (!base.buffer) for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) if (fsw[c] >= MTLTextureSwizzleRed) fsw[c] = (uint8_t)(MTLTextureSwizzleRed + c);
```

`base` is expected to be an `MTLTexture`. Here it is an `NvPkg` (the host's packaged-texture object, `nvn_mtl.m:2303`), which has no `buffer` method, so the message raises `NSInvalidArgumentException` and the process aborts.

`treg_tex` is `r->gone ? tex_made(&r->t) : tex_mtl(&r->t)`, and `tex_made` does:

```objc
id have = tex_get(t->serial);
if ([have isKindOfClass:[NvPkg class]]) { NvPkg *pk = have; return pk->view ? pk->view : pk->tex; }
return have;
```

So an `NvPkg` reaching `tex_by_id` means the lookup returned the package object itself instead of its `tex` / `view`.

## Correlation with the save commit

In the second session the exception is thrown on the line right after the save commit:

```
[dm] save commit #6: .../save.work swapped atomically into .../save
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException' ...
```

The first session had 5 commits and the last logged lines before the exception are texture view upgrades:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] texture upgraded to allow image writes ser=1176686 base format 70 -> view format 53 (upgrades=1054)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] texture upgraded to allow image writes ser=1176684 base format 93 -> view format 93 (upgrades=1055)
*** Terminating app ...
```

Note the game's save thumbnail is a copy of a texture to a buffer (`caption.sav`, see the profile README "Saves"), which may explain why the draw-argument path that fails is the one used around a commit.

Immediately before both crashes the log also shows, for `tex_release 2`:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] texture made again over released storage ser=477419 768x768 format 0x4b 771 KB:
     no host texture: reads the released zero pages (12 copied, 3 not)
```

## Measurements at the crash

| Session | `tex_release` | frame | wall | footprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 (profile) | 27,300 | ~455 s | 9,439 MiB |
| 2 | 1 (`DM_TEX_RELEASE=1`) | 19,500 | ~518 s | 10,143 MiB |

## Tried, did not help

- `DM_TEX_RELEASE=1` (fewer pools released): crashed again, with a higher footprint and earlier.
- Memory pressure does not look like the cause; the two runs differ in footprint but the exception is identical.

## Related

- #1467 (`obj_is_tex`, the per-class `conformsToProtocol:@protocol(MTLTexture)` answer) notes that the serial table holds `NvPkg` and a few texture classes. If a check that treats a table object as a texture answers per class, an `NvPkg` can reach a call that sends texture selectors.
- #1473 (`tex_mtl`, `tex_by_id` and `rp_begin_ex` return unretained) describes the same three functions' return paths; this build predates it (`tex_by_id_raw` is absent), so it is not the cause here.

## Suggested fix

Guard the base object's class before using texture selectors, or make the lookup return `pk->tex` / `pk->view` in every path that can hand an `NvPkg` to `tex_by_id`. `tex_made` already unwraps the package; the path that does not is the one that aborts.
title: Ocarina of Time (Mac app): abort on [NvPkg buffer] unrecognized selector in tex_by_id, right after a save commit

```
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

The thread that aborts is the game's own worker `bake::ModuleMgr` (priority 55, created at tick 0, CPU 0.05 s); it is running, not waiting, at the dump.

A few frames earlier there is also a red line that may or may not be related:

```
[nvn-mtl] [RED] texture type mismatch: shader 9808aabbd3219e97_b (stage 1) declares slot 1 as Metal type 2, texture ID 10847 is type 7 (NVN target 2, format 0x3f, Metal format 92); bound as is
```

Before the crash the run was healthy: `on-screen up to frame 1200: 300 frames, dropped 0, p99 16.67 ms; footprint 4417 MiB`, 60 fps.

Note: the docs entry "ReadTexels on a texture of a sparse pool" says the #471 fix keeps the `up_owner_check` abort on purpose ("a texture upload on another thread is still a bug to find"). This crash reaches `tex_mtl_` → `pkg_upload` on a game thread, so `mtl_read_texels` still needs an upload for this texture instead of reading it from its storage.

### What you expected

Entering the shrine works. `ReadTexels` on a game thread should read the texture from its storage (or hand the upload to the submit thread) without aborting.

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, `0100F2C0115B6000`, update 1.4.3 (v720896), no DLC.

stitch. (`010025801CEA8000`, update 1.2 / v65536, Unity 6000.0.68f1, SDK 21.4.4, NVN) plays on a provisional profile from origin/main c78d7375, on the Mac and on an iPhone 17 Pro. Taps and drags work. Docked mode turns touch off, as the game does on the Switch, so it is played handheld. It runs at 60 fps. I wanted a 30 fps choice for power, and found two things before writing any code. I'd like to know the direction you prefer.

### 1. `unity_fps.py` finds no internal-call table on this build

`unity_fps.py main` prints `no Unity internal-call table`.

- The names are in `.rodata`: `UnityEngine.Application::set_targetFrameRate` at main+0x25e4a79, `UnityEngine.QualitySettings::get_vSyncCount` at main+0x2649681.
- Nothing points at either of them. There is no relocated pointer, no `adrp`+`add` or `adr`, and no 32-bit relative offset.
- A block of 16-bit values sits just before the name block (around main+0x25bdee4). 6000.0.68 seems to register its calls from a compact table instead of the pointer pairs the tool reads (6000.0.64f1 on The Rogue Prince of Persia).

### 2. The NVN device takes the vsync count only when it is created

Writing the quality level's `vSyncCount` (the Unity path of `hle_fpslock.c`) would not change this game's rate:

- **At creation.** main+0x7db564..94 reads the current quality level's `vSyncCount`, at `[[QS]+0x20] + [[QS]+0x64] * 0x100 + 0x88`, the same layout as Rogue Prince's (QS from `GetManagerFromContext(11)`). It stores `max(count, 1)` into a global, main+0x32014ac.
- **The window.** main+0x7f42a0 passes that global to `nvnWindowBuilderSetPresentInterval`. The game fetches that function by name at main+0x16911d8.
- **No later change.** The game never calls `nvnWindowSetPresentInterval`: the host logs no "the game sets present interval" line.
- **Probes.**
  - At creation, the level's count is 0: `DM_PROBE=main:7db58c` shows `w8 = 0`. So the window gets interval 1.
  - Later, quality level 1 holds `vSyncCount 2`. But it never reaches the device: there were no hits on the quality apply (main+0x1002ea4, main+0x1002efc) or on the device's own vsync setter (main+0x7e3954, which writes the same global).
  - A script call `QualitySettings.set_vSyncCount(2)` returns early at main+0x1003944, because the level already holds 2.
  - `Application.targetFrameRate = 30`, which the game sets itself at frame 4 (`DM_PROBE main:213eff0`), does not change the rate either.

**Experiment.** I changed one instruction in a local `patches.py` (build `8e3517b0…`): main+0x7db590 `csinc w8, w8, wzr, gt` → `mov w8, #2`. Results:

- The host logs `present interval set by the game 2`.
- On the Mac (M5 Max, macOS 27.2), frame time was p50 33.33 / p95 33.38 ms over 1,800 frames. A scripted `drag` still advanced the tutorial from 1/8 to 2/8.
- On the iPhone 17 Pro, frame time was p50 33.34 ms. CPU energy dropped from 0.60 W to 0.39 W and CPU use from 19% to 13% against the same app at 60 fps.
- Unity steps by frame time, so the game keeps its real speed.

This is only a build-gated proof, not something to ship.

### Questions

1. Would you take a **Frame rate 30 / 60** choice for Unity NVN games that sets the device's count at creation, with the game's own rate as the default?
   - The count could be found without a build ID: it is the global loaded right before the call through the pointer the game fetched for `nvnWindowBuilderSetPresentInterval`.
   - Or would you rather the host apply the choice in its `nvnWindowBuilderSetPresentInterval`, although Unity's own frame wait reads the same global?
2. Should `unity_fps.py` learn 6000.0.68's table anyway, for `targetFrameRate` and the other settings? Or is the device global the better hook for this Unity line?
3. Separately, would a **stitch. profile PR** be welcome? It would be the profile, the note and the games-table row, tested on the Mac and an iPhone 17 Pro, without the 30 fps cut.

Not checked: other Unity 6000.0.6x games, and whether 6000.0.64f1 (Rogue Prince) creates its device the same way.
title: Unity 6000.0.68f1 (stitch.): the NVN device takes vSyncCount once at creation, and unity_fps.py finds no internal-call table — direction for a 30 fps choice?

**What happens**

With engine pin `f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1` (NX2Apple 1.3.0-rc5, chain `1d619d0f520b`) the AV1 movie corruption of #1528 is gone, but about 94 s into play (frame 5375) one command buffer fails with a GPU address fault, and the run ends in the #1788 way: at frame 16481 the Metal 4 command queue fails every submission with `MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain error 1` and the host exits 70.

Three address faults are reported before the queue dies (`1 failed of 37426`, `2 failed of 76110`, `3 failed of 78384` command buffers); the game keeps drawing between them. This looks like #1737 (one command buffer, the game survives) escalating into #1326/#1788 (hang, GPU access revoked).

**Environment**

- Mac: Apple M2 Max, 38-core GPU, 32 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123), built-in Liquid Retina XDR, 2992x1878 fullscreen
- App: NX2Apple 1.3.0-rc5, engine_id `f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1-c65b42ce7e50`
- Game: `0400486024DEC000` v131072 (Switch 2), Mac app built from the game's 25.6 GB NUP; 42,848 shaders built for chain `1d619d0f520b`
- Settings at the time: `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`, `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, `DM_LANG=zh-Hans`
- No other GPU-heavy app running; resident 8004 MB, GPU allocated 10079 MB at frame 5400

**The log** (`~/Desktop/games/log/0400486024DEC000.log`, 2 MB; excerpts, paths shortened, long shader lists cut)

The first fault, frame 5375, fence 32378 segment 9, right after two pools were rebuilt with textures that "have no storage (memory pool finalized or gone)", and a frame with 465 first texture uploads / 198.7 MB:

## What

`0100AC101BFA2000` Fit Boxing 3 -Your パーソナルトレーナー-, Unity IL2CPP, SDK 17. Base `.xci` + update v1.3.0 (v524288) + three DLC. No profile in the repository, so `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` wrote a provisional one from the survey (`profile_guess.py`) and built a Mac app: 4.4 GB, all six verify checks pass, 8,874 shaders, chain `1d619d0f520b`.

It boots and plays. The tutorial runs to the end and the game writes its saves (`ExerciseLogData`, `UserTutorialData`, `UserAchievementData`, `UserPlayRecord`). Then it aborts.

## Where

```
game called nn::diag abort: Result 0, call site sdk+0x13b2b8
bt: sdk+0x13b2b8 sdk+0x135608 main+0x7a068c main+0x7ca340 main+0x79a688 main+0x578dd04 main+0x5b50cc main+0x7d8b44 main+0x79a9f0 main+0x7ca49c main+0x7a054c main+0x7a0cf4 sdk+0x1357a0 sdk+0x13b6a4 dm_thread_enter+0x18
FATAL game aborted
CRASH sig=6
```

Decoded with `nso2elf.py` plus the `JUMP_SLOT` / `RELA` entries (the ELF has no section headers, so this came out of `PT_DYNAMIC` by hand):

| Address | Is |
|---|---|
| `main+0x7a0688` | `bl` to `nn::os::CreateThread(ThreadType*, func, arg, void*, size_t, int, int)` |
| `sdk+0x135604` | `bl` to `nn::os::detail::ThreadManagerImplByHorizon::MapAliasStack(void**, void const*, size_t)` |
| `sdk+0x13b2b4` | `bl` to `nn::diag::detail::AbortImpl()`, so the call site `sdk+0x13b2b8` is that call's return address |
| inside it | `bl` to `nn::os::detail::StackGuardManager::MapAtRandomAddress(...)`, whose result 1 goes through `cmp w0, #1` / `b.ne` into `AbortImpl` |

So a thread is created, `MapAliasStack` asks for a random address for its stack in the alias region, and that lookup gives up.

## SVC trace before the abort (`DM_SVC=1`)

```
MapPhysicalMemory 0x70e4040000+0x840000
MapMemory 0x702646b000 <- 0x70e4046000 +0x800000
MapPhysicalMemory 0x70e3840000+0x840000
MapMemory 0x701d9c7000 <- 0x70e3846000 +0x800000
MapPhysicalMemory 0x70e3040000+0x840000
game called nn::diag abort
```

8 MB stacks, so these are Unity's workers. The two `MapPhysicalMemory` / `MapMemory` pairs before it returned 0. The third `MapPhysicalMemory` returned 0 too, then no `MapMemory` follows.

## Two sessions, same abort

| Session | Reached | Threads created | Alias mapped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 269.76 s, frame 16,079 | 571 | 5.00 GB deepest |
| 2 (`DM_SVC=1`) | 20 s | 221 | 0.75 GB |

Same abort line and the same `bt` both times, at very different thread counts, so it is not a count that runs out.

## What it does not look like

- **Not the alias region filling up.** It aborted with 0.75 GB mapped in the second session, and the first session's deepest address was `+5.00 GB` in 64 GB.
- **Not a refused SVC.** `case 0x04` logs `[RED] MapMemory refused (%#x)` for every refusal, and `case 0x2C` logs `SVC %#x outside the alias region` for range refusals. Neither line appears in either session.

## Profile it ran on

```
mem_reserve	0x140000000
mem_alias	0x118000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0xCD500000
```

## Question

Is `MapAliasStack` failing to find a random address here something the profile's `mem_stack` can explain, or does the host's `QueryMemory` answer for a free range inside the alias region (`hle_svc.c` case 0x06) make the SDK's range check reject every candidate? I did not patch anything; both sessions are stock `1794a35a` with the classic builder.

Happy to run a build with whatever probe helps, or to hand over the `DM_SVC=1` log (1,300 lines, ends at the abort) if it is useful.
title: Fit Boxing 3 (0100AC101BFA2000, Unity, SDK 17): nn::os::CreateThread aborts in MapAliasStack, the random stack address fails on a provisional profile

### What happened

Since ea0c98df ("Honor NVN queue dependencies…"), DRAGON BALL Sparking! ZERO stops presenting frames right after the title screen. It happens every time, at the first load after pressing A at the title.

- **iPad mini (A17 Pro), unsigned IPA:** the screen goes black, sound keeps playing and the overlay shows 0 fps. After about a minute the game aborts itself with Unreal's `LowLevelFatalError`, which is UE's GPU-hang handling.
- **Mac (`--platform mac`), same save, `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0xC8000000`:** the same stall. `DM_HITCH_DUMP=4000:30` reports `no present for 4001.0 ms`, and the game never recovers.

The stuck threads in the hitch dump:

```
'RHIInterruptThread' at: __psynch_cvwait _pthread_cond_wait nvn_sync_wait h_nvnSyncWait dm_bigstack_ret main+0x42c85ac main+0x42e73a4 main+0x1e52b5c ...
'RenderThread 0'     at: ... svc_thread svc_dispatch gate_dispatch sdk+0x123678 main+0x1e512b0 main+0x1eb8084 main+0x1e5da44 main+0x35ad90 main+0x42d5ac8 ...
'RHIThread'          at: ... svc_thread svc_dispatch gate_dispatch sdk+0x123678 main+0x1e512b0 main+0x1e5e590 main+0x1e5de94 main+0x2611758 ...
'GameThread'         at: __psynch_mutexwait ... _pthread_cond_wait block svc_thread sdk+0x12378c main+0x1e512a0 main+0x2600538 ...
```

`RHIInterruptThread` waits in `nvnSyncWait` → `nvn_sync_wait` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_queue.inc`) on a sync whose queue job is never encoded. The render thread waits on the interrupt thread, and the game thread waits on the render thread.

Bisect and checks (Mac, same route):

- `git revert --no-commit ea0c98df` on 1794a35a: the hang is gone. The route reaches the tutorial battle at 60 fps, and the scene draws correctly.
- 1794a35a with only the `nvn_queue.inc` hunk of 04419bc2 applied (the WRITE-signal release at encode): still hangs at the same place, with the same stacks. That change covers event waits, while this hang is a sync wait.
- These didn't change the result: `DM_FPS_TARGET=30`, no alias limit (Mac default), and leaving out one DLC.

The game ran on this route with f5f6d4b5 (the profile commit). ea0c98df landed about 8½ hours later, and its message notes that its regression reach was not measured yet.

### What you expected

The game loads into the battle, as it does with ea0c98df reverted.

### Game, title ID and version

DRAGON BALL Sparking! ZERO, 010035F022078000, update v327680, with DLC

### nxnative commit

1794a35a (official profile `dm/games/010035F022078000`), plus the `nvn_queue.inc` part of 04419bc2 for the second check

### Shader chain version

579d06bf3932

### How it was built and run

iPhone or iPad, unsigned IPA from build_ipa_from_nsp.py. Reproduced on the Mac with `--platform mac`, running the host from a terminal.

### Device and OS

iPad mini (A17 Pro); Mac: Apple M4 Max, macOS 27.0.1

### Settings and environment overrides

Mac run: `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0xC8000000 DM_FOCUS_KEEP=1 DM_HITCH_DUMP=4000:30 DM_AUDIO=0 DM_CTL=<file>` (the control file presses A at the notice and at the title). iPad: none.

### Logs

The stacks above are from the Mac hitch dump. I can attach the full host log or the iPad `log.txt` if you'd like them. They contain no game files.

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

# Fast Fusion (040041E0212AE000) — Black screen caused by incomplete shader map and Metal shader library

## Summary

Fast Fusion launched but displayed a black screen during gameplay. The issue was resolved by rebuilding the shader inventory, shader map, and Metal shader library using the complete shader scan rather than the incomplete shader data included in the original build.

The original build contained only **28 shader-map entries**, while a complete scan of the game's RomFS and main executable identified **2,976 shaders**.

After rebuilding and packaging the complete shader data, the game launched correctly and gameplay worked.

## Game information

- Game: Fast Fusion
- Title ID: `040041E0212AE000`
- Platform: Nintendo Switch game running through nxnative on macOS
- Graphics backend: Metal
- Original problem: Game launched, but the screen remained black.

## Root cause

The original packaged application used:

- Shader map containing only 28 entries.
- Old shader library chain: `844bf1a5ea8f`.
- Runtime reported 26 missing shader keys.
- Runtime also reported that a RED program had no vertex shader mapped.

A complete shader scan identified 2,976 shader entries, including:

- 1,398 vertex shaders
- 1,431 pixel shaders
- 85 compute shaders
- 31 mesh shaders
- 31 task shaders

All 26 shader keys reported missing by the original runtime were found in the complete shader inventory, with matching shader stages and source assets.

This strongly indicated that the original shader map and library were incomplete.

## How the issue was fixed

I performed a complete shader scan using the game's RomFS image and main executable.

The scan generated a complete shader inventory and associated pipeline data. I then rebuilt the Metal shader library and compiled the host against the matching shader profile.

The rebuilt shader library used:

- Shader chain: `094f939bfef9`
- Input stamp: `106b1084aa78`
- Shader map: 2,976 entries
- Metal library: `b-094f939bfef9.img`

I packaged a new application using the rebuilt host, complete shader map, matching Metal library, RomFS, and generated profile tables.

## Results

The rebuilt application successfully:

1. Launched without the original black screen.
2. Loaded the complete shader map.
3. Loaded the matching Metal shader library.
4. Started the game successfully.
5. Ran actual gameplay successfully.

The runtime log confirmed that the application was loading resources from the new test bundle and using the new shader chain.

## Suggested fix

Investigate why the original shader packaging/build process produced only 28 shader-map entries instead of the complete inventory.

The build process should ensure that:

1. The shader scanner processes all relevant shader sources in RomFS and the main executable, not just the NDSR subset.
2. All discovered shader stages are included in the generated shader map.
3. The Metal shader library is built from the same complete shader inventory.
4. The host, shader map, profile tables, and Metal library all use matching build inputs and chain identifiers.
5. The packaged application actually includes the generated shader map and library from the same build.

The important part is that the shader map and Metal library must be generated from the same complete shader inventory and remain synchronized.

## Additional information

The full Metal build reported 70 shader translation failures. Despite those failures, the rebuilt application successfully launched and ran gameplay. Those remaining failures may affect shaders used in other areas of the game and should be investigated separately.

I can provide the original and rebuilt runtime logs, shader-map comparison, and build details if needed.

**The rebuilt application works. The original black screen was resolved by using the complete shader inventory and a matching rebuilt Metal shader library.**
title: Fast Fusion (040041E0212AE000) — Black screen caused by incomplete shader map and Metal shader library

body:
## Summary

Ocarina of Time repeatedly spent 11–14 minutes on **Preparing shaders** on an M5 MacBook Air, recompiling **the same 7,131 render pipeline bases** on consecutive launches despite a persistent pipeline archive. The end-of-prewarm archive write failed with:

```text
[RED] pipeline archive: writing …/pso_archive/01073.mtl4a failed: Failed to generate machO:error: cannot write 'UNITS' database: MDB_MAP_FULL: Environment mapsize limit reached
[RED] pipeline archive: compaction left the old files (the flush failed)
```

Tracing the host's archive lifecycle points to an oversized consolidation capture: it combines newly compiled bases and recaptured archived bases into one serializer and suppresses intermediate flushes throughout prewarm. If that final write fails, the new bases in that period are not persisted either, and the same expensive work repeats on the next launch.

A local bounded-batch implementation completed consolidation successfully. The next launch prepared a slightly **larger** list in **3.84 seconds**, with **8** new render bases compiled instead of 7,131.

## Hardware, game and build

- **Mac:** MacBook Air, `Mac17,3`, Apple M5; 10 CPU cores (4 Super + 6 Efficiency), 10 GPU cores, **24 GB unified memory**.
- **OS:** macOS **27.0.1**, build **26A434**.
- **Display:** external **1920×1080** monitor, fullscreen.
- **Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, title ID `0400486024DEC000`, update `v131072`, packed from a NUP as a Mac app.
- **Reproduced host:** upstream commit **`bd979ced3ae6`**, shader chain **`3ee52af3ca18`**, all 42,848 translated game shaders built; bundled archive `applegpu_g17g.mtl4a`, about 4,720 MB.
- **Preparation:** 10 workers; Metal 4 pipelines and pipeline prebuild enabled. This concerns the ordinary list-driven prepare step, not a deliberate shader-chain rebuild at every launch.
- Final settings: `DM_OPMODE=1`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`, `DM_UPSCALER=game`, `DM_FULLSCREEN=1`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0`, `DM_METAL_HUD=0`.
- There was about **64 GiB free** on the volume during investigation. The reported error is Metal's database **map-size limit**, not an observed full-filesystem error.

The local patched build is based on `bd979ced3ae6`; its embedded commit line still names that revision. This is not a claim that the patched run was built from current main.

**Update after fetching current main:** upstream already addresses the unbounded-period cause in **`eed7c429`** (included in `c78d7375bea9`): it hands over periods at 2,000 captures, supports multiple consolidation periods, and falls back to the plain compiler when capture fails. The analysis below describes the reproduced **older build**, not a claim that main still has its unbounded-period behavior. Our measurements independently support the bounded-period approach. I have not run upstream's implementation on this hardware/cache. Any follow-up PR will preserve that newer implementation and cover only remaining complementary behavior/tests, rather than duplicate or replace it.

## Measured consecutive starts

These are the host's **prepare-step times**, not total time from clicking the app to gameplay. Archive opening and other startup work are separate. The lists grow as play encounters additional shaders/configurations; these are not identical-workload cold-cache benchmarks.

| Host / start | List entries | Prepare time | Render bases compiled | From archive | Reused in memory | Render specializations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original, earlier start | 33,596 | **840.03 s** (~14 min) | **7,131** | 2,720 | 620 | 10,471 |
| Original, following start | 35,743 | **706.50 s** (~11.8 min) | **7,131** | 3,246 | 680 | 11,057 |
| Local bounded-batch fix, first consolidation | 37,931 | **1,204.12 s** (~20 min) | **7,131** | 3,911 | 700 | 11,742 |
| Local fix, next warm start | 38,002 | **3.84 s** | **8** | **11,065** | 701 | 11,774 |

The first patched start **was not faster**: it still did the expensive preparation and consolidation. The improvement appeared on the following start, after its results were successfully saved. The warm-start measurement was taken after a normal save/quit and relaunch, without deleting the cache or rebuilding the shader chain.

Relevant successful-write and warm-start logs:

```text
pipeline archive: 128 new pipeline bases written to 01147.mtl4a (8.3 MB, 417 ms)
pipeline archive: 128 new pipeline bases written to 01148.mtl4a (9.5 MB, 421 ms)
pipeline archive: 128 new pipeline bases written to 01149.mtl4a (21.3 MB, 2101 ms)
...
pipeline prepare: 37931 lines (24227 shaders, 11742 render pipelines, 1962 compute pipelines) in 1204.12 s on 10 workers before the first frame, progress screen shown; bases 7131 compiled, 3911 from the archive, 700 reused; 11742 specializations
pipeline archive compacted: 596 files of bases with a vertex layout gave 2771 bases to bounded replacement files and were removed
```

The archive directory had **634 files** before that preparation and **116** after successful consolidation; 78 replacement files were recorded, with no failure marker remaining. A little additional gameplay brought the next launch to 118 files:

```text
pipeline archive …/pso_archive: 118 files (38 of bases without a vertex layout), 7373.1 MB, opened in 1974.3 ms
pipeline prepare: 38002 lines (24257 shaders, 11774 render pipelines, 1971 compute pipelines) in 3.84 s on 10 workers before the first frame, progress screen shown; bases 8 compiled, 11065 from the archive, 701 reused; 11774 specializations
compute pipelines so far: 1971 from the archive bundled with the app, 0 from this device's archive, 0 built (337.1 ms looking up, 0.0 ms building)
```

## Why the counter increases and the beginning appears instant

The progress counter is not a count of newly compiled shader binaries. It includes `S` shader-loading rows, `R` render-pipeline configurations and `C` compute pipelines from the bundled and device prewarm lists.

During investigation, the user list contained **35,741 unique rows**: 22,760 `S`, 11,057 `R`, and 1,924 `C`. There were no exact duplicate rows, and every recorded shader key matched the game's shader map. Of the first 6,176 entries in the combined list, **6,149 were shader-loading rows**. This explains why the initial thousands can complete almost immediately while later pipeline work is slow. Additional play legitimately adds entries; that growth alone does not explain recompiling the same thousands of bases.

## Relevant code path / failure mechanism

In `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`:

1. `pso4_init()` enables consolidation when more than `PSO_ARCH_COMPACT` (8) ordinary archive files exist.
2. `pso_build_ex()` recaptures prewarm archive hits from their original shader functions into the current capture period. Archive misses compile into that period too.
3. `arch_flush()` returns while consolidation and prewarm are active, deliberately retaining the entire capture in one serializer until prewarm ends.
4. `arch_write()` calls `serializeAsArchiveAndFlushToURL:error:` on the resulting dataset. Here it returned `MDB_MAP_FULL` for both `00997.mtl4a` and `01073.mtl4a` on consecutive original-host launches.
5. The old archives are correctly retained after the failed write. However, the new captures in the failed period are not saved for the next process, and the recovery marker is unlinked after the serialization call even when it returns failure. The next launch can retry the same oversized consolidation.

The exact internal Metal map-size ceiling is not established. Apple's public serializer API does not expose a map-size setting. An [Epic report describes the identical UNITS/MDB_MAP_FULL error](https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/metal-binaryarchive/2647805/4) with the older binary-archive API and suggests splitting inputs; that is supporting context, not proof of identical implementation details or a universal size threshold.

## Candidate fix and validation

The local implementation:

- Bounds each capture period to **128 capture reservations**, including concurrent compiles still under way, using a separate compiler/serializer per period; full periods can be saved during prewarm.
- Reopens serialized files before publication and keeps old files until all required replacement writes succeed.
- Keeps consolidation failure state across subsequent successful batch writes and retains the recovery marker on failure.
- Seals the replacement set after queued compute recaptures, without blocking the game's first frame on those background captures.
- Atomically records the completed replacement filenames in `compacted.tsv`. Otherwise the replacement shards would themselves exceed the old eight-file threshold and trigger consolidation again at every launch.
- Requires no cache deletion, shader rebuild, game-specific profile switch, or change to rendering semantics.

Targeted tests passed: **1,456 archive checks**, fresh-process seed/consolidate/verify tests with disk-built shaders, injected `MDB_MAP_FULL` followed by successful later writes, a held capture across batch handoff, warmup through both pipeline paths, stalled compiler, pending pipeline, bundle and serialized-key tests. The Mac host builds and documentation checks pass.

**Limitations:** this is one real-game/hardware validation, not a five-game regression result. The required LLVM/clang-tidy toolchain was unavailable locally. A count bound is not a guaranteed byte-size bound; exceptionally large captures can still fail, and adaptive splitting remains open. A persistent pipeline-to-archive lookup index is not implemented. I am preparing a focused PR separately.

## Related reports

- #1747 reports the **same serialization failure** and repeated preparation on an M4 Pro, but also a 309 s warm start with **zero** new render bases compiled. Its shader-loading / task-mesh observations may represent additional costs that this result does not establish as fixed. This issue isolates the lost-capture/consolidation failure with M5 measurements and a successful-save/warm-restart comparison.
- #342 concerns a different Metal **serialization crash** during consolidation; this reproduction is a returned database-capacity error, not that crash.
- #807 also mentions `MDB_MAP_FULL` at startup in Tears of the Kingdom; no claim is made here that this patch fixes its later shrine stalls.
title: Metal archive compaction hits MDB_MAP_FULL and repeatedly loses 7,131 prewarm bases (OoT, M5 Air)

## Summary
On macOS, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (title 0400486024DEC000, NUP v131072) crashes after a few minutes of play with a GPU Hang that makes macOS revoke the process's GPU access, so the game quits.

The Mac app log (`~/Library/Logs/nxnative/0400486024DEC000.prev.log`) shows:
- `MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=1` -> `Caused GPU Hang Error (00000003:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)`
- then `Error Code=5 Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)`
- `GPU access revoked: the display command buffer was ignored ... macOS runs none of this process's GPU work any more, so the game stops`

## Environment
- Mac: Mac14,12 (Apple M2 Pro)
- macOS: 26.6.2
- Xcode 27.2 (Build 27B52), metal 32023.922 (metalfe-32023.922.4)
- nxnative collector checkout: 51ecd693 (the app did not record its own build commit / shader chain)
- Saved choices: DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx, DM_METAL_HUD=1, DM_LANG=zh-Hans

## Build & run
Built with `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac-app` (full shader build, 42,850 shaders). Ran the produced .app. Changing the present upscaler to `metalfx` at runtime did **not** avoid the crash - it still hit the GPU hang.

## Reproduction
1. Launch the mac-app built from the v131072 NUP.
2. Play for roughly 9 minutes (~frame 16800).
3. The game quits with the GPU access revoked error above.

This is the GPU Hang / GPU access revoked crash class previously diagnosed as #1326. Logs and full device info are in the attached `nxnative-report-0400486024DEC000-2026-11-08.zip` (generated by `scripts/bug_report.py`).
title: [0400486024DEC000] Ocarina of Time (macOS): GPU Hang -> 'GPU access revoked', game quits

A device report for the new iPad mini with the A20 Pro (iPad19,1, 128 GB, iPadOS 27.2). I ran three Switch 2 / Switch games on main at 865cc35f.

**Setup**
- Each game was built with `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform ios --prepare-xcode` and installed through Xcode with development signing. The entitlements were Increased Memory Limit only, without Extended Virtual Addressing.
- **Memory:** the iPad mini gets about **12 GB of room to the memory limit**: `room to the memory limit 11.96–11.97 GB` in the `[mem] guest memory` line. On an iPhone 18 Pro with the same build it's 7.97 GB, so roughly 4 GB more per app.
- **Launcher:** Docked, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_METAL_HUD=1`. Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza also had `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`. Everything else was left at the defaults.

| | Mario Kart World (base v0) | Donkey Kong Bananza (v458752) | Tears of the Kingdom |
|---|---|---|---|
| memory pool / room | 9.00 / 11.97 GB → anonymous | 9.00 / 11.96 GB → anonymous | 3.21 / 11.96 GB → anonymous |
| session | ~10 min at 60; ~28.5 min with `DM_FPS=30` | ~15.5 min, of which ~1 min gameplay | ~90 min |
| end | background (60); **killed by iPadOS** (30) | background | background |
| frame rate | 60 with dips; steady 30 with `DM_FPS=30` | 45–60 | mostly 60, a ~15 min stretch at 33–38 |
| GPU time p50 | ~14 ms | ~13.5 ms | ~10.5–12 ms (12–15 in the slow stretch, p95 17–21) |
| footprint | 6.0 → 11.94 GB | 2.0 → 5.5 GB in 1 min | 2.4 → 5.4 GB |
| heat | thermal 1, never 2 | thermal 1 | thermal 1 at 344 s, never 2 in 90 min |

**Heat:** this was the main difference from the iPhone 18 Pro. With the same Mario Kart World build, the iPhone reached thermal 2 within minutes and its GPU time went from ~15 to ~34 ms. The iPad mini never reached thermal 2 in any of these sessions, including 90 minutes of TotK at 60 fps docked.

**Mario Kart World: memory despite the larger limit.** With a 9 GB pool and ~12 GB of room, main picks anonymous memory, not the guest file. In the 28.5 min session, Metal allocations grew from 6.1 to 9.5 GB and iPadOS ended the app with the footprint within ~50 MB of the limit. So the extra 4 GB isn't enough for a 9 GB title over a long session. Donkey Kong Bananza has the same 9 GB pool and was heading the same way: Metal grew from 1.4 to 4.0 GB in its first minute of play. I haven't run a long session of it yet. A margin in the guest-file decision (for example, files when pool + 4 GB > room) would cover both titles. `DM_GUEST_FILE=1` is my next test on this device.

**Donkey Kong Bananza, first start:** with no pipeline archive yet and the launcher's default `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1`, the 21,225-pair prebuild ran before the game's first frame. It took ~13.5 min on 5 workers, and the game drew its first frame at ~882 s. That's a long wait for a new user, maybe worth a note on the progress screen or an option to start the game while the prebuild continues. The archive it wrote (~1.6 GB) should make later starts quick. iPadOS also logged a `cpu_resource` report for `MTLCompilerService` during the prebuild, with no action taken.

**Tears of the Kingdom:** the best of the three. Memory peaked at 5.4 GB with 6.9 GB of room left, with no stalls over one second in 90 minutes. One `[RED]` line, a texture type mismatch (shader `9808aabbd3219e97_b`, slot 1).

Logs are available if useful.
title: iPad mini (A20 Pro, ~12 GB memory room): Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza and Tears of the Kingdom on main 865cc35f

body:
### What happened

One guest thread (priority 59) sat at **983 ms/s — a whole core — for the entire run**, with no underruns, no dropped frames and no `[RED]` line. The run was otherwise healthy at 60 fps.

The thread dumps (`DM_THREAD_DUMP`) show it `running/not waiting` with **163,922,328 SVCs in 35 s** (about 4.7 million a second), every one of them `WaitForAddress` (`svc 0x34`), `lr=sdk+0xc808e0`.

`DM_FUTEX_LOG` names the call:

```
[futex] t=0x1002 addr=0x10fe57a54 type=2 want=1 now=0x1 timeout=0 cond_held=1 blocked=1 r=0xea01
```

The condition holds (`value == 1`), the timeout is **0**, and the host returns `0xea01` (timeout) at once, so the thread polls again immediately.

The power line before the change:

```
power: CPU energy 4.00 W, 66.7 mJ per frame (60.0 fps); CPU 103%; thermal 1
```

### Cause

`dm/host/hle_thread.c`, the `WaitForAddress` case: `block(t, 3, poll_wait_begin((int64_t)regs[3]))`, and `block()` treats `ns == 0` as an immediate timeout (its comment says `ns<0 infinite, 0 immediate timeout`).

This game's engine calls `WaitForAddress` through the SDK's no-timeout form (`nn::os::WaitForAddress(const long*, long)`, SDK 19+), which passes **0** in x3. It expects to sleep until another thread signals the address. The host returned instead, so the engine's audio thread spun on a core.

### What was tried, and the result

A switch, `DM_FUTEX_WAIT0_INFINITE`, makes a zero timeout in this SVC block instead of returning:

```c
int64_t to = (int64_t)regs[3];
if (to == 0 && w0) to = -1;
```

With it on, the same thread reports `waits:address`, 958 SVCs in 16.5 s, and the game still runs at 60 fps with music and voices, no deadlock:

```
power: CPU energy 0.02 W, 0.3 mJ per frame (60.0 fps); CPU 31%; thermal 0
```

### Open question

I do not have Nintendo's documentation for `svcWaitForAddress`'s zero timeout. The evidence above says this title treats it as "no timeout", and the game behaves correctly when it blocks. Whether **0 means poll** for other titles is exactly what I cannot check here, which is why this is behind a switch rather than unconditional. If the semantics are confirmed, the switch could become the default (or the SVC could keep 0 as a poll and the SDK wrapper could pass −1, whichever matches Horizon).

### Verified on

- Title ID `01007ED02424E000` (base game; not in the supported games table).
- Source commit `b7dc7a9a` on top of `f8a5618d` (the `0 == immediate` behaviour is in `f8a5618d` too).
- iPad Pro M1, iPadOS 15.6, unsigned IPA built with `build_ipa.sh` (`DM_IOS_MIN=15.0`).
- No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.

### Note

Submitted with AI assistance: measurements are from the device above, the fix is behind a switch and nothing here has been reviewed by a person. Rewrite or ignore it if the maintainer prefers a different shape.
title: WaitForAddress with a zero timeout returns at once, so an engine that polls a lock spins a core

Environment

Hardware: MacBook Pro, M3 Max, 36 GB unified memory

Frontend: NX2Apple 1.3.0 RC3

NX2Apple-reported upstream revision: [f25fa956](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1)

Long-session runtime commit: Not recorded in log

Long-session shader chain: 1d619d0f520b

Game title ID: 0400486024DEC000

macOS version: 27.0

Build target: macOS native application

Graphics API: Metal

Display output: 2560 × 1440 in the initial windowed configuration

Final-image upscaling: MetalFX during the recorded long session

Gameplay Progress and Stability

I have successfully played from the beginning of the game through completion of the Forest Temple and Fire Temple, including the Phantom Ganon and Volvagia boss encounters.

No crashes or forced restarts occurred during gameplay. All sessions ended voluntarily.

A recorded gameplay session lasted approximately 5 hours and 37 minutes, with normal termination.

Despite graphical defects, all required gameplay progression has remained possible through completion of the Fire Temple.

Graphical Issues

1. Missing or Invisible Geometry

Certain Fire Temple platforms and surfaces were not rendered, although collision remained functional.

This made navigation difficult, particularly when attempting to reach the boss room. Initially, I believed I had missed a puzzle mechanic, but the required geometry was simply invisible.

2. Volvagia Boss Arena — Black Rendering Artifacts

During the Volvagia boss encounter, large black visual artifacts obscured significant portions of the arena.

The encounter remained functional, and I successfully defeated the boss, but visibility was substantially impaired.

3. Dynamic Resolution and Image Softness

The game becomes noticeably softer when looking toward complex environments.

Looking down at simpler geometry often produces a dramatically sharper image.

MetalFX final-image upscaling significantly improved perceived sharpness, although internal resolution fluctuations remained noticeable.

4. Improvements Between Engine Revisions

An earlier NX2Apple build reporting upstream [88c7e03f](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03) exhibited severe lighting problems and missing terrain.

Updating to the NX2Apple build reporting [f25fa956](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/f25fa9562ee96d06f1e6412dbb91aab2b7035ec1) substantially improved visual correctness and overall playability.

Performance

Overall gameplay has generally felt smooth on the M3 Max, with portions of the recorded session operating near 60 FPS.

The longer gameplay log provides actual timing data:

Recorded runtime: Approximately 5 hours, 37 minutes

Severe frame stall: Frame 736583 took approximately 2,243.8 ms

Submit/present time during that stall: Approximately 2,234.8 ms

GPU execution time during that stall: Approximately 27.5 ms

Shader compilation during that stall: None recorded

Peak recorded memory footprint: Approximately 17 GiB

The severe slowdown occurred during a session where I had experimented with upscaling settings. A direct causal relationship between those settings and the slowdown has not been established.

The substantial difference between CPU-side submission/presentation time and GPU execution time suggests that the worst stall warrants investigation beyond raw GPU rendering performance.

Additional Rendering Diagnostics

The attached log records repeated texture-type mismatch warnings.

Three distinct shaders appear to bind 3D textures to slots expecting 2D-array textures, with at least 202 binding events identified during log analysis.

These are potential rendering investigation leads, but there is currently no confirmed relationship between these warnings and the invisible Fire Temple geometry or black Volvagia artifacts.

The log also documents successful loading of GPU-specific pipeline archives and MetalFX spatial upscaling.

Summary

Ocarina of Time has remained playable through completion of the Fire Temple on an M3 Max with 36 GB unified memory.

Key observations:

No crashes or forced restarts

Over five hours of recorded gameplay in one session

Generally smooth performance, with intermittent severe frame-time stalls

Significant improvements from newer NX2Apple/nxnative builds

Missing geometry and black rendering artifacts remain problematic

No permanent progression blockers encountered so far

I am continuing through the remaining dungeons and can provide additional testing observations.

A detailed gameplay log is attached for investigation.
title: Ocarina of Time — Extended Gameplay Report (M3 Max, 36 GB, NX2Apple RC3)

body:
> Filed through the GitHub API, so the fields of the **Game request or bring-up report** form are reproduced as sections below. This is filed upstream only: the NX2Apple fork's `game_problem.yml` says the `fork patches` line decides where a report belongs, and this build's game log starts with `fork patches: none`. Full host logs are posted as a comment on this issue (the API cannot attach files).

## Game, title ID and version

**EA SPORTS FC 26**, base title ID `01004FF021942000`, US release. Base game `v0` + update `v1376256` (`1.87.2a1e`) + 1 DLC, all from one XCI.

Main build `e05f8f071e0ec7b38e6a42a55b0002c6`, sdk `a65883c2863f42f93e0f43f2d7aba0e8`, `nnSdk-19_3_3-Release` (major 19), confirmed by the runtime log. A separate `[UPD]` NSP of the same update was also present; adding the `[v1376256]` tag and rebuilding produced byte-identical extracted data, so it is not a factor.

## Engine and graphics API, if known

Frostbite (EA), reading `Data/layout.toc` / `Data/initfs_NX` superbundles and Oodle-compressed shaders in `CompiledBytecode` resources. NVN on Switch, translated to Metal by the host. The builder recognises the superbundles and decodes the shaders with the game's own Oodle decoder (`DM_OODLE_SERVE`, build-time only). The survey noted SDK 19 differs from the SDK 16 the host's NVN object layouts started from; `survey.md` itself is not attached (see the note at the end of this section).

## Survey and what happened

**There is no FC 26 profile in `dm/games`.** The build uses a provisional profile from `profile_guess.py`:

```
[14:39:20] no game profile for 01004FF021942000: reusing the provisional profile from the last run
[14:39:20] [RED] provisional game profile: values guessed from the survey, the game may not boot; bring it up per docs/agents after packing
[14:39:27] [RED] this Mac app was built from a provisional game profile and the game may not boot
```

`game.tsv` starts with `# Provisional game profile (generated ... from the survey with dm/games/profile_guess.py, not checked by hand)`. The only EA profile in `dm/games` is **FC 27** (`0100C49025D3E000`, SDK 22.2.0, update v393216), the result of a manual bring-up; it cannot be reused for an SDK 19.3.3 build.

**The build itself fully succeeds.** `01004FF021942000.app` (36.8 GB), 430-entry RomFS, 11,225 shaders extracted and 14,199 Metal shaders compiled, `Dependencies: all present`, both Metal compilers match the pin. So this is not a packing, extraction, toolchain or shader failure.

**Every run is 100% reproducible: the window opens and stays completely white.** No logo, no audio, no first frame. There is **no `[nvn] frame N` line and no `nvnDeviceGetInteger` / device-API line at all** — the game stalls before graphics device initialization. It is a hang, not a crash: no GPU fault, no `CRASH sig=`, the host process stays alive.

Key runtime lines:

```
[dm] sdk: NintendoSDK nnSdk-19_3_3-Release (major 19)
[dm] force: 389 entries hit, 857 not referenced by this game
[dm] >>> nninitStartup
[dm] [mem] heap 1.24 GB (heap region 1.25 GB)
[dm] fs open [0.14s] rom:/Scripts/BootIni/MemoryInit.ini mode=1 → image entry 90
[dm] [mem] alias region mapped up to +0.28 GB (alias region 64.00 GB)
[dm] >>> nnMain
[dm] front end: window visible
[dm] fs path not found: download:/LCU/layout.toc
[dm] fs path not found: download:/LCU/initfs_NX
[dm] fs stat not found: eadpsdk_rom:/eadpsdk.json
[dm] fs stat not found: eadpsdk_rom:/assets/eadpsdk.json
[dm] [RED] watchdog: no progress since second 8, stuck at tick 0 / stage startup
```

Thread dump at the stall:

```
thread 0x1005 'AssetStream::Load'      priority 42  waits:condvar  ... main+0x27a415c main+0x25faf98 main+0x192a754 ...
thread 0x1006 'AssetStream::Unpack'    priority 42  waits:condvar  ... main+0x27a50a4 main+0x25faf98 main+0x192a754 ...
thread 0x1007 'AssetStream::Translate' priority 44  waits:condvar  ... main+0x27a6760 main+0x25faf98 main+0x192a754 ...
thread 0x1002/1003/1004 NetLib / SocketRecv / SocketSend  exited at tick 0 (offline)
thread 0x1001 'main thread'  priority 59  CPU 7.8 s  svc 225,279,149  last svc 0x6 (svcQueryMemory)  waits:running/not waiting
    backtrace: sdk+0x9d1a0 sdk+0x9d134 sdk+0x9cfa8 sdk+0x9c4f4 main+0x1c21590 main+0x1c3ba24
              main+0x1b68b1c main+0x9088b6c main+0x907fa6c main+0x8945a8 ...
```

### Bring-up evidence from `DM_PROBE`

Following `docs/agents/03-bringup.md`, I rebuilt the host with the FC 26 provisional profile (`DM_GAMES_DIR=.../profile make -C dm/host GAME=01004FF021942000 dmhost`, 14 s, arm64). It reproduces the stall exactly, so this is not a stale build artifact.

`DM_PROBE=main:1c21590` installs but **never hits** — that address is only a return address on the stack. Probing the real execution point `DM_PROBE=sdk:9d1a0` hits immediately:

```
PROBE sdk+0x9d1a0 #1 [0.3274s] T=1001 x0=0x1 x2=0x1735d56dc x19=0x1735d5738
      x8=0x2000 x9=0x1000 lr=0x11aee91a0
bt: sdk+0x9d134 sdk+0x9cf6c sdk+0x9c4f4 main+0x1c21590 main+0x1c3ba24 ... guest_main+0x1ec
PROBE #2 x8=0x3000  /  #3 x8=0x4000  /  #4 x8=0x5000 ... #8 x8=0x9000
```

`x8` advances by exactly `0x1000` (one 4 KB page) per hit; `x0`/`x2`/`x19`/`lr` stay fixed. The object at `x19` is a table of `(address, 0x1000)` region records, reaching addresses around `0x4_af0d1000` by second 8. So the main thread is **walking the guest address space page by page through `svcQueryMemory`** during Frostbite startup, while the three `AssetStream` threads sit on condvars that are never signalled.

### Three observations that may matter for the fix

1. **The memory layout was never measured.** The provisional `game.tsv` says `mem_reserve 0x140000000` (5 GB), `mem_alias 0xd0000000` (3.25 GB), `app_pool 0xCD500000`, and contains the comment `heap check: 2026-11-08, the heap request did not fit; set mem_alias`. FC 27's hand-tuned profile uses 7 GB / 5.25 GB because Frostbite reserves 264 arenas, with the **same** `app_pool`. FC 26's profile also records that in its first 15 s in `nnMain` the game's regions reach `alias +0.48 GB`, matching the runtime line `alias region mapped up to +0.28 GB (alias region 64.00 GB)` — the guest keeps touching address space while stalled. `docs/reference/memory.md` documents a similar ~62 GB region from `nninitStartup` for another SDK 19.3.1 title, so a large virtual address region is known SDK 19 behaviour; what FC 26's page-walk expects from it is not.
2. Runtime profile overrides `DM_PROF_MEM_RESERVE=0x1c0000000` + `DM_PROF_MEM_ALIAS=0x150000000` (FC 27's values, applied at start, no rebuild) do **not** clear the stall. On the Mac the host reports a 64.00 GB alias region, so `mem_alias` is not obviously the limiter — but the FC 26 layout is still unmeasured.
3. `eadpsdk_rom:/eadpsdk.json` and `/assets/eadpsdk.json` are both missing, and `download:/LCU/*` paths fall back to `rom:/Patch` and `rom:/Data`. After those two stat misses there is no further filesystem activity for the rest of a 4-minute run. The offline EADP SDK path may be waiting on something the host does not provide.

**Explicitly NOT a defect:** the log's two `undefined weak _ZTHN2EA4Jobs8Internal... bound to 0` lines are Horizon rtld's expected behaviour (`dm/host/loader.c`, `bind_sym`; the same file cites Octopath Traveler 0's `_ZTHN13LowLevelTasks5FTask10ActiveTaskE` and warns that adding a stub makes the game call it). Checked so nobody spends time "fixing" it. `force: 389 entries hit` and `sdk: 47 bound to an earlier module's definition` are normal loader output too.

### A methodological correction, and the long run

Runs with `DM_WATCH_STALL=8` are terminated by the host's own watchdog (`crash.c`: `_exit(128 + SIGALRM)`) at second 8, so `no progress since second 8` is a diagnostic, not a spontaneous game exit. A **240-second run with no watchdog switches** was therefore done: the log ends at 89 lines with **zero `[RED]` lines, zero `[nvn] frame N` lines and zero presents**; after the two `eadpsdk.json` stat misses and `oe focus state → 2`, there is no further filesystem or graphics activity for the remaining four minutes. This is a **true hang, not slow startup**.

### Already ruled out (all reproduce the identical `tick 0 / stage startup` stall)

- Reinstalling / rebuilding: one rebuild was entirely `reused (inputs unchanged)` (the app's `dmhost` timestamp did not move); a forced rebuild with corrected update-NSP tagging succeeded with exit 0 and identical extracted data.
- Missing shaders / EA superbundles / update / DLC / keys / RomFS integrity: 430-entry RomFS mounts, `Patch/` and `Data/` `layout.toc` and `initfs_NX` open successfully.
- Missing dependencies or a wrong toolchain: `Copy diagnostics` reports `all present`.
- Runtime switches, each in a separate run: `DM_LANG=en-GB` (saved choice is `zh-Hans`, the game defaults to `en-GB`), `DM_PREEMPT=1`, `DM_DETCLOCK=1`, `DM_OPMODE=0`, `DM_FOCUS_KEEP=1`, `DM_METAL_HUD=1`, `DM_BOOTPROF=1`, `DM_HID_LOG=1`, `DM_NVN_API=53.313`, `DM_QOS_MAP=1`, `DM_PROF_MEM_RESERVE` + `DM_PROF_MEM_ALIAS`.
- Rebuilding the host from current sources with this game's profile (official bring-up step 1).
- No mods, no cheats (`[dm] cheats: ... no file for build E05F8F071E0EC7B3`).

**Note on `survey.md`:** the game folder was cleaned from disk after diagnosis, so the survey file itself is no longer available to attach. Its relevant conclusions (SDK 19.3.3, NVN, Frostbite superbundles, the SDK 16 → 19 object-layout caveat) are summarised above. All four host logs are posted verbatim as a comment instead, with local user names shortened to `~` and the `prod.keys` path redacted.

## Device and OS you would play on

Mac app (built for This Mac): **Apple M5, 16 GB RAM, arm64, macOS 27.3 (26C5035r)**, Xcode 27.2 (27B52), iOS SDK 27.2, Metal compiler 32023.922 (matches the pin). Front end: NX2Apple 1.2.3 (official release), engine `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03-46919438b5de`, shader chain `adec7d81d970`, Python 3.13.18, .NET 10.0.403. Built from my own legally dumped game files and keys; opened from Finder.

## No game files

- [x] **Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.**

Only host logs and the launcher's own diagnostics text are provided: no XCI/NSP/NCA/NSO, no RomFS contents, no `prod.keys` contents, no shader/metallib binaries, no build products.

## Related issues

- `seedds/nxnative#169` "Request: EA FC 25/26/27" — closed with **FC25/26 support remains unvalidated**; game-level issues were said to need separate tracking. This is that separate report.
- `seedds/nxnative#1750` / `LNPANDY/NX2Apple#923` — FC 27 first-screen freeze / GPU page fault on M5 + macOS 27.2, still open.
- `seedds/nxnative#1696` (PR, FIFA 23) — adds EA-specific shader archive parsing (BIG4 / EASF / NXSHADER). FC 26's shaders were already extracted successfully, so this does not look like the blocker.

## Request

Please consider a proper bring-up for FC 26 (`01004FF021942000`, update `v1376256`, SDK 19.3.3). The most useful first steps look like: identifying what the `svcQueryMemory` page-walk at `main+0x1c21590` is waiting for, checking SDK 19.3.3 `QueryMemory` / address-region behaviour against the host, measuring the real memory layout (the current one is a failed heap-check fallback), and checking whether the offline EADP SDK path needs a hook for the missing `eadpsdk.json`. Happy to run further probes and provide logs.
title: [Bring-up request] EA SPORTS FC 26 (01004FF021942000) hangs at tick 0 / startup on Mac — provisional profile, no frame ever submitted

body:
### What happened

I rebuilt Nintendo Switch Sports Resort from an extracted dump containing `base/` and `updates/65536/` using the local nxnative checkout and `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<dump folder>" --platform mac-app`. The checkout had no registered profile for this title, so the script generated a provisional profile.

With a clean shader cache, **11,053 of 11,059 Mac shaders compiled successfully. Six failed at the mesh stage.** The log groups the six failures under “shared memory of its own, or stage memory past Metal's limit.”

### GPU pipeline archive

- On the previous attempt, offline pipeline archive compilation ran for **over eight hours without completing**.
- On this run, `metal-tt` queued 10,783 graphics pipeline bases and 291 compute pipelines for `applegpu_g13s`. I manually stopped the GPU compiler after 22 minutes while it was still on batch 1 of 30. The packer then produced the Mac app without the offline archive.

### Startup crash

The packaged Mac app crashes on launch before reaching gameplay. Two consecutive launch logs show the same guest fault and host exit status. The latest run logged that the window was visible before the crash.

```text
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x150 pc=main+0x9d7c60 lr=main+0x9d7c08
[dm] bt: main+0x9d8f90 main+0x55b2ec main+0x67f15c main+0x67ea70 main+0x681e14 main+0x33c750 main+0x33ceac main+0x33cde0 main+0xb122b4 main+0x1cd318 guest_main+0x1ec
launcher: the host exited with 139
```

The relationship between this crash and the shader or pipeline archive failures is unknown.

### Build details

- Game — Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (`04008E001F098000`), update `v65536`, no DLC
- nxnative commit — `eed7c4295853a22045e28ef60b3c1aba609e160e`
- Shader chain — `094f939bfef9`
- Device — Apple M1 Pro, macOS 27.2 (`26B123`), Xcode 27.2 (`27B52`)

### Logs

```text
Mac shaders (31:31): 11,053 of 11,059 shaders ready (0 from the cache); 6 failed
shaders 11059: ok 11053, mesh stage failed 6
  [mesh stage failed]     6  shared memory of its own, or stage memory past Metal's limit
pso_offline: applegpu_g13s: metal-tt, 10783 bases, 291 compute pipelines (minutes) ...
```

body: ## What happened I built EA SPORTS FC 27 for macOS using NX2Apple. The build completed successfully, and the generated `.app` launches and displays the initial game screen. However, the screen then stops updating, and I cannot proceed to the main menu. The runtime log records a GPU Page Fault at submission `fence=94`, with the failed submission state reporting `frame 89`. The next submission, `fence=95`, also faults. Subsequent rendering and display command buffers report `SubmissionsIgnored`. ## Expected behavior The game should continue through startup and reach the main menu without GPU faults or a frozen screen. ## Game and build information | Item | Value | | --- | --- | | Game | EA SPORTS FC 27 | | Title ID | `0100C49025D3E000` | | Main build ID, first 16 hex digits | `570DC9F1750FA7EA` | | Game display version | Tentatively identified as `1.8d.6523` from a matching build ID; not yet confirmed from the package metadata | | Build method | Mac `.app` built through NX2Apple | | Device / GPU | Apple M4 Pro | | macOS version | [Fill in] | | NX2Apple version | [Fill in] | | Xcode version | [Fill in] | | nxnative commit | The runtime log says `commit not recorded` | | Shader chain | `adec7d81d970` | | Metal compiler reported in the log | `32023.922` | | Nintendo SDK | `nnSdk-22_2_0-Release` | | NVN API | `55.15` | | Fork patches reported by the launcher | `none` | The tentative display-version identification comes from [this report with the same build ID](https://gbatemp.net/threads/fpslocker-ea-sports-fc-27-switch-60-fps-patch-for-v1-8d-6523.686239/). ## Difference from the registered game build The current [FC27 profile](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/dm/games/0100C49025D3E000/game.tsv) registers: - Display version: `1.8d.310c` - Package version: `v393216` - Main build ID: `a48c0de3bc353efa0e4d359bde05ef24` My main build ID is different. I do not know whether that difference is related to the GPU fault. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Build FC27 as a Mac app through NX2Apple using the game build identified above. 2. Launch the generated app. 3. Wait for the initial game screen. 4. The picture stops updating, and the log reports GPU Page Faults followed by ignored submissions. Reproduction frequency: [Every launch / intermittent — please specify]. ## Relevant log excerpts Build metadata: ```text [dm] build: commit not recorded, shader chain adec7d81d970, profile 0100C49025D3E000 ``` First underlying GPU error: ```text Caused GPU Address Fault Error (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault) ``` Failed submission state: ```text [dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] state of the failed submission fence=94: frame 89; since the last submission: passes +14, first texture uploads +0, re-uploads +0, serial table changes +0; deferred-release queue 0 ``` Shaders listed in the first failed command buffer: ```text 8f294518dc3892b9_b 190387905fb193e4_b 3ea91659e0281eb9_b 7b5f4966f12f0d08_b 77fb662292697f64_b c9444ca2e8b2df0d_b ``` After the two Page Faults, subsequent submissions and the display command buffer report: ```text Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors) (00000004:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored) ``` ## Settings and additional observations The following are recorded in the failing run: - Present upscaling: `off, bilinear`. - Present snapshots: off. - Frostbite simulation settings are changed from 30 to 60 by the game profile. - The pipeline archive opens in approximately `54.6 ms`, and preparation of the recorded prewarm rows completes in approximately `0.03 s`. - The window has regained focus and is visible before the first GPU fault. - Audio callbacks continue to appear in the log after graphics submissions are ignored. The complete settings and environment overrides still need to be included from NX2Apple diagnostics. Is this game build expected to work with the current FC27 profile?
