body:
### What is missing

nxnative currently exposes a single local account (`hle_account.c`: one fixed `Uid`, `GetUserCount` always 1) and one active save tree per title:

`~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/<title-id>/save/`

Two people on the same Mac (or two playthroughs) therefore share that folder. In-game slots help for progress files, but shared files such as `option.sav` / `account.sav` still collide (settings, motion options, etc.).

There is also no UI to pick a **named save profile** in the Mac launch window (or on iOS). The only workaround today is renaming folders by hand or scripting `DM_SAVE` / copying `save/` while the game is quit — which forces a full cold start each time someone switches, and title load time is already long for large Switch 2 games.

### What you propose

**In the Mac settings / launch window (and ideally iOS launcher):**

1. A **Save profile** control: list existing named profiles, create new, rename/delete.
2. On Play: use that profile's save directory (e.g. `…/nxnative/<title-id>/profiles/<name>/save` or swap into the current `save/` with a `CURRENT` marker), and set `DM_NICK` from the profile name if unset.
3. **Nice to have — switch while the host is running** (or without tearing down the whole Metal/shader warm state): remount / swap the save transaction to another profile after a safe flush, so players avoid a multi‑minute reload. If live remount is hard, a lighter path would be: quit only the guest, keep the host/process warm, remount save, re-enter `nnMain` — still much better than relaunching the `.app` from cold.

**Scope notes (for agreement):** this is a front-end + `DM_SAVE` / account-nick convenience feature, not real Horizon multi-user. Cloud saves (`DM_SAVE_SYNC`) should key off the active profile so two profiles do not overwrite one `save.dmsync`.

### Workaround script (external)

Until something lands in-tree, the shell script below is what we use locally: backup active `save/` (+ optional side-car `saves/` and `env.txt`) under a per-profile folder, then restore another profile. **The game must be fully quit** before switching. Paths and names are genericized; set `TITLE_ID` yourself.

<details>
<summary>switch_user.sh (sanitized workaround)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Workaround: named save profiles for one Mac nxnative title (quit game before switching).
# Usage:
#   TITLE_ID=<16-hex> ./switch_user.sh <profile>
#   TITLE_ID=<16-hex> ./switch_user.sh backup <profile>
#   TITLE_ID=<16-hex> ./switch_user.sh who
set -euo pipefail

TITLE_ID="${TITLE_ID:?set TITLE_ID to the game title id (16 hex)}"
GAME_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BACK_ROOT="${SAVE_BACK_ROOT:-$GAME_DIR/save_back}"
CURRENT_FILE="$BACK_ROOT/CURRENT"
AS_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/nxnative/$TITLE_ID"
AS_SAVE="$AS_DIR/save"
AS_SYNC="$AS_DIR/save.sync"
AS_ENV="$AS_DIR/env.txt"
# Optional extra tree some setups keep beside the game files (cloud sync side-car, etc.)
GAME_SAVES="${GAME_SAVES_DIR:-$GAME_DIR/saves}"
DEFAULT_PROFILE="${DEFAULT_PROFILE:-player1}"

die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
info() { echo "$*"; }

require_game_quit() {
  if pgrep -qf "Application Support/nxnative/$TITLE_ID|/MacOS/dmhost"; then
    die "game appears to be running — quit the app completely, then retry"
  fi
}

current_user() {
  if [[ -f "$CURRENT_FILE" ]]; then
    tr -d '[:space:]' <"$CURRENT_FILE"
  else
    echo ""
  fi
}

set_current() {
  mkdir -p "$BACK_ROOT"
  printf '%s\n' "$1" >"$CURRENT_FILE"
}

valid_name() {
  [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || die "profile name must be letters/digits/_/- : $1"
}

backup_user() {
  local user="$1"
  valid_name "$user"
  require_game_quit
  [[ -d "$AS_SAVE" ]] || die "no active save at $AS_SAVE"

  local dest="$BACK_ROOT/$user"
  local stamp
  stamp="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  if [[ -d "$dest" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$BACK_ROOT/.history"
    mv "$dest" "$BACK_ROOT/.history/${user}.$stamp"
    info "previous backup of '$user' kept as .history/${user}.$stamp"
  fi

  mkdir -p "$dest/app_support" "$dest/game_saves"
  ditto "$AS_SAVE" "$dest/app_support/save"
  [[ -f "$AS_SYNC" ]] && cp -p "$AS_SYNC" "$dest/app_support/save.sync"
  [[ -f "$AS_ENV" ]] && cp -p "$AS_ENV" "$dest/app_support/env.txt"
  if [[ -d "$GAME_SAVES" ]]; then
    ditto "$GAME_SAVES" "$dest/game_saves"
  fi

  set_current "$user"
  info "backed up active save → save_back/$user"
}

write_nick_env() {
  local user="$1"
  mkdir -p "$AS_DIR"
  if [[ -f "$AS_ENV" ]] && grep -q '^DM_NICK=' "$AS_ENV" 2>/dev/null; then
    local tmp
    tmp="$(mktemp)"
    grep -v '^DM_NICK=' "$AS_ENV" >"$tmp" || true
    printf 'DM_NICK=%s\n' "$user" >>"$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$AS_ENV"
  else
    {
      [[ -f "$AS_ENV" ]] && cat "$AS_ENV"
      printf 'DM_NICK=%s\n' "$user"
    } >"$AS_ENV.tmp"
    mv "$AS_ENV.tmp" "$AS_ENV"
  fi
}

clear_active_for_new() {
  require_game_quit
  mkdir -p "$AS_DIR"
  rm -rf "$AS_SAVE" "$AS_DIR/save.work"
  mkdir -p "$AS_SAVE"
  rm -f "$AS_SYNC"
  mkdir -p "$GAME_SAVES"
  rm -rf "$GAME_SAVES/$TITLE_ID"
}

restore_user() {
  local user="$1"
  valid_name "$user"
  require_game_quit
  local src="$BACK_ROOT/$user"
  [[ -d "$src/app_support/save" ]] || die "no backup for '$user' at save_back/$user"

  mkdir -p "$AS_DIR"
  rm -rf "$AS_SAVE" "$AS_DIR/save.work"
  ditto "$src/app_support/save" "$AS_SAVE"
  if [[ -f "$src/app_support/save.sync" ]]; then
    cp -p "$src/app_support/save.sync" "$AS_SYNC"
  else
    rm -f "$AS_SYNC"
  fi
  if [[ -f "$src/app_support/env.txt" ]]; then
    cp -p "$src/app_support/env.txt" "$AS_ENV"
  fi
  write_nick_env "$user"

  if [[ -d "$src/game_saves" ]] && [[ -n "$(ls -A "$src/game_saves" 2>/dev/null || true)" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$GAME_SAVES"
    find "$GAME_SAVES" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec rm -rf {} +
    ditto "$src/game_saves" "$GAME_SAVES"
  fi

  set_current "$user"
  info "restored save_back/$user → active"
}

switch_to() {
  local target="$1"
  valid_name "$target"
  require_game_quit

  local cur
  cur="$(current_user)"
  if [[ -z "$cur" ]]; then
    cur="$DEFAULT_PROFILE"
    info "CURRENT unset — treating active save as '$cur'"
  fi

  if [[ "$cur" == "$target" ]] && [[ -d "$BACK_ROOT/$target/app_support/save" ]]; then
    info "already on '$target' — refreshing backup from active save"
    backup_user "$target"
    restore_user "$target"
    return
  fi

  if [[ -d "$AS_SAVE" ]]; then
    info "backing up current profile '$cur' …"
    backup_user "$cur"
  else
    info "no active save to back up"
  fi

  if [[ -d "$BACK_ROOT/$target/app_support/save" ]]; then
    info "restoring '$target' …"
    restore_user "$target"
  else
    info "no backup for '$target' — creating empty new save"
    clear_active_for_new
    write_nick_env "$target"
    set_current "$target"
    backup_user "$target"
    info "new profile '$target' ready"
  fi

  info "now playing as: $(current_user)"
}

cmd="${1:-}"
case "$cmd" in
  ""|-h|--help)
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  TITLE_ID=<id> ./switch_user.sh <profile>
  TITLE_ID=<id> ./switch_user.sh backup <profile>
  TITLE_ID=<id> ./switch_user.sh who
EOF
    exit 0
    ;;
  who)
    u="$(current_user)"
    if [[ -z "$u" ]]; then
      info "CURRENT unset (active save not tagged yet)"
    else
      info "current profile: $u"
    fi
    ;;
  backup)
    [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "usage: ./switch_user.sh backup <profile>"
    backup_user "$2"
    ;;
  *)
    switch_to "$cmd"
    ;;
esac
```

</details>

Example:

```bash
TITLE_ID=0100xxxxxxxxxxxx ./switch_user.sh backup player1
TITLE_ID=0100xxxxxxxxxxxx ./switch_user.sh player2   # creates empty profile if new
TITLE_ID=0100xxxxxxxxxxxx ./switch_user.sh who
```

### Platforms

Mac (primary ask), iPhone / iPad launcher welcome too
title: Mac/iOS launcher: named save profiles (switch without sharing one save tree)

body:
### What happened

Every start of the Mac app spends about 5 minutes on "Preparing shaders" before the first frame, including a start where everything comes from the caches and nothing is compiled. `docs/development.md` (The prepare step) says such a start should take well under a second.

Two starts in a row, launched with `--no-launcher` and closed after the prepare step. Before the first start, the device's `pso_archive` and the app's Metal cache folder (`$TMPDIR/../C/org.nxnative.0400486024dec000`: `com.apple.gpuarchiver`, `com.apple.metal`) were deleted.

| Start | Prepare | Bases compiled | From an archive | Specializations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (cold) | 457.5 s | 7,606 | 797 | 8,994 |
| 2 (warm) | 309.1 s | 0 | 8,403 | 8,994 |

Both starts prepared the same 29,713 lines: 19,622 shaders, 8,994 render pipelines and 1,097 compute pipelines, on 14 workers. The lists are the profile's `pso_manifest.tsv` (9,625 lines) and `pso_user.tsv` (29,712 lines).

In start 2, the `pipelines up to frame 300` line accounts for little of the 309 s:

```
archive lookups found 8403 / 11203.6 ms, found none 0 / 0.0 ms, specializations 8994 / 180.3 ms, bases compiled 0 / 0.0 ms
```

That is about 11.4 s of thread time across all workers. I have not timed the shader step separately. By elimination, most of the 309 s is in the 19,622 shader rows.

Metal's archiver store also fills after one cold start. After start 1, `com.apple.gpuarchiver` was 1.4 GB. Start 2's flush then failed:

```
[RED] pipeline archive: writing …/pso_archive/00043.mtl4a failed: Failed to generate machO:error: cannot write 'UNITS' database: MDB_MAP_FULL: Environment mapsize limit reached
[RED] pipeline archive: compaction left the old files (the flush failed)
```

Before the caches were deleted, the device archive held 191 files that were never compacted, from the same failure.

A related point, which #1368 may address: with `DM_PSO_PREPARE=0` the title came up in 1.7 s. Loading a save then held one frame for 68.3 s (`new pipelines 69`), and the picture stayed black for several minutes. The host built task / mesh pipelines on first use, many in over a second each (`task / mesh pipeline: … 1861.6 ms`). `pso_user.tsv` holds no `M` rows on main (1,097 `C`, 8,993 `R`, 19,622 `S`), so these are built again in every session.

Every start, the same.

### What you expected

A second start whose pipelines all come from the archives prepares in seconds, as described in the prepare step's documentation.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072 (NUP)

### nxnative commit

main `e940e1f` plus #1377, #1379, #1459, #1707, #1714, #1722, #1735, #1742 and a port of #1350 (local merge, not pushed)

### Shader chain version

`1b64a2d2c5e7`, all 42,848 shaders built

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py … --platform mac-app -l fr`. Mac app, docked (`DM_OPMODE=1`), bundled archive `applegpu_g16s.mtl4a` (4.8 GB, "holds the bases of every shader pair").

### Device and OS

Mac with Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Xcode 27.2

### Settings and environment overrides

`DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, `DM_PAD_IDENTICAL=0`, `DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission`, `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`. `DM_PSO_PREPARE=0` only in the related point above.

### Logs

The relevant lines are quoted above.

Not tested: a start with only the profile's `pso_manifest.tsv` (without `pso_user.tsv`), `DM_PSO_PREPARE_THREADS`, and timing the shader rows on their own.

Drafted with Claude Code.

body:
## What happens

`DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1` kills the host inside Apple's Metal driver as soon as Ocarina of Time's gameplay starts. The title screen and the opening movie are fine; the crash comes on loading a save, which is where the game's effect system begins issuing its per-frame batch of about 140 compute dispatches.

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x98
  pc=AGX::ComputeContext<AGX::G13::Encoders, …>::prepareForEnqueue(bool)+0x284
  lr=…prepareForEnqueue(bool)+0x270 sp=0x702272f4e0
launcher: the host exited with 139
```

The fault is in `AGX::ComputeContext::prepareForEnqueue`, not in guest code or in the host, at a near-null address. The host's own crash report shows the guest threads parked normally — the main thread in a condvar, the resource threads waiting — so nothing guest-side had gone wrong first.

The option was in effect (`[dm] [nvn-mtl] compute dispatches: each in an encoder of its own (DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1 or DM_NVN_PASSGPU)`), and the run reached frame 3600 with GPU times of 0.3–0.4 ms a frame before dying at the save load.

## Setup

- `main` `bd979ced3ae6` with #1331 cherry-picked (the host also carries that PR's NDVE movie scaling, which was enabled in this run). The crash path is compute-encoder creation and has nothing to do with that patch, but I have not re-run it on plain `main` to confirm, so take the base as stated.
- Profile `0400486024DEC000`, v131072 from a NUP, shader chain `3ee52af3ca18`, `--platform mac-app`, offline pipeline archive for `applegpu_g13s`
- MacBook Pro **M1 Max**, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1 DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:300 DM_UPSCALER=game DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`

## Why it matters beyond the switch

`DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN` and `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` are the two ways to get per-dispatch GPU times, and on this game neither is available: `DM_NVN_PASSGPU` is off under Metal 4, and `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN` crashes. So a frame whose largest single item is a 9.5 ms compute encoder with ~143 dispatches cannot be broken down any further with what the host offers today. That is what I was trying to measure for [#1658](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1658) when I hit this.

## Guesses, not findings

An encoder per dispatch with full barriers means roughly 140 compute encoders a frame where the default is one. Whether the driver has a limit this crosses, or whether the host leaves something unset on the per-dispatch path that only shows at that rate, I do not know — I have not read the encoder-creation path. The smaller `DM_NVN_CS_HOIST=0` does not crash and keeps 21 compute encoders a frame.

The host log for the crashing run is kept, including the full crash report and thread dump; say what would help and I will attach it.
title: DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1 crashes in AGX::ComputeContext::prepareForEnqueue on Ocarina of Time, so per-dispatch GPU times cannot be measured under Metal 4

body:
## What happens

One command buffer fails with a GPU address fault about 2.5 minutes into play. The host reports it, the game carries on, and the run reaches its end normally — nothing visible was noticed at the time, and the host exited 0 after another 575 seconds of play.

This is **not** [#1326](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1326), which is `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang` on this same game and ends in revoked GPU access and exit 70. This one is a page fault that does not escalate.

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] segment command buffer execution error: Error Domain=MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=1 "(null)"
  UserInfo={NSMultipleUnderlyingErrorsKey=(
    "Error Domain=MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=2 \"Caused GPU Address Fault Error
     (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)\"
     UserInfo={NSUnderlyingError=… {Error Domain=IOGPUCommandQueueErrorDomain Code=11}}"
  )}
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] game shaders of failed command buffer #1 (fence 7118, segment 12): 257: 14b728f8d7b9718c_b …
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] game shaders by failed/ran over 1 failed of 7925 command buffers: 01fb30494148820b_b 1/1, …
```

Frame 1185, at 158.73 s. That frame also reports a nonsense GPU time, which is what a command buffer that never delivered its timestamps looks like:

```
[dm] [longframe] frame 1185 (158.73 s) whole frame 300.0 ms, submit+present 299.7 ms, GPU 6148483371437.2 ms;
  new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0, 0.0 ms in all; texture uploads 519 first + 0 re-uploads, 281.1 MB / 35.1 ms
```

Frames 1184 and 1186 either side are ordinary (135.0 ms and 72.5 ms whole frame, GPU 24.5 ms and 40.7 ms). The run went on to frame 25014 at 735.01 s and `launcher: the host exited with 0`.

## Setup

- `main` `bd979ced3ae6`, shader chain `3ee52af3ca18`, profile `0400486024DEC000`, v131072 from a NUP, `--platform mac-app`, offline pipeline archive for `applegpu_g13s`
- MacBook Pro **M1 Max**, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- Windowed, `DM_UPSCALER=game`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`, `DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:600`

## What the log gives, and what it does not

`cbs_feedback` named the failed command buffer's 257 game shaders, but with a single failure the failed/ran tally is 1/1 for every one of them, so it does not narrow anything down. A second occurrence would.

The line immediately after the failure is the one lead I have, and I want to be clear that it is weak:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] raw global memory: the stores wrote in 6 pool(s) the host had not learned
  (log 8767, 14 such pools so far, 15 learned; the pools were added 98084-98084 ms before):
  0 of them hold one of the 3 uniform shadows taken from that submission
```

Stores into memory pools the host has not learned is a plausible way to produce an address the GPU cannot translate. **But that line appears 8 times in this run and the fault happened once**, so on its own it explains nothing — at most it says the two live in the same area. I have not shown they are connected.

Also unexplained: why it does not escalate. The same class of failure on other titles ends the run ([#1289](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1289) freezes the picture, [#149](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/149) had every later submission ignored). Here one segment died and everything afterwards was fine, with no `InnocentVictim` or `SubmissionsIgnored` anywhere in the log.

## Reproducing

Not established. It happened once, in one run, about 2.5 minutes in, and I have not tried to hit it again. The full log is kept if any of it would help — say which parts and I will attach them.

Filed as an observation with the evidence I have, not as a diagnosis.

body:
## What happened

On the Mac, Mario Tennis Fever (0400D4201C6EA000) hangs the GPU whenever Donkey Kong is on court, as the player's character or as the CPU opponent. The first `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang` is followed by more, then every submission is refused (`Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)`): the picture freezes while the game and its audio go on. In the later runs the hang also ended the macOS session: the Mac went back to the login window and every app had to be reopened.

Timing varies. It most often comes at or within about a minute of DK's special shot, sometimes 22 s into a session, once before the first point. In 9 sessions with DK on court it hung every time. Two sessions without DK, 10 and 30 minutes of play including a full tournament, had no hang.

## Narrowing it down

- `[RED] game shaders of failed command buffer` over 24 hangs from 4 sessions: every failed command buffer held Donkey Kong's model shaders (`model/nxr/nxr_character/pc/donkey_rally/donkey_rally_rig.narc/113`). Seven of its vertex shaders are in 22 of 24 and ran in only 640 command buffers.
- Bisecting with `DM_NVN_SKIP_FS` over the 11 fragment shaders DK's draws use:

| Skipped | Result |
|---|---|
| all 11 | no hang, 3 specials |
| `84bdc3da404e8f14,5c1269abdfe46d99,7554f8e83fc9ece7,d2f7f656db14eee5,66eb4aefc102b419` | 12 hangs, at the first special |
| `7ddd32f1c85b5cc1,252bece9255e6922,e27206787bc56841` | no hang, 3 specials |
| `7ddd32f1c85b5cc1` | 10 hangs; no failed buffer held it |
| `252bece9255e6922` | 16 hangs; no failed buffer held it, all held `e27206787bc56841` |

So the suspect is `e27206787bc56841`, `donkey_rally_rig.narc/113#BNSH@0x80000#var83`. It is drawn with vertex shaders `73c5918c5bcd4303` (var2) and `ab14ad7bdba2d2e7` (var10), 10 instances per draw, which looks like fur shells. A run with only this shader skipped was not made, because each hang logged the user out.

Its MSL has no loops. Compared with its sibling `252bece9255e6922`, which did not hang, it samples a third texture (`tcb_10`) and has two `discard_fragment()`.

## Ruled out, as far as these runs go

- **Residency:** `DM_RES_CHECK=1` reported no `missing residency` and no `released too early` in a session that hung 8 times.
- **Draw shapes:** a local draw watch over DK's vertex shaders, about 175,000 draws, found no indirect or multi-draw. The largest count was 10,182 vertices and 10 instances, every index range was inside its buffer, and no base vertex was past its stream.
- **Bindings:** `DM_NVN_KEYDUMP=e27206787bc56841:400` saw normal bindings: three 2048x2048 mipmapped textures, all resident, and plausible uniforms. It only covered frames 1182–1231, and the hang came at frame 3264.
- **Launcher settings:** starting with `--no-launcher` still hung.
- **Metal API validation:** with `MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1`, the run crashed in `-[MTL4GPUDebugCommandBuffer applyResidencySets:]` (`objc_opt_isKindOfClass`) at the racket select, before reaching the hang. It reported no `Invalid Metal usage`.

## Workaround

Not playing with or against Donkey Kong. `DM_NVN_SKIP_FS=e27206787bc56841` probably avoids it too, with part of DK missing, but that has not been validated over a long session.

## Game, version, build

- Mario Tennis Fever, 0400D4201C6EA000, update 1.1.1 (v327680), packed from a NUP with `--platform mac-app`
- nxnative commit `b2d46b8`, shader chain `844bf1a5ea8f`
- Apple M4 Max, 36 GB, macOS 27.2, fullscreen, Metal 4 pipelines on (defaults)

Logs can be attached on request (redacted).
title: Mario Tennis Fever (Mac): GPU hang with Donkey Kong on court, isolated to his pixel shader e27206787bc56841; repeated hangs log the user out

body:
### What happened

I started the game without a controller and walked to Kokiri Village with the keyboard. Music/BGM plays fine. As soon as I connect a Switch Pro Controller over USB (or Bluetooth / different USB ports tested too), the music stops completely while SFX keep playing. This happens every time I run the game. If I never connect the controller and just play with KB, the BGM works.

The attached log (0400486024DEC000_controller_audio.log) shows what happens at connect:

```
1. 'Pro Controller' connected: player 1 (npad 0)  [GameController path]
2. 'Pro Controller' disconnected: player 1 (npad 0) is free
3. 'Pro Controller' (HID) connected: player 1 (npad 0)
4. 'Pro Controller' (HID) connected: player 2 (npad 1)
   Both come from the same device (057e:2009, USB location 0x100000) and the same
   report 0x30 stream. Log line: "GameController lists 1 of 2 pads of this model".
5. From then on, every frame:
   oe library applet: controller support
   oe focus state -> 2 (library applet open)
   hid controller applet: 1 to 1 players wanted, 2 connected
   oe focus state -> 1 (library applet closed)
   (339 times in the attached log, about one per frame, until I quit)
```

The audio renderer itself looks healthy during this. Render time is a mean of 0.09 ms with a max of 0.26 ms. Every report shows 0 underruns and 0 zero-padded frames, including the one covering the connect.

The game calls `oe::SetFocusHandlingMode 2` (focus notifications). My guess, _which the log doesn’t prove_, is that the focus flipping every frame makes the game pause or mute its BGM stream.

An earlier log from a session where the controller was already connected at boot shows the same pattern.

**Workaround**
- #1657 sees the same issue, and using ```DM_HID_PADS=0``` in `env.txt` **works as a workaround**.

**Suggested fixes by Claude**
1. Deduplicate pads in the HID path (the root fix).
```
The log shows the pad registered once through GameController (player 1, with motion and haptics). It’s then dropped (“is free”) and re-registered twice by the HID path (player 1 and player 2).
Both HID entries have the same USB location, 0x100000.
Key HID devices by their IOKit location ID, or serial number if present, and create one npad per key. Ignore a second matching callback for a key that’s already registered.
The line GameController lists 1 of 2 pads of this model suggests the code matches pads by model counts. Matching by location ID would be more reliable, and would also keep two real Pro Controllers apart.
Also check why the GameController registration gets torn down before the HID takeover. If the two paths hand off, the handoff should leave one pad, not two.
```

2. Make the controller applet stub resolve the mismatch.
```
When the game asks for 1 player and 2 are connected, the stub should keep one pad (the lowest npad or the most recently active) and hide the rest from the game. Then it should return success.
It currently returns with “2 connected” still true, so the game calls the applet again every frame. That’s a bug even with a legitimate second controller.
```

### What you expected

One Pro Controller should register as one player. The music should keep playing with the controller.

bd979ced

body:
### What happened

Luigi's Mansion 3 held a steady 60 fps on the Mac with a `--platform mac-app` build from **0c94284** (Oct 30). Builds from **30fb213** and **db206a4** (Nov 7) run at about **22–25 fps**, from the first frames on and in every scene, including the title screen with no input. No crash and no new `[RED]` lines.

## Cause: 51cc8bce (`vi::ListFrameHistory` returns the last 8 presents)

Before 51cc8bce, `h_vi_FrameHist` in `dm/gfx/hle_vi.c` returned 0 entries. Since then it returns the last 8 presents, marking each one shown (status 2) only once the present queue has handed it on, with its present tick taken from the drawable's presented time. LM3 (Next Level Games' engine) calls it at start: the log prints `vi::ListFrameHistory: 1 of the last 8 presents returned (up to frame 1, the present queue at 0)`, which 0c94284 never prints.

A/B on **one** db206a4 host (`--platform mac`, title screen, no input, 2560x1440 window, `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`). The only change was a local test switch that makes `ListFrameHistory` return 0 again:

| db206a4 host | frame time p50 / p95 | fps | main thread | worker core 2 | main yields / 300 frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ListFrameHistory` returns 0 (as before 51cc8bce) | 16.67 / 16.94 ms | 60.0 | 580 ms/s | 490 ms/s | ~7,300 |
| unchanged | 37.3–40.6 / 41.8–47.8 ms | ~25 | 807–865 ms/s | 780–840 ms/s | 5,300–8,000 |

With 0 entries every number matches the good 0c94284 build (60.0 fps; main 567 ms/s, worker core 2 492 ms/s, ~7,600 yields). For reference, the unchanged db206a4 Mac app gives 41–45 ms (22–25 fps).

Likely mechanism (not verified in LM3's code): the engine paces itself on the frame history, waiting until its previous frame is reported shown. In a window the host reports a present as shown about 50 ms after the game queues it (`submission ahead of target display p50 49.9 ms` in the display link lines), so the game settles near 24 fps. On the Switch a present shows within a vsync or two.

Ruled out on the bad build: `DM_SPIN=0` and `DM_YIELD_BACKOFF=0` (no change: the main thread waits on worker core 2, which waits on the frame history); the Game Mode opt-out (`LSSupportsGameMode=false`, cb59a672) removed from the app (no change); LM3's profile (only its README changed between the builds). A `sample` profile shows no page-fault or signal time. My earlier suspects (8ea2778, 9d71e27, 411223c, 7550be1) are not involved.

## A possible fix (yours to choose)

The test switch I used, in `h_vi_FrameHist` before `if (!out || n <= 0) return VFH;`:

```c
{ static int off = -1; if (off < 0) off = getenv("DM_VFH_OFF") && atoi(getenv("DM_VFH_OFF")); if (off) return 0; }   // no frame history, as before 51cc8bce
```

Options, as I see them:
1. **Per-game opt-out:** a profile key (e.g. `vi_frame_history 0`) for LM3 that keeps the old 0-entry answer, while Unreal titles (Minecraft Dungeons II, Octopath Traveler 0 / II) keep the history they need.
2. **Report presents as shown sooner:** mark an entry shown when the present queue hands it on, rather than at the drawable's presented time. That is closer to the Switch's latency and may suit both engines, but I haven't tested it.
3. **Env switch only:** ship `DM_VFH_OFF` (or similar) as a diagnostic, so players can opt out while a proper fix is worked out.

I'm happy to test a candidate fix on LM3.

## Also noticed

The 0c94284 app's bundled pipeline archive no longer opens on macOS 27.2 ("deployment target for architecture applegpu_g14s found in archive"), so it prebuilds 3,852 pairs (~14 s) at every start. Frame rate is unaffected.

### What you expected

A steady 60 fps in the same scene, as with the 0c94284 build.

### Game, title ID and version

Luigi's Mansion 3, 0100DCA0064A6000, 1.4.0 (v327680), US, plus both Multiplayer Packs (DLC 1 and 2)

### nxnative commit

db206a4 (also slow on 30fb213; last good 0c94284)

### Shader chain version

1d619d0f520b (db206a4 build)

### How it was built and run

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro 16" M2 Pro (19-core GPU), 16 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Xcode 27.2 (Metal 32023.922)

### Settings and environment overrides

Identical for all runs (set in the Mac settings window):

```
DM_FPS_TARGET=60
DM_OPMODE=1
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off
DM_LANG=en-US
DM_FULLSCREEN=0
DM_RUMBLE=0
DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0
DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0
DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN=0
DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0
DM_PSO_MTL4=1
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0
DM_FPS_HOLD=on
DM_METAL_HUD=1
```

### Logs

Host log of a db206a4 run attached (`~/Library/Logs/nxnative/0100DCA0064A6000.log`). The 0c94284 and 30fb213 logs were overwritten by later runs; the figures above come from them.

[lm3-db206a4-host-log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34524859/lm3-db206a4-host-log.txt)

body:
> **Update (2026-11-07):** the cause described below is wrong. The host ignores NVN cross-queue event waits (`nvnCommandBufferWaitEvent` is a no-op), so the shadow compute on queue 5 runs before queue 1 has written this frame's depth. #1245 fixes it: tested in replays and in play, with dynamic resolution on. See [this comment](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1245#issuecomment-6713438416). The analysis and the `DM_NVN_MOVE_FILL` patch below are kept for reference only. ### Summary At one spot in Kokiri Forest, the ground shadows drop for a single frame every time Link runs past. The game moves its half-resolution depth buffer to an address where, on a Switch 2, last frame's depth is still in memory. The host instead hands back the Metal texture it made for that address about 280 frames earlier, with stale depth. A local test patch that gives the moved buffer last frame's depth removes the glitch, both in a deterministic replay and in the player's own play. Related: #1698, which suspects the same class of problem at resolution changes in Castle Town. ### What happened In Kokiri Forest, the 3D scene now and then shows one frame where the ground shadows are missing or in the wrong place. The next frame is right again, and the HUD and minimap do not change. - It happens every time Link runs past the rock and the wooden bridge near the start of the forest, and in some other places too. - It also happens at dynamic-resolution steps. `DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission` pins the resolution and removes those. - It happens in both handheld and docked mode. - It does not happen on a Switch 2 (the player's own observation). ### Cause The pass dump names below come from a deterministic replay; how to run it is under Reproduction. Formats are MTLPixelFormat numbers: 10 R8, 55 R32F, 70 RGBA8. 1. **The shadow mask's R channel comes from a compute chain that reads last frame's depth.** The RGBA8 1440x810 mask (shader `9aa7f545bb5abcae`) takes its R channel directly from an R8 720x405. That R8 comes from compute `990c4f533a4ebd0d` followed by four blur dispatches (`66c383579c983d46` and `5473fbd870e70a60`), all reading an R32F 720x405, the half-resolution depth. The compute runs early in the frame, before that frame's own draw writes the R32F (`d8bbabcb9d1fdcf1`, a half-resolution depth copy). So it reads the previous frame's half-resolution depth. 2. **At the rock, the game switches its render setup and moves that buffer.** It turns off an RG32F 360x202 pass, and its allocator moves the R32F 720x405 between pool offsets 0x15d5200 and 0x13b0800. The moves happen at F1352, F1371, F1649 and F1764 in the replay, stamped at texture init, which runs one frame ahead of the pass dump. 3. **On the Switch, the new address holds last frame's depth.** In the other setup, the game's R32F 1440x810 full-resolution depth lives at offset 0x10e9000 with size 0x4ec000, and it is written every frame. That covers all of 0x13b0800 to 0x1518800. When the buffer moves there, the compute reads the previous frame's depth bytes, in another layout. After the blur the shadows come out right. 4. **On the host, the new address gives an old texture.** For the texture created at 0x13b0800 in F1649, the alias table (pool, offset, description) returns the Metal texture it made the last time the buffer lived there, at F1352–F1371. The test host logged this as "R32F ser … reuses a shared Metal texture …". Its content is about 280 frames old: depth from another camera position. That stale texture got through two checks: - **No eviction.** When the 1440x810 took over that storage at F1368, `alias_take_over` did not evict the entry. It spares entries seen in the last `ALIAS_IDLE` submissions and entries a live serial holds. - **No refresh.** Nothing replaces the entry's content with what the overlapping texture wrote since. The shadow term is computed from the wrong depth for one frame. If the entry had been evicted, the new texture would be zero-filled; depth 0 is wrong as well, though differently. **The resolution-step trigger looks like the same class.** There the R32F buffers are re-created at the new sizes, 854x480 and 427x240. Their first read gets untranslated or empty texels, which rendering.md already lists: "Inherited texels are not translated between incompatible texture layouts". ### Test fix A local, env-gated patch on `a260844`. When an R32F 2D single-level texture is created, or re-used from the alias table, it is filled with the previous R32F texture of the same size. That previous texture holds last frame's half-resolution depth. | Replay frames 1420–1800 | Shot 1651 (setup switch) | Shot 1765 (switch back) | Largest other outlier | |---|---|---|---| | Without | 6.6 | 3.9 | 1.1 | | With | 0.0 | -0.4 | 1.1 | Outlier score is above the local median; about 1 is normal camera motion. By eye the shadows stay in place (`fix_comparison.jpg`). This patch only shows the cause; it is not the fix. The player also played with the test fix in the Mac app at the spot and saw no glitch at all.
The test patch (diagnostic only, not for merge; on a260844, env-gated by DM_TEST_INHERIT=1) ```diff diff --git a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m b/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m index bcbf740..ed39f9e 100644 --- a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m +++ b/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m @@ -2769,6 +2770,30 @@ static void up_blit_add(id src, size_t off, size_t row, size_t image, id dst, NSUInteger slice, NSUInteger level) { up_blit_add_at(src, off, row, image, size, dst, slice, level, MTLOriginMake(0, 0, 0)); } static id pkg_upload_(const tex_t *t, uint64_t *stamp, id reuse, MTLTextureUsage keep); +// DM_TEST_INHERIT=1 (local test only): a new or re-used R32F 2D single-level texture starts with the content of the previous R32F texture of the same size +// (Ocarina of Time's half-resolution depth, read before it is written in the frame the game moves it; the host's alias entry for the new address holds stale bytes) +#define TI_N 8 +static __strong id g_ti_prev[TI_N]; static __strong id g_ti_buf[TI_N]; +static void test_inherit(id mt) { + static int on = -1; The general fix: when an alias entry is re-used, or a texture is made over storage that another GPU texture has written since, give it the content of the texture that last wrote that storage. - **Exact:** go through the block-linear byte image, as the hardware does. - **Approximate:** use a scaled copy when the format matches. This would also cover the resolution steps. ### Reproduction (deterministic replay) A `DM_REC` recording of the player's input, from a copy of the save made just before it. Both are available on request: a game save and an input log, not game data. ``` DM_FRAME_DELTA=0 DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission DM_KEYS=@rec.keys (save copy as DM_SAVE) ``` - **Route:** `DM_FRAME_DELTA=0` was also set while recording, so the route stays the same however slowly the replay runs. - **Glitch frame:** the glitch is usually shot 1651, which is pass-dump frame F1650; a shot shows the frame before its number. Of 9 replays with shots, 6 show it at 1651 and 2 at 1650. In one replay the route drifted slightly and the switch came later. - **Where it shows in the dumps:** in `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`, the mask's R channel is uniform in F1650 (mean 255, against 198 in F1649 and F1651); G and B match. `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL` shows the compute chain and its order. - **Debug options used:** pool offsets came from `DM_NVN_TEXINFO=720x405` plus a local log of texture inits overlapping an offset range. ### What was ruled out on the way | Test | Result | |---|---| | `DM_NVN_BARRIER=full` | Glitch still there | | Samples-passed results forced to 1,000,000 (test host) | Unchanged | | `segment` instead of `submission` timestamps | Unchanged | | Docked (`DM_OPMODE=1`) | Unchanged, one frame earlier | | Colour clears done as a real clear in a pass of their own (test host) | Unchanged: the read comes before the clear | | Capture load (screenshots every frame, against none) | The switch lands on the same frame | ### What you expected The shadows stay in place across the frame where the game changes its render setup, as on a Switch 2. ### Game, title ID and version The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), 0400486024DEC000, update v131072 ### nxnative commit `a260844`, which is 490859e plus #1543 and #1644; neither touches this area. The first recordings were on `490859e`. The test hosts were `a260844` with local, env-gated diagnostic patches. The 14 commits on main after 490859e (up to 24fe1e5) do not touch the alias table, judging by their descriptions; not retested on main. ### Shader chain version 3ee493b2c3a4 ### How it was built and run Mac app (--platform mac-app). Headless replays ran the build folder's `dmhost`, or a test build of it, with the app's settings. ### Device and OS MacBook Pro Mac16,8, Apple M4 Pro (`applegpu_g16s`), 24 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Xcode 27.2 (27B52) ### Settings and environment overrides - **Player** (read from the app logs): handheld (`DM_OPMODE=0`), fullscreen, Performance HUD on, Upscaling "Standard", Game's upscaler "Game's own" (`DM_UPSCALER=game`), Frame buffering off, Metal 4 pipelines and Pipeline prebuild on, Encode thread off. - **env.txt:** `DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission`; for the recording also `DM_FRAME_DELTA=0` and `DM_REC`. - **Headless runs:** the same settings, plus the capture variables named above. ### Logs `run-redacted.log`: an app log of the player at the spot, whole, with the home folder replaced by ~. body:
### What happens

In Hyrule Castle Town, while Link moves and the camera turns, single frames go wrong and then snap back. Two kinds:

1. A whole frame comes out hazy and washed out, then the next one is crisp again. Shadows keep their shape but lighten and darken.
2. Object shadows blink. A dappled foliage shadow (likely the hanging flower baskets) covers the railing, a post and the ground in one frame and is gone in the next.

Models also drop to low detail when the dynamic resolution steps down. The player sees both while moving. Standing still is mostly fine.

### Measurements

Headless runs on an M5 Pro (48 GB, macOS 27), same save (Castle Town street by the railings), the same scripted movement and camera turns, and all 600 frames from 6000 to 6599 captured at 60 fps. A pulse is a frame whose brightness differs by more than 3 levels from both neighbours, with camera cuts left out.

| run | pulses |
|---|---|
| profile default (`gpu_timestamps segment`) | 27 |
| same, repeated with a pass dump | 32 |
| `DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_DC=0` | 25 |
| `DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission` (holds the top resolution) | 8 |

- **What the pin removes:** the alternating hazy and crisp frames at 6254-6262 and the light/dark object shadows at 6541-6545.
- **What's left:** of the 8 remaining pulses, two sit next to camera cuts, and 6574-6579 is the camera passing a near railing post. That one is in every run.
- **Draw counts:** at dynamic resolution they swing between 709 and 1371 on consecutive frames.

### Lead (from a pass dump, not yet proven by a run)

- In frame 6255 a compute pass samples the sun cascade (1600x1600 D16, 3 slices) **before** that frame clears and re-renders it. It writes 64x36 3D textures, likely the volumetric fog volume. So it relies on the previous frame's cascade still being in memory, as it would be on the console.
- The game creates a new cascade texture object every frame. The Metal texture behind it changes every 3 frames or so (0x7c158f3200, 0x7c156b2080, 0x7c15f36080, 0x7c15531900 over frames 6252-6262).
- If a new Metal texture doesn't hold last frame's depth, the fog sees an empty shadow map for that frame and lights the whole volume. That would be the hazy frame.
- The object shadow map also changes size every frame (941 to 1266 px).
- Every 8 frames a 128x128 probe update runs. At dynamic resolution, pulses lean toward those frames.
- **Not tested yet:** `DM_NVN_POOL_HEAP=0`, `DM_NVN_RT_CONTINUE=0`, and a `DM_NVN_TEXINFO` run for where the cascade's storage comes from.

#1350 and #1676 make dynamic resolution see the right GPU time. This report is a different problem: when the resolution does change, content that should carry over to the next frame seems to be lost. So even correct timings would flicker whenever the resolution moves.

### Workaround and a play test

`DM_NVN_GPU_TS=submission` holds the top resolution (1536x864). The player played Castle Town with it and saw no flicker and full detail.

From his session log, over 43 windows of 300 frames:
- **Frame time:** median p50 16.51 ms and median p95 18.25 ms. The worst window's p95 was 36.6 ms, a load or first compile.
- **GPU:** median p50 13.2 ms. The heaviest stretch reached 18.5 ms.

**Performance caveat:** this is a high-end MacBook Pro (M5 Pro, 48 GB). The pin turns off the game's resolution scaling, so a smaller Mac would drop below 60 fps where the game would otherwise lower its resolution. It's a workaround, not a fix.

### Also checked: the grass shadows (5e344a87) are not a flicker source

- **What the two draws are:** the foliage point meshes that 5e344a87 lets link (mesh `a203347bb7bdbd03`, `3a6340a04bf09797`). They draw only into a dedicated 2400x2400 grass shadow map. One box draw reads it and writes two channels of the screen shadow mask. Objects use a separate shadow map and the cascades.
- **Flicker:** repeat runs with and without those draws are within run-to-run noise. Flip-back on the near ground is 0.01-0.31 per mille either way.
- **Cost:** about 0.2-0.6 ms of GPU.
- **The padding is right:** the pixel shader reads generic attribute 5 as an alpha-test coordinate, but the mesh shader writes nothing there. So the (0,0,0,1) padding most likely matches the hardware, and the points draw as solid 2-6 texel squares.

### Build

Upstream main 12ddb1fb plus #1673, #1350, #1530, #1446, #1543, #1565, #1453, #1368. One Mac, one save, one game. `scripts/regress.py` was not run. The full runs, pass dumps and images are on the reporting machine and can be shared.

— Claude, Santi's agent

body:
### Context
**Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom  
**Version:** 1.4.3 (package v720896)

### Problem
`pack_ipa.py` packs NVN shader libraries as a single `Payload/DmIOS.app/msl/b-<chain>.img`. For this title/version that file is about **2.10 GiB** (≈2,256,627,772 bytes), which is **above 2³¹−1**.

AltServer then fails with the same class of error previously seen for a bundled oversized `romfs.img`:

> The file “b-….img” couldn’t be saved in the folder “msl”

`--romfs separate` already avoids the RomFS half of this; the msl image still hits the limit.

### Workaround
```bash
python3 dm/tools/shader_lib.py expand <shader-ios>/b-<chain>
# ensure pack maps the folder (not the .img), then re-run build_ipa.sh / pack_ipa
```
Resulting IPA is still ~2.1 GB but with tens of thousands of small `msl/` members (largest on the order of a few hundred KB). The host already supports folder libraries.

### Ask
When the NVN library image would be ≥ 2 GiB, pack the IPA with the **folder** form (or otherwise split) automatically so AltServer/AltStore can install without a hand expand. Keep the single-file `.img` for smaller games and for Mac apps if desired.

Happy to test a fix against TOTK 1.4.3 with `--romfs separate` + AltServer.
title: AltServer: NVN msl single-file library ≥2 GiB fails install (TOTK 1.4.3)

body:
**1.2.3 (engine `88c7e03f51e3`), iPhone 17 (A19, g18p), iOS 27.2. The same title on an A15 iPad runs the whole prebuild under 1.1.0 (`641d1480`).**

**Symptom.** I built *Echoes of Wisdom* (`01008CF01BAAC000`, v196608) for the iPhone with the launcher's **Metal 4 pipelines** and **Pipeline prebuild** both on. The game starts with no prebuild wait at all, and then stutters exactly where the prebuild is supposed to help:

- `pipeline prebuild done: 7495 pairs, 0 bases built, 0 already archived, 7495 left to the draws, 0 failed, 0.6 s`
- 564 pipelines compiled on the submit thread, 23,310 ms across 1,133 s of play; the worst frame 2,592.8 ms (71 pipelines + 6 shader libraries), the next 1,565.1 ms; 96 frames over 100 ms
- `draws with a hybrid pipeline` is 0 for the whole session, so the stand-in path is out too: every unseen pipeline is waited for on the submit thread

Nothing in the UI says the toggles are inert for this title, and neither toggle can fix it: both are runtime settings, and the build never reads them.

**Root cause.**

1. `dm/games/01008CF01BAAC000/game.tsv` sets no `pso_mtl4` (44 lines, no such key). `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py:2379-2381` therefore has `ios_gpus` return `'none'`, and `build_framework.log` records `no pipeline archive (DM_PSO_GPUS=none)`.
2. The same key decides the pulling libraries, twice over: `:2384-2388` `ios_wants_pulling` returns False, so `:2375` calls `shader_lib.pack(..., leave_out=True)` and `dm/tools/shader_lib.py:113-115` drops every `<key>_bp.metallib` from the iOS image, leaving the marker `_bp_left_out` behind; and `:2440` sets `DMSH_IOS_PULL=0`, so dmsh_build.py never compiles them at all. They are missing before the image is packed, not merely dropped from it.
3. On the device, `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:6243` opens `<key>_bp.metallib` for each pair with a pulling entry; `:6249` logs `[RED] pulling library of … not usable (no library …): its draws wait for their pipelines`; `:7443` returns without a base (`if (!pull && [vj[@"vertex_inputs"] count]) return nil;`) and `:7463` counts the pair as left to the draws.
4. So the two halves fail together: there is no archive to open (`0 files … opened in 0.4 ms`) and no way to build one. The 99 bases written at run time (`00000.mtl4a`, 5.1 MB) are the draw-time ones, which do not need `_bp`.

**This is a change in behaviour, not a title that never worked.** The 1.1.0 pin `641d1480` has no `ios_wants_pulling` and no `DMSH_IOS_PULL` in the NSP script (0 occurrences of each), so its iOS image keeps the pulling libraries whatever the profile says. The same title, same two toggles, on an iPad mini 6 (A15), chain `95ba69b5403e`:

```
pipeline prebuild done: 7488 bases built, 7 already archived, 0 left to the draws, 0 failed, 513.3 s
```

647 MB in `pso_archive`, and 0 pipelines compiled at run time over 622 s. On the iPhone, chain `adec7d81d970`, the same prebuild builds nothing.

`cb34473fed` made the pulling libraries conditional on the profile's `pso_mtl4`. That is right for build time and wrong for a device that has to build the bases itself: `gpus == 'none'` is precisely the case where the device reads `_bp`.

`dm/ios/tools/build_ipa.sh:376` encodes the same assumption one level lower: `[ -n "${PSO:-}" ] || [ "${IOS_PULL:-$PULL}" = 1 ] || PACK_OPTS+=(--skip-suffix _bp.metallib)`. Both paths read "no archive, so nothing reads `_bp`". The case both miss is the one this title is in: **no archive, so the device builds the bases — `_bp` is then the one file it cannot do without.**

**Evidence.** Counts on the same 1.2.3 build:

```
$ strings -a shader/ios/b-adec7d81d970.img   | grep -c '_bp.metallib'
0
$ strings -a shader/cache/b-adec7d81d970.img | grep -c '_bp.metallib'    # the Mac image, same build
5268
$ strings -a shader/ios/b-adec7d81d970.img   | grep -m1 'left out'
the pulling vertex libraries are left out: nothing in this build reads them (dm/tools/shader_lib.py)
```

Device log:

```
pipeline archive .../pso_archive: 0 files (0 of bases without a vertex layout), 0.0 MB, opened in 0.4 ms
pipeline prebuild done: 7495 pairs, 0 bases built, 0 already archived, 7495 left to the draws, 0 failed, 0.6 s
[RED] pulling library of 7344d79668f81aa9_b not usable (no library: cannot open .../msl/b-adec7d81d970/7344d79668f81aa9_bp.metallib): its draws wait for their pipelines
```

**Workaround.**

- `--gpu g18p` on the build packs both halves, and the device opens the archive instead of prebuilding.
- `IOS_PULL=1` brings back only the pulling libraries; the device then waits once for the full prebuild (513 s on A15, less on A19).
- Until either is used, **Pipeline prebuild** can never do anything on this title, so switching it off loses nothing.

**Suggestions.**

1. Add `pso_mtl4 on` to this title's profile, as #1241 does for Super Mario Odyssey. Its `depth_mode zero` is already set, so the offline bases have to use `main0_z`. With that, `--gpu` defaults to `g18p` and the build packs the archive and the pulling libraries together.
2. #1177 is not in 1.2.3: the prebuild still ends `0 built … 0.6 s` with nothing that says why. Its summary line should carry the pairs skipped for a missing pulling library, so this cannot read as a finished prebuild.
3. `ios_wants_pulling` returning False when `gpus == 'none'` reads backwards: no archive means the device builds the bases, which needs `_bp`, so that is the one case where it must be true whatever `pso_mtl4` says. The same holds in `build_ipa.sh:376`, where `PSO` empty is the reason to skip `_bp`.
4. The two launcher toggles are already collected at build time (`build_framework.log: launcher: … DM_PSO_MTL4 DM_PSO_PREBUILD …`) but never reach `ios_gpus` / `ios_wants_pulling`. Reading them there would also let the build ship an archive for a profile that has no `pso_mtl4`.

**A title whose profile omits `pso_mtl4` now gets a build that can neither ship the bases nor build them, and the only trace is a 0.6 s line that looks like success. For this title the fix is one key.**
title: Echoes of Wisdom (01008CF01BAAC000): an iPhone build ships neither the archive nor the pulling libraries, and the prebuild ends in 0.6 s as if finished

body:
**Hades II: reproducible host crash in `h_codec_HwOpusFini` ~3.5 minutes into play (old hwopus C interface state misread as a manager `opus_dec`)**

## Environment
- main@f25fa956, chain 223f10d34f97, host built with Xcode 27.2 + Metal Toolchain 27B47
- M3 Pro (12-core), macOS 27.2 (26B123)
- Game: Hades II `0100A00019DE0000`, update v131072-era title data (`patched_v131497`), profile's shader map; three local host patches (window default 1080p #619, `DM_FOCUS_NOTIFY` #622, `DM_HANDOFF_CAP_US` #623) — none touch audio
- Unattended run: `DM_AUDIO_MUTE=1`, default window, ~60 fps throughout until the crash

## Repro
2/2 runs, crash at frame 12,600–12,900 (≈3.5 min of play, unattended menu/attract path — no input):

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=h_codec_HwOpusFini+0xcc lr=h_codec_HwOpusFini+0x58 sp=0x7ec51d68e0
```

Both runs same pc/lr, differing sp. No [RED] lines before it. Earlier smoke windows on the same build that stopped at ≤7,500 frames never reached it, so this may have been latent since the Opus manager work landed (67f1d005 era) and only exposed by longer runs.

## Analysis
Hades II uses the **older C hwopus interface**: `h_codec_HwOpusInit` stores the software decoder state directly in objmap under the game's handle:

```c
void *s = objmap_get(hw); if (!s) { s = calloc(1, SOFT_OPUS_STATE); objmap_put(hw, s); }
```

`h_codec_HwOpusFini` first asks `opus_mgr_dec_fini(hw)`, which does:

```c
opus_dec *d = objmap_get(hw); if (!d || !d->work) return 0;   // the older interface's state has no work buffer of its own
```

For the old interface, `objmap_get(hw)` returns the raw `SOFT_OPUS_STATE` bytes, now misread as an `opus_dec *`. The `!d->work` guard reads offset +0x10 of the software state — which is live decoder state, not a pointer, and is nonzero once the decoder has actually decoded audio. The guard then passes, and the teardown walks garbage `m`/`wait`/`done` fields of a struct that was never an `opus_dec`, ending in the null deref at `HwOpusFini+0xcc`. Consistent with the timing: decoders finalized before any decoding (state still zeroed at +0x10) take the clean old path; one finalized after ~3.5 min of audio crashes the host.

The manager form's decoders moved to the `gd + 1` key this cycle (`OPUS_MGR_KEY`), so the manager and old-interface entries no longer collide by key — but `opus_mgr_dec_fini` still type-tests the old interface's entry by content, which is the hole.

Full crash log available if useful; happy to test a candidate fix — the repro window is short and deterministic on this machine.
title: Hades II: reproducible host crash in h_codec_HwOpusFini ~3.5 min into play (old hwopus C-interface state misread as a manager opus_dec)

### What happened

Divinity: Original Sin 2 - Definitive Edition shows almost nothing: about 90 `[RED] shader … is not in the shader map` lines at startup, and black or broken screens. The shader split finds only 73 shaders, all of them from `main`:

```
✓ [6/9] shader split (0:29): 73 shaders
```

The game keeps everything else in 47 Larian LSPK archives under `Data/` (10.6 GB, `.pak`), which the split does not read.
- **Archive format:** version 13. The file ends with the header length and `LSPK`, and the file list is an LZ4 block of 280-byte entries, stored, zlib or LZ4.
- **Where the shaders are:** the compiled shaders are the `.bshd` entries of `Materials.pak` (5,448), `EngineShaders.pak` (152) and `Engine.pak` (135).
- **What a `.bshd` holds:** 4 header bytes (bit 31 set, then the length), then a zlib stream with the program's GLSLC outputs. That is a vertex and a pixel shader in 5,703 of them, and one compute shader in 5. 27 hold no compiled code, only names and reflection.

The diff below adds `lspk_entries`, `lspk_jobs` and `lspk_shaders` to `shader_split.py`, the same way as the other archive readers (`kpka_jobs`, `pkz_jobs`). Only the `.bshd` entries are read, every file found is passed to the existing `glslc_shaders`, and a program's two stages get one `#var` label so `var_pairs` pairs them. Other LSPK versions are named in red and left out. `dm/tools/tests/test_split_lspk.py` (new, synthetic archives) checks the file list, every compression and the pairing.

On d70e6a3 with this change, for 010027400CDC6000 v786432:
- The split finds 12,329 shaders, and all of them build (`Mac shaders: 12,329 of 12,329`).
- On the Mac, the loading screen, the title screen and the hints draw correctly at the game's 30 fps, with no `[RED]` shader line.

Not checked: `regress.py`, any other game, iPhone. Still open, and not part of this change: after A on the title screen, the game stays on the loading screen. It keeps reading `Mods/DOS2_Arena/meta.lsx` from `Arena.pak` about 40 times a second, and it does not crash.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..fb4d223
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dm/tools/tests/test_split_lspk.py
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+"""shader_split: Larian LSPK archives, version 13 (Divinity: Original Sin 2 - Definitive Edition's Data/*.pak), are read by their file list at the end of the file, and the compiled
+shaders among their entries (.bshd: 4 header bytes, then a zlib stream of GLSLC outputs) are scanned; a program's vertex and pixel shaders pair. No game files needed."""
+import os
+import struct
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+import zlib
+from unittest import mock
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / 'dm/gfx/tools'))
+_had = os.environ.get('DM_GAME'); os.environ['DM_GAME'] = '010029B0118E8000'   # shader_split loads a profile at import; other tests expect no default game
+import shader_split as ss
+if _had is None: del os.environ['DM_GAME']
+else: os.environ['DM_GAME'] = _had
+import lz4.block
+
+
+def lspk(files):
+    """files: [(name, bytes, flags)] → a version 13 LSPK: the data, the LZ4 file list, the header and its length + 'LSPK' at the end"""
+    data, ents = b'', b''
+    for name, body, flags in files:
+        stored = zlib.compress(body) if flags & 0xf == 1 else lz4.block.compress(body, store_size=False) if flags & 0xf == 2 else body
+        ents += struct.pack('<256sIIIIII', name.encode(), len(data), len(stored), len(body) if flags & 0xf else 0, 0, flags, 0)
+        data += stored
+    lo = len(data); lst = struct.pack('<I', len(files)) + lz4.block.compress(ents, store_size=False)
+    head = struct.pack('<IIIHBB', 13, lo, len(lst), 1, 0, 0) + bytes(16)
+    return data + lst + head + struct.pack('<I4s', len(head) + 8, b'LSPK')
+
+
+def bshd(payload):
+    z = zlib.compress(payload)
+    return struct.pack('>I', 0x80000000 | len(payload)) + z
+
+
+class Lspk(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(); self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+
+    def write(self, name, b):
+        p = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, name); open(p, 'wb').write(b); return p
+
+    def test_entries_and_jobs(self):
+        p = self.write('Materials.pak', lspk([('Public/A_NX.bshd', bshd(b'one'), 0), ('Public/A.lsb', b'x' * 40, 2), ('Shaders/NX/B.bshd', bshd(b'two'), 1)]))
+        es = ss.lspk_entries(p)
+        self.assertEqual([e[0] for e in es], ['Public/A_NX.bshd', 'Public/A.lsb', 'Shaders/NX/B.bshd'])
+        jobs, taken = ss.lspk_jobs([(p, 'Data/Materials.pak'), (self.write('other.pak', b'not an archive' * 4), 'Data/other.pak')])
+        self.assertEqual(taken, {p})
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(e[0] for _, _, (tag, ents) in jobs for e in ents), ['Public/A_NX.bshd', 'Shaders/NX/B.bshd'])   # only the compiled shaders
+        self.assertTrue(all(tag == ss.LSPK for _, _, (tag, _) in jobs))
+
+    def test_a_program_pairs_and_every_compression_is_read(self):
+        p = self.write('Shaders.pak', lspk([('S/Stored.bshd', bshd(b'P1'), 0), ('S/Zlib.bshd', bshd(b'P2'), 1), ('S/Lz4.bshd', bshd(b'P3'), 2), ('S/Compute.bshd', bshd(b'C'), 0)]))
+        seen = []
+        def fake(d, label, need=True, skip=()):   # stands in for the GLSLC scan: what it was given, and a program of each payload
+            seen.append(d)
+            return [(f'{label}#GLSLC@0x18', 'cs', b'c', b'k')] if d == b'C' else [(f'{label}#GLSLC@0x18', 'vs', d + b'v', b'k'), (f'{label}#GLSLC@0xf18', 'ps', d + b'p', b'k')]
+        out = []
+        with mock.patch.object(ss, 'glslc_shaders', side_effect=fake):
+            ss.lspk_shaders(p, 'Data/Shaders.pak', tuple(ss.lspk_entries(p)), out)
+        self.assertEqual(seen, [b'P1', b'P2', b'P3', b'C'])   # each entry decompressed by its flags, then its zlib stream
+        pairs = [w for w, *_ in out if w.endswith('#var')]
+        self.assertEqual(len(pairs), 6)   # vertex and pixel of each program share a label, so var_pairs pairs them
+        with mock.patch.object(ss, 'skey', side_effect=lambda ctl, code: ctl):   # the stand-in sections are no real control sections
+            self.assertEqual(len(ss.var_pairs(out)), 3)
+        self.assertIn(('/Data/Shaders.pak#S/Compute.bshd#GLSLC@0x18', 'cs', b'c', b'k'), out)   # a compute shader stays alone
+
+    def test_other_versions_and_files_are_no_lspk(self):
+        self.assertIsNone(ss.lspk_entries(self.write('short.pak', b'LSPK')))
+        b = bytearray(lspk([('a.bshd', bshd(b'x'), 0)])); hs = struct.unpack_from('<I', b, len(b) - 8)[0]; struct.pack_into('<I', b, len(b) - hs, 15)
+        with mock.patch.object(ss, 'red') as red:
+            self.assertIsNone(ss.lspk_entries(self.write('v15.pak', bytes(b))))
+        red.assert_called_once()
+

body:
### What happened

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000, v131072). Since b97f0dc6, parts of the Deku Tree's walls are not drawn. In Gohma's room the lit surface behind the wall shows through jagged holes. The holes stay fixed on the wall as the camera moves, and some wall pieces only appear when Link stands right next to them.

- Bad: shader libraries from b97f0dc6 onward, still on main as of 7fe9fc4d.
- Good: the same host with libraries from 1a410e6e, or from b2d46b86.

No [RED] line in the log.

### Bisect

1. The host is not the cause. A host from 7fe9fc4d with the good libraries draws the walls. The pipeline archives are not the cause either: with no archive at all, the holes are still there.
2. I found which shader does it by laying single shaders over the good library: a `b-<chain>/` folder beside the good `.img`, with the reflection's `"chain"` restamped.
   - The frame at the warp in Gohma's room uses 434 shaders, and 66 of them differ between the good and bad libraries.
   - Halving those 66 leaves one: **`35785cddc971290c`**, a mesh shader (`Model.Product.110.product.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha`, BNSH@0x11543000, var810).
   - That shader from the bad build alone makes the holes. The other 65 changed shaders together do not.
3. I translated that one shader with the translator from each commit between b2d46b86 and 13b432b4. Its MSL is byte-identical up to 1a410e6e and changes first at b97f0dc6.

### The change in that shader

All the differences come from the LEA part of b97f0dc6. Twelve `LEA.HI` with bit 73 set and shift 16 changed:

```
// before b97f0dc6 (high word from c, here zero)
uint t = uint(int(uint(a) >> uint(16)));
int  r = int(t) + b;

// since b97f0dc6 (bit 73 read as .SX32: the high word is a's sign)
int  hi = a >> 31;
int  t  = (hi << 16) | int(uint(a) >> 16);
int  r  = t + b;
```

I reverted only this line of b97f0dc6 and rebuilt the translator from source:

```
Operand hi = x.Bit(73) ? context.ShiftRightS32(lo, Const(31)) : AGet(context, c);
```

to `Operand hi = AGet(context, c);`. The shader's MSL is then byte-identical to 1a410e6e's. A full library build with only that line reverted, and everything else as on 7fe9fc4d, draws the walls whole: no red line, 60 fps. The IADD3, PLOP3, POPC/FLO and negated-B parts of b97f0dc6 do not change this shader.

So for these instructions, either bit 73 is not .SX32 in this form, or .SX32 does not sign-extend the shifted value like this. These are 16-bit unpacks (`a >> 16` plus an offset) in a mesh shader. Checking this shader's LEA.HI encodings with nvdisasm should settle it.

### Setup

- MacBook Pro, Apple M5 Pro, 24 GB, macOS 27.0.1, Metal 32023.922.
- Built from 7fe9fc4d plus a few open PRs (the host is not involved, see the bisect).
- Bad chain 57da6a2d2750 (also d866f9700d78 and d8b43fd2152e), good chain 5c852d7989ac.
title: Ocarina of Time: holes in the Deku Tree's walls since b97f0dc6 (LEA.HI bit 73 read as .SX32)

### What happened

The NSP script stops at the UE shader decode step for Tetris Effect: Connected:

```
[RED] the RomFS has Unreal paks, but none under …/extract/v1310720/RomFS.img holds a shader code archive: where the shaders are has to be found first
```

It stops at every build. The cause is in `uepak.inline_shaders`. `TetrisEffect-Switch.pak` (version 11, UE 4.26) has an encrypted index, and `inline_shaders` returns `False` for any encrypted index, as for Octopath Traveler 0's. So the pak counts as one with shader code archives. But read with the key from main (`find_key`), its 1,625 files hold no `.ushaderbytecode`, only `Engine/GlobalShaderCache-SF_GLSL_SWITCH.bin`. The materials' shaders are inline in the export bundles of `TetrisEffect-Switch.utoc` (TOC version 3, 10,271 bundles, no shader library), the same layout as Mario & Luigi: Brothership.

The local changes:
- `inline_shaders` reads an encrypted index with the key from the game's mains (`uepak.pak_key`, kept per pak and per list of mains), then applies the same test as to a plain index.
- Without a key, it answers as before.
- `unreal_paks`, `profile_guess.build_sources`, `shader_split`'s inline check and `uepak.job` pass the mains.

It builds on #1646, which is still open: it uses `find_key(…, first=)` and `ue_legacy_jobs(…, mains=)`, and the shader split needs it to read the encrypted pak's entries.

With #1646 and this change on c8bfa16:
- The build of 0100DE501433A000 v1310720 goes through. The shader split finds 11,923 shaders and all of them build.
- The game reaches its title screen and plays with no `[RED]` line, given two other changes that are not part of this report (#1668).
- The `uepak` tests (39, one new: an encrypted v11 index with a synthetic key in a synthetic main), `test_uepak_v8`, `test_uepak_legacy_key`, `test_uepak_key` and `test_profile_guess` pass.

Not checked: `regress.py` and any other game.

The build goes on to the shader split, which reads the global shader cache from the pak and the materials from the container.

Tetris Effect: Connected, 0100DE501433A000, 2.0.2.2 (v1310720)

88c7e03 (the engine NX2Apple 1.2.3 ships) for the failing build; current `main` (c8bfa16) has the same `inline_shaders`

body:
### What is missing

The open question in [Online SDKs in NROs are never loaded](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/services.md#online-sdks-in-nros-are-never-loaded) ("always load, refuse online SDKs (as now), or decide per profile") now has a game where refusing breaks it.

Tetris Effect: Connected (0100DE501433A000, 2.0.2.2 / v1310720, UE 4.26, provisional profile) registers `nro/EOSSDK-Switch-Shipping.nro` in `ModuleInfo.nrr` and uses it through the Redpoint EOS online subsystem. With the NRR refused (`ro::RegisterModuleInfo: refused an NRR that registers only online SDKs (1 hashes)`), it reaches the title screen and then crashes about 24 s in: `CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=main+0xb64bec`. Just before, the code builds `FName(TEXT("RedpointEOS"))`, gets the subsystem, and calls its virtual at +0x58 for an interface. The interface comes back null, and the code calls through it without checking. Unlike Hades and Absolum, this game has no offline path for a missing EOS platform.

With the NRO packed and loaded (a local experiment that skips the `ONLINE_SDKS` refusal in `nro_collect.py` and the `EOS_Platform_Create` check in `ro::LoadModule`), the game goes through the warning screens and the title into play at 60 fps, with no `[RED]` line, over about 90 s on a MacBook Pro M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1. Checked from the frame-time lines and screenshots. Audio and saves were not checked. The build was c8bfa16 with #1646 and two other local changes. The host was offline as always: `nifm` says no network, `Socket` / SSL fail, so the SDK reached nothing.

Loading it also showed a host bug that only an online SDK reaches. The host's event descriptors start at `EFD_BASE = 0x4000`, and the SDK's network thread puts one in an `fd_set` (`FD_SET` after `_nnmusl_socket_TranslateNnmuslFileDescriptorOrPassThrough`, `nro0+0x9886b0`). Bit 16384 of a 1024-bit set is about 1.9 KB past it on that thread's stack: SIGBUS. Small descriptor numbers (3 up), with `Select` answering for event descriptors as `Poll` does, fixed it locally.

### What you propose

Which of the three the docs list do you want: always load, keep refusing, or decide per profile (for example a profile key that lets a game load its online SDK, while every other game keeps refusing)?

### Platforms

Mac (checked); iPhone and iPad (not checked)
title: Online SDKs in NROs: Tetris Effect: Connected (0100DE501433A000) needs its Epic Online Services NRO loaded

### What happened

On an iPad the game aborts about 7–10 minutes into play (frames ~13,200 and ~19,500 in two runs) when it first reaches an indirect mesh draw. The deferred encoder (**Encode thread, on by default on iOS**) has no stand-in for that Metal call:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] FATAL deferred encoding: DmRecEnc has no stand-in for -drawMeshThreadgroupsWithIndirectBuffer:threadsPerObjectThreadgroup:threadsPerMeshThreadgroup: (DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0 runs without it)
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8 pc=__pthread_kill+0x8 lr=pthread_kill+0x10c
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 -[DmRecEnc forwardingTargetForSelector:]+0 -[DmRecCB forwardingTargetForSelector:]+0 <redacted>+0x98 <redacted>+0x60 mtk_encode+0x1fc draw_+0x704c draw+0x374 mtl_exec+0xff4 mtl_exec+0x76c mtl_exec+0x76c h_nvnQueueSubmitCommands+0x12c ...
```

Both runs had the shell's "Encode thread" setting at its default (`boot: DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`). With "Encode thread" turned off in the game's settings (`boot: DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0`), a 20 minute run did not hit it.

A related observation (possibly a docs mismatch, not sure of the cause): putting `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0` in `Documents/env.txt` did **not** turn it off here. The next boot log still said `boot: DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1` and `boot: DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=` was empty, whereas in the same shell app `DM_ALIAS_SIZE` from the same `Documents/env.txt` was applied (`DM_ENV_FILE_KEYS=DM_ALIAS_SIZE`). `docs/playing.md` says lines like `DM_OPMODE=0` in `Documents/env.txt` win over the settings screen, so either that is not true for settings that the game's list offers (such as this one), or the file was not read for this key. The switch in the game's settings did work.

### What you expected

Either a stand-in for `drawMeshThreadgroupsWithIndirectBuffer…` in `DmRecEnc`, or Encode thread defaulting to off in this game's profile on iOS, so an iPhone or iPad player does not hit this around the 10 minute mark.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), 0400486024DEC000, update v131072, built from a NUP.

Not recorded in the log; NX2Apple 1.2.3's engine pin `88c7e03f51e3`.

`build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NUP> --shell-framework`, then `build_shell.sh --prepare-xcode` (one game in the shared app) and installed with `devicectl`.

body:
Just reporting this in case it helps with development. I played the game and ran the tests myself, and used an AI assistant to help read the logs and the Instruments trace and write this up. Happy to rerun anything you need on my M2 Max. Below are my + ai's findings.

## Setup

- **Mac:** MacBook Pro 16" (Mac14,6), Apple M2 Max with 38-core GPU, 32 GB, on AC power
- **OS / tools:** macOS 27.2 (26B123), Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Metal Toolchain 32023.922
- **Launcher:** NX2Apple 1.2.3 (bundled engine), shader chain `adec7d81d970`, commit not recorded in the log
- **Game:** Switch 2 NUP, update v131072 only (no base game in the NUP), built with `--platform mac-app`
- **Settings:** Handheld (`DM_OPMODE=0`), `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`, window mode
- **env.txt:** `DM_FOCUS_KEEP=1`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0`, `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`

## Symptom

In Kokiri Forest, gameplay runs at about **39 fps**. The game's speed follows its frame rate, so everything plays in slow motion and audio drifts out of sync with the picture. Movies and the title screen hold 60 fps with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`, and about 35 fps without it. Docked mode runs about the same as Handheld (GPU p50 25-29 ms), so the cost doesn't scale with resolution. Dynamic resolution settles the main pass at 854x480.

## Measurements (Kokiri Forest, settled)

**Host log:**

```
timing: frame time p50 ~25.2 ms / p95 ~28 ms; NVN submit+present p50 ~10-11 ms; GPU p50 ~24.5 ms
power: ~39.5 fps, CPU ~336% (one core = 100%)
```

**Metal System Trace** (Instruments, 8 s, attached to dmhost):

- **GPU performance state:** Maximum for the whole capture. Game Mode is not involved: `LSSupportsGameMode` is false and gamepolicyd started no gaming session.
- **GPU busy, any channel:** **~71%**. Compute 36-38%, fragment 20-25%, vertex 14-18%.
- **GPU idle between encoders:** **~11-13 ms per frame**.
- **Encoders per frame:** ~165 compute (median ~1 us each), ~94 render passes, ~10 vertex-only.

**`DM_NVN_GPUPROF` (frame 1200, gameplay):**

- **Frame-start compute batch:** `compute / copy after pass ...141 ... dispatches 115` takes **8313 us**, about half of the frame's 16.0 ms total encoder time.
- **Next biggest encoders:**
  - a compute/copy of 1337 us
  - render passes at 854x480 of 758, 495, 412 and 382 us; each loads 3.2 MB and stores 1.6-3.2 MB
- **Frame span:** 25.6 ms, of which ~16.0 ms is GPU work.

## Switches tried (each one alone, on top of the env.txt above)

| Switch | Gameplay fps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DM_NVN_TBDR=0` | 41.0 | Gameplay about the same; movies fall to ~35 fps |
| `DM_NVN_TBDR=1` (baseline) | 39.5 | Movies locked at 60 |

body:
Since 463d21f7 (PR #859), a keyboard receiver becomes player 1 on the Mac, and the real controller is pushed to player 2.

**Setup:** macOS 27.0.1, M3 Max. A Keychron Link receiver (3434:d030, keyboard and mouse dongle) over USB, and a Nintendo Pro Controller over Bluetooth. Main at d777f0a3. The controller code is unchanged on my branch (`pad_hid_mac.h`, `pad_hid.h`, `pad_slots.h`).

**What happens** (Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000):

```
[dm] controller 'Keychron Link ' (HID, 3434:d030): GameController says it lists it but has not after 2 s, so it is read as HID
[dm] controller 'Keychron Link ' (HID) connected: player 1 (npad 0)
[dm] controller 'Pro Controller' connected: player 2 (npad 1), with motion (gyro)
[dm] hid controller applet: 1 to 1 players wanted, 2 connected
```

The game wants one player, so it reads only player 1, the receiver. The Pro Controller does nothing. The controller applet is then opened again and again (`1 to 1 players wanted, 2 connected`).

**Before 463d21f7:** the same setup worked. A device that `+[GCController supportsHIDDevice:]` answered YES for was skipped, so the receiver never became a pad.

**Cause, as far as I can see:** the receiver exposes a Generic Desktop GamePad or Joystick collection, so it matches the HID pad filter (`pad_hid_mac.h`, the matching dictionaries at line 246). `supportsHIDDevice:` answers YES for it, GameController never lists it, and after `HIDPAD_GC_WAIT` it is read as HID. It never sends input, but it takes the lowest free player.

**Workaround:** `DM_HID_PADS=0` in the player's `env.txt`. The Pro Controller is player 1 again.

**Possible fixes:**
- Do not give a player to a raw HID pad that was only hinted (`gc_hint`) until it sends its first button press.
- Or skip devices that also expose a keyboard or mouse collection.
title: Mac: a keyboard receiver (Keychron Link) becomes player 1 as a raw HID pad since PR #859

### What happened

Since main's 473c9026 (a pixel shader's depth after a partly written target), a dark box surrounds each kart's shadow on the title screen and in races, and the other vehicles' shadows have one too. The shadow's shape is right inside the box; the box itself is uniformly dark.

473c9026 is right: it made the agl `agl_common` depth downsample (`3738806f0474308c`, mask 0x100) write a real 480x270 depth where it used to be far everywhere. That depth is what lets the box decal `8206d20d0055515d` reach the ground for the first time, and the decal shows a host bug:

- The blob shadows are two R8 2D arrays, 64x64x128 and 128x128x64, one layer per character or vehicle. A draw copies each silhouette into level 0 of its layer; a compute pass then writes that layer's mips through one-layer array views bound to image slots its shader declares as 2D (`DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` `W` lines: `target=3 shader wants target 2`).
- `img_binding` adapts only the format class of an image slot, not its type, so the array view goes to a `texture2d` argument as is, and Metal drops the stores. Levels 1 and 2 of every layer stay zero (dumped with `DM_CTL texraw`), while level 0 is right.
- The decal samples with implicit level of detail. The box is small on screen, so it reads those zero mips: blob = 0 means full shadow across the whole box.

Checks: dropping the decal (`DM_NVN_SKIP_FS=8206d20d0055515d`) removes the box in the same scene; an override that outputs the decal's raw sample shows the whole projected box at 0; one that draws its UVs shows them varying normally, so the projection and the depth are fine.

### What you expected

Soft blob shadows under the karts, no box.

### Game, title ID and version

Mario Kart World, 0400C3F00006E000, base game v0 (dump)

### nxnative commit

3ccb7da0 (and later main; first seen after the rebase past 473c9026)

### Shader chain version

b1b4b0b399f0 (main's chain plus local profile work; the box comes from the host, not the chain)

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py games/MarioKartWorld --platform mac`, run headless and windowed with `DM_GUEST_FILE=1 DM_OPMODE=0`

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro M1 Pro, 16 GB, macOS 27.2

### Settings and environment overrides

`DM_GUEST_FILE=1`, `DM_OPMODE=0` (handheld)

### Logs

No red line points at it. The pass dump's image lines for the mip pass: `W … st5 reg0 … ser=… fmt=10 64x64 view_sl=10 array=1 target=3 shader wants target 2`, and the same for 32x32 and 16x16.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
