### What happened

The game aborts within a second of boot, before the first picture. The same game files, patch and settings built from an earlier nxnative (around 10/31) play fine.

The swap chain is 3 textures, 1920x1080, format 0x25. Its storage is now classified as CPU-written. The log lists ser=3…6 (1920x1080 format 0x25 target 1) as "CPU-written texture … uploaded / re-uploaded like a swizzled texture". So when the present thread resolves the presented texture, tex_mtl_ takes the packaged path, calls pkg_upload and then up_begin. up_owner_check then aborts:

[dm] [nvn-mtl] CPU-written texture ser=3 1920x1080x1 format 0x25 target 1 levels 1: uploaded / re-uploaded like a swizzled texture
[dm] [nvn-mtl] CPU-written texture ser=4 1920x1080x1 format 0x25 target 1 levels 1: uploaded / re-uploaded like a swizzled texture
[dm] [nvn-mtl] CPU-written texture ser=5 1920x1080x1 format 0x25 target 1 levels 1: uploaded / re-uploaded like a swizzled texture
[dm] [nvn-mtl] CPU-written texture ser=6 1920x1080x1 format 0x25 target 1 levels 1: uploaded / re-uploaded like a swizzled texture
...
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] GPU deswizzle does not support format 0x25 target 5; falling back to the CPU
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] deswizzle failed format 0x25 target 5
...
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] upload batches belong to the submit thread only: up_begin called on thread 'nvn-present'
0   DmIOS  up_owner_check.cold.1 + 104
1   DmIOS  __up_flush_block_invoke + 0
2   DmIOS  up_begin + 28
3   DmIOS  pkg_upload + 1488
4   DmIOS  tex_mtl_ + 2928
5   DmIOS  tex_mtl + 84
6   DmIOS  present_now + 692
7   DmIOS  present_main + 372
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8

Runs:

On 581f9c1d (11/07 12:31), the same abort happened on thread nvn-present-link, through -[NvMetalDisplayLinkDelegate metalDisplayLink:needsUpdate:] → present_now → tex_mtl → pkg_upload → up_begin.
On 822f724c (11/07 09:20), the same abort happened on thread nvn-present, as above. So e2b76d4e / b547f1e2 are not the cause.

My guess, not verified by bisecting: 733dff9d (11/04, "COMPRESSIBLE textures in a pool the CPU writes keep their content") or 75e5ddd8 (11/04, "Uncompressed textures the CPU wrote, in a pool the GPU has not written, take their storage at first use"). This game's profile README says its textures are in a CPU_CACHED | GPU_CACHED | COMPRESSIBLE pool (flags 0xa4) and use tex_dirty_upload. The swap-chain textures probably share that pool, so they would now count as CPU-written. I will report back with a build from e250bb8b (the parent of 733dff9d).

### What you expected

The game boots to the title as it did before. A present-time texture resolution should never start an upload batch on the present thread. The swap-chain images the GPU renders into should not be treated as CPU-written.

The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles (Japanese release, 大逆転裁判1&2), 0100D7F00FB1A000, base 1.0.0 (v0), DLC 0100D7F00FB1B001 (v65536). Built with --profile-from 010036E00FB20000, as for GitHub issue #568.

body:
With **Press a button to join** on (`DM_PAD_PRESS_TO_JOIN=1`, 62be7fac), a connected controller is no player until it presses a button. When a game opens the controller applet (`nn::hid::ShowControllerSupport`) wanting more players than have joined, the host's stand-in (`ctrl_support`, `dm/host/hle_hid.c`) answers at once and cancels, as a player closing it would. Seen in Mario Kart World 1.8.0 on the Mac (PR #1596): `hid controller applet: 2 to 2 players wanted, 1 connected: too few, closed as the player would (canceled)`, and the game's player screen closed.

On a Switch the applet stays open until enough controllers are there, or the player closes it. Without press-to-join the host has nothing to wait for, but with it, it does: controllers that are connected and not yet joined.

What a fix needs to settle:

- Wait on the game's thread inside the stand-in until `playerCountMin` have joined, with a way to cancel (B or Escape, a time limit, or the window losing focus), and an answer when no controller is waiting at all.
- Something on screen while it waits (the Mac's Home-quit prompt has an overlay to borrow; iOS has its own views), saying how many players are wanted and joined.
- Both front ends: the waiting count comes from `front_mac.m` and `DmGamepad.m`.

Until then, `docs/settings.md` says to press a button on every controller before the game asks how many play.
title: Controller applet stand-in: with Press a button to join on, wait for presses instead of cancelling

body:
### What happened

The intro movie never plays. Umineko no Naku Koro ni Saku ~Nekobako to Musou no Koukyoukyoku~ boots on the iPhone, and menus and gameplay render fine at 60 fps. At the intro movie (H.264 1920×1080 High profile + AAC 2ch 48 kHz, through `movie::Decoder` from `subsdk0` NintendoSDK_movie), the screen stays almost empty (2 draws per frame) for about 10 s. Then the game destroys both decoders and goes on to the title. It happens every time: two runs gave identical counts.

```
[movie] decoder 0x701094d440 destroyed: 12 packets in, 11 frames out; decoded 12 packets, average 0.34 ms per packet, longest 3.74 ms   (AAC)
[movie] decoder 0x701094d3c0 destroyed: 8 packets in, 4 frames out; decoded 8 packets, average 3.11 ms per packet, longest 8.86 ms     (AVC, reorder depth 4)
```

With `DM_MOVIE_TRACE=1`, the game's threads are:
- `0x1717bb000`: demux / feeder (every `SendInputBufferForDecode`)
- `0x1718c7000`: video consumer
- `0x1719d3000`: audio consumer

The decoders are `0x1099bbc00` (video) and `0x1099bf800` (audio). The trace shows:

1. **Audio:** each `SendInputBufferForDecode` on the feeder is followed by `AcquireOutputBufferIndex` on the audio thread, for 11 packets.
2. **Audio stops:** the 12th AAC packet (`index 0 length 676 time 256000 µs`, "1 packets queued") is sent, and the audio thread never calls `AcquireOutputBufferIndex` again. There are no more audio calls at all.
3. **Video:** 8 packets go in (pts 33366 … 266933, out of order as expected with reorder depth 4). VideoToolbox returns 4 frames (33366, 66733, 100100, 133466). The video thread releases each one and re-acquires input buffers 2, 1, 0 (`→ 0`), but the feeder sends no further video packets.
4. **Nothing else:** no movie calls for about 10 s, until both decoders are destroyed.

So the stall starts at the last audio packet. It is queued in the host decoder, but its output is never picked up. Perhaps the output-available event is not signalled, or it is signalled before the game waits on it. The game's feeder seems to pace on the audio clock, so video stops too.

```
[0x1717bb000] [0x1099bf800] SendInputBufferForDecode index 1 offset 0 length 676 time 234666 µs flags 0 (1 packets queued)
[0x1719d3000] [0x1099bf800] AcquireOutputBufferIndex → index 0 time 234666 flags 0 left 0
[0x1719d3000] [0x1099bf800] GetOutputBuffer index 0 → PCM 4096 bytes
[0x1719d3000] [0x1099bf800] release output index 0 (0 packets queued)
[0x1717bb000] [0x1099bf800] SendInputBufferForDecode index 0 offset 0 length 676 time 256000 µs flags 0 (1 packets queued)   <- never output
[0x1718c7000] [0x1099bbc00] AcquireInputBufferIndex → 0 index 2 left 0
[0x1717bb000] [0x1099bbc00] SendInputBufferForDecode index 2 offset 0 length 7898 time 266933 µs flags 0 (3 packets queued)
[0x1717bb000] [0x1099bbc00] SendInputBufferForDecode index 1 offset 0 length 217 time 200200 µs flags 0 (3 packets queued)
[0x1717bb000] [0x1099bbc00] SendInputBufferForDecode index 0 offset 0 length 2938 time 233566 µs flags 0 (3 packets queued)
[0x1718c7000] [0x1099bbc00] AcquireOutputBufferIndex → index 0 time 33366 flags 0 left 0
...
[0x1718c7000] [0x1099bbc00] AcquireOutputBufferIndex → index 1 time 133466 flags 0 left 0
[0x1718c7000] [0x1099bbc00] release output index 1 (0 packets queued)
(no movie calls for ~10 s, then both decoders are destroyed)
```

Setup lines:
```
[movie] decoder 0x701094d3c0: type 1 output 4 mode 1 priority 16
[movie] Configure: MediaData width 1920 height 1080
[movie] decoder 0x701094d440: type 4 output 1 mode 1 priority 16
[movie] Configure (AAC): 2 channels 48000 Hz, headers 0 + 0 bytes
[movie] AAC: 2 channels 48000 Hz, AudioSpecificConfig 2 bytes (object type 2)
[movie] AVC: VideoToolbox decoding 1920×1080, profile 100, reorder depth 4
```

The intro movie plays with picture and sound, as it does in Ryujinx with the same game files.

body:
## What happened

Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope (regional title ID `0100FC60185AE000`) exited during static initialization, before `nnMain`. The iPhone build and a Mac host using the same 5 GB guest layout hit SIGBUS at `main+0x164990` on a write to `0x20000ffff`. The Snowdrop constructor requested a 12 GB virtual reservation while the profile's alias range was 4.375 GiB.

With the seven local build-gated cuts, the same Mac layout reached `nnMain` and ran for an eight-second smoke test. The cuts sized the three page ranges and the reservation to fit, adjusted the large allocator's page count, and reduced the unused slot pool from 4,194,304 slots to 65,536. The resulting unsigned iOS framework built successfully.

## What I expected

This regional build starts with a guest layout that fits the available virtual address space.

## Game, title ID and version

- Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, `0100FC60185AE000`.
- Update `v393216`, display version `1.6.2225577`.
- Main build `2545826ca04fc82c8cc6cc426281edf3`.

## nxnative commit and shader chain

The original failing build used chain `95ba69b5403e`. Its exact engine revision was not retained. The follow-up framework used `b-223f10d34f97`. The results above are from the November 5–6 local tests.

I checked current source at `08c27ed7`. The generalized Snowdrop matcher in [eae1d0a0](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/eae1d0a0290c5cff5f99ec5d177495baede8f031) now covers the page-pool constructor. The separate slot-pool cut in the Sparks of Hope profile is registered for `0100317013770000`, main build `5b76a43b231e0640521ac66203f7c178`. I could not find this regional ID or build in the profile tables.

## How it was built and run

NX2Apple iPhone build and a terminal Mac host using the same guest layout, with a local exact-build profile. Extend RAM was enabled during the original phone report. The archived Mac smoke test covers startup. The latest matcher and the slot-pool cut have not been isolated in a new runtime test for this exact build.

## Logs and related issue

Recorded crash tuple: `SIGBUS`, `main+0x164990`, write to `0x20000ffff`, before `nnMain`. This report is for the startup path in the regional build above. [#1010](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/1010) tracks the first-planet abort in the other regional build.

- [x] Nothing attached contains game files, keys, or extracted game data.
title: Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope (0100FC60185AE000): startup SIGBUS on the regional build

body:
### What happened

In NX2Apple 1.2.3, build Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter using the Asian release with update 1.0.7. The build extracts ExeFS and RomFS and generates a provisional profile. It then aborts while rewriting ExeFS `main`, leaving `patched_v458752.partial`. Observed in one build.

### What you expected

The main NSO rewrite completes and the build proceeds to packaging.

### Game, title ID and version

Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter (하늘의 궤적 the 1st), Asian release, Title ID `01001E9023920000`, update `1.0.7 (v458752)`, SDK 21, main Build ID `4f4fd1aed39eb96a649aba489ad3767d`. DLC present in the build.

### nxnative commit

NX2Apple engine snapshot `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03-46919438b5de`.

### Shader chain version

`adec7d81d970`.

### How it was built and run

The NSP script failed before anything ran. Build started through NX2Apple 1.2.3.

### Device and OS

Apple M4 (Mac16,10), macOS 27.3 (26C5035r), Xcode 27.2 (27B52).

### Settings and environment overrides

The build used an automatically generated provisional profile. Other overrides were not verified.

### Logs

Full contents of `rewrite_main.log`, with the local path shortened. The full launcher console output is unavailable.

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "dm/tools/patch_nso.py", line 1311, in <module>
    assert not any(y.address in done for y in rb[0]), f'retry block overlaps a window {rb[0][0].address:x}'
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AssertionError: retry block overlaps a window 2cd3a0
```

### Related work

- #176 targets the same Title ID on 1.0.6.1 and describes a similar exclusive-window rewriter failure. This report is for 1.0.7 with a different main Build ID.
- #877 tracks another regional release (`01002C9022770000`), whose comments also report this assertion at `0x2cdeb4`.
- #1171 fixes the same assertion in Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter. Whether that patch also fixes this build is untested.

body:
### What is missing

The NSP script knows an update's version only from the `[v<N>]` tag in its file name: [`version_of`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L540-L542), called by [`scan_nsps`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L593), and [`nsp_versions`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L681-L691) maps the profile's build rows to update files by that tag.

The package says its version itself, in its content meta. The script already reads the content meta in two other cases:

- for a merged package ([L584](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L584), `nx_extract --contents`, #842);
- for the title ID of a package with neither a ticket nor a tag (85578fc9, from #666).

It does not read it for the version of an ordinary update.

What the name decides today (main 581f9c1d):

- **No tag.**
  - A single untagged update is taken for the newest version the profile registers.
  - When the folder holds any other update, every untagged one is left out (`[RED] leaving out update NSPs without a version tag`, [L690](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L690)).
  - PR #393 works around one such name, `….v720896.UPD.nsp`, by parsing more forms of it.
- **A wrong tag.** The file is taken for the version its tag says.
  - The newest version is chosen by tag ([L3019](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L3019), `max(have, key=vnum)`), so with several updates a wrong tag can pick the wrong file.
  - For a registered version, the extracted modules' build IDs then differ from the build row. The script does not stop: it packs from a derived profile instead ([L3073-L3076](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L3073-L3076)), without that build's fixes, and only after the whole extraction.
  - Only a provisional profile stops on the mismatch.

Tags do drift in real collections. A base NSZ of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse (0100BA4026E94000) here was tagged `[v0]`, while its content meta and cnmt.xml both say v65536 (1.1.0): the eShop serves that base at 1.1.0. A base's tag is ignored, so that one did no harm. The same slip on an update would go unnoticed until the fallback above.

### What you propose

Take each update's and DLC's version from its content meta, as merged packages already do, and keep the `[v<N>]` tag only as a cross-check: when they disagree, the scan says so before any extraction.

- A file's name then no longer matters to the build: untagged updates work however many there are, and a wrong tag is reported in the first seconds instead of after the extraction.
- The cost is small. [`check_keys`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/581f9c1dbcee690b24f4e2a376ca51e2f4fa07b1/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L2982) already builds the probe nx_extract on every NSP-folder scan, so `from_package.contents` on each update and DLC adds only those short runs, which read headers only.

Before a PR, I would like to know:

1. Is this the direction you want: the content meta gives the version, and the name is only checked?
2. When the tag and the content meta disagree, should the scan use the content meta and warn, or stop and ask for the file to be renamed?
3. PR #393 parses more name forms (a bare `v<N>` word) for the same untagged-update problem. With the version read from the package, that part is no longer needed; its other two fixes (title ID from cnmt.xml, TMPDIR) are independent of this. Should a PR for this replace that part of #393?

Once the direction is agreed, I can send a PR: the scan's version source and its tests, one concern.

### Platforms

All (the NSP script, for Mac apps and IPAs)
title: NSP script: read an update's version from its content meta, not only from the [v<N>] in its file name

body:
### What is missing

A front end with a game library wants to show the game it's building by the game's own name and icon while the build runs. With `--progress json`, the build says which game it is only in a `say` message, which is text for people:

```json
{"ev": "say", "msg": "app name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time; version: 1.0; bundle ID: org.nxnative.0400486024dec000; app: …/Ocarina of Time/The Legend of Zelda - Ocarina of Time.app"}
```

That comes 44 seconds into a Mac app build of Ocarina of Time from a `.nup` (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072), right after `unpack v131072`. The build was still compiling Mac shaders 15 minutes later. Until it ends, a front end has only the game's folder or file name to go by:

- the `.nup`'s file name carries no title ID, and the NUP container isn't part of docs/frontends.md;
- blawar/titledb has no entry for this title, so there's no eShop name or art;
- the name and icon are in the app's `Info.plist` and `AppIcon.icns`, which exist only once the build ends.

Reading the name out of the `say` text would break the first time its wording changes, so [Switch Player](https://github.com/DigitalN/SwitchPlayer), a Mac front end that keeps to docs/frontends.md, doesn't (DigitalN/SwitchPlayer#42).

### What you propose

One more build event, sent once where the NSP script says `app name: …` today ([line 3101](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/2d544e0df662420436908bffd10ae5ac6b2878a5/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L3101)), with `ev` and `t` as every event has:

```json
{"ev": "game", "title_id": "0400486024DEC000", "name": "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time", "version": "1.0",
 "bundle_id": "org.nxnative.0400486024dec000",
 "out": "…/Ocarina of Time/The Legend of Zelda - Ocarina of Time.app",
 "icon": "…/Ocarina of Time/0400486024DEC000_build/extract/v131072/icon.jpg"}
```

- `title_id`: the base game's, as `DMTitleID` records it.
- `name`, `version`, `bundle_id`: what the app will carry, after `--app-name` and `--bundle-id`.
- `out`: the IPA or Mac app the build will write.
- `icon`: the game's own icon as extracted (`icon.jpg`, 256×256), or `null` when it has none. It's in the build folder, so a front end copies it.

`PROG.event()` already sends `shaders_stale` this way ([line 213](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/2d544e0df662420436908bffd10ae5ac6b2878a5/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L213)), and the icon is the one the script already picks for the app at [line 3151](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/2d544e0df662420436908bffd10ae5ac6b2878a5/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L3151), so it's a few lines plus a row in docs/frontends.md's event table:

| `ev` | Fields | When |
|---|---|---|
| `game` | `title_id`, `name`, `version`, `bundle_id`, `out`, `icon` (a path, or `null`) | once, when the app's name, version and bundle ID are settled, before the shader stages |

It belongs to the build-events layer of #388.

### Platforms

Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: `--progress json`: a `game` event with the title ID, name, icon and app path once the build knows them

Built from the fork [cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake](https://github.com/cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake) (its V6 state), not from `main`; the fork has issues turned off, and most of its Ocarina of Time code comes from here. Possibly related to #1326 (a GPU hang about 10 minutes in), but here it comes within seconds to minutes, on an M1, together with memory pressure.

### Setup

- MacBook Air M1 (8-core GPU, `applegpu_g13g`), 16 GB, fanless
- macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2, Python 3.15.2 (Homebrew, arm64)
- The fork at `d1d672ac` (branch `kid-with-sword-remake`)
- Game: a `.nup` with update v131072 and **no base game** (the script took the update as the whole game). One RomFS file is reported damaged and replaced at every start: `Tex/CmnTex_Map_Soil_FairyFountain_Floor_D_Nrm.bntx.zs` ("not a zstd stream, begins 00 00 00 00")
- Built with `--platform mac-app --env-file mac_env.txt` (`DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0x200000000`) and the resolution overlays from the game note (handheld 0.666667, docked 0.9375, `flat`). Build: 42,853 of 42,854 shaders, pipeline archive for `applegpu_g13g` made (30,515 render + 4,125 compute bases)
- Launcher: Handheld, 30 fps, Upscaling off, full screen

### What happens

The picture freezes for good while the game goes on (sound and input still work). The log shows a segment command buffer failing with `Caused GPU Hang Error (00000003:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang)`, then `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored` on every later submission.

It happened in every one of 7 runs, at the start of the game, between a few seconds after loading the save and about 3 min of gameplay (frames 565 to 3836). In the last run I stood still for 1.5 minutes without a hang; it froze a few seconds after I started walking (frame 3512). An earlier guess (picking up a blue rupee) did not hold: it also froze without one.

No `more memory pools than the 4095 entries` line (the known Ocarina of Time hang in `docs/reference/shaders.md`), no new pipelines or shader libraries in the frames before the hang.

### What I tried (no change to the hang)

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| 720p overlay instead of the game's dynamic resolution | GPU time about the same (about 50 ms → 53 ms per frame in gameplay), still hangs |
| `DM_GUEST_FILE=1` | footprint about 11 GB → 8.4 GB, frame p50 about 45-53 ms → 41 ms, GPU allocated unchanged (about 9 GB), still hangs |
| `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OVERLAP=0` | still hangs |

### Performance before the hang

- Frame time p50 about 42 ms (about 24 fps) even when standing still; the host steps the present interval between 2 and 3 all the time
- `DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:300`: GPU busy 17-22 ms a frame (render 12-19 ms, compute / copy 4-6 ms), but first start to last end 27-44 ms, so the GPU is idle for about 40% of the frame span. Largest passes: the first compute / copy encoder (about 5 ms, about 100 dispatches) and the 1280x720 main passes (2-4 ms)
- GPU allocated 8.4-9.9 GB, resident 7.5-8.4 GB (with guest files)

### The hang comes with memory pressure

In a 7th run I sampled `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` and `vm.swapusage` every 2 s next to the game. Loading the save took free memory from 74% to about 46%; then macOS reported pressure level 2 (warn) for 11 s, swap grew from 1.5 GB to 3.0 GB, free memory fell to 21%, and the GPU hang (frame 565) fell inside that window, a few seconds after the save had loaded. Pressure went back to normal right after the hang. Activity Monitor showed the game at about 13 GB at that moment. This also fits the other runs: no hang standing still, a hang soon after loading or walking into new parts of the area.

For comparison, the fork's game note (`docs/games/kid-with-sword-remake.md`) measured a peak footprint of 5.2-5.5 GB on a 16 GB MacBook Air M5 with `tex_release 2`; here the footprint is 8-11 GB (8.4 GB with guest files, whose pages still take RAM) with about 9 GB GPU allocated. I do not know why the M1 needs so much more, or whether the scenes compare.

`DM_NVN_HANGLOG`, mentioned in `docs/reference/shaders.md`, does not seem to exist in the fork's tree, so I could not name the hung shaders. I can provide full logs if useful.
title: Ocarina of Time on an M1 (16 GB): GPU hang (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorHang) under memory pressure, about 24 fps at 720p / 30 fps

body:
### What happened

`shader_split.py` takes only 8 shaders from the game's `main` and prints 659 `[RED] main control section @…: no code area …; left out` lines. The game's other shaders are in TT Games' DAT archives, which it doesn't read at all. So a build from upstream would have almost none of the game's shaders.

TT Games' engine stores each shader's code area right next to its control section, with no data record pointing at it and no address built for it in the code. So `raw_shaders` never finds a match. The rest of the shaders are in Oodle-compressed `.nnx_shaders` files inside the `.dat` archives.

### What you expected

The split finds the game's shaders, in `main` and in the archives.

### Suggested fix

Three changes fix it:

1. When nothing points at a control section's code area, take the neighbour right before or after it if exactly one passes the length and stage checks.
2. Compute code areas have no header, so both neighbours can pass. In that case take the one that contains a Maxwell `EXIT`.
3. Read the `.nnx_shaders` files from the DAT archives (a small file-table reader; the Oodle chunks are decoded with the game's own decoder through the host) and search them the same way.

With these, `main` gives 667 shaders (142 vertex, 440 pixel, 85 compute) with none left out, and the whole split gives 98,294. Every shader the game asks for up to the first level is in the map. Other games' splits are unchanged; I checked Mario Kart 8 Deluxe. There's a synthetic test for the neighbour rules.

body:
### What happened

Since large pools are split into chunks (1d4b8e82), all the text in LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga is garbled. With `DM_NVN_POOL_CHUNKS=0` it's fine.

The game copies its font textures around inside one big 1.4 GB pool. The chunk a copy lands in is created on first use, and by then the dirty tracker has already made those pages read-only. Metal doesn't complain, but any GPU write through a buffer made over read-only pages is silently dropped, even if you make the pages writable again before the copy. I confirmed that with a small standalone Metal program.

### Suggested fix

Make the pages writable in `big_new` before creating the buffer, the same way a host write does:

```c
dm_guest_write_prepare((void *)lo, end - lo);
id<MTLBuffer> buf = [g_dev newBufferWithBytesNoCopy:(void *)lo length:end - lo ...];
```

The textures there get re-uploaded and protected again as usual. I added a `t_pool_chunks` case for it (fails before, passes after), the other pool and dirty-tracking tests still pass, and the game's text is correct again.

body:
Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, `0400486024DEC000`, v131072) on a 16 GB Mac. While Kokiri Forest loads, render targets pile up in the residency set until wired memory and swap reach the machine's limits.

**What was measured** (M2 Pro 16 GB):
- The residency set went from 1.6 to 6.6 GB in about 30 s, 3.2 GB of it render targets (72 → 1,068 textures, 31 → 313 descriptors).
- Wired memory went from 3.0 to 9.8 GB while swap rose from 1.1 to 3.2 GB and available memory fell to 15%. Runs reached a +4 GB swap limit.
- At f1,200: 781 live render targets (2,788 MB of sizes) over 74 MB of pool storage. 716 of the 828 live ones (2,697 MB) had their whole range overwritten by other targets since their own last write.

**Why the existing sharing doesn't catch it:**
- The objects stay live, so the [storage takeover](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/rendering.md#shared-storage-entries-taken-over-by-a-new-texture) keeps them.
- [Live resolution variants](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/rendering.md#live-resolution-variants-share-physical-image-storage) covers `COMPRESSIBLE|IMAGE` families at one offset, not render targets that move within a pool.
- `treg_tex` makes a Metal texture for every registered ID, dead or not.

**What decides the design** (standalone probes in #1583):
- On a placement heap, a texture reads another's bytes only with the same width, height, bytes per pixel and compression (`heap_alias`). So a reclaimed texture can be handed only to the same descriptor, or must be cleared.
- 855 dynamic-resolution steps at 2048×1152 fall into 21 RGBA8 allocation sizes (`rt_sizes`). A free list keyed on the allocation size would reuse across steps; one keyed on width × height almost never would.
- Simulating dead-by-overwrite reclaim on a logged write / release trace takes render targets from about 3.5 GB to 1.2 GB (`rt_reclaim_sim.py`).

**Proposed:** a texture whose pool range other targets have fully overwritten (whole-attachment passes only) is dead. Its Metal texture goes to a free list keyed on the descriptor (fenced, zero-filled, trimmed after 15 frames), and its ID reads as an empty slot until a pass writes it again. The PR is behind `DM_NVN_RT_RECLAIM=1`, off by default.

Questions for other games with storage-shared render targets (Wonder, Breath of the Wild, STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT): does any of them read a target after another has overwritten its whole range? That is the case the exclusions are meant to catch.
title: Ocarina of Time: render targets dead by overwrite keep their Metal textures (3.2 GB during the Kokiri load)

## Status — generic BFRES/NVN correction implemented, acceptance still open

**Latest upstream integration:** #1609 remains **Ready for review**, now at [13d67c62](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1609) after a normal merge of upstream main eed7c429. Its conflict with the new deferred NVN queue is resolved: the submit thread pins the four-byte ticket and copies a canonical DRAW_IDX+END snapshot into queue-owned bytes before asynchronous replay. Native-512-byte direct/nested ticket RED/GREEN, CPU lifetime checks and two queue-specific 38/38 suites pass. GitHub reports MERGEABLE; new-head CI is still running. This does not add new signed gameplay evidence or change the manual acceptance requirements.

The original-RESTBL BFRES resource-budget failure is explained and corrected for the measured model requests by **generic, opt-in four-byte NVN tickets in [ready-for-review #1609](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1609)**. This is neither a title-specific +16 KiB RESTBL/heap workaround nor a fabricated GetUsed result. The Edition profile is still [ready-for-review #1563](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1563) because upstream review and manual gameplay gates remain open.

### Measured cause and correction

The host previously recorded a 40-byte direct indexed draw plus eight-byte END where native-compatible terminal command memory can use four bytes. BFRES sizes guest model command scratch from the *used* byte count, causing actual allocation overrun:

| Original-RESTBL model | Old requested bytes | Four-byte fix | Resource budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `NpcCommonerA` | `0x5424` | `0x4efc` | `0x5000` |
| `PlayerPeachElpWM` | `0x400c` | `0x3fd0` | `0x4000` |

The [#1609](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1609) implementation writes **four real guest command bytes** and **48 real guest control bytes** for eligible canonical indexed DRAW+END, reports both GetUsed counters honestly, pins an immutable snapshot over command capture/preindex/replay/commit, retires overlapping/partial regrants, rejects stale generations and preserves CopyCommands/OP_CALL/canonical relocation. Its opt-in is default **OFF** for unrelated titles. Earlier eight-byte tickets and 32-byte draw compaction alone did not fit both models. The original resource table, ROMs, saves and signed applications were never modified for this correction.

### Evidence, limits and remaining work

- Previously completed **1,464/1,464** headless NVN/capture tests across four game profiles, separate **150/150** unrelated-title default-off tests and **108/108** focused merged ticket/capture checks. The source-integrated required stack previously passed **399/399** focused headless checks plus an arm64 host-only build.
- The separate signed original-RESTBL Edition preview's real **World 1 frame 2350** had **five submits**, **409 segments**, **33 canonical ticket expansions** and **2/2 identical presented-image replay digests**. However **69/334,308 post-frame memory blocks differed**; this is *one presented frame*, not complete replay-state or course validation.
- A later [credited Program0 indexed RomFS fork-only source `2d7b6a4d`](https://github.com/ishtiaq156/nxnative/tree/integration/program1-indexed-romfs-w10-20261107) protects separately supplied original images from source/output, symlink and cleanup aliases. The [required-stack fork-only review `61d42837`](https://github.com/ishtiaq156/nxnative/tree/integration/wonder-required-ci-hygiene-20261107) combines the original-author Program1, SDK21, Control, Mac identity, generic NVN, Edition profile and independent CI fixes. Its exact packer/identity suite passed **116/116 Mac/NSP**, **11/11 documentation** and pinned Python lint. These are not gameplay results and have not merged upstream.
- **Native NVN command-memory minimum is 512 bytes**; synthetic 32/128-byte grant tests are defensive and below that contract. The 31-bit ticket generation registry fails closed on exhaustion. Sustained multi-queue overlap and direct host-lent handle provenance/lifetime remain unproven.
- The actual update-only Edition extraction has Program0 NPDM but **no Program0 RomFS directory** by design. A separately provided original complete image was original-title/index checked read-only, **not** proven natively content/version equivalent. Missing index0 must fail closed.
- The preserved signed preview uses shader chain **`844bf1a5ea8f`**, incompatible with newer integrated source **`3ee52af3ca18`**; no speculative current-head signed app or mass shader/PSO rebuild was produced.

### Acceptance gates

Maintain this issue **OPEN** and do not merge the now-ready-for-review PRs #1609/#1563 until applicable new-head CI and dependencies are reviewed, and the remaining **manual** observations are confirmed: original-RESTBL New Game progression, cloned Sample Place Continue, a complete course clear, Bellabel Park entry, physical DualSense rumble, audible audio and SDK21 movie playback. A historical +16 KiB diagnostic overlay demonstrated a budget condition but **does not** validate the permanent original-RESTBL fix. No new game frame harness or automated gameplay was used for the current source/CI pass.

nxnative: Crash Bandicoot 4 – It's About Time shader extraction fix

Game: Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time
Title ID: 010073401175E000
Tested nxnative commit: b2d46b86d03f4b03afe11ea61c67cdf00d7a5345

Problem

The nxnative conversion initially failed with:

[FAIL] shader split failed
the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS:
the game keeps them in a form shader_split.py does not read;
locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader

The game stores its Unreal Engine shader archives inside its PAK files. These PAK files use Unreal PAK version 9 with FrozenIndex, which the current uepak.py PAK detection does not recognize.

Specifically:

  • uepak.footer() does not recognize the version 9 footer.

  • uepak.unreal_paks() consequently skips these PAK files.

  • The shader archives are never extracted for the shader-splitting process.

Location of the shader archives

The game's RomFS contains:

Lava/Content/Paks/pakchunk0-Switch.pak
Lava/Content/Paks/pakchunk1-Switch.pak

The FrozenIndex contains these shader archive entries:

Lava/Content/ShaderArchive-Global-GLSL_SWITCH.ushaderbytecode
Lava/Content/ShaderArchive-Lava-GLSL_SWITCH.ushaderbytecode

The PAK version 9 FrozenIndex was successfully parsed manually. The index is not encrypted.

The extracted archive sizes were:

Archive | Compressed file size -- | -- Global | 7,711,237 bytes Lava | 328,479,644 bytes

All 51,447 records:

  • Decompressed successfully.

  • Parsed as valid LSLG records.

  • Matched their expected shader stages.

  • Passed the shader control-section and code-area validation checks.

No shader validation failures occurred.

Recommended permanent fix

Update the Unreal PAK reader in dm/gfx/tools/uepak.py to support PAK version 9 FrozenIndex.

The reader should:

  1. Recognize the version 9 footer and its FrozenIndex flag.

  2. Parse the FrozenIndex structures and enumerate the PAK file entries.

  3. Identify .ushaderbytecode files in the PAK contents.

  4. Extract the shader archive payloads.

  5. Decode the individual LZ4 shader records.

  6. Write the reconstructed decoded archives to the normal ue_shaders directory.

The existing shader_split.py processing should then be able to consume these archives without requiring a manual workaround.

Verified workaround

Until native version 9 FrozenIndex support is implemented, the following workaround successfully converts the game:

  1. Parse the PAK version 9 FrozenIndex manually.

  2. Extract the two .ushaderbytecode archives.

  3. Decode their LZ4 shader records.

  4. Rebuild the archives using uepak.decoded_archive().

  5. Place the decoded archives in:

extract/v131072/ue_shaders/

The nxnative Launcher GUI then successfully completed the Crash Bandicoot 4 conversion and compilation.

Conclusion

This is a reproducible compatibility issue involving Unreal PAK version 9 FrozenIndex support and the extraction/decompression workflow.

The game does not have missing or invalid shaders. Both archives were successfully extracted, all 51,447 shaders passed validation, and the game port compiled successfully using the decoded archives.

Supporting this PAK format in nxnative should eliminate the need for manual extraction and make Crash Bandicoot 4 conversion work directly through the Launcher GUI.
title: Crash Bandicoot 4 – It's About Time shader extraction fix

body:
**Machine:** MacBook Air M4, 24 GB, macOS 27.2, built-in display (fixed 60 Hz).
**Game:** The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000`, v131072), `--platform mac-app`.
**Tree:** main 75c1a8cf + #1453, #1455, #1332, #1446, LeonardoBai12's frame-delta change (f3b26180 from `oot-mac`, which gives `main` a frame-step state page, so `DM_FPS_TARGET=30` applies) and #1527. The display-link code (`link_range`, `link_latency`, `link_sync`, the display-link delegate) is the same on current main (0c7e88b9).
**Settings:** handheld (`DM_OPMODE=0`), `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`, `DM_FPS_TARGET=30`; window = 2560x1440 drawable, fullscreen = `DM_FULLSCREEN=1`, 3840x2410 drawable.
**Route:** scripted with `DM_CTL`: the Kokiri Forest autosave in Link's house, 90 s idle in the house, then out of the door, through Saria's greeting, and 180 s of scripted stick pushes outside (the walk). One run per row.

### What happens

| run | house fps | house frame p50 / p95 / p99 | walk fps | walk frame p50 / p95 / p99 | walk frames > 50 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| window | 30.0 | 33.3 / 34.3 / 34.6 ms | 29.7 | 33.4 / 36.1 / 38.4 ms | 4 |
| fullscreen, run 1 | 30.0 | 33.3 / 34.3 / 34.7 ms | 24.2 | 33.6 / 68.0 / 71.5 ms | 996 |
| fullscreen, run 2 | 29.1 | 33.3 / 34.5 / 67.2 ms | 27.7 | 33.4 / 66.5 / 69.1 ms | 388 |

Uncapped, fullscreen and window are the same (46.3 and 44.9 fps in the house), so it is specific to the 30 fps target in fullscreen.

Present intervals over the walk, in 60 Hz vsyncs (`DM_NVN_TSV` `@frame_ms`):
- window: 2 vsyncs 5,430, 3 vsyncs 7, 4 vsyncs 0
- fullscreen, run 1: 2 vsyncs 3,425, 3 vsyncs 53, 4 vsyncs 965
- fullscreen, run 2: 2 vsyncs 4,647, 3 vsyncs 46, 4 vsyncs 369

So in fullscreen a late frame stays on screen a whole 30 Hz tick (66.7 ms), not one more refresh (50 ms).

### Why

Both modes log `present pacing mode 0 → 3`. At `mtl_fps_target() == 30`, `link_sync` asks for the 30 Hz link (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:14161` on main), and `link_range(3)` returns `CAFrameRateRangeMake(30, 30, 30)` in both, with no virtual ticks, since 60 is a multiple of 30 (`nvn_mtl.m:14110-14120`). `front_screen_match(30)` changes nothing on a 60 Hz screen. Both run at frame latency 1 (`link_latency`, `nvn_mtl.m:14130`), logged as `(window)` and `(fullscreen, fixed refresh)`. So the virtual-tick path is not involved; the difference is how the system shows the layer:

- The callback leads its target display time by about 50 ms in the window and by 32.8 ms in fullscreen, one tick of the 30 Hz link (`submission ahead of target display p50` in the `display link up to tick` lines).
- In fullscreen the link skipped ticks. From the `display link up to tick N: ticks 300, presents M` lines and the frames' `@t_s`, the link called back 16.5-25.4 times a second in 8 of the 30 windows of 300 presents during the two fullscreen walks. In both window runs it called back 30.0 times a second in every window. A skipped tick keeps a frame on screen 66.7 ms. The game is paced by the ticks at its acquire (`mtl_link_wait_tick`), so it also presents 66.7 ms apart.
- It is not GPU load. In run 1, frames 9393-9614 (222 in a row) came 61-72 ms apart with a GPU span of 24-40 ms and 10-18 ms of submit, and `@sync_ms`, `@wait_ms` and `@pq_wait_ms` were 0 for all of them. In the same run, 48 of the first 58 frames after boot came 66.7 ms apart with 0.3-1.2 ms of GPU each (run 2 did not do this at boot).

This looks like the late presents and skipped ticks in [Frame latency 2 for the display link in fullscreen](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/frame-rate.md#frame-latency-2-for-the-display-link-in-fullscreen) (#347, #348), here on a fixed-rate screen with the 30 Hz link, where each skipped tick costs 33.3 ms. Why the system skips ticks is not known.

#614 (Pokémon Legends: Z-A on a MacBook Air M4 in fullscreen at its 30 fps: 33/50 ms frames, one 101.8 ms frame with 2.1 ms of GPU, and the lag gone while macOS screen recording was on) may be the same; it was closed after a pipeline archive fix.

### Reproducing on main

On main, Ocarina of Time's 30 cap is not applied: without a frame step or an engine limiter, `fps_present_cap` logs `present cap 30 fps ... not applied`. These runs therefore need the frame-delta change. On main, the same path should apply to any game whose target is 30 in fullscreen on a fixed-rate screen: a frame-step game at `DM_FPS_TARGET=30`, a game that presents at interval 2 for a second, or `DM_FPS=30`. I have not run those.

Logs and `frames.tsv` of the runs are available.
title: Mac: at a 30 fps target in fullscreen on a fixed 60 Hz screen, the 30 Hz display link skips ticks and frames stay up 66.7 ms

body:
### What happened

A Mac app built from main bd9f422 draws regular dotted rows across the whole 3D scene from the first gameplay frame in Kokiri Forest: thin dark dotted lines every few pixel rows over terrain, foliage, Link and the sky, the UI untouched. The orientation follows the camera (vertical stripes in the Saria cutscene, horizontal from the balcony autosave). The same route on the app built from 671c68e (chain adec7d81d970) is clean.

| bd9f422, balcony autosave | 671c68e, same spot |
|---|---|
| ![dotted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonpage0/nxnative/evidence/oot-dotted-rows-2026-11-06/evidence/oot-bd9f422-dotted-rows-balcony.jpg) | ![clean](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonpage0/nxnative/evidence/oot-dotted-rows-2026-11-06/evidence/oot-chain-adec7d81d970-balcony.jpg) |

Saria scene, bd9f422: ![saria](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonpage0/nxnative/evidence/oot-dotted-rows-2026-11-06/evidence/oot-bd9f422-dotted-rows-saria.jpg)

### Bisection

Same app, same autosave, driven by `DM_CTL`, one thing changed at a time:

- **Not the host.** The tree's own host, a host with 16 open PRs on top, and a host with #1368/#1307 reverted draw the same rows. (Main's host changes since 671c68e were covered by those builds.)
- **Not 0f510fd.** A second full build with its five C# files back at 0f510fd^ (translator rebuilt) draws the same rows.
- **Not #1414** (applied locally): 801 sampled shaders, the 69 agl_ndsr* shaders among them, translate to byte-identical libraries with and without it.
- **`DM_UPSCALER=metalfx` changes nothing**, but it replaces only agl_ndsr.pck's 22 shaders; Ocarina's gameplay upscaler is agl_ndsr_vr.pck (20) and agl_ndsr_vr_light.pck (17), which keep running — so that switch excludes nothing here.
- **The rewrite.** The 89 network shaders (agl_ndsr, agl_ndsr_vr, agl_ndsr_vr_light, the Ndve movie networks; 71 of them call `dmsh_hmma16816_f16`) rebuilt with `dmsh_build.py`'s `hmma_msl` returning the MSL unchanged (the translator's lane-by-lane helper body stays), their reflection restamped to the host's chain and laid over the image in `msl/b-<chain>/`, everything else equal: **the rows are gone.**

![hmma rewrite off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonpage0/nxnative/evidence/oot-dotted-rows-2026-11-06/evidence/oot-hmma-rewrite-off-balcony.jpg)

So it is bd9f422's simdgroup_matrix path (the TensorPass flags and `hmma_msl`'s slots / A reuse / direct A load) on Ocarina's gameplay upscaler network, which the commit's checks did not cover (the title and opening movie network, Donkey Kong Bananza's upscaler). `test_dmsh_hmma.py` passes here, so the shape it checks is right; the failing case is one of agl_ndsr_vr's dispatches. A `DM_NVN_SHOT` from the Kokiri balcony autosave shows it on the first frame. Happy to run a translator build with a candidate fix, or to dump the 20 agl_ndsr_vr shaders' MSL before and after `hmma_msl`.

Workaround used here: `git revert bd9f422` (translator republished), which restores the previous simdgroup_matrix rewrite; the title movie then costs what it did before.

Apple M3 Max (36 GB), macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2 (Metal 32023.922), `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac-app`, in-tree profile, no profile changes.
title: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000 v131072, Mac M3 Max): regular dotted rows across the whole 3D scene since bd9f422 (HMMA chains keep their accumulators in the SIMD-group's matrices, PR #1456)

**What I am asking.** Whether an 8 GB Mac is in scope for this title, and if so, whether the low-memory settings
the iPhone port used belong in the profile. I am not asking you to merge anything yet. If your newer memory work
already covers this, tell me and I will test against it and close this.

**The machine.** MacBook Neo, Apple A18 Pro (2 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 6-core GPU), 8 GB unified,
macOS 27.2. Not a 16 GB machine.

**What it does here.** Building from a 4 November snapshot of plumber-racer-2, a race holds 50 to 58 fps on light
courses and 40s on heavy ones, at 1080p upscaled to the window. Footprint is 3.9 GB in a race, flat over three
minutes, 4.48 GB after every course has been driven, with about 700 MB of swap.

**The gap.** Upstream's profile for `0400C3F00006E000` carries `mem_reserve`, `mem_alias`, `mem_stack` and
`app_pool`, and nothing else. The build that runs on 8 GB also carries six keys, two of which are host code rather
than settings:

| Key | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `tex_soft` | host, `nvn_mtl.m` | large BC textures lose their finest level, and CPU uploads keep pools from being wired. Wrapped pools went from 3.7 GB to 851 MB on the iPhone |
| `mem_file` | host, `hle_svc.c`, `nvn_dirty.c` | guest memory in a shared file mapping. A whole cup ran at 3.9 GB |
| `tex_release` | host | terrain tile pages return once uploaded, about 860 MB |
| `mem_map_limit` | host | the game's reported free memory falls, so it releases blocks. Mapped memory 2.4 GB to 1.25 GB by the fourth race |
| `op_mode handheld` | profile | 720p-class rendering rather than docked |

Without them, the fork's own notes record a Mac race at **9.4 GB**. That is the number this is about: 9.4 into 8 does
not go.

# New issue draft — a dump folder for a game with no profile is refused, and `is_dump()` needs `base/`


---

### What happened

Bringing up a title nxnative has no profile for (`0400486024DEC000`), starting from a decrypted dump folder:

```
$ python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <dump> --platform mac-app --work-dir <work> -o <app>
[01:41:16] a dump folder: 0400486024DEC000, 0 update(s), 0 DLC
[RED] a dump folder packs only a game with a profile, and 0400486024DEC000 has none: the survey that makes a provisional profile reads NSPs
```

Two smaller things found on the way:

1. **`pack_dump.is_dump()` requires the `base/` layout.** A folder with `exefs/` + `romfs/` at the top (which switch2mac's own `build` accepts, and which `romfs`-extracting NUP tools naturally produce) is not a dump here:
   ```python
   def is_dump(folder):
       return (folder / 'base/exefs/main.npdm').is_file() and (...)
   ```
   With a flat folder the script falls through to the NSP path and asks for `prod.keys`. Moving the two folders into `base/` fixes it. Worth saying in the docs ("a dump is `base/exefs` + `base/romfs`, or `updates/<version>/`"), and/or accepting the flat form.

2. **A guessed profile from a dump is not reachable from the builder.** nxnative has `dm/tools/profile_guess.py` (it is what made a provisional profile for this title when switch2mac drove it), but the builder's own survey path is NSP-only, so from a dump there is no automatic way to get a profile.

### What I expected

A dump folder (or a `.nup`, which the script already accepts) of a game with no profile surveys itself the way an NSP folder does — the RomFS manifest part of the survey reads the dump fine — and a provisional profile is written, as it is for a game supplied as NSPs.

### Workaround used

- Extracted the `.nup` to `base/exefs` + `base/romfs`
- Ran `dm/tools/profile_guess.py` indirectly (switch2mac's `build` on an older engine) and copied the resulting profile into `dm/games/<title ID>/`
- Then the builder accepted the dump

That is three tools and an older engine for what the survey does automatically for NSPs.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072.

### nxnative commit

`e03bdc8f6838` (also seen with `865cc35fad70`).

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 27.2 (26B123).

### No game files

None attached; the title ID and the error text are all that is needed to reproduce with any unregistered game.
title: Bring-up from a dump or .nup of a game without a profile is refused, and is_dump() requires the base/ layout

body:
### What is missing

A Mac app built with `--seen-shaders` (minutes instead of hours for a large game) draws nothing for a shader its partial library lacks: the host logs `[RED] shader <key> (<stage>) failed to load` and the draw is dropped until the next build. The remedy today is to quit, run the NSP script again so it reads the log, and start over. For a game whose whole map takes hours (Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza), a new area is a black or holed picture until then.

I have been playing with a local prototype that closes this loop while the game runs (on 975bb4c1, before the one-file library): a script follows the app's log, builds the keys it reports missing with the same tools the NSP script uses, and the running host picks the new libraries up, so an area the partial library does not cover draws a few seconds late instead of not at all. With an option it also builds the rest of the shader map in the background at low priority, so over a few play sessions the library becomes the whole map with no long build up front.

### What you propose

On current `main` the host already takes each library file from the folder `b-<chain>/` before the image `b-<chain>.img` (`msl_image_file`), so a library built while the game runs is found without a second folder. Two pieces are missing:

1. **Host (`nvn_mtl.m`, about 15 lines).** `prog_get` keeps a program it built with a stage missing (the serial table and its last-result cache), so the shader is never looked for again. The change: the program remembers that a stage was missing and a generation number; a one-second timer on the library folder's modification time bumps the generation when files arrive; `prog_get` builds such a program again when the generation has moved. Programs with every stage are untouched, and with no new file nothing changes. Mac only: an iPhone loads no code it did not ship with.
2. **Script (`scripts/live_shaders.py`, about 200 lines).** Follows `~/Library/Logs/nxnative/<title ID>.log`, collects the keys of `failed to load` lines, builds them with `own_compilers.py` → `dmsh_build.py` and the build's per-shader cache, and moves the libraries into the library folder, the `.metallib` files before the `.json` files the host reads first. The keys go to `<work>/shader/partial-keys.txt`, so the next `--seen-shaders` build packs them. `--fill` builds the rest of the map a chunk at a time at background QoS.

Questions before I write it against `main`:

- Is this wanted in nxnative at all, or is it a front end's job (the script) with only the host piece here?
- Is the library folder the right place for the new files, or should they go to a folder of their own that the host is told of (my prototype used `DM_MSL_LIVE`), so a full build's folder is never written by a second tool?
- The host piece could instead be a `DM_CTL` line (`shaders`) that the script appends after each batch, with no timer. Which do you prefer?

It stays under 300 lines with its tests and docs. I would send the host piece and the script as two PRs.

### Platforms

Mac
title: Proposal: live shaders on the Mac: build the shaders a partial library lacks while the game runs

body:
## Request

Cross-game dedup for porting outputs: a shared content-addressed pool (or per-SDK-build-ID cache) so identical work isn't repeated per game.

## Rationale

The shader CAS (`cas.db`) lives inside each game's build folder, so identical Metal compiles across games miss — relevant for engine-common shaders (UE, Unity) that recur across titles. The same applies at the module level: `sdk`/`subsdk` are byte-identical across games on the same SDK version, and their rewrite could be cached by build ID rather than repeated per game. Modest per-build win for users porting several titles, growing with library size.
title: Feature: cross-game dedup of porting outputs (shared CAS / per-SDK-build rewrite cache)

body:
## Request

Overlap the pipeline-archive prebuild with the shader stage: archive each pair's bases as its libraries become ready, instead of a strictly serial ~67 min stage after all ~42k shaders finish.

## Rationale

On a large Switch 2 build the two dominant stages run back-to-back: `Mac shaders` ~98 min then `Pipeline archive` ~67 min (measured on Ocarina of Time, mac-app build). The archive needs a pair's libraries, not all pairs' libraries — streaming it behind the shader stage could hide a large part of its wall time, especially the tail where translation is winding down. Both stages are compiler-bound so gains are partial, and ordering the archive's pairs toward the manifest first would also get the hot path archived earliest.
title: Feature: stream the pipeline-archive prebuild behind the shader stage

body:
## Request

A fast mode for unprofiled games (`--quick` or similar) that produces a testable app in tens of minutes instead of hours, so bring-up failures are discovered before the full shader cost is paid.

## Rationale

For a game with no profile, the build surveys, then translates and Metal-compiles every shader found (Ocarina of Time: 42,854 shaders, ~98 min on an M-series Mac), then prebuilds the pipeline archive (~67 min), before the app exists at all. But most bring-up failures abort in the first minutes of runtime — this game's run reached presenting and died in `nn::font` init, learned only after ~3 h of build time. The iteration loop on a provisional title is dominated by work the test doesn't need yet.

A quick mode could:

- compile only a boot-path shader set (what the survey/menu path implies), or defer the rest to lazy compilation / background completion
- skip the pipeline archive prebuild entirely (it exists for gameplay smoothness, not boot correctness)
- skip or defer final packaging weight where safe (e.g. the ad-hoc signing pass over a 30+ GB app on every iteration)

Fail-fast changes unprofiled porting from "wait hours, learn it crashes" to "wait minutes, learn it crashes" — and on success the same build folder's caches keep the full build incremental.
title: Feature: quick/boot-first build mode for unprofiled games (fail-fast porting)

body:
## Request

Longer-term: synthesize motion vectors for games that don't ship them, so the MetalFX temporal scaler and (per #1509) the frame interpolator can serve non-DLSS titles.

## Rationale

Both MetalFX temporal features need per-pixel MVs. DLSS games hand them over; NDSR-upscaler games (Bananza, Ocarina of Time) and most Switch 1 titles don't. But the host sees every frame's depth and can reproject: a previous-frame reprojection using the game's own view-projection matrices (derivable from the shader's uniform buffers or the pass state) would give camera-motion vectors; object motion is the harder remainder but camera vectors alone already improve reconstruction.

Ambitious and research-y — filing for tracking rather than expecting a quick implementation.
title: Feature: synthesized motion vectors for games without them (temporal scaler / interpolation coverage)

body:
## Request

A dynamic-resolution governor: the host already measures per-frame GPU time (segmented submission timestamps) — a render-scale control could trade internal resolution for frame rate the way consoles do.

## Rationale

Today `renderScale` is a fixed per-game setting. The host knows per-frame GPU cost continuously (segment timestamps, the frame-step controller's cost model). A governor that lowers render scale when frames over-run and restores it when they fit would hold 60 in scenes that dip, without permanently lowering quality — strictly better than a static scale picked for the worst case.

Natural integration: the same cost signal the frame-step logic already uses (`nvn_fstep`), but acting on resolution instead of frame hold, and gated so it does not fight the game's own dynamic resolution where one exists.
title: Feature: dynamic resolution governor driven by per-frame GPU cost

body:
## Request

Extend the NVN prewarm/archive machinery — `pso_manifest.tsv` bundled lists, `pso_user.tsv` accumulation, offline `MTL4Compiler` archives — to the Vulkan and OpenGL layers.

## Rationale

The docs note prewarm is NVN-only today (Hades builds its own 1,856 pipelines while loading, on its own clock). Vulkan and GL games still compile pipelines on the submit path at first draw, which is the hitch the NVN machinery exists to remove. The same three pieces map across:

- a per-game manifest recorded from a play session (both layers already log pipeline creation)
- a user list that grows with the player's routes
- bundled bases shipped in the app via the existing `pso_bundle` mechanism where a Metal 4 descriptor exists for them
title: Feature: prewarm lists and pipeline archives for the Vulkan and OpenGL layers

body:
## Request

Present-time upscaling through MetalFX's *temporal* scaler (`MTL4FXTemporalScaler`) where the game supplies motion vectors — an upgrade from today's spatial-only `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx`.

## Rationale

`DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE` uses `MTL4FXSpatialScaler`, which is a single-frame upscale. The host already builds a `MTL4FXTemporalScaler` for the NVN2 DLSS path with the game's real depth and motion vectors — the same inputs a temporal present-scale would need. For games that hand the host MVs (DLSS path), a temporal scaler at present would give markedly better reconstruction quality than spatial for games rendering below display resolution.

Scope like #1509 (frame generation): opt-in, only when the frame carried usable motion data; falls back to the spatial scaler otherwise.
title: Feature: temporal MetalFX upscaling at present for games with motion vectors

body:
## Request

A profile key (e.g. `tbdr on`) that enables `DM_NVN_TBDR` per game, for titles verified safe against the bindless-read problem that keeps the optimizations off globally.

## Rationale

The replay's TBDR optimizations (store/load elision, pass merging, same-target continuation, plus the `DM_NVN_UNWRITTEN_DC` / `DM_NVN_ZSKIP` / `DM_NVN_XV` skips that run under it) are off by default because bindless textures defeat the read inference. But whether a game actually reads attachments through bindless paths in a way the inference misses is per-game, not universal — many NVN games don't use bindless at all, and for others the failure is narrow enough to gate by build/shader, the way other per-game rules already work.

On Apple's TBDR GPUs, load/store elision and pass merging are the highest-leverage bandwidth savings available: fewer tile flushes and merged passes directly cut GPU time and power.

## Suggested shape

- `tbdr on` in `game.tsv` (default off, matching today), documented with the same caution the env switch carries
- A bring-up recipe: run with `DM_NVN_TBDR=1` + `DM_AB` on the game's problem passes and look for wrong pictures, the same way other profile keys are proven before a row is added

Happy to test on a few titles (BotW, Ocarina of Time) and report.
title: Feature: per-profile TBDR enablement (profile key for DM_NVN_TBDR)

body:
## Request

An opt-in frame-generation pass in the present path, built on macOS 26 / iOS 26's `MTL4FXFrameInterpolator`, scoped to games that hand the host usable motion vectors — in practice, the NVN2 DLSS path.

## Why this is feasible here

The host already encodes Metal 4 MetalFX work in the right places: `MTL4FXTemporalScaler` for NVN2's DLSS and `MTL4FXSpatialScaler` for `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx` / `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE`. The interpolator's inputs line up with what the DLSS eval already collects:

- `colorTexture` / `prevColorTexture`: the present thread sees both frames
- `depthTexture` / `motionTexture`: the DLSS path already takes the game's depth and motion textures plus jitter (the NGX feature flags give the MV layout)
- `deltaTime`: the present/vsync cadence
- `uiTexture`: optional; games that composite UI into the presented frame can leave it out and accept HUD artifacts, or the UI composite pass could feed it where one is identifiable
- `shouldResetHistory`: scene-cut / first-frame heuristics the present already tracks

For games without a motion source (NDSR-upscaler games like Bananza, Ocarina of Time), MV-less interpolation is the mushy case, so I'd scope this to *interpolate only when the frame carried usable motion data* — an env switch / launcher toggle like `DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE`, default off.

## Use case

30 fps Switch 2 titles presenting at 60, or 60 → 120 on a 120 Hz screen. Caveats are the usual: one frame of added latency, interpolation artifacts, no benefit where MVs are absent.

## Environment to test on

Apple silicon Mac, Xcode 27.2 / Metal 32023.922, building Switch 2 games from NUPs through the `mac-app` path.
title: Feature: frame generation for games with motion vectors (MTL4FXFrameInterpolator)

body:
I compared our working Ocarina of Time downstream build with main `bd9f422` and the open PRs. This source-only contribution isolates one remaining difference.

## Problem and patch

Two live GPU-written pages that hash to the same bucket replace the ledger's page identity with a wildcard. A third, untouched page with that hash is then also considered written, refusing a safe partial uniform shadow and ending the render pass. Main's 65,536 buckets reduce the frequency but do not remove this case.

The patch preserves main's bucket count and hash. It retains four identities per bucket, spills crowded buckets, reuses completed entries, and keeps a conservative overflow fence on allocation failure. No live hazard is discarded. `DM_NVN_GW_ASSOC=0` selects conservative one-entry tracking for comparison; `ab` uses the existing A/B mechanism.

This complements #1320's wide-write intervals: the regression uses small writes that still collide. The tradeoff is explicit: the two inline ledgers grow from 2 MiB to 11 MiB, plus spill storage.

## Checked

Apple M4 Max, 48 GB, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.1.

- `t_ubp_running`: 21 checks pass on `bd9f422` plus this patch, including actual shadow bytes, real hazards, spill, overflow completion and slot reuse.
- Negative control: one-entry tracking fails four intended collision checks.
- Full `make -C dm/gfx/tests GAME=0400486024DEC000 run`: passed. An initial invocation stopped on an unquoted workspace path; the completed run used a no-space `CURDIR` alias, without changing repository source for that issue.
- All 11 documentation tests pass; symptom index regenerated; `git diff --check` clean; patch applies to the clean base index.
- Scoped LLVM 23.1.3 static analysis: exactly the same 62 finding records as unchanged main after normalizing line numbers. Both ratchets exit 1 for three existing file/check pairs; no introduced findings.
- Not run: current-main gameplay A/B, multi-game `regress.py check`, iOS gameplay. The installed downstream build was left unchanged. Earlier downstream measurements used a different host and a 4,096-bucket ledger, and do not establish an FPS gain here.

## Overlap review

No duplicate submissions of #1357 (parser depth), #1368 (mesh first-use/prewarming), #1390/#1447 (GPU-written ranges), #1489 (pool-table patching), or the raw-lookup, indirect-mesh, foliage and linear deferred-release fixes already on main.

Our downstream cached-root-use stamps and range-specific takeover notes depend on the older fork's retained-view lifecycle. Main and #1489 changed that lifecycle, so those require a fresh reproduction before a follow-up is justified.

The attachment contains only source changes, synthetic tests, documentation and the MIT license. No game files, keys, extracted shaders, saves, screenshots or compiled libraries. Please review the collision-tracking approach and memory tradeoff before adopting it.

[nxnative-collision-source-only-20261106.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34484619/nxnative-collision-source-only-20261106.zip)
title: Contribution: retain GPU-write page identities across hash collisions (current-main patch)

### Game, title ID and version

Spelunky 2, 01007EC013ABC000, 1.28.0 (v524288)

### Engine and graphics API, if known

Custom C++ engine (BlitWorks / Mossmouth), NVN, FMOD audio, SDK 13.3.0

### Survey and what happened

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` on an unmodified checkout of `origin/main` (`88c7e03f`, shader chain `adec7d81d970`) stops during the rewrite of `main`:

```text
AssertionError: no split reaches: the back patch area reaches no site below 0xe9a0000, too close to the front area's reach
[RED] patch_nso.py exit code 1 on main (full output: logs/rewrite_main.log)
```

`main` is 346.1 MB (`text_end` `0x1571f130`, bss `0xe71fd8`). `nso_code.data_blocks` finds a 337 MB data block inside text from `0x32aea4` to `0x154ffd50`, leaving code only at `0..0x32aea4` and `0x154ffd50..0x1571f130`. All 2,869 `mrs tpidr_el0` sites are in the first 3.3 MB; the last 2.2 MB has 2,005 `x18` uses (first at `0x1550407c`). There are no rewrite sites in the 337 MB middle gap.

`patch_nso.py:57` asserts `BACK_MIN < 0x8000000 - 0x200000`, which expects a module under 256 MB where the front and back patch areas overlap. Setting `SPLIT = BACK_MIN` lets `patch_nso.py` rewrite `main` and `sdk` with no branch out of range (252,620 front patch bytes at `-0x1000000`, 97,508 back patch bytes at `0x168a0000`).

The next blocker is the shader split. The RomFS is an 88-byte placeholder, and the assets and shaders (`CircleOccluder_PS_p.nvn`, `_VS_vv.nvn`, `Combine_PS_p.nvn`) appear to be compressed inside `main`'s 337 MB data block. `shader_split.py` stops with:

```text

## What happened

The NSP build script prepends its fallback `TOOL_PATHS` to the caller's `PATH`. A shell that deliberately selects project-local tools (for example through mise or a virtual environment) can therefore silently use Homebrew tools instead during the build.

This is reproducible on main at `88c7e03f51e3934dc227089ea81ec64fcd525b03`, without building or reading any game files. The relevant line in `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` is:

```python
env = dict(os.environ, PATH=os.pathsep.join(TOOL_PATHS + [os.environ.get('PATH', '/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin')]))
```

## Expected behavior

Respect the caller's explicit tool ordering, and use the additional GUI-oriented directories as fallbacks when a tool is missing from the incoming PATH.

## Reproduction

1. Have zstd installed both in a project-local prefix and in `/opt/homebrew/bin`.
2. Put the project-local bin directory first in the incoming PATH.
3. Compare `shutil.which('zstd', path=os.environ['PATH'])` with resolution using the script's constructed PATH.

Observed locally (project path abbreviated):

```text
incoming PATH:     <project>/.mise/local/zstd/bin/zstd
upstream build:    /opt/homebrew/bin/zstd
fallbacks at end:  <project>/.mise/local/zstd/bin/zstd
```

The same ordering can affect other tools present in both locations. This report demonstrates executable selection, not a claim that a particular game fails with either zstd version.

## Proposed change

This local one-line change preserves the selected project-local tool while retaining the fallback directories:

```python
env = dict(os.environ, PATH=os.pathsep.join([os.environ.get('PATH', '/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin')] + TOOL_PATHS))
```

Related: #1233 addresses choosing a dotnet with SDK 10. This report covers the broader caller-PATH ordering, including zstd, XcodeGen and glslang. A dotnet-specific fix alone would not address those other tools. I did not find an existing issue specifically covering this behavior.

## Environment and checks

- Apple silicon Mac, Xcode 27.2; project-local Python 3.14.7 and .NET SDK 10.0.403 managed with mise.
- `dm/gfx/tools/tool_lock.py --check-tools`: passed.
- `test_nsp_env_checks.py`: 16 tests passed with the local PATH-order change.
- Local build-entrypoint test rejecting global-tool fallback: passed.
- Python dependency check: passed.
- Actual incoming/upstream/patched zstd executable selection compared as shown above.
- Full IPA build and device installation on this revision: not performed.
- No game files, keys, device identifiers or extracted game data are included.
title: NSP script overrides caller-selected project tools by prepending Homebrew to PATH

body:
Would you support moving game profiles into a separate repository that both nxnative and NX2Apple can build from? I’m volunteering to do the migration end to end. Before I start, I’d like to know whether this is a direction you want for nxnative and what you would need to see before merging it.

### How a game contribution reaches both projects today

We regularly hear from contributors at NX2Apple who have gotten a game running and want to share it. Today, we direct them to open a profile PR in `seedds/nxnative` first and link it from the relevant NX2Apple issue. Normally, they wait for the change to land and for NX2Apple to pick up that engine revision. An NX2Apple maintainer can carry a verified profile as a temporary patch, but then someone has to track the same change in both projects. [NX2Apple’s contributor guide](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/8d13135e2a1eec10406f6b486157ec1d2f56eafd/CONTRIBUTING.md#L23-L37)

The Hades II 1.0.137848 update is a good example. The NX2Apple patch changed one `game.tsv` file. Its header says “Profile data only” and references both NX2Apple issue #123 and nxnative PR #485. The contributor had supplied the build information, and the engine already had the capabilities the update needed. Getting that information to players still took coordination across two repositories. [Hades II profile patch](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/8d13135e2a1eec10406f6b486157ec1d2f56eafd/patches/0011-hades2-update-profile.patch)

With a shared catalog, that contributor could open **one profiles PR**, whichever project they came through. A profile maintainer who owns the game could reproduce the result and review it. Once accepted, both projects could use the profile with a compatible engine revision. That gives more people a way to help maintain game support and frees nxnative’s maintainers from having to approve every title update.

### Why I think the review boundary matters

I looked at 994 proposed nxnative PRs through November 5, 2026, including open and closed submissions. Of those, **598 (60.2%) were prompted by particular games**. The breakdown was 199 direct game-support PRs, 367 shared fixes prompted by a named game, and 32 game-related packaging or player fixes.

The weekly change was revealing. From October 23–29 to October 30–November 5, direct-support PRs went from **95 to 96**, while shared fixes prompted by a game went from **109 to 243**. In a random sample of 50 from that shared-fix category, **at least 37 lacked documented evidence that a second distinct game exercised the changed behavior**.

I wouldn’t expect a repository split to remove 60% of engine PRs. Games routinely uncover real engine defects. What the figures point to is a review burden: a contributor can have convincing evidence that a patch fixes their game while the maintainer still has to establish whether it belongs in the shared engine. A profiles repository would let the contributor ship the verified result while that second question is investigated.

### What belongs in each repository

**nxnative would own** the builder and bundler, guest-code rewriter, host, app lifecycle and API hooks, graphics translation layers, and the interfaces profiles use.

**The profiles repository would own** title and build IDs, per-game settings and patches, title-specific handlers, shader inputs and replacements, compatibility notes, test routes, and the playable-games catalog.

Monster Hunter Rise illustrates the distinction. The host knows how to write a frame-rate limit. The build ID, pointer location, and field offset for Monster Hunter Rise 16.0.2 describe one particular game build. The host should provide the write operation, and the profile should supply those values. Someone porting the next update could then change the addresses without editing shared host code. [Current frame-limit implementation](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/865cc35f/dm/host/hle_fpslock.c#L24-L33)

Players would keep using the normal build command, with an official profile catalog as the default. A contributor could point the builder at another repository or a local folder to test a change before submitting it. A selected profile could patch verified guest instructions, provide a shader replacement, or compile a title-specific handler through a versioned interface. The build would record which engine and profile revisions it used. nxnative’s existing support for external profile directories gives us a starting point. [Current profile lookup](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/865cc35f/dm/games/game.py#L62-L75)

### When a game-discovered fix should move into nxnative

I propose a **two-game validation rule** for promoting a profile fix into the engine. The contributor would name two distinct games, show how each exercised the changed operation, and record the expected and observed result. The second game can demonstrate that an existing case still behaves correctly. It doesn’t need to reproduce the original failure.

- **Cricket 24’s black player kits.** The contributor traced the problem to a texture-copy pattern and verified the repair during a match. The PR also explicitly says Cricket 24 was the only game run. Under this proposal, the fix could ship with Cricket 24 while someone with another game validates the same operation. [PR #1187](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1187)
- **Super Mario Galaxy’s Vulkan shader-link failure.** Galaxy packed successfully after the fix. A contributor then ran Hades through the same changed linker step and verified that its output library was byte-identical. I would accept that as two-game validation. The second contributor supplied exactly the evidence the engine reviewer needed. [PR #701 and follow-up](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/701)

### What I’ll take on

I’m volunteering to set up the profiles repository, migrate the existing profiles and title-specific code, build the profile-selection and build-time interfaces, update NX2Apple integration, and handle testing, documentation, and cleanup of the engine tree. Before removing the existing copies, I’d compare the migrated profiles against the current builds and document which gameplay routes were verified.

I’d judge the migration by a practical test. **Hold the nxnative engine revision fixed. Add a new game through one profiles PR, then fix an existing game through another. Build both through the normal nxnative command and through NX2Apple, without an engine PR or a temporary NX2Apple patch.** That would demonstrate the benefit from the contributor’s side and the maintainer’s side.

**Would you be willing to adopt this split and merge a migration that meets acceptance criteria we agree on upfront?** I’m happy to adjust the design with you. I’ll wait for that agreement before creating the repository or starting implementation.
title: Proposal: give nxnative and NX2Apple a shared game-profile repository
