### What happened

An iPhone build of Super Mario 3D All-Stars with `--work-dir` builds all three programs (the launcher, Super Mario 64, Super Mario Sunshine), then stops at the app build:

```
[20:07:20] one app holding programs 0, 1, 2
[6/7] app build · starting …
✗ app build (1s)
[RED] missing RomFS marker 'MovieData/BgMovieGalaxy.mp4' in <work dir>/extract/v393216/RomFS.img
[20:07:20] FAIL: no RomFS at <work dir>/extract/v393216/RomFS.img (missing MovieData/BgMovieGalaxy.mp4)
[RED] build_ipa.sh exit code 1
```

Cause: `other_programs` runs `main` once per program, each meant to use its own build folder, but `main` takes `work = work_dir(args) or nsp_dir / f'{g.id}_build'` (`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py:3018` on c83c48f2). Under `--work-dir` all three programs get the same folder, so each one's `extract/v393216/RomFS.img` replaces the one before. Program 1 extracts 56.5 MB and program 2 1.3 GB into the same `extract/v393216/`, and the package then finds Sunshine's image where the launcher's should be. Without `--work-dir` each program has its own `<id>_build`, so this only shows up with the flag. NX2Apple always passes it.

A fix with a test is in a PR that links this issue.

### What you expected

The IPA builds, as it does without `--work-dir`.

### Game, title ID and version

Super Mario 3D All-Stars, `010049900F546000`, update 1.1.4 (v393216), with programs `010049900F546001` and `010049900F546002`.

### nxnative commit

7249ee9f (as pinned by NX2Apple 1.2.1). The same line is on c83c48f2.

### Shader chain version

223f10d34f97

### How it was built and run

NX2Apple 1.2.1, "Export as IPA" with "One game, all inside":

```
build_ipa_from_nsp.py <staging> -k <keys> --progress json --env-file <file> --work-dir <work dir> --platform ios --romfs bundle -o <ipa>
```

### Device and OS

Built on a MacBook Pro (M1 Max), macOS 26.7.2. Run on an iPhone 13 Pro, iOS 27.0.1.

### Settings and environment overrides

`DM_PROF_TEX_BC_CPU=1` (NX2Apple's "Older devices" option; the iPhone 13 Pro's A15 has no BC formats). It has nothing to do with the build failure.

### Logs

The build output is quoted above. With the fix applied to that engine, the same build finished, and the launcher ran on the phone. Choosing Super Mario 64 went through `oe::ExecuteProgram(1, 16 bytes of parameters …): recorded, this program ends`, and the restart came up as `program 1 of 0 1 2`. Its JIT requests were served from the image, and it ran 300+ frames at 30 fps with sound and saves, and looked right. Sunshine was built but not yet run on the phone.

### What happened

### What happened
Taking out the Ocarina and playing any note aborts the game at once, every time (reproduced 5 times, with rumble on and with rumble off). On the Mac the window just closes.

```
[RED] sf: the game connects to service hid itself, which the host does not serve
game called nn::diag abort: Result 0xe15, call site sdk+0x6c8e54
FATAL game aborted
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

### Where (sdk symbols, read with `dm/tools/nso_syms.py` from this game's `sdk`)
```
sdk+0x6c8e54 -> nn::hid::detail::PermitVibration(bool) +0x104   (nearest symbol to the abort site)
sdk+0x6c9390 -> nn::hid::detail::IsOunceVibrationDeviceMounted(bool*, nn::hid::VibrationDeviceHandle const&) +0x20
sdk+0x6cd610 -> nn::hid::IsOunceVibrationDeviceMounted(nn::hid::VibrationDeviceHandle const&) +0x20
```

### Cause
SDK 22 has a Switch 2 ("Ounce") variant of `IsVibrationDeviceMounted`. Its own call opens the hid service, which `sm` refuses (0xe15), the same chain as in "Whether a vibration device is mounted" in `docs/reference/services.md` (Super Mario Odyssey). The host answers `nn::hid::IsVibrationDeviceMounted` but not `nn::hid::IsOunceVibrationDeviceMounted`, on main `865cc35f` too. Turning rumble off (`DM_RUMBLE=0`) does not avoid it: the game asks when a note is played either way.

### Fix (tested)
Answer the Ounce variant as the existing hook does (`dm/host/hle_hid.c`). It applies cleanly to main `865cc35f`:
```diff
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn3hid24IsVibrationDeviceMountedERKNS0_21VibrationDeviceHandleE", "vibration: device mounted when the channel has an output", unsigned, h_hid_VibMounted, const uint32_t *h) {
     return h && vib_targets(*h);
 }
+// SDK 22 (Switch 2, "Ounce") asks the same through its own entry point, which reaches the hid service the same way (sm refuses it: nn::diag abort 0xe15 under
+// hid::detail::IsOunceVibrationDeviceMounted). The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (0400486024DEC000) asks it when the player plays a note on the Ocarina, with rumble on or off
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn3hid29IsOunceVibrationDeviceMountedERKNS0_21VibrationDeviceHandleE", "vibration (SDK 22): device mounted when the channel has an output", unsigned, h_hid_VibMountedOunce, const uint32_t *h) {
+    return h && vib_targets(*h);
+}
```

**Result:** the Ocarina plays every note, and there's no crash with rumble off or on (the run ends with `host exited with 0`). No `service hid` line any more. I felt no controller vibration in this game at all, with or without the change, so the path where a device is reported mounted and the game then vibrates isn't verified. Not run: the tests, other SDK 22 games. A reference entry is not written.

### Game, build, device
- `0400486024DEC000`, update-only NUP v131072, Mac app (`--platform mac-app`)
- stan69b's `oot-clean` `6c71e575` + #1345, #1332, #1350, #1343, #1376 merged locally, translator rebuilt, chain `ba403debcc6c`, plus this change (and the `NvPkg` unwrap that #1420 also makes)

- `env.txt`: `DM_FULLSCREEN=0`, `DM_ALIAS_SIZE=0x400000000` (and `DM_RUMBLE=0` for the rumble-off run)

Happy to open a PR with it if that's preferred.

body:
# Switch 2 title `04004860224DEC000` (Zelda, "TLZOT" NSW2 1.1.1): boots to `nnMain`, streams assets, then aborts on an async null

First bring-up attempt for this title. No profile existed, so it was surveyed and packed with a provisional one. The build works end to end; the game dies at runtime in two different ways, both after a long, healthy boot.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5 (25F71), Xcode 26.6 (17F113) + Metal Toolchain 17F109, Apple M4 Pro, 24 GB
- `nxnative` main, Python 3.15.2 venv, dotnet 10.0.403
- Source: one `.nup` holding only the update (`v131072`, 24.47 GB, `standalone_update`), no base game — the sanctioned path per the README
- Build: `--platform mac-app --allow-other-metal --work-dir <...>/oot_build`

## Two build issues that needed local patches (may be worth fixing upstream)

1. **Xcode 26.6 cannot compile the Mac host.** `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` sets `MTL4FXTemporalScaler` offset properties inside `if (@available(macOS 27.0, iOS 27.0, *))`. A runtime check does not satisfy clang when the SDK headers do not declare the property:

   ```
   error: property 'colorContentOffsetX' not found on object of type 'const __strong id<MTL4FXTemporalScaler>'
   ... 8 errors, 56 warnings
   ```

   Workaround: wrap the block in `#if __MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED >= 270000` so it compiles on a 26.x SDK and stays identical on 27.x. With that, the host builds and `--allow-other-metal` carries the shaders.

2. **The pipeline prebuild is hard-coded on** (`DM_PSO_PREBUILD='tool'` at `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py:2668`), so there is no way to reach a run without it. It took 35+ minutes here and was the only thing between a build and a test run. Patching that line to honour the env var makes `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0` work, matching `regress.py --quick`.

## Runtime symptom 1 — guest assert, empty message (the blocker)

The game boots cleanly and gets far: SDK init, audio, save, RomFS, window, scene assets.

```
[dm] >>> nnosInitialize
[dm] >>> nninitInitializeSdkModule
[dm] >>> nninitStartup
[dm] [mem] heap 6.20 GB (heap region 9.12 GB)
[dm] >>> nnMain
[dm] audren: render thread 0 started ...
[dm] fs mount save: → .../run/save.work (transactional save ...)
[dm] RomFS image ...: 187186 entries
[dm] [nvn] WindowCrop 0,0 2048x1152
[dm] fs mount _npln: → .../RomFS.img (read-only)
[dm] fs open not found: _npln:/npln_config.json
[dm] fs open [51.33s] content:/Tex/ShadowCastle.bntx.zs mode=1 → image entry 31721
[dm] MapMemory 0x42f751000 <- 0x442c76000 +0x10000
[dm] [diag] abort at :  (:0) message format
[dm] game called nn::diag abort: Result 0, call site sdk+0xb8fe8
[dm] bt: sdk+0xb8fe8 sdk+0xba138 sdk+0x7bd670 sdk+0x777f30 main+0x21f0c80
[dm] FATAL game aborted
```

Disassembly notes (patched modules):

- `sdk+0xb8fe8`, `sdk+0xba138` and `sdk+0x7bd670` are abort thunks (`bl <helper>` then `udf #0`), so the real frames are `sdk+0x777f30` and the game's `main+0x21f0c80`.
- The game code at `main+0x21f0c7c` is `bl <import stub>` (returns to `main+0x21f0c80`, matching the backtrace).
- Immediately before the abort call in `main`:

  ```
  main+0x21f0c44: ldr x8, [x23, #0xf8]
  main+0x21f0c48: cbz x8, #0x21f0c7c     ; null -> abort path
  ```

  So an object it expected at `[x23 + 0xf8]` is null: an asynchronous load/creation returned nothing, and the game asserts with no message.

The abort **point moves between runs** with identical inputs — right after the `_npln` mount in one run, after 50+ asset opens in another — which points at an async/thread interaction rather than a fixed missing file. Attaching lldb (after codesigning `dmhost` with `get-task-allow`) changes the timing enough that it stalls in `audren` before reaching the assert, which is consistent with that.

## Runtime symptom 2 — Metal crash while materialising the pipeline archive

Roughly 1 run in 3:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=objc_retain+0x10
     lr=_ZN26MultiLevelAirntBinaryCache23getElementAtDestinationEP12MTLBinaryKeyRPU27objcproto16O...
```

and, building the same pipelines in-app instead of from the offline archive:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=dispatch_retain+0 lr=-[_MTLBinaryArchive materializeAirNTFromOnlineForSlice:]+0x1bc
```

The offline prebuild itself is clean, which is why it is the better route:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline prebuild done: 33190 pairs, 30515 bases built, 0 already archived, 2675 left to the draws, 0 failed, 821.1 s
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline archive: 1000 new pipeline bases written to p00018.mtl4a (31.0 MB, 2048 ms)
```

`DM_PSO_MTL4=0` removes this crash but then the guest assert fires much earlier (before any asset open), so it is not a workaround.

## What was ruled out

- **Asset data is fine.** Read the RomFS image directly and decompressed: `/Tex/ShadowCastle.bntx.zs` 47,238 → 184,432 bytes, magic `BNTX`; `ShadowHyrule_Adult` 203,767 → 708,720; `KokiriForest_shadow_leaves` 530,665 → 2,587,472. All valid, plain zstd (dictionary ID 0).
- **Not network.** The host's nifm is offline-cut already; NPLN is not usable and the game proceeds past the missing `npln_config.json` in the runs that get furthest.
- **Not movies** — `nn::movie` is bound to `subsdk0` but never called before the abort.
- **Not the heap.** `mem_reserve` had to be raised (`g_reserve = mem_reserve − mem_alias`, so the provisional 0x1f0000000 left only 2.87 GB for a 5.8 GB request; 0x380000000 fixed it).
- **Not the window** — booting headless asserts at the same site, so `DM_WINDOW=1` is required but is not the cause.

## Repro

```
cd <work>/oot_build
DM_WINDOW=1 \
DM_NVN_SHMAP=$PWD/profile/04004860224DEC000/shader_map.tsv \
DM_ROMFS=$PWD/extract/v131072/RomFS.img \
DM_SAVE=$PWD/run/save DM_TEMP=$PWD/run/temp \
DM_MSL_DIR=$PWD/shader/cache \
<nxnative>/dm/host/dmhost $PWD/patched_v131072
```

`DM_PSO_ARCHIVE=$PWD/pso/mac` makes the pipeline screen load from the archive (fails at the same guest assert, much later, after the "Preparing pipelines" screen completes).

## The ask

1. What is the SDK-22 object at `[x23 + 0xf8]` in this pattern, and is there a known host hook that must answer before `main+0x21f0c80` returns? The same assert fires earlier with `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`, which may narrow it.
2. Does a Switch 2 title need `_npln` (system data) at all here — is a stand-in needed like the existing `MiiModel` one, and what does `npln_config.json` have to contain?
3. Is the `AirNT`/`MTLBinaryArchive` crash a known Metal-version issue (Xcode 26.6 here, chain lock says 27.2), i.e. should this build wait for the supported toolchain?

Host logs (assert with `DM_SVC`/`DM_FS` trace, assert without, Metal `AirNT` crash, `DM_PSO_MTL4=0`): https://gist.github.com/JaydenElworthy/9d563e8ba41e802672d5d1c571e12a4a

The survey, the provisional profile and its `shader_map.tsv` are available on request. No game files are included anywhere.
title: Switch 2 04004860224DEC000 (Zelda NSW2 1.1.1): boots to nnMain, streams assets, then aborts on an async null; plus AirNT archive crash

body:
## Summary

Hi,

I've brought **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Complete Edition** up on nxnative, on Apple-silicon Macs and on an M4 iPad Pro. I'd like to contribute the general pieces back to the project: shader container readers, a translator fix for bindless handles, and a compute-based adaptive tessellation path.

The tessellation path is the largest piece. Upstream's [`docs/reference/shaders.md`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/shaders.md) currently lists "Tessellation stages are not drawn" with "Fix: not done" (Luigi's Mansion 3, Bayonetta 3). This change would fill that gap.

Everything below was checked against `main` at `865cc35f` (6 November 2026). Before preparing PRs I'd like to agree on the scope, especially for tessellation. I'll port each piece separately onto current `main`, rather than proposing my fork as one change.

## 1. Game, devices and builds

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Game | The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Complete Edition, `0100A0800E9C4000` |
| Tested version | 4.04b: base game v0 + update v458752 (RU release), SDK 15, REDengine 3 on NVN, modules `main` and `sdk` |
| Mac | M1 Max, macOS 27.2: Mac app |
| iPad | M4 iPad Pro (16 GB), iPadOS 27.2: IPA |
| Toolchain | Xcode 27.2, Metal 32023.922 (the repository's lock records 32023.921, so builds used `--allow-other-metal`) |
| Fork | Preview branch [`Melaylou/nxnative@witcher3-preview`](https://github.com/Melaylou/nxnative/tree/witcher3-preview), based on `5474c6f3`. It's a test build for players while we discuss this, not something to merge: the PRs would be ported onto current `main`. |
| Shader chain | `20cee2f628fe` in the fork. It will change when the pieces are ported to current `main`. |
| Build | `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` (`--platform mac-app`, and `--platform ios --romfs separate`), plus an env file that sets the guest memory alias (`DM_ALIAS_SIZE`; see section 3) and, for the iPad, an entitlements plist |

Both builds come from the same renderer source and translated shaders. Only the final Metal compile differs per platform.

I also rebuilt both from the NSPs in a clean room (fresh clone, fresh venv, empty work folder, no reused caches). All Mac and iOS shader libraries came out byte-identical to the tested builds. The other differences were commit strings, timestamps, a font file from a newer fonttools, the signatures, and the pipeline archive (see section 6).

The base game without the update has not been tested. The profile registers only 4.04b.

## 2. General changes

### A. Shader containers (`shader_split.py`)

The game keeps its shaders in its own containers, which the split did not read:
- `content/*/shadernx.cache` and each DLC's (RDHS v3: `{u64 hash, u8 1, u32 raw, u32 stored, zstd frame}` records with a footer index);
- `content/content0/staticshadernx.cache` (an FZLC header, chunked zstd).

With these readers the split finds **29,673** shaders, against the 621 the generic split found. All of them translate and compile. In the Kaer Morhen benchmark scene, draws dropped for a missing shader went from 158–175 per frame (with the 621) to 0, and none were seen in the other tested scenes.

Also in this area:
- **A hand-written pairs table, `shader_pairs_manual.tsv`:** `shader_split.py` merges it into the generated pairs, as it already merges `shader_facts_manual.tsv` into the facts. The Witcher needs 713 vertex/pixel pairs that the split cannot infer. Without the table, its pair tables could not be reproduced by the split, so the NSP script refused the profile. `shader_split.py` is not a chain tool, so this doesn't change the chain.
- **A `SeparateSamplerId` decoding fix (`dmsh_build.py` `decode_tex`):** for handle types 2 and 3, only the first offset names the texture; the second is a word in the sampler's bank. It comes with a regression test. Upstream has since added its own `samp_ubo` binding kind, so I'll check how much of this still applies on current `main`.

### B. Bindless handles through phis (Ryujinx `BindlessElimination`)

When `BindlessElimination` could not trace a texture handle, it **deleted the read and returned 0**. In the Witcher this happened for 2,971 reads in 2,504 shaders, including the deferred shadow resolve (14 reads every frame) and the environment-probe ambient.

The handles are ordinary `(c10 word << 20) | c2 word` combinations. They reach the read through phis that the translator's SSA builds from predicated Maxwell code.

`TryResolveHandlePhi` runs only where a read would otherwise be deleted. It rebuilds the handle from the phi's inputs:
- drop undefined, non-handle and loop-back inputs;
- drop constants when there is a constant-buffer input;
- merge identical inputs;
- of `{x, x << 20}`, take the shifted one;
- take the most complete handle when it contains all the others.

It accepts only a single complete handle; anything else keeps the old behaviour. **1,866 reads are restored.** 1,105 handles chosen at run time still read 0: they index dynamic texture tables.

An unmodified rebuild of the translator gives byte-identical SPIR-V, so the change is only the fix. It changes the bundled `Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader.dll`, and with it the chain.

Upstream's `4a0551e4` has since reworked phi handling in the same file. I'll re-measure on current `main` with the `[RED]` build report, and propose only what is still needed.

### C. Compute-based adaptive tessellation

Witcher 3 draws its outdoor terrain and its water as tessellated quad patches (NVN primitive type 14), and those draws were skipped. Outdoors, the ground and river were black holes: the depth buffer had no geometry below the horizon.

The game has 7 hull and 13 domain shaders, all of them quad / fractional_even / clockwise. Three combinations appear in play: two instanced terrain combinations (1 control point) and one indexed water combination (4 control points).

How it is drawn, with no Metal tessellator:
1. **Vertex capture:** the vertex shader runs in a pass without attachments and writes its outputs to a buffer.
2. **Hull:** the hull shader runs as a compute kernel (SPIRV-Cross already emits it as one) and writes the control points and per-patch edge and inside factors.
3. **Expansion:** a kernel sizes each patch from its factors, adaptively. Levels are clamped to [2, 64]. It culls patches whose outer factors are ≤ 0 or NaN, and appends cell entries for an indirect draw.
   - The layout is the hardware's: an inner grid, plus an outer ring stitched to each edge's own fractional_even points.
   - Neighbouring patches with different levels therefore meet without cracks or folded triangles.
4. **Domain:** `dmsh_tess.py` rewrites the domain shader as a plain vertex function. It draws once per tessellated draw, with the game's own fragment shader and render state.

Each domain's mode and winding are read from its own control section, so nothing is keyed to a game. Unsupported cases are refused with `[RED]` lines. The code is in `nvn_tess.inc` and `dmsh_tess.py`, about 580 new lines, plus about 50 changed lines in `nvn_mtl.m`, `dmsh_build.py` and the chain tool. The tuning switches are `DM_NVN_TESS_MAX`, `DM_NVN_TESS_BUDGET` and `DM_NVN_TESS_LEVEL` (`DM_NVN_TESS_LEVEL=8` draws a fixed grid for comparison).

**A recorder op.** The hull kernel calls `setThreadgroupMemoryLength:atIndex:`, and the deferred recorder (`nvn_rec.h`) had no stand-in for it. With the encode thread on (the iOS default), the game stopped at its first tessellated draw: "FATAL deferred encoding: DmRecEnc has no stand-in for -setThreadgroupMemoryLength:atIndex:". I reproduced it on the Mac with `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`. A new recorder op, `RO_C_TGMEM`, fixes it. Nothing else calls this method today, so the op belongs in the tessellation change.

**Validation:**
- **Synthetic GPU tests,** on the shipped MSL, 2 seeds, both windings:
  - 24,092 patches, about 16.5 M triangles: 0 folds, 0 overlaps, 0 non-manifold edges, area exactly 1. Edge positions match an independent fractional_even reference to within 7.7e-8.
  - 48 meshes of 10×10 patches, in all 8 orientations, half with inside = min of the edges (which the game's hulls write): 0 cracks, 0 folds.
  - The expansion kernel's counts, culling and budget behaviour are exact, and it never writes out of bounds.
- **On the Mac:**
  - Scenes: White Orchard (hillside, road, lake shore) and a Kaer Morhen interior, plus a 19-minute scripted run.
  - 0 GPU faults, and no holes in the depth readbacks taken looking at terrain.
  - The only skipped draws are water draws with 0 instances, which draw nothing on hardware either. GPU memory is flat after warm-up.
- **GPU time,** against a fixed 8×8 grid:
  - GPU frame time p50 9.9 against 11.9 ms; domain shading and rasterising about 1.4 against 2.4 ms. The frame rate is unchanged, because the game caps itself at 30 fps.
  - Tessellation as a whole costs about 2 ms of a 10 ms frame. The vertex capture, about 0.5 ms, is the largest fixed cost.
- **iPad:** the same code runs on the iPad, with no platform-specific renderer branches. In one session the adaptive tessellator processed 570,960 patches, culled 200,810 and dropped 0 over budget. The run reached 4,200 frames without a crash.

**Known limitations** (the scope questions are in section 5):
1. **Spacing is not checked.** Every quad domain gets fractional_even positions, even one that declares `equal` or `fractional_odd`, so another game would get wrong geometry with no warning. This needs either the other spacings or a refusal.
2. **Budget overflow drops whole patches.** A draw that needs more than `DM_NVN_TESS_BUDGET` (2 M) cells loses patches, which leaves holes. Witcher never comes close: its levels stay at or below 16. At level 64, 2,996 patches would need 12.3 M cells. A fix would scale the levels down, or size the list before allocating.
3. **`gl_PrimitiveID` runs on across instances,** where hardware restarts it at 0 for each instance. That is safe for Witcher only because its shaders use it just to address their own outputs.
4. **Triangle and isoline domains** are refused, not implemented.
5. **Edges shared by two patches** can differ by up to 16 ulp (fast-math division). Exact fixed-point positions, as hardware uses, would make them bit-identical.
6. **Smaller items:**
   - indirect tessellated draws are refused;
   - the index buffer is read on the CPU;
   - each tessellated draw splits the game's render pass;
   - the per-draw cell lists are sized for level 64, which costs about 100–130 MB more GPU memory than Witcher's levels need.
7. **Testing gaps:**
   - the synthetic harness is not a repository test yet (I can turn it into one);
   - no other tessellated game has been tried;
   - Witcher's mountain terrain is untested;
   - there is no comparison against a real Switch.

## 3. The Witcher 3 profile

Once the general pieces are in, I'd send the profile as its own PR:
- **The profile:** `game.tsv`, the regenerated shader tables, `shader_facts_manual.tsv` / `shader_pairs_manual.tsv`, and the prewarm seed list `pso_manifest.tsv`. The seed list has 1,031 rows, recorded on a White Orchard route. A fresh install prepares in about 1.9 s, with no pipeline compiles during play on that route.
- **`depth_mode zero`:** the game selects near = 0 depth. Without this key, the bundled pipeline archive is built for the other depth mode and goes unused, and a first launch builds all 25,330 pipelines (about 3.5 minutes).
- **Docs:** the game note, the games-table row, `validated.tsv` from `scripts/regress.py`, and a Mac screenshot for the gallery.

**Memory.** The game needs a **64 GiB alias region**:
- A `DT_INIT_ARRAY` constructor reserves a 48 GiB region (`main+0x89e8`).
- Later allocations use fixed offsets up to alias +48.97 GiB, so no smaller region works.
- On the Mac this is only address space.
- My fork passes it through `DM_ALIAS_SIZE`. For upstream I'd put it in the profile's `mem_alias` instead, since the docs list `DM_ALIAS_SIZE` as a diagnostic switch.

**iPad.** The iPad's requirements are configuration only:
- Without the **extended virtual addressing** entitlement, iPadOS grants about 6 GB of address space.
- With it, the M4 (16 GB) granted 50.6 GB but refused 64.6 GB.
- So the iPad build uses a **50 GiB** alias, which still covers the game's +48.97 GiB.

On `main`, `build_ipa.sh` adds only Increased Memory Limit, so my fork passes a plist through `DM_ENTITLEMENTS`. The open PR [#1103](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1103) would make extended virtual addressing part of the default entitlements. If it lands, the iPad build would need only the 50 GiB alias, with no entitlements file of its own (question 5).

The upstream change that keeps guest memory in files (`865cc35f`) addresses the memory footprint, not address space, so it doesn't remove this need. iPhone is untested.

**Open items I'd document in the note:**
- **Refused pipeline (iPad only):** one pipeline is refused on the iPad: the terrain material copy, shader `2dcecea911db30ef`, which writes into an `R16Uint` target. A fix that forced an integer entry point was tried and reverted.
- **Soft distant terrain:** distant terrain looks soft on both platforms (open).
- **Resolution cap:** the game caps itself at 1280×720 in both modes (`rendering.ini`). Raising it in that file crashes the game at graphics start-up, so it would need a code patch. MetalFX upscaling costs about 1.5–2 ms on an M1 Max.
- **Console mode:** handheld mode (`DM_OPMODE=0`) works, with the game's handheld layout.

**Frame rate.** My fork has a 60 fps toggle for games capped only by their present interval. The game keeps its real speed at 60, and movies stay at 30. I'd fold it into the existing Frame rate setting (`DM_FPS_TARGET`, `fps_target` / `fps_max`) rather than add a new setting, if you agree.

## 4. Proposed PR sequence

1. **Shader containers:** the RDHS / FZLC readers in `shader_split.py`.
2. **Hand-written pairs table:** `shader_pairs_manual.tsv`, with its docs.
3. **Bindless handles through phis:** only what is still needed after `4a0551e4`, with before/after `[RED]` counts and SPIR-V diffs on other games.
4. **Compute-based tessellation:** with the recorder op, a `docs/reference/shaders.md` entry, the synthetic harness as a test, and whatever generalization we agree on below.
5. **The Witcher 3 profile:** Mac first. The iPad comes in that PR or a follow-up, depending on question 5 and on [#1103](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1103).

The `SeparateSamplerId` fix would join PR 1 or PR 3, if current `main` still needs it.

Each PR would be on current `main`, with the tests that apply, `regress.py` on the games a chain change reaches, and the template filled in. No game files, keys or extracted shader binaries would be included. The profile tables (shader keys and facts) are the same kind as other profiles'.

## 5. Questions

1. **Tessellation design:** is a compute hull kernel, an adaptive expansion kernel and the domain as a vertex function a direction you'd take for nxnative? Or would you prefer another design?
2. **First version's scope:** would quad domains be enough for a first version, with triangle and isoline domains refused with `[RED]` lines? For spacings other than fractional_even, should the first version implement them, or refuse them? And should budget overflow be handled (scaled levels) before a first merge?
3. **Testing:** would the synthetic GPU tests (as a repository test) plus Witcher 3 on the Mac and iPad be enough for a first review? Or should Luigi's Mansion 3 or Bayonetta 3 be checked first? I don't have them myself.
4. **PR split:** does the split above suit you?
5. **iPad memory:**
   - Is [#1103](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/1103) (extended virtual addressing by default) the way you'd go? If so, I'd wait for it rather than add a profile key.
   - How should a profile give a different alias size on iOS (50 GiB) than on the Mac (64 GiB)?

## 6. Other findings that may be useful

- **`metal-tt` is not deterministic.** Rebuilding the offline pipeline archive (`applegpu_g13s.mtl4a`) from an identical `metal-tt` input script gave different bytes on the same Mac: 801,131,344 against 801,139,520 bytes, from the same 25,330 bases and pair digest. So archives can be compared only by their inputs, not byte for byte. Every other build output reproduced exactly.
- **`DM_ENTITLEMENTS` must be an absolute path.** `build_ipa.sh` changes into its own folder (`cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`) before it copies the plist. A path relative to the caller's folder fails at "copy DM_ENTITLEMENTS". This is a possible small fix: resolve the path before the `cd`.

## Closing

The aim is reusable improvements, not Witcher-specific rules in shared code. The game plays on both platforms, but one game doesn't prove the tessellation path correct for the rest of the library, which is why I'd like your view on its scope first.

I'm happy to split the work further, follow upstream's conventions, and provide sanitized logs or more measurements.

Thanks for nxnative and for considering this.
title: Proposal: The Witcher 3 support, and compute-based tessellation for every game

### What happened

With `debug: false` in a translation job (the AST optimizer on; production keeps `debug` on, `dmsh_build.py` `XLATE_DEBUG=1`), two shared-memory cases go wrong on `main` (865cc35):

- A shared store of 8 or 16 bits (`STS.U8 [R36+0x100], R31`, `STS.U16 [R6], R34`, encodings from real compiled code) makes the translator throw: `InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader.StructuredIr.AstOperation' to type 'Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader.StructuredIr.AstOperand'`, or `KeyNotFoundException` on an `AstOperand` key. 12 / 12 such stores refused.
- An `ATOMS` whose result goes to RZ (`ATOMS.ADD RZ, [R7.X4+0x1000], R14`, a histogram's increment; `ATOMS.EXCH RZ, [RZ], RZ`) is dropped: the SPIR-V has no atomic at all. With `debug: true` the atomic is there.

### What you expected

The same code with either setting: the stores translated, the atomic kept.

body:
In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (`0400486024DEC000` v131072, docked, the Link's house autosave, MacBook Air M4), `fb_prepare` ends about 74 render passes a frame, out of about 178.

**Measured.** This is from an existing log, on a host built from lunks's `fix/gmem-pool-table` (574a38f0) because the game's profile is still in #1299.
- The `same-pass feedback sampling` line counts 0 passes ended at snapshot #1 (frame 2346) and 74,042 at snapshot #1000 (frame 3345).
- `DM_NVN_TSV` gives 178.4 passes a frame over the same 1,000 frames, all in Link's house.
- That counter (`g_fb_split`) covers both of `fb_prepare`'s rules: a colour attachment an earlier draw sampled, and the depth attachment after `g_fb_dread`. So how many of the 74 are depth splits isn't measured yet.

**The rule.** `g_fb_dread` is set for every fragment shader with texture pool bindings (TEXP / SAMPP) or dynamic handle arrays, `fs->rf.pool || fs->rf.dyn` ([nvn_mtl.m line 10222 on main 865cc35f](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/865cc35f/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L10222)). That's because which texture a pool handle names is known only on the GPU. #1068 (185b7dbf) narrowed the same rule for TEXU handles.

**What I'm working on.** I'll link the PR here.
- Count those splits by cause in the periodic line.
- Treat a pool shader as a depth reader only when a pool table bound for the draw (`pool_gpu`) has an entry whose storage overlaps the depth attachment's. Storage is compared by address range, so aliases and views count. Otherwise it's a reader, as today. `DM_NVN_FB_DPOOL=0|1|ab` switches between the rules.
- An A/B benchmark in this scene (`DM_AB`) and screenshot diffs.

If the game registers its depth buffer in the same pool, with the texture type the shaders read, the tables hold it and this gains nothing. The counts will show whether that's the case.

_Drafted with Claude; reviewed by me._
title: Ocarina of Time: about 74 of 178 render passes a frame end in fb_prepare, and every texture pool shader counts as a depth reader

## Summary

Assassin's Creed: The Rebel Collection boots and relaunches successfully on `975bb4c14456d145eb3d969814534eecdd996ce9`, but Black Flag's opening scene has missing world geometry and characters. The HUD, ocean, rain and fire render while the ship and characters are absent.

A local shader-extraction fix and two observed shader-pair entries restore the ship, characters and lighting through the opening ship combat. These changes are local and have not been submitted upstream.

This is separate from the older startup/relaunch report #1248, which is resolved by upstream display/lifecycle support plus the title's index-0 self-relaunch configuration. Related game-support request: #116.

## Tested configuration

- Title ID: `010044700DEB0000`; game version 1.0.0 / v0; NintendoSDK 8.2.0.
- Mac app, Apple Silicon, Metal backend.
- nxnative revision: `975bb4c14456d145eb3d969814534eecdd996ce9`.
- Shader chain: `d5fe9ae8bfba`.
- Generated provisional game profile; index 0 maps back to the same program and passes the launch parameter through.

These runtime results apply to that revision, not a claim that the current upstream tip was gameplay-tested. A subsequent source check at `865cc35fad7034d17c2190f8ce349f61f5bcaba1` found no `.forge`/scimitar handling in `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

1. Extract shaders and build the Mac app from this title using the tested revision's existing extractor.
2. Configure index-0 self-relaunch, launch the collection, and select Black Flag.
3. Enter the opening ship scene, with the objective to reach the ship's wheel.
4. Observe the HUD, ocean and effects, but missing ship/character geometry. The ship and characters should be visible and lit.

## Root cause and local fix

### Compressed archive contents were not scanned

The extractor scanned compressed Anvil `.forge` data as loose assets. It found only 326 shaders in `main`, missing the world-material shaders stored inside the archives.

The local change adds a bounded reader for version-27 `scimitar` archives, their linked index tables, length-prefixed dependency lists, and LZO1X sections. Both observed chunk-size encodings are supported: version 1 with 16-bit sizes and version 2 with 32-bit sizes. The reader validates file bounds, chunk lengths and decoded sizes, then feeds decoded bundles to the existing shader scanner and deduplicates results. It uses the `lzokay` Python dependency.

The complete scan extracted 147,601 shaders with zero unreadable archives. All 181 shader keys missing from the captured baseline runtime were recovered.

### Two offline shader pairings were missing

After archive extraction, geometry appeared but some lighting draws still failed. Metal rejected an unwritten fragment input at `locn3` for two observed vertex/fragment pairings.

Adding those runtime-observed pairs to the local profile's `pso_pairs.tsv` allows the existing `vs_pad` mechanism to supply the default unwritten varying `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. This restores lighting without disabling a rendering pass or skipping draws. No runtime shader compiler was added.

## Validation and limits

- All 147,601 shaders compiled; generated variants also passed.
- Host rebuild and Mac app packaging passed.
- A 240-second standalone run with the complete library had zero red warnings and was intentionally stopped at the test limit.
- Interactive packaged gameplay reached the opening ship-combat objective, "sink enemy ships," with the ship, characters and lighting visible.
- The captured packaged runtime had zero missing shader keys, pipeline failures or spontaneous crashes. Three transient audio callback warnings occurred; later callback telemetry showed no underruns.
- The tool suite ran 1,121 tests with 23 skipped and no failures, including nine archive-reader tests.

Later missions, a full campaign, Rogue, Freedom Cry on the final build, and iOS remain unverified. A separate regression-harness pass used the original 326-shader baseline and is not evidence for the expanded shader library; the compilation and explicit runtime checks above cover that local candidate.

## Scope of this report

The proposed fix is archive-aware extraction plus the observed profile pairings. No source patch is attached yet. This report contains no local filesystem paths, personal identifiers, hardware serial numbers, credentials, keys, saves, raw logs, game binaries or extracted shader files.
title: The Rebel Collection: compressed .forge shaders are skipped, leaving world geometry and lighting missing

### What happened

With #1299 (and #1300, #1312), the title movie and the title screen (whose backgrounds are 60 fps AV1 loops) run at about 28 fps on an M1 Max. Every frame, the movie library runs its NDVE network: 14 compute dispatches, 34.7 ms of GPU (`DM_NVN_GPUPROF` with `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1`). The rest of the frame is about 0.1 ms. Handheld mode (`DM_OPMODE=0`) runs the same work.

| Stage | ms | Stage | ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e6be82d835fbe4d3` (×2) | 7.1 + 7.1 | `a8b4fb48fee0ccf8` (×2) | 1.7 + 1.7 |
| `0a56002cdc7e1fce` (×2) | 3.3 + 3.2 | `5a7d69b067a7f011` | 1.5 |
| `4f41ccf24f163e0d` (upscaler) | 3.5 | `d15370a382630d4e` | 1.5 |
| `ba079f68ae288dba` | 2.1 | others | < 1 each |

- **The HMMA helper:** stubbing only the body of the helper `dmsh_hmma16816_f16` (all inputs kept live) takes the frame to 22.4 ms, so the helper accounts for about 12.5 ms. Most of the rest is the LDSM emulation feeding it.
- **Faster helpers tried:** two register variants moved fragments by `simd_shuffle` straight into `simdgroup_matrix` thread elements, with no threadgroup round trip. Both were bit-exact against a CPU reference of m16n8k16 but slower on M1: 6.97 and 5.90 ms against 4.24 ms for 4.2 M simdgroup-HMMAs.
- **Bypassing NDVE** (locally: its 8 network stages do nothing and its last stage copies the decoded picture to the upscaler's input, through a host switch that loads replacement libraries): 60 fps, about 7.7 ms of GPU a frame. The picture differs from the filtered one by 1.1/255 per pixel on average, with colours unchanged.

Would a profile or env option to skip NDVE on GPUs that cannot run it in a frame be acceptable? Or would you rather speed up the HMMA path, for example by keeping fragments in `simdgroup_matrix` across chained HMMAs? We can prepare either. We are not attaching the bypass libraries: they are made from the game's shaders.

### What you expected

The title movie and title screen at 60 fps, as #1299 reports on an M5.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, 0400486024DEC000, v131072 (1.1.1), from a NUP

### nxnative commit

Local branch: main 95f9a6a9 + #1299 + #1300 + #1312, plus our LDSM, AV1 and RemoveNode changes (not pushed)

### Shader chain version

43d0d49ea599

### How it was built and run

Mac app (--platform mac-app)

### Device

MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, 64 GB, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.2

Drafted with Claude; reviewed by me.

### Setup

Ocarina of Time (Switch 2), `0400486024DEC000` v131072 from a NUP, Mac app. Apple M4, 16 GB, macOS 27.2. The base is main at `f8a5618`, with these applied locally:

- #1299's BNSH slot 7/8 split change
- #1312
- #1320
- #1343

The map now holds 42,851 shaders, the same count #1299 reports.

### 1. Eight Foliage mesh shaders don't translate, so the door of Link's house is still missing

With the slot 7/8 change, 500 of the 508 new task/mesh shaders build. The 8 that fail are all mesh shaders from `/Shader/Foliage.Product.110.product…` (BNSH @0x25a000, 0x2a6000, 0x2cd000, 0x325000; variations 0 and 3):

- `604134a5262ff670`, `ca03b41694d4c196`
- `fed302d791a4ba43`, `819c33c90234fcb6`
- `9ecd96cec34c7315`, `740e2b04db624fb1`
- `ecead5cd0569091f`, `adbaa02880733cf0`

The translator stops on two unimplemented Ampere opcodes:

```
NotSupportedException: Ampere instruction 243 at 0x370  (000fe4000000c4ff00000005ff057243) is not implemented
NotSupportedException: Ampere instruction 243 at 0x38e0 (000fe2000000c4ff00000016ffdf7243) is not implemented
NotSupportedException: Ampere instruction 3a9 at 0x8370 (000ea400001ee12700000026242473a9) is not implemented
```

The same two opcodes also stop the compute programs `8692b34b521225be` and `83df46a0b1b379b4` (ApplicationPackage BAHS @0x1a098 / @0x1af18). One task/mesh program fails on `ISBERD mode b8 in a task or mesh shader`.

In play, these show as `shader … (mesh) failed to load` and `DrawMeshTasks without its task and mesh shaders: draw skipped`. The door of Link's house stays transparent and some of the ground is missing. I couldn't find 0x243 or 0x3a9 anywhere on main or in #1299.

### 2. Two compute shaders exceed Metal's bracket nesting limit

`1f78730053feb036` and `e172bd7ec218ab8e` (`/Lib/agl/agl_resource` BAHS @0x18ec00 / @0x18ee08) failed Metal compilation with `fatal error: bracket nesting level exceeded maximum of 256`.

Locally, `mac_compile` in `dmsh_build.py` now retries a failed compile with `-fbracket-depth=2048`. Both compile that way. Only failed compiles are retried, so `MAC_RECORD` and every other cached library stay the same.

### 3. Memory on a 16 GB Mac

With the mesh shaders in, the on-screen line reports `footprint 13928 MiB` by frame 2100. Before the change it was about 12.7–13.0 GB. Within a few minutes the whole Mac stalls, with audio callbacks missing for 200+ ms, and the game has to be force-quit. The log has no command buffer errors, so this looks like memory pressure, not the GPU hang in #1326.

A task/mesh pipeline also took 13.4 s to compile in the background on first use.

_Drafted with Claude; reviewed by me._

body:
### What happened

On a game whose engine opens two AudioRenderers (48 kHz, 240 samples per frame, two sink inputs each), one renderer's voices did not play correctly:

- A voice played as **one 5 ms frame** followed by silence; sound effects were missing entirely.
- The other renderer (music) played continuously, but occasionally had exactly **one all-zero 5 ms block**.
- No underrun, no `[RED]` line, no saturated samples; the AudioOut `appended` / `released` counts stayed balanced (a constant 4 blocks in flight), so nothing was leaking or starving.

Dumping each output separately (`DM_AUDIO_DUMP`) and cross-correlating them: of the 92 isolated 5 ms fragments on the voice output, 19 matched the music output's waveform with a correlation above 0.9 (max 0.997). The fragments were the other renderer's audio, not voice.

### Cause

`dm/host/hle_audren.c`, `render_main`:

```c
static int16_t data[NBUF][FRAME_MAX * 2]; static gbuf bufs[NBUF];
```

These are function-level statics, so **every renderer's render thread uses the same four PCM blocks**. `h_au_Append` (`dm/host/hle_audio.c`) queues only the pointer; the bytes are copied in `pull()` on the device callback. A block queued for one renderer can therefore be rewritten by another renderer's thread before it has been played.

The two-renderer support commit `18b435ac` split the renderer state into `ar_t` but left this block pool shared. Any game with more than one AudioRenderer can hit it (Mario & Luigi: Brothership and Unreal's mixer come to mind), not only the game this was found on.

### Fix that was verified here

Making the pool per thread is enough, since each renderer has its own render thread:

```c
static __thread int16_t data[NBUF][FRAME_MAX * 2]; static __thread gbuf bufs[NBUF];
```

(or move it into `ar_t`). With that change the isolated fragments and the missing sound effects disappeared on the device; music and voices both played normally.

### Verified on

- Source commit `f8a5618d` (the shared pool is still present there), shader chain `08342eb9cca8`.
- iPad Pro M1, iPadOS 15.6, unsigned IPA built with `build_ipa.sh` (`DM_IOS_MIN=15.6`).
- Title ID `01007ED02424E000` (base game; not in the supported games table). No game files, keys or extracted data are attached.

### Note

This report was submitted with AI assistance and is meant as a reference: the analysis and the one-line fix above were checked on the device named, not reviewed by a human. Feel free to rewrite or ignore it if the maintainer prefers a different shape for the fix.
title: audren: two renderers share their PCM blocks, so one overwrites the other's queued audio

### What happened

Differential testing of the Ampere translator (`dmsh_xlate`, built from source) found five ALU mismatches. Single instructions whose encodings were all checked with nvdisasm 13.5 (sm_86) each ran in a small fragment shader on an Apple M5 (inputs from c[1], destinations and a predicate mask to an RGBA32Uint target) and were compared with an interpreter written from Mesa NAK's hardware-checked `fold()`s:

1. **IADD3 with two carry predicates**: they are set to the bits of the carry count (`& 1`, `& 2`); NAK's fold gives `sum >= 2^32` and `sum >= 2 * 2^32`. The high word's `IADD3.X` adds both, so a carry of 2 loses 2^32 in a 64-bit three-operand add (`IADD3 R7, P0, P1, -RZ, -0x1, -RZ` sets P0 = 0).
2. **PLOP3 with two destinations**: the first destination is written before the second result is computed, so `PLOP3.LUT P2, P0, P2, PT, PT, 0x0, 0xf0` gives P0 = the new P2.
3. **POPC / FLO, immediate form**: bit 63 is applied as a bitwise not in every form; in form 4 it is the immediate's top bit. `POPC R18, 0x800000ff` gives 23, not 9 (nvdisasm shows no `~`).
4. **LEA.HI.SX32** (bit 73) is ignored: the high word is 0 rather than a's sign extension (`LEA.HI.SX32 R6, R5, RZ, 0x1` with R5 = 0x80000000 gives 1, not 0xffffffff).
5. **LEA with a negated B**: with `.X` it is negated arithmetically, where it is the bitwise not (NAK's `OpLeaX`); without `.X` the `+ 1` of `~B + 1` is left out of the carry out (`LEA R6, P0, RZ, -RZ, 0x0` should set P0).

### What you expected

The NAK semantics above (and, for 1, the carry the high word's IADD3.X needs). A PR with the fix and regression tests follows.

### Game, title ID and version

None: no game has shown these yet. Found on nvdisasm-checked encodings (CuAssembler sm_86 corpus, nvdisasm-guided fuzzing and variants), not on game shaders.

### nxnative commit

cb34473 (first found on 056e41f)

### Shader chain version

6e0c43ea7b30

### How it was built and run

`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate` built from source with `dotnet build -c Release` (.NET 10.0.403); translated jobs (`arch: sm86`, stage `ps`) converted with spirv-cross and run with a small Metal harness.

### Device and OS

MacBook with Apple M5, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.2

### Settings and environment overrides

None.

### Logs

Not a run of a game. Lower-priority observations from the same testing, outside the fix: NaN results are Metal's `0x7fc00000` rather than NVIDIA's canonical `0x7fffffff`, and `-x * 0` gives `+0` because spirv-cross lowers a NoContraction `OpFMul` to `fma(a, b, 0)`.

### No game files

title: Ampere ALU: IADD3 carry predicates, PLOP3 second result, POPC/FLO immediates, LEA.SX32, LEA's negated B

About 10 minutes in, just after I got control of Link, the GPU hung at **614.6 s (frame ~24,596)**.
- In the frames just before, the game was loading new data: 46 and 71 first texture uploads in two long frames, and a run of `alias region mapped 2.00 GB` lines.

body:
## Symptom

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 4.0.1 (derived profile) on the Mac: finishing a Grand Prix starts the staff credits (`UI/cmn/movie/StaffCredits.mp4`, H.264, about 136 s) and the game never leaves them. No button closes them. Quitting is the only way out (clean exit 0).

Reproduced on two builds: one from `cd859c38` (2026-10-31) and one from `975bb4c1` (2026-11-04, containing the latest `hle_movie.c` work including the H.264 drain / EOS fixes). The credits hang in both, so it does not appear to be the drain.

## What `DM_MOVIE_TRACE` shows

The profile says the game's movie library (`subsdk0`, SDK 4.4.0) plays the menus' H.264 previews; the credits go through the same player.

- **Never an end-of-stream packet.** Every `SendInputBufferForDecode` for the credits movie carries `flags 0`, in both sessions. Nothing in the log ever carries the `BUFFER_FLAG_END_OF_STREAM` bit, so the host's H.264 EOS path (`md_pump`, `avc_drain`) is never reached on this game.
- **The player stops feeding the decoder well before the movie ends**, then never calls `AcquireInputBufferIndex` / `AcquireOutputBufferIndex` again while the credits keep rendering:

| Session (host build) | Last packet sent into the credits stream | Leftover |
|---|---|---|
| `cd859c38`, 2026-10-31 | `time 136550000 µs`, `flags 0` | `4 packets queued` |
| `975bb4c1`, 2026-11-04 | `time 21824000 µs`, `flags 0` | `1 packets queued` |

  Both sessions stop silently: no further `[movie]` lines, no `Stop`/`Flush`, no `[RED]`, the game keeps presenting frames at 60 fps.
- For comparison, the menus' preview movies (short streams) call `Start` … `Stop` / `Flush` normally (lines `[movie] Start` → `[movie] Stop` → `[movie] Flush` in the log). The credits movie's `Start` (two of them close together, line 3195-3196 — video and audio decoders?) is never followed by a `Stop`.

So the SDK 4 movie player detects the end of `StaffCredits.mp4` by something other than an EOS input packet on the Switch, and that "movie finished" condition never fires against the host's `movie::Decoder`. My best guess as a non-expert: the player stops feeding once its extractor reaches the file's EOF and then waits for something from the decoder (an EOS output event? a position/clock read?) that the host never answers.

## Environment

- Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), Apple M1 Pro (`applegpu_g13s`), macOS 26.x, derived 4.0.1 profile with the Wave 1-6 DLC unlocker NSP.
- The full log of the 2026-11-04 session (includes the whole `[movie]` trace of the credits) is attached as a gist: https://gist.github.com/GB59/2f75679d86c0f2367704e9ff7f865af5
title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe 4.0.1 (Mac): the Grand Prix staff credits movie never ends

### Game, title ID and version

Wolfenstein: Youngblood (Deluxe Edition), `01003BD00CAAE000`, update 1.6 (main build ID `3a04994c1f53710a7672c64132e3438a`), with all four add-ons.

### Engine and graphics API, if known

id Tech 6 (Panic Button port), NVN, SDK 8.2.0. Also uses Havok, Wwise and Bink.

### Survey and what happened

**Playable on the Mac. Boots and plays on the iPhone, but slowly.** I wrote a profile and the engine changes it needs, working against engine `cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651`. Patch, notes and survey: https://gist.github.com/dnick90/02f595a9f42366ce9d587c690ff8ffb2

- **Mac (M5 Pro):** menus, cutscenes and mission 1 play fully textured with HUD and minimap, at a steady 30 fps (the game's cap) after about a minute of pipeline compiles. Footprint is ~4.7 GB.
- **iPhone 15 Pro Max:** no memory kill and no smearing. 30 fps in menus and while standing still, 16–20 fps in heavy spots while moving (GPU-bound).

What was needed, in short:
1. A reader for id Tech IDCL shader archives (`idtech.py`), plus a fix for the GLSLC 0x1e.4 compute control length. Result: 6,627 of 6,627 shaders translate.
2. A never-fenced `nvnSyncWait` is reported as signaled. This fixes the boot hang and is gated to this build ID.
3. New profile key `shader_bindless_pool`: material handles are read from the whole texture and sampler pools. Also a new resource kind `img_ubo` for image handles stored in a game uniform buffer.
4. The profile turns on `tex_flush_upload` and `tex_dirty_upload`, because id Tech streams textures into CPU pools.
5. New profile key `geo_lean_depth`, and command allocators that grew during load are replaced by fresh ones. Together these took memory from 8.8 GB to 4.7 GB.
6. New profile key `geo_mesh_ext`, with `geo_mesh.tsv`: lean geometry pairs run as mesh draws, which cut render passes from ~460 to ~80 a frame. Also a fix for a stage-2 uniform-update conflict that smeared the picture on iPhone while moving.

The patch is about 11k lines, most of them shader tables, and it was made against an older engine. I'm opening this issue to agree on the scope before splitting it into PRs on current `main`, as CONTRIBUTING asks for anything over ~1,000 lines. Still open: a faint ghost near the screen centre, first-minute stutter (no tuned `pso_manifest` yet), and iPhone GPU time. The game's `rs_forceFractionX/Y` setting works through the game's launch arguments and could become a `game_args` profile key.

### Device and OS you would play on

Mac (Apple silicon) and iPhone 15 Pro Max (A17 Pro).

### What happens

Mario & Luigi: Brothership 1.0.0 (`01006D0017F7A000`, main `59874c9b`) runs on a MacBook Air M1 with 8 GB of memory. The build is main `975bb4c1`, from 2026-11-04.

In the field, Mario jumps into the heart block and the camera swings in and back. Every time, the ground and the big rocks disappear for one frame, and the sea shows through. Characters, blocks, plants and the far islands stay drawn. A screen recording caught the frame: the frames before and after it are complete, and the camera moves smoothly through all three.

### What the game submits in that frame

We ran with `DM_NVN_COUNT=1` and `DM_NVN_TSV` and recorded two hits on the block. Both showed the same pattern:

| Frames | Draws per frame | `ReportCounter` per frame |
|---|---|---|
| steady view before the hit | ~460 | ~63 |
| camera move (1139–1162 and 1206–1226) | 990, falling to 250, back to ~1000 | 22 to 260 |
| **1163 and 1227** | **443** | **57** |
| 1164 and 1228 | ~1000 | ~197 |

The two dips are 64 frames apart. The two flashes in the recording are the same time apart.

So in the flash frame the game itself submits fewer draws, and Unreal culls the ground on its occlusion results. The host does not drop the draws.

### Console variables tried at run time

These were set with DM_CTL `cvari`. The offsets were found with `ue_cvar.py`'s `find()`.

| Variable | Offset in main | Value | Flash | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `r.AllowOcclusionQueries` | `0x6c84470` | 0 | gone (7 hits, none seen) | about 40% more GPU time: GPU p50 29 → 37–46 ms, about 60% more draws |
| `r.NumBufferedOcclusionQueries` | `0x651f620` | 3 | gone (seen by eye over several hits) | none measured: GPU p50 28–35 ms, the same as before |

### Workaround applied locally (attached `fix.txt`)

- `ue_cvar.py`: `r.NumBufferedOcclusionQueries` added to `NAMES`, so the rewriter writes its `UE_CVAR` fixup.
- `game.py`: a new profile key, `ue_occlusion_frames` (0 = the game's value, 1–4), giving `DM_GAME_UE_OCCLUSION_FRAMES`.
- `hle_uecvar.c`: `occlusion_frames_tick` writes the value into both copies, the same way the texture pool's code does. `DM_UE_OCCLUSION_FRAMES` overrides it.
- Brothership's `game.tsv`: `ue_occlusion_frames 3`.
- Documentation: a key table row, an `env_switches.tsv` row, and an Open entry in the game's note.

This is a workaround, and the root cause is open. Our guess, not confirmed: the host writes samples-passed reports when the submission's GPU work completes (`post_run`). With the engine's own buffering, Unreal sometimes reads a result that is stale once the camera jumps. Other Unreal 4.27 games with occlusion queries (OCTOPATH TRAVELER II) may show the same on a fast camera cut.

`scripts/regress.py` was not run. We tested only Brothership on an M1 MacBook Air.


[fix.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34413936/fix.txt)
title: Mario & Luigi: Brothership: ground and rocks vanish for one frame on a sudden camera move (Unreal culls them on occlusion results); r.NumBufferedOcclusionQueries 3 removes it

body:
At main `f8a5618d5f505a4c0a0bcac7c413872d3a53c009`, the NDSR reader raises `struct.error: iterative unpacking requires a buffer of a multiple of 16 bytes` when scoring a short pack's possible record starts.

`ndsr_shaders.records_from` tests offsets `0x10` and `0x14` with `struct.iter_unpack('<4I', d[o:o + 16 * 16])`. When fewer than 16 complete records remain, the slice can contain a partial record. The two offsets have different alignment relative to the end of the file, so aligning the whole file cannot make both slices safe. The subsequent record walk already checks for a complete 16-byte record.

Minimal synthetic reproduction from the repository root:

```python
import os
import sys
os.environ['DM_GAME'] = '010015100B514000'
sys.path.insert(0, 'dm/tools/fuzz')
import fuzz_shader_split as fz
fz.check(b'NDSR' + bytes(28))
```

Expected: an empty result for this empty pack, with no raw exception. Actual: `struct.error` in `records_from`.

A saved 127-byte synthetic fuzz input also reproduces this exact failure through the existing corpus replay. Its SHA-256 is `9d903df3733ee25bd443545b5e5a7764796dd37428106f82b0fd36aa831d7560`. No game files, keys or extracted data are involved.

The narrow fix is to score at most 16 **complete** records from each candidate start. Both supported layouts and valid shader/pair extraction need regression coverage. This is parser robustness work related to #313; it is separate from the older findings resolved in #452 and from the Monolith support in #1255/#1258.
title: shader_split: short NDSR packs raise struct.error while scoring record starts

body:
Findings from bringing Splatoon Raiders (0400380020056000) and Donkey Kong Bananza (040074A01BF12000) to an M2 MacBook Air (16 GB), 2026-11-03 to 11-04. The host changes are local, not yet a PR; posting so the findings are not lost and to agree on what to upstream.

## The big one: GPU timestamps without the idle gaps
- **Problem:** a game's dynamic resolution steers by the GPU time its timestamp reports give. With `gpu_timestamps segment` those times included the GPU's idle gaps between a submission's segments, where the GPU waits for the host to translate and commit. SR read about 16 ms of GPU time where the GPU worked about 8, and held its view at 0.50-0.57 of full size.
- **Change (`nvn_mtl.m`, `rep_ticks`, `seg_gaps`):** segment times are moved back by the gaps before them, so the time between two reports is the GPU's own work. `DM_NVN_GPU_TS=segment_gaps` keeps the old behaviour.
- **Result, played:** SR's render width median 0.57 -> 0.94 of full size, a third of frames at full size; dropped frames 4 -> 35 per 300. A large visual gain, still very playable.
- **Side effect:** the game now fills its measured budget, but the host's own GPU work after its last report (present copy, MetalFX) is not counted, so the real span settles near 18.7 ms. `DM_NVN_GPU_TS_PAD=<factor>` adds headroom (1.10: drops 11.5% -> 6.0%, width 1568 -> 1344 of 1920).
- **Reaches** every game with `gpu_timestamps segment` (SR, Breath of the Wild); BotW not yet checked.
- A scripted run that stands still hid it: SR had hardly any gaps there.

## Other wins (local)
- MetalFX scaler sizes in 16 px steps: scalers made 306 -> 147 per 1,000 frames, submit median 13.2 -> 7.0 ms, hitches gone.
- `image_shape` takes COMPRESSIBLE textures without IMAGE: dynamic-resolution targets share heaps; smoother.
- `bf_fn` keyed by binary keys: instructions per draw 71k -> 47k.
- Per-pool indexes of the sharing table and live descriptions: no walks over ~2,000 textures and ~100,000 serials per creation (~4% of the submit thread).
- Argument slots copied when only uniform buffers changed: CPU per draw 4.88 -> 4.31 us (one comparison).
- MetalFX colour for sRGB upscalers (`upscaler_color srgb`; upstream cee65140 derives it from the shader).
- `DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=game`: Bananza's speed no longer oscillates.

## Tried, no gain or reverted
- Draw-pass end barrier without resource-alias%2
title: Performance findings on a 16 GB M2 Air (Splatoon Raiders, Donkey Kong Bananza): GPU timestamps without idle gaps, and what else helped or did not

body:
### What happened

Played the opening, character creation and the first level up to the tutorial's last stage. The picture breaks in two ways, in this order:

1. A rectangular field of pink and white noise where the dialogue scene should be, with the rest of the 3D scene drawn as black silhouettes. The HUD, the ink counter and the game's own text are correct. This is not the ASTC error colour: the pixels are a random mix, not a flat (1, 0, 1).
2. Some time later the picture stops on whatever frame was up, which may be a normally drawn one: the second screenshot is the frame that froze, and nothing on it looks wrong.

The game keeps running while the picture is stuck: the log keeps writing audio callbacks (no underruns), save commits carry on, and the controller still moves the character behind the frozen picture. Only the GPU stops.

In the log the queue reports

```
Caused GPU Address Fault Error (0000000b:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)
```

and after it either every later submission is refused (`kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored`) or the failed ones come back as `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorInnocentVictim`. In run A the GPU time reads 0.0 ms from the fault on.

It has happened at the same place in the tutorial in three sessions. The last two, with the overrides below, are attached in full.

| | run A | run B |
|---|---|---|
| override in `env.txt` | `DM_NVN_CUT=0` | `DM_RES_CHECK=1` |
| first failed submission | `fence=69940`, frame 13,987 | `fence=102045`, frame 20,408 |
| how it ends | fatal, frame 15,862; 3,844 `SubmissionsIgnored` | I quit at frame 20,409; 36 `SubmissionsIgnored` |
| `missing residency` lines | 0 | 0 |
| footprint at the end | 9,451 MiB | 9,333 MiB |

Frame timing before the fault is healthy: frame p50 16.66 ms, GPU p50 12.23 ms, p95 13.91 ms over 300-frame windows.

An earlier session with no override at all behaved the same way: two faults it recovered from after 43.8 s and 96.7 s, then a fatal one at 787.9 s. That log has been rotated away, so it is not attached.

### What I expected

The picture keeps drawing. The note for this game says "about 4.5 minutes in the last session with no crash"; both sessions here go past that (frame 13,987 is about four minutes in, frame 20,408 about six) and end this way.

### Game, title ID and version

Splatoon Raiders, `0400380020056000`, update `v65536` over the base game (SDK 21.4.4, the Switch 2 `Ounce` build), no DLC.

### nxnative commit

`641d1480`, the engine the NX2Apple 1.1.0 launcher ships. The log says `build: commit not recorded`.

### Shader chain version

`95ba69b5403e` (`shader/cache/mac-b-95ba69b5403e.key` in the build folder; the log line is `build: … shader chain 95ba69b5403e`). 27,155 of 27,195 shaders built.

### How it was built and run

Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), started from the app's icon, so `DM_LAUNCHER=0`.

### Device and OS

Apple M5, 10-core GPU, 24 GB, macOS 26.6.2, Metal 4.

### Settings and environment overrides

The profile is the one in the tree, unchanged. `game.tsv` and both `env.txt` states are in the gist. `DM_LAUNCHER=0`. Otherwise none.

### Logs

Both runs in full, with the settings and the fault lines on their own: https://gist.github.com/ZhaowTao/740142f2f793dce7ad27ffd38f19ac5e

The two screenshots could not be attached through the API; I will add them in a comment.

### What I ruled out so far

- The submission boundary: the default (`DM_NVN_CUT` unset) and `DM_NVN_CUT=0` both fault, at different frames, so it does not follow a segment count.
- Residency sets: `DM_RES_CHECK=1` reports no `missing residency` in either run, so it is not the path of the Travincal fix.
- Memory: the footprint stays at 9.3 GB of 24 GB and nothing swaps. This is not the 16 GB case of #1281.
- The audio-device freeze of #1030: audio runs with no underruns.
- `DM_UPSCALER=metalfx` (#1156): the default upscaler is in use.
- `docs/agents/symptoms.md` has no entry for `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`, `InnocentVictim` or "address fault", so this is not one of the documented symptoms.

### What repeats and might be related

`texture type mismatch: shader d0ce73e71074df85_b (stage 1) declares slot 0 as Metal type 6, texture ID 428 is type 5 (NVN target 4, format 0x44, Metal format 134); bound as is`, 180 in total across the run (`tex_mis_note`). The note's Open list has this line and says it is seen once; here it is bound as is, and it is the only `[RED]` line besides the faults. I have not shown that the slot it names is the one the failing submission reads, so this is a guess, not a finding.

### Questions

1. Is `DM_NVN_MAGSCAN` the right tool for this? Its comment says it is a self-check for the magenta squares and can drop a shader's draws per phase; the blocks here are noise rather than one solid colour, so I do not know whether it sees them. It needs a fragment shader key: should I take `d0ce73e71074df85_b`, the one the type mismatch names?
2. Is there a key that prints or dumps what the failing submission bound, so the draw that faults can be named? I see `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` / `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL`, `DM_NVN_CBDUMP`, `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`, `DM_NVN_TEXRAW` and `DM_NVN_T2T_TRACE`; which of them is affordable at a frame just before the fault, and in what order would you try them?
3. Does `1d4b8e82` (task and mesh shaders, sparse textures and pools) change anything for this game? I stopped before rebuilding with it: the chain version changes, so it is a full shader rebuild, and #1263 says the split stops on this game's `NigoProc` `BAHS@0x9188` since that commit. If the profile line is the only thing in the way I will do the rebuild and report.
title: Splatoon Raiders (0400380020056000): a GPU address fault about four minutes in, then the picture freezes while the game keeps running

body:
### What happened

Nintendo Switch Sports reaches its splash and runs about 115 frames, then the host aborts inside Metal validation:

```
-[MTLTextureDescriptorInternal validateWithDevice:]:1421: failed assertion `Texture Descriptor Validation
MTLTextureDescriptor has height (32768) greater than the maximum allowed size of 16384.
'
[dm] CRASH sig=6 ...
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

Every run, at the same point (early in the splash, before any input). The title has no repository profile, so this build ran the NSP script's provisional profile  - but the abort is in the host's linear-texture path, not profile data: NVN permits a linear texture taller than any texture dimension Metal allows on Apple GPUs.

### What you expected

A representation path for linear textures taller than 16384, or a clear [RED] line naming the texture instead of a Metal assert.

### Game, title ID and version

Nintendo Switch Sports, 0100D2F00D5C0000, base v0 + update 1.5.0 (v589824). No DLC.

### nxnative commit

975bb4c1 (host log line: `build: commit 975bb4c14456`)

### Shader chain version

d5fe9ae8bfba

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py "<folder with base + update NSPs>" -k prod.keys --platform mac-app` and opened the app from Finder; the same crash reproduces by running the bundle's `dmhost` directly.

### Device and OS

Mac mini M4 (Mac16,10), macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2.

### Settings and environment overrides

none for the crash itself. Diagnostics used: DM_NVN_LOG, DM_NVN_TEXCPU; and a conditional lldb breakpoint on `-[MTLTextureDescriptorInternal validateWithDevice:]` (height > 16384) to read the descriptor as it dies.

### Logs

The descriptor at the abort (Presentation Thread, first oversized call):

- `width 1024, height 32768, pixelFormat 10 (MTLPixelFormatR8Unorm), textureType 2 (2D), arrayLength 1`
- host stack: `tex_by_id(tid=285)` → `treg_tex` → `tex_mtl` → `tex_mtl_` (`nvn_mtl.m:3402`) → `tex_linear` (`nvn_mtl.m:3068`, `[b newTextureWithDescriptor:offset:bytesPerRow:]`)
- so: a game texture in a memory pool, sampled through an NVN texture-ID register inside a submitted draw of the splash; the value is not garbage  - 1024×32768 is exactly what the game asked NVN for.

Tegra permits linear rasters up to 32768 per dimension (the swizzled cap is 16384); Apple GPUs cap every dimension of every texture type at 16384. `tex_linear` maps the NVN linear texture 1:1 (zero-copy) onto a Metal texture over the pool buffer, a mapping that physically cannot represent this texture. Adjacent symptom-index entries (absurd sizes from command-record copies, null textures) are different failure classes  - here the request is legal and the GPU cannot express it.

### What I think it needs (and questions)

Any representation needs the storage split across at least two 1024×16384 Metal textures plus sampler-coordinate splitting for the shaders that sample the one NVN texture. The host has precedent for "represent what the API asked for through a different GPU object" (uncompressed shadow for compressed render targets, compatible views for type mismatches, sparse pools), so:

1. Is there appetite for an oversized-linear feature, and which layer should own the coordinate rewrite  - the translator's sampler path (like the `fs_dual` entry for dual-source blending) or a runtime specialization?
2. I can dump which UV range the splash shaders compute for tid 285 (if it never leaves one half until a later scene, a narrower first implementation may cover it)  - say the word.
3. Worth a survey-time warning for front ends: the NSP script could flag linear textures with any dimension > 16384 it sees during the boot check, so "this title needs oversized-linear support" is visible before a long shader build.
title: [Bring-up] Nintendo Switch Sports 1.5.0 splash aborts on a 1024x32768 linear texture (NVN allows 32768, Metal caps every dimension at 16384)

body:
### What is missing

Most texture data lives twice on the Mac: once in the game's memory pool (the NVN description points into it, in the Switch's tiled layout) and once as a private Metal texture, since Metal cannot sample that layout from a buffer. For Switch 1 games (about 3.2 GB of game memory) this fits. A demanding Switch 2 game uses close to its 9 GB pool, and twice that does not fit on a 16 GB Mac, where macOS and a few apps leave about 12 GB.

**Measured, Splatoon Raiders (0400380020056000), M2 MacBook Air 16 GB, docked, fullscreen, MetalFX, `DM_MEMSTAT`, 5.5 minutes of play:**
- footprint 11.0 → 14.2 GB; at 14 GB macOS swapped 6.8 GB and the game fell to about 1 fps (frames of 0.5–1.4 s, GPU 500–750 ms a frame)
- at 210 s (footprint 12.6 GB): Metal's private memory (the kernel's graphics ledger) 6.3 GB; the game's own memory 5.6 GB charged, of which only 1.3 GB resident and the rest compressed or swapped; the compressor held 5.3 GB
- the step at about 195 s is a load: the game mapped more of its application pool (4.2–4.5 → 5.28 GB); Metal's allocation count moved only 9.7 → 10.3 GB over the session
- macOS can compress the game's half; it cannot compress Metal's, which is the half that runs the Mac out of memory

**Other reports that look like the same budget:** Mario Kart World runs out of GPU memory on a 16 GB Mac (#1193) and is ended at about 8 GB on iPhone (#1184, #1237); OCTOPATH TRAVELER II hits iOS's 6 GiB (#1226); Tears of the Kingdom grows in the Depths until the 24 GB watchdog (#832).

Related work that lowers memory in other ways: placement sparse tiles shared by physical memory (1110473c), pools backed only as far as used (1d4b8e82), unmapped guest memory returned (8ea27784), resolution variants sharing one heap (c484b13c), view retirement (#923). None removes the second copy of an ordinary texture.

### What you propose

Aim: each byte of game data in RAM once, either as the game's bytes or as a Metal texture. **Constraint: no re-uploads during play.** Making Metal copies purgeable and re-uploading them from the pool on the next use was considered and rejected: it saves memory by adding hitches exactly when memory is short.

1. **Accounting first** (small, log only): bytes of texture ranges held both in a pool and as a Metal copy, by pool type (`CPU_NO_ACCESS`, CPU-written, render targets), next to Metal-only bytes, guest-only bytes and the host's own extras. It says what each step below can save, per game.
2. **Pools the CPU cannot access: Metal's copy is the only copy.** The game cannot read these pages, and render targets already never touch them. Check whether the host itself writes the guest bytes when it uploads or copies into such a texture, and stop if it does; a range reinterpreted later (as a buffer, another view, an alias) reads back from Metal once, or is a red line. The hard part: pools are also Metal buffers, so any shader, copy or vertex fetch that reads a texture's range as a buffer needs the bytes.
3. **CPU-written textures: release the guest pages after upload, Metal authoritative.** Catch later CPU access with page protection (the host already write-protects these pools to see CPU writes) and restore from Metal on a fault. Costly only for a game that reads texture memory back; to measure.
4. **Formats that grow on the way to Metal** (D24S8 → Depth32Float_Stencil8 doubles depth) and **the host's own extras** (staging blocks, MetalFX textures, present and feedback snapshots, shadow copies, the pipeline archive), counted and given a budget.

The steps touch where every texture's bytes live in `nvn_mtl.m`, so a mistake shows as a wrong texture in any game, intermittently, under memory pressure: each needs synthetic GPU tests and `regress.py check --games`, and played runs on a 16 GB Mac for the games it is meant to fix.

### Platforms

Mac, iPhone, iPad
title: Textures held twice: Switch 2 games outgrow a 16 GB Mac (Splatoon Raiders swaps at 14 GB)

body:
### What happened

The NSP script stopped at the shader split on FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, on the first build of the game (one run; the check below is deterministic):

```
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps them in a form shader_split.py does not read; locate them (docs/agents) and add a reader
```

The cause looks like the `GlobalShaderCache-` clause that 18b435a (Mario & Luigi: Brothership) added to `uepak.inline_shaders`. It is still on main at cb39b33. RESONANCE's pak names a global shader cache too, so it now counts as an inline pak, although its shaders are in the IoStore container's shader libraries:

| Checked on the extracted 1.0.1 | Result |
|---|---|
| `FFRS/Content/Paks/FFRS-Switch.pak` | version 11, index not encrypted |
| Names in its directory index | 0 `.ushaderbytecode`, 0 `.uexp`, 1 `GlobalShaderCache-SP_GLSL_SWITCH.bin` |
| `uepak.inline_shaders(pak)` | `True` |
| `profile_guess.build_sources` | `ue_decode` False, `ue_legacy` True |
| IoStore containers | `FFRS-Switch.utoc`, `global.utoc`; shader libraries in `FFRS-Switch.utoc` |

So `UE shader decode` never runs, nothing reaches `<version dir>/ue_shaders`, and the split ends with `shaders: 0`. The docstring's "FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE's pak holds configs only" does not hold for this file.

Possible fix, a pak with a global shader cache counts as inline only when no container holds shader libraries:

```diff
-    return b'.ushaderbytecode\0' not in d and (b'.uexp\0' in d or b'GlobalShaderCache-' in d)
+    return b'.ushaderbytecode\0' not in d and (b'.uexp\0' in d or (b'GlobalShaderCache-' in d and not io_shader_tocs(os.path.dirname(path))))
```

With it, `inline_shaders` returns `False` and `build_sources` gives `ue_decode` True, `ue_legacy` False, and `dm/tools/tests/test_uepak*.py` pass (22 tests).

Not checked:
- A complete build with this change: one is running, and I'll add its result here.
- Brothership: I don't have it, so I couldn't confirm it stays inline. It should if its containers hold no shader libraries.
- The JP release (`0100606026F12000`): I only have the Asian release, so I don't know whether its pak names the same file.
- `regress.py`, and no test for this case yet.

### What you expected

The Asian profile's `UE shader decode` step runs and the split finds the 73,496 shaders its note lists.

### Game, title ID and version

FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (Asian release), 0100B8A026F14000, 1.0.1 (v65536), `main` b7f965b9d7227db8e29f04e84ea7331b, with 3 DLC

0ad559cdbb28

`--env-file` with `DM_NICK` only. No other overrides.
