body:
## What is missing

Joy-Con 2 and the Pro Controller 2 are not HID or GameController devices on macOS, so a Mac app sees no controller at all. I have a working Mac implementation on a branch and would like to know how you want it split and whether the launcher change is welcome before I open any PR. Tested on a left and a right Joy-Con 2, macOS 27, Apple silicon.

## What you propose

### What it does

- **A CoreBluetooth module in the host** (`dm/host/switch2_proto.h`, pure C with tests; `pad_switch2_mac.h`) speaking Nintendo's GATT protocol, the same one PR #645 ports to iOS. It runs the handshake, reads the 63-byte reports, and feeds the existing pad, motion and haptics paths.
- **A new "Switch 2 controllers" section in the Mac launcher**, with a **pairing sheet** (`Switch2Pairing.swift`): pair a controller once (hold Sync), and from then on any button press wakes it toward the Mac and the game connects, no Sync. Pairing gives the controller the Mac's Bluetooth address and the pairing keys with the console's 0x15 commands (the controller forgets any console it was paired with). The section also has a Use Switch 2 controllers switch (`DM_SW2`) and, per game, which Joy-Cons play together or alone (`DM_SW2_GROUPS`). The Mac app's Info.plist gets `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription`; without it the module stays off, because macOS ends a process that scans without it.
- **Joy-Cons as devices of their own in `hle_hid.c`**: a pair is a JoyDual npad with a sensor per Joy-Con; when a game asks for single assignment (or the controller screen needs more players than controllers) the pair splits into JoyLeft / JoyRight on two npads; the game's assignment calls now take effect. A game that supports no Joy-Con style gets the merged state as before. This is the part that touches shared code.
- **Rumble** to each Joy-Con's vibration channel (the right and left ones differ), through a per-player output hook in `haptics_apple`.
- **Home** (the existing hold-to-quit prompt) and **Capture** (a PNG in `Pictures/<game>/`).

### Size and checks

About 1,460 added lines in 14 files before docs (about 1,180 are new files). Rebased on current `main`: the host tests (143 checks, 64 of them new), the ASan and UBSan job and the tool tests pass locally; docs and the switches table are written. Checked by hand in Super Mario Odyssey, Super Mario Bros. Wonder, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate and Donkey Kong Bananza, and a normal Pro Controller still works through GameController.

### Proposed split (one concern per PR, each on current main)

1. Protocol, Bluetooth module, pairing sheet and launcher section: Switch 2 controllers as Pro-style pads with motion.
2. Joy-Con modes in the host: dual / single npads, per-Joy-Con sensors, per-game grouping on the cards.
3. Rumble.
4. Home and Capture.

### Questions

- Is a new launcher section plus a pairing sheet welcome, or would you rather keep controller setup outside the app (a front end, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`)? The launcher has to do the pairing, because the host starts after it.
- PR #645 (iOS Pro Controller 2) ports the same protocol. Should the protocol header be shared, and which lands first?
- Pairing writes into the controller (the Mac's address and keys). Are you comfortable with that, and with the pairing keys being the community-published constants?
- Is a change to `hle_hid.c`'s npad model acceptable as its own PR first, since it affects every game that supports Joy-Con styles?

### Not done / limits

Pro Controller 2 report, motion and rumble are from the community notes and **untested** (I have no Pro Controller 2). The Joy-Con 2 mouse pointer sensor is not built: no game that runs asks for its data (Donkey Kong Bananza only initializes it). Switch 1 Joy-Cons are not covered. The left Joy-Con 2's own sensor axes were not measured separately.

### Credit

The protocol is the community's reverse engineering: Peter Sharma's Finally the Controller Works, ndeadly/switch2_controller_research, trevlars/switch2-controllers-linux, Nadeflore/Switch2Connect. I measured the Joy-Con 2 axes and report layout and found the left Joy-Con's rumble channel on real hardware. Written with Claude Code.

## Platforms

Mac. The launcher change is Mac only; the protocol header is portable, and PR #645 is the iOS side.
title: Switch 2 controllers on the Mac (Joy-Con 2, Pro Controller 2): Bluetooth LE support, pairing in the launcher, Joy-Con modes, rumble. Scope and how to split it

body:
### What happened ## Pokémon Scarlet 4.0.0 (Mac): the game deadlocks in Trinity's per-frame thread rendezvous — main parks and is never woken **TL;DR** — Scarlet freezes at random points (frame 3,000 to 51,300; sometimes within ~100 s) while audio keeps playing, the host stays alive and nothing errors. The engine's main thread has parked itself waiting for a worker to say "frame work done", and that wake is **never sent**. I instrumented the host's condition-variable SVCs and measured it directly: across 641,221 records the handshake is perfectly regular, then one park gets no answer and the game waits forever. Reproduced **seven times**, including twice with no instrumentation at all, and on current `main` (`975bb4c1`). The GPU is idle and fully caught up at the hang, so this is purely CPU-side. I have not found the cause — details and everything I ruled out are below. ### Environment | | | |---|---| | nxnative | `975bb4c1` (current `main`); also reproduces on `a34c8283`, 199 commits earlier | | Machine | Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) | | Game | Pokémon Scarlet `0100A3D008C5C000`, base v0 + update 4.0.0 (v786432) | | Builds | `main` `421c5411…`, `sdk` `bb560bdf…`, SDK 13.3.13 | | Engine | Game Freak's Trinity (the same rendezvous exists in Violet and Legends: Z-A) | | Settings | Mac app, docked (`DM_OPMODE=1`), nothing else changed | ### What is actually happening Trinity runs each frame's work as a rendezvous between three threads: the main thread and two job threads. Main hands out the frame's work, then **parks itself** and waits. Whichever job thread finishes last "claims" main's park and wakes it up. This is not a once-per-frame thing — main parks and is woken about **10 times per frame, ~315 times a second**. Roughly once in every 160,000 of those handoffs, main parks and **nobody ever wakes it**. The engine's own "work is finished" flag is set, so main should have stopped parking and carried on with the frame — but it is already asleep, waiting for a signal that never arrives. Everything else keeps working, which is why it looks like a graphics hang but isn't: - **Audio keeps playing** — the audio renderer is a separate thread and never stops. - **The GPU is completely idle and caught up** — every fence and present has completed. It is not waiting on anything. - **Nothing errors.** No `[RED]` line, no abort, no crash report. The process stays alive and attachable. - **Input does nothing**, because the thread that would read it is asleep. The interesting part is *which* kind of failure this is. My first assumption was that the host lost the wake-up somewhere in its condition-variable implementation. It did not: I traced every relevant SVC and **the wake is never issued in the first place**. The worker that should have claimed main's park decided it had nothing to claim. ### The one measurement that matters I added a diagnostic to `dm/host/hle_thread.c` that records every `0x1C WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic` and `0x1D SignalProcessWideKey` on one condition variable into a lock-free ring buffer. In health the cycle is strictly regular — 2,048 consecutive cycles in the retained window, **zero** deviations: ``` 1D enter JobThread1/2 (a worker signals) 1D woke ... n=1 (it found main waiting, and woke it) 1C wake main thread (main's wait returns) 1C enter main thread (main parks again) ``` At the hang: ``` 6498.856 ms 1C wake main thread word=0x2 n=0 6531.346 ms 1C enter main thread word=0x1 (nothing follows, ever) ``` **No `0x1D` is ever issued for that key.** Every one of the 2,048 successful cycles has `n=1` — the signal always finds the waiter. So the host did not drop a wake; no wake was sent. ### How to reproduce 1. Pack Scarlet 4.0.0 as a Mac app with the profile from `dm/games/0100A3D008C5C000/`. 2. Launch with an empty `env.txt` and play. It hung between frame 3,000 and 51,300 in six of seven attempts; ~100 s in the fastest case. 3. When the picture freezes while audio continues, attach and call `crash_dump_now("live")`. ⚠️ **Do not use a diagnostic that write-protects pages or serialises guest threads — it will not reproduce.** See the suppression table below; this cost me most of a day. ---
The seven reproductions | capture | frame | generation | instrumentation | |---|---|---|---| | `20261103-185212` | ~36,000 | 0x8e1d | `DM_PROBE_WATCH` | | `20261103-185342` | ~36,000 | 0x8e1d | `DM_PROBE_WATCH` | | `20261103-201214` | 51,300 | 0xc88e | `DM_PROBE_POLL` | | `20261104-110519` | 3,000 | 0xc4f | **none** | | `20261104-115533` | 15,900 | 0x3ecf | `DM_CV_WATCH` (ring) | | `20261104-132551` | 12,300 | 0x3061 | **none, on current `main`** | Not load-dependent: the 15,900 capture ran at a flat 33.33 ms frame time with GPU p50 10.4 ms right up to the freeze, and at the hang `main fence submitted 3151 / completed 3151`, `present queue in 3151 / done 3151`, uploads pending 0. The participant and coordinator addresses are identical in every capture, including across the 199 commits (`coordinator 0x70eff3a210`, participants `0x70f0030000` / `0x70f0030550` / `0x70f0030aa0`).
The stuck state, read live from the frozen process `main` thread `0x1001` is blocked in `nn::os::WaitConditionVariable`: ``` 0x1001 backtrace: sdk+0x372274 main+0xb47d18 main+0xb47594 main+0x2b7aaf8 main+0x92d340 main+0x165e93c main+0x165cb7c ``` `main+0xb47594` is the return address in Trinity's submit function, whose loop is `while (coord+0x20d && !coord+0x20c) B(coord+0x18)` at `main+0xb47584`. `main+0xb47d18` is inside `B`'s park. | field | value | meaning | |---|---|---| | `participant0+0x514` | **1** | handshake state: main is parked | | `coordinator+0x20c` | **1** | release flag: **set** | | `coordinator+0x20d` | 1 | the rendezvous is enabled | | `participant0+0x4e0` | 0 | the mutex is **free** — nobody holds it, nobody is blocked in `LockMutex` | | `participant0+0x4ec` | 1 | condition key: a waiter **is** registered | | `[participant0+0x4f0]+0x40` | signalled | main's `SignalEvent` stands; nobody cleared it | | `coordinator+0x208` | = all participants' `+0x500` | generations agree; no counter wrap | So the release flag is set — main's submit loop should have exited — but main is parked inside `B` and nothing wakes it.
The ring trace in detail (641,221 records) `word` is `participant0+0x514`, the handshake state. Healthy, with every field: ``` 1D enter JobThread1/2 key=0x1 word=0x2 1D woke JobThread1/2 key=0 word=0x2 n=1 1C wake main thread key=0 word=0x2 n=0 1C enter main thread key=0 word=0x1 ``` Only `main` ever waits on this key, so `n` can only be 0 or 1. Timing, over 2,047 claimed parks: | gap | p50 | p95 | |---|---|---| | park → claim (`1C enter` → `1D enter`) | 0.014 ms | 31.4 ms | Two populations: ~9 parks per frame are claimed in ~14 µs, and one per frame is the frame-boundary park claimed after ~32 ms. The failing park is a frame-boundary one — its 32.49 ms gap sits right among the other long gaps (32.414, 32.442, 32.518, 32.724 ms) — and is otherwise structurally identical to the 2,047 that succeeded: `word=0x1` at park, `word=0x2` at claim, claimed by either job thread in similar proportions (`0x100c` 1,118, `0x100d` 929).
Why the captured state looks unreachable — the weakest part of this report The completer at `main+0x2d0010c` sets the release flag as its very first instruction (`main+0x2d00120 strb w9, [x8, #0x20c]`), then reads the state word. Its full decision table: | `ldar` at `main+0x2d00134` sees | action | result | |---|---|---| | 2 | return | no signal, state stays 2 | | 1 | locked tail `main+0x2d00180` | state=2, `ClearEvent`, **signal** | | 0, CAS `main+0x2d0015c` succeeds | return | no signal, **state = 2** | | 0, CAS fails, re-reads 1 | locked tail | **signal** | | 0, CAS fails, re-reads 2 | return | no signal, state 2 | It signals whenever it sees 1 and otherwise leaves 2. Main's park retries on `stlxr` failure (`main+0xb47cc0`–`0xb47ccc`) and re-checks under the mutex (`main+0xb47ce0`–`0xb47cec`), bailing to `main+0xb47ed8 stlr wzr` if the word is no longer 1 — so main must observe that 2 and must not park. A whole-image census settles who can write that word: of **44,617** release/exclusive stores in `main.patched.bin`, **208** store a constant 1, and resolving each base to its `add Xn, Xm, #imm` leaves exactly **two** at `#0x514` — `main+0xb47cc8` and `main+0xb47cec`, both in main's own park, both guarded. Every other writer of that word stores 2. Likewise `coordinator+0x20c = 1` is reachable from exactly one instruction, `main+0x2d00120` (the other six `strb [Xn, #0x20c]` sites address unrelated structures, shown by their neighbouring field widths). So the captured state requires the completer to have read something other than 1 while main had just written 1 — which under correct ARM64 ordering should not be possible. **Since that cannot be true, something in this reading is wrong, and I have not found what.** I had two enumeration errors earlier in this investigation (a 48-instruction resolution window that hid an entire completer region, and a post-wake path I had never disassembled), so treat this section as a lead, not a result.
What I ruled out, and how - **The probes themselves.** Reproduced with no instrumentation at all (`20261104-110519`, `20261104-132551`). - **Mapping or aliasing.** `vmmap` reports the page holding the state word as `SM=PRV` — a single private `rw-` anonymous mapping. No alias, no sharing, no COW, so there is no separate-exclusive-monitor story. - **The rewriter or hot-patching.** The live instruction bytes at `main+0xb47cb8`–`0xb47cdc` and `main+0x2d00130`–`0x2d00164` in the frozen process are byte-identical to `main.patched.bin`. Neither exclusive window was split or relocated. - **A lost condvar wake across SVC 0x1C / 0x1D.** No `0x1D` is ever issued, so `hle_thread.c`'s 0x1C ordering fix and `t_condvar` are not in play. - **Two concurrent exclusive CAS both succeeding.** A standalone test using the game's exact `ldaxr`/`cbnz`/`stlxr` sequence on plain private memory, two threads, **3,000,000 rounds**: both stored 0 times, exactly one stored 3,000,000 times. The hardware honours exclusives for this pattern on this machine. - **The completer claiming the wrong participant.** `coordinator+0x18` is written in the coordinator's constructor (`main+0x11d23b0`, beside the `+0x20d` write) and is stable across all captures.
Every instrument that adds latency or a shared lock suppresses it | instrument | result | |---|---| | `DM_PROBE_WATCH` (write-protects the page) | clean to 91k and 97k frames, twice | | `DM_PROBE_POLL` (spins `vm_read_overwrite`) | clean to ~94,800 frames / 74 min | | `DM_CV_WATCH` logging via `LOG` (takes `flockfile(stderr)`) | clean | | `DM_CV_WATCH` + one relaxed load of the **coordinator's** cache line | clean | | none | hung at frame 3,000 | | `DM_CV_WATCH` as a lock-free ring | **hung at frame 15,900** | Reading participant 0's own contended words does not suppress it; adding a single relaxed load on the *coordinator's* line does. That bounds the race window to roughly the cost of one contended lock, and explains why no probe that protects the page or serialises the two threads can see it. It is also why the first version of my own instrument was useless — `LOG` takes `flockfile(stderr)`, a lock shared between the waiting thread and the signalling one, inside the window.
Related reports — not #271, but probably the comment on it **Not** issue #271 (Violet, GPU BIF0 read page faults). That one wedges submissions with GPU faults; this capture has **zero** GPU faults or failed submissions and the GPU is idle and caught up at the hang (`main fence submitted 12385 / completed 12385`, `present queue in 12385 / done 12385`). But [the comment on #271 from alarkaspar98-code](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/271#issuecomment-6549600165) (2026-10-31) looks like this bug, filed on an unrelated issue. Reading the log and sample attached there: frames stop at 7,500 while audio callbacks run on to 182,000; no GPU page fault and no failed submission anywhere in the log; and `main` thread `0x1001` is parked in `dm_gate → gate_dispatch → svc_dispatch → svc_thread → block → _pthread_cond_wait → __psynch_cvwait` for all 1,314 samples. Converted against that log's module bases (`main 0x10b0a0000`, `sdk 0x10f584000`): | frame | that report (Violet 1.0.0, SDK 13.3.5) | this report (Scarlet 4.0.0, SDK 13.3.13) | |---|---|---| | SDK condition-variable wait | `sdk+0x371c54` | `sdk+0x372274` | | park inside `B` | `main+0x9a4928` | `main+0xb47d18` | | caller in submit | `main+0x9a41b4` | `main+0xb47594` | | gap between the last two | 0x774 | 0x784 | Same SDK wait and the same "B parked, called from submit" shape in a different build. That reporter sees it in **Violet 1.0.0 as well as Scarlet**, so the bug is not specific to 4.0.0, to Scarlet, or to one machine. Not conclusive — their log contains no state dump, so `participant0+0x514` and `coordinator+0x20c` could not be checked, and they are on a fork with ~35 extra patches. A `crash_dump_now("live")` on that freeze would confirm or rule it out in one capture.
Caveats and what I can share - The `DM_CV_WATCH` ring trace was taken on `a34c8283`. Everything else, including the most recent capture, is from current `main` `975bb4c1`. The stuck state is byte-identical across the two and the guest heap addresses are unchanged, so the trace is still representative — but it was not re-taken on `main`. - The "unreachable state" argument rests on my reading of the guest's code, which has been wrong twice already in this investigation. The directly measured facts are the stuck state, the absence of any `0x1D`, and the suppression table. - Participant and coordinator addresses are fixed values from this build's deterministic heap layout, not derived at runtime. Available on request: host logs with the ring dumps and lldb state dumps for all seven reproductions, a healthy control dump for comparison, and the standalone exclusives test. `dm_cv_watch.patch` (the diagnostic, ~100 lines against `dm/host/hle_thread.c`) is attached — environment-only, off unless set, no page protection and no locks on the recording path. Happy to turn it into a PR if it is wanted.
### What you expected _No response_ ### Game, title ID and version 0100A3D008C5C000, v4.0.0 ### nxnative commit 975bb4c1 ### Shader chain version d5fe9ae8bfba ### How it was built and run Mac, the host from a terminal (--platform mac) ### Device and OS M5 Max, macOS 27.0.1 ### Settings and environment overrides DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=metalfx ### Logs [nxnative-report-0100A3D008C5C000-2026-11-04.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395105/nxnative-report-0100A3D008C5C000-2026-11-04.zip) [dm_cv_watch.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395237/dm_cv_watch.patch) [exclusives-test.c](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395236/exclusives-test.c) [ring-trace-hang-20261104-115533.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395239/ring-trace-hang-20261104-115533.log) [state-hang-on-current-main-20261104-132551.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395238/state-hang-on-current-main-20261104-132551.txt) [state-hang-with-ring-20261104-115533.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395240/state-hang-with-ring-20261104-115533.txt) [state-HEALTHY-control-for-comparison.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34395235/state-HEALTHY-control-for-comparison.txt) ### No game files - [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.

body:
## Upstream status checked before filing

**These runtime results are from `6b0cffbb5e5c`, not current HEAD.** On November 4, I checked upstream `975bb4c14456d145eb3d969814534eecdd996ce9` and found that it already includes both the named `vi::OpenDisplay` hook and a non-returning ExecuteProgram implementation with `DM_PROGRAMS`, `DM_LAUNCH_PARAM` and `DM_PREV_PROGRAM` support. Related work: #1135 and #841 (both closed).

This report preserves title-specific evidence and the observed index-0 `/launcher:off` request. **The Rebel Collection has not been retested on that newer revision**, so I am not claiming the two older crashes remain unfixed upstream. The next step is to verify how this title's apparent same-program relaunch should be packaged/configured with the new lifecycle support, then test progression beyond the menu. The included local VI patch is historical reproduction/test material against the old revision, not a request to duplicate the hook now upstream.

Current source: [VI hook](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/975bb4c14456d145eb3d969814534eecdd996ce9/dm/gfx/hle_vi.c), [program lifecycle](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/975bb4c14456d145eb3d969814534eecdd996ce9/dm/host/hle_oe.c).

## What happened

Assassin’s Creed: The Rebel Collection reaches its collection menu after a local fix for a missing named `vi::OpenDisplay` hook, but advancing from that menu crashes with SIGILL. The guest calls `nn::oe::ExecuteProgram(0, ..., 81)`; the host logs the unsupported operation and returns, then the guest executes `udf #0` at `main+0x13a08dc`.

The menu-launch failure occurred twice, including once with a targeted probe immediately before ExecuteProgram. This report concerns the remaining ExecuteProgram failure. **The unmodified revision first hits a separate OpenDisplay startup crash**, described below with the prerequisite patch.

## What you expected

ExecuteProgram should transfer control to the requested program/relaunch with its launch parameters, without returning to the caller. The selected game should proceed beyond the collection launcher. Campaign gameplay has not been verified.

## Game, title ID and version

- Assassin’s Creed: The Rebel Collection — `010044700DEB0000`, 1.0.0 / v0.
- NintendoSDK 8.2.0. The runtime reports add-on content indices `{1,9}`.
- Generated provisional profile; no registered game profile at the tested revision.

## nxnative commit

`6b0cffbb5e5c5f1b9e78937b2287f3a2273e1aae`, with the local named OpenDisplay hook described below. Candidate logs correctly identify the build as `6b0cffbb5e5c+dirty`.

## Shader chain version

`b3ca4b7c621f`, confirmed in the candidate runtime log.

## How it was built and run

Mac app (`--platform mac-app`). The candidate host was built in an isolated source snapshot and packaged into a separate app using `dm/mac/pack_app.py`, reusing the existing rewritten modules and shader libraries. Diagnostic runs invoked the packaged host directly with private saves, temp and pipeline-cache paths. The original app and existing saves were preserved.

## Device and OS

Apple M5 Max, 128 GiB RAM, ARM64; macOS 27.0 (26A428).

## Reproduction

1. Apply `vi-opendisplay.patch` to the tested revision, rebuild the host using the title’s generated provisional profile, and package a separate test app. This fixes the earlier startup failure; it does not change ExecuteProgram.
2. Start with disposable saves. Launch the app and press Play.
3. Dismiss any collection-menu notification and select a game. The recorded path calls ExecuteProgram with index 0; these runs do not establish separate Black Flag and Rogue coverage.
4. Observe the ExecuteProgram warning followed by SIGILL at `main+0x13a08dc`.

The successful automated route used:

```sh
DM_KEYS='f1100:A~f12,f1400:A~f12,f1700:A~f12'
DM_PROBE='main:13a08d4'
DM_PROBE_LIMIT=2
```

These are environment variables supplied to the isolated packaged host. The frame-based run failed at frame 1730, after 68.259 seconds. A previous run using `DM_KEYS=40:A~0.2` failed after 50.721 seconds. A follow-up with that single timed press did not reach ExecuteProgram before its 75-second timeout, so the seconds-based route is timing-sensitive.

## Logs and diagnosis

```text
[dm] [RED] oe::ExecuteProgram(0, 81 bytes of parameters): the host runs only this program; the game carries on
[dm] CRASH sig=4 addr=main+0x13a08dc pc=main+0x13a08dc lr=main+0x13a08dc
```

The probe at `main+0x13a08d4` observed `x2=0x51` and the parameter prefix:

```text
/launcher:off /gamesoundlanguage:en /gamemenulanguage:en /gamerewardsPurchased:
```

This is a truncated string preview, not the complete 81-byte payload. Index 0 plus `/launcher:off` suggests a relaunch of the current program with the launcher disabled; full parameter parsing and program identity still need verification.

The immediate call sequence is:

```text
main+0x13a08d0  add x2, x8, #1
main+0x13a08d4  mov w0, wzr
main+0x13a08d8  bl  0x2a35c40  ; ExecuteProgram PLT
main+0x13a08dc  udf #0          ; 00 00 00 00
```

Original and rewritten bytes in this window match. The containing unnamed function spans `[main+0x13a06b0, main+0x13a08e0)`; the following address starts a different function. The crash stack also contains `h_oe_ExecProgram+0x4c`.

In [`dm/host/hle_oe.c` at the tested revision](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/6b0cffbb5e5c5f1b9e78937b2287f3a2273e1aae/dm/host/hle_oe.c#L107-L114), ExecuteProgram is documented as non-returning on hardware but its host hook only logs and returns. Related hooks always return no launch parameters (`TryPopLaunchParameter`) and previous program index -1 (`GetPreviousProgramIndex`). Correct relaunch behavior needs those lifecycle states to agree; skipping the UDF would not implement the requested launch.

### Prerequisite: original OpenDisplay crash and local fix

On the unmodified revision, two fresh runs failed after approximately 1.2–1.4 seconds:

```text
CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=sdk+0x3b65e4 lr=sdk+0x3b65e0
```

The instruction is `ldr x8, [x0]`, with `x0=0`, inside `nn::vi::OpenDisplay(Display**, const char*)`. The game calls it from `main+0x913c1c` using the name `Default` returned by ListDisplays. Only OpenDefaultDisplay was hooked; the named opener remained in the SDK and dereferenced the absent VI service pointer from `sdk+0xcd3450`.

The linked source patch registers `_ZN2nn2vi11OpenDisplayEPPNS0_7DisplayEPKc` in `dm/gfx/hle_vi.c`. It returns the existing host display object for `Default`, clears the output on failure, rejects invalid names with the observed SDK validation result, and rejects other names. It includes a regression test and Makefile integration. It does not patch guest instructions or alter ExecuteProgram.

The patched app renders the collection menu. Host and graphics unit suites passed, the VI test passed under ASan/UBSan, and host build, app packaging and signature verification passed. An isolated original/candidate Arceus boot comparison reached at least 600 frames in both runs without a new crash. The standard regression harness was not run because it would clean caches/create a stash commit; clang-tidy was unavailable. These checks validate the local VI change, not a fix for ExecuteProgram.

Missing shader mappings and a vertex/fragment interface mismatch are also logged. No complete rendering or campaign-gameplay claim is made.

## Settings and environment overrides

Paths below are placeholders for private per-run directories and packaged resources. Full sanitized environments and run outcomes are in `runs.json`.

<details>
<summary>Environment for the frame-based reproduction</summary>

```text
DM_OPMODE=1
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off
DM_LANG=en-US
DM_FULLSCREEN=0
DM_RUMBLE=1
DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0
DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0
DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0
DM_PSO_MTL4=1
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0
DM_METAL_HUD=1
DM_ROOT=<isolated-run>
DM_SAVE=<isolated-run>/save
DM_SAVE_SYNC=0
DM_TEMP=<isolated-run>/temp
DM_ROMFS=<app-resources>/romfs.img
DM_AOC_DIR=<app-resources>/aoc
DM_MSL_DIR=<app-resources>/msl
DM_NVN_SHMAP=<app-resources>/dm/shader_map.tsv
DM_FONT_DIR=<app-resources>/dm/font
DM_PSO_ARCHIVE=<isolated-run>/pso
DM_PSO_USER=<isolated-run>/pso_user.tsv
DM_WINDOW=1
DM_AUDIO=1
DM_KEYS=f1100:A~f12,f1400:A~f12,f1700:A~f12
DM_PROBE=main:13a08d4
DM_PROBE_LIMIT=2
```

</details>

## Full logs and source patch

[Full sanitized logs, run metadata and source patch](https://gist.github.com/cparmn/8f5d88ef7117995969f9bf7a1432f494) are available in a GitHub gist containing:

- `baseline.log`: full original startup SIGSEGV run.
- `packaged-stability.log`: full first ExecuteProgram SIGILL run; despite the run label, it failed.
- `executeprogram-probe.log`: full timed-input attempt that did not reach ExecuteProgram and was stopped at 75 seconds.
- `executeprogram-frame-probe.log`: full frame-based reproduction and probe, ending in SIGILL.
- `runs.json`: commands, settings, timestamps and exit status for those four runs.
- `vi-opendisplay.patch`: host source/test changes needed to reach the collection menu.

Only the local home-directory prefix in logs/metadata has been replaced with `/Users/USER`; the logs are otherwise complete. SIGALRM / exit 142 in the timed-out probe run is the diagnostic runner’s intentional stop. SIGILL / exit 132 in the two failing runs is not a timeout.

## No game files

- [x] The linked evidence files contain logs, run metadata and nxnative source changes only; no game binaries, keys, saves, RomFS, NSOs or shader files are included.
title: The Rebel Collection: index-0 relaunch findings on 6b0cffbb5e5c; needs retest with new lifecycle support

body: ### Summary In Adventure Mode, two persistent issues occur regardless of language localization or launcher setting toggles: 1. **Low / Unstable Frame Rate (30–45 FPS):** Frame rate immediately drops to an unstable 30–45 FPS (approx. 31–32 ms frame time with pacing spikes) as soon as free movement begins indoors (Director's office) and continues outdoors. 2. **Broken Outdoor Textures:** Stepping outside into the central plaza hub causes the ground surface and fountain statue to render pitch black (likely missing deferred lighting/shadow passes). 3. **Match Status Note:** Free Play singles on Stadium Court (Grass) remain locked at a stable 60 FPS. Matches within Adventure Mode have not been reached or tested yet. ### Troubleshooting Attempted - **Launcher Settings Toggled:** Tested different combinations in the settings launcher: - Toggled `Upscaling` between `MetalFX` and native/disabled. - Toggled `Frame buffering`, `Metal 4 pipelines`, `Pipeline prebuild`, and `Encode thread` on/off. - *Result:* None of these setting changes resolved the black textures or the 30–45 FPS drop during Adventure exploration. - **Language Localization:** Tested in both **English** and **Latin American Spanish (ES-419)**; behavior and graphical glitches remain identical across both languages. ### Game & Environment Info - **Game:** Mario Tennis Fever (Switch 2) - **Title ID:** `0400D4201C6EA000` - **Game Version:** Update v327680 (1.1.1) - **Host Device:** MacBook Pro with M3 Pro, 18 GB - **Tested Launcher Settings:** Metal 4 pipelines, Frame buffering, Encode thread, Pipeline prebuild, MetalFX. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch Mario Tennis Fever.app and enter Adventure Mode. 2. Complete the initial conversation in the Director's brown office. 3. Walk around the room: notice performance fluctuates between 30 and 45 FPS immediately. 4. Exit the door into the outdoor central plaza courtyard. 5. Observe the ground and fountain statue rendering completely black, while characters, water, and signs render correctly. ### Screenshots

### What happened

Following up on #1116, where you asked for 1.8.0 results. Mario Kart World 1.8.0 was packed from a dump (base + v917504) with the NSP script, which derives the profile from the v0 one.

**Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), MacBook Pro M5 Pro:** the title and the menus run at 60 fps (frame time p50 16.67 ms, p95 17.1–17.3 ms, GPU p50 about 8 ms, footprint 8.3 GB); no race has been played on the Mac yet. The title-scene trees that flickered for us on 1.8.0 (reported on #1116) no longer do since e07cba1c.

**iPhone 18 Pro Max (12 GB, iOS 27.0.1), built and run with Xcode (Increased Memory Limit):** boots and reaches the menus at 60 fps (GPU p50 8–10 ms), but iOS kills the app when the first race loads. In two runs the log stops with no crash line. The last memory lines show `headroom to the system memory limit` at 113 MB and 214 MB, with a footprint of 8,078 and 7,977 MiB, so the app's limit on this phone is about 8.2 GB. In the second run the race had started, and the last lines are `[RED] nn::codec VP9: a packet refused with 12 pictures waiting for a released buffer` (four times) right after the course intro movie's VP9 decoder (2560x1440) started. No JetsamEvent report was written. The menus alone already sit at 8.0 GB: 6.6 → 8.0 GB within the first minute, 6.9 GB of it allocated by the GPU.

- The split finds 11,604 shaders and 11,603 translate. `078997bf631992c5` (compute, `DrivePassShaderDefault.sharcb#BAHS@0xa1de4`, not in v0's map) fails: `NotSupportedException: Ampere instruction 481 at 0x0 (000000000000000000000000020c0481) is not implemented`.
- Address region check: in its first 15 s in nnMain the game's regions reach alias +2.34 GB, within the profile's 4 GB.
- On iOS without a pipeline archive, first-use pipeline compiles dominate the first races: 1,012 new pipelines in about 3 minutes of play (58.6 s compiling, about 200 ms each), since the profile's pair lists come from v0.

A race to load on the iPhone.

### Game, title ID and version

Mario Kart World, 0400C3F00006E000, 1.8.0 (v917504), no DLC

02c91cd4, plus local changes that are not on main: translator fixes found on Yoshi and the Mysterious Book (a pending Ampere write under complementary guards, a predicated LDG into its own address register, two-word handles in uniform buffers, 64-bit image atomics through a patched SPIRV-Cross, images whose handle is in a uniform buffer), SDK 19's fill order for registered video buffers, and a Switch 2 Pro Controller driver. Mac app (`--platform mac-app`); iPhone, built and run with Xcode (`--prepare-xcode --romfs separate`)

MacBook Pro (Mac17,9) M5 Pro, 24 GB, macOS 27.0.1; iPhone 18 Pro Max (iPhone19,7), iOS 27.0.1

### What is missing

`dm/tools/nacp.py` `LANGUAGES` lists the 16 languages of the NACP's `SupportedLanguageFlag`. Donkey Kong Bananza (`040074A01BF12000`, update v458752) ships more than that. Its `System/RegionLangMask.txt` lists 17 region-language packs and `Mals/` holds one archive for each:

`JPja USen CNzh KRko TWzh EUen EUde EUes EUfr EUit EUnl EUru USes USfr USpt THth EUpl`

Fifteen of them map to codes in `LANGUAGES` (everything except the European Portuguese `EUpt`, which this game does not ship). `THth` (Thai) and `EUpl` (Polish) have no entry, so:

- a player cannot pick Thai or Polish in the Game language row, and `DM_LANG=th` or `pl` is not a code the NSP script's language check or `hle_sdk16.c`'s `k_lang_code` table knows,
- I do not know what `nn::oe::GetDesiredLanguage` returns for them on a Switch 2 SDK, so I did not guess a code.

I have not run the game with either language. This is read from the RomFS file names and `RegionLangMask.txt` only.

### What you propose

If you know the language codes Switch 2 SDKs use for Thai and Polish, add them to `LANGUAGES` (and the host's table) so a game that ships them can offer them. If a Switch 2 game's languages cannot be read from a NACP at all, seedds/nxnative#1208 reads the list from `System/RegionLangMask.txt` or `Mals/` instead, and Thai and Polish would be the first tags it cannot map.

### Platforms

Mac, iPhone, iPad

body:
### What happened

**Main regression reported by the player: On the same iPhone and game version, the early nxnative build does NOT crash from excessive memory, whereas ALL newer builds I have tested do. Rolling back to the first-support revision 16f4889 (archive 83 / app 1.1.19, with the full MOD) is the only tested configuration that remains playable without this memory-related crash. Please prioritize this working-early / failing-newer comparison when investigating.**

The latest newer baseline tested here is f2a50f35; “all newer builds” refers to the player’s tested builds, not every upstream commit or untested current HEAD.

OCTOPATH TRAVELER II exits to the iOS home screen at **the end of Hikari’s chapter-one first Boss battle, or the victory/results screen**. This is the chapter Boss, not the opening/tutorial fight. Recent owner-tested builds fail here; rebuilding the first Octopath II support revision makes the game playable without this reported crash. The strongest captured failure is a **6 GiB hard per-process memory-limit kill**, not a guest exception. The regression is not bisected and a leak has not been proved.

### Reproduction and comparison

Load progress before Hikari’s chapter-one first Boss, complete the battle, then observe the return to the home screen at battle end/results before the next save.

| Personal app build | nxnative baseline | Resources | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1.1.19 / archive 83** | **[16f4889192dd9bc6363a77b5d8b9654fe65441a2](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/16f4889192dd9bc6363a77b5d8b9654fe65441a2)**, first Octopath II support | Full Huanxiang / 幻想 5.1 MOD | Owner reports this is the only tested edition that is playable without this crash. |
| **1.1.17 / archive 81** | **[f2a50f35226ea4c7495f8698ef6ec5d7a0f439ef](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/commit/f2a50f35226ea4c7495f8698ef6ec5d7a0f439ef)** | Same full MOD | Boss-end failure; correlated app/system diagnosis below. Complete fresh rebuild and clean installation did not prevent it. |
| **1.1.18 / archive 82** | Same f2a50f35 runtime | Original resources, no MOD | Owner also reports the problem without the MOD. Host executable sections, embedded game modules, shaders and defaults were verified unchanged from 1.1.17. No independently correlated kernel kill from this control is retained. |

App numbers above are personal packaging versions. The game is always **1.1.1 (v131072), title ID `0100A3501946E000`**, SDK 12.3.2, original Japanese/English voices and original Travel Provisions DLC.

The no-MOD edition preserved progress/settings, so a previously MOD-created save remains a variable. Earlier feedback about original resources was inconsistent; the latest report is that no-MOD can also fail. Successful rollback still uses the full MOD. These observations suggest investigating a runtime regression, but do not conclusively exclude MOD/save effects. Current repository HEAD has not been tested here.

### Device, settings and captured failure

Same **iPhone 17**, last recorded **iOS 26.3**; exact OS build not retained. Correlated 1.1.17 failure: **Handheld, 30 fps, MetalFX; Metal 4 OFF, pipeline prebuild OFF, encode thread OFF, frame hold OFF**. Increased-memory authorization was verified in the actual XML/DER signature, provisioning profile and live entitlement record.

The preserved diagnosis records these exact phrases/numbers from the original read-only capture (the block is an excerpt summary, not a raw system-log file):

```text
2026-11-04 20:28:11.843 +0800, DmIOS PID 13862
kernel: ActiveHard 6144 MB (fatal)
kernel termination size: 6305317KB
launchd termination: (1, 7, 9)
SpringBoard: jetsam(1) code:per-process-limit(7)

Last periodic footprint: frame 63000, 4578 MiB
Last detailed report: frame 61500, resident 4576 MiB,
  GPU allocated 2585 MiB, headroom 1567 MiB,
  freed-but-still-live pools 0 bytes
Final app log reached frame 63145.
```

Periodic app samples missed approximately **1.54 GiB of late growth** before the kernel kill. GPU allocation overlaps process footprint and must not be added to it. No allocation owner, CPU/GPU split or continuous leak is established.

Earlier diagnoses also record highwater kills at this transition: app 1.1.11 on Nov 3 at 13:58 (+0800), **6,293,621 KB**; app 1.1.12 at 19:36:37, PID 3337, **6,296,229 KB**. App 1.1.10 was `(1, 2, 9)` highwater, without a measured final footprint; it must not be relabelled a measured hard-limit event.

### Rewrite verification and rollback differences

The f2a50f35 build freshly extracted/rewrote **main, subsdk0 and sdk**, regenerated Mac/iOS shaders and derived tables, and rebuilt the host with new DerivedData. Old rewritten modules/`dm/` payload were not reused. Package checks confirmed `OBS_UE_REGION` at `main+0xbec3b0`, the allocator patch at `main+0xbecc08`, SDK node-area reduction and 2 MB alignment changes. Runtime confirmed:

- No active `-SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=2048` argument.
- `[mem] Unreal's engine region` and FMallocBinned3 using a host malloc zone.
- Alias-map milestones up to **+0.75 GB** in the failure. This is virtual mapping, scene-dependent, not a physical-process memory cap.

Rollback 16f4889 intentionally restores the historical 2048 argument, constructor NOP at `main+0xbecc08`, allocator gate at `main+0xbecc0c`, and 62 MB SDK node-area cut; it predates `OBS_UE_REGION` and later 2 MB alignment changes. Core memory/rewriter/graphics sources match 16f4889. Personal overlays concern Chinese UI, controls, metadata/entitlement and build compatibility.

**This is not a single-variable A/B:** old runtime embeds a RomFS directory; newer build embeds `romfs.img`. Both used Xcode 27.2, but old/new Metal versions are **32023.921 / 32023.922**, shader chains **`a488ed0aecd3` / `7a9c6fdfce40`**. Historical translator fingerprints match; old SPIRV-Cross lock executable was unavailable, so the supported `own_compilers.py` flow used `7900af1f054da889` versus recorded `d9dc197f061b42a5`. These differences prevent attributing the regression to one patch.

### Logs and investigation request

The evidence ZIP attached below contains **two full sanitized no-MOD 1.1.18 runtime logs**, preserved dated diagnoses, module Build IDs/hashes, a current detailed report and provenance/limitations. These two logs are **later sessions, not PID 13862**; they select standard rendering (`DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off`), and one records `DM_NVN_PREDICT=0`. They must not be substituted for the correlated crash-session settings.

Original older raw unified-log archives and the full 1.1.17 crash-session app log were removed in owner-requested old-version cleanup before this issue request. Only their previously written excerpts/conclusions remain, clearly labelled. No contemporaneous allocation backtrace/detailed JetsamEvent or new successful rollback log is attached. Successful rollback gameplay is owner-reported; no agent gameplay was performed.

Could you help narrow the change between **16f4889 and f2a50f35**, and advise on tracing large allocation/page-touch events around victory/results? Logging **before** large malloc/realloc and Metal allocations, with thread/guest return address and physical footprint, might capture the final rise missed by periodic statistics. No speculative code fix is claimed. Related symptom, different trigger/device: #925 (boarding the ship); shared cause is unproven.

- [x] No game files, extracted binaries/shaders, MOD payloads, saves, keys or signing credentials are attached. Private paths/installation identifiers are redacted.

[octopath2-hikari-boss-memory-evidence-20261105.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34383607/octopath2-hikari-boss-memory-evidence-20261105.zip)

### Additional owner observation (2026-11-05)

With the **in-game settings “Performance Monitor” enabled**, the owner observes memory **continuously increasing while the character stands still**. This refers to the app setting, not the system Metal HUD. **The same stationary scene with the monitor disabled has not yet been compared**, so the monitor itself causing a leak is not established. Please consider the monitoring/overlay allocation path alongside the Boss-transition peak; whether they share a cause is unknown. No measurement rate or allocation backtrace for this stationary case is available yet.


Evidence ZIP SHA-256: `d2ef3f9e31d3d25517c9c7b8339780a277f08d2d999abedc36e9d416e081ca69` (50,098 bytes; 10 files, ZIP CRC and redaction checks passed).

### Game, title ID and version

Absolum,  0100A83022A22000, 1.2.1 (v589824)

### Engine and graphics API, if known

_No response_

### Survey and what happened

### What Happened
Building and running Absolum with update 1.2.1 (v589824) on an unmodified checkout results in a video playback crash on startup (`logos_switch.mp4`) when using a derived profile:

```text
[dm] UNIMPL _ZN5movie12SetAllocatorEPFPvmmS0_EPFvS0_S0_EPFS0_S0_mS0_ES0_
[dm] [game] nx_video_player_load : trying to open movie rom:/data/videos/logos_switch.mp4
[dm] UNIMPL _ZN5movie9ExtractorC1ENS_13ContainerTypeE (x0=0x314c2edf0 x1=0x1 x2=0x10)
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x10 pc=main+0x3b7078 lr=main+0x3b7060 sp=0x16fbfe7c0
```

[0100A83022A22000.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34378560/0100A83022A22000.log)

#### Findings & Analysis
1. **Module Reorganization**:
   - In update 1.1.2 (v458752), `subsdk2` was `NintendoSDK_movie` (`ca1378cdd05a...`), while `subsdk0` and `subsdk1` were unused NVIDIA GPU drivers.
   - In update 1.2.1 (v589824), the developers updated to SDK 20.5.29 (`a5813da32d12...`) and reorganized the ExeFS modules.
   - `subsdk0` is now `NintendoSDK_movie` (`SDK_movie-20_5_29-Release`, build ID `1e59dde5383b9cfb60f3e67e92add78b`), and `subsdk2` is no longer present.

2. **Derived Profile Behavior**:
   Because `dm/games/0100A83022A22000/game.tsv` lists `modules main subsdk2 sdk`, `derive_profile` drops `subsdk2` (since it does not exist in 1.2.1) and omits `subsdk0` (since it was not in the profile's module list). This leaves only `main` and `sdk`, causing the `movie::Extractor` crash.

3. **Solution**:
   Adding `subsdk0` to `modules` in `game.tsv` and registering the build row:
   ```tsv
   build	v589824	1.2.1	main=ddfad5275db77013c5788385984b744d	subsdk0=1e59dde5383b9cfb60f3e67e92add78b	sdk=a5813da32d12ef17099152ca79c9b24d
   modules	main subsdk0 subsdk2 sdk
   ```
   This allows `subsdk0` to be extracted, rewritten, and loaded by `dmhost`, after which the game plays the video and boots smoothly into gameplay at 60 fps. This is shown in the previous log which was made after these changes and testing them out with initial gameplay in the tutorial. I'm not quite sure if it affects anything else so instead of using this hacked together solution, I'm just putting up an issue instead.

Log of the successfully running game:
[0100A83022A22000.prev.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34378555/0100A83022A22000.prev.log)

Readme generated based on instructions:
[report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34378742/report.md)

I made a clean build with no other local changes; the fixed runner had some other local changes and the fixes themselves.

### Local changes for the successfully running version of the game:
```diff
diff --git a/dm/games/0100A83022A22000/game.tsv b/dm/games/0100A83022A22000/game.tsv
index ffb36d62..7a9087f2 100644
--- a/dm/games/0100A83022A22000/game.tsv
+++ b/dm/games/0100A83022A22000/game.tsv
@@ -20,9 +20,8 @@ package	v458752
 shader_versions	v458752

-# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk2 = NintendoSDK_movie, for FNA3D's video player). Not loaded: subsdk0 (NVIDIA's Vulkan driver) and subsdk1 (NVIDIA's OpenGL driver):
```

body:
# Build time: nx_extract is rebuilt more than once per run; a dump build repacks an unchanged RomFS image

While measuring where rebuild time goes on a dump-based rebuild, two steps stand out as avoidable work, plus a smaller reporting idea.

## 1. nx_extract is built once per stage that needs it, not once per run

`build_nx_extract()` does a full `dotnet build` into a temporary folder and copies the result over, with no fingerprint check of its sources (`dm/tools/nx_extract`). On the first build of a game without a profile, one invocation can build it three or four times:

- `package_title_reader` builds it into a `tempfile` directory when a package has neither a ticket nor a `[title ID]` in its name,
- `same_build()` builds it into `<id>_survey`,
- `survey()` builds it again into the same survey folder (the previous copy is removed first),
- the main flow later builds it once more into `<id>_build`.

Each of those is a full toolchain build plus a copy for identical sources. Fingerprinting the tool's sources the way the other stages do, or building it once per run and passing the path along, would collapse these into one.

## 2. A dump made from a previous build's extract repacks an identical RomFS image

The dump layout takes `base/romfs` and `updates/<v>/romfs` as trees, and `pack_dump.pack_version` packs them into `RomFS.img` (with `--reuse`, so a repeat run over the same tree is already cheap). But when the dump folder was made by exploding a previous build's `RomFS.img`, the first run does image -> tree -> image for byte-identical content: both the explode step and the pack step are full passes over the game files.

Letting the dump layout accept an already-packed image (`base/romfs.img`, `updates/<v>/romfs.img`) beside or instead of the tree would skip that round trip. The existing reuse machinery could verify the image against the tree when both are present, or take the image alone.

## 3. Smaller: an end-of-build summary of what was rebuilt and why

Each stage already prints whether it was reused, and `stale_shaders()` computes why cached shader libraries cannot be reused (chain change, profile inputs, toolchain). Those reasons are scattered across a long log. A short summary at the end of the build (stages rebuilt vs reused, with the dominant cause) would make it obvious when a full rebuild was actually necessary and when something incidental forced it.
title: Build time: nx_extract is rebuilt more than once per run; a dump build repacks an unchanged RomFS image

body:
### Game, title ID and version

DOOM 3, 010029D00E740000, update 1.0.5 (v1)

### Engine and graphics API, if known

id Tech 4 (the BFG Edition renderer), OpenGL through EGL. Its GLSL is assembled at run time from the renderprogs in its .resources archives. SDK 14.

### Device and OS you would play on

MacBook Pro 14-inch, M2 Pro (Mac14,9), macOS 27.3 · iPhone 13 Pro (iPhone14,2, A15), iOS 27.3 (24C5037i)

### Survey and what happened

DOOM 3 has no profile on `main`. I got it playable on the Mac and, with an ETC2 transcode of its DXT textures, on an iPhone 13 Pro, which is below the supported devices. This report says what was needed and how, in case it helps the maintainer or anyone porting another OpenGL game. The whole change is attached as one patch against `b1dee89c` ([doom3-and-a15-changes-on-b1dee89c.patch](https://gist.github.com/zKipp3r/6c45358ebb3cb80297647d9d724d51bc), 19 files, about +1,260 / −150, plus two new files). It is not a pull request because it mixes several concerns, `main` has moved on since (about 140 commits), and the A15 part needs your decision first ([CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#large-changes-and-other-platforms)). I can split it into PRs on current `main` if any of it is wanted.

### Status

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Mac (M2 Pro) | Plays: the first level and further, lighting, shadows, flashlight and post-processing correct. Played by hand for several sessions |
| iPhone 13 Pro (A15) | Plays. Handheld mode is noticeably smoother than docked (no frame times measured) |
| iPhone gyro aim (new setting) | Works well in play |
| Mac mouse aim without a button held | Works well (confirmed in play) |
| iPhone volume-up as fire | Fires, but at a lower rate than tapping the on-screen button; known bug: once the volume is lowered it cannot be raised again while the app runs (see Input) |
| iPhone cloud-save folder picker fix | Does not work yet: the picker still comes up empty |

### Profile (provisional, from the NSP script)

```
title_id	010029D00E740000
build	v1	1.0.5	main=367c9c29427a5262d0c687d6d884d5c4	sdk=2aef2cffb104ee7c9e212fd2f4c731e9
modules	main sdk
romfs_marker	base/_sound_console.resources
zip_store	.bik:.resources:.metallib
mem_reserve	0x100000000
mem_alias	0x10000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0xCD500000
sys_resource	0x0
shader_groups	/base/=base
```

Built with `--env-file` holding `DM_GL_STUBS=1` (a GL function the layer lacks gets a stub that reports its first call instead of a jump to 0).

### What was needed, in the order it was found

**1. It stopped before the title: the extension list and ARB names** (`dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m`)
- The renderer checks a fixed list of extensions (including `GL_ARB_fragment_program`) and stops with "<name> not available" otherwise: the layer now lists them.
- It then asks `eglGetProcAddress` for the ARB names. Aliases were added for the buffer functions (`glBindBufferARB` … `glMapBufferARB`, `glGetBufferParameterivARB`), compressed textures, vertex attributes and `glActiveTextureARB` / `glClientActiveTextureARB`.
- ARB assembly programs (`glGenProgramsARB`, `glProgramStringARB`, …) only record the call. It draws with GLSL.

**2. Its shaders exist only at run time** (`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`, `dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py`)
- `main` holds two `#version` strings that are templates, so the NSP script did not capture. `DM_FORCE_GL_CAPTURE=1` makes it capture in the Mac host anyway.
- 62 GLSL stages were captured (some first seen in levels, with `DM_GL_CAPTURE` during play).
- `gl_shaders.py` fixups:
  - `sampler` used as a variable name is renamed (a reserved word for glslang -V).
  - Redeclarations of `gl_FragCoord` / `gl_FragDepth` are dropped.
  - `gl_FrontColor` / `gl_Color` become one varying, `dm_Color`, and `gl_FragColor` becomes output 0.
  - `invariant gl_Position` is added to vertex shaders: DOOM 3 lights a surface only where its depth equals the depth pre-pass, and without invariance the depth-equal test failed in places.

**3. Shadows** (`hle_gl.m`)
- Shadow volumes use two-sided stencil: `glStencilFuncSeparate` / `glStencilOpSeparate` now map to Metal's front and back stencil descriptors.
- A program with only a vertex shader (the shadow volumes) links to a pipeline with no fragment function, which still writes depth and stencil.

**4. Black world: `glCopyTexImage2D` / `glCopyTexSubImage2D` were stubs** (`hle_gl.m`)
- Each frame the BFG renderer copies the lit frame into `_currentRender`, and a post-processing draw (program 75 here) puts it back on screen. With the copy missing, that draw covered everything with black.
- Found with a pass-by-pass framebuffer dump (`DM_GL_SNAP`, see 8).
- Now a blit from the read framebuffer's colour attachment, in command order:
  - The texture takes the source's pixel format, so the copy is a plain blit.
  - The rectangle is clipped to both images.
  - A depth copy or a format mismatch is reported.

**5. Rainbow lighting: `GL_UNPACK_SWAP_BYTES` was ignored** (`hle_gl.m`)
- The light projection and falloff images are RGB565 stored big-endian, and the game sets `glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_SWAP_BYTES, 1)` (0x0CF0) before uploading them. They came out as red/green bands.
- Found by dumping the sampled textures at the snapshot frame and decoding them.
- Each 2- or 4-byte element is now byte-swapped before the pixel conversion, reading the last row without its alignment padding.

**6. Smaller things DOOM 3 needed** (`hle_gl.m`)
- `glCompressedTexSubImage2D` (it streams DXT images).
- `glBindBufferRange` with a range shorter than the uniform block: it binds only the joints of a skinned model out of its 6,528-byte `matrices_ubo`. The bytes there are used, zeros after.
- `GL_MAX_*` queries for uniform blocks and draw buffers.
- `glDetachShader`.

**7. Also in the patch, from N++ (01000D5005974000), which plays on the Mac and an iPad Air M1** (`hle_gl.m`, `gl_shaders.py`)
- Named uniform blocks (`glGetUniformBlockIndex`, `glUniformBlockBinding`, `glBindBufferBase`; the `n:` rows of the shader tables).
- Interface-block varyings matched by block name instead of instance name.
- Up to 8 colour attachments with `glDrawBuffers` / `glReadBuffer`, per-buffer clears (`glClearBufferfv`), `glEnablei` / `glColorMaski`.
- Sampler objects.
- A one-time warning for `glLineWidth`.
- Known gap: a scissored clear of a draw buffer other than 0.

**8. Bring-up aids, probably not for `main` as they are** (`hle_gl.m`)
- `DM_GL_SNAP=<seconds>:<dir>`: one frame saved pass by pass as PPM files, named with draw count, program, blend and stencil state.
- `DM_GL_SNAP=0:<dir>`: shot k is taken when a file `go<k>` appears.
- At the snapshot frame, the textures of the lighting draw are dumped as raw level 0.
- A per-program sampler log (unit, texture, size, format).
- `DM_GL_DBG_DEPTHEQ` / `DM_GL_DBG_NOSTENCIL` switches.

### iPhone 13 Pro (A15): an ETC2 path for GL games on GPUs without BC

- The A15 has no BC texture formats. `front_ios_device_check` (`dm/ios/Sources/main.m`) and `mtl_init` (`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`) now let an OpenGL or Vulkan game start on such a GPU. NVN games are still refused, as before.
- New file `dm/gfx/gl/etc_transcode.h`:
  - Converts BC1 / BC2 / BC3 blocks in place (same size) to ETC2 RGB8 / EAC RGBA8 when `glCompressedTexImage2D` / `SubImage2D` gives them. `hle_gl.m` then makes the texture in that format.
  - The encoder is chosen for load time over quality: ETC1-compatible individual and differential modes only, least-squares modifier tables, EAC alpha from the block's range.
  - Block rows are converted in parallel with `dispatch_apply`.
- BC1's punch-through alpha is lost (ETC2 RGB8 is opaque) and counted in `etc_lost_alpha`. BC4–7 are not converted and are drawn black. DOOM 3 uses only DXT1 and DXT5 (YCoCg in DXT5), so all of its textures convert.
- `DM_GL_FORCE_ETC=1` forces the conversion on a Mac, to check it there.
- Not compared side by side with BC: in play it looks right.
- The IPA was signed with a free Personal Team: `DM_ENTITLEMENTS=` (no increased-memory-limit entitlement), `--romfs separate`, `romfs.img` copied in through Finder. It ran without memory kills.
- Question: would you take this (GL and Vulkan games on A15 / A16 iPhones through ETC2) as a supported path? If so I can send it as its own PR.

### Input (general, any game)

- **Mac, mouse aim "as right stick"** (`dm/host/front_mac.m`, Controls menu)
  - For games that aim only with the stick, like DOOM 3: a click captures the mouse, its speed becomes right-stick deflection past a 0.18 dead zone, and Esc releases it.
  - `mouseMoved` without a button held never reached the view, because it goes to the window's first responder. A local `NSEvent` monitor now takes it while captured. Confirmed in play.
  - A "gyro" mode feeds the mouse to player 1's motion instead, for games that aim with motion.
- **Mac, Controls › Configure Buttons**: a per-game keyboard and controller remap saved in the app's preferences (`controls.keys`, `controls.pad`). For DOOM 3: Space = B (jump), E = X (use), R = Y (reload), Q = R (next weapon). Controllers keep their own layout.
- **Mac, in-game Settings menu**: the launcher.json settings while the game runs. Console mode, display mode and rumble apply at once; the rest restart the game through a `<DM_ROOT>/restart` marker that `dm/mac/launcher.c` re-execs. The menus are in Spanish when the Mac's language is Spanish (`dm/mac/strings_es.json`).
- **iPhone, gyro aim** (`DM_GYRO_AIM`, `DM_GYRO_SENS` in `dm/games/settings.tsv`; `gyro_aim()` in `dm/ios/Sources/DmGamepad.m`)

### What happened
Building Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`) with the NSP script filled the disk: the build cache grew past **200 GB** and the build crashed because there was no space left.

### Why it matters
Pokopia has 131,426 shaders in `shader_map.tsv`, and a full build translates and compiles all of them. Anyone who runs it on a Mac with a normal internal disk can hit this, and a crash from a full disk can leave the build folder in a partial state.

### What I don't know yet
- Which folder under `<id>_build/` held the 200 GB (`shader/cache/cas/shader`, `cas/metallib`, `cas/variant`, the `b-<chain>` libraries, the work folder, or something else).
- Whether it was one full build or several builds after updates (see #1033, where old chain entries were never pruned).
- Mac or iOS output, and the build step it died in.

I'll add `du` output per subfolder as soon as I have it.

### Related
- #1036: the full Pokopia shader build is very slow, and a partial library of the 8,157 shaders the playtest used is the current workaround.
- #1033: the shader cache keeps growing with every chain change (stale `cas/shader` entries); closed, but a full Pokopia build multiplies any such growth by about 4.6 compared with Tears of the Kingdom.

### Request
Make the build's disk use much smaller and bounded for large shader sets:
1. Measure and report the size of each cache folder after a Pokopia build, so the biggest consumer is known.
2. Check free space before the shader step from the expected size, and stop with a clear message instead of crashing mid-build.
3. Drop intermediates (`.metal` sources, JSON, duplicate copies) once a shader's library is published, or do not keep them per shader.
4. Prune stale entries as proposed in #1033, and cap the cache.
5. For Pokopia, make building only the shaders a player needs (`shader_seen.tsv`) a supported path, not a manual recipe.
title: Pokémon Pokopia: build cache grew past 200 GB and the build crashed on a full disk

body:
**Symptom:** with the launcher's upscaler set to MetalFX (`DM_UPSCALER=metalfx`), Splatoon Raiders (`0400380020056000`, v65536) looks washed out docked: lifted shadows, low contrast. Handheld is fine (the game doesn't upscale there), and with the game's own upscaler docked is fine.

**Cause:** `up_mfx_encode` (`nvn_mtl.m`) runs MetalFX in HDR mode, taking the network's input and output as linear. That holds for Donkey Kong Bananza's `agl_ndsr.pck` (release library): its network encodes linear input right after reading it. Splatoon Raiders ships the debug library's variant (`c1b8edc09e3313b1`): no encode after the reads, and its last step decodes the result with the sRGB curve (0.04045, 1/12.92, ((x + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4, 240 times in the translated shader). So its input is sRGB-encoded and its output linear, and MetalFX passed the encoded colour through.

**Local fix (tested on an M2 MacBook Air, macOS 27, docked from a save):** a profile key `upscaler_color` = `linear` (default) / `srgb` (`game.py` → `DM_GAME_UPSCALER_SRGB`). With `srgb`, the scaler runs in perceptual mode into an RGBA8Unorm texture, and the copy into the game's output reads it through an RGBA8Unorm_sRGB view, which decodes it to linear. That takes the indirect path always. SR's colour then matches its own upscaler.

**Why it may be global:** any game whose agl build ships the sRGB variant of NDSR gets the same wash-out with MetalFX. Which variant a game has shows in the shader (an encode after the reads, or an sRGB decode before the writes). So the key could be replaced by a fact the shader chain derives, at the cost of a chain change and a shader rebuild.

**Not done yet:** `regress.py check --games` (only DK and SR have the upscaler setting), and a `rendering.md` entry with the symptom index.
title: DM_UPSCALER=metalfx washes out games whose agl upscaler reads sRGB-encoded colour (Splatoon Raiders): a profile key for now, detection from the shader later

body:
## Summary

The Cloud Saves directory picker in the upstream nxnative iOS launcher fails to return a selected folder. This prevents configuring Cloud Saves using either iCloud Drive or On My iPhone.

The issue occurs in multiple independently built games, including Super Mario Odyssey and Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

This was originally reported in [[LNPANDY/NX2Apple#599](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/599)](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/599). After reviewing the logs, NX2Apple collaborator @v0lumehi confirmed that my IPA uses the upstream nxnative launcher (`dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift`), rather than NX2Apple's iOS shell, and requested that I report the issue here.

## Environment

- **Device:** iPhone 18 Pro (physical device)
- **iOS:** 27.2
- **Mac:** M1 MacBook Pro
- **macOS:** 27.0 (26A428)
- **Source repository:** `seedds/nxnative`
- **Source commit:** `8c80f39a`
- **Build method:** Terminal, directly from upstream nxnative
- **Installation method:** FlareStore
- **Affected games:** Super Mario Odyssey and Pokémon Legends: Z-A
- **Odyssey title ID:** `0100000000010000`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build an iOS IPA using upstream nxnative.
2. Install and launch the game on the iPhone.
3. Open the launcher's settings and navigate to Cloud Saves.
4. Attempt to select a save directory in iCloud Drive or On My iPhone.
5. Select a directory and tap **Open**.

The issue also occurs when selecting a folder directly under On My iPhone and immediately tapping Open, without navigating through any subfolders.

## Expected behavior

The selected directory should be returned to the launcher, saved as the Cloud Saves destination, and available for subsequent save synchronization.

## Actual behavior

- The document picker sometimes dismisses automatically without any apparent user interaction.
- When the picker remains open, tapping **Open** does not successfully select the directory.
- No selected folder is saved.
- Both iCloud Drive and On My iPhone exhibit the same failure.

## Relevant iPhone Console errors

I captured the iPhone's system Console output while reproducing the problem. The log contains errors that appear to directly explain why the directory selection fails.

At **16:14:01.706**, process `DmIOS` reports:

```text
[ERROR] Could not resolve bookmark.
Error: NSError: Cocoa 257

Failed to create a url from bookmarkableString
(Error Domain=NSCocoaErrorDomain Code=257)

Tried to call delegate
-documentBrowser:didPickDocumentURLs:
with an empty array of items.
This indicates the items failed to be prepared
and materialized on disk.
```

The same sequence appears again at approximately **16:14:02.622** and **16:14:17.643**.

Other errors captured during reproduction include:

**DocumentManager:**
```text
com.apple.DocumentManager.Service
Missing entitlement.
```

**LaunchServices:**
```text
DmIOS
Sandbox: deny(1) forbidden-map-ls-database

Error Domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain Code=-54
"process may not map database"

Failed to initialize client context
```

**DocumentManager scene failure:**
```text
FBSWorkspaceErrorDomain
Code: 1 ("InvalidScene")
"scene invalidated before create completion"
```

The bookmark-resolution errors and empty selection callback are the clearest evidence of the failure. It is not yet established whether the entitlement, LaunchServices, or scene errors are causes or secondary symptoms.

## Troubleshooting already completed

1. Updated the upstream repository using `git pull --ff-only`.
2. Confirmed the current source commit was `8c80f39a`.
3. Verified that commit `dad38db` was included in the source history.
4. Rebuilt Super Mario Odyssey from scratch using the updated source and original game files.
5. Reinstalled the freshly built IPA using FlareStore.
6. Reproduced the issue with both local storage and iCloud Drive.
7. Attempted to select a folder immediately without opening subdirectories.
8. Confirmed similar behavior in Pokémon Legends: Z-A.
9. Captured both the game's `log.txt` and the iPhone system Console log.

The game's internal `log.txt` ends at `launcher: 13 settings shown` and does not record the folder-selection failure. The system Console log captures the relevant errors.

I have not tested another iPhone or iOS version, nor an IPA produced by NX2Apple.

## Diagnostic attachments

The following files are attached separately:

- `log.txt` — game launcher log
- `ios-picker-console.txt` — iPhone system Console log captured during reproduction

No encryption keys, game files, or extracted game assets are included.

## Questions

Could the failure to resolve security-scoped bookmarks, the apparent entitlement problem, or the LaunchServices permission denial be preventing `UIDocumentPickerViewController` from returning the selected folder URL?

Is there a required entitlement or signing configuration for the upstream Terminal-built IPA that might be missing when installed through FlareStore?

I can test a targeted patch or alternative build configuration if needed.

**Original investigation:** https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/issues/599


[log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34344107/log.txt)
[ios-picker-console.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34344108/ios-picker-console.txt)

### What happened

The build stops in the shader split, every time:

```
[RED] Data/Resources/unity default resources: Unity serialized file without type trees, and no bundle has a Shader type tree of the same hash to borrow
[RED] shader_split.py exit code 1
```

The game has no bundles (0 `UnityFS` headers in the RomFS) and all its serialized files are stripped. `KNOWN_TREES` in `dm/gfx/tools/unityfs.py` has Shader layouts for 5.5, 2017.4, 2018.3, 2019.4, 2020.3, 2021.2, 2022.3 and 6000.0, but none for 2021.3. The game's Shader type hash is `f0c184272a05e54447e36366ec4876a6`, the same in all its stripped files.

Fix I used (diff below): `SHADER_2021_3` = `SHADER_2021_2` plus `m_PlayerSubPrograms` / `m_ParameterBlobIndices` in `SerializedProgram` and `stageCounts` in `Shader`; `m_SerializedKeywordStateMask` stays in the pass.

```
diff --git a/dm/gfx/tests/test_unity_known_trees.py b/dm/gfx/tests/test_unity_known_trees.py
index 42f406ba..5a15233f 100644
--- a/dm/gfx/tests/test_unity_known_trees.py
+++ b/dm/gfx/tests/test_unity_known_trees.py
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ import unityfs
 # An entry dropped from KNOWN_TREES stops the split on every stripped player of that version.
 SHADER_HASHES = {'5.5': '4496e93f2179252104401c8dda0a1751', '2017.4': '266d53113fa30d2b858f2768f92eaa14', '2018.3': '8db760073e1392061e4a36995f0735af',
                  '2019.4': 'ed2a06ce7fb8203f6efb5ab5e0ce20d5', '2020.3': 'a30e3dcf6c6d25153d6f64e5e41caf4e',
-                 '2021.2': 'd8236c9bd87d85edb203acf352348124', '2022.3': 'ea424a5fc1e48db62144df956f9e1005',
+                 '2021.2': 'd8236c9bd87d85edb203acf352348124', '2021.3': 'f0c184272a05e54447e36366ec4876a6', '2022.3': 'ea424a5fc1e48db62144df956f9e1005',
                  '6000.0': '2ec7223dce3af4232b14ae1441bd7999'}
 COMPUTE_HASHES = {'2017.4': '20291e020d10074c35d8286f5191593f', '2019.4': '1a95529ac2eb1a97cd9d2a4356bd722f',
                   '2020.3': 'd0171b849bb064b2424893e7d4809be5', '2021.3': 'abd9135b8ce83d043fef4e9ec7f53366', '2022.3': 'bfdf63ab0ce84d5a2c765ee560d90fe7',
diff --git a/dm/gfx/tools/unityfs.py b/dm/gfx/tools/unityfs.py
index 85b9b794..d6a686d5 100644
--- a/dm/gfx/tools/unityfs.py
+++ b/dm/gfx/tools/unityfs.py
@@ -301,7 +301,15 @@ PPtr<Shader>: int m_FileID; SInt64 m_PathID
 Shader: string m_Name; SerializedShader m_ParsedForm; vector<data:unsigned int>~ platforms; vector<data:unsigned int>~ offsets; vector<data:unsigned int>~ compressedLengths; vector<data:unsigned int>~ decompressedLengths; vector<data:UInt8> compressedBlob; vector<data:PPtr<Shader>>~ m_Dependencies; bool! m_ShaderIsBaked'''
 
 CLASS_COMPUTE_SHADER = 72
+# Unity 2021.3 (Dynablaster, 2021.3.25f1: no bundles, every serialized file stripped): the 2021.2 layout with the player subprograms of 2022.3 in each program and the shader's stageCounts;
+# the keyword state mask stays in the pass. Checked by reading all 50 Shader objects of the player's stripped files to their exact ends
+SHADER_2021_3 = SHADER_2021_2.replace('SerializedProgram: vector<data:SerializedSubProgram> m_SubPrograms; SerializedProgramParameters m_CommonParameters',
+    'SerializedPlayerSubProgram: unsigned int m_BlobIndex; vector<data:UInt16> m_KeywordIndices; SInt64 m_ShaderRequirements; SInt8! m_GpuProgramType\n'
+    'SerializedProgram: vector<data:SerializedSubProgram> m_SubPrograms; vector<data:vector<data:SerializedPlayerSubProgram>> m_PlayerSubPrograms; vector<data:vector<data:unsigned int>> m_ParameterBlobIndices; SerializedProgramParameters m_CommonParameters'
+    ).replace('vector<data:UInt8> compressedBlob;', 'vector<data:UInt8> compressedBlob; vector<data:unsigned int> stageCounts;')
+
 KNOWN_TREES = {(CLASS_SHADER, bytes.fromhex('4496e93f2179252104401c8dda0a1751')): ('Shader', SHADER_5_5),
+               (CLASS_SHADER, bytes.fromhex('f0c184272a05e54447e36366ec4876a6')): ('Shader', SHADER_2021_3),
                (CLASS_SHADER, bytes.fromhex('ea424a5fc1e48db62144df956f9e1005')): ('Shader', SHADER_2022_3),
                (CLASS_SHADER, bytes.fromhex('d8236c9bd87d85edb203acf352348124')): ('Shader', SHADER_2021_2),
                (CLASS_SHADER, bytes.fromhex('2ec7223dce3af4232b14ae1441bd7999')): ('Shader', SHADER_6000_0),
```

How I found it: I read the Shader objects of `unity default resources`, `unity_builtin_extra` and `globalgamemanagers.assets` (50 objects) with each existing layout and with all 8 combinations of the three differences between 2021.2 and 2022.3, and counted objects read exactly to their end:

- **player subprograms + stageCounts: 50/50**

body:
DK's launcher has a Render scale setting (`DM_RENDER_SCALE`), but on v458752 nothing reads it. This is a local rewriter patch that makes it work. It's in the profile's `patches.py` as a `FRAME_STEP` entry for main build `e25c90c1c136638885659fd55bf8a03b` (it sets `ctx.render_scale = 1`), and no other build is affected.

**What it does:** `main+0x78fdc` sizes the 3D views. It loads a float scale pair from the settings at `+0x1b0` / `+0x1b4` (at `main+0x79024`): 0.8 docked of a 2880x1620 base, 1.0 handheld of 1920x1080. It multiplies that pair by each view's integer base size (`main+0x790a4` .. `main+0x790d0`, stored at view `+0x770` / `+0x774`). The patch replaces the two loads at `main+0x79024` with a branch to a stub. The stub does the same loads, then multiplies both by the host's render scale (state `+0x10`), unless that's 0 or less, and branches back to `main+0x7902c`.

Because it scales the game's own size pair, the game's dynamic resolution keeps working under it, and 1.0 gives the original sizes. `x10` is rewritten at `main+0x79034` before it's read. `s17` is caller-saved and not set before the site in that function, so neither is live.

**Status:** used on the Mac (M2 Air, handheld and docked) at the default 1.0, with the launcher's slider. Lower values aren't measured yet. Its BINDING row is `build`; the goal is `game`, which is blocked because frame-step stubs have no function-matched form yet.

**Still needed for a PR:** DK's note (what the profile needs and why) and `docs_patches.py`.

### Summary

Adds full support for **Super Mario 3D All-Stars** across its 64-bit programs (base `v0` / `1.0.0` and update `v393216` / `1.1.4`):
- **Program 0 (`010049900F546000`)**: the collection's launcher and soundtrack player (sead / agl / gsys on NVN, SDK 10.8.1 / 9.5.1).
- **Program 1 (`010049900F546001`)**: **Super Mario 64** (N64 emulator on Vulkan with an `nn::jit` plugin NRO).
- **Program 2 (`010049900F546002`)**: **Super Mario Sunshine** (NERD's Hagi GameCube layer on Vulkan with an LZ4-packed `.nrolz` NRO).

---

### Root Causes & Fixes

1. **Crash at boot in `nn::font::ScalableFont::SetAlternateChar(0xe06b)` (`main+0x62d20` in `v0`, `main+0x63780` in `v393216`, `SIGSEGV` at `0x38`)**:
   - The launcher's complex font (`fcpx/NX_std.bfcpx` in `Font/Font.Nin_NX_NVN.bfarc.zs`) sets `U+E06B` as its alternate character at boot, and `ScalableFont::SetAlternateChar` dereferences the glyph pointer returned for that code point without a null check.
   - `dm/tools/make_ext_font.py` now maps every unassigned private-use code point in `U+E000–U+E1FF` to a fallback ring glyph (`icon`).

2. **Black screen and flat lavender movie cards in the launcher (`010049900F546000`)**:
   - The menu wraps its clears in NVN conditional rendering (`render_cond on`).
   - `agl` decodes each tile's background movie (`BgMovie64.mp4`, `BgMovieSunshine.mp4`, `BgMovieGalaxy.mp4`) into an RGBA target (`bf1135fd591c81ef`) and applies in-place gamma correction (`021631192bc452b6`) in the same render pass by sampling attachment 0 while rendering into it. Setting `feedback_snap 021631192bc452b6` snapshots the colour attachment before the gamma draw.

3. **Multi-program handoff (`oe::ExecuteProgram`, `DM_PROGRAMS`, `DM_LAUNCH_PARAM`) and Galaxy's tile (`main+0xc040` / `main+0xc270`)**:
   - `oe::ExecuteProgram(index, param, n)` (`dm/host/hle_oe.c`, `dm_host_shutdown_then` in `dm/host/hle_lifecycle.c`) looks up `index` in `DM_PROGRAMS`, writes the launch parameter to `<cwd>/launch_param.bin`, sets `DM_LAUNCH_PARAM`, and `execve`s the target program's host after a graceful shutdown. `oe::TryPopLaunchParameter` reads `DM_LAUNCH_PARAM` first and falls back to the profile's `launch_param` (`lang8 f32:1 f32:1`) when a sub-program is started directly.
   - Because program 3 (Super Mario Galaxy inside the collection) is a 32-bit `AArch32` binary, a cut in `dm/games/010049900F546000/patches.py` at `main+0xc040` (`v0`) and `main+0xc270` (`v393216`) makes the menu tile decide function return `false` when the selected content is `2` (Galaxy's game tile), while keeping Galaxy's artwork, description, and soundtrack player active.

4. **Super Mario 64 (`010049900F546001`) and Super Mario Sunshine (`010049900F546002`)**:
   - `dm/host/hle_jit.c` implements `nn::jit` on a host thread with dual-mapped `vm_remap` code memories (`R-X` / `R--` and `RW`).
   - `dm/tools/nro_collect.py` unpacks `.nrolz` LZ4-framed NROs, `dm/host/hle_offline.c` stubs `nn::web::OfflineWebSession`, and `dm/gfx/vk/hle_vk.m` handles the Vulkan paths needed by both emulators.

---

### Verification

- Verified on macOS (Apple Silicon) with `v393216` (1.1.4):
  - Program 0 (`010049900F546000`) boots cleanly, plays the opening movie, renders all menu tiles and background movies at 60 fps (16.66 ms p50), plays soundtracks, and ignores `A` on Galaxy's game tile.
  - Selecting Super Mario 64 or Super Mario Sunshine with `DM_PROGRAMS` cleanly hands over execution via `oe::ExecuteProgram` and `oe::TryPopLaunchParameter`.
  - `test_patches.py`, `test_lint_c.py`, `test_lint_python.py`, `test_env_switches.py`, and `test_docs.py` all pass.
