body: ### Game, title ID and version MIO: Memories in Orbit, `01000A001E978000`, 1.2.0 (update v196608) ### Engine and graphics API Survey: NVN (main, sdk); Unreal markers (main); FMOD. Modules `main` and `sdk`. The NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource, and `main` asks for a 3.14 GB heap. ### What happened With a provisional profile, three things came up on the Mac. Two of them have workarounds; the third is open. **1. Abort at boot: `mem_used` is not set for a game with virtual address memory that sets a heap** ~~~ [dm] [mem] SetHeapSize 0xc9400000 + modules 0x4400000 > app pool 0xcd500000 (used memory reported 0x4000000 + bss 0) [dm] game called nn::diag abort: Result 0, call site main+0xf56d10 [dm] FATAL game aborted ~~~ The heap check set `mem_alias 0x50000000` for the 3.14 GB request, but the rewritten modules are 68 MB, more than the default 64 MB of used memory. `refine_after_rewrite` in the NSP script returns early when the NPDM declares a system resource, so it never sets `mem_used`. Adding `mem_used 0x4800000` to the provisional `game.tsv` by hand made the game boot and play. **2. `MDI_MAX` (1,024) cuts off the GPU-driven scene** ~~~ [RED] indirect-count multi-draw of up to 8192 draws: only the first 1024 are made [RED] indirect-count multi-draw of up to 4594 draws: only the first 1024 are made ~~~ Most of the level geometry was missing. As an experiment I raised `MDI_MAX` to 8192 (`hle_nvn.c`) and `MDX_SLOTS` to 65536 (`nvn_mtl.m`, so one scan can take both calls). After that the red lines are gone, `indirect-count multi-draw masking: first time, 12786 draws`, and on the Mac frame time is p50 33.35 ms (the game's 30 fps), submit+present p50 6.20 ms, GPU p50 9.28 ms. I have not measured what this costs on an iPhone, or on other games. **3. Open: the scene is shaded flat (fog colour) though its depth is right** The pass dump of frame 2400 (`DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` + `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`) shows a visibility-buffer renderer: - Pass 117301 draws the multi-draws into depth `ser=1630` (D32F) and two R32Uint targets (`ser=1636` and `ser=1638`). The first pair of shaders in it is vs `9b8eb03e940d03e3_b` and ps `cf1df95194da749e_b`. That ps writes `(flags << 17) + (flat input & 0x1FFFF)` to colour 0 and another flat input to colour 1. - The half-resolution passes 117315–117317 (RG16Unorm `ser=1640`/`1639`, R16Unorm `ser=1641`) are built from depth alone, and their dumps show the whole scene correctly. - The full-screen resolve, pass 117332 with ps `967a32fa1a31e797_b`, reads depth `1630`, the ID target `1636`, `1654` (R32Uint) and a 22 MB storage buffer. It writes `ser=1658`, which comes out almost uniformly the fog colour. Only the forward-drawn black silhouettes and the character look right. The game calls `nvnCommandBufferSetProvokingVertexMode` (mode 0), which is unimplemented: ~~~ [RED] NVN unimplemented function called: nvnCommandBufferSetProvokingVertexMode (x0=… x1=0 x2=0x40000) ~~~ **My hypothesis, not confirmed:** the visibility pass stores a per-vertex value (likely the vertex index) through a flat varying. NVN uses the last vertex as the provoking vertex, as GL does, but Metal always uses the first. So the resolve rebuilds the wrong triangle. I could not confirm which vertex shader pairs with `cf1df95194da749e` in that pass, because the dump lists only the first shaders of each stage. Screenshots of the final frame and of the pass dump images are attached below. ### Environment - nxnative `bfc70881` + the two local changes above (provisional profile `mem_used 0x4800000`; `MDI_MAX` 8192 / `MDX_SLOTS` 65536) - Mac `applegpu_g16g`, macOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2. The Metal compiler was 32023.922 with `--allow-other-metal`, not the locked 27.1 one. - Built with `--platform mac-app --allow-other-metal --keep-extracted` ### Device and OS you would play on iPhone 16 (and the Mac) ### Screenshots **Final frame on the Mac** (the scene is drawn flat in the fog colour; only the forward-drawn black silhouettes and the character are right): **Pass dump, frame 2400, `rt_164000` (ser 1640, RG16Unorm, pass 117315):** built from depth alone; the whole scene is correct. **`rt_164100` (ser 1641, R16Unorm):** also depth-derived and correct. **`rt_165800` (ser 1658, output of the resolve pass 117332):** almost uniformly the fog colour. - [x] No game files, keys or data extracted from a game are attached
title: Bring-up: MIO: Memories in Orbit (01000A001E978000): mem_used, MDI_MAX and a flat-shaded visibility buffer

### Game, title ID and version
Lost in Random: The Eternal Die, `0100F0701F9B0000`, 1.5.30637 (update v327680), with 3 DLC

### Engine and graphics API
Unity (IL2CPP), NVN, SDK 18. Modules `main`, `subsdk0` (NintendoSDK_movie) and `sdk`.

### What happened
**It plays with the provisional profile, unchanged, on the Mac and on an iPhone 16.**
- Mac: about 5 minutes of play with no red lines; 59.8 fps (frame time p50 16.67 / p95 16.93 ms), GPU p50 4.0 ms, 0 audio underruns, saves committed, resident memory about 2.9 GB.
- iPhone 16: plays through LiveContainer with Increased Memory Limit.

**Point to watch: the alias region fills with address space, not memory.** The provisional profile is a 5 GB block (`mem_reserve 0x140000000`, `mem_alias 0x118000000`), and the heap check set `app_pool 0x40000000`. In play, the `[mem]` high-water mark climbs in 0.25 GB steps (+2.27 → +4.25 GB of 4.38 GB in one session), while what is mapped stays at 1.26–1.76 GB:
~~~
[dm] [mem] alias region mapped up to +4.25 GB (alias region 4.38 GB)
[dm] [mem] alias region mapped 1.76 GB (application pool 1.00 GB)
~~~
This looks like the pattern in "Size-class alignment doubles Unity's regions" (Sea of Stars). Longer sessions may run out of address space, and on the iPhone the block cannot grow past 5 GB.

### Environment
nxnative `bfc70881`; Mac `applegpu_g16g`, macOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2 (Metal 32023.922, `--allow-other-metal`); iPhone 16.

body:
## Scope request

I would like to contribute generic GPU-image visibility for `nvnMemoryPoolInvalidateMappedRange` / `nvnBufferInvalidateMappedRange`, building on the existing mirror rather than importing a downstream renderer.

This is a **scope proposal with runnable synthetic evidence, not a fix PR**. `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires agreement before adding a second implementation of an existing path. Current main already has the eager storage-backed render mirror from #604 (`843252110717362781ac047d7d0e127c5c69c6cc`). A separate deferred registry/readback path would overlap its publication and lifetime responsibilities. I am asking which integrated design you want before writing that production change.

## Current-main findings

Base checked: `99330eb81c873c3aafe9fc92194c9687d77fcdbb`.

- [`hle_nvn.c`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/99330eb81c873c3aafe9fc92194c9687d77fcdbb/dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c#L2063): both mapped-range invalidators are empty. This alone does **not** prove the known grass bug is still present on main.
- [`rt_mirror_add` / `rt_mirror_flush`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/99330eb81c873c3aafe9fc92194c9687d77fcdbb/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L3240) already write storage-backed render targets through `mirror_readback`; its passing control must be preserved.
- [`tex_storage_dst`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/99330eb81c873c3aafe9fc92194c9687d77fcdbb/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L10301) excludes GPU-owned storage from that mirror. This leaves a distinct mapped-invalidate visibility case.
- Existing `mirror_rb_land` publishes after GPU completion. A controlled CPU-newer stress case below demonstrates that a safe shared publication contract is still needed. It is **not** a claim that a game follows that artificial ordering.
- #923 is an open draft about retiring compatible texture views, not mapped-pool visibility. A production implementation would need to preserve its descriptor-lifetime work; the diagnostic branch does not modify those files.

## Runnable, asset-free evidence

Test-only commit: https://github.com/dansenxl/nxnative/commit/6b1dd7d75213b08f13cdf40e9ece4fa94f208225

[Fixture and exact instructions](https://github.com/dansenxl/nxnative/blob/6b1dd7d75213b08f13cdf40e9ece4fa94f208225/dm/gfx/tests/POOL_VISIBILITY_REPRO.md). Only three files change: the synthetic Objective-C fixture, its manual Makefile target and this explanatory test document. **No production renderer changes.** Modes asserting missing contracts deliberately return 1 and are excluded from the automatic run list.

All cases use a synthetic 37x29 RG8 texture, six mips, CPU_CACHED | GPU_CACHED anonymous memory. They check the real ownership classification and independently blit/read all actual GPU mips against literal values. The readback queue explicitly waits for the exact producer event; no game shaders or data are used.

| Case | Result on base, fast-wake 0 and 1 |
|---|---|
| CPU-written/storage-backed control, 16 create/render/invalidate/finalize cycles | 480 checks pass, all GPU and CPU mip bytes correct |
| GPU-owned image, invalidate after producer completion | Actual GPU mip bytes correct; 2,806 guest texel bytes differ (stale zeros); exit 1 |
| CPU-newer stress: gate feedback, wait exact GPU signal, write CPU bytes, release feedback | Actual GPU mip bytes correct; 2,806 of 7,168 newer storage bytes overwritten; exit 1 |
| Eight concurrent invalidators of the GPU-owned image, after producer completion | Actual GPU mip bytes correct; 2,806 guest texel bytes differ; exit 1 |

Case 2 intentionally separates completed GPU work from delayed host effects. It is a publication stress test, not proof that an unsynchronized guest is entitled to arbitrary cache-invalidation behavior, and not proof of a new real-game failure. The implementation needs an agreed ownership/order contract instead of relying on page stamps or byte comparison as a complete concurrency proof.

## Proposed bounded implementation

1. **One shared publication mechanism.** Reuse/refactor the existing `mirror_readback` / `mirror_rb_land` swizzle and storage publication machinery. Keep the eager path where CPU-visible/uncached or storage-backed semantics require it; add invalidate-triggered visibility for GPU-owned images only with an explicit scope/ownership contract. Do not add a second renderer or per-game switch.
2. **Track real producers, not descriptors alone.** Record actual image identity, pool generation, layout and written subresources at render, compute/image, clear and copy writers. Retain the actual image rather than resolving through a CPU-upload shortcut. Avoid a per-pass/per-mip GPU snapshot backlog. Bound memory and make unsupported format/layout/capacity failures explicit.
3. **Exact synchronization in both directions.** Serialize capture/publication with the existing submission ownership rules. Wait only recorded, committed producers; use an explicit shared-event dependency on the readback queue, and keep later writers from racing that readback. Never wait on a future fence that may depend on the invalidating CPU thread. Associate completion/error with the relevant producer, with finite error/timeout handling and no publication of failed or incomplete data.
4. **Real layout and requested ranges.** Use current NVN layout/swizzle helpers for supported mips/layers/formats. Preserve padding and bytes outside the agreed invalidated/cache-line extent. Establish explicit behavior for partial ranges, aliasing, linear/shared storage, sparse, compressed, multisample and depth images; do not silently treat them as simple RG8.
5. **CPU ownership and retirement.** Protect CPU-newer own bytes without treating adjacent writes in a shared host page as texture changes. Revalidate pool generation and current image ownership before publishing. Descriptor retirement must not erase a still-live pool's pending GPU result; pool destruction/remapping must prevent late writes to a reused address. Retained Metal objects alone do not prove that guest memory is still live. Handle overlapping image owners deterministically.
6. **Independent tests before a PR.** Extend these fixtures across formats, arrays/mips/partial ranges, multiple producers/queues, overlapping aliases, CPU-newer writes, capacity/timeout/GPU-error paths and destroy/recreate at the same address. Preserve #604's storage-backed control and descriptor-retirement regressions; run sanitizer, Metal validation, builds and the selected game regression routes. No shader-chain changes are proposed.

Please confirm whether you prefer to extend the existing eager mirror's ownership/publication layer, or a deferred record for the GPU-owned subset with a shared publisher, and what initial format/target coverage you would accept. I will keep this as one coherence concern and prepare the production PR against current main after that scope is agreed.

## Validation actually performed this round

Apple M5, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2; Metal API validation enabled:

- Current-main Mac host build: PASS (existing compiler warnings remain).
- Related suites: `t_readback` fast-wake 0/1, `t_cpu_tex --metal`, `t_perf_order`, `t_tex_fit_root`, `t_direct_upload`, `t_dirty_retire_race`, `t_tex_layout`, `t_sparse_layout`: all PASS.
- CPU texture ASan/UBSan suite: 5,344/5,344 PASS. Documentation tests: 11/11 PASS.
- Synthetic fixture ASan/UBSan: no sanitizer diagnostics; the visibility assertions above still fail as expected. Existing HLE metadata exceptions plus a narrow `global:e_nvn*` exception preserve the fixed-stride NVN linker table; no production function is excluded. LeakSanitizer is disabled, so no leak-free claim.
- TSan, fast-wake 0: no race report; expected visibility outcomes unchanged. Default fast-wake 1: **not PASS**, an existing lazy-initialization race in `seg_ts` (`nvn_mtl.m:1322`) is observed between feedback and early completion. A fixture-only `DM_REPRO_PRIME_TS=1` control initializes this setting before GPU work; all four cases then reproduce without TSan reports. This is not a production fix or race suppression.
- **Not run:** full game regression routes, complete GPU-suite sweep, a new upstream iPad gameplay run, IPA build/signing or device installation. This is scope/reproduction evidence, not merge acceptance or a performance claim. No game shader chain was regenerated.

## Separate downstream evidence and public boundary

An earlier downstream iPad Pro M4 / TotK 1.4.3 Build 24 fixed the observed grass disappearance with on-demand GPU-image-to-pool visibility. Grass remained for the measured 90-second fixed-camera window and a short movement/save-load/controller/amiibo regression. Its actual host is different from this main; this does **not** prove current-main gameplay validation, universal correctness or an FPS improvement. Its narrow texture filter, diagnostic limits and private source tree are not proposed as an upstream patch.

The public branch is original synthetic test code under the repository's MIT terms, using the existing MIT test conventions. No GPL implementation was copied and no third-party dependency was added. No RomFS, NSO/SDK, translated game shaders, saves, signing assets, device identifiers, private logs, screenshots, reward images or other private assets are attached or pushed.
title: Scope proposal: GPU-owned texture visibility on mapped-pool invalidation

body: # Scope proposal: Diablo III support and shared NVN lifetime/depth-feedback fixes I would like to contribute Diablo III: Eternal Collection (`01001B300B9BE000`), update **2.7.7.92380**, based on `main` at `f108343ac5c0`. Following CONTRIBUTING.md's scope-first rule, I am asking for agreement before opening a PR. A branch is already prepared: **one commit, 30 files, 2,654 additions / 21 deletions**. Most additions are generated profile metadata (1,364 shader records and 585 stage pairs). I recognize that the scope discussion should precede a large implementation; the branch is available for inspection and is not a PR. Proposed scope: - A game profile using existing memory, texture upload and external DLC paths, without game-specific guest cuts. - A bounded Blizzard CPK v6/v7 reader that discovers `.shd` assets on demand, with synthetic framing, corruption and scanner-dispatch tests. - Resolve graphics stage combinations at draw consumption: D3 retires menu programs before separately binding replacement vertex and fragment programs, so eager composition can read a freed fragment program. - Snapshot attached depth before soft particles sample it, with read-only reuse and write/clear/barrier invalidation. Preserve the color feedback cache. This removes dark rectangles around opening lanterns. - English game/reference documentation, generated indexes and before/after screenshots. D3 normal-hero gameplay, save/readback and regression tests pass on Mac, along with Python/host tests, targeted Metal checks and LLVM 23.1.4 lint. An earlier local IPA also runs successfully on my iPad mini. Testing used Xcode 26.6; validation of this branch with Xcode 27.2 and on-device remains open. ## What happens
FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (`0100B8A026F14000`, AS, update 1.0.1) Mac app (`--platform mac-app`, built 10-31) crashes after ~22 min of gameplay (1342 s, frame 79853):

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x2c33398156a0e72a pc=nvn_sparse_protect+0x40 lr=nvn_sparse_protect+0x28
x8=0x2c33398156a0e722 (garbage pointer)
launcher: the host exited with 139
```

No `FATAL image atomics` (unlike #270). Audio healthy (0 underruns, 240-frame buffers). Long frames with heavy texture re-uploads just before crash (252 first + 1514 re-uploads, 11 MB; then 121 + 867, 79 MB).

## Why I think it happens
`nvn_mtl.m:6947` already documents a sibling: Mario Party Superstars crashed once in `nvn_sparse_protect` (pkg_upload <- tex_by_id <- pool_gpu) on a garbage page table pointer. The `tex_storage_live()` guard covers freed pools (magic check) but this looks like a live sparse pool whose page table pointer went stale — x8 garbage suggests use-after-free of the page table, not the pool.

## Environment
- nxnative f108343, Mac Studio M5 Ultra, macOS 27.2
- Log: 1.3 MB, crash at the tail (frame 79853)

## Suggested fix
Extend `tex_storage_live()` or the pool_gpu walk to validate the sparse page table pointer before `vpt_walk`, same way the pool magic is checked. Happy to provide the full log on request.
title: FFR 1.0.1 Mac: CRASH sig=11 in nvn_sparse_protect after ~22min play (f108343)

body:
# Issue: Donkey Kong Bananza drops from 60 FPS to ~15 FPS on iPhone 17 (Switch 2 title, untested platform)

## Summary

Donkey Kong Bananza (`040074A01BF12000`, update v458752) runs on Mac via nxnative, but on an iPhone 17 it does not hold a playable frame rate. Starting from the first open room, the game begins at ~60 FPS. The drop has occurred intermittently since the beginning of the game, but right now it happens every time on loading into Ingot Isle (the area where Pauline is first encountered in rock form): immediately after the loading spike around frame 1467 (geometry mesh pipeline build + 185 texture uploads), the frame rate drops and never recovers: the in-game counter reads 13-15 FPS, and the game thrashes between present interval 2 (30 FPS target) and 3 (20 FPS target) even though GPU time stays at ~13-15 ms (60 FPS-capable). Pausing/resuming (backgrounding) temporarily restores 60 FPS for a few seconds before it degrades and thrashes again.

This is reported as a first-time issue. Per the README, Donkey Kong Bananza is currently marked "Mac only, from a dump; iPhone and iPad are untested", so this is effectively a first iPhone datapoint for this title.

## Environment

- **Device:** iPhone 17
- **iOS:** 27.0 (all screenshots show iOS 27.0)
- **nxnative build:** latest (built from FelixA02/nxnative, "Build IPA" workflow)
  - nxnative commit: ff88eaf0b3fe
  - shader chain: b7cd656abd7c
- **Game:** Donkey Kong Bananza (Switch 2)
  - Title ID: `040074A01BF12000`
  - Version: base + update v458752 (per dm/games/040074A01BF12000/README.md)
  - SDK 20.5.19, NVN2; engine: Nintendo EPD (sead / agl / gsys, Phive); modules main + sdk
- **Environment overrides (settings screen / env.txt):** DM_OPMODE=0, DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off, DM_SHOW_FPS=1, DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS=1, DM_RUMBLE=1, DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0, DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0, DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0, DM_PSO_MTL4=0, DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1, DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1, DM_METAL_HUD=1, DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=0 (run 1 only, via env.txt)
- **Log:** full run log available (frame-time / longframe trace). Can be attached as log.txt or packaged with `python3 scripts/bug_report.py 040074A01BF12000 --ios-log log.txt`. No game files, keys, or extracted assets are attached.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build the Donkey Kong Bananza IPA with the latest nxnative "Build IPA" workflow (no title_id input needed, the NSP carries a readable title ID).
2. Sideload and launch on an iPhone 17.
3. Enter Ingot Isle, the area where Pauline is first encountered in rock form (the first open room / starting area).
4. Observe the frame rate over the next ~10-20 seconds.

## Expected behavior

Stable ~60 FPS (or at least a steady 30 FPS) with low input latency, comparable to the Mac build, or at least no sustained 15 FPS lock.

## Actual behavior

- Game starts at ~60 FPS.
- Around frame 1467 a loading spike occurs (geometry mesh pipeline build + 185 texture uploads, 37.2 MB).
- After the spike the frame rate drops and never recovers: the in-game counter reads 13-15 FPS.
- In-game Metal HUD during the degraded state: GPU ~50 ms, frame interval ~73 ms (~13-14 FPS).
- The game thrashes between present interval 2 (30 FPS target) and 3 (20 FPS target) for the rest of the run.
- Pausing/resuming (backgrounding) temporarily restores 60 FPS for a few seconds, then it degrades and thrashes again.

## Evidence

In-game FPS overlay (screenshots attached). Measured values:

| Screenshot | State | FPS (counter) | GPU time | Frame interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IMG_1370 | Good | 59.87 | 14.92 ms | 16.70 ms (~60 FPS) |
| IMG_1373 | Good | ~60 (label "60 fps") | 13.80 ms | 16.67 ms (~60 FPS) |
| IMG_1374 | Degraded | 31.30 | n/a | 31.95 ms (~31 FPS) |
| IMG_1369 | Degraded | 29.12 | 20.62 ms | 34.35 ms (~29 FPS) |
| IMG_1372 | Degraded | 29.99 | 30.81 ms | 33.34 ms (~30 FPS) |
| IMG_1371 | Degraded | 15 (confirmed) | ~50 ms | ~73 ms |
| IMG_1376 | Degraded | 14 (confirmed) | ~50 ms | ~73 ms |
| IMG_1377 | Degraded | 13 (confirmed) | ~50 ms | ~73 ms |

All on iPhone 17, iOS 27.0, Metal 4, ~3.64-3.71 GB app memory, Game Mode On. Available memory ~1.86-1.87 GB.

Screenshots attached: IMG_1369-IMG_1378.

## Notes / possible leads

- Possible related issue (tested, ruled out): #737 (TotK shrine drops to ~15 fps under the same-pass feedback snapshot rule). DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=0 was set via Documents/env.txt and confirmed active in the log (boot: env DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=0 (env.txt) and [nvn-mtl] same-pass feedback sampling snapshot: off (DM_NVN_FB_SNAP)), but the frame rate still drops to ~13-15 FPS. So this is not the same-pass feedback snapshot mechanism. It is a distinct issue. The #737 workaround does not apply here.
- Log findings (run 1, with DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=0, first ~86 s): frames 1-1500 hold 60 FPS (frame time p50 16.67 ms, GPU p50 ~5-7 ms). Around frame 1514 a one-time loading spike (whole frame 579.6 ms, GPU 302.3 ms: geometry mesh pipeline build 112.9 ms + 185 texture uploads / 37.2 MB), after which the run degrades and never recovers: sustained frame times 30-55 ms (GPU 20-55 ms), the game flips present interval 2 to 3 (20 FPS target), memory climbs to ~4.8 GB resident / ~3.4 GB GPU allocated, and per-frame attachment traffic is huge (load 200-260 MB, store 240-310 MB, 50-100 load-all/store-all passes). Thermal state stays 0 throughout, so this is not thermal throttling. The in-game counter reads 13-15 FPS.
- Log findings (run 2, pause/resume experiment, ~142 s): the game starts at present interval 2, switches to 1 (60 FPS) after loading, then at frame ~1467 hits the same loading spike (geometry mesh pipeline 207.7 ms + 185 texture uploads / 37.2 MB, GPU 315 ms). Immediately after, present interval flips 1 to 2, and from ~frame 1553 the game thrashes between present interval 2 and 3 (2 to 3, dozens of flips) for the rest of the run. The in-game Metal HUD during this degraded state shows GPU ~50 ms and frame interval ~73 ms (~13-14 FPS). The host log's per-frame GPU time for the same window reports ~13-15 ms, so the two measurements disagree (different scopes); the in-game counter reads 13-15 FPS. Pausing/resuming the app (backgrounding) temporarily restores present interval 1 (60 FPS) for a few seconds before it degrades and thrashes again. The game also switches present pacing mode 1 to 3 at frame 4538. Thermal state stays 0. The run ends with the app backgrounded (audio suspended).
- Interpretation: this is a frame-pacing / adaptive present-interval problem. The initial loading spike appears to trip the game's frame-rate adaptation, after which it oscillates between 30 and 20 FPS targets. The in-game Metal HUD reports GPU ~50 ms / frame interval ~73 ms during the degraded state, while the host log's per-frame GPU time reports ~13-15 ms for the same window, so the two measurements disagree (possibly different scopes). Either way the game is stuck well below 60 FPS. Pausing/resuming resets it briefly. This is distinct from #737's same-pass feedback snapshot mechanism (already ruled out). Likely candidates: the game's own present-interval heuristics on the mobile path, or the host's present pacing interacting with the game's interval changes (period 33.33 ms to 50.00 ms observed).
- If maintainers want, I can provide a longer capture (frame-time log) or test with --show-fps / different settings.

## Labels (suggested)

body: ### Game, title ID and version The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD, `01002DA013484000`, version 1.0.0 (USA), no update. Code build IDs: main `d824d4b1bbd45d03668380d6d041ba4c`, sdk `b39add63421be525d352e576dab438d3`, subsdk0 (GLSLC) `4dd097b435891c5e0e15a65dbe47124f`, subsdk1 (movie) `535249a546887cac875a099e9c8ef367`. ### Engine and graphics API, if known Nintendo's own engine (Wii-era, ported by Tantalus), NVN, SDK 11.4.0. The survey reports the same. ### Survey and what happened Built with `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ... --platform mac` from `main` at `5474c6f`. A provisional profile; `survey.md` is attached. 1. **Black screen with sound (fixed, PR A).** The first build drew nothing: music, menu sounds and the opening movie played, but every frame was black. The log had 109 `[RED] shader … is not in the shader map` keys and `program has no vertex shader`. The split found 58 shaders, but the game initializes about 2,100 programs at boot. The shaders are in `Shaders/Shaders.arc.gz`, a plain gzip stream around a U8 archive of 2,096 GLSLC outputs, which the split did not inflate. With PR A the split finds 2,470 shaders and the game draws. Normal gameplay looks right and runs at 60 fps on an M5 MacBook Air. 2. **Dual-source blending (needs profile rows, plus PR B).** Link's eyes were oversized. Four pixel shaders blend output 1 as the second source: `dd2644e0543addd9` (Link's eyes), `e6cefebf79fa784c`, `1886490570e87890` and `deb4bc0d6f105e01` (all listed by `DM_NVN_DUAL_WANT`). Adding them to `dual_want.tsv` did nothing until PR B: the shader cache key ignored the list. With both, the eyes draw right and the red line is gone. Sky Recomp (the static recompilation of this game) made the same fix for the same symptom. 3. **Yellow fog in cinematic shots (open, details below).** **The open problem: yellow fog and dark-brown silhouettes in the opening's cinematic shots** Gameplay looks right. The title screen's sky island and the opening's camera shots (the Loftwing flight and the Skyloft flyover) look wrong: - A yellow-brown haze covers distant scenery, and near objects become flat, dark-brown silhouettes. In the bisect shots: the tower in front of Skyloft, the underside of the diving platform, and the Loftwings against the sun. - The cast comes and goes over a few seconds as the camera moves. Between those phases the same shots look clean, with a blue sky and white clouds. - Sky Recomp shows these shots clean on the same Mac. Screenshots of the yellow and clean phases are attached, with the pass dump and texture dump of one yellow frame (`DM_CTL` `passdump 1` / `texdump`). What a bisect with `DM_NVN_SKIP_FS` (made re-readable at run time for this) and texture dumps showed: - Dropping the 126-vertex draw of fragment shader `05e6dea39075fe9e` (the sky, drawn with depth range 0..0 and `GEQUAL`) turns every shot yellow. The yellow is the target's clear colour (0.725, 0.682, 0.667) under fog. So in the yellow phases, the sky and the fog in front of it are what go wrong. - The final steps do not cause it: dropping the depth-of-field composite (`6bf0c49b66d54395`), the two full-screen overlays (`a83080232dce4963`, `5e950a4a20b58873`) or the flares (`bcd6bf27e370ca3e`) leaves the yellow in. The 539×962 / 270×481 / 135×239 targets are the game's own transposed separable blur, not a size bug. Ruled out: - Missing shaders. No `not in the shader map` lines after PR A. - Dual-source blending. No red lines after the four rows. - Depth clamp. The game never calls `SetDepthClamp`. Forcing clamp at run time, on the sky draw or on every draw (a diagnostic `DM_NVN_CLAMP_FS`, not part of the PRs), changed nothing. - `DiscardColor`. The game never calls it. - Depth read through a reinterpreting view. The passes sample the D24S8 target (`fmt=260`) as depth (`swz=2222`). - Movie colour conversion. The opening movie, `THP/Demo01_01.webm` (VP9, `color_range=tv`, colour space undeclared), is the storybook intro and looks right. Its chroma is upsampled nearest-neighbour in `md_rgba`; FFmpeg's bilinear would be smoother, but that is cosmetic and separate. A guess, not checked: the fog is computed from depth or view-space z, and in these shots the camera's near/far range (or the depth mode: the log shows `depth mode near=0`, with `DeviceSetDepthMode` called 3 times at init) does not match what the fog constants assume. Gameplay cameras would then fall in a range where the error does not show. Also seen, not investigated: the picture sits about 120 px low in the window, with a black band at the top in these shots. body:
### What is missing

Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave (Switch 2, 04007EF01F8AE000, SDK 22.2.0) aborts when its first movie starts, with `nn::diag abort: Result 0xe15` in `nn::codec::InitializeAv1DecoderByTransferMemory` (from its movie module). Three things are missing:

1. **The SDK 22 names of the decoder API.** SDK 22 calls the `nn::codec` video decoder API under other names than SDK 20, whose names the host takes over today: `Initialize…DecoderByTransferMemory` / `…ByRemoteMemory`, `Get…DecoderSubmissionReadyEvent`, `MakeDecodeImagePreference` with an `ImageTilingMode`, `InitializeDecoderImagePool` without a codec mode, and `ReadDecoderOutputImageRgbaHdr`. Each goes to the decoder service, which the host does not serve.
2. **An AV1 decoder.** All 91 of the game's movies are AV1 (WebM). The host has none: `t_codec_video` checks today that AV1's Initialize is refused.
3. **The GPU route.** The game's player draws decoded pictures from the GPU, through `nvnNativeImageInitialize` and `nvnTextureInitializeFromNativeImage`, rather than reading them back.

Donkey Kong Bananza's player imports the AV1 decoder too, though its own movies are VP9.

### What you propose

I have this working on a branch and would like to agree on the scope before opening the PR. CONTRIBUTING asks for that before a change over about 1,000 lines, and this one vendors a library.

**The decoders.** `hle_codec_video.c` takes the SDK 22 names over with the existing SDK 20 implementations, and AV1 joins VP8, VP9 and H.264 as another decoder family. A new `hle_movie_av1.c` decodes it with:

- **VideoToolbox, where the chip has an AV1 decoder** (`VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported`: Apple M3 and A17 Pro on). The SDK passes no codec private data, so the `av1C` record is built from the stream's sequence header OBU.
- **dav1d everywhere else, or with `DM_AV1_DAV1D=1`.** VideoToolbox makes no AV1 session on Macs and iPads with M1 or M2, which README lists as supported. dav1d is VideoLAN's AV1 decoder (BSD 2-Clause), with arm64 NEON assembly.

**The GPU route.** `nvnNativeImageInitialize` gives a native image a host-made NVN memory pool holding one RGBA8 picture, and `nvnTextureInitializeFromNativeImage` makes a linear texture over it, so the GPU reads each new picture in place.

**How dav1d would be shipped.** Release 1.5.4 (54706fc), unmodified, under `dm/third_party/dav1d`, the way libvpx is shipped, so nothing is fetched at build time:
- Only the arm64 sources are kept: headers, `src/*.c`, and `src/arm/64` assembly. That is 130 files, about 80,000 lines, byte-identical to the tag.
- `config/config.h` is meson's own output for arm64 Apple targets, verbatim. A macOS build and an iOS cross build give the same file.
- One small wrapper per template and bit depth lets a project with one set of defines (the iOS build) compile the templates.
- `dm/host/Makefile` builds it into `gen/dav1d/libdav1d.a`: about 0.7 MB of code in the host.

**Size of our own change.** About 540 lines outside docs:
- `hle_movie_av1.c`: 260
- the `hle_codec_video.c` changes: about 170
- `t_codec_video`: 66, plus a 38-byte SVT-AV1 key frame I encoded
- the Makefiles

**What was checked.**
- `t_codec_video` (ASan and UBSan) decodes the AV1 key frame through the SDK 22 calls on both backends. It also checks a native image's pool, texture and picture against recorded NVN entry points.
- On the game's opening movie (2560×1440, 8-bit), VideoToolbox and dav1d give the same pictures, bit for bit, over the first 600. Each decodes about 450 pictures a second on an M3 Pro.
- The movie plays in the game on the Mac.
- Host tests, sanitizer builds, `dmhost` for CI's games, and the iOS compile check all pass.

**Not checked or open.**
- An iPhone or iPad build on a device.
- A Mac or iPad without hardware AV1, where dav1d is the only path. I've tested dav1d on an M3 Pro with the switch only.
- The game's second movie waits for a handler thread that never starts. Not yet traced; it may be unrelated to the decoder.

**Questions for the scope.**
1. Is vendoring dav1d acceptable, or would you prefer it fetched at a pinned commit, or AV1 limited to VideoToolbox? VideoToolbox only would leave M1 and M2 Macs and iPads without these movies: there, AV1's Initialize would be refused, as it is everywhere today, and the game would take its error path.
2. Should the iOS app link dav1d too? Every supported iPhone (A17 Pro and later) has hardware AV1, but M1 and M2 iPads don't.
3. Should this be one PR (the decoders, AV1 and the GPU route, which the game needs together) or two (the vendored dav1d first, then its use)?

The branch's other changes for this game are separate, smaller PRs: the update-only dump, the SDK 22.2.0 node cut, the shader split speed-up, the Nmouse and aud:u takeovers, NVN2 DLSS as a scaled copy, and the Ampere translator fixes.

### Platforms

Mac (tested); iPad and iPhone (compile-checked only)
title: AV1 movies for SDK 22 games: VideoToolbox where the chip has it, vendored dav1d elsewhere (scope before a PR)

body:
### What is missing

Today each game is its own app: the host and the game's rewritten modules are linked into the IPA, and the host finds its sections through the main executable. A front end that wants one app to play many games has no supported way to load a game after the app has started.

I've been doing this in NX Pocket (https://github.com/zkkzkk/nx-pocket): each game is built as a framework and loaded with dlopen. It works on iPhone with Hades II, Super Mario Maker 2, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, Mario Tennis Aces and others, but it needs a few changes in nxnative itself, which I keep as a patch.

### What you propose

Three small changes, each usable on its own:

1. The host finds its own sections through the image it is linked into (dladdr on a host symbol), so the same code runs as an app, as a dynamic library or as the Mac host. Today it assumes the main executable.
2. An entry point for a game built as a library (for example dm_pack_start(window, folder, data folder)) that does what main() does now, with the game's files and save folder passed in rather than taken from the app bundle and Documents.
3. RomFS read from an offset inside a larger file (an image start and size, e.g. DM_ROMFS with DM_ROMFS_SIZE), so a game's data can stay inside a single file without being copied out.

The packing side (a build_pack.py that builds the library from a prepared Xcode project) can stay outside nxnative. I can send 1–3 as separate small PRs if you'd like them.

### Platforms

iPhone, iPad, Mac
title: Run a game from a library loaded at run time (one app, many games)

body:
### What happened

Every time the ship is boarded from the world map (the "sail / board ship" interaction, not Castti's prologue scene), the iOS app is killed and returns to the home screen. It happens on every attempt, including after other apps have been closed.

The play log from the attempt that ends on that interaction has no `[RED]` line. It is still at about 2.6 GB resident when the log stops, on the first geometry draw of the session:

```
[dm] game arguments from the game profile: -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=2048
[dm] [nvn-mtl] memory up to frame 300: resident 2465 MB, GPU allocated 1067 MB, ... headroom to the system memory limit 3678 MB
[dm] [nvn] on-screen up to frame 2100: ... footprint 2644 MiB
[dm] [nvn-mtl] geometry compute: vertex a5b39b7f22099447_b, geometry 9093df2f7ece5fa8_bg3, 287 input primitives, 1 instances
```

That geometry shader is `DefaultTextMaterialOpaque` (`gs_engine.bin` entry 6, `9093df2f7ece5fa8`). The log ends there.

A later attempt's JetsamEvent (2026-11-02 10:17:31 +0800, bug_type 298) shows the process actually being killed for memory, not a guest abort:

- `largestProcess`: `DmIOS`, pid 83500, priority 100 (foreground), `idleDelta` none
- `reason`: `vm-pageshortage`
- `pageSize` 16384, `rpages` 391830, `lifetimeMax` 391831 → 5.98 GiB, so this was the peak, not a leftover
- `physicalPages.internal`: [19378, 116087] → 2.11 GiB of internal pages
- system `memoryPages.free`: 1944 (~30 MB)
- device `iPhone17,1`, iOS 26.6.2 (23G90)

The in-game headroom line (2465 + 3678 MB) is the same ~6 GB cap, so `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit` is already in effect. The IPA is a `--romfs separate` build from 2026-10-28 18:31.

The ~4 GB gap between internal pages and `rpages` is not the packed game (the RomFS image is about 5.5 GB on disk and is not mapped in as a private copy). Switch has 4 GB unified RAM and this scene runs there. The charged memory above the ~2 GB engine region looks like the host's Metal/IOSurface copies of streamed textures for the sea and coast. That is an inference from the jetsam split, not a root cause we have pinned to one function.

Upstream `main` as of `f108343a` does not touch `dm/games/0100A3501946E000`. `8ea27784` (unmapped guest pages returned to the system) saves on the order of hundreds of MB on a Mac and is marked unmeasured on iPhone, which is smaller than this jump from ~2.6 GB to 6 GB.

### What you expected

Boarding the ship should stay under the iOS memory limit, as the same scene does in the Switch's 4 GB.

### Game, title ID and version

OCTOPATH TRAVELER II, 0100A3501946E000, update 1.1.1 (v131072). No DLC.

### nxnative commit

`6ba3adc2` (2026-10-28 18:30 +0800), the checkout the 2026-10-28 18:31 IPA was built from. Local Intel packing patches were also in that tree; they do not change the NVN memory path.

### Shader chain version

iOS libraries packed in that IPA: `b-8b14bcc653a3` (`shader/ios/b-8b14bcc653a3`, 13979 libraries). `dmsh_chain.h` at `6ba3adc2` says `a78f966a7b38`; the pack reused the existing `b-8b14bcc653a3` iOS cache.

### How it was built and run

iPhone or iPad, unsigned IPA from build_ipa_from_nsp.py

### Device and OS

iPhone 16 Pro (iPhone17,1, A18 Pro), iOS 26.6.2 (23G90)

### Settings and environment overrides

From the launcher, written into the run log:

```
DM_FPS_TARGET=30
DM_OPMODE=0
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off
DM_LANG=zh-Hans
DM_SHOW_FPS=0
DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS=0
DM_RUMBLE=0
DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0
DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0
DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0
DM_PSO_MTL4=0
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=1
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1
DM_FPS_HOLD=on
DM_METAL_HUD=0
```

No `Documents/env.txt` overrides beyond those. Handheld and 30 fps were already selected. Closing other apps does not avoid the kill.

### What happened

`make -C dm/host/tests GAME=<id> memory` aborts on `main` since `8ea27784` (Unmapped guest memory goes back to the system). The **Host unit tests** and **Sanitizers** CI jobs fail on `main` because of it ([run 41365856879](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/actions/runs/41365856879)), and PRs based on that commit show the same two red checks (#913).

```
[dm] FATAL SVC 0x2c mprotect <addr>+0x4000 errno=13
Assertion failed: (WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 77), function fatal, file t_svc_memory.c, line 139.
make: *** [memory] Abort trap: 6
```

| Commit | `memory` test, run locally | CI `tests` workflow |
|---|---|---|
| `26ef5c2a` | passes: fatal lines for both SVC 0x2c and 0x2d | cancelled |
| `8ea27784` | fails: fatal line for 0x2c, then the assertion | failure |
| `a1693dc4` | fails: the same | not finished when this was written |

### What you expected

The `memory` test passes on `main`.

### Likely cause

This comes from reading the code. I have not tested a fix.

`failures()` in `dm/host/tests/t_svc_memory.c` makes `mprotect` fail through `fail_protect`, and expects each SVC to die with exit code 77. `8ea27784` moved UnmapPhysicalMemory to `guest_release`, which calls `mmap` first and only falls back to `mprotect` if that fails. The test's wrapper only fails `mprotect`, so `mmap` succeeds and `fatal(0x2d, alias, 0x4000, 0)` no longer dies. That matches the output above: the fatal line for 0x2d is gone at `8ea27784`.

The heap shrink in `fatal(1, 0, 0, 0)` now takes the same path, so it probably needs the same treatment. The test aborts before reaching it.

If this reading is right, the test's expectation is out of date and the host is behaving as that commit intended. I did not run any game on `8ea27784`, so I can't speak to game behaviour.

### Game, title ID and version

None: this is a host unit test. Locally it was run with `GAME=0100D9F01D474000`.

### nxnative commit

`8ea27784` is the first failing commit; `a1693dc4` also fails.

### Shader chain version

Not relevant to this test.

### How it was built and run

`make -C dm/host/tests GAME=0100D9F01D474000 memory`, with no local changes for the three commits in the table. CI fails in the steps `Host unit tests (dm/host/tests)` and `ASan and UBSan, every host unit test (dm/host/tests)`.

### Device and OS

Apple M1 Pro, macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2. CI fails on the `xcode-27` runners too.

### Settings and environment overrides

None.

### No game files

This report contains no game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: t_svc_memory fails on main since 8ea27784: Unmap no longer dies when mprotect is made to fail

body:
### What happened

Pikmin 2 (Nintendo Switch HD release, title ID 0100D680194B2000) launches successfully through nxnative on macOS and reaches gameplay. However, it repeatedly crashes after several minutes with a guest SIGSEGV at address 0x10.

Two separate runs crashed in different functions operating on the same intrusive-list data structure:

Run | Crash location | Details -- | -- | -- First (~412 seconds) | main+0x3f03c4 | Null-pointer access while manipulating a list node, on guest main thread 0x1001 Second (~248 seconds) | main+0x3f02f0 | lr=main+0x3dd558, null-pointer access in another list-removal path

The second run terminated with exit status 139.

Technical findings

  • The list uses linked nodes with apparent owner, previous and next pointers at offsets +0x08, +0x10 and +0x18.

  • One observed call path operates on embedded nodes at offset +0x60 inside objects with a 0x90-byte stride.

  • The first crash occurred on guest thread 0x1001.

  • In the second crash dump, guest main thread 0x1001 was waiting on a condition variable.

  • Multiple guest threads are assigned to virtual core 0.

The Nintendo Switch version of Pikmin 2 uses Nintendo's Hagi compatibility technology. Other Hagi-based titles, including Super Mario Galaxy, already have nxnative profiles.

Diagnostic experiment

We locally instrumented dm/host/hle_thread.c to observe SVC 0x0D priority transitions from nonzero priority to priority 0 and overlapping marked intervals on the same virtual core.

The modified host compiled successfully and the subsequent log confirmed:

[dm] [BOOST-DIAG] enabled
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x10 pc=main+0x3f02f0 lr=main+0x3dd558

No begin, OVERLAP or LONG entries were observed.

This does not rule out a scheduling issue. The detector only covers a narrow priority-transition pattern, and the root cause remains unknown.

Possible areas to investigate

  • A stale or concurrently modified intrusive-list node.

  • Hagi's object lifetime and callback behavior.

  • Guest same-core scheduling semantics versus independent macOS pthread execution.

  • Whether the crash originates from guest code, memory corruption, or incorrect host semantics.

No scheduler fix has been applied.

Expected behavior

Pikmin 2 should remain stable during gameplay without unexpected guest segmentation faults.

Environment

  • Game: Pikmin 2

  • Title ID: 0100D680194B2000

  • Reported main NSO build ID: 9A257FAB83444214

  • Platform: Apple Silicon Mac, M4 Pro

  • Game profile: provisional external profile generated by nxnative's NSP workflow

  • Build: macOS app using the native dmhost executable

  • Diagnostic override: DM_BOOST_DIAG=1 for the second crash

  • Game version, macOS version, nxnative commit, shader chain: pending local report collection

Reproduction

  1. Build the Mac app for Pikmin 2 using its provisional profile.

  2. Launch the resulting app.

  3. Play normally for several minutes.

  4. Observe a SIGSEGV in the guest list-manipulation code.

The crash is intermittent and has not yet been reduced to deterministic reproduction steps.

Logs

Full logs and metadata are to be provided through scripts/bug_report.py, after checking that the archive contains no game files, keys, extracted code or shaders.

Any guidance on distinguishing a Hagi guest object-lifecycle bug from an nxnative scheduling or memory-semantics issue would be appreciated.

body:
Projects that build on nxnative, like NX2Apple, take `main` in with every update. We read the commits, but we cannot reliably tell which ones matter to us. nxnative has no releases and no tags, so there is no place that says what changed for a front end. Three kinds of changes are hard to see:

- **Changes that break something that already exists.** Since `7c23cc0` ("backslashes separate path components", PR #513) a save that an older host wrote as `\savedata0.bin` is not found, because the host now looks for `savedata0.bin`. Link's Awakening (`01006BB00C6F0000`) shows "New game" for every file, and the saves are still in the folder. A patch that copies them is in https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/pull/461. The shader chain is another case: a bump moves it, and every game built before it has to be built again.
- **Changes to an interface a front end uses.** A new or changed environment variable, script argument, JSON progress event or field, manifest or profile field, file or output path.
- **New functions a front end could offer.** A new setting, a new kind of input (a merged NSP, a folder without `prod.keys`), a new kind of game (Switch 2), a new requirement.

The last update was 53 commits. We cannot tell for sure which of them touch these three.

Would you add a short convention? For example a section "For front ends" in the pull request description, with one line for each of the three kinds when a change has one, and the same line in the squash commit message. Then `git log --grep` finds them for everyone who follows `main`. If you prefer another place, such as a `docs/CHANGES.md`, that works for us too. We can also help to write the list for commits that are already in. Our own reading of the 53 commits is a start.
title: Changes in main that downstream projects need to know about: how do they find out?

body:
**Game:** SEGA Mega Drive Classics, title ID `0100F7300B24E000`, version 1.0.2 (update v131072). Unity 2017.4.4f1, SDK 4.5.0, NVN.
**nxnative:** commit `2006d5ed8690`, Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), provisional profile (no profile in `dm/games`).
**Mac:** Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.2 (+ Metal Toolchain 27B47).

## Summary

1. **Crash when the second intro movie starts** ‚Äî fixed locally, patch below.
2. **Black screen with sound**: the game draws a full-screen opaque black UI quad (a fader) every frame and never fades it out. Underneath it the bedroom menu renders correctly.
3. The likely root cause of (2): **the intro movies are decoded but never drawn**. Unity's VideoPlayer (`Hidden/VideoDecode` is in the shader map) never creates its video plane textures, so the intro sequence presumably never completes and the fader stays up.

## 1. Crash on the second movie (fixed)

**Symptom:** the first intro movie plays (with sound), then the process aborts as the second one starts: `CRASH sig=5 pc=main+0xe6dcc8` (the game's abort observer, "Assertion failure"), host exits with 133. Same on every boot.

**Backtrace:** `nn::diag::detail::OnAssertionFailure` ‚Üê `nn::os::TimedWaitSystemEvent` (assertion on the `SystemEventType` state byte at +0x28 being neither 1 nor 2), called from the game's audio thread (`main+0x1135018`), which waits on the renderer event at `this+0x9f0` in a 100 ms loop.

**Cause:** each movie closes and reopens the audio renderer with the **same** `SystemEvent`. On the reopen, `ar_open` (`hle_audren.c`) calls `DestroySystemEvent` on the local event the SDK just created in place, then `hle_bind_system_event`. That returns early because the binding table still holds an entry for the address from the first open (the SDK overwrote the struct in place without destroying it, so `CloseHandle` never ran and `se_unbind` never removed the entry). The event is left destroyed (state 0), and the waiting audio thread trips the assertion.

**Fix:** drop the stale binding before re-binding:

```diff
--- a/dm/host/hle_audren.c
+++ b/dm/host/hle_audren.c
@@ ar_open
     if (ev && *(int32_t *)(param + P_DEVICE) == 0) {
         static void (*destroy)(void *); if (!destroy) destroy = gsym("_ZN2nn2os18DestroySystemEventEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeE");
-        destroy(ev); hle_bind_system_event(ev, 1);
+        destroy(ev); hle_forget_system_event(ev); hle_bind_system_event(ev, 1);
     }
--- a/dm/host/hle_thread.c
+++ b/dm/host/hle_thread.c
+// Drops a binding whose SystemEvent the SDK has overwritten in place without destroying it (its handles are gone from the struct), so the next bind creates a new kernel event
+void hle_forget_system_event(void *ev) {
+    pthread_mutex_lock(&G);
+    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_se_lock); uint32_t wh = se_find(ev); pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_se_lock);
+    if (wh) se_unbind(wh);
+    pthread_mutex_unlock(&G);
+}
--- a/dm/host/dm.h
+++ b/dm/host/dm.h
+void hle_forget_system_event(void *g);   // hle_thread.c: drop the binding of a SystemEvent the SDK re-created in place (the next bind makes a new kernel event)
```

The old kernel event's handles leak (one pair per reopen); they are no longer reachable from the struct. **Result:** all three intro movies play through, and the game runs to the menu with no crash (45 s+ tested).

## 2. Black screen with sound

**Symptom:** after the fix the game runs at 60 fps with music, but the window stays black. A few columns at the far left and right edges show picture.

**What the pass dump shows** (`DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`, `DM_NVN_TEXDUMP`):
- The G-buffer and lit scene targets hold the correct bedroom (posters, shelf, TV).
- The last draw into the 1280√ó720 scene target before the final blit is `vs=02abd0d9b0df0279_b fs=29e9eb31c851398a_b` (`unity_builtin_extra#UI/Default`), 6 indices, white 4√ó4 texture (`ser=11`), `_TextureSampleAdd = 0`.
- Its vertex buffer (`DM_NVN_CBDUMP_KEY=02abd0d9b0df0279_b`) is a full-screen quad with vertex colour `00 00 00 ff`: **opaque black**. This is the game's own fader, not a translation error. It stays at alpha 1 at frame 330 (intro) and frame 1500 (menu).
- `fs=97c2c1139a3637a2_b` also blacks out most of the frame. Skipping only `29e9eb31‚Ä¶` leaves edge columns visible, and skipping only `97c2c113‚Ä¶` leaves the frame black. With both skipped the menu is fully visible and playable:

```
DM_NVN_SKIP_FS=97c2c1139a3637a2_b,29e9eb31c851398a_b
```

(Used as a workaround in `Resources/dm/env.txt`. I have not established what `97c2c113‚Ä¶` draws or whether it is also intended content.)

## 3. Intro movies decoded but never drawn (likely root cause)

- `movie::Decoder` type 1 (AVC), output 4, mode 1 (NV12 into client buffers), 1920√ó1080, plus AAC. VideoToolbox decodes every packet: `241 packets in, 241 frames out`. Unity calls `GetOutputFormat`, `GetOutputBuffer` (3,110,400 bytes per frame) and `ReleaseOutputBufferIndex` normally, and `Stop` / `Flush` at each movie's end.
- The shader map contains `Hidden/VideoDecode` (var19.0‚Äì19.17), so this is Unity's VideoPlayer.
- **No video plane texture is ever created or sampled.** The 18 CPU-written textures are all ‚â§1024 wide, and no R8 1920√ó1080 or RG8 960√ó540 texture appears in any pass. No draw uses a `VideoDecode` key.
- The host's output format keys are the full set (`width`, `height`, `crop`, `stride`, `slice-height`, `nv12-*`).
- The renderer the movie path opens logs `audren: rendered 200 frames, 0 of them not silent`, which may or may not matter if Unity's video clock follows its audio.

So Unity takes the decoded frames but never gets as far as creating its planes. Nothing in the log explains why; there is no `[RED]` line.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build the Mac app from base + update v131072 .
2. Start it without any `DM_NVN_SKIP_FS`. With the patch from section 1, the intro sounds play and the window stays black with sound.
3. Optional: `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP=330 DM_NVN_PASSDUMP_ALL=1 DM_NVN_CBDUMP=<dir> DM_NVN_CBDUMP_KEY=02abd0d9b0df0279_b` shows the black fader quad.

I can provide logs and pass dumps on request.
title: SEGA Mega Drive Classics: intro movies never drawn, black overlay never fades (+ crash fix on the 2nd movie)

body:
Thank you very much for nxnative. While following up the tutorial-video concern mentioned in #885, I traced a separate H.264 output-order defect into the host. I am reporting it separately from the optional resolution/HDR experiment so it can be reviewed independently. Please redirect this if another existing report would be a better home.

### What happened

Odyssey's looping gameplay tutorials become irregular after the first loop. Output timestamps jump forward and backward among B pictures even though all pictures are present and the player consumes about 30 pictures per second. This was reproduced in the initial **right-stick / Look Around** tutorial.

The initial subjective report was “twice as fast.” **The sustained measurements do not establish 2× playback.** A short decoder-acquisition window delivered 1 s of media in 0.501 s, but included prefetch. The confirmed defect is picture order across restarted loops; I am not claiming this proves every perceived speed issue or every cutscene is fixed.

### What you expected

Each loop should retain presentation order, including its tail pictures, at the authored cadence. Gameplay should retain its existing 60 fps target.

### Game, title ID and version

Super Mario Odyssey, `0100000000010000`, base + update **1.4.1 / v393216**; main build `b424be150a8e7d78701cbe7a439d9ebf`. The tested tutorial track is 480×272 AVC, 60 pictures at 30 fps, a 2 s loop.

### nxnative commit

Gameplay was checked in a local NX2Apple checkout `df713726c682cc936ac47d8ea17fa35fa522acb1`, vendored nxnative base `ee6648cb2bb46c19255c1d04f88e9c40d36ef6b4`, with earlier local changes including the isolated rendering work described in #885. **This is not a clean current-upstream gameplay test.**

The unmodified AVC source in that checkout matches the current upstream blob `a852d5659a071dfd2ff4418812311912ad528661`.

The source-only patch below was adapted to current upstream `cd859c38a8f8890ddbb57a23d6f45e23ba9e6651`, preserving its newer native-texture slot-release tests. `git apply --check` passes there. The adapted synthetic test was also compiled and run against that revision's movie implementation. This is an apply/unit check, not a gameplay test of that revision.

### Shader chain version

`6c889f0966bc` in the local gameplay app. This decoder fix does not change the shader translation chain.

### How it was built and run

Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), launched through its native prelaunch GUI. Only the host executable was rebuilt and repackaged; existing rewritten modules, shader libraries and pipeline archives were reused. Original user saves were preserved separately during the fresh-save tutorial test and restored afterward.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro, Apple M3 Max, 64 GB; macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), built-in Retina display.

### Settings and environment overrides

Docked mode, windowed, Italian, native 60 fps gameplay target. The isolated local enhancement preset retained a 4K dynamic maximum and experimental scene-derived HDR, as described in #885. Runtime selections: `DM_FULLSCREEN=0`, `DM_LANG=it`, `DM_METAL_HUD=0`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0`, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=0`, `DM_PSO_MTL4=1`, `DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0`, `DM_RUMBLE=1`, `DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0`, `DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0`. The enhancement plan sets `DM_FPS=60`, `DM_EDR_TRANSPORT_PROBE=1` and `DM_ODYSSEY_SCENE_HDR=1`.

Small read-only diagnostics were added to decoder acquisition / CPU output-copy calls to count pictures, detect within-loop PTS regressions and measure complete loops. No whole-game 30 fps cap, playback delay, timestamp clamp or frame skip was added.

### Cause and local fix

The client loops the MP4 by submitting another IDR with restarted PTS, **without an EOS or Flush**. The host's single depth-4 queue sorts by PTS across all loops. The previous loop's four high-PTS tail pictures remain behind every new low-PTS picture. They occupy the entire lookahead, so subsequent loops effectively leave in decode order.

The patch tags pictures by coded sequence, advancing once per access unit containing an IDR. It sorts by sequence, then PTS; completed-sequence pictures drain before the next sequence, while the current sequence retains its normal lookahead. Flush resets both the queue and sequence state. All pictures are retained. VideoToolbox decode flags remain synchronous.

This is a different mechanism from #700: that report concerns native-texture slot reuse; this one is in the AVC reorder queue and was observed on CPU/NV12 output. The patch does not replace or remove that report's slot-release handling.

### Verification

- **Synthetic regression:** three B-picture sequences with restarted PTS; all 36 pictures must leave exactly once in presentation order. It also checks a completed sequence with fewer pictures than the lookahead and Flush reset. Existing POC-type-2 and constrained-output-slot EOS tests still pass. Local AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer checks pass.
- **Real R-stick clip, three-loop private replay:** 180 pictures. Old decoder: 123 wrong PTS positions and 116 misplaced images after the first loop. Fixed decoder: zero of each; repeated loops have matching per-picture image hashes.
- **All 24 local PlayGuide tracks:** three loops each, **7,632 pictures**, chronological output and matching repeated-image hashes, including the cap-throw tutorial. The private replay converts MP4 length-prefixed samples to the Annex B packets supplied by the SDK. No media or media-derived bytes are shared here.
- **Actual gameplay tutorial:** a quiet 12-loop sample had 60 pictures per loop, median **2.000021 s**, range **1.995349–2.037966 s**, no within-loop PTS regressions. A separate 75-loop window while other codec tests ran had a longest loop of 2.400337 s; that remains in the evidence and is not claimed eliminated by an ordering fix.
- Other games and iOS have **not** been runtime-tested with this change; no full five-game `scripts/regress.py check` is claimed. The modified host is installed only in the isolated Odyssey app. The source mechanism is generic AVC handling, so broader validation would still be needed before merging.

### Logs

A complete sanitized gameplay run log is supplied in the accompanying expandable comment as gzip/base64 with a checksum, alongside readable examples. Personal paths have been replaced by `<TITLE_DIR>`, `<NX2APPLE_CHECKOUT>` and `<HOME>`. The pre-existing `SetRenderEnableConditional: the host draws anyway for now` warning is retained; it is not claimed fixed here.

### Source and reproduction

The accompanying source comment contains only the two-file host/test patch. Save it as `movie-loop-order.patch`, review it, then on a matching checkout:

```sh
git apply --check movie-loop-order.patch
git apply movie-loop-order.patch
make -C dm/host/tests GAME=0100000000010000 build/t_movie_avc
dm/host/tests/build/t_movie_avc
```

For an actual game test, rebuild/repack the host using the existing matching title work directory; keep its extraction, rewritten modules, shader libraries and compatible pipeline archives. No shader or full NSP rebuild is required by this change itself. Test saves should remain separate from normal progress.

The patch is offered under the project's MIT license, retaining upstream attribution. No new repository is needed. Thank you for considering it; please treat this as a focused, locally tested fix offered for review, rather than a claim of complete movie compatibility.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game. Only engine/test source changes, aggregate measurements and a sanitized text log are included.
title: Odyssey: looping H.264 tutorials lose B-frame order when PTS restart (source fix and regression test)

body:
### Proposal and scope

Thank you very much for nxnative and for all the work that makes these experiments possible. Apologies if optional rendering enhancements are outside the intended scope of the project; please feel free to redirect or close this if it is not useful. This is a small experimental report and an offer of reviewable source, not a request to support a new set of promises.

I have been testing higher internal resolutions and scene-derived HDR on a local Mac build of **Super Mario Odyssey**. I am keeping the separate bloom/sampler investigation in #612; this thread concerns optional enhancements only.

### Game, build, host and device

- Odyssey `0100000000010000`, update 1.4.1; main build `b424be150a8e7d78701cbe7a439d9ebf`.
- Local NX2Apple checkout `df713726c682cc936ac47d8ea17fa35fa522acb1`, with earlier local fixes; vendored nxnative base `ee6648cb2bb46c19255c1d04f88e9c40d36ef6b4`. This is **not a clean upstream build or a merged change**.
- Existing shader chain `6c889f0966bc`. Build-specific changes are gated by build ID, rewritten-baseline SHA and expected instruction sites.
- Apple M3 Max, 64 GB; macOS 27.0.1 (26A434). Built-in HDR Retina display, plus a PA278CV SDR monitor.

### What changed locally

**Internal resolution, not just window upscaling.** Raising the docked framebuffer dimensions alone left the scene G-buffer at 1600×900. The prototype changes the matching docked quality tiers in the owner's local `ProjectGraphicsQuality` data too, preserving dynamic-resolution ratios. Scene/depth attachments were verified at 1080p, 1440p, 1800p and 3840×2160.

Larger targets also need matching memory budgets. At 4K the tested configuration uses a 576 MiB texture pool / 656 MiB AglHeap. Raising only the host reservation still failed because the game requests its own fixed application and root heaps. Increasing both game-side heaps by 512 MiB, with matching isolated host-profile limits, allowed the original world allocation to succeed. The helper refuses an unknown rewritten baseline rather than guessing patch addresses.

**Frame rate.** Odyssey already targets 60 fps. This is **not a new 120 fps patch**, and I have not validated simulation speed at other limits. The launcher exposes 60 only. Higher rendering resolution and higher simulation frequency should remain separate capabilities.

**Scene-derived HDR.** An isolated compose-fragment experiment uses scene plus bloom, with the game's exposure, before the original tone curve/LUT. It preserves the original graded SDR RGB below scene-linear white and adds a bounded shoulder from real scene highlight energy above white. The post chain/window use FP16; the final linear copy is not decoded from sRGB again, and HUD white remains at SDR white. This is a custom enhancement, **not Nintendo's Switch 2 implementation, native Switch 2 game support, or a calibrated visual match**.

**Moving between SDR and HDR displays.** The initial prototype configured EDR only at launch. The updated local runtime keeps a stable linear FP16 render/window ABI whenever HDR is requested. Each compose draw receives an immutable frame-arena selector: original graded SDR channels on SDR displays, the highlight shoulder on HDR displays. Screen notifications update EDR metadata independently. Starting on SDR and then moving HDR → SDR → HDR was verified in actual 3D gameplay without a restart; logs confirm the compose selection follows every move. Resolution, refresh and backing scale remain separate. This is local functional validation, not a calibrated measurement of the physical display.

### Verification and limits

- 1800p raw FP16 output after UI: 334,122 pixels above SDR white, peak luminance 3.998×, finite channels; sampled coin/bottom HUD white stayed at 1×.
- A quiet 2,101-frame opening-scene sample at 1800p: frame p50/p95/p99 16.658/17.011/17.792 ms, GPU p50/p95 7.543/8.248 ms. A 4K opening sample had frame p50/p95/p99 16.669/16.919/17.082 ms.
- These are bounded opening-scene results, **not whole-game 60 fps guarantees**. A later position showed GPU p95 above 16.67 ms on both displays. A 75 Hz window also has uneven cadence for 60 fps; changing display refresh cannot fix an independent GPU bottleneck.
- 126 synthetic GPU checks passed for transport, highlight range, original SDR channel preservation, promotion guards and the display-dependent selector. Existing modules, shader libraries and archives were reused; only one custom compose fragment was compiled, with its few affected pipeline bases created as needed.
- The user has also reported overly fast embedded tutorial videos. Their source tracks are authored at 30 fps, and playback timing remains under investigation; this prototype must not be read as a claim that all movies or scene transitions have correct timing. No 120 fps game patch is involved.
- No other game, iPhone/iPad, MetalFX+HDR combination or 120 fps gameplay has been validated here.

### What might generalize

Stable linear output surfaces, display-aware SDR/HDR selection, capability descriptions, cache reuse and version-gated enhancement profiles could be reusable mechanisms. The patch addresses, tier names, heap sizes and compose shader are **Odyssey-specific**. Another game needs its own scene/tone-map/UI analysis and timing checks; these values should not become global defaults.

The extra fragment binding in this isolated experiment would need proper ABI/chain integration and review before any upstream use. The sources are a prototype for inspection, not a ready-to-merge patch or a request to change current defaults.

### Source and reproduction material

I will add the source-only helper, narrowly scoped host patches, the HDR math/fragment-regeneration script and synthetic tests in expandable comments below, so no new repository is needed. Generated game shaders, rewritten modules, overlays, keys, saves, captures and game artwork are not included. Reproduction uses the owner's own matching local game inputs/cache. The graphics and launcher/preset proposals are intentionally separate.

Would any of this be useful in a smaller, properly scoped form—for example display-aware output first, with optional per-build enhancements kept separate? Thank you again; there is no expectation that the project should maintain this experiment.
title: Experimental Odyssey rendering enhancements: higher internal resolutions and scene-derived HDR (Mac prototype)

body:
## Problem or idea

Two virtual-gamepad improvements discussed with @v0lumehi (he took them on when the fork's earlier attempts were closed — this issue keeps them from getting lost; the owner asked for it to be written down):

**1. A words-only hint for the 3D layout's right-stick zone.** The right stick answers anywhere in the right third of the screen but is drawn nowhere (its centre follows the finger, so a fixed ring would mislead). Players look for a stick and find none — the fork collected reports within days, on Pokémon Legends Z-A among others. The direction agreed during device testing on the fork: **words only, once per launch, two seconds** — nothing stick-shaped (a ring reads as a fixed stick). The fork's patch carried a dashed-boundary-plus-words version; @v0lumehi said he had a better take, and it is his call.

**2. A layout editor for the virtual gamepad.** The control positions are compiled-in constants that do not fit every hand, every game or every grip. The fork's attempt (device-verified by the owner) had: a long-press on the layout button opens an editor where every movable control drags anywhere, **each face key adjusting on its own** with the diamond's spot as fallback, a one-tap reset, and — the bug class worth remembering — the saved position read where drawing, touch hit-test and the editor's grab all read it, so a moved key cannot trigger at its old spot. Positions as screen fractions in NSUserDefaults, per game, built-in layout as fallback, editor holds no game input. The first version scattered the controls for players (the diamond broke, keys drifted), so the lesson is: per-key geometry must be verified on a device before it ships.

Both are upstream-facing UX for every player, so they belong here rather than as fork patches. Fork reference implementations: patches 0035 and 0036 (reverted, in the fork's history).
title: The virtual gamepad: a words-only hint for the 3D layout's right-stick zone, and a layout editor

body:
## Scope
Add optional Mac local-player setup in the existing launch window: connected controllers only, explicit own/shared player roles, optional keyboard on a selectable player, and app-local left/right input splitting for combined Joy-Con pairs. Show only active players, reject conflicting main-device assignments, support hotplug, and preserve the current automatic defaults.

## Native API constraints
GameController does not expose a documented persistent physical controller ID or arbitrary Joy-Con unpair/regroup API. Source objects must remain in one process; copying names or enumeration indexes between launcher and host would misassign identical controllers. Split input cannot promise independent half motion/rumble. Saved model preferences can restore unique matches, but they are not physical-device identities.

## Integration
The local implementation keeps configuration and gameplay in the same process for opt-in configured Mac apps, using a profile/ABI/executable-paired loadable host and the existing native launch settings UI. There is no second post-Play dialog. Legacy standalone/headless hosts, existing settings/save paths and explicit launcher bypass behavior remain separate. No synthetic input or private Apple APIs are used.

## Local implementation update — 2026-11-03

This is an issue, not a published controller PR. The implementation below is in the local working copy and installed Mario Kart 8 Deluxe app; it is **not available on current upstream `main`**.

```text
existing launch window
  ├─ Controls: assign each connected input to a player
  ├─ combined Joy-Con input: Together / Separate
  └─ Remember player setup
       Play → save model preferences + keyboard slot/mode
       next launch → unique model match restores automatically
                     ambiguous/incomplete model → choose saved row, press controller button
```

- Player summaries and active input rows are embedded in the initial launch window. Inputs can share a player or choose a new player. Combined Joy-Con sources split into sideways left/right inputs; this is not Bluetooth unpairing.
- **Remember player setup** now saves whole/split controller routes and keyboard choices per app. A complete vendor/category description restores automatically only with one saved and one connected match. Duplicate or unclear devices require explicit button confirmation; discovery order is not identity. A late duplicate arrival revokes automatic, but not explicit, assignments.
- Missing/unconfirmed profiles are retained; **Forget** is an explicit preview action. Only **Play** commits edits. Play with Remember unchecked clears the setup preferences. Quit, closing the window or disabling setup does not save preview changes. Legacy keyboard-only preferences keep Remember enabled.
- Fixed a launch-window crash: `LauncherPlayersView.sizeThatFits` forced AppKit layout while SwiftUI was measuring it, re-entering the ancestor `NSHostingView` and aborting in AttributeGraph. Constraint-based `fittingSize` measurement now runs without that nested layout call.

### Evidence

- Native routing/persistence tests pass, including reversed discovery order, split routes, duplicate/missing/incomplete models, button-only confirmation, late hotplug, conflicts, legacy preferences, Forget and cancellation.
- `python3 -m unittest dm.ios.tests.test_launcher_storage`: 3 tests pass. The hosted-layout regression aborts with the old layout call and passes with the fix.
- Real installed-library view-only and never-shown SwiftUI hosting checks pass. Packaging/library integration checks pass. No window was shown or app activated by these checks.
- Updated the installed app's host/library pair while retaining the repaired launcher code, original derived game profile and shader chain. ABI/profile/executable-hash pairing was checked before signing; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes after installation. All 66 snapshotted user-data files and app preferences were unchanged.
- Interactive controller save/relaunch and multiplayer gameplay validation remain pending. These checks are not a claim of gameplay or multi-game regression coverage.

### External launchers

The current embedded setup is per app and requires its launch window. It does **not** supply saved assignments to an external launcher starting games with `--no-launcher`.

The proposed direction is **one shared assignment implementation and configuration model** for the embedded window and external launcher UIs, not an independent name-ordering system. An external launcher would show its own UI, save selected assignments and pass those preferences to nxnative at launch; the host would resolve live devices and apply the choices using the same logic, without opening its settings window. The concrete handoff is not designed or implemented yet. A launch option may be a thin adapter to the common implementation, rather than a second set of routing rules.

Gonzalo-Bruna has offered to help implement a small piece and test it with an Xbox and 8BitDo controller. The follow-up comment invites collaboration on that non-UI integration and asks for the relevant launcher code. The local controller work first needs a focused source PR against `main`; no external integration has been assigned or completed. Dynamic discovery, missing-device reservations/fallbacks and identical-model ambiguity must be covered by shared tests.
title: feat(mac): configure local player inputs in the launch window

The Switch 2's NSO GameCube controller has no iOS driver, so it never shows up as a GameController pad and can't be used in the iPhone app. I have it working, and I'd like to know whether you'd take it as a PR, and in what shape.

**What it does**
- Up to four NSO GameCube controllers connect over Bluetooth LE through NSOGCKit (MIT, https://github.com/pookee/nso-gamecube-ios).
- Each is a player of its own, as in `DmGamepad.m`. The buttons map by position, both sticks and the analog triggers keep their range, and rumble goes to the controller.
- Their reports go into the same per-player state as GameController pads, and the touch gamepad hides while one is connected.

**Tested** on an iPhone (A20 Pro, iOS 27) with Super Mario Bros. Wonder and Animal Crossing: New Horizons, in a build that embeds the game in another app.

**Size:** the changes to `DmGamepad.m` and the project are small. The controller library itself is about 2,000 lines, which is why I'm asking first, per CONTRIBUTING. It could be a vendored copy under `dm/ios/Sources/NSOGC` (what I have now) or a Swift package dependency, whichever you prefer.
