body:
# iOS: every cheat is turned off — `mprotect` on a code page fails with EACCES (errno 13)

## Summary

On a real iPhone the cheat engine loads and parses the file correctly (right build ID, right entry names), but **every entry is turned off** because writing a code page fails:

```
[dm] cheats: writable alias of main not mapped (mprotect toggle fallback)
[dm] cheats: …/Documents/games/0100F2C0115B6000/cheats/277178B7DBA1B6D4.txt: build 277178B7DBA1B6D4
[dm] [RED] cheats: no writable alias of main, code pages go through an mprotect toggle that races with the game's own execution
[dm] [RED] cheat "№ 1. Inf. Health": mprotect of a code page failed (errno 13), turning it off
[dm] [RED] cheat "№ 2. Inf. Stamina": mprotect of a code page failed (errno 13), turning it off
[dm] [RED] cheat "№ 4. Inf. Battery": mprotect of a code page failed (errno 13), turning it off
```

This matches the PR note "The iPhone: the engine compiles into the iOS host but was not run there" — this report is that first run.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | NX2Apple 0.7.2, carrying this branch's `hle_cheats.c` |
| Game | The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom 1.4.3, title `0100F2C0115B6000`, build `277178B7DBA1B6D4` (v720896) |
| Cheat file | Atmosphère format, 89 entries, parsed without errors |
| Device | iPhone (A-series), iOS 27.2, developer mode on |
| Layout | slim IPA, game data as `Documents/romfs.img` (`DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO`) |

## Reproduced in three signing configurations

| # | Signing | `get-task-allow` | Debugger attached | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Distribution profile (third-party cert) | `false` | no | 3 × `mprotect … errno 13` |
| 2 | Personal team dev cert (`Apple Development: …`) | `true` | no | 3 × `mprotect … errno 13` |
| 3 | Same dev cert, launched from Xcode | `true` | yes (`debugserver` running) | 3 × `mprotect … errno 13` |

So neither `get-task-allow` nor `CS_DEBUGGED` (debugger attach) is enough. The write is refused at the kernel level.

## Why

`alias_setup()` — the writable-alias path that the Mac host uses — is deliberately a no-op on iPhone (`dm/host/hle_cheats.c`, iOS branch):

```c
#if TARGET_OS_IPHONE
static void alias_setup(void) { g_alias = NULL; }
#else
static void alias_setup(void) {
    … mach_vm_remap(mach_task_self(), &dst, size, 0, VM_FLAGS_ANYWHERE,
                    mach_task_self(), (mach_vm_address_t)(uintptr_t)m->base, FALSE,
                    &cur, &mx, VM_INHERIT_SHARE);
    … mach_vm_protect(mach_task_self(), dst, size, 0, VM_PROT_READ | VM_PROT_WRITE);
    g_alias = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)dst;
}
#endif
```

with the comment `(unsampled, plain C must stay compiling)`.

So on iOS the only remaining path is the per-page `mprotect` toggle in `main_write_pages`. But `main` is not backed by anonymous memory: `gen_embed.py` puts the image into `__TEXT,__dm<name>x0` / `__TEXT,__dm<name>x1` (executable, read-only), and `loader.c`'s iOS branch reserves one contiguous range and `vm_remap`s the pieces back into it. Those pages keep their code-signing provenance, so `mprotect(PROT_WRITE)` on them returns `EACCES`. Writing to a `__TEXT` page of a signed executable requires the Apple-granted `dynamic-codesigning` entitlement; `get-task-allow` and a debugger are not sufficient (measured above, case 3).

## Two observations that may matter for a fix

1. **A writable segment for the image already exists and is unused on iOS.** `gen_embed.py` emits `__DM<name>W,__img` — an RW segment holding `[round16K(TEXT_END), PATCH_OFF)` — and prints the `-segprot` flags for it. Nothing in the iOS cheat path reads it: the engine only knows `g_alias` (no-op on iPhone) and the mprotect fallback. It is not enough by itself for entries that patch code in `x0`/`x1`, but it does suggest the intended design.
2. **`docs/frontends.md` reads as if the phone works.** The paragraph

   > **The iPhone.** The engine is compiled into the iOS host too (without safe mode), with the same folder rule, but the iOS app sets neither `DM_CHEATS` nor `DM_ROOT`, so cheats are off there unless `Documents/env.txt` names a folder with `DM_CHEATS`. …

   describes the switch, not the write path; front ends outside this repo (NX2Apple ships a "Manage → Cheats" UI for iPhone and iPad) read it as "set the env switch and it works". A sentence stating that the write path is unimplemented on iPhone would prevent that.

## Directions that could actually work on iOS

- **Bake at build time.** Apply the enabled entries to `patched_*/main.patched.bin` before signing (the engine and `cheat_anchor.py` already know how to resolve addresses; this needs the write at build, not at run time). Static, survives code signing, no entitlement.
- **Run the game image from anonymous memory.** Map a private RW copy of the image and execute from it; then the toggle works. Requires `dynamic-codesigning` on iOS, i.e. not shippable to sideloaded builds.
- **Keep it unsupported on iPhone** and say so in `docs/frontends.md` and the `docs/reference/cheats.md` platform table.

## Not a CI regression

The "Unsigned iOS app (synthetic modules, Swift and link)" job builds the iOS project with synthetic modules and does not launch it, so a green run there says nothing about this path. There is no job that reaches `main_write_pages` on a device.

## Logs

Happy to attach full `Documents/log.txt` from all three runs, plus the generated `xcode/Gen/embed.S` and the `codesign -d --entitlements` output of each build, if that helps.
title: iOS: every cheat is turned off — mprotect on a code page fails with EACCES (errno 13)

body:
### What happened

The host's `NVNbuffer` keeps a magic word at +0x0, the pool at +0x8, the offset at +0x10 and the size at +0x18. A game that writes a buffer's offset and size into the object itself, at +0x18 and +0x20, doesn't get them back: its offset lands in the host's size field, and `nvnBufferGetAddress` / `nvnBufferGetSize` keep returning what the buffer was initialized with.

Since a game writes those two fields on purpose, it looks like the console driver keeps a buffer's offset at +0x18 and its size at +0x20.

I ran into it with LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga. It hands out its uniform data from one ring inside a single pool:

- It initializes each `NVNbuffer` once, with `SetStorage(pool, 0x100, size)` (`main+0x5e0060`).
- For every allocation from the ring, it writes the allocation's offset at +0x18 and its size at +0x20 (`main+0x5e008c`).
- Then it binds what `nvnBufferGetAddress` and `nvnBufferGetSize` return (`main+0x5e7bd0`).

Every uniform buffer it bound came out at the same address (pool + 0x100), with the allocation's offset as its size (values like `0x4b296000`). The game kept running with sound, but every menu draw came out empty and the screen stayed black.

### What you expected

`nvnBufferGetAddress` and `nvnBufferGetSize` returning the offset and size the game wrote.

### Game, title ID and version

Found on LEGO® Star Wars™: The Skywalker Saga, `010042D00D900000`, update v589824 (1.10.0) on top of the base game. NintendoSDK 12.3.6. Main build ID `ec593a5f9552100a9fe95c4ca9e34873`.

### nxnative commit

Seen on the copy vendored in NX2Apple (upstream 5d2bf73), and the same on upstream ee6648cb. The buffer layout is unchanged on `main` today (b17bd8a8).

### Shader chain version

`373efc7add5f` when I found it, `b3ca4b7c621f` now.

### How it was built and run

Built as a Mac app with the NSP script (`--platform mac-app`) from a provisional profile, and started from the app.

### Device and OS

Mac16,13, Apple M4, 24 GB, macOS 27.0 (26A428)

### Settings and environment overrides

Defaults. The address and size values above came from extra logging I added while tracing it.

### Logs

The relevant values are above; the log itself only shows a normally running game with a black screen.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: NVNbuffer: a game that writes a buffer's offset and size into the object gets the wrong address and size back

## What happened

Entering a specific pipe in the Sand Kingdom crashes the game every time. It happens with a Switch Pro Controller and with an Xbox controller. With **Rumble off on nxnative's settings screen** the pipe works and there is no crash; turning rumble off in the game's own options (with nxnative's Rumble left on) still crashes.

Both crashed sessions end the same way (`log.txt` and `log.prev.txt`, attached):

```
[dm] [RED] sf: the game connects to service hid itself, which the host does not serve
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=sdk+0x24254c lr=sdk+0x24254c sp=0x17440e850
[dm] bt: sdk+0x24c65c main+0x5d32d4 main+0x227fb4 main+0x6c76b4 main+0x67f60c main+0x614888 ...
```

With `sdis.py --sym` on the sdk image:

```
0x24254c _ZN2nn3hid6detail24IsVibrationDeviceMountedEPbRKNS0_21VibrationDeviceHandleE+0x3c
0x24c65c _ZN2nn3hid24IsVibrationDeviceMountedERKNS0_21VibrationDeviceHandleE+0x1c
```

So `nn::hid::IsVibrationDeviceMounted`, part of the SDK's vibration API behind HD Rumble (it asks whether a controller's vibration device is attached), called by the game at `main+0x5d32d4`, runs the SDK's own client: it connects to `hid` through sm, `h_sf_Connect` refuses it (0xe15), and the SDK reads a null service object. Of the four device-level vibration calls Odyssey imports (`GetVibrationDeviceHandles`, `InitializeVibrationDevice`, `SendVibrationValue`, `IsVibrationDeviceMounted`), it is the only one `hle_hid.c` doesn't take over. The game only reaches it when `GetVibrationDeviceHandles` returned handles, which is why nxnative's Rumble setting decides it and the in-game option doesn't. It is still missing on current `main` (51904e7). The symptom index has the related `VibrationNode::Update` entry (values flushed through `SendVibrationValues`), but nothing for this call.

Possible fix (untested: I build on GitHub Actions and haven't run it yet), answering as `GetVibrationDeviceInfo` does:

```diff
--- a/dm/host/hle_hid.c
+++ b/dm/host/hle_hid.c
@@ -813,6 +813,11 @@ HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn3hid23GetActualVibrationValueEPNS0_14VibrationValueERKNS0_21Vib
     uint32_t targets = h ? vib_targets(*h) : 0;
     *v = targets ? dm_haptics_actual(__builtin_ctz(targets), *h >> 16 & 1) : (dm_vibration){0, 160, 0, 320};
 }
+// Super Mario Odyssey 1.4.1 asks on entering a Sand Kingdom pipe (main+0x5d32d4); the SDK's own call reaches the hid service (sm refuses it, then a null read in
+// hid::detail::IsVibrationDeviceMounted, sdk+0x24254c). Mounted when the channel has an output, as GetVibrationDeviceInfo reports it
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn3hid24IsVibrationDeviceMountedERKNS0_21VibrationDeviceHandleE", "vibration: device mounted when the channel has an output", unsigned, h_hid_VibMounted, const uint32_t *h) {
+    return h && vib_targets(*h);
+}
```

## What you expected

The pipe loads, with rumble on.

## Game, title ID and version

Super Mario Odyssey, 0100000000010000, 1.4.1 (v393216), no DLC

e4292dded574

### What happened

Pokémon Legends: Arceus on the Mac crashes after 40–65 minutes of normal play, always at the same place: 3 crashes in 3 sessions on 2026-10-30, after 2626 s, 2441 s and 3890 s. The registers are the same each time:

```
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x118 pc=main+0x16e34fc lr=main+0x16e34ac
x0=0x315d718c0 x1=0 ... x8=0 ... x19=0x315d718c0 x20=0x42d05a6b0 x21=0x32a3d3e80 x22=0 x23=0x316acbf70
[dm] bt: main+0x19d244c main+0x1cd25e0 main+0x1cceda8 main+0xace34c main+0x1bd9e9c main+0x2968538 main+0x296d7c8 main+0x29497b4 sdk+0x349d98 sdk+0x3501d4 dm_thread_enter+0x18
```

The crashing thread is `JobThread2` (0x1003). No `[RED]` line comes before the crash.

What the code at the crash does (from a disassembly of the rewritten `main`):

- The function at `main+0x16e33ec` is called from `main+0x19d2448` with `w1 = [x21 + 0x7e4]` of the caller, which is 0 in all three crashes (`x22=0`).
- If `[this + 0x88]` is not null, it uses that object. If it is null, it stores 0 in a stack local (`main+0x16e341c`: `stur xzr, [x29, #-0x60]`), looks the ID up through a global manager (`[[global] + 0xd0] + 0x58`, vtable slot 0x50; the lookup returns an object, `x19=0x315d718c0`), and then reads `[local + 0x118]` at `main+0x16e34fc` with the local still 0.
- So every call that finds `[this + 0x88]` null crashes. On the console this path probably never runs, so I think something sets `+0x88` too late here (a timing or ordering difference), but I could not find out what.

The last inputs before the third crash were menu or dialogue input: Up and Down, B, then A every one or two seconds. The last A came 69 frames before the crash. The last frame took 1.2 ms of GPU time, so the screen was probably a menu or a dialogue box, not the open field.

I have the input recording of the third session (`DM_REC`, 7,145 steps over 65 minutes) and a copy of the save it started from. I can send them if they help; they are not attached here.

### What you expected

The game keeps running.

### Game, title ID and version

Pokémon Legends: Arceus, 01001F5010DFA000, base v0 + update 1.1.1 (v262144), no DLC. Both dumped from my own Switch; the NSP hashes match the ones I keep.

- Crash 3: `ee6648c` plus the same local commit (rebased).

The local commit changes only input in `dm/host/front_mac.m`: it maps the right stick to the keys P L ; ' and to a two-finger trackpad scroll, through the same `dm_input_set` call as a controller. The crash is in game code on a job thread, so I do not think it is the cause, but I have not played the same length of time without it.

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NSP folder> -k prod.keys --platform mac-app`, started as the Mac app. Keyboard and trackpad, no controller.

body:
## What happens

Opening **amiibo** in Hyrule Warriors: Definitive Edition terminates the Mac host instead of showing the game's NFC-unavailable message.

The game initializes `nn::nfc` separately from `nn::nfp`. Existing NFP hooks do not intercept `nn::nfc::Initialize`, so the original SDK code tries to connect to the unsupported `nfc:user` service. The recorded run reports the unserved service, then `Break#1`, and exits with code 42.

## How to reproduce

1. Launch Hyrule Warriors: Definitive Edition 1.0.1 (`0100AE00096EA000`).
2. Reach the title screen and open **amiibo** with the controller's R button.
3. The host aborts during NFC initialization.

## Expected behavior

Report NFC as unavailable through the SDK API so the game can show its existing message, dismiss it and return to the menu. Actual NFC hardware access and amiibo scanning are outside this fix.

## Proposed fix

[PR #711](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/711) handles `nn::nfc::Initialize`, `Finalize`, `GetState` and `IsNfcEnabled` in the host. It maintains library state and reports NFC disabled. With the fix applied, the unavailable-NFC dialog can be opened, dismissed and reopened without terminating the game.

## Environment and evidence

Mac mini M4, macOS 27.0.1; US game version 1.0.1, SDK 3.5.1.

- [Reproduction logs and screenshots](https://github.com/monoquark/nxnative/releases/download/hwde-compatibility-evidence/hwde-validation.zip): the NFC removal control records the `nfc:user` abort; the patched run records the unavailable dialog. Exact source revision and run settings are included in the bundle.
- [Validation logs and screenshots](https://github.com/monoquark/nxnative/releases/download/hwde-compatibility-evidence/hwde-fe6d3dfa-validation.zip): repeated dialog opening/dismissal with the fix, plus the focused NFC fixture and sanitizer results.

These links contain test evidence only; no game files, keys or saves are included.
title: Hyrule Warriors: Definitive Edition crashes when opening amiibo with NFC unavailable

body:
### Symptom

On an iPhone with a monitor or TV on a USB-C cable, the game is only mirrored: the phone's whole screen, touch controls included, is shown on the display, letterboxed on every side. A 16:9 game on a 16:9 TV does not fill the screen.

### Cause

The app declares an external display scene in `Info.plist` (`UIWindowSceneSessionRoleExternalDisplayNonInteractive`, `UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes`), but an app built with the iOS 27 SDK is offered that scene only after it registers a scene accessory (`registerSceneAccessory`); the manifest entry alone is ignored, so iOS falls back to mirroring.

### Fix (tested on an iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27, with a monitor on a USB-C cable; AirPlay not tested)

The change is in `dm/ios/Sources/main.m`, `dm/ios/Sources/front_ios.m` and `dm/ios/project.yml` (about 100 lines, on current main):

- The root view controller registers the scene accessory at launch; the `Info.plist` scene manifest (`External` configuration, `ExternalSceneDelegate`) and multiple-scene support stay for earlier systems.
- `application:configurationForConnectingSceneSession:` returns the `External` configuration for that role.
- `ExternalSceneDelegate` creates a window on the display's scene. The game's view (the same `CAMetalLayer`, no second renderer) and the frame-rate counter move into it, fitted 16:9 at the display's scale; the phone keeps the touch pad, black when a controller is connected.
- When the display goes, the view moves back to the phone.
- The log names each scene role, screen and move (`front end: scene connecting, role …`, `external display scene accessory registered …`).

Happy to open a PR with it if this direction is right.
title: iOS: on an external display the game is only mirrored (iOS 27 SDK needs a registered scene accessory)

body:
Six findings from reviewing the tree as synced into [LumaNX](https://github.com/Xc1Ym/LumaNX) (PR #29, synced 2026-10-30). Line numbers refer to that pinned tree; all six were verified by reading the code. One issue for all of them since each is small — happy to split if preferred.

## 1. `nvnCommandBufferDrawTexture` decodes the sampler ID from the full 64-bit handle

**Path:** `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`, `nvnCommandBufferDrawTexture`
**Finding:** `sid = (uint64_t)h >> 20` reads the whole 64-bit handle, missing the truncate-to-32-bit rule that `bind_handles` in the same file already implements for exactly this handle shape ("EA SPORTS FC 27 binds separate textures with bit 32 set (0x1000001d1): read whole, its sampler ID was 4096, beyond any pool").

```c
// nvnCommandBufferDrawTexture:
uint64_t tid = (uint64_t)h & 0xfffff, sid = (uint64_t)h >> 20;

// bind_handles, same file:
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) r->h[i] = (uint32_t)h[i];   // "the GPU never sees the upper half of the 64-bit handle"
```

**Evidence:** a DrawTexture handle with bit 32 set yields `sid = h>>20 ≥ 4096 (+samp_base)`, beyond any sampler pool — the recorded draw replays through the wrong sampler (Streets of Rage 4's movie-frame path draws this way). The fix is to decode both IDs from `(uint32_t)h`, mirroring `bind_handles`.

## 2. `bnd2_resources` inflates resources without error handling

**Path:** `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`, `bnd2_resources`
**Finding:** the per-resource `zlib.decompress(raw)` is unguarded, so one damaged resource raises `zlib.error` inside `scan_file_in` and the whole bundle is marked unreadable. For Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit Remastered's SHADERS.BNDL that drops all ~2,112 GLSLC outputs with one red line. `monolith_cmp_data` in the same file already handles this failure class per payload (`except zlib.error as e: red(...)`).

**Fix:** wrap the per-resource decompress in `try/except zlib.error`, note and skip that resource.

## 3. `cap_layout` fingerprint says `ops 52`, the assert requires 53

**Path:** `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_capture.c`, `cap_layout` (~line 33–37)
**Finding:** `_Static_assert(OP_COUNT_ == 53, ...)` sits directly above `cap_layout()`, but the fingerprint string returns `"format 1\nops 52\n"` — the count was bumped by one instead of two for `OP_DRAW_TEX` + `OP_ALPHA_REF`. Nothing breaks today (the walk compares the whole string), but the recorded capture metadata misstates the op count and invites drift on the next op.

## 4. `impl_sys_off` can cache 0 and lose both its cache and the struct offset

**Path:** `dm/host/hle_audren.c`, `impl_sys_off` (~line 416)
**Finding:** an `add x0, x0, #0` prologue decodes `imm12 = 0`, so `off` becomes 0 — which the `if (off) return off` cache check treats as unresolved. Every render then re-runs the scan and re-LOGs, and `render_once(impl + 0)` reads the wrong fields as the execution mode/device — the exact silent-audio failure the function comment's SDK 16/3.4 history describes.

**Fix:** skip `imm12 == 0` adds in the scan, or guard the static with a separate resolved flag.

## 5. `fetch_timed`'s `pthread_create` fallback has no time bound

**Path:** `dm/host/save_sync.c`, `fetch_timed` (~line 371)
**Finding:** when `pthread_create` fails (thread exhaustion at startup), the fallback runs `front_save_sync_fetch` synchronously on the calling thread with no limit — defeating FETCH_MS and the documented bound "a download iCloud never finishes must not hold the game at its first save mount".

**Fix:** return `-1` in that path (play on with this device's save, send later).

## 6. `fb_tick` aborts the instance-cache walk on a failed field read

**Path:** `dm/host/hle_fpslock.c`, `fb_tick` (~line 203)
**Finding:** the field-read guard uses `return` where the sibling guard on the line above uses `continue`:

```c
if (!rd(...cache word...) || !inst || !rd(inst + 8, &tinfo, ...) || tinfo != ti) continue;   // keep scanning
if (!rd(inst + fb.off_rate, &rate, ...) || !rd(inst + fb.off_max, &max, ...)) return;       // skips the remaining cache words
```

**Evidence:** cache word 0 naming a half-torn instance whose `ForceSimRate`/`MaxSimFps` pages fault the vm read, with the live instance in word 1: the simulation rate is not written that frame, nor any frame after while the stale word sorts first.

**Fix:** `continue`.
title: DrawTexture decodes the sampler ID from the full 64-bit handle (+5 smaller findings from LumaNX's sync review)


## Disassembly readout
`sdk+0x56e830` is the SDK's memset (fill byte in x1, count in x2). Entry sequence:
```
sdk+56e830  cbz   x2, #0x56e8f8
sdk+56e834  add   x8, x2, x0
sdk+56e838  cmp   x2, #3
sdk+56e83c  strb  w1, [x0]        <- crash (x0 == 0), sig 11/addr 0
```
The caller at `main+0x2037ef0..0x2037f00`:
```
main+0x2037ef0  ldr   x9, [x22]           ; x22 = object+0x2c8, the array's base pointer — returned 0
main+0x2037ef4  lsl   x2, x8, #1          ; length in bytes (uint16 array)
main+0x2037ef8  mov   w1, wzr
main+0x2037efc  add   x0, x9, x24, lsl #1 ; dest = base + count*2
main+0x2037f00  bl    #0x2930120          ; -> sdk memset
```
i.e. a `memset(collection.array + count*2, 0, len*2)` where the collection's backing array base is null while count x8 ≈ 0x1002001-ish is not — a buffer whose allocation the host never satisfied.
Related: `alias region mapped 1.01 GB (application pool 3.21 GB)` prints right before the crash, on the metagame's Nifm retry path; the provisional profile's `region`/`stdalloc_cap` geometry may not fit what the metagame allocates in its first PlayQuickRace load. `x19=0x7130d9e880` looks like a stack frame whose *x19 readback showed `0x800101`, then zeros.

## Attachments ready
A `scripts/bug_report.py` zip is generated for this exact crash (`nxnative-report-010083802449A000-2026-10-30.zip`, 68 KB, no game files). Say the word and I'll attach it here or on request via email.

I'll keep testing DM_PROBE / region introspection next (in this same issue) as I try to pin whether the null base is the region map order or a stdalloc_cap play.

body:
## Summary

Art of Rally (provisional profile, no upstream entry) builds and launches, but the game renders as **abstract shapes instead of the scene**. The host reports that the scene's render target is a compressed-format texture, which it refuses to attach, so the draws are lost:

```
[RED] render target is a compressed-format texture (Metal format 198 1857x1045 layers 1,
      view format change 0 → NVN 0): not attached; draws to this attachment are lost
[RED] no render target could get an MTLTexture
[RED] texture object invalid while recording (uninitialized or already finalized):
      0x701db03558 index 0, call site main+0x75b33c
```

Metal format 198 at 1857x1045 — a BC-compressed color format, i.e. the game is rendering into a compressed texture. Metal cannot attach a BC texture as a color attachment, so everything drawn there is dropped; the visible shapes are the passes that render elsewhere.

## Environment

- **Title** `0100A88012504000`, update `v458752` (the base XCI has no ticket and needed its ID in the filename).
- Build: `a31235713eee` chain, 48,683 shaders, 6.94 GB app, installed on iPad Pro 11" (M4).
- **No profile in `dm/games`** — provisional. Frame step is stable (`p50 33.33 ms`), the game runs; only rendering is wrong.

## Questions

- Is a compressed render target something the host should translate (decompress on first use / allocate a renderable stand-in and copy back), or does it indicate the attachment's format was misread from the NVN texture object?
- The same texture appears at the second red line as "texture object no longer valid (magic 0, first case ser=479)" — possibly the game creates it, renders into it, and frees it inside one frame; a lifetime issue rather than a format one.

Happy to run any instrumentation (`DM_NVN_POOLPEAK`, texture tracing) on this build and report back; it reproduces in seconds.
title: Art of Rally renders into a compressed-format render target (Metal format 198) — draws dropped

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] Metal device Apple M4 Pro
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline archive bundled with the app: this system cannot open /tmp/t_pso_bundle.ZG05Ga/bundle/applegpu_g16s.mtl4a
  (deployment target for architecture applegpu_g16s found in archive '…/applegpu_g16s.mtl4a' is not compatible with current OS;
  made for another system version, or an OS update changed the GPU compiler): the bases are built on the device
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline archive /tmp/t_pso_bundle.ZG05Ga/archive: 0 files (0 of bases without a vertex layout), 0.0 MB, opened in 0.1 ms
bundle: opened: expected 1, got 0
bundle: first among the files without a vertex layout: expected 1, got 0
```

The remaining eight failures all follow from that first one — with no bundled archive, every base is built on the device:

```
covered: one pair built on the device: expected 1, got 3
covered: its base compiled: expected 1, got 3
covered draw: its base from the bundle: expected 1, got 0
covered draw: none compiled: expected 0, got 1
covered draw: nothing captured for the device's archive: expected 0, got 1
other pairs: two bases from the bundle: expected 2, got 0
other pairs: one compiled: expected 1, got 3
probe: the bundled archive holds them: expected 1, got 0
```

## Cause

`dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py` defaults `--os-min` to the SDK's major version:

```python
def os_min_default(platform):
    v = subprocess.run(['xcrun', '-sdk', sdk(platform), '--show-sdk-version'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    return v.split('.')[0] + '.0'
```

With Xcode 27.1 that is **27.0**, so the archive is stamped for macOS 27.0 and macOS 26.6.2 refuses to open it. This is exactly the behaviour the tool documents at `dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py:25`:

> `--os-min`: the archives' minimum OS (default: the SDK's major version, e.g. 27.0; **a device on an older system cannot open them and builds the bases itself**)

So neither the tool nor `nvn_mtl.m` is misbehaving — the fallback at `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:5591` fires and reports it clearly. But `t_pso_bundle.m:99` asserts the archive opens, unconditionally:

```objc
EXPECT("bundle: opened", 1, g_arch_bundle != nil);
```

and it invokes `pso_offline.py` without `--os-min` (`t_pso_bundle.m:58-59`), so on macOS 26.x the archive it builds can never be opened by the machine that built it.

## Why CI does not see it

`.github/workflows/tests.yml` does not run the GPU tests ("GPU tests stay local"), and GitHub's `xcode-27` image is macOS 27, where SDK major and OS major agree. The failure only shows up on a developer's own Mac — the one place the README sends people to run these tests.

## Suggested fix

Either would do:

1. **Pass `--os-min` from the running OS in the test**, so the fixture is built for the machine that will open it. This keeps all 52 checks meaningful on macOS 26.x.
2. **Skip the GPU half gracefully when the SDK's major version exceeds the running OS's.** The test already has two such skips — no Metal compiler (`t_pso_bundle.m:46`) and no `metal-tt` (`t_pso_bundle.m:61`) — and a third in the same style would fit:

   ```
   t_pso_bundle: SDK 27.0 is newer than this system (26.6.2), the bundled archive cannot be opened here; GPU checks not run
   ```

Option 1 seems better: it tests the real path rather than skipping it. Option 2 is a one-liner if the fixture is meant to match what `build_ipa.sh` ships byte for byte.

## Related, and possibly the more interesting half

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py:2021` also calls `pso_offline.py` with no `--os-min` for the `mac-app` platform:

```python
cmd = [py, repo / 'dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py', '--game', g.id, '--msl', lib, '--out', out,
       '--work', work / 'pso/mac-work', '--gpu', arch, '--platform', 'macos']
```

If I read that right, a `mac-app` built on macOS 26.x with Xcode 27.1 ships a pipeline archive the same machine cannot open, and compiles every base on the GPU at first run — the long first-boot stutter the archive exists to avoid, silently, with only a log line to say so. For a Mac-only app whose target is the machine doing the build, taking `--os-min` from `sw_vers -productVersion` rather than the SDK would avoid that. (I have not run a full `mac-app` build — no game files here — so this part is inference from the code and from the test's identical failure, not something I have observed end to end.)

Happy to send a PR for whichever shape you prefer.
title: t_pso_bundle: 10 checks fail on macOS 26.x with Xcode 27.1 (archive stamped for the SDK's OS, 27.0, which the running system refuses)

Five retained iPhone crash reports from October 27–28, 2026 show iOS killing DmIOS during background suspension. One is for title ID `01007EF00011E000`, app/build version 1.9.0, and four are for `0100F2C0115B6000`, version 1.4.3. The reports identify iOS 27.2; the exact nxnative source commit and build settings are not established by these logs.

Every report has `EXC_CRASH / SIGKILL`, `FRONTBOARD 0x8BADF00D`, and a `scene-update` watchdog timeout of 10 seconds. The main thread waits in `__psynch_cvwait → _pthread_cond_wait → dm_gfx_suspend → -[_UISceneLifecycleMonitor didEnterBackground]`. Application CPU is only 0.328–0.430 seconds during the watchdog interval, which is consistent with waiting. This establishes a blocked suspend path, but not which render-thread condition failed to complete.

Investigate the condition-variable handshake in `dm_gfx_suspend` when UIKit backgrounds the scene. Reproduce on the affected build, capture the render-thread state, and confirm background/resume completes within the lifecycle budget after a fix. After loading my save, choosing to travel to The Somniel from the world overview screen crashes the game during the loading screen. It happens every time, including from a clean start (close the app, relaunch, load the save, go straight to The Somniel).

Crash line, identical in both attached logs:
CRASH sig=11 addr=0x1fffe0 pc=main+0x9a4664 lr=main+0x9a4658

In both crashes x8 = x22 = 0x200000 (a 2 MB pool request failed). Mapped alias memory was about 2.0 GB of the 2.5 GB application pool at the crash, so this looks like address-space fragmentation rather than exhausted memory. The alias region had already reached 4.26 of 4.38 GB early in the first run.

log.txt: crash at frame ~20,400, after an autosave and about 9 minutes of play.

body:
### What happened

Forwarded from LNPANDY/NX2Apple#204 (reported by @shikosu, who did most of the narrowing down). Two rendering defects, in every scene tried, every time.

**A. Hard-edged dark box in the lighting.** Mostly indoors and under decks. A region with sharp, world-space edges (a box seen in perspective) is much darker than the rest of the scene. Its shape stays the same at every time of day, and its darkness grows with the time of day. Elsewhere it shows as a lighter translucent rectangle.

**B. Stretched geometry streaks.** Long thin wedges from small objects and characters, a dotted streak across a staircase, characters stretching.

What narrows it down:
- `DM_NVN_HILITE=93d0e7a7c14cdfb0` (solid magenta) removes the box and keeps the streaks. That pixel shader is `shd_lgt.wishp` HCPS var4.3 (VS `468bd9c28161136f`), the indirect-lighting pass: four 2D textures, one cube-map array (slot 5), three uniform buffers. So A comes from that pass, and B does not.
- Weak lead: in a `DM_NVN_TEXINFO=64x64` run, 3 of the 21 64x64 cube-map arrays (serials 3379, 3386, 3393) hold far fewer non-zero bytes (2 to 4 KB against 20 to 32 KB).
- No visible change on A or B with `DM_NVN_LAZY_CLEAR=0`, `DM_NVN_CUT=0`, `DM_NVN_TBDR=1`, `DM_NVN_FB_SNAP=all` or `DM_NVN_DISPATCH_OWN=1`. `DM_NVN_CLEARLOG=1` logs nothing over about 9,900 frames.

Suspicions, not verified:
- A: the cube-map array lookup in the lighting shader (layer or face addressing for the probe of that volume), or the uniform data that selects the probe.
- B: vertex inputs. 256 vertex shaders use `gl_VertexIndex` with a dynamic uniform-array access and a `cb_extent.tsv` entry (e.g. `00717317b42d5543` slot 1: 528 B). An extent that is too small for a draw with many vertices would make the later vertices read zeros.

The reporter offered to run `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP`, `CBDUMP` / `CBDUMP_KEY`, `KEYDUMP=93d0e7a7c14cdfb0` or a GPU capture at the spot. Which one would help most?

### What you expected

The original look: no dark box, no streaks.

### Game, title ID and version

Xenoblade Chronicles 2, 0100E95004038000, 2.1.0 (v983040) and 3.0.1, same result on both

### nxnative commit

5d2bf73f (the pin of NX2Apple 0.6.0, built from NX2Apple d5b7823 with its fork patches: runtime-profile, bc-cpu-decode, touchpad-geometry and others, as listed in the original report. None of them changes the NVN translation on a Mac, but a check on a plain nxnative build is still open.)

body:
## What happens

Since 625a260 (#452), the Mario Kart 8 Deluxe build (0100152000022000, 4.0.0 + 4.0.1 + DLC, registered profile) stops at the shader split:

```
[RED] 28 file(s) could not be read, their shaders are left out (first: /UI/EUde/race.sarc/rc_L_Rank_00.szs/#7: the archive members add up to more than 16 times the file (members that overlap)); ...
```

The 28 files are the race and result layout archives (`rc_L_Rank_00.szs`, `tv_L_Rank_00.szs`, `rc_Page_RaceResult.szs`) in each language's UI archives, in both update versions. None of their members overlap.

## Why

`scan_blob` charges each member `len(d)` **after** Yaz0 decompression. `UI/EUde/race.sarc` is 203,690 bytes and holds one Yaz0 member: 203,562 bytes that expand 9.0 times, to 1,831,040 bytes. The budget therefore pays twice for the same decoded bytes:

- once for the member itself (9×);
- once more for its members (about 9×).

That adds up to 17.9 times the file. Counting the member by what it takes up in its archive, before Yaz0, gives 10.0 times, within the budget.

## Proposed fix

Charge a member its stored size and keep everything else as it is (patch below):

- **The budget base is unchanged.** It is still `NEST` times the file's decoded size, in line with the "count decoded bytes" note on the Sumo path in main.
- **The members of an expanded archive are still charged in decoded bytes.** They lie in the decoded data.

Overlap is still stopped:

- `corpus/shader_split/sarc-fanout.bin` still ends in the overlap `red()`.
- A compressed fan-out also ends there after fewer than 200 `scan_blob` calls (8^6 without a bound). In that fan-out every level is 8 members spanning one Yaz0 of the next level, padded to expand far.

One trade-off: the work bound becomes the Yaz0 ratio times what it was. Yaz0 packs at most about 90 times, so the work is still linear in the file, not exponential.

If you would rather keep decoded-byte charging, a per-archive overlap check would also work: the members of one archive must add up to at most that archive's data. It would stop fan-outs at the first level. I went with the smaller change.

## Checked

- **New test** `dm/tools/tests/test_split_nesting.py`, with 3 tests:
  - `test_compressed_member_is_not_overlap`: race.sarc's shape. It fails on main with the same red line as the game.
  - `test_overlapping_members_are_stopped`: the fan-out corpus input.
  - `test_compressed_overlapping_members_are_stopped`.
- **Existing tests:** `test_fuzz_corpus`, `test_split_unreadable` and the `dm/gfx/tests` shader_split tests pass (monolith, needle, pg_shader, gfpak, pkz, snowdrop, unity_*, vbf, ue3_cache, shader_split_progress).
- **Lint:** ruff 0.17.2 matches the baseline; pyright 1.1.414 reports 0 errors on the new file.
- **Where the patch applies:** both ac9598a and 393af57 (main). It touches the `NEST` comment and two lines in `scan_blob`.
- **Mario Kart 8 Deluxe with the fix:**
  - The shader split finished in 9:53 with 29,785 shaders and 0 unreadable files.
  - The app runs on an A20 Pro iPhone (iOS 27.2) at 60 fps through a full race.

## Patch

```diff
--- a/dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py
+++ b/dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py
@@ -2112,3 +2112,5 @@ def unity_text_glslc(x, base):
 NEST = 16   # archives in archives scan_blob opens (SARC, PlatinumGames' DAT): real files nest a few. A damaged or crafted one could nest one per header's length, or have every
-            # member point at the same inner archive, its work doubling with each level: the members a file's archives open may add up to at most NEST times the file
+            # member point at the same inner archive, its work doubling with each level: the members a file's archives open may add up to at most NEST times the file.
+            # A member counts what it takes up in its archive, before Yaz0: its expansion is not overlap (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's UI/<lang>/race.sarc, 204 KB, is one layout
+            # archive that expands 9 times, whose members then counted 18 times the file); the work stays within the Yaz0 ratio times that
 def scan_blob(d, label, out, depth=0, left=None):
@@ -2119,2 +2121,3 @@ def scan_blob(d, label, out, depth=0, left=None):
     for m in re.finditer(b'SLCT\x03\x10\0\0', d): out.extend(slct_shaders(d, m.start(), label))
+    stored = len(d)   # what the member takes up in its archive
     if d[:4] == b'Yaz0': d = yaz0(d, label)
@@ -2122,3 +2125,3 @@ def scan_blob(d, label, out, depth=0, left=None):
     else:
-        left[0] -= len(d)
+        left[0] -= stored
         if left[0] < 0: red(f'{label}: the archive members add up to more than {NEST} times the file (members that overlap)')
```

The new test file (74 lines) goes in the PR.
title: shader_split: the archive budget counts a Yaz0 member's expansion as overlap (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: 28 UI archives left out)

body:
## Goal

Keep game-specific code to the minimum. Every per-build patch has to be redone for each new game version (#375: Smash 13.0.1 lost its cuts). A general mechanism covers games and updates nobody has seen yet. This issue proposes rules for how general each patch must be, with a classification of every patch we have today ([docs/agents/game-patches.md](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/agents/game-patches.md)), and asks for input before the classes go into the patch files.

## Binding: what a patch depends on

A patch's **binding** is what its correctness is anchored to. From the loosest to the tightest:

| Binding | Anchored to | Found by | Survives |
|---|---|---|---|
| **host** | Horizon / NVN / Vulkan semantics | nothing in the binary | every game, every update |
| **sdk** | Nintendo SDK code (`sdk` module) | symbol, or a fingerprint per reviewed SDK implementation | any game shipping that SDK implementation |
| **engine** | middleware code: Unreal, Unity, Snowdrop, KTGL, sead, PhysX | registered name, string, or a fingerprint per engine version | any game on that engine version |
| **game** | the game's own code | function fingerprint (`MATCH_CUTS`) | the game's updates that keep the function |
| **build** | fixed offsets | NSO build ID | nothing: redone every update |

A second axis is the **purpose**: address space (an iPhone's ~6 GB), race (a race or timing problem the host exposes), frame rate / resolution (an enhancement), power.

## Rules (proposed)

1. **Bind a patch as loosely as the thing it depends on.** A patch is good design when its binding is the loosest that is correct. The gap between a patch's binding now and the loosest it could have is the work list.
2. **Mechanism general, decision in the profile.** Where only the decision is the game's (hold Unity's vSyncCount at 1, raise Unreal's t.MaxFPS), the code that finds the place is host / sdk / engine and the choice is a profile key. No per-game branch in the host.
3. **Discover once, in the rewriter.** Addresses found from the binary (names, strings, fingerprints) are found by `patch_nso.py` and passed to the host through the fixups. No fixed-address tables in `dm/host`.
4. **A build row is a starting point, not a destination.** A new `CUTS` row is fine for a bring-up; it should name the binding it can move to.
5. **Correct semantics are defaults.** A profile key that makes the host behave as Horizon or the GPU does is on for every game, after `regress.py check`. Keys stay per game only for real per-game data or decisions.
6. **No game's choice in a shared file.** `sdk_patches.py` holds fixes every game shipping that SDK build needs. A tuning one game needs goes in that game's profile.
7. **Remove what a general mechanism replaced**, after a boot check of the games that had it.
8. **Every patch states its binding**: now, the loosest it could have, purpose, why, and what was checked. This replaces the free-text `GENERALIZE` note, and `docs_patches.py` lists the gaps.

## Where each patch stands

The classification lives with the patches and is generated, so it cannot drift: each patch file's `BINDING` table, and `dm/tools/docs_patches.py` for the host's build-keyed rows, translator rules and profile switches. The page is [docs/agents/game-patches.md](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/agents/game-patches.md):

- [Binding](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/agents/game-patches.md#binding): the five classes, the statuses and the evidence kinds.
- [Gaps](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/agents/game-patches.md#gaps): every patch bound tighter than it could be, the loosest goals first. That is the work list.
- Each game's section: every one of its patches with its binding now, goal, purpose, status and evidence.

Status is computed: **at goal**, **gap**, **blocked** (with the reason it cannot close yet) or **kept** (left open on purpose, with the decision). Evidence is **checked** (what was checked on game files, and when) or **judgement**. `test_patches.py` fails when a patch file has no `BINDING` or when an entry's goal is tighter than its binding now, and the generator stops on any unclassified host row, translator rule or switch.

The page shows this once the change that adds `BINDING` is on `main`.

## Proposed order

1. Removals: Scarlet's cut, the dead NieR row, the SDK rows the rules reproduce.
2. Unreal discovery in the rewriter (cvars and allocator), replacing `k_locks`' Unreal rows, `k_ue` and the Unreal `CUTS`/`OBS`.
3. `BINDING` in every patch file; `docs_patches.py` lists the gaps.
4. Semantic profile keys to defaults, one at a time with `regress.py check`.
5. Function-matched rules (and a matched form of frame-step stubs) for the `game`-bound patches, as updates come.

## Input wanted

- Are these the right five bindings? Is anything missing, for example a separate **shader** binding for translator rules, or **data** for profile keys?
- Rule 3: should the host keep a runtime search (as `dm_ue_cvar` does now), or should all discovery move to the rewriter?
- Rule 5: which of the semantic keys has a reason to stay off by default that this list misses?
- The 2 MB alignment rows: an SDK-wide rule for those SDK implementations, or per-game choices?
- Frame-rate enhancements: should they stay `build`-bound on purpose, so that a game update never inherits a 60 fps change nobody checked?
title: Patch design: bind every patch as loosely as what it depends on (host, sdk, engine, game, build)

**What.** The iPhone Duo's inner screen is a tall, nearly 3:4 screen that people hold upright. Today the app shows up there as a landscape window scaled into the portrait screen. I would like to add, for that screen only (recognized by its shape, native size 0.7035 wide to tall, not an exact size):

1. A portrait layout: the game's picture centred in the top half, every on-screen control in the bottom half over a dark background image. New iOS setting "iPhone Duo portrait: game above the controls" (`DM_PORTRAIT_LAYOUT`, on by default), listed only on an iPhone Duo.
2. A "Gyro rotation" setting (`DM_PHONE_ROTATE`: Automatic, 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°) for a screen that sits turned against the body. Automatic adds nothing on iOS 27 and later (the iPhone Duo ships with iOS 27.1), where Core Motion already delivers the motion in the picture's frame (#569); on iOS 26 it adds one quarter turn on that screen in every orientation.

**Scope.** iOS front end only (`DmGamepad.m`, `front_ios.m`, `Launcher.swift`, `project.yml`), the present pass in `nvn_mtl.m` (the split, as fractions of the canvas height, only while the layout is on), the settings table and docs. No other iPhone and no iPad is affected: the app allows portrait only on the inner screen once the game runs; the settings screen and every other screen stay landscape. About 300 lines on top of two small PRs (control editor, bars around the picture), which it builds on.

**Why an issue.** The Duo is not in the supported-devices list in README.md. I understand device support is your call; the code is a small, shape-gated path that does nothing on any other screen. If you would rather not carry it, tell me and I keep it in my fork.

Tested on an iPhone Duo with Super Mario Galaxy: portrait, landscape and closed, gyro on Automatic in each.
title: iPhone Duo (foldable) inner screen: portrait layout and automatic gyro rotation

body:
### What happened

I'm trying to get LEGO® Star Wars™: The Skywalker Saga running on my Mac. There's no profile for it yet, so I built it with the provisional one. It opens a window, draws a couple of frames and then quits, every time:

```
[dm] Break#1 reason=0 Result=0 svc at sdk+0x397640
[dm] bt: sdk+0x1470d8 sdk+0x147238 sdk+0x33f454 sdk+0x4d9bc render_main+0x190 sdk+0x342188 sdk+0x348714 dm_thread_enter+0x18
launcher: the host exited with 42
```

It turned out to be the audio side, not graphics. The abort is `nn::os::SignalSystemEvent` (sdk+0x33f454), called from `nn::audio::ExecuteAudioRendererRendering` (sdk+0x4d9bc) on the host's audio render thread. The event it's given has 0 in its state byte at +0x28, so the SDK aborts.

From what I could see, the game opens the audio renderer with a `SystemEvent` that sits on its own stack (`main+0x58f9a34`, `OpenAudioRenderer(handle, sp+0x10, …)`) and then returns from that function. The game asks for the DSP device, and on the console that path leaves the handle's event word at 0 (sdk+0x4d2b4), so the event memory is never touched again. Under the host's CPU + manual rendering the SDK stores the event pointer in the handle instead (sdk+0x4d274), and the render thread later signals that stack slot after it's gone.

I checked this with two probes (`DM_PROBE=sdk:4d274@20,sdk:33f418@20`): the pointer stored at sdk+0x4d274 on the main thread (`0x173eb9af0`, right next to the parameter block on the same stack, called from `main+0x58f9a38`) is the same one `SignalSystemEvent` gets when it aborts.

Separately, almost none of the game's shaders were found (the shader split got 8, all pixel shaders from `main`), so I expect the picture to be the next problem.

### What you expected

The game to keep running past its first frames.

### Game, title ID and version

LEGO® Star Wars™: The Skywalker Saga, `010042D00D900000`, update v589824 (1.10.0) on top of the base game. NintendoSDK 12.3.6. Main build ID `ec593a5f9552100a9fe95c4ca9e34873`, sdk `26dfae95ca29ae3c49dfd84d69f8b7fd`. I have the DLC, but it isn't involved.

### nxnative commit

The copy vendored in NX2Apple (upstream 5d2bf73). The audio renderer event code looks the same in `main` today (32b12b4).

### Shader chain version

`373efc7add5f`

### How it was built and run

Built as a Mac app with the NX2Apple 0.6.0 launcher (the NSP script with a provisional profile) and started from the app.

### Device and OS

Mac16,13, Apple M4, 24 GB, macOS 27.0 (26A428)

### Settings and environment overrides

Defaults, no `env.txt`. The probe runs only added `DM_LAUNCHER=0` and `DM_PROBE`.

### Logs

The relevant lines are above. The full log of the crashing run (with the two probes) follows in a comment.

### No game files

- [x] Nothing attached here contains game files, keys or data extracted from a game.
title: LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga 1.10.0 on Mac (M4, mac-app): aborts in SignalSystemEvent on the audio render thread after two frames

body:
# MGS3 on M1 iPad: local bring-up findings

Sharing lessons from a locally modified d2r-mobile/Touchable runtime related to nxnative. This is an engineering experience report, not a ready-to-apply patch against current main or a claim that unmodified nxnative supports this game.

The player reports that our latest local build26 has no visible triangle-grid artifacts and broadly normal frame rate. Earlier versions had severe gameplay slowdown, black movie pictures, audio stutter and transition crashes. Full-game completion and sustained60FPS have not been established. The final visual result is a user observation, not a controlled experiment proving one root cause.

## Environment and scope

- Game: METAL GEAR SOLID3, version3.0.0, program ID `010047F01AA10001`.
- Original main Build ID: `278093478a0a4a591946b7eb33ed0ab1505fd10e000000000000000000000000`.
- Device: M1 iPad Pro11-inch, third generation, iPadOS27.2.
- Historical/custom build environment: Intel Mac, macOS15.8.2, Xcode26.2 / iPhoneOS SDK26.2. This differs from current upstream requirements. Native ARM64 gameplay and Metal4 were tested on iPad, not this Mac.
- Local d2r-mobile dependency: `2eb5758771f110cd53082b999d88d242766610da`, plus substantial local changes. This is not a tested nxnative main revision.
- Runtime modules: main, subsdk0, subsdk1, subsdk9, sdk; do not execute Switch rtld.
- Local shader-chain identifier: `0f2b873197f7`; runtime fragment variants also receive the transformation below.

No game code, extracted shaders, assets, keys, saves, signing material or raw device logs are attached.

## 1. CPU: count x18/far-branch traps before blaming the GPU

An early gameplay capture had a frame-time median near341ms while GPU time was near23ms. Late snapshots counted roughly430–450 thousand far traps per second. Raw M1-versus-Switch specifications did not explain this CPU-side overhead.

A separately signed executable prefix containing near thunks allowed eligible rewritten sites to use direct branches instead of repeatedly entering the far-trap path. Original module offsets and data/BSS layout stayed unchanged. The completed candidate covered7,517 static sites, including99 bounded two-exit conditional thunks; two indirect sites retained their old handling.

Checks that mattered:

1. Pin original Build IDs/hashes; never reuse fixed addresses across versions.
2. Compare registers, NZCV, SIMD, memory effects and return PCs, including both conditional outcomes.
3. Verify branch/ADRP reachability, disjoint thunk spans and removal of obsolete trap registrations.
4. Verify the executable-prefix mapping and actual embedded module bytes in the final iOS Mach-O.
5. Retain unsupported cases. Do not place thunks in apparently unused zero padding without proving it has no code/data/unwind references.

The first7,418 sites each passed three emulator fixtures. The99 additional conditional thunks passed6,534 execution comparisons. Fixtures verify instruction behavior, not arbitrary device pointers or whole-game correctness. Device testing then changed severe slowdown to playable movement. MGS3 alone also used Release-O2; other games were not globally switched.

## 2. Black movie output needs a decoder, not per-cutscene skips

The local runtime initially lacked a working `movie::Decoder`. Returning errors from unavailable NVIDIA driver calls could avoid a crash but could not produce video. Subtitles/sound over black output did not establish a generic scene-rendering failure.

The shared backend uses VideoToolbox for AVC and AudioToolbox for AAC, retaining the SDK demuxer and game clock/subtitle flow. An inventory found67 avc1 MP4s at1280x720,480x270,512x448 and128x96, with no embedded audio tracks identified. AAC is a backend capability, not evidence these MP4s contain AAC tracks.

Important details:

- Explicit slot ownership/backpressure; reject duplicate submissions/releases.
- Drain pending pictures before EOF; empty EOF must not overwrite the last valid texture with black.
- Stop/Configure permits resolution changes; Flush clears queues and requires Start.
- Validate NV12/RGBA format, stride and texture extent; signal client sync after output is visible.
- Preserve errors rather than returning successful black output.
- **AVC parser ambiguity:** length prefixes for256–511-byte NALs can resemble Annex-B start codes. Validate the complete length-prefixed stream before selecting Annex-B parsing. Two real clips failing at269/407-byte NALs passed after this correction.

Four real video sizes were checked in NV12/RGBA with presentation-order tests. Synthetic lifecycle/malformed-input tests supplemented real compressed-video tests; they did not substitute for iPad playback. No filename-specific cutscene bypass was used.

A separate failed-allocation cleanup crash dereferenced an unavailable nvdrv connection. Consistent rejection of Ioctl/Ioctl2/Ioctl3/Close/MapSharedMem without altering output buffers avoided continuing into a null driver vtable.

## 3. Scalar MSL optimization: preserve tested rounding boundaries

The final local candidate changes only the attributes of scalar `spvFMul(T l, T r)` and `spvFAdd(T l, T r)` helpers:

```diff
-[[clang::optnone]] T spvFMul(T l, T r)
+[[clang::noinline]] T spvFMul(T l, T r)
-[[clang::optnone]] T spvFAdd(T l, T r)
+[[clang::noinline]] T spvFAdd(T l, T r)
```

Bodies and matrix/vector helpers stay unchanged. This was opt-in for MGS3 runtime alpha-test fragment variants only, before the existing alpha-test transform, with `fastMathEnabled = NO`. It was not a global replacement across all shaders.

Always-inline was rejected:1,753 bitwise mismatches in262,144 finite-range synthetic outputs even with strict math. A volatile alternative restored equality but was slower. Keeping a noinline call boundary permitted body optimization while preserving the tested non-NaN results.

Validation:

-262,144 finite-range outputs: zero bitwise mismatches.
-262,144 broad bit-pattern/edge outputs with runtime compiler options: zero non-NaN and signed-zero mismatches;19 NaN payload differences classified separately. Not universal bitwise equivalence.
- Six observed fragment shaders compiled for iOS after the exact attribute-only change.
- Bounds/policy tests, alpha-test/sample-mask/position-invariance regressions and PSO-key separation checks passed.
- Synthetic Intel GPU runtime-options probe: median14.55ms before /5.45ms after. These are not iPad or whole-game timings.

Encode this policy in shader/PSO cache keys. Locally an existing byte became a bitset: bit0 position invariance, bit1 scalar policy. Vertex-function selection tests only bit0, not the entire byte as a boolean. A dedicated field also works. Reusing an old key for changed shader source invalidates comparison.

The player reported no grid in the final configuration, which also retained earlier interface/uniform fixes. A one-variable on-device comparison is still needed before assigning sole causality to scalar optimization.

## 4. Rendering findings and rejected shortcuts

- In six observed shader pairs, fragments read a vertex-varying W that was never written. Standalone translation lacked next-stage component information. Initializing declared varyings to reference defaults `(0,0,0,1)` before explicit writes recovered missing textures, but triangle seams remained at that stage. Not the complete grid fix.
- Isolating uniform snapshots from tile-batching policy with a local `DM_NVN_UBV=1` override gave limited improvement; grid remained in that intermediate trial. This switch describes our local implementation, not guaranteed upstream behavior.
- Grid-affected draws showed fill mode2,2xMSAA, GEQUAL depth and Depth32Float_Stencil8. Blanket depth-write disable, relaxed depth tests and forced sample masks were not accepted as fixes.
- Copy/render encoder transitions must maintain GPU resource-alias visibility; CPU copy completion alone is insufficient evidence.

## 5. FPS unlock and measurement

A separate build-specific60FPS patch was matched against the exact original Build ID and expected instruction sites. It was separate from CPU/GPU optimization.60Hz display settings or handheld/docked mode alone do not establish60FPS game updates. No third-party patch archive or game instruction payload is redistributed here.

After CPU improvements/unlock, player feedback still put heavy scenes near9–15FPS. Heavy captures showed approximately2,400–2,700 draws/frame, replay CPU around5–6ms and GPU medians above the16.67ms budget. That motivated investigating GPU/shader cost instead of assuming CPU traps remained the only bottleneck.

- Window FPS = completed frames / actual elapsed time; `1000/p50(frame_ms)` is not average FPS.
- Report p50/p95 and long frames; separate menus/movies/gameplay or label unknown scenes.
- Exclude background/suspension gaps. A trace containing only compositor/another app is not a game profile.
-60Hz missed refreshes are not automatically missed30FPS game updates.
- An FPS unlock, a brief60FPS interval and sustained60FPS gameplay are different claims.

The latest player result is encouraging: no visible grid, broadly normal performance. Quantified sustained60FPS, thermal runs, full-game stability and a minimal patch rebased onto current nxnative remain unverified. These notes share mechanisms and failed approaches rather than proposing wholesale import of an old fork.

body:
### What happened

**DRAGON QUEST XI S 1.0.4 freezes with corrupted graphics during startup on an iPad mini 7 (A17 Pro) when Frame buffering is enabled. Disabling only Frame buffering allows entering the game.** The same installed IPA and external RomFS were retained throughout; no reinstall, save reset or cache clearing was performed.

The paired 30 fps logs contain identical launcher values except `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1` versus `0`. The successful run reaches more than 5,400 frames, with no GPU command-buffer error or snapshot timeout in the captured log. This is one successful user-tested workaround, not a long-term stability or artifact-free gameplay claim. The pipeline registry was larger on the later run, so this was not a randomized cold-cache experiment.

| Run | Frame buffering | FPS target | Encode thread | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Failed A | on (`1`) | 60 | on (`1`) | Startup freeze/corruption; GPU submissions subsequently ignored |
| Failed B | on (`1`) | 30 | off (`0`) | Same GPU errors; snapshot-copy timeout |
| Successful comparison | off (`0`) | 30 | off (`0`) | User can enter the game; log reaches 5,400+ frames; no GPU submission errors |

To reproduce the reported sequence: install the DQ11 IPA and matching separate image, enable **Frame buffering**, start the game and observe the early freeze/corruption; relaunch with **Frame buffering off**, leaving the other settings unchanged. The failure appeared in both preserved on-runs. The exact number of attempts outside these captured runs is not known.

### What you expected

Enabling the optional Frame buffering setting should not corrupt the initial frames or leave GPU submissions unusable. For now, leaving it off is a verified way past this startup failure on this device.

### Game, title ID and version

DRAGON QUEST XI S: Echoes of an Elusive Age – Definitive Edition, `01006C300E9F0000`, update **1.0.4 / v262144** over base v0, five DLCs (indices 21–25).

### nxnative commit

Built on 2026-10-29 from `beea17cfdbd8fe6112de9d1c191c0488da7970bf` plus local touch-control, localization and packaging changes. This is **not an unmodified current-main build**. No local NVN replay or shader-chain source changes were applied to the installed IPA. The DQ11 `game.tsv` is byte-identical to official main `f78eec796ff180b8453f41c7864df4be2be572a0` inspected during diagnosis. The local packaging helper also scopes `SDKROOT` to the Mac helper build; it does not alter the iOS graphics path.

### Shader chain version

`b-fda42ce035db`; runtime shader input stamp `0c05695f9241`. Runtime accepts the stamp and loads a 38,892-entry shader map. Xcode 27.1 and the locked translator/compiler checks were used, with no mismatch bypass.

### How it was built and run

Unsigned universal IPA from `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`, subsequently device-signed and installed. `--romfs separate --keep-extracted --package v262144 --language zh-Hans`. `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` was verified in the executable signature and device provisioning profile. The normal DQ11 virtual memory layout and `-SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=4064` were retained. Both failing logs mount the image (111 entries) and all five DLCs successfully.

### Device and OS

**iPad mini 7 (A17 Pro), model `iPad16,1`, iPadOS 26.7.1 (23H30).** I understand the README names M-series iPads as its tested iPad scope; this report does not assume that iPad mini 7 is already validated upstream.

### Settings and environment overrides

No `Documents/env.txt`. Paired failed/successful 30 fps runs:

```text
DM_FPS_TARGET=30
DM_OPMODE=1
DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE=off
DM_LANG=zh-Hans
DM_SHOW_FPS=1
DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS=0
DM_RUMBLE=0
DM_RUMBLE_GAIN=1.0
DM_RUMBLE_MIN=0
DM_PRESENT_SNAP=1   # failing run; 0 in successful run
DM_PSO_MTL4=0
DM_PSO_PREBUILD=0
DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=0
DM_FPS_HOLD=on
DM_METAL_HUD=0
```

The switch `DM_PSO_MTL4=0` changes pipeline creation, not the use of the Metal 4 command queue.

### Logs

Complete privacy-redacted application logs for both failed runs and the successful comparison, diagnostic summary and uninstalled source-only candidate:

[DQ11-iPad-mini7-frame-buffering-diagnostics-20261029.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34133175/DQ11-iPad-mini7-frame-buffering-diagnostics-20261029.zip)

Archive SHA-256: `da5fd68a9af1813d7cfed7fe8cc486b61de0b5098ed1d1b1f2535ff16019eae1`. No game content is included.

The failing runs report, from the first displayed frames:

```text
[RED] display command buffer error: Error Domain=MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=1
  MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=5
  Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)
  (00000004:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored)
[RED] present snapshots: the previous copy into a ring slot did not finish within 2 s
```

Upload, segment and display command buffers then continue failing. **`SubmissionsIgnored` is a consequence; these logs do not expose the original GPU fault.** Three system reports terminate under `FRONTBOARD`, `0x8BADF00D`, with main-thread stacks in `dm_gfx_suspend` / `mtl_drain` (scene-update or process-exit watchdog). They do not report Jetsam or a per-process memory-limit termination.

With Frame buffering off, the log instead reaches:

```text
[dm] [nvn] timing up to frame 5400: frame time p50 33.34 / p95 34.01 / max 69.04 ms (300 frames); ... GPU p50 22.81 / p95 29.49 / max 33.34 ms (300 frames)
[dm] [nvn] on-screen up to frame 5400: 300 frames, dropped 0 (discarded 0), p99 33.34 ms; footprint 2502 MiB; ... thermal 0
```

### Possible mechanism — not a confirmed fix

In the built [`snap_take`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/beea17cfdbd8fe6112de9d1c191c0488da7970bf/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m#L11016), `tex_mtl(t)` can resolve a new source allocation into the main residency set, but the copy is committed after committing only the separate snapshot-destination set, without calling `res_commit()` for the source first. `present_now` does call `res_commit()`, but it runs after the snapshot copy has already been queued. This resembles the project's [documented first-present residency failure](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/f78eec796ff180b8453f41c7864df4be2be572a0/docs/reference/rendering.md#the-residency-set-committed-before-a-present). The inspected latest source also retains this snapshot gap.

A one-call `res_commit()` candidate immediately after resolving the source is included for discussion, **not installed or validated on the iPad**. A local Apple M4 harness confirms that the original leaves the source-residency set dirty while the candidate commits it; however, both versions complete the copy and return correct pixels on M4, with shared and private storage and both encoder-thread settings. That test does **not** reproduce the iPad GPU failure and does not prove this candidate fixes it. Feedback on the earliest snapshot/initialization submission would help identify the original fault.

### Separate residual rendering warning

The successful Frame-buffering-off run still has texture-type fallback warnings, so they should not be presented as the proven cause of the startup freeze:

```text
[RED] texture buffer (... 5 elements of format 0x2f at pool offset 41680) has no 2D-row form for a wrapped 1D fetch: the slot reads 0
[RED] texture type mismatch: shader 75ce37340dc04b55_b (stage 5) declares slot 0 as Metal type 2, ... type 9 (NVN target 10, format 0x2f, Metal format 123, ... 16 past the linear-texture alignment); a buffer texture: the slot reads 0 (dummy)
[RED] texture type mismatch: shader ceaa7713a39eae47_b (stage 0) declares slot 0 as Metal type 2, ... type 9 (NVN target 10, format 0x16, Metal format 105, 8192 elements at pool offset 168656, 16 past the linear-texture alignment); a buffer texture: the slot reads 0 (dummy)
```

I have not isolated their visible effect; they may deserve a separate issue once investigated.

### No game files

- [x] This report and its diagnostic archive contain no game files, keys, extracted NSOs, RomFS, shader code, saves, device profiles or credentials. Full logs retain their sequence; private local paths, app-container UUIDs, signing/device identifiers and any logged keyboard input are redacted.
title: DQ11 1.0.4 on iPad mini 7: Frame buffering causes startup freeze/corruption; disabling it boots

body:
When `DM_ROMFS` names a path that does not exist, the host logs `fs mount rom: → <path> (read-only)` and continues. `mount_ex` in `dm/host/hle_fs.c` does not check the path. The game then fails to read its files and crashes later, far from the cause.

Found on Echoes of Wisdom 1.1.0 (Mac): an old run command still pointed at `extract/v196608/RomFS` after a rebuild replaced the folder with `RomFS.img` (#369). The result was `CRASH sig=11 addr=0x88 pc=main+0x16c46d4` about 0.3 s after `nnMain`.

Proposal: stop at mount with a clear error when the `rom` path is neither a folder nor an image file.
title: Host mounts a missing DM_ROMFS without an error; the game crashes later

body:
Another data point on the ProMotion fullscreen late-present problem, plus a separate bug in the `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY` workaround itself.

**Short version:** `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` removes the problem completely here, where frame latency 2 does not. And `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY=3` cannot do anything, because macOS clamps `CAMetalDisplayLink.preferredFrameLatency` to 2 — which also makes `link_sync` rewrite and re-log the property on every frame.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Mac | MacBook Pro `Mac15,9`, Apple M3 Max, 48 GB |
| Screen | built-in Liquid Retina XDR, 3456x2234, **120.00 Hz** (ProMotion) |
| macOS | 26.6.2 (25G83) |
| Xcode | 27.1, `Apple metal version 32023.921 (metalfe-32023.921.6)` (matches `dmsh_chain.lock`) |
| nxnative | commit `123e3b4` |
| Game | Mario Kart 8 Deluxe `0100152000022000`, packed from v1507328 (4.0.1) with a **derived** profile (no v1441792 in the folder) |
| Build | `--platform mac-app` |

This is the game and screen class that [#348](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/issues/348) covers, and `docs/reference/frame-rate.md` lists "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on the M4 with latency 2" under **Not checked**.

## Symptom

In true fullscreen, with the Metal HUD reporting **Direct** presentation, the game sits around 40 fps with visibly unstable frame times. In a window, where the HUD reports **Composited**, it holds a flat 60.

Metal HUD at the moment of the switch out of Direct:

```
M3 Max   3456x2168                 Composited
Metal: 1.32GB            App: 3.44GB
Game Mode                         Off
FPS                             41.26
GPU                            3.26ms
Frame Interval                 24.24ms
```

GPU time is 3.26 ms against a 16.67 ms budget, so this is not a load ceiling. 24.24 ms is consistent with the mechanism already described in `frame-rate.md` — on-time frames at 16.7 ms mixed with skipped-tick frames at 33 ms average out near 25 ms, i.e. alternating 60 and 30 rather than a steady 40.

(Game Mode reads `Off` because it was disabled by hand for an unrelated test; the app's `LSApplicationCategoryType` is `public.app-category.racing-games` and Game Mode engages normally otherwise.)

## Finding 1 — `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` resolves it

```
DM_PRESENT_LINK=0
```

Fullscreen on the 120 Hz ProMotion panel then holds a stable 60 fps, with the HUD still reporting **Direct**. No screen-rate change, no window mode, no added input lag.

With the link off the log contains no `display link:` lines at all, confirming the object is never created rather than reconfigured.

This looks untried for this issue. The writeup's **Note** records `DM_PRESENT_LINK=2` (a 120 Hz link, still 102–209 late presents per ~9,600) and the **Fix** records frame latency 2, but `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` — the classic path where the present thread acquires its own drawable — is not mentioned. Since every documented symptom here is *the link* skipping a tick, removing the link removes the symptom.

`nvn_mtl.m:388` notes "no difference from 0 at a steady 60", which matches what I see: nothing was given up at this frame rate.

Whether this generalises to games that lean on link pacing under load, I can't say — it was tested on one game that has plenty of headroom.

## Finding 2 — `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY` above 2 is silently clamped, and spins

`DM_PRESENT_LATENCY=3` is accepted and reaches the property. The log shows it applied:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link: frame latency 3 (DM_PRESENT_LATENCY; frame 2769)
```

But macOS caps `preferredFrameLatency` at 2, so the write never sticks. Minimal repro:

```objc
// clang -fobjc-arc -framework Foundation -framework QuartzCore -framework Metal
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
#import <QuartzCore/QuartzCore.h>
#import <QuartzCore/CAMetalDisplayLink.h>
#import <Metal/Metal.h>
int main(void) { @autoreleasepool {
    CAMetalLayer *layer = [CAMetalLayer layer];
    layer.device = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice();
    CAMetalDisplayLink *link = [[CAMetalDisplayLink alloc] initWithMetalLayer:layer];
    printf("default = %g\n", (double)link.preferredFrameLatency);
    for (int v = 1; v <= 5; v++) {
        link.preferredFrameLatency = (float)v;
        printf("set %d -> readback %g\n", v, (double)link.preferredFrameLatency);
    }
} return 0; }
```

On macOS 26.6.2 / M3 Max:

```
default = 2
set 1 -> readback 1
set 2 -> readback 2
set 3 -> readback 2
set 4 -> readback 2
set 5 -> readback 2
```

Two consequences:

**It is a no-op.** Fullscreen already uses latency 2 via `link_latency()`, so `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY=3` and above change nothing while appearing in the log as though they applied. Anyone following the workaround in `frame-rate.md` and reaching for a larger value gets a silent dead end.

**It rewrites and re-logs every frame.** `link_sync` guards on a readback comparison (`nvn_mtl.m:10901`):

```c
int lat = link_latency();
if (lk && lk.preferredFrameLatency != lat) { lk.preferredFrameLatency = lat; MLOG("display link: frame latency %d (%s; frame %llu)", ...); }
```

With the target clamped the condition is permanently true, so every frame performs a redundant property write and emits a log line. In one short run I measured **2,783 `frame latency` lines across 2,783 frames**, in a 327,602-byte log. It grows without bound for the length of the session.

(That log has since rotated out on my machine, but `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY=3` plus `grep -c "frame latency"` reproduces it in seconds.)

Setting `preferredFrameLatency` on every frame may also perturb the link's own scheduling, so the flag could plausibly be slightly *worse* than leaving the default — I did not try to measure that.

### Suggested fix

Clamp on read, so the comparison is against a value that can actually hold:

```c
if (latency && atoi(latency) > 0) g_present_latency = atoi(latency) > 2 ? 2 : atoi(latency);
```

Or compare against what stuck rather than what was asked for, and warn once when a requested value cannot be applied. Either way the per-frame write and the log storm go away, and the docs could note the ceiling of 2 where `DM_PRESENT_LATENCY` is described.

## Suggested docs change

If `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` holds up on other machines, it's worth adding to the §"Frame latency 2 for the display link in fullscreen" workaround list — it's cheaper than switching the screen rate and costs no input lag, unlike latency 2.

## Not checked

- Other games, and games with less GPU headroom than this one.
- Whether `DM_PRESENT_LINK=0` regresses anything under load, where link pacing is said to even out frame intervals.
- External screens, and entering/leaving fullscreen while running.
- Whether latency 2 alone (the default) would have been enough here — the comparison I ran was link-on (latency clamped to 2) against link-off.
title: MK8D - ProMotion fullscreen late-present problem

### What is missing

On iOS, game rumble goes to exactly one place. If a controller is connected, it goes to the controller only. The phone's haptic engine is used only when no controller is connected([`haptics_apple.m`, `configure`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/2e07a8803d6b2a6ea2d163080328710e6ffc7993/dm/host/haptics_apple.m#L366-L371)):

```
#if TARGET_OS_IPHONE
    else if (!p && phoneSupported) {
        add_engine(p, -1, @"phone", ...);
    }
#endif
```

So with a controller that has no haptics support on iOS, or one whose haptics iOS doesn't expose, there is no rumble at all, on either the phone or the controller.

### What you propose

### Use case

- Playing with the phone mounted on a controller or held close, where the phone's Taptic Engine adds feel even when the controller rumbles too.

### Possible approaches (just ideas)

- A launcher setting such as **Rumble output: Controller / Phone / Auto**, with the current behavior as the default.
- Or, more minimal: fall back to the phone when the connected controller reports no haptic localities.
- An `env.txt` switch only (for example `DM_PHONE_RUMBLE=1`) would also be fine for me if a UI setting isn't wanted.

For reference, I drafted a local patch that adds the phone engine next to the controller channels for player 1. It also re-adds it in the `fallback` / `merge` paths, and `DM_PHONE_RUMBLE=0` turns it off. `apply()` already iterates over every channel, so the change looked small. I have not compiled or tested it on a device yet, so please treat it only as a sketch. I'm happy to share it, or open a PR if you'd prefer that.

I can test builds on an iPhone 16 Pro with Monster Hunter Rise (0100B04011742000) once I have my build set up.

If this is out of scope or conflicts with plans for the haptics code, no problem at all. Thanks for considering it.

iPhone
