body:
### What is missing

A `--romfs separate` iOS build expects `Documents/romfs.img`, but the builder produces its source as `extract/<version>/RomFS.img`. The official `scripts/push_romfs.sh` copies it to the correct lowercase destination. A manual copy through Finder/Files into a LiveContainer guest retains the capitalized source name, and the app reports that no game image exists even when the full image is in the guest's Documents folder.

Observed with South Park: The Fractured But Whole 1.05 (`01008F2005154000`) on an iPhone 15 Pro Max running iOS 27.0.1. The guest had `Documents/RomFS.img` at the expected 18,209,832,114 bytes. Its log said `game files not found (Documents/romfs.img, Documents/romfs or <App>/romfs)` and reported the image missing. After renaming that same file in place to `Documents/romfs.img`, the user confirmed the game launched and played successfully.

### What I propose

In `dm/ios/Sources/main.m`, accept `Documents/RomFS.img` as an alternate image filename for manual transfers. Prefer `Documents/romfs.img` when both are valid, and apply the existing complete-image and `romfs.id` identity checks to whichever candidate is selected. Include the alternate in backup exclusion and diagnostics. This can stay a narrow filename fallback; the builder's `RomFS.img` extraction path and the official `push_romfs.sh` destination can remain as they are.

### Platforms

iPhone and iPad (iOS/iPadOS separate-RomFS builds).
title: iOS: accept RomFS.img in Documents after a manual separate-RomFS transfer

body:
Undertale 1.11 gets through extraction and code rewriting, but the provisional build fails during OpenGL shader translation. The preceding Mac shader-capture run also stops on an unserved `audout:u` request. No IPA was produced.

### Game and build

- Undertale, title ID `010080B00AD66000`, display version **1.11**, update package reported as `v1`; base NSP plus update NSP, no mods or DLC.
- No registered profile; the script generated a provisional profile and selected `main subsdk1 sdk`, omitting `subsdk0` (NintendoSDK_OpenGL).
- Survey reports SDK 4 and OpenGL. The generic console message mentions LÖVE/Balatro as an example; that is not an engine identification for Undertale.
- Main build ID: `24db41fcd513d080b4a3bfe4a0e46cf3`
- SDK build ID: `d95547528dcd684e2813ec83d338a472`
- nxnative commit: `9093aea5af2450199c8836ea61c65a4c89362c1b` (branch with touch-control settings, based on upstream `40ddca1`; not tested against current main).
- Shader chain header: `3d5af9d36e1e`; this failure uses `gl_shaders.py`, not the NVN translation path.
- Apple M4, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Python 3.12, glslang 16.6.0.
- Target: unsigned iOS IPA. The capture step ran on the Mac; no iPhone test took place.

### Reproduction

Put the base and 1.11 update NSPs in one folder, then run:

```sh
J=8 python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py /path/to/Undertale \
  --keys /path/to/prod.keys \
  --out /path/to/Undertale/Undertale.ipa \
  --gpu none --progress lines
```

The recorded run used a wrapper that suppressed writing `survey.md` and changed the survey-report reference to “console output.” It did not alter extraction, the generated profile, shader translation or host behaviour. No custom environment file or gameplay overrides were supplied.

Expected: a best-effort IPA, or a diagnostic identifying the missing compatibility support. Observed in this attempt: extraction succeeds (222 files, 171.5 MB), rewriting succeeds, capture exits 42 after about one second, and translation fails before packaging.

### 1. Shader translation

Capture wrote **48 distinct shaders: 24 vertex and 24 fragment**. None has an explicit `#version` directive. All 48 fail with:

```text
ERROR: #version: ES shaders for SPIR-V require version 310 or higher
ERROR: Linking vertex stage: Missing entry point: Each stage requires one entry point
```

The corresponding fragment errors name the fragment stage. `gl_shaders.py` then invokes `metallib` with no input AIR files and raises `CalledProcessError`:

```text
metallib: error: no input files
```

Code observation, not a verified fix: `translate()` takes `r.stdout[r.stdout.find('#version'):]` after preprocessing. With no directive, `find()` returns `-1`, so this appears to discard the preprocessed source. Handling sources without a version directive needs investigation; simply inserting a version has not been tested and may expose further syntax or reflection issues.

### 2. Audio request during capture

The Mac host stops after shader creation with:


body:
### What is missing

A16 and older iPhones (iPhone 14 Pro / Pro Max, 15 / 15 Plus) report `supportsBCTextureCompression` NO. #4 showed the cost of that: the host stores every BC texture decompressed, at 2 to 8 times the size, and Breath of the Wild is killed for memory even with `increased-memory-limit`. I know A16 is outside the supported devices and that #4 was closed as out of scope. I am not asking you to support it. I am asking whether an opt-in path that leaves texture memory as it is would be acceptable upstream, or whether it should stay in a fork.

### What you propose

BC2, BC3, BC5, BC6H and BC7 take 16 bytes per 4x4 block, the same as ASTC 4x4, and each block stands alone. A build-time tool can therefore re-encode each block **where it lies** in a copy of the RomFS. Sizes, offsets and block-linear addresses stay the same, so the game reads its files unchanged. The host then creates those textures as ASTC 4x4 LDR / sRGB behind a switch, and texture memory is the same as on a device with BC.

- **Encoder:** Xcode's TextureConverter (decodes BC, encodes ASTC 4x4 with ARM astcenc, quality Normal, alpha kept), with results cached by hash. A second implementation uses Apple's texture encoder (libate) instead.
- **Host:** a format remap behind a switch (`DM_NVN_BC3_ASTC` for NVN, `DM_VK_BC7_ASTC` for Vulkan) plus the sRGB view pair. That is about 10 to 15 lines per graphics API.
- **Per engine:** each engine packs its textures differently, so the tool needs one reader per container format, the same way `shader_split.py` has one per archive.

What I have:

| Game | API, format | Branch | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hades `0100535012974000` | Vulkan, BC7 in Supergiant packages (610 of 671 textures) | [`hades-bc7-astc`](https://github.com/son17112001/nxnative/tree/hades-bc7-astc) (`pkg_astc.py`, `--bc7-astc`, on current `main`; PR #571). A second implementation using libate is on [`a16-bc7-astc`](https://github.com/son17112001/nxnative/tree/a16-bc7-astc) | on the Mac it draws correctly with the re-encoded textures; about 0.1 s per 2048×2048, PSNR 49 dB |
| Frostpunk Demo `0100193028708000` | NVN, BC3 / DXT5 in Liquid Engine `textures-s3.dat` (3,402 of 3,585) | [`frostpunk-bringup`](https://github.com/son17112001/nxnative/tree/frostpunk-bringup) (`liquid_astc.py`, `--bc3-astc`) | 3,402 textures in about 110 s on an M4; on the Mac it looks as with BC3 |

On an A16 iPhone: Hades built with `--bc7-astc` plays on an iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16). Frostpunk Demo has not been run on a device yet.

Limits:
- BC1 and BC4 use 8-byte blocks, so they cannot be re-encoded in place: ASTC 4x4 needs 16 bytes per block.
- Textures the game encodes on the GPU, such as Breath of the Wild's BC4 in #4, are not covered.
- ASTC 4x4 is lossy on top of BC.
- Each engine needs its own container reader.

Would you take any of this, for example only the host switches with the tools kept outside the repository, or should it stay in a fork?

### Platforms

iPhone (A16 and older)

body:
### What happened

I packed the Japanese release of The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles. It isn't the registered title (`010036E00FB20000`), so the NSP script made a provisional profile. Its `main` build differs from the Western release's (`d871b992…` vs `1da748fc…`); `sdk` (`d9add76f…`) and `subsdk0` (`84e50460…`) are the same builds.

**1. Black screen with the provisional profile.** The frame loop ran at 30 fps but the screen stayed black (`packaged textures: first uploads 0`). Copying these keys from `dm/games/010036E00FB20000/game.tsv` into the provisional `game.tsv` fixed it:

```
tex_flush_upload	on
tex_dirty_upload	on
depth_mode	zero
romfs_marker	nativeNXx64/sa/NX_64/root.arc
```

(The provisional `romfs_marker` was `nativeNXx64/movie/GO/CREDIT.mp4`.) Could the Japanese release be a derived profile of `010036E00FB20000`?

**2. Court-record pictures black, or showing the previous item.** With those keys, evidence and profile pictures in the court record were often black: a thumbnail sometimes came back, but the enlarged picture stayed black. After a first local change they appeared, but moving through the court record could show the previous item's picture. The autopsy report's slot and its enlarged picture showed the school badge, while the name and description were the autopsy report's.

What I found (Mac, `DM_NVN_TEXINFO=256x256`, `DM_NVN_DIRTYCHECK=1`):
- They are 256x256, 512x512 and 2048x2048 textures of format `0x42` with no packaged layout, in a `CPU_CACHED | GPU_CACHED | COMPRESSIBLE` pool (flags `0xa4`). At first use `TEXINFO` showed `swizzled=0` with 31,800 of 32,768 bytes non-zero, and the dirty check reported no missed writes. The Western release's note describes texels copied after `nvnTextureInitialize`; these images are written **before** `nvnTextureInitialize`, with no flush. `tex_dirty_upload` stamps a texture at registration, so it never sees those writes, and the texture stayed a GPU texture of zeros.
- For the next item, the game writes the new image into the same storage and **builds a new texture object over it** with the same description. The storage-sharing table (`g_alias`: pool, offset, description) then hands back the earlier GPU texture, which still holds the previous picture.

**Local change** (`tgaa-jp-court-record-textures.diff` in the attached zip, on top of `062cd06`). It sits behind an environment switch (`DM_TEX_CACHED_FILL=1` in the app's `env.txt`), because I can only test this game:
- In `tex_mtl_`, before the GPU-texture path: a texture that `ft_add` registered, in a `CPU_CACHED` pool, of a compressed format (so not a render target), with no layout, and whose storage holds data at its first use, is marked CPU-written (`mtl_tex_cpu_written`). It then takes the packaged path: it is uploaded from its storage and re-uploaded when its pages change, and a new object over the same storage gets its own upload instead of the shared texture.
- In `tex_init_fill`: a first version that filled such textures once from their storage. The change above mostly supersedes it.

Result: on the Mac the court record's pictures are right, also when moving back and forth. The log has `CPU_CACHED texture written before its first use …` (8 lines, its limit) and no `[RED]` line or `dirty-page miss`. The IPA with the change installs and runs on the iPhone.

A general fix would probably count storage that already holds data at first use as CPU-written content, at least for compressed formats, without the switch. I haven't checked other games, or whether the Western release shows the court-record problem.

The game draws its screen with the profile the NSP script makes, and the court record's evidence and profile pictures match the selected item, as on the Switch.

### What is missing

On iPhone the app is landscape only, with the touch controls drawn over the picture. On the iPhone Duo's inner display (unfolded, roughly 7:10 when held upright), landscape leaves large black bars, and the controls still cover the game. Held upright, the screen has room for a full-width 16:9 picture with the controls below it. The Duo's fold appears to run across the middle of the upright screen, so the picture can stay clear of it when the phone is half folded.

### What you propose

An opt-in launcher setting, off by default, so nothing changes for anyone who leaves it alone:

- `DM_PORTRAIT` (Controls → "Portrait layout", iOS only, one row in dm/games/settings.tsv). When it is on, the app also accepts portrait once the game starts (`application:supportedInterfaceOrientationsForWindow:` in main.m and the root view controller). The settings screen stays in landscape, and Info.plist is unchanged.
- Held upright: the picture fills the width of the top half, centred vertically in it. The existing 2D / 3D touch controls are laid out in the bottom half with the same code as in landscape. Their unit is limited by the area's width as well as its height, and they are drawn slightly stronger because they sit on black. Only touches on the picture reach the game's touch screen.
- `DM_PORTRAIT_INSET` (env.txt, 0–25, default 6): moves the controls in from the sides and the bottom by that percentage of their area.
- In landscape, everything is laid out as before.

The change is about 100 lines, mostly in front_ios.m and DmGamepad.m (one shared function gives the picture rect and the controls' area), plus docs/settings.md and docs/env_switches.tsv. env_switches.py --check and the launcher settings tests pass.

Tested on an iPhone Duo (iOS 27.2), built and run with Xcode from 3950976, with Rhythm Heaven Groove: upright and landscape, with the setting on and off.

Known limit: upside-down portrait does not rotate on the Duo's inner display, even with every orientation allowed in the app and in Info.plist. Apple's "Prepare your app for iPhone Duo" tech talk says the inner display doesn't honor an app's supported interface orientations, so this looks like system behaviour. Rotating the view manually on UIDevice orientation changes didn't help either, so the layout stays at all orientations except upside down.

Related: I couldn't find an existing issue or PR for a portrait layout. #482 (iPhone Duo iOS shell items) doesn't touch the in-game layout. #433, #500 and #258 also change DmGamepad.m, so I'd rebase onto whichever lands first. #433's DM_TOUCH_EDGE is similar in spirit to DM_PORTRAIT_INSET, and I'm happy to merge the two ideas if you prefer.

The code was written with help from an AI assistant (Claude) and tested by me on the device. I have a branch ready and can open a PR if this scope looks right to you.

### Platforms

iPhone (opt-in; tested on iPhone Duo)
title: Portrait layout for iPhone: picture in the top half, touch controls in the bottom half

body:
### What happened

Entering 2-player mode the first time after launch hangs the game on its 2P screen: the picture stops, the music keeps playing, and neither controller (nor L+R) does anything. The game window stays frontmost and key the whole time, and the hang lasts indefinitely (50+ s in the attached run). **Clicking another window and then back on the game unsticks it immediately**, every time. Leaving 2P and entering again in the same session does not hang. Single-player is fine. Happens every launch.

Two DualShock 4 controllers over Bluetooth, both connected from launch (`controller 'DUALSHOCK 4 …' connected: player 1 (npad 0)` / `player 2 (npad 1)`).

The attached log (`.prev.log` of the run at 09:42) shows it:

- From about frame 1900 the game draws the same screen: 161 draws per frame at 60 fps, nothing loading, no pipeline or texture work, the guest main thread waiting on vsync as usual. No focus change is logged during that time (the game stays InFocus).
- Lines 546–551, the only focus change in the run: I made another app frontmost for a second and then the game again.
  ```
  [dm] oe focus state → 2
  [dm] oe notification popped by the game: 15
  [dm] oe focus state → 1
  [dm] oe notification popped by the game: 15
  ```
- In the next window (frame 5100) the game moves on (178, then 315 draws per frame: the 2P character select), and plays normally from there.

The game sets `oe::SetFocusHandlingMode 2` (focus notifications).

### Likely cause (my guess, not traced)

On a Switch, picking 2P opens the controller applet (`hid::ShowControllerSupport`). While it is up, the application goes OutOfFocus, and when it closes, the application gets InFocus back, with notification 15 each time. The host answers `ShowControllerSupport` at once (`h_hid_ShowCtrl` / `h_hid_ShowCtrl0` in `dm/host/hle_hid.c`) without that focus round trip, so Mario Kart seems to wait for a focus notification that never comes, until the window really loses and regains focus. That would also explain why the second entry does not hang, if the game only shows the applet once.

I have not confirmed with a trace that `ShowControllerSupport` is the call made at that point. A fix could be for the controller applet HLE to do what `hle_oe.c`'s resume path already does (`dm_focus_set(2); dm_focus_set(1);`) around its answer, so a game that waits for the applet's focus notifications sees them.

Workaround for players: when 2P hangs, click another window and then back on the game.

### What you expected

2P character select appears right after picking 2P, as on a Switch.

### Game, title ID and version

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, 0100152000022000, update 4.0.1 (v1507328), Booster Course DLC (add-on content 1)

ce99604 (the controller applet code in `hle_hid.c` is the same on current `main`)

### What is missing
My copy of Age of Calamity (`01002B00111A2000`) is v327680, same as the profile, but it shows 1.4.1 and `main` is a different build:

- profile: 1.3.0, main `c3cf52bf2b05d7310884971b50bcccb8`
- mine: 1.4.1, main `e5f275b5d0889899e55de1a164eef060`

`subsdk0` and `sdk` are the same. Because `main` isn't registered, the 60 fps frame step doesn't get applied.

### What you propose
I ported the frame step to this build. The patched instructions are identical, only the addresses moved:

| | 1.3.0 | 1.4.1 |
|---|---|---|
| device config | `0x8d94b0` | `0x8d9ae0` |
| task fps | `0x166dab4` | `0x1670124` |
| object step | `0x166dc60` | `0x16702d0` |
| frame-rate block | `0x269e150` | `0x26a2280` |
| device pointer | `0x2bac798` | `0x2bb0798` |
| 59.94 constant | `0x1ef5f3c` | `0x1ef8ddc` |

`frame_step` now takes the address table, and `FRAME_STEP` has an entry for the new build. The output for 1.3.0 is the same as before (I compared all 69 emitted words). On 1.4.1 it runs at 60 fps on my Mac, and battles run at normal speed.

<details><summary>diff</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/dm/games/01002B00111A2000/patches.py b/dm/games/01002B00111A2000/patches.py
index e961542..1ed1aee 100644
--- a/dm/games/01002B00111A2000/patches.py
+++ b/dm/games/01002B00111A2000/patches.py
@@ -14,9 +14,16 @@ from nso_asm import ADRP, B
 # together. With only the task's wait at 1/60 s the game clock ran at twice real time; with the clock fixed and the block left at 30, battles still ran at twice (Link covered
 # twice the ground in a 3 s stick hold; enemy waves came early). Off (target 0), the device frame rate follows the game's fps (29.97 at 30, as with interval 2) and the steps and
 # the block stay the game's. x16, x17, s16–s18 and the flags are dead at both sites; the function uses no x16 / x17
-def frame_step(ctx):
+# The same three stubs on 1.4.1 (main e5f275b5…): every replaced instruction and register is unchanged; the code moved +0x2670 (config +0x630), the frame-rate block +0x4130,
+# the device pointer +0x4000 and the 59.94 constant +0x2ea0 (found by the replaced words, the block's {30, 2, 30, 30.0} and the device's +0x32d0 / +0x2aa4 users)
+addr_130 = dict(cfg=0x8d94b0, fps=0x166dab4, step=0x166dc60, block=0x269e150, dev=0x2bac798, hz=0x1ef5f3c)
+addr_141 = dict(cfg=0x8d9ae0, fps=0x1670124, step=0x16702d0, block=0x26a2280, dev=0x2bb0798, hz=0x1ef8ddc)
+def ldst(op, a, rn, rt): return op | (a & 0xfff) // 4 << 10 | rn << 5 | rt   # str/ldr w or s, [xN, #page offset of a]
+def frame_step_at(A):
+    return lambda ctx: frame_step(ctx, A)
+def frame_step(ctx, A=addr_130):
     here, emit, fs_site, fs_put, FS_STATE_OFF = ctx.here, ctx.emit, ctx.site, ctx.put, ctx.state
-    fs_site(0x166dab4, '68734339'); fs_site(0x166dc60, 'e83640b9'); fs_site(0x8d94b0, '4900c0f2')
+    fs_site(A['fps'], '68734339'); fs_site(A['step'], 'e83640b9'); fs_site(A['cfg'], '4900c0f2')
     # nnMain builds KTGL's device config on its stack and inits the device once (main+0x8d94c4 → main+0x17c34f0): {1920, 1080, 3, 9, 5, interval 2, 9, …}. The device keeps the
     # interval (main+0x17c4ba8 → device +0x2aa4, passed to every present at main+0x17ced78, which sets it on the window when it changes) and its frame rate, 59.94 / interval
     # (main+0x17c37c8 → device +0x32d0). Interval 1 above a 30 fps cap (the engine's own 60 fps mode), else the game's 2. x16, x17 and the flags are dead up to the init call
@@ -27,8 +34,8 @@ def frame_step(ctx):
               0x5400006d,   # b.le two (+3)
               0xf2c00029):  # movk x9,#0x1,lsl #32   interval 1
         emit(w)
-    emit(B(here(), 0x8d94b4)); emit(0xf2c00049); emit(B(here(), 0x8d94b4))   # two: movk x9,#0x2,lsl #32 (the original)
-    fs_put(0x8d94b0, [B(0x8d94b0, start)], 'KTGL device config present interval: 1 above a 30 fps cap, else the game\'s 2 (state page target fps)')
+    emit(B(here(), A['cfg'] + 4)); emit(0xf2c00049); emit(B(here(), A['cfg'] + 4))   # two: movk x9,#0x2,lsl #32 (the original)
+    fs_put(A['cfg'], [B(A['cfg'], start)], 'KTGL device config present interval: 1 above a 30 fps cap, else the game\'s 2 (state page target fps)')
     start = here(); emit(ADRP(16, here(), FS_STATE_OFF))
     for w in (0xbd400210,   # ldr s16,[x16]          target fps (0 = off)
               0x1e202208,   # fcmp s16,#0.0
@@ -39,12 +46,12 @@ def frame_step(ctx):
               0x1ac80a31,   # udiv w17,w17,w8        vsyncs per update
               0xb9002a11):  # str w17,[x16,#0x28]    this update's vsyncs (on)
         emit(w)
-    emit(ADRP(16, here(), 0x269e150))
-    for w in (0xb9015208,   # str w8,[x16,#0x150]    the game's frame-rate block: fps
-              0xb9015611,   # str w17,[x16,#0x154]   interval
-              0xb9015a08,   # str w8,[x16,#0x158]    fps
+    emit(ADRP(16, here(), A['block']))
+    for w in (ldst(0xb9000000, A['block'], 16, 8),        # str w8,[x16,#0x150]    the game's frame-rate block: fps
+              ldst(0xb9000000, A['block'] + 4, 16, 17),   # str w17,[x16,#0x154]   interval
+              ldst(0xb9000000, A['block'] + 8, 16, 8),    # str w8,[x16,#0x158]    fps
```

body:
### What happened

With `DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:300` the Mac host aborted about six minutes into Tears of the Kingdom:

```
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSInvalidArgumentException', reason: '-[AGXG16XFamilyComputeContext_mtlnext writeTimestampWithGranularity:afterStage:intoHeap:atIndex:]: unrecognized selector sent to instance 0x786417caa0'
[dm] CRASH sig=6 ...
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 ... objc_exception_throw+0x1c0 -[NSObject(NSObject) __retain_OA]+0 ___forwarding___+0x5e0 __forwarding_prep_0___+0x60 up_flush+0x74 pkg_upload+0x...
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

The selector is the render encoder's timestamp method, sent to a Metal 4 compute encoder.

**Cause (from reading `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m` at d0b7c84):** every encoder end goes through `m4_end` (line 780), which calls `gp_end(e)` for any encoder, including the upload queue's compute encoder that `up_flush` ends. `gp_end` does not check which encoder it was given: it takes the label of the profiled encoder currently open on the main command buffer (`g_gp_cur`, set by `gp_begin` at 827 for a draw pass) and, for a kind `'R'` label, sends `writeTimestampWithGranularity:afterStage:intoHeap:atIndex:` (line 851) to `e`. When `up_flush` runs while a profiled draw pass is open (a texture upload landing in a profiled frame), `e` is the upload compute encoder and the call throws. It needs an upload in one of the profiled frames, so three 200 s runs survived and the fourth did not. The same label leak means that even when the kinds happen to match, the draw pass's end stamp is written by the wrong encoder, so that pass's GPU time is wrong in the profile.

**Suggested fix:** remember the encoder in `gp_begin` (a `static id g_gp_e`) and have `gp_end` return at once when `e != g_gp_e`, so old-queue encoders (upload, diagnostics, present) never touch the open label. A one-line guard; `gp_end` already returns for `g_gp_cur < 0` (line 847).

### What you expected

The profile to leave other queues' encoders alone, or the profiled pass's end stamp to be skipped when another encoder ends in between.

### Game, title ID and version

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, `0100F2C0115B6000`, 1.4.3 (v720896)

### nxnative commit

The engine of the NX2Apple fork's sync of upstream 75065df (the profiler code is unchanged at d0b7c84: `m4_end` 780, `gp_begin` 827, `gp_end` 847–852).

### Shader chain version

b-157e1b96c8da

### How it was built and run

`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac-app` (NSP script), run as the Mac app from Finder.

### Device and OS

MacBook Pro 14-inch, M4 Pro (20-core GPU), macOS 27.0.1, Metal 4.

### Settings and environment overrides

`DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:300`, `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1`, `DM_PRESENT_LINK=2`, `DM_FULLSCREEN=1`, `DM_FPS_HOLD=off`, `DM_METAL_HUD=1`, `DM_THRCPU=<path>,5`. Two earlier runs with the profiler and the encoding thread off, and one with both on, ran 190–200 s without the crash; the fourth run crashed at about frame 23,000.

### Logs

The exception, the host's `CRASH` block and thread dump are quoted above; the whole 790 KB log is available on request.

body:
### What happened

Building Luigi's Mansion 3 as an unsigned IPA with `--romfs separate` completed successfully, but the NSP builder printed this red error after packing:

```text
[RED] the extraction holds a RomFS folder, not an image: this build carries no identity for it, and push_romfs.sh packs the folder first (delete extract/ and build again for an image)
```

The generated `RomFS.img` was a regular file. The IPA included `Payload/DmIOS.app/romfs.id`, and its recorded identity matched the generated image. The output also included the `push_romfs.sh` command pointing to that image. The warning therefore gives the user incorrect recovery instructions despite a successful build.

### What I expected

When `--romfs separate` produces an image file with a matching `romfs.id`, the script should print the transfer command without a `[RED]` warning. The warning should remain for a real legacy RomFS directory, if that case still needs special handling.

### Game, title ID and version

Luigi's Mansion 3, `0100DCA0064A6000`, update 1.4.0 (`v327680`), with Multiplayer Pack 1 and 2.

### nxnative commit

Built with `af3e391`. The same `image.is_dir()` check remains in current upstream `75f63ab`.

### Shader chain version

`beaff5e82328`.

### How it was built and run

iPhone/iPad unsigned IPA using `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --romfs separate -p v327680`. The build completed successfully; it was not installed or run on an iPhone.

### Device and OS

Apple M6 Mac, macOS 27.0.1 (build host).

### Settings and environment overrides

`--romfs separate`; Python 3.15; Xcode 27.1 / Metal toolchain 27.1. No game runtime overrides.

### Logs

Relevant final output:

```text
[6/8] iOS shaders: 5,317 of 5,317 shaders ready
[8/8] IPA pack: ... 521.4 MB
done: ... (0.5 GB)
the game files are not in this build. Copy them to the phone once ...
  scripts/push_romfs.sh <device UDID> org.nxnative.0100dca0064a6000 "<generated RomFS.img>"
[RED] the extraction holds a RomFS folder, not an image: this build carries no identity for it ...
```

The image's file size and index identity matched the `romfs.id` embedded in the IPA. No game files, keys, or extracted game data are attached.

### Reproduction and likely cause

On the build above, this check reproduced the mismatch:

```text
romfs.Path(image).is_dir()       -> True
pathlib.Path(image).is_dir()     -> False
pathlib.Path(image).is_file()    -> True
```

`say_push_romfs()` calls `image.is_dir()` on the custom `dm/tools/romfs.Path`. That path API reports directories inside the virtual RomFS image, so the image root is seen as a virtual directory even though its backing path is a regular image file. The check needs to inspect the backing filesystem path (for example, with `pathlib.Path(image).is_dir()`) instead of the virtual RomFS path API.

Relevant code: [`say_push_romfs`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/75f63ab/scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py#L2013) and [`romfs.Path`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/75f63ab/dm/tools/romfs.py#L219).
title: [Bug] --romfs separate emits a false RED warning for RomFS.img

## Smash 13.0.5 on iPhone: opening-movie audio decoded but not heard (video plays, audio silent until a blip at the title)

**Device**: iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 27.2), Increased Memory Limit
**Build**: Smash 13.0.5 (v2031616, registered build), packed with base + update + the 99 DLC licence NSPs

**Steps**: cold launch → the opening movie plays (video smooth at 60 fps) → **no audio during the movie** (silent switch off, volume up, `AVAudioSessionCategorySoloAmbient` set successfully) → a brief blip near the title screen → menu click sounds play normally from there.

**From the app's `log.txt`** (same session):

```
[dm] [movie] GetOutputBuffer index 10 → 1382400 bytes
[dm] [movie] Stop
[dm] [movie] decoder … destroyed: 4276 packets in, 4268 frames out; decoded 4267 packets, average 6.05 ms per packet, longest 38.08 ms
[dm] [movie] decoder … destroyed: 8024 packets in, 6106 frames out; decoded 8020 packets, average 0.10 ms per packet, longest 6.43 ms
[dm] audio #0 device callbacks 32000: 240–240 frames each, 5.0 blocks queued on average at callback; in these 2000, 0 underruns, 0.0 ms zero-padded
```

So the movie's two decoders ran to completion (video ~6 ms/packet, audio ~0.10 ms/packet, thousands of frames out), the AudioUnit callback path was live the whole time with zero underruns — and the game's own audio (menu click) is audible. The movie's decoded audio appears not to reach the mix during playback.

**Ask**: is Smash's opening-movie audio expected to mix through the movie path on iOS, or is the movie's audio track routed differently for this title (the game note lists the opening movie among the Mac-tested steps)? Glad to capture a longer log segment around the movie (and a Mac-vs-iPhone comparison) if that helps pin where the samples stop being mixed.

*(Filed alongside #503 — same session, different mechanism: that one is the main-menu SIGSEGV when packed without the DLC licences.)*

### Game, title ID and version Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2, 0100CC00102B4000, 1.0.3 (v196608) ### Engine and graphics API, if known Unreal Engine 4 (pak version 8), NVN, Wwise ### Survey and what happened Built as a Mac app (`--platform mac-app`, provisional profile) with NX2Apple 0.5.0 on 27 Oct, base cartridge dump (Europe) + update 1.0.3 (v196608), DLC included. **It boots and runs, but the window stays black.** The log shows the game alive: Unreal's GameThread / RHIThread / RenderThread running, audio rendering with no underruns, a steady 30 fps (frame time p50 33.4 ms), the Xbox controller detected. But 157 `[RED] shader … is not in the shader map` lines (155 distinct shaders), plus `program has no vertex shader (or it is not mapped)` and `the dispatched program has no compute shader`. **Likely cause: the paks are version 8.** The shader split found only the 32 shaders inside `main` (`shaders: 32 (compute 8, pixel 22, vertex 2); sources main 32`), none from the 45 paks in `Base/Content/Paks`. The footer of `pakchunk0-Switch.pak` reads **version 8**, index not encrypted. As far as I can tell, `uepak.py` handles version 11 (4.26+) and the legacy version 4 (DRAGON QUEST XI S), so the Unreal 4.22–4.25 era paks of this game are not read, and the material shaders never reach the shader map. A version 8 reader would probably help other Unreal games from 2019–2021 too.

body:
Asking about scope before proposing this as a PR, as CONTRIBUTING.md says for a change of this size. I should be straight about the order: it is already written and tested locally, about 800 lines, so this issue is as much "is this wanted at all, and in this shape" as "may I start".

## What is missing

A save made on one device stays on it. Saves live in `Documents/save`, so moving progress between an iPhone and an iPad means copying a folder by hand through the Files app, and a reinstall that lands in a new data container loses it unless the player thought to copy `save/` first (README already warns about that).

## What you propose

One `CKRecord` per game in the player's private CloudKit database, holding one snapshot of its committed save trees. It is general to every title rather than written for one, because the host already has the one place that knows a save was published.

**Where it hooks in.** `fs::Commit` already clones the working directory and swaps it atomically with the committed one. It gains one call, `front_save_committed(dir)`, once per published tree, after the mount and path locks are released, and never for a refused transaction, which keeps calling `front_save_failed` alone. Weak default in `hle_fs.c` as `front_save_failed` has, so the Mac host and the tests are unaffected.

**What a snapshot is.** `$DM_SAVE` and, for a game that mounts both, `<$DM_SAVE>_device`, with the title ID and a SHA-256 over the whole tree. The working trees beside them stay out. One subtlety worth naming: a commit swaps a tree atomically underneath a walk, so a snapshot that spans one is neither version — `dm_fs_commit_count()` is read before and after the walk and the snapshot is retaken if it moved.

**How a sync decides.** Three digests — this device's, the last both sides acknowledged, and the record's — giving equal / empty / upload / download / conflict. A poll reads the digest alone; the snapshot itself is fetched only to restore it or to keep it as a conflict. Uploads use `CKRecordSaveIfServerRecordUnchanged`, so a device that saved first wins and the other re-decides instead of overwriting. When both moved on, neither version is dropped: both are written to `Documents/iCloudSync` and the player chooses at the next start.

**When a restore may happen.** Only before the host mounts anything, guarded twice. The tree being replaced is copied to `Documents/iCloudSync/Backups` first.

**Turning it on.** `--icloud-container iCloud.<id>` at prepare time writes the identifier into the Info.plist and the iCloud keys beside the memory limit in the entitlements. Without it nothing reaches the network and saves stay on the device, exactly as today.

## The reason this may not be wanted

The container is an entitlement, so this only works for someone building with their own Apple developer account through `--prepare-xcode`. An unsigned IPA cannot have it, and that is how most people install. So the feature would serve the Xcode path only — which may be too narrow to be worth the surface it adds to the host, the iOS app and the packing script. That is the scope question I am actually asking.

## What is not covered

No testing against a real CloudKit container: there was no second device to hand, so the network paths — account check, fetch, upload with its compare-and-swap — are verified by compilation only. The Mac app has no sync. Nothing is differential: a whole snapshot per commit, refused above 64 MB. The conflict choice is a native alert before the game starts rather than part of the settings screen, because Swift and Objective-C only meet through `@_cdecl` here and the settings screen would have meant changing `dm_show_launcher`'s signature.

What is checked: the snapshot codec, its validation and its atomic restore run on macOS with synthetic saves (9 cases, including a record whose digest is correct but whose path escapes the save directories, and a symbolic link refused rather than skipped); `t_fs_commit_list.c` gains three checks that exactly the published transactions are reported; the full host suite, the iOS compile check and the packing tests pass.

Happy to push the branch somewhere you can read it, or to drop it entirely if the answer is that the Xcode-only reach makes it the wrong trade.

## Platforms

iPhone, iPad (the Xcode-signed path only)
title: iCloud save sync, one record per game, driven by the host's save commit
Interesting

Found by fuzzing with synthetic inputs (the harnesses and their corpus are in #455). The files are the player's own, so this is robustness, not security: a damaged or truncated file should stop with a clear `[RED]` line, not with a traceback, a wrong result or gigabytes of allocation. Each case has a tiny input in `dm/tools/fuzz/corpus/` that reproduces it.

- [ ] **Runaway recursion:** in `scan_blob`, a SARC member that spans the whole archive is scanned as itself until `RecursionError`, copying the archive at every level, about 1000 copies (`corpus/shader_split/sarc-self.bin`). This gets past `scan_file`'s catch-all.
- [ ] **Readers raise raw exceptions instead of `red()`** on truncated or out-of-range data: `mshd_shaders`, `bnsh_shaders` (pointers unchecked), `sdf_shaders`, `glslc_shaders`, `tfxo_shaders`, `bahs_*`, `sarc_members`, `yaz0` (stream cut short), `arh_entries` (non-ASCII path suffix), and `scan_blob` (a BNSH magic within 0x20 bytes of a file's end). `scan_file`'s catch-all turns them into an "unreadable" line, but one that names no cause.

*Possible fix:* a depth limit (or a "member is the whole archive" check) in `scan_blob`, and bounds checks in the readers that `red()` with the file and offset.
title: shader_split: runaway recursion on a self-containing SARC, and readers that raise instead of red() (fuzzing)

The files are the player's own, so this is robustness, not security: a damaged or truncated file should stop with a clear `[RED]` line, not with a traceback, a wrong result or gigabytes of allocation. Each case has a tiny input in `dm/tools/fuzz/corpus/` that reproduces it.

- [ ] **Huge allocation from the header:** `nso_image` allocates the image the header lays out, up to 8 GiB, from a 256-byte file (`corpus/nso/huge-segment.nso`). The same loader is copied in `uepak.nso_image`, `dm/tools/nso.py`, `patch_nso.py` and `nso_code.py`.

*Possible fix:* one shared NSO loader that checks each segment's offset and size against the file and against a sane image size before allocating, and that fails on a short segment. The five copies then go away.
title: NSO loaders: an 8 GiB allocation from a 256-byte file, and a silently short image (fuzzing)

`dm/ios/tests/test_launcher_storage.py` fails now and then on GitHub's runners, in the Mac settings window's layout check (`launcher_layout_check.swift`, from 1e207fa / d919b4b):

```
FAIL native Form fits its measured height (advanced=true, width=560.0, height=1282.0)
launcher storage: 1 failed
```

**Evidence that it's timing, not code:**
- #412 ([run 40547943819](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/actions/runs/40547943819)) and #439 ([run 40548065262](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/actions/runs/40548065262)) failed in Tool tests with this line. Neither PR touches the launcher or its tests.
- #443 and #386, on the same `main` base, passed.
- Pushing #412 and #439 again with identical content (only a new commit date): both green.
- Locally (Apple silicon, many cores) it passes every time, also with ten busy loops running beside it.

**Likely cause:** `measure()` gives SwiftUI a fixed `RunLoop.current.run(until: Date().addingTimeInterval(0.05))` after each layout change, and then reads the `fit` callback's `extra`. On a 3-vCPU runner, 50 ms isn't always enough for the grouped `Form` to finish measuring after Advanced opens, so `extra` is still the old value.

**Possible fix:** run the loop in small steps until `extra` stops changing (for example three 10 ms steps in a row with the same value), with an upper bound of a second or two, instead of one fixed 50 ms. The check stays as strict; it only waits for the layout to settle. I can't reproduce the failure locally, so I'd rather leave the fix to someone who can watch it on a runner, or I can open a PR and let CI show it over a few runs.
title: test_launcher_storage: the Mac window's layout check is flaky on CI (fixed 50 ms waits)

Environment: Pokémon Violet (01008F6008C5E000) update 3.0.1 (v720896), app built with `--platform mac-app` from a provisional profile
(Mac only: 20 GB guest block, `mem_reserve 0x500000000` / `mem_alias 0x380000000`, see PR #415), M4 Pro / 24 GB, macOS 26.6.2.
Base game + update extracted from a 1G+1U+2D XCI split into NSPs with LibHac; no 2K/shadow/LOD patch is applied in the stock build.

## 1. A 2K shadow mod crashes the game when the map screen opens

The community 2K shadow patch for 3.0.1 is one instruction: `main+0x146e80c`, `mov w8,#0x400` (1024) → `#0x800` (2048)
(pchtxt from Fl4sh9174's mod set, `[2K Shadows v4.0.0]`). Applied to the rewritten `main.patched.bin` at the same offset
(verified the rewriter leaves that word untouched), the game boots and plays, then **SIGSEGVs every time the map opens**
(press Y). The stock build at 30 fps opens the map fine.

Crash: `host exited with 139`, main thread `sdk+0x372274 main+0xc54ce0 main+0x130412c ...`; at `main+0xc54ce0`
(`add x8,x19,#0x248; ldarb w8,[x8]`) `x19` is not a valid object. It reproduces with the shadow patch alone (no other
mod), and it does not reproduce with the other mods of the same set:

- `Improved Graphic Quality` (DoF off + two constants): fine, map opens.
- `Draw Distance Improved` + `Improved LODs` on top of it: fine, map opens (they only crashed when 2K shadows was also in).

So 2048 px shadow textures put some resource path used by the map screen into a state where the game dereferences a null.
It looks like a host-side assumption about the shadow texture (allocation, view or sampling) rather than the mod, but I
have not traced which one. Anything obvious in `dm/gfx/nvn` that would only break with a 2048 shadow texture?

## 2. The community Dynamic 60 fps patch runs the physics at 30 on nxnative

`[Dynamic FPS Violet v4.0.0][ASM]` (Fl4sh9174, 143 instructions incl. injected code at `main+0x1760ec8`) gives a
p50 of 16.7 ms per frame on the Mac, so presents do run at 60 — but the jump height is about half of the stock 30 fps
build (long-press A still differs from tap, so the hold is detected; the whole arc is scaled down). The same patch is
correct in yuzu/Ryujinx.

The patch changes `main+0x3c2fbb0` (frame time 33.33 ms → 16.67 ms) but not `main+0x5befce4`. The community 60 fps cheat
for this build changes both:

```
[60 FPS]
04000000 05BEFCE4 00000001     ; frame-rate mode
04090000 03C2FBB0 00FE502B     ; 16,666,667 ns
[Default 30 FPS]
04000000 05BEFCE4 00000002
04090000 03C2FBB0 01FCA056
```

That suggests the engine scales its physics by the *mode* value, and the ASM patch only moves the present interval, so the
game is told "30 fps physics" while it renders 60. If someone has already read this engine's VFR/timing code, a pointer
would help; otherwise this is more of an FYI for the "60 fps" table.

## 3. There is no cheat loading in nxnative (for the record)

The Bilibili video "Mac 上运行《旷野之息》2k+60fps+金手指" is nxnative with local modifications (its description links this
repo and MacNativeGames); the cheat panel and frame generation are not in the tree. The only public implementation I found
is MacNativeGames' Ori port (`games/ori/runtime/cheat_vm.c`, `cheats.c`, and the `TOTKCheatPanel` overlay), which parses
Atmosphère cheat programs and would be a reasonable thing to port for Violet's published cheats (60 fps, resolution,
items). Not a request, just where the code is if cheats are ever wanted here.

Happy to test fixes for 1 or 2 on the Mac.
title: Pokémon Violet: 2K shadow mod crashes the map screen; the community 60 fps patch runs physics at 30

Description

I'm experiencing a system-level Kernel Panic when running The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom through LumaDock / nxnative on an Apple Silicon Mac.

Unlike a normal application crash, the entire macOS system freezes and automatically reboots.

This has happened twice. Both incidents appear to involve the same kernel call stack, suggesting a potentially reproducible GPU driver-related issue.

System Information

Hardware: Apple Mac mini, M4 Pro, 24GB
macOS Build: 25G83

Architecture: Apple Silicon (ARM64)

Operating System: macOS

Frontend: LumaDock v0.2.7

Emulation engine: nxnative (bundled with LumaDock v0.2.7; exact commit unknown)

Game: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

Steps to Reproduce

Launch Tears of the Kingdom through LumaDock / nxnative.

Start playing the game.

During gameplay, the system freezes.

The entire Mac automatically reboots.

After rebooting, macOS generates a Kernel Panic report.

The issue has occurred twice.

Expected Behavior

The game should run without causing a system-level crash. If an unrecoverable graphics error occurs, ideally the application should terminate gracefully rather than triggering a full system reboot.

Actual Behavior

macOS experiences a Kernel Panic, resulting in a complete system reboot.

Both crash reports contain references to the following components:

Panicked task: dmhost
Exception: Kernel data abort
IOGPUFamily: 130.16.4
Apple.AGXG16X: 353.14
Common crash location: IOGPUFamily +0x20854

The two incidents appear to have similar kernel backtraces.

Additional Information

The crash appears to involve the macOS GPU driver stack, although I cannot determine whether the underlying cause is an nxnative graphics command, a Metal driver issue, or an interaction between the two.

I noticed that there have been recent fixes related to Metal pipeline handling, but I have not verified whether they address this particular system-level crash.

I have not attempted further testing because the issue causes a complete system reboot.

I'm intentionally not attaching the full macOS panic reports, as they may contain device identifiers and other private system information.

Any guidance on whether this is a known issue, or whether a specific fix addresses this Kernel Panic, would be appreciated.
title: [macOS / Apple Silicon] Kernel Panic and full system reboot when running Tears of the Kingdom on M4 Pro

body:
Found by clang's static analyzer while adding clang-tidy to CI (#313). All four are low severity, and none crashes on normal input. I'm filing them in one issue rather than four, since each fix is a line or two. Line numbers are on 1963fab7.

- [ ] **`dm/host/hle_hid.c:235` and `:361`:** `player_of(id)` is checked through `style_of()`, then called again. If the controller disconnects in between, the second call returns −1, and `1u << -1` is undefined behaviour. *Fix:* call it once and reuse the result.
- [ ] **`dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c:1695`:** `fstep_on()` checks `fps_step_cap() != 0`, then `fstep_tick` reads the cap again and computes `60 / c`. If the cap drops to 0 in between, that's a division by zero. On arm64 it gives `kmin = 0` instead of a trap. *Fix:* pass `c` into `fstep_tick`.
- [ ] **`dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c:1258`:** in `nvnWindowInitialize` the loop checks each `tex[i]` for null, but the log line uses `CTX(o->tex[0])` unchecked. It crashes if a game passes `ntex > 0` with `tex[0]` null. *Fix:* test `o->tex[0]` instead of `o->ntex`.
- [ ] **`dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m:9331–9333`:** `clear_tex` checks `if (c->tex)`, then `PD(...)` reads `c->tex->serial` unconditionally. It can only crash with `DM_NVN_PASSDUMP` on and a null texture.

The clang-tidy baseline in the lint PR lists these, so the entries go away with their fixes.
title: Four small host bugs from clang's static analyzer (TOCTOU on a controller and the frame cap, two unchecked null pointers)

body:
## Bug Description

I'm experiencing a graphical rendering issue with **STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town** when running it through nxnative on both macOS and iPadOS.

The game runs and is playable, but the entire 3D game world appears heavily blurred or out of focus.

Interestingly, the UI elements, dialogue boxes, and text remain sharp and clearly rendered.

This issue occurs during normal gameplay, not just during the opening cutscenes.

## Environment

- **Game:** STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town
- **Title ID:** `0100ED400EEC2000`
- **Mac:** MacBook Pro with Apple M3 Max, 36 GB RAM
- **macOS:** 27.0.1
- **iPad:** iPad Pro M4
- **Build method:** `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py`
- **Platforms:** macOS `.app` and iPadOS (Xcode-installed app)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the game using nxnative.
2. Launch the game on macOS or iPadOS.
3. Start a new game and enter normal gameplay.
4. Observe the character, ground, grass, buildings, and other 3D objects.
5. Compare the 3D scene with the UI and dialogue elements.

## Expected Behavior

The game world, characters, and environment should render with normal visual clarity, without excessive blur.

## Actual Behavior

- The entire 3D environment appears significantly blurred.
- Characters, grass, buildings, and objects are noticeably out of focus.
- UI elements, text, and dialogue boxes remain sharp.
- The same issue occurs on both my MacBook Pro M3 Max and iPad Pro M4.
- Switching between Docked and Handheld modes does not resolve the issue.
- Enabling MetalFX upscaling does not resolve the issue.

## Additional Findings

I checked the generated `main.fixups.tsv` files for this game and could not find a `RENDER_SCALE` entry.

The Render Scale option is also unavailable in the iPadOS launcher.

I inspected the filtered runtime logs but did not identify a clear shader or pipeline failure that explains the blurring.

## Possible Cause

This may be related to depth-of-field post-processing, depth handling, or another graphics translation issue.

I noticed that nxnative previously documented a similar full-screen blurring issue involving depth mode in The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening.

Reference: https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/blob/main/docs/reference/shaders.md#depth-mode-near--0-needs-the-per-mode-entry-points

I'm not sure whether this game has the same underlying issue.

## Screenshots

I have attached screenshots showing the blurred 3D environment while the UI remains sharp.

## Request

Could you please investigate whether this is a game-specific depth-of-field or shader/post-processing issue?

I'd be happy to provide additional logs or perform further testing if needed.

Thank you for your work on nxnative!
title: STORY OF SEASONS: Friends of Mineral Town - 3D graphics are heavily blurred on macOS and iPadOS

body:
Found by ThreadSanitizer while adding sanitizers to CI (#313).

**Where:** `dm/host/hle_thread.c` (lines on 349abd06):
- `CreateThread` links the new thread into `g_all` (:842);
- `thread_main` later sets `t->host_work`, `mport` and `qos` without holding `G` (:293);
- `dm_yield_to_core_peers` (:164) calls `thr_runnable` (:130), which reads `host_work` under `G` once the thread is started.

So a yield on another core can read `host_work` while the new thread writes it.

**Repro:** `t_notify_sched` under TSan: `data race hle_thread.c:293 in thread_main`.

**Possible fix:** set those fields under `G` before the thread waits for its start (:295), or make `host_work` atomic.
title: hle_thread.c: host_work, mport and qos written without G after the thread is in g_all (TSan)

body:
Found by ThreadSanitizer while adding sanitizers to CI (#313).

**Where:** `dm/host/hle_audio.c` (lines on 349abd06):
- `au_open_at` publishes the new output in `g_aos` (:334);
- `au_create` then sets `a->au` on its own thread (`au_open`, :210);
- meanwhile the AudioUnit watchdog reads `a->au` under `g_aos_lock` (`au_watchdog`, :284).

The write isn't under the lock, so the watchdog can see a half-initialised output.

**When:** a second output opened while the watchdog runs. In `t_audio` under TSan, about one run in two.

**Possible fix:** create the AudioUnit before the output is published in `g_aos`, or set `a->au` under `g_aos_lock`.
title: hle_audio.c: a->au written outside g_aos_lock while the watchdog reads it (TSan)

body:
Found by UBSan while adding sanitizers to CI (#313). Harmless on arm64 in practice, but undefined behaviour in C, and a sanitizer build stops on it.

**Where:** `dm/host/hle_audren.c` `cmd_ok` / `cmd_size` / `cmd_id` (~:200-203 on 349abd06).

**What happens:** `capture()` looks for the command header layout by walking a command list in each layout in turn, SDK 8–20's first. On an SDK 4/6 list (Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, Fire Emblem: Three Houses), the SDK 8–20 layout reads the 16-bit command ID at +6 as the size. The next "command" then starts 2 bytes into a word, and `cmd_ok` loads its `uint32_t` magic from a misaligned address (:203).

**Repro:** `t_audren_layout` built with `-fsanitize=undefined`: `runtime error: load of misaligned address … for type 'uint32_t'`.

**Possible fix:** read the header fields with `memcpy`, or check the magic before trusting the size. Either way, no change in which layout is picked.
title: hle_audren.c: misaligned loads while capture() probes the command header layout (UBSan)

body:
Design proposal for the #313 item "`DM_NVN_CAPTURE` plus a replayer". I'd like your view on the open questions at the end before writing code, since this touches the core of the NVN layer.

## Why

`regress.py` checks a change on the games you have, but a smoke run takes minutes per game, and it reaches only what its route reaches. The replay half of the NVN layer, `nvn_mtl.m` (`mtl_exec` and everything under it), changes in about one commit out of three. A recorded frame that can be replayed against new code in seconds would let:
- **an owner** check a PR on all their games in a minute instead of playing each one;
- **a scheduled run on your Mac** replay a few frames of every game you own against `main`, so a change that breaks a game shows up the same day with the pass that changed.

**What it can't do:** let someone without a game test it. A capture holds that game's textures, buffers and shader keys, which is game data. **Captures never leave the owner's disk.** The repository and reports keep only digests and timings, as `regress.py` does today.

## What the code gives us (survey of `main`)

- **The boundary:** `nvnQueueSubmitCommands` (`hle_nvn.c`, ~:1172) hands each command buffer handle to `mtl_exec` (`nvn_mtl.m`, ~:9613). Above it, the game thread records `op_hdr` + payload records (`nvn_obj.h`) into the game's command memory. Below it is the replay on Metal. The gfx tests already drive that replay with synthetic records (`emit(OP_…)` → `mtl_exec`, e.g. `t_perf_order.m`). A replayer is the same thing with recorded records.
- **The records aren't self-contained.** They hold raw pointers:
  - `p_bind_program.prog` (`prog_t*`), `p_set_pool` (`dpool_t*`), sync and event pointers, deferred-bind sources re-read at replay;
  - `tex_t` snapshots with `mem` / `pool`;
  - GPU addresses, which are host addresses of pool storage (`newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`).
- **State replay reads besides the records:**
  - pool contents (BotW: ~1,760 live pools);
  - the texture / sampler registry (`g_treg`, `g_sreg`);
  - program keys → `shader_map.tsv` + `b-<chain>` libraries;
  - render targets in private Metal textures (not mirrored in guest memory);
  - the window's swapchain, syncs, queries.
- **Determinism:** `DM_DETCLOCK` (fixed clock step and seeded entropy), `DM_KEYS f<frame>`, frozen saves. Existing dumps (`DM_NVN_TEXRAW`, `DM_NVN_SHOT`, `DM_NVN_CBDUMP`, `DM_CTL memdump`) cover pieces. `DM_GPU_CAPTURE` writes Metal traces (1.5–2 GB) that can't be replayed against new host code.

## Proposal

**Capture** (`DM_NVN_CAPTURE=<first frame>:<frames>:<path>`, in the host):
1. At the first frame's first submit:
   - every live pool's contents (compressed);
   - the texture / sampler registry;
   - each `prog_t`'s stage keys;
   - a readback of every GPU-owned texture (render targets, images), keyed by serial;
   - the window's swapchain.
2. At each submit: the record bytes of every reachable segment (following `OP_JUMP` / `OP_CALL`), with each pointer field written as an object index. The relocation table follows the payload structs in `nvn_obj.h`, and a static assert per struct keeps it in step.
3. Between submits: the pool pages the CPU wrote, from the dirty-page tracker (`nvn_dirty_*`), so later frames are deltas.
4. A header: chain id, host commit, profile, build ID, frame range, `DM_*` settings. Everything goes in one file under the game's work folder.

**Replayer** (`dmhost --replay <capture>`, or a gfx-tests-style binary that includes `nvn_mtl.m`):
- maps pools at fresh addresses and relocates;
- recreates registry and textures;
- loads programs from the current `b-<chain>`;
- feeds the records to `mtl_exec`;
- writes a digest per presented frame, optionally per pass (`DM_NVN_TEXSNAP`-style), with GPU and CPU times.

No guest code runs, so a frame replays in milliseconds to seconds.

**Comparison** (`regress.py replay`): new code against the baseline commit on the same capture.
- Exact digests first. Then a tolerance for a frame that differs, like today's dHash / RGB thumbnail; FLIP could come later.
- On a mismatch, the first pass whose digest differs.

## Steps (each a PR)

1. Capture of **one** frame plus replay of it, on one simple NVN game (a 2D one) and on Breath of the Wild. Success means a replay gives the same frame as the live run, bit for bit. If it doesn't, that's a bug in the capture or a source of nondeterminism worth knowing about. **Landed as d9c2d5e7 (#473):** `DM_NVN_CAPTURE=<frame>:<file>` and `dm/gfx/tests/nvn_replay`, which compares memory hashes, the presented frame's SHA-256 and its pixels (`--repeat`, `--max-pixels`). The replay found a `tex_fit` view bug, fixed in the same commit. Open, in Breath of the Wild's note: fresh replays of one outdoors frame differ from the live frame and from each other in 3 to 124 pixels of two G-buffer targets; the cause is not found.
2. Several frames with pool deltas.
3. `regress.py replay` and `capture`, with digests in the report.
4. Captures per game at fixed points (`DM_KEYS f<frame>` routes, `DM_DETCLOCK`), and the scheduled run on your Mac if you want it.

## Limits

- **It checks the replay half only.** A change in how records are written (`hle_nvn.c`, the game-thread side) needs new captures. That side changes much less often.
- **A capture belongs to a profile, a build and a translator chain.** A chain change replays with the new libraries (that's the point), but a change in a shader's *interface* can make old records invalid. The replayer should report that clearly, not render garbage.
- **Size:** BotW moves ~900 MB of attachments a frame and has ~1,760 pools. A first-frame capture may be hundreds of MB compressed. That's fine on the owner's disk, but it's why the number of captured frames stays small.
- **Timing and synchronization bugs** (CPU waits, the encode thread, present pacing) won't reproduce in a replay. These stay with `bench.py` and smoke runs.

## Open questions for @seedds

1. Is `nvnQueueSubmitCommands` → `mtl_exec` the boundary you'd want, or would you rather capture one level lower or higher?
2. Relocating pointers into indices means one table per payload struct. Would you accept that in `nvn_obj.h` (next to the records, with static asserts), or keep it in a capture file of its own?
3. Would you run the scheduled replay on one of your Macs (`main` only, never PR code), or should captures stay a per-owner tool?
title: Design: capture a few frames per game and replay them against new host code (DM_NVN_CAPTURE + replayer)

body:
**Engine checked:** `4f24ce6` (and `main` `e09ff95`; `patch_nso.py` unchanged in that range)  
**Toolchain:** Xcode 27.1, Metal `32023.921`

## Summary

`patch_nso.py` stops on `br x18` jump tables in the main module of **Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy** (`0100D1B006744000`, v1.0.0, SDK 3.5.3, main build `29e1a37d84227147a50a18d055fbb032`). The title has no profile in `dm/games`, so this is a provisional-profile bring-up. Both jump tables are valid: their targets are inside the function and 4-byte aligned.

```text
AssertionError: jump table 997b78
```

## Pattern A — copy before the check, base setup after it

```text
main+0x997b5c  mov    w18, w14
main+0x997b60  cmp    w14, #3
main+0x997b64  b.hi   ...
main+0x997b68  adrp   x2, 0x323c000
main+0x997b6c  add    x2, x2, #0x3a0
main+0x997b70  ldrsw  x18, [x2, x18, lsl #2]
main+0x997b74  add    x18, x18, x2
main+0x997b78  br     x18
```

Table base `0x323c3a0`, four signed entries → targets `0x997b7c`, `0x997bb4`, `0x997bc8`, `0x997b7c`.

## Pattern B — mask after the check

After fixing A in a scratch copy, the next site is:

```text
main+0xefcc18  cmp    w8, #3
main+0xefcc1c  b.hi   ...
main+0xefcc20  and    x18, x8, #0xffffffff
main+0xefcc24  ldrsw  x18, [x17, x18, lsl #2]
main+0xefcc28  add    x18, x18, x17
main+0xefcc2c  br     x18
```

## Why the current code misses them

`jump_offsets()` walks back from the `ldrsw`. It only recognises the bounds check when the index register already contains the checked register at the point the `cmp` is met, or `check_before_copy()` when the `cmp`/`b.hi` are immediately before the load. Here:

- the copy/mask is **before** the check (A) or **between** the check and the load (B);
- the `adrp`/`add` table base is **between** the `cmp`/`b.hi` and the `ldrsw` (A);
- the check is on `w14`/`w8`, while the load indexes with `w18`/`x18`.

`check_before_copy()` currently requires `ctx[k-1] == b.hi` and `ctx[k-2] == cmp`, so the base setup breaks it; `jump_offsets()` sees the `cmp` before it expands the index with the earlier copy.

## Suggested fallback

A generalized fallback for `check_before_copy()` works in a scratch copy:

- find the nearest `cmp wS, #N; b.hi` before the load, allowing base setup instructions after the `b.hi`;
- accept a `mov wD, wS` or `and xD, xS, #mask` copy from the checked source into the index anywhere before the load;
- require the copy/mask to be the last writer of the index and the checked register, and check that neither is written between the copy and the load;
- the existing `jump_offsets()` then computes the table base and targets normally.

Sketch (not a polished PR):

```diff
-    k = ctx.index(ld)
-    if k < 2 or ctx[k - 1].mnemonic != 'b.hi' or ctx[k - 2].mnemonic != 'cmp': return None
-    m = re.fullmatch(r'(w\d+), #(0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)', ctx[k - 2].op_str)
-    if not m: return None
-    src, kl = m.group(1), insl.index(ld)
+    k = ctx.index(ld); kl = insl.index(ld)
+    cq = None
+    for bi in range(k - 1, max(0, k - 8) - 1, -1):
+        if ctx[bi].mnemonic == 'b.hi' and bi >= 1 and ctx[bi - 1].mnemonic == 'cmp':
+            m = re.fullmatch(r'(w\d+), #(0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)', ctx[bi - 1].op_str)
+            if m: cq = bi - 1; break
+    if cq is None: return None
+    m = re.fullmatch(r'(w\d+), #(0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)', ctx[cq].op_str)
+    if not m: return None
+    src, n = m.group(1), int(m.group(2), 0) + 1
@@
-    for q in range(kl - 3, max(0, kl - 64) - 1, -1):
-        p = insl[q]
-        mm = re.fullmatch(r'(w\d+), (w\d+)', p.op_str) if p.mnemonic == 'mov' else None
-        if mm and mm.group(1) in idx and mm.group(2) == src: break
+    for z in range(kl - 1, max(0, kl - 64) - 1, -1):
+        p = insl[z]
+        mm = re.fullmatch(r'(w\d+), (w\d+)', p.op_str) if p.mnemonic == 'mov' else None
+        ma = re.fullmatch(r'([wx]\d+), ([wx]\d+), #(0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)', p.op_str) if p.mnemonic == 'and' else None
+        if mm and mm.group(1) in idx and mm.group(2) == src: break
+        if ma and ma.group(1) in idx and ma.group(2) == src and (int(ma.group(3), 0) & (n - 1)) == (n - 1): break
         if writes(p) & (idx | {src}): return None
     else: return None
-    return ctx[k - 2]
+    return ctx[cq]
```

## Test evidence (scratch copy only)

- `~/nxnative` was not modified.
- `main` rewrite completes: `slot_refs 11187`, 3 jump tables, patch 449,532 bytes.
- `subsdk0` and `sdk` rewrites with the fallback are **byte-identical** to the unpatched run:
  - `subsdk0` `dd79afab…`
  - `sdk` `d4496d71…`
- Full build/boot not attempted: the title has no profile and the host would still need a bring-up.

No game files, keys, or firmware are included; the report only uses addresses, build IDs, and disassembly.
title: patch_nso: Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy main jump tables (bounds check before the index copy)

Luigi's Mansion 3 1.4.0 (`0100DCA0064A6000`) on iOS: the shared-texture alias table and the residency set grow together until jetsam, about 4.5 minutes in.

Reported on the NX2Apple fork (LNPANDY/NX2Apple#23) with two full logs; reported with the reporter's permission. It is `dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m`, which the fork does not patch.

## The numbers

From the reporter's log 4, the same diagnostic line every few hundred frames (iPhone, Apple A20 Pro, iOS 27.0.1, 12 GB):

| frame | resident | GPU alloc | residency set | serial objects | shared textures | unreferenced | evicted with pools | storage takeover |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 300 | 2905 MB | 2749 | 427 | 568 | 396 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 900 | 6060 MB | 5727 | 1364 | 1550 | 1333 | 52 | 0 | 1 |
| 1500 | 7212 MB | 6846 | 1642 | 1919 | 1611 | 2 | 0 | 52 |
| 5100 | 7484 MB | 7088 | 1931 | 2190 | 1900 | 64 | 0 | 119 |

## What the columns say

1. **`shared textures` and the residency set grow in lockstep** (396 → 1900 and 427 → 1931) and resident memory grows with them (2.9 → 7.5 GB). The memory is not lost in raw buffers; it is texture objects that stay registered with Metal and stay referenced.
2. **`freed but alive 0`** in every sample, and **`memory pools 13 (resident 3)`** never changes: the pool layer is clean, nothing is freed-but-retained, no new pools accumulate.
3. **`evicted with pools 0`** in every sample, so no pool is ever finalized — `mtl_alias_drop_pool` never runs in this title. That path exists for the same class of bug in STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT (the source comment names it: 468 entries and 1.58 GB after 24,000 frames).
4. **`on storage takeover` climbs** (0 → 119) but far too slowly: 119 evictions against ~1500 new shared textures. That path is gated by `ALIAS_IDLE = 16` (`nvn_mtl.m`, a compile-time constant, not an environment switch), an entry looked up within the last 16 submissions is spared. This title appears to cycle through textures faster than that window can retire them.

So the shared-texture table (`g_alias`) accumulates one entry per texture built on a long-lived pool, and both mechanisms that would retire them — pool finalization and idle-based takeover eviction — barely fire here. Roughly +1.1 GB per 300 frames reaching 7.5 GB at frame 5100 matches the ~4.5 minutes to jetsam the reporter measured.

## What would settle it

* Whether `ALIAS_IDLE` = 16 is meant to be the only idle-based retirement path, or whether a title that reuses a long-lived pool this fast needs either a shorter window or a second criterion (age in frames rather than last-lookup).
* The reporter says it crashes just after the first cutscene, and that it also happens when entering a new area — so both a per-scene render-target pattern and a never-finalized pool are on the table.
* `DM_ALIAS_WINDOWS` and `DM_MEMSTAT` output from a run would give a second, independent view of the same growth if that helps.

The reporter's two logs are attached to LNPANDY/NX2Apple#23 and I can paste either one here if you would rather keep it in this tracker.
title: Luigi's Mansion 3 1.4.0 (0100DCA0064A6000) iOS: the shared-texture alias table and the residency set grow together until jetsam

body:
Graphical front ends come up almost daily: #104, #244, #264, #332, #374. [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) already builds games, keeps a library and starts them with their settings. To follow `main`, it re-applies patches to nine of our files on every sync ([`sync_upstream.py`](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple/blob/main/scripts/sync_upstream.py)). I think the useful work here isn't another GUI in this repository. It's a clear interface between the engine and any app around it, so front ends can build on nxnative without forking or patching it.

## Three layers

1. **The game's own app** (`front_mac.m`, `front_ios.m`, the iPhone's settings screen). Everything that has to appear while a game runs lives here, because no other app is on screen then: a controller that went away, "Preparing shaders", a thermal hint, an error.
2. **The interface between the engine and its front ends**, versioned, documented and tested:
   - *in*: `settings.tsv` → `launcher.json` → environment switches (exists);
   - *out while building*: the NSP script's `--progress json` events (exists);
   - *out while a game runs*: **missing**. Today the host reports only in its log, as text meant for people.
3. **Front ends outside this repository**: building, a library, launch options, artwork, updates. NX2Apple is one.

## Steps

- [x] The Mac app carries its settings list, `Contents/Resources/dm/launcher.json` (#352, merged). NX2Apple's launch options already read it.
- [x] Document the interface: `docs/frontends.md`, and NX2Apple at the top of the README (#387, merged).
- [x] Point people to front ends before they open an issue: NX2Apple first in the issue chooser, a "Graphical front ends" section in CONTRIBUTING.md (#306). Landed as 81d53bf.
- [x] **Choices that hold however the app is started.** (landed as 6d1e07b, #431: `launcher.<VAR>` in the app's preferences domain; order: launch environment, the player's `env.txt`, the bundle's `env.txt`, saved choices, tested defaults; `DM_SAVED_CHOICES=0` ignores them) The iPhone app keeps a player's choices in its own preferences, `launcher.<switch>` (only those that differ from the tested default). A Mac app has no such store, so choices made in a front end apply only when that front end starts the game, and a start from Finder or the Dock uses the defaults. Proposal: the Mac launcher (`dm/mac/launcher.c`) reads the same keys from the app's preferences domain (`org.nxnative.<title ID>`, CFPreferences, no Swift needed), with the order the iPhone has: environment, then `env.txt`, then stored choices, then defaults. A front end writes them there, and an in-app window, if #374 gets one, would use the same store, so the two never disagree.
- [ ] **Runtime events.** (in review: #474, then #481 for `controller`, `thermal`, `save` and background prewarm progress) The host writes one JSON object per line to a file or descriptor a front end names (e.g. `DM_EVENTS=<path|fd:N>`), in the same envelope as the build events (`ev`, `t`). First events: the game started its frame loop, shader preparation progress, controller connected or disconnected, thermal state, a `[RED]` line, and why the game ended. The schema lives in `docs/frontends.md`, and a test fails on an event the docs don't list, as `test_env_switches.py` does for switches. Both the in-app overlay and outside front ends read the same events.
- [ ] **The controller applet with a native dialog.** (in review: #480. It asks only when fewer players are connected than the game needs and the device can reach that number. Landed alongside: each controller gets a player of its own on iOS, as on the Mac, fdea829c (#504); a controller's Home and Capture buttons stay with the game, 062cd06e (#541).) On a Switch, a game that needs controllers calls the controller applet, and the system shows its dialog and waits. The host answers `ShowControllerSupport` at once with whoever is connected (`dm/host/hle_hid.c`), so a game whose controller went away carries on without one. Answering it with a native sheet (AppKit / UIKit) that waits for the players the game asks for would fix this for every game at once, following Horizon's semantics rather than per-game logic.
- [ ] **Status in the game's app**: small notices in `front_mac.m` / `front_ios.m`, driven by the same events. (in review: #489, building on #481)
- [ ] **Fewer patches for forks.** Each file a front end has to patch on every sync marks a hook nxnative is missing. Bring them in one small PR at a time, so a front end can follow `main` as it is. Landed: #478 (32ae3b11), #476 (a0b8bdb3), #477 and #487 together (c464cb24). In review: #475, #485, #486, #490, #494 (#488, CPU BC decoding, was declined). Also in review: #492, a proposal for a runtime game profile (one host binary for every game). Still to come: the iOS per-game data folder, after #460.
- [ ] **Controls on the same store**: `launcher.DM_KEYMAP` / `launcher.DM_PAD_MAP` as saved choices, checked with the host's own parser (in review: #386). The mapping UI from #104 follows on top.
- [ ] **A data folder per app**: `dataFolder`, and `DM_SAVE` / `DM_LOG_DIR` relative to the app (in review: #460).
- [ ] **Community front ends**: a page that lists front ends against this interface, with each author adding their own row (in review: #484).
- [x] **Scope decision (@seedds):** should a game's Mac app have its own settings window, drawn from `launcher.json` like the iPhone's (#374)? Or should Mac apps start with their tested defaults, with settings coming from front ends? Decided: yes. The window landed as 1e207fa (#379), drawn from `launcher.json` and keeping its choices in the saved-choices store.

## Design

What the player sees should be the same everywhere: the setting names, sections, tested defaults and "Reset to tested defaults" come from one list, `settings.tsv` / `launcher.json`, and every front end draws from it. How it looks follows each platform's own conventions (SwiftUI forms, Apple's Human Interface Guidelines), not one front end's style.

## Out of scope here

An app to build games or keep a library inside this repository. Those stay separate projects, with nxnative providing what they need.
title: Front ends: one interface between the engine and graphical apps (settings, build progress, runtime events)

body:
Edge case, low priority: it only happens with a damaged NSP, and re-downloading fixes it. But the crash hides the real cause.

With a damaged Tears of the Kingdom base NSP (4 files failing the NCA hash check), nx_extract crashes partway through the RomFS:

```
Unhandled exception. System.InvalidOperationException: The LinkedList is empty.
   at System.Collections.Generic.LinkedList`1.RemoveLast()
   at LibHac.Tools.FsSystem.CachedStorage.GetBlock(Int64 blockIndex)
   at LibHac.Tools.FsSystem.CachedStorage.Read(Int64 offset, Span`1 destination)
   at P.Write(IFile f, String op, Int64 size, Byte[] buf) in dm/tools/nx_extract/Program.cs:line 219
   at P.Copy(IFileSystem fs, String dst, String cmpDir) in dm/tools/nx_extract/Program.cs:line 203
```

So nx_extract never gets to its own "the NSP is damaged: N files fail the NCA's hash check" message, and `--allow-damaged` doesn't help either.

**Why:** LibHac's `CachedStorage.GetBlock` removes a block from its cache before reading it and only puts it back if the read succeeds. Each hash failure loses one block. The cache holds 4, so the 4th damaged file empties it, and every read after that throws. With the hash check skipped, all of those later files read fine.

**Possible fix:** after a hash failure in `Copy`, open a fresh RomFS storage for the remaining files, so the damaged-file list is printed (and `--allow-damaged` works) however many files are damaged.
title: Edge case: nx_extract crashes with "The LinkedList is empty" instead of reporting a damaged NSP
