body:
## Proposal

Show a small settings window when a game's Mac `.app` starts, before the game runs. This is the same idea as the iOS launcher from #64, and it draws from the same `dm/games/settings.tsv`. Old PC games used a window like this to choose the resolution and graphics options before the game started. The Switch games do not have these settings in their own menus.

The window opens with the basic settings. An "Advanced settings" row opens the rest.

| Basic | Advanced settings open |
|---|---|
| ![Basic view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/surajmandalcell/nxnative/34b86fae5c95b9d2392a9bc54a21b97982135fc0/mac-launcher-basic.jpg) | ![Advanced view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/surajmandalcell/nxnative/34b86fae5c95b9d2392a9bc54a21b97982135fc0/mac-launcher-advanced.jpg) |

*Mockups with the settings that Breath of the Wild has today. The real window uses the app's own icon.*

- **Basic:** Resolution, Display mode, Frame rate, Console mode, Game language, Rumble.
- **Advanced:** Upscaling, Rumble strength, Metal performance HUD, Frame hold, Frame buffering, Metal 4 pipelines, Prebuild pipelines, Encode thread.

## Why now

In #64, the answer for the Mac was "no macOS launcher", because the Mac had no `.app` packaging then. The Mac has `.app` packaging now (`dm/mac/pack_app.py`, `--platform mac-app`), so players double-click a game app. To change a setting, they still have to edit `env.txt` or start the app from a terminal.

## Design

- **One table:** the window draws from `dm/games/settings.tsv` and `settings.py`, the same as iOS. A row can name its platforms and whether it is basic or advanced. `DM_SHOW_FPS` and `DM_TOUCH_HAPTICS` stay iOS-only, and a Mac-only Display mode row sets `DM_FULLSCREEN`.
- **Real values:** resolution shows real pixels, from the game's base view size times `DM_RENDER_SCALE`. For example, BotW docked shows 800×450 to 1600×900. The values the host reads do not change.
- **No new process:** `dm/mac/launcher.c` already sets up the environment and starts `dmhost`. The window opens before that spawn. Play sets the environment variables, and then the game starts as it does today. Values from an env file are shown locked, the same as on iOS.
- **Skipping the window:**
  - A "Show this window at launch" check box, saved in UserDefaults.
  - Holding Option while the app opens shows the window again.
  - `open Game.app --args --no-launcher` skips the window.
  - `DM_LAUNCHER=0` skips the window, the same switch as on iOS.

  Scripts and tests keep their current behaviour with `DM_LAUNCHER=0`.

## Open for contributors (later)

Anybody who wants to pick these up is welcome to. None of them is in the first PR.

- [ ] **Mods:** the host can already read replacement game files from a list of folders (`DM_ROMFS_OVERLAY`, `hle_fs.c`). A per-game mods folder with one switch per mod would fit in the window. Mods that change the game code (ExeFS) are not supported.
- [ ] **Resolution above 100%** (1440p, 4K) when #159 lands.
- [ ] **120 fps** in the Frame rate list when #76 lands.
- [ ] **More display modes**, such as a borderless window or fixed window sizes.
- [ ] **A controller-friendly layout**, so the window works without a keyboard.

A draft PR with the first part will follow and will link here.
title: Mac: a settings window before the game starts (resolution, display mode, frame rate)

body:
### Context

I am testing Super Mario Bros. Wonder through the nxnative-based pipeline to investigate a rendering failure.

### Environment
- Game: Super Mario Bros. Wonder
- Title ID: `010015100B514000`
- Device: Apple device with A16 GPU
- Graphics backend: NVN to Metal
- StikDebug: tested both enabled and disabled

### Steps to reproduce
1. Build and install the IPA.
2. Launch the game and press Play.
3. Let the game begin rendering.
4. Observe the crash after a few frames.

### Observed behavior

The game starts, mounts its RomFS successfully and submits rendering commands. It then crashes with this Metal validation error:

```text
MTLTextureDescriptor has invalid pixelFormat (140).
```

The stack trace includes:

```text
pkg_upload
tex_mtl
tex_by_id
encode_args_
encode_args
draw
mtl_exec
h_nvnQueueSubmitCommands
```

### Additional observations
- The RomFS mount succeeds: 19,012 files, 167 directories and 47 shards.
- The log identifies shader route B (translated Switch originals).
- The log reports zero shader keys missing from the shader map.
- The same error occurs with and without StikDebug.
- The failure happens during rendering, unlike a crash during initial module loading.

### Questions

1. Can the NVN texture format responsible for Metal pixel format `140` be identified from this error path?
2. Does this indicate an unsupported texture format, an invalid descriptor, or another issue in texture upload or lookup?
3. Is there a recommended diagnostic build or logging point to capture the original NVN format before it reaches Metal?

I can provide both logs, with StikDebug enabled and disabled.

I have not confirmed the exact cause, so I am reporting the reproducible failure rather than assuming that a specific format mapping is incorrect.

**Hardware note:** this test was performed on an A16 device. If this title requires a newer GPU than the one I tested, please let me know whether the result is useful for investigating the general texture-handling path.
title: Super Mario Bros. Wonder crashes during rendering with invalid Metal pixelFormat (140)

The developer confirmed that the diagnosis was correct and that the fix implemented the proposed solution by using `segs[0][1]` as the lower bound for the gap scan and adjusting `CODE_RANGES`, while leaving the NSO path unchanged.

The developer also mentioned that the fix had not been verified against a real Final Fantasy X/X-2 NRO and requested a build log to confirm it end to end.

### Environment
- Game: Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster
- Device: Apple device with A16 GPU
- Frontend: NX2Apple
- StikDebug: tested both enabled and disabled

### Current behavior

The game still aborts before reaching the main menu. Both runs produce the following fatal error:

```text
FATAL .../dm/nro.tsv: more NROs than module slots (MAX_MOD 128)
```

The stack trace includes:

```text
abort
read_layout
host_preload
preload_thread
```

The failure occurs during startup, before gameplay or rendering begins.

### Relationship to the previous fix

I understand that commit `4b86323` fixes the NRO header offset issue in the gap scan and that this fix was not originally validated against a real Final Fantasy X/X-2 NRO.

The current crash reports a module-slot limit (`MAX_MOD 128`), which may be a separate issue from the previous gap-scan bug.

### Questions

I can provide both logs and the relevant build output to help verify the previous fix against a real game.

body:
## Setup
- MacBook Pro, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Xcode 27.1
- nxnative `8334fdf` (current main), `--platform mac-app`
- Controller: **GameSir Cyclone (PC)** over Bluetooth. It presents itself as a DualShock 4: HID vendor `054C`, product `05C4`, GameController `productCategory` "DualShock 4", vendor name "DUALSHOCK 4 Claire", localities All, Default, Handles, Left Handle, Right Handle.
- Games: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (4.0.1) and Breath of the Wild (1.9.0)
- The same controller rumbles in a Switch emulator on this Mac (SDL).

## What happens
No rumble at all. The log shows the handle route failing, then (with the change below that falls back after repeated player failures) the default locality failing the same way:

```
haptics: player 1 controller DUALSHOCK 4 Claire, localities All, Default, Handles, Left Handle, Right Handle, 2 channels
[RED] haptics: controller left handle create player: Couldn’t communicate with a helper application. (NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097)
[RED] haptics: controller left handle create player: Couldn’t communicate with a helper application. (NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097)
haptics: player 1 retrying with the default controller locality
[RED] haptics: controller default create player: Couldn’t communicate with a helper application. (NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097)
```

On current main a "create player" failure is retried on the same handle for good (by design since 0f99c35), so the route never leaves the failing left handle, and each failure clears the player's output.

## It is not nxnative
A minimal Swift app (AppKit, `GCSupportsControllerUserInteraction`, nothing from nxnative) that makes an engine for each locality and plays a 0.7 s continuous event gets the same error everywhere:

```
controller DUALSHOCK 4 Claire localities ["All", "Default", "Handles", "Left Handle", "Right Handle"]
Default: FAILED NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097 Couldn’t communicate with a helper application.
Handles: FAILED NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097 Couldn’t communicate with a helper application.
Left Handle: FAILED NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097 Couldn’t communicate with a helper application.
Right Handle: FAILED NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097 Couldn’t communicate with a helper application.
```

#219 (Sifu, M3 iMac, the same macOS build 26A434) logged the same `NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097` for left/right controller haptics, controller not named.

## What works
Sending the DualShock 4 Bluetooth effects report directly, as SDL's hidapi driver does (report `0x11`, 78 bytes, flags `0xC4`, rumble-only flag `0x01`, CRC32 over `0xA2` and the first 74 bytes) with `IOHIDDeviceSetReport`: the controller rumbles and stops as asked.

## Mario Kart 8 Deluxe keeps rotating motors running
With the report path and a linear mapping (strong motor = low band, weak motor = high band, as emulators map it), Mario Kart 8 Deluxe sends low-band values of 0.1–0.4 for the whole race, about 30 changes a second, with 0.84 peaks every few seconds (`DM_RUMBLE_LOG=1`, 5 s windows):

```
frame 2700 (45 s):   0 reports                  (menus, countdown)
frame 3300 (55 s):  79 reports, max strong 255
frame 3900 (65 s): 151 reports, max strong 214
...                ~150 reports every 5 s until the race ends
frame 8400 (140 s): 46 reports, last "strong 0 weak 0"   (back to the menu)
```

On a Joy-Con's resonant actuator that is a texture; on the DS4's rotating motors it is rumble that never lets up. With amplitudes below 0.45 silenced (and the rest stretched to the full range), only crashes and drifts rumble, which matches what the emulator gives on this controller. Breath of the Wild needs no threshold (rumble on hits and chopping, then it stops).

A PR with the change follows.
title: Mac: no rumble on a DualShock 4-compatible controller (GameSir Cyclone): Core Haptics fails with NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097 on every locality

## Summary

After #273 (landed as `d50ecc1`), `patch_nso.py` no longer stops on this title's jump table (`7340b8`) — the rewrite completes. The game then crashes in its **static initialisers** on the Mac host, before any NVN or shader work, with a write to an address far outside the guest address space.

```
>>> nninitStartup
SetHeapSize 0x6400000 -> base 0x7138000000 mprotect=0 errno=0
main: DT_INIT +0x24 (init_array 5214 entries)
CRASH sig=10 addr=0x20000ffff pc=main+0xea25b8 lr=main+0xea25b4
x0=0 x1=0x200000000 x2=0x10000 x3=0 x4=0 x5=0x10000
```

## The faulting frame

`main+0xea25a8` … `0xea25bc`:

```
0xea2590: ldr   x0, [x20, #0xa8]
0xea2594: cmp   w19, #2
0xea2598: mov   w8, #0x10000
0xea259c: mov   w9, #0x80000
0xea25a0: csel  x2, x9, x8, eq
0xea25a4: mov   w3, wzr
0xea25a8: sub   x1, x21, x0        ; x1 = 0x200000000
0xea25ac: mov   w4, wzr
0xea25b0: bl    #0xf59ff8          ; x0 = x0 + x1; then 0x1b5b218(x0, size 0x10000)
0xea25b4: mov   w8, #0xffff
0xea25b8: strb  w19, [x21, x8]     ; fault: 0x200000000 + 0xffff
```

`x21` is `0x200000000` (8 GiB, i.e. 2^33) and the game writes through it. The host's guest address space is `0x7000000000 + 0x140000000` (heap `0x7138000000`, alias `0x7010000000`), so `0x200000000` is not mapped by anything and the process takes SIGBUS. The callee at `0xf59ff8` adds `x1` to `x0` and passes a `0x10000` size on — consistent with the game treating `0x200000000` as a real, mapped base.

## Environment

- Title `010067300059A000`, update **v589824 (1.9.589692)**, `sdk: NintendoSDK nnSdk-4_4_0-Release (major 4)`.
- Mac host (Apple silicon), built from a worktree with **#273 + #234** merged; #234 makes no difference here (the crash is before the shaders, and the capture run reports `captured only 0 run-time shaders` for the same reason).
- ExeFS of this build: `main, main.npdm, rtld, sdk, subsdk0, subsdk1`.
- **No profile in `dm/games`**, so this is the provisional path. Its layout:

```
modules      main subsdk0 sdk
mem_reserve  0x140000000
mem_alias    0x118000000
mem_stack    0x10000000
app_pool     0xCD500000
```

Note the profile's `modules` omits `subsdk1`, which the ExeFS does contain — I added it by hand and rebuilt the host, and the crash was unchanged (same `pc`, same `x21`).

## What I'm asking

The rewriter side looks solved for this title; this looks like the memory layout the provisional profile guesses (`mem_reserve` / `mem_alias` / pool placement) not matching what the game expects — most likely this title needs its own `dm/games/010067300059A000` profile rather than a guess. Pointers welcome: is the right next step to raise `mem_reserve`, to give the game its pool at a specific base, or to look at what `main+0xea2590`..`0xea25b0` is initialising (it runs from `init_array`, so it is constructor-time state, not gameplay)?

I can run any instrumentation you want on this build and report back — the crash is 100% reproducible on the Mac, in about two seconds.
title: After #273, Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle crashes in static init writing to 0x200000000 + 0xffff

body:
**Summary:** On an M4 Pro, Tears of the Kingdom holds a flat 60 fps fullscreen until a heavier moment (rain starting). The frame step then goes to 30, and macOS drops the GPU to its **lowest clock (338 MHz)**. It keeps it there for about 40 s **while the GPU is 75–92% busy**. Every probe back to 60 fails, because at 338 MHz a frame takes ~18–20 ms of GPU time. When the clock rises again on its own, the next trial returns to 60. At normal clocks the same scene needs ~5–6 ms, so the hardware can hold 60 with plenty to spare.

### Setup

- MacBook Pro M4 Pro (Mac16,8), 48 GB, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- On AC power and charging, `pmset` power mode 2 (High Power). The host logged no thermal pressure.
- Mac app (`--platform mac-app`) built from `ff44c59` on 2026-10-26
- TotK 1.4.3, fullscreen on an external 144 Hz 4K screen. The host switched it to 120 Hz (`screen at 144 Hz switched to 120 Hz for 60 fps in fullscreen`).
- env.txt: `DM_METAL_HUD=1`, `DM_RENDER_SCALE=1.0`, `DM_FPS_TARGET=60`, `DM_OPMODE=1`

### 1. GPU profile (`DM_NVN_GPUPROF=every:600`, earlier session, same place)

| Profiled frame | Situation | GPU time per frame | Same passes, relative to frame 2400 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2400 | clear, 60 fps | 5.29 ms | 1.00 |
| 3000 | rain starting, still 60 | 13.81 ms | ×2.19 (median) |
| 3600 | rain, 30 fps | 21.02 ms | ×3.01 (median) |
| 4200 | back to 60 | 5.81 ms | ×0.93 |

The ratios compare ~130 passes per frame that are the same work in both frames: the same size and draw count, ≤ 20 draws, such as downsampling and blur chains. Every pass slowed down evenly, so the cause is the GPU's speed, not a rain-specific effect. Rain adds only ~10–15% draws (2,102 → 2,366 → 2,992).

### 2. GPU clock during a second session (`sudo powermetrics --samplers gpu_power -i 1000`)

The game log puts this session's start at about 23:50:25. The frame step went to 30 at 42.75 s (`present 2175`) and came back at ~86 s (`present 3585`, a trial).

| Wall time | GPU HW active frequency | GPU busy | Requested state | Game |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23:50:46 – 23:51:06 | 1,250–1,490 MHz | 62–75% | P6–P10 | 60 fps |
| 23:51:07 | 1,007 MHz | 68% | P6 | late frames → 30 |
| **23:51:08 – 23:51:46** | **338 MHz** (lowest) | **72–92%** | **P1** | 30 fps; 6 probes, all failed |
| 23:51:47 – 23:51:49 | 683 → 1,149 MHz | 23–36% | P1 → P10 | trial at 60 holds |

The frame step's summary for the session: `held 1 / 2 / 3 vsyncs 591 / 1209 / 0 frames, 228 late … 9 up / 9 down (6 probes, 6 failed trials)`.

The probes are triggered (`probe, GPU 1.3–1.4× its time at hold 1`), but each one ends after 3 late frames, about 33 presents in. Over those 0.5 s the sampled clock never rises above 338 MHz. So the governor doesn't react within a probe's length, and at 30 fps the GPU finishes inside its 33 ms deadline at the lowest clock, so it has no reason to raise it. That looks like the loop `docs/development.md` (Power) describes for the iPhone, but on the Mac, at the minimum clock, and while the GPU is busy most of the time.
title: Mac: TotK drops to 30 fps because macOS pins the GPU at its lowest clock, and the frame step's probes can't bring it back

body:
**Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (0100152000022000, 4.0.0 / v1441792, the profile's registered build), Mac app (`--platform mac-app -p v1441792 --gpu none`), host built at 40b643b.** In a window the game runs at a steady 60 fps. After entering macOS fullscreen (green button or ⌃⌘F) with the built-in display on ProMotion, it drops to about 30 fps with many frames merged or dropped, while the CPU and GPU cost per frame stays well under one vsync. Leaving fullscreen brings back 60 fps at once. Two setups stay at 60 fps:

- A window zoomed to nearly the fullscreen size (title-bar double-click).
- Fullscreen with the built-in display set to a fixed 60 Hz.

## Environment

- MacBook Pro, Apple M4 (`applegpu_g16g`), built-in Liquid Retina XDR display (ProMotion, up to 120 Hz), panel 3024x1964, in a scaled display mode (the fullscreen drawable is 3600x2260)
- macOS 26.6 (25G72), Xcode 26.3 (17C529), Metal toolchain 32023.864
- AC power, Low Power Mode off
- `--gpu none` because the offline pipeline archive failed on one vs/ps pair (`4a692bc0ada44684` + `4d40191226180ee7`). That failure is #283, fixed in ff44c59, which this build predates. It is not related to the issue described here.

## Runs

Three sessions, with values from the host's 300-frame summaries.

| Display refresh | Mode | Drawable | Frame time p50 / p95 (ms) | GPU p50 (ms) | fps (power summary) | On-screen per 300 frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ProMotion | Window | 2560x1440 | 16.67 / 17.35 | 7.85 | 60 | 289 shown, 8 dropped |
| ProMotion | Fullscreen, 1st | 3600x2260 | 17.81 / 34.68 → 16.52 / 18.94 → 52.85 / 57.30 → 52.91 / 59.07 → 50.96 / 61.00 | 7.0–9.4 | 43.9 → 57.2 → 30.0 → 30.0 → 30.0 | 240 shown / 173 dropped (82 discarded) → 151 / 151 (148 discarded) → then no `on-screen` lines for 900 frames |
| ProMotion | Window again | 2560x1440 | 16.66 / 17.63, 16.69 / 17.34 | 7.6–8.7 | 60.0 | 300 shown, 2 dropped |
| ProMotion | Fullscreen, 2nd | 3600x2260 | 18.68 / 61.02 (with a 3.7 s loading stall), 27.81 / 42.56 | 4.5–8.0 | 24.1, 32.7 | 255 / 140 dropped (69 discarded) → 155 / 155 (153 discarded) |
| ProMotion | Zoomed window | 3600x2196 | 16.63 / 17.81, 16.60 / 18.16, 16.66 / 17.46 | 10.6–12.9 | 60 | 300 shown, 0 dropped |
| **Fixed 60 Hz** | **Fullscreen**, ~14,700 frames (~4 min) | 3600x2260 | 16.4–16.7 / 17.2–18.6 | 6.3–12.4 | 60.0 (59.8 once) | 300 shown, 0 dropped in every summary after the first two (21 and 4 dropped while loading) |

**Display link rate.** I took the time of each `display link up to tick N` summary from the nearest `[longframe]` timestamps:

- ProMotion, fullscreen, ticks 906 → 1206: 281.7 s → 301.7 s, so 300 ticks in about 20 s (~15 Hz).
- ProMotion, window, ticks 2413 → 2719 → 3028: about 5 s per 300 ticks (~60 Hz).
- Fixed 60 Hz, fullscreen, ticks 5410 → 13510: between ~103 s and ~240 s, so 8,100 ticks in ~137 s (~59 Hz).

The ProMotion summaries around the switch to fullscreen:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link up to tick 302: ticks 300, presents 301, empty ticks 1 (held for the present interval 0), old frames dropped by merging 2; submission ahead of target display p50 49.638 ms / min 47.557 ms; game enqueue to target display p50 80.582 ms / min 56.675 / max 202.813 ms
[dm] front end: drawable 2560x1504
[dm] front end: drawable 3600x2260
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link up to tick 606: ticks 300, presents 696, empty ticks 18446744073709551526 (held for the present interval 0), old frames dropped by merging 14; submission ahead of target display p50 32.880 ms / min 29.482 ms; game enqueue to target display p50 63.266 ms / min 37.659 / max 92.138 ms
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link up to tick 906: ticks 300, presents 996, empty ticks 18446744073709551526 (held for the present interval 0), old frames dropped by merging 137; submission ahead of target display p50 31.550 ms / min 14.760 ms; game enqueue to target display p50 62.684 ms / min 44.398 / max 94.063 ms
[dm] [nvn-mtl] display link up to tick 1206: ticks 300, presents 1296, empty ticks 18446744073709551526 (held for the present interval 0), old frames dropped by merging 437; submission ahead of target display p50 16.247 ms / min 15.938 ms; game enqueue to target display p50 79.809 ms / min 78.674 / max 82.369 ms
```

Frames in the 2nd ProMotion fullscreen episode are cheap but long:

```
[dm] [longframe] frame 18121 (585.42 s) whole frame 35.9 ms, submit+present 2.5 ms, GPU 0.6 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 18122 (585.45 s) whole frame 34.0 ms, submit+present 0.5 ms, GPU 0.7 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 18139 (585.87 s) whole frame 33.1 ms, submit+present 0.4 ms, GPU 0.3 ms
[dm] [longframe] frame 18145 (586.02 s) whole frame 33.6 ms, submit+present 0.4 ms, GPU 0.4 ms
```

Other observations:

- No log has a `frame step:` line. The frame step never leaves hold 1, which differs from #347.
- No log has a `front end: screen at … Hz` line. No screen mode switch happened, which fits: 120 Hz is already a multiple of 60.
- `empty ticks` underflows (18446744073709551526 = −90 as u64) once presents outrun ticks within a summary window. This looks like a cosmetic counter bug, and it shows in the fixed-60 Hz run too.

## What is known

- It needs ProMotion. Fullscreen at a fixed 60 Hz holds 60 fps with 0 dropped frames for ~4 minutes, with the display link at ~59 Hz.
- It needs a fullscreen space. On ProMotion, the zoomed window at 3600x2196 has 97% of the fullscreen pixel count and the same scaled mode, and it holds 60 fps with 0 dropped frames, at a higher GPU cost (11–13 ms).
- It is not CPU or GPU cost. On ProMotion fullscreen, GPU is 7–9 ms per frame (0.3–1.6 ms in the cheap frames above) and submit+present is at most 3 ms.
- On ProMotion in a fullscreen space, the `CAMetalDisplayLink` delivers about a quarter of the expected updates (~15 Hz).

## What is not known

- Why `CAMetalDisplayLink` ticks at ~15 Hz on ProMotion in a fullscreen space. A guess, not checked: in fullscreen the window server lets the variable refresh rate drop and the link's preferred range (60, 60, 60) is not honoured there.
- Whether current `main` behaves the same. Since 40b643b, fb34a93 (#324) changed display-link pacing, but by its description only for the high-refresh display mode, keeping 60 Hz pacing as before.
- Whether an external display is affected. I have none to test.
- How this relates to #347. Both are ProMotion-only on the built-in display, with the same host commit and a fixed 60 Hz as the fix, so they may share a root cause. The symptoms differ, though:
  - #347: in a window, through the frame step.
  - Here: only in fullscreen, through the display link itself, with the frame step at hold 1 throughout.

## Workarounds

- Set the built-in display to a fixed 60 Hz (System Settings → Displays → Refresh rate).
- Or play in a zoomed window (double-click the title bar, or Option-click the green button) instead of fullscreen.

I can attach the full host logs or record a `DM_NVN_TSV` trace in ProMotion fullscreen if that helps.
title: Mac app: in macOS fullscreen on a ProMotion built-in display the display link ticks at ~15 Hz and the game drops to ~30 fps; at a fixed 60 Hz, or in a zoomed window, it holds 60

body:
**Tears of the Kingdom (0100F2C0115B6000, 1.4.3), Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), host built at 40b643b, windowed.** The same slowdowns were seen in Super Mario Bros. Wonder, but no log was kept for that game.

Environment: MacBook Pro with Apple M5 Max (`applegpu_g17s`) and its built-in ProMotion display (up to 120 Hz), macOS 27.0.1 (26A434). For comparison, two external 100 Hz monitors (5120x2160 and 3840x2160).

## Symptom

On the built-in display, with the refresh rate set to ProMotion, the game regularly slows down for about 1–1.5 s. It happens on battery and on AC power, with Low Power Mode off, and without anything on screen changing (no volume overlay or notification). On the external 100 Hz monitors it does not happen. With the built-in display set to a fixed 60 Hz (System Settings → Displays → Refresh rate) it is mostly gone.

Each slowdown is the host's frame step stepping up on frames whose cost is well under a vsync:

```
[dm] [nvn] frame step: hold 1 → 2 vsyncs at present 1634 (3 late frames; cost 0.43 vsyncs, GPU 0.42; hold 1 held at 0.51)
[dm] [longframe] frame 1626 (45.82 s) whole frame 33.5 ms, submit+present 6.4 ms, GPU 9.3 ms; …
[dm] [longframe] frame 1627 (45.85 s) whole frame 33.3 ms, submit+present 6.5 ms, GPU 10.5 ms; …
[dm] [nvn] frame step: hold 2 → 3 vsyncs at present 1637 (3 late frames; cost 0.72 vsyncs, GPU 0.72; hold 1 held at 0.51)
[dm] [longframe] frame 1639 (46.27 s) whole frame 50.7 ms, submit+present 6.8 ms, GPU 11.3 ms; …
… (frames 1639–1647 all about 50 ms, submit+present 6–7 ms, GPU 5–12 ms)
[dm] [nvn] frame step: hold 3 → 2 vsyncs at present 1671 (trial; cost 0.54 vsyncs, GPU 0.54)
[dm] [nvn] frame step: hold 2 → 1 vsyncs at present 1701 (trial; cost 0.54 vsyncs, GPU 0.54)
```

## Runs

| Screen | Frame step changes | Cost when it stepped up |
|---|---|---|
| External 100 Hz (virtual 60 Hz ticks), session of about 40 min | none (`0 up / 0 down` in every 30 s summary) | — |
| Built-in, ProMotion, battery | 1 → 2 → 3 at present 1767, frames at ~66 ms until the trials at 1824 / 1854 | 0.71 vsyncs |
| Built-in, ProMotion, AC | 1 → 2 at 2317; 1 → 2 → 3 at 4469; 1 → 2 at 5008 | 0.81; 0.57 / 0.67; 0.03 |
| Built-in, ProMotion, AC, `DM_PRESENT_SNAP=2` | 1 → 2 → 3 at 1634 (log above), plus two steps right after the start | 0.43 / 0.72 |
| Built-in, fixed 60 Hz, AC, about 6,300 frames | 1 → 2 at 1433, back at 1464 | 1.24 vsyncs (GPU 0.89): a really expensive scene |

On a 120 Hz screen `link_range` asks for (60, 60, 60) with no virtual ticks, and the log has no `display link at the screen's … Hz` line in the built-in runs. Present snapshots did not help, so it is not a GPU running at a low clock waiting for the swapchain.

## What is not known

Why frames count as late on the ProMotion display when their CPU and GPU cost is about half a vsync. A guess, not checked: with a variable refresh rate the system does not deliver `CAMetalDisplayLink` updates at an even 60 Hz, so frames miss their tick and the frame step reads that as load. A per-frame trace (`DM_NVN_TSV`) on the built-in display would show the tick intervals; I can record one if that helps.

fb34a93 (#324) changes display mode above 60 Hz only and keeps game-interval and frame-step pacing in 60 Hz vsync units, so I don't expect it to change this. The app was built before it.

## Workaround

Set the built-in display to a fixed 60 Hz while playing.
title: Mac: on a ProMotion built-in display the frame step drops to 30 / 20 fps on frames that are not expensive; at a fixed 60 Hz it does not

body:
**Tears of the Kingdom (0100F2C0115B6000, 1.4.3), Mac app (`--platform mac-app`), host built at 40b643b. The compaction code is unchanged up to c484b13.**

Environment: Apple M5 Max (`applegpu_g17s`), macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Metal toolchain 32023.921.

## Symptom

The game ran normally for a long session. After that, every start crashes right after the pipeline prepare step: the window appears briefly and the launcher reports `the host exited with 139`. Two starts in a row crashed with the same backtrace.

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline archive …/nxnative/0100F2C0115B6000/pso_archive: 26 files (16 of bases without a vertex layout), 1868.6 MB, opened in 366.8 ms
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline prepare: 8012 lines (3944 shaders, 3987 render pipelines, 81 compute pipelines) in 1.07 s on 18 workers before the first frame, progress screen not shown; bases 64 compiled, 3518 from the archive, 405 reused; 3987 specializations
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline prewarm done: …
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=dispatch_retain+0 lr=-[_MTLBinaryArchive materializeAirNTFromOnlineForSlice:entryList:]+0x1c4
[dm] bt: __55-[_MTLBinaryArchive airntSerializeToURL:options:error:]_block_invoke.230+0x228 _dispatch_client_callout+0x10 _dispatch_lane_barrier_sync_invoke_and_complete+0x38 __55-[_MTLBinaryArchive airntSerializeToURL:options:error:]_block_invoke+0x1b8 _dispatch_client_callout+0x10 _dispatch_lane_barrier_sync_invoke_and_complete+0x38 -[_MTLBinaryArchive airntSerializeToURL:options:error:]+0x180 arch_flush+0x1e0 __arch_flush_now_block_invoke+0xc _dispatch_call_block_and_release+0x20 …
launcher: the host exited with 139
```

`x0` is 0 at `dispatch_retain`: Metal retains a null object while it materializes an entry for serialization.

## What triggers it

At crash time `pso_archive/` held 10 files of bases with a vertex layout (`00123`–`00133.mtl4a`, written during the earlier session) and 16 `p*.mtl4a` files. 10 is more than `PSO_ARCH_COMPACT` (8), so `pso4_init` turns compaction on (`g_compact_opts.lookupArchives` = the run files). The prewarm then recaptures the bases it takes from those files through `ga_capture(b, g_compact_opts, nil)`. The flush after the prewarm (`arch_flush_now` → `arch_flush` → `serializeAsArchiveAndFlushToURL:`) is where Metal crashes. The crash happens before `arch_compact_finish`, so the old files remain, compaction runs again on the next start, and the game never starts again.

Confirmation: after moving the ten `0*.mtl4a` files out of `pso_archive/` (leaving the `p*` files), the game starts and runs again.

Not established yet: whether the null object belongs to a base recaptured through `lookupArchives`, or to something else that the serializer captured in the same flush. It is also unknown whether this is new with the macOS 27 / Metal 32023 toolchain: docs/development.md describes compaction working on Breath of the Wild.

## Workaround

Quit the game, move `~/Library/Application Support/nxnative/<title ID>/pso_archive/0*.mtl4a` somewhere else, and start again. It comes back once more than 8 such files have accumulated.

## Expected

Compaction should not be able to make the game unstartable. If the serializer cannot write recaptured bases on this system, the host should keep (or skip) the old files and start normally rather than crash every time.
title: Mac: pipeline archive compaction crashes the host in Metal's serializer (SIGSEGV in airntSerializeToURL), on every start once more than 8 run files exist

body:
`--platform mac-app` stops at the pipeline archive for ANIMAL WELL (`010020D01AD24000`):

```
[RED] pso_offline: no base to build
[RED] pso_offline.py exit code 1 (full output: …/010020D01AD24000_build/logs/pso_offline_mac.log)
```

`pso_offline_mac.log`:

```
pso_offline: 0 pairs: 0 bases, 0 left to the device (function constants), left out as the host leaves them: reflection 0, stage inputs 0, library 0, layer 0, entry 0 (0.0 s)
[RED] pso_offline: no base to build
```

**Cause:** `mac_app()` runs `mac_pso()` for an NVN game whenever `shader_pairs.tsv` exists, but ANIMAL WELL's table holds only its header line (0 pairs). `pso_offline.py` exits with an error when there are neither bases nor rest pairs (line 198), so the whole build fails. `mac_pso()` already handles "no archive" (no `*.mtl4a` → returns `None`, and the app builds what it needs on its first start); it just never gets there.

**Expected:** the app is packed without a pipeline archive, as with `--gpu none`.

**Workaround:** `--gpu none` packs the app (52 MB) without an archive.

**Possible fix:** treat zero pairs as "nothing to build" in `pso_offline.py` (exit 0 with no archive), or skip `mac_pso()` when the pair tables hold no pairs. Other profiles whose `shader_pairs.tsv` has no pairs, which may hit this if they're NVN: Bayonetta (`010076F0049A2000`), Bayonetta 2 (`01007960049A0000`), Hades, Hades II, Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth, Super Mario Galaxy 1/2, Balatro.

nxnative `c484b13`, macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2, M3 Max.
title: `--platform mac-app` fails when a profile's shader_pairs.tsv has no pairs (ANIMAL WELL): "pso_offline: no base to build"

body:
Found with the regression harness's usage count (#328 / #329), Mac host at 89744da7, M2 Max, a 60 s run of the Hades smoke route (title screen into the game). The game itself plays fine; the cost is CPU (and on an iPhone, power and heat).

HLE call counts for that run (`hlecount.tsv`):

| call | count in 60 s |
|---|---|
| `nn::nifm::IsNetworkRequestOnHold` | 951,890,659 |
| svc 0xB (SleepThread) | 951,904,347 |
| `nn::nifm::SubmitNetworkRequest` | 707,702 |
| `nn::nifm::IsNetworkAvailable` | 707,701 |
| `nn::nifm::CancelNetworkRequest` | 475,591 |

So one thread polls `IsNetworkRequestOnHold` with a yield in between (about 16 million times a second), while the request is submitted again about every 85 µs.

**Suspected cause (not verified):** `dm/host/hle_net.c` holds an offline request for `NIFM_HOLD_NS` (50 ms) after `SubmitNetworkRequest`, and every submit stores a new timestamp. With a submit every 85 µs the 50 ms never run out, so `IsNetworkRequestOnHold` stays true and the polling thread never sees the request settle. On Horizon, submitting a request that is already on hold doesn't restart its evaluation, as far as I know, so keeping the first submission time while a request is pending may be the root-cause fix. I haven't confirmed which thread does what, or the exact loop in the game.

To reproduce: run Hades for a minute with `DM_HLECOUNT=hlecount.tsv` (the counts `regress.py usage` in #329 collects) and look at the nifm rows.
title: Hades spins on the offline nifm request: ~952 million IsNetworkRequestOnHold calls in 60 s

body:
Building on @jthrilly's analysis in #272: one translator and one host serve every profile, but each of us can only test the games we own, and CI has no game files and no Metal 4 (#112). So a change that is well tested on its own games can still break others. Examples: c3a0880 broke SMT V and Yoshi (#173, #218, #272); my prepare step hangs on Odyssey (#294, #276); my offline pipeline archive fails on TotK (#283).

I'm pausing my own feature work (Arkham Knight, 4K) to help put a foundation in place first. Nothing here needs a feature freeze. Every step below is a small PR that stands on its own, keeps the current behaviour, and is proven before it lands.

## What the numbers say (upstream/main, last ~460 commits)

- **Merge conflicts sit in a few files.** `docs/development.md` (49 PRs), the generated `docs/agents/symptoms.md` (47), the games table (41), `dm/gfx/tests/Makefile` (36) and its `.gitignore` (28), plus 80 commits that edited the game count line in `AGENTS.md`. 28 of 58 open PRs are conflicting.
- **The host only accepts libraries built by its exact chain version.** `DMSH_CHAIN` was bumped 17 times in 15 days. Every bump rebuilds every game and moves every game onto an unvalidated translator. A cold rebuild of TotK takes 45 min for the Mac, 42 min for iOS and 7 min for the pipeline archive. The driver segment layout is written down twice: `nvn_mtl.m` and `dmsh_build.py`.
- **`nvn_mtl.m` has 10,617 lines and 1 MB (~290k tokens)** (10,961 on Oct 27, 11,178 on Oct 28, 11,944 on Oct 31). It holds about 780 `g_*` globals and 125 `getenv` calls; 40 tests include it, and it was touched in 144 commits and 75 PRs. An agent has to load all of it for a small change.
- **Only 14 of 63 gfx tests run in CI.** No test works at the frame level.
- **There are 229 `DM_*` variables, 66 of them undocumented.** The 39 profile keys, by contrast, are all documented.

## What stays

These are the right decisions and remain:
- one translator for every game;
- profiles with every fixed address gated by build ID;
- the per-service host;
- the record format with its static asserts;
- fail-soft sidecars and the `[RED]` discipline;
- the content-addressed Metal compile cache;
- the docs culture, including `test_docs.py`.

The problem is coupling and centralisation, not these decisions.

## Steps (each one a PR; the order puts safety before refactoring)

**Conflicts out of the way**
- [x] Issue forms, PR template, CONTRIBUTING.md (#306, landed as 81d53bfe)
- [x] gfx tests: the run list and `.gitignore` come from the sources (#307, landed as 6c4a81d4)
- [ ] Docs de-conflict: drop the game count from `AGENTS.md` (`test_docs` derives it), regenerate `symptoms.md` in CI, one file per reference entry for new findings (the game count: #398, landed as 3cf4c2d7; reference entries and the index merged with git's union driver, guarded by `test_docs`: #400; README's gallery written from a table: #401, landed as 9c52eaa; the symptom index regenerated on `main` by CI: #472; one file per entry left out, see #472)

**A safety net that knows every game**
- [x] `scripts/regress.py` (#328, building on #272's shader regression check; first results: it confirmed the #283 fix on TotK and found #334 on Hades), run locally on the games you own. It reports, per game, the translator diff (shaders newly failing or with changed MSL, by hash), boot smoke (frames reached, crash or hang, new `[RED]` lines, prepare time, frame times) and screenshot hashes. The report holds only numbers, hashes and shader keys; no game data leaves the machine.
- [x] One documented developer loop for people and agents: a single page (docs/agents) that lists every tool and when to use it (build and run, the GPU diagnostics from #225 and the dumps, `bench.py`, `regress.py`, what CI covers and what runs locally), with a "before you open a PR" checklist tiered by what changed. `AGENTS.md`, CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template point to it. It comes with the `regress.py` PR (#328).
- [x] Usage manifests (#329, landed as b3f97efe): each profile lists the NVN functions, services and shader features its game uses (names and counts only). `regress.py impact` then tells a PR author which games their change can reach, including games they don't own.
- [ ] `DM_NVN_CAPTURE` plus a replayer (design: #402): capture a few fixed frames per game once, then replay them against new code in seconds. Captures stay on the owner's disk; the repo keeps only image digests. (step 1, one frame: #473, landed as d9c2d5e7, with a `tex_fit` view fix the replay found. Open, in Breath of the Wild's note: fresh replays of one outdoors frame differ from the live frame and from each other in 3 to 124 pixels of two G-buffer targets, with segmented submission on or off. The variation follows the outcome of the G-buffer pass's depth-equal tests and points to the GPU (5d2bf73f). It stays open in the note. Step 3, `regress.py capture` and `regress.py replay`, landed as 8325eefb: one frame per game, and a candidate beyond twice the capture's noise is a `REGRESSION`. Next: several frames with pool deltas, step 2 of #402)
- [x] Reproducible bug reports without sharing game data:
  - `DM_REC` records a player's inputs with timestamps in `DM_KEYS` syntax. With the reporter's save and the same build, that replays the path to the bug. (#448, landed as 96820ed5, with `DM_KEYS=@<file>` for long recordings. Replay is frame-exact since 710559cf.)
  - A diagnostic bundle holds the log, the build and environment, and the pass list of the broken frame (shader keys, formats, draw state), with automatic per-pass findings: white or black output, NaN, flicker. It never contains textures, shaders or other game assets, and the bug report form asks for it (the form itself is in #306). First part, the log, build, device and settings without the pass list: #465, landed as f96d01ec.
- [ ] Nightly Metal tests on Apple silicon (all 63 gfx tests and the translator GPU tests), on a self-hosted runner or a scheduled job on the maintainer's machine.

**A reproducible setup**
- [ ] One command each for the tools: a Brewfile, `requirements.txt` and `global.json`, plus Dependabot for the Actions and a check that the committed translator matches its lock (#322, by @PrashantJi02)

**Code quality checks in CI** (free on GitHub's runners for public repos; each one is a ratchet, so nothing goes red today, only regressions do)
- [x] ASan, UBSan and TSan over every host and CPU gfx test, plus clang's static analyzer (host and texture tests: #412, landed as ce99604a with root fixes for #409, #410 and #411; the CPU gfx tests follow, now that #307 has landed; the static analyzer landed with #425 as a345f5b0)
  - Proposed by @relay4 below: `implicit-conversion` and `local-bounds` in the CI's ASan and UBSan builds, and a separate integer target for buffer and count arithmetic. LeakSanitizer, RealtimeSanitizer and TypeSanitizer as local audit tools with Homebrew Clang, not in CI. The RealtimeSanitizer finding, logging in the audio callback, is in #731 by @thehobbit85.
- [ ] A pre-commit hook with the fast checks (game files and keys refused, the lint ratchet with CI's pins, `test_docs`, the `DM_*` registry, the chain header), so `main` doesn't go red after a push (#407; the lint ratchet is on the dev loop's pre-PR list since 9333825d)
- [x] ruff and pyright for the Python toolchain (`dmsh_build.py`, the NSP script, the split) (#323, landed as 7f5ef415)
- [x] Coverage for the host, the CPU gfx tests and the Python tools, as a job summary with diff coverage per PR (Codecov becomes optional once the owner installs its app) (#439, landed as 68db7956: host 61.7%, CPU textures 85.4%, Python tools 51.9% at landing. The translator tests stay out of it for now.)
- [ ] CodeQL for Python and C: no workflow needed. The owner turns on CodeQL's **default setup** (Settings → Code security), which analyses Python, and C/C++ without a build step. CodeQL doesn't read Objective-C, so the `.m` half of the NVN layer stays with clang-tidy (#425). Not enabled on 2026-10-31: the Actions workflow list has no CodeQL entry, and no CodeQL check runs on `main`.
- [x] Fuzzing of the file parsers (NSP/NCA/NSO and the shader split's container readers), with synthetic seeds only (#455, landed as 7a3a8751: five harnesses, nightly; found 25 bugs, filed as #451–#454; #451 fixed in 39509760, one NSO loader for every tool that checks a module as Horizon does; #452 in 625a2600, #453 in 966f2017, #454 in 713ecaa4 from #605 by @mrkayhyun)
- [x] clang-tidy~~, plus clang-format on changed lines only (no reformatting of existing code)~~ (#425, landed as a345f5b0: a clang-tidy ratchet with the static analyzer that only shrinks, 273 findings as the baseline at landing. It found #424. The clang-format part is dropped. `.clang-format` cannot state the house style, and a root `.clang-format` would let editors reformat dense lines on save.)
- [ ] Work the baselines down once the checks are in: the lint ratchet's findings, clang-tidy's baseline (#425), the sanitizer ignorelist and `tsan.supp` entries that are not test fixtures (#412's real-bug suppressions are already gone: ce99604a), the fuzzer's expected failures (#455; all rows are gone since 713ecaa4, and `known.tsv` is empty). One small PR per finding or file, each fixed at its cause; the ratchets keep the numbers from growing back.
- [x] Rule for every PR: a bug found along the way gets its own issue or PR instead of riding along (followed for the sanitizer findings: #409–#411 and #443, the analyzer's: #424, fixed in 18d65b3e, the fuzzer's: #451–#454, all fixed (39509760, 625a2600, 966f2017, 713ecaa4), a stale generated header in the host tests: #466, landed as 201dfd12, and an ASan finding in `t_fpslock`: #648, landed as 9474a631)
- [x] Flaky tests fixed at their cause, starting with the audio device-stall check (#317, landed as b7654d49) and the Mac launcher's layout check (#445, fixed in e8f3a8f2)

**Decouple the chain**
- [x] `dmsh_abi.h` as the single source for the driver layout and binding kinds, read by both `dmsh_build.py` and the host, with a cross-check test (#391, landed as 03628c8e: identical host objects, all 19,592 BotW shaders unchanged; reviewing it found a binding-kind mismatch in the `DM_NVN_RT_RANGE` check, fixed in 2f1a0442)
- ~~The host loads libraries by ABI compatibility.~~ Dropped: the host is built into the IPA or Mac app, and the NSP script builds it and the shader libraries in the same run, so a new host never meets old libraries in practice. The real cost of a chain change is rebuilding the shaders, which the fingerprints below address.
- [x] Per-pass fingerprints in `dmsh_build.py`, so a tool change rebuilds only the shaders whose output changes (#467, landed as d0b7c846: a comment, docstring or layout edit no longer translates every shader again; a split per pass was analysed and left out, since most edits land in code every shader runs through. For the same reason @seedds moved the tool lock checks out of the chain in faabe056.)
- [x] Game files stay on the device for repeated iPhone builds: the RomFS, which changes only with the game's version, goes to the app's `Documents/romfs.img` once per game and version, and every later build is a slim IPA (host, modules, shaders). A cold Breath of the Wild build on an M2 Max took 53 min: shaders 27.2 (19,592, Mac and iOS), IPA pack 10.9 (14.7 GB, nearly all RomFS), shader split 7.3, app build 5.0 (pipeline archive about 4.5), extraction 2.7. The pack is the step every rebuild pays. The parts exist (`push_romfs.sh`, `main.m` reading the image, `DM_COPY_ROMFS=NO` in #478); missing are an NSP script option (`--romfs separate`), a RomFS identity (title, version, digest) so a mismatched image is refused with a clear message instead of a crash, and docs that make it the route for repeated builds. #478 and #493, landed as 32ae3b11 and 9ac535bb: `--romfs separate`, and `romfs.id` checked by the app at start. The add-on content follows the same way (`Documents/aoc`, #486 and its follow-up), and NX2Apple's installer pushes the image once per game and version, then installs slim IPAs; the identity file is the interface between the two.
- [x] An incremental pipeline archive, keyed per pair (about 4.5 of the 53 min, so behind the item above and #275)
- [x] Incremental IPA and Mac app builds: unchanged IPA entries and derived-profile shader outputs are reused (#279, by @surajmandalcell, landed as 09f3778c)
- [x] Shader builds compile only the metallibs a target needs, so an iPhone build skips the macOS half (#275, by @JMRBDev, landed as 712eb816)
- [x] A `chain_validated` row per profile, so each game shows which chain it was last green on (#464: `regress.py --record`, `dm/games/<id>/validated.tsv`; landed as 76c54532)

**Rules that enforce themselves**
- [x] Docs that still name removed switches corrected (#312, landed as de135721)
- [x] An environment registry, with a test that fails on an unregistered `getenv("DM_…")`. #318, every `DM_*` switch listed with its meaning taken from the commit history (landed as cc626e7f, with `test_env_switches.py`).
- [ ] Architecture checks as ordinary tests in `dm/tools/tests`, written as ratchets: today's state is the baseline, and a check fails only when things get worse. Examples: file size limits, no game-specific branches in the host core. First: no title IDs in the host (#422, landed as c7da003c; build IDs outside the classified host rows are stopped by `docs_patches.py` through `test_docs`). A generated index of every game-specific patch, with a note per `patches.py` on whether a general rule could replace it, landed as 68fbe843 (`docs/agents/game-patches.md`, checked by `test_docs`). @seedds's #635 goes further: every patch states what it depends on and how loosely it could be bound (ed0360b2 and later); file size limits wait for a decision (nvn_mtl.m grew 2,221 lines in three days).
- [x] Size limits for C, Objective-C and Python, as a ratchet so nobody, person or agent, piles another 10,000 lines into one file: a file over the limit (aiming under 1,000 lines per file, new files at most about 800, lowered step by step as modules come out; third-party code excluded) may not grow, and a new file may not start over it; functions over a length limit are flagged by clang-tidy's `readability-function-size` in #425's ratchet (lizard does the same for Python). The numbers are @seedds's call. Comes after the `nvn_mtl.m` split, which brings the largest file from 11,923 lines to topic parts of at most 1,467.

**Extract, one module at a time, each proven by identical object code or replay digests**
- [ ] A mechanical split of `nvn_mtl.m` into included fragments, still one translation unit (an updated #133, re-cut by a script, `dm/tools/split_nvn_mtl.py`, so it can be redone on any `main` instead of waiting for a quiet hour). On its own this only helps reading: every part still sees every static. It is the first step, not the goal. (#479, re-cut on 2006d5ed: 632 lines stay in `nvn_mtl.m`, 14 parts from 342 to 1,467 lines, same machine code apart from `res_add_at` line numbers. It conflicts with today's `main` again.)
- [ ] A coupling measure as a second fitness function, since line counts are only a proxy. `dm/tools/coupling.py` reads clang's JSON AST (`clang -fsyntax-only -Xclang -ast-dump=json`, which works while the parts are still one translation unit) and, per part or module, counts:
  - the mutable file-scope variables it touches that another part defines (an extracted module should reach zero: everything through its interface);
  - which parts it calls and is called from, and the cycles between them;
  - once modules are files of their own, the symbols each imports and exports (`nm`) and its includes (`clang -MM`).
  A baseline table and a test in `dm/tools/tests` fail when a number grows, like the lint ratchet. It comes right after the split (before it, everything is one file) and orders the decoupling: the least entangled part goes first, and each decoupling PR shows how far its numbers fell.
- [x] Right after the split, the decoupling: `shlib` (the shader library loader, ~500 lines; it is the ABI boundary), then `pso`, `present` and `diag`, each a module with its own header and interface instead of shared statics, one PR each. Each is checked with replayed frames (`DM_NVN_CAPTURE`, #473) before and after, plus `regress.py`. The size limit below goes down as modules come out.
- [ ] Per-build host tables (`hle_fpslock.c`, `hle_uemalloc.c`) become profile rows (#339 adds Arkham Knight's rows to both, in today's form; they move with the rest). #339 is closed. Arkham Knight landed separately in d8bc9210, with one UE3 row in `hle_uemalloc.c`. #635 removes most Unreal rows another way: the rewriter finds FMallocBinned3 and the console variables by name, with no build ID (51904e70, 602ed115). The rows left are for builds that have nothing to find by name. On 2026-10-31 `hle_fpslock.c` holds 11 rows for 7 builds and `hle_uemalloc.c` one row (Arkham Knight). Moving them to profile rows waits on #492, the run-time profile proposal, which has no reply yet.

**A clear platform scope**
- [ ] A short "Supported platforms" section in the README, as tiers. Tier 1 is supported and tested: Apple silicon Macs on macOS 26+, iPhones with an A17 Pro or later on iOS 26+, iPads with an M1 or later. Everything else (Intel Macs, GPUs without Metal 4, iOS below 26, tvOS) is out of scope upstream; forks are welcome to carry it. Changing a tier goes through an issue. PRs like #310 and #189 show the question keeps coming up, and the answer is the maintainer's to give. (#446)
- [ ] Make the requirements hard to miss: today they are one sentence under the games list, and the same question keeps coming in as issues (#165, #8, #4, #54). A "Requirements" line near the top of the README and again in the install steps, the same tiers in CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue forms (#306), with a required "my device meets the requirements" checkbox in the bug form. In part: #306 (CONTRIBUTING.md and the forms), #333 (the build requirements in the README). (#446)
- [x] The build Mac's toolchain is part of the scope: the README states the tested one (macOS 26.6+, Xcode 27.1 / Metal 32023.921, the chain's lock), the shader build stops on a different Metal compiler unless overridden, and `spirv-cross` is pinned with the chain like the translator, so every Mac produces the same MSL (#242: corruption on an M5 and an iPhone 17 built with Xcode 26). PRs: #333 (the tested Metal compiler), #337 (spirv-cross pinned), landed together as 4eeac03a.
- [x] CI builds and tests with that toolchain: the macOS jobs run on GitHub's `xcode-27` image with Xcode 27.1 named in `DEVELOPER_DIR`, the build check compares the runner's Metal compiler with `dmsh_chain.lock`, and a test keeps the workflow, README and the NSP script naming the same Xcode (#421, landed as ce99604a). Until now CI used Xcode 26.6, which inlined differently and made known TSan races appear under other names in #412.

**Triage, so issues and PRs find each other**

When this was written, 61 open issues had no label, 24 had no reply, none of the 74 open PRs linked the issue it fixes, some were already covered by `main` (#315, #316, both closed since), and 33 of the 74 conflicted with it. On Oct 27: 78 open issues, none labelled, 33 without a reply; 121 open PRs, 60 of them conflicting. On Oct 31: 112 open issues, one of them labelled, 64 without a reply, and 183 open PRs.
- [ ] Area labels from the changed paths: `host`, `nvn`, `shader chain`, `packing`, `tools`, `docs`, …, `game: <title ID>` and `new game`, applied by a workflow that never runs PR code (#408). The issue forms set their own label.
- [ ] A keyword check on new issues for devices outside Tier 1 (Intel, iOS below 26, A16 and older) that answers with the requirements from the README. No model, no secret. (#462, on #446)
- [ ] A regular triage report on open PRs and issues: which PRs are already in `main`, which conflict and since when, which issue each PR fixes, and likely duplicates (several profiles for one title ID, for example). Generated by a script from the API by fixed rules, not by anyone's judgement, so it can run on a schedule and anyone can check it; the maintainer decides what to close. Where it is posted (its own issue, a Discussion or a page) is still open. Later, after the items above.

## What only the repository owner can switch on

Each of these is optional and takes one click:
- Discussions, for design questions like this one;
- branch protection with a merge queue;
- Copilot code review on all PRs, via a ruleset (Settings → Rulesets → "Automatically request Copilot code review"). It needs a Copilot plan on your account, and GitHub offers Copilot Pro at no cost to maintainers of popular open source repositories: if you qualify, Copilot settings (avatar → Copilot settings) shows "Get access to GitHub Copilot" ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/manage-your-account/get-free-access-to-copilot-pro)). A second, independent review on every PR would help with the volume of PRs coming in;
- CodeQL's default setup (see the item above);
- a weekly release tag.

I'm happy to set these up and to do the work above.

@JMRBDev, your Wonder data in #272 is exactly what the translator diff would report automatically. Anyone who owns games we don't have: running `regress.py` on them (it landed with #328) is the most useful thing you can do.

_Status (Oct 31): the boxes are ticked once the PRs land. Landed since Oct 28: #448 (96820ed5, frame-exact replay in 710559cf), #425 (a345f5b0, without the clang-format report), #439 (68db7956), the fix for #454 (713ecaa4, from #605) and `regress.py capture` and `replay` (8325eefb). #339 is closed, since Arkham Knight landed separately in d8bc9210. Open now: #322, #400, #407, #408, #422, #446, #457, #462, #472, #479, #486. Next, in this order: the `nvn_mtl.m` split (#479, re-cut on 2006d5ed, conflicting again with today's `main`), the coupling measure, then `shlib` as the first module, checked with `regress.py replay`. Also open: several frames per capture (step 2 of #402), the Breath of the Wild replay noise from #473, and two more timed rebuilds, one with nothing changed and one with a real chain change, to complete the picture of where a rebuild spends its time. Graphical front ends have their own issue: #388._
title: Roadmap: keeping every game green as the project grows

body:
Two Ubisoft Mario + Rabbids games have no profile. A provisional Mac build (`scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac`, current main) does not produce a bootable app for either. Filing this so the bring-up notes are in one place. No game files or keys attached.

## Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle

- Title ID `010067300059A000`, update v589824, display version 1.9.589692
- SDK 4.4.0 (`NintendoSDK_NVN-4_4_0`). Modules: `main`, `subsdk0` (GLSLC, build `3758eb95355911f578cd54846e006a5a`), `sdk`
- Markers: NVN, Havok, Wwise, and an Unreal string in `main`
- RomFS is 4004 files / 2.82 GB, all under `moria/sdf/` (`.sdfdata`, plus `.sdftoc` / `.sdfver` / `.mapping` / `.mchunks`). No top-level BNSH/BAHS
- `main` holds 1 GLSL source and calls `glslcCompile` in `subsdk0`, so the script boots the game to capture run-time shaders

### 1. GLSLC jump table the rewriter rejected

`patch_nso.py` stopped on `subsdk0` with `AssertionError: jump table 7340b8`.

The site is the existing `check_before_copy` form, with the `mov` 71 instructions back instead of within 64, because another switch sits in between:

```
subsdk0+0x733f94  mov  w18, w17
...
subsdk0+0x7340a8  cmp  w17, #4
subsdk0+0x7340ac  b.hi ...
subsdk0+0x7340b0  ldrsw x18, [x9, x18, lsl #2]
subsdk0+0x7340b4  add  x18, x18, x9
subsdk0+0x7340b8  br   x18
```

Nothing writes `w17` or `w18` between the `mov` and the `cmp`. Widening that lookback from 64 to 96 instructions lets `subsdk0` rewrite (`br` sites: 7). `main` and `sdk` already rewrote. The lookback is only used after the other jump-table forms have failed.

```diff
-    for q in range(kl - 3, max(0, kl - 64) - 1, -1):
+    for q in range(kl - 3, max(0, kl - 96) - 1, -1):
```

### 2. SIGBUS during DT_INIT, before any shader is captured

After that fix the heap check / GLSLC capture boots the game, reports a 0.10 GB heap, then dies in a static constructor. `nnMain` is never reached, so the capture saves 0 shaders and the script stops.

```
[dm] main: DT_INIT +0x24 (init_array 5214 entries)
[dm] CRASH sig=10 addr=0x20000ffff pc=main+0xea25b8 lr=main+0xea25b4
x0=0 x1=0x200000000 x21=0x200000000
```

The faulting instruction is `strb w19, [x21, x8]` with `x8 = 0xffff`, so the address is `x21 + 65535`. `x21` is `0x200000000`, which is not a mapped guest pointer. The caller (`main+0xea6a9c`) is itself a constructor invoked from the init array at `main+0x148`.

### 3. Shaders are inside `moria/sdf`

Even with a boot, `shader_split.py` has no reader for `.sdfdata`. The one GLSL source in `main` is not enough to draw the game.

## Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope

- Title ID `0100317013770000`, update v393216, display version 1.6.2225577
- SDK 13.3.5. Modules: `main` and `sdk` only (no GLSLC module)
- Same markers (NVN, Havok, Wwise, Unreal string). RomFS is 352 files / 5.86 GB, again entirely `moria/sdf/*.sdfdata`
- Provisional build: `main` and `sdk` rewrite, heap check reports 0.01 GB, then shader split stops:

```
[RED] the shader split found no shaders in main or the RomFS: the game keeps them in a form shader_split.py does not read
```

So this one does not even get a play boot. The blocker is the same archive, not the jump-table bug.

## What a recipe would need

A reader for Ubisoft's `moria/sdf` containers (shaders, and whatever else the RomFS is hiding), then a real boot past Kingdom Battle's DT_INIT SIGBUS. I do not have either, so this is not a profile yet.
title: Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle and Sparks of Hope: moria/sdf archives, GLSLC jump table, Kingdom Battle SIGBUS in DT_INIT

body:
## Problem

Currently, nxnative produces standalone IPA packages that include the complete game data. When users rebuild an IPA after updating nxnative or making changes to the host, graphics implementation, or rewriter, they generally need to sign, transfer, and reinstall the entire package.

For larger games, this can mean repeatedly transferring several gigabytes of unchanged data.

This affects two common scenarios:

- **Developers and contributors:** Frequent testing of new builds on physical iPhones or iPads, particularly when investigating device-specific bugs that cannot be reproduced on macOS.
- **Regular users:** Rebuilding and sideloading their own game ports after pulling upstream updates, applying fixes, or switching to a newer version of nxnative.

In both cases, most game resources remain unchanged between builds, making repeated full-IPA transfers unnecessarily time-consuming.

## Existing Support

nxnative already provides some relevant functionality:

- `--prepare-xcode` supports direct deployment through Xcode, with incremental resource synchronization during subsequent builds.
- `dm/ios/Sources/main.m` supports loading RomFS from `Documents/romfs`, taking precedence over the bundled resources.
- [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) demonstrates a slim IPA approach with separately deployed game resources.

However, the Xcode workflow primarily serves users with a suitable Apple development environment, while those relying on standalone IPA packages and third-party sideloading tools still face the overhead of repeatedly transferring bundled game data.

The upstream packaging workflow currently lacks an officially supported option for generating lightweight IPA updates that reuse previously installed resources.

## Proposal

Consider introducing an optional resource-separated packaging and update workflow for iOS.

Possible improvements include:

1. **Thin IPA packaging:** Allow generating an IPA without embedding the full RomFS, while preserving the existing standalone IPA workflow as the default.
2. **Persistent game resources:** Support an initial resource deployment followed by lightweight application updates that reuse the existing `Documents/romfs`.
3. **Simplified update workflow:** Provide a documented way for users to generate and install updated application packages without repeating the entire resource transfer.
4. **Installation compatibility:** Document the behavior of different signing and sideloading methods, particularly whether application data is preserved when updating an existing installation.
title: Provide a resource-separated iOS deployment workflow for faster physical-device iteration

**Odyssey (0100000000010000, v393216): the "Preparing pipelines" step deadlocks mid-list — progress freezes at ~6,000 of 20,740 and never advances or times out (main@4639c51, chain 8393d85a4eae, Mac).**

- The on-screen progress line and the log's last prebuild line both stop at `pipeline prebuild: 6000 of 20740 pairs, 1991 built, 4009 already archived, 0 left to the draws, 0 failed` — the game keeps presenting the progress screen forever (left 10+ min), and every boot lands at the same number.
- During the frozen phase the same-core handoff cap logs hits: `same-core wake handoff hit its 5000 us cap` ×6 (we carry the bounded variant of `dm_yield_to_core_peers` from #247; the wait gives up but the prebuild's progress never recovers) — so it looks like the prepare workers fall into the same unrecoverable-wait family as #247/#259, not a slow compile.
- Smaller lists complete fine here: TotK 20,016 pairs → 15,437 bases in 318 s ("done"); Silksong 1,185 pairs done; Hades II 0. Only Odyssey (the largest list with 27,984 shaders, cache 103,187 entries) hangs.
- Workaround we ship: `DM_PSO_PREPARE=0` — the game boots straight through (11,700 frames in 200 s at the title, CRASH 0, RED 0) with the prewarm in the background and the hybrid stand-ins covering the gaps.

Happy to run any instrumented build on this list if useful.
title: Odyssey: "Preparing pipelines" deadlocks at ~6,000 of 20,740 (handoff-cap hits during the freeze) — DM_PSO_PREPARE=0 works around

body:
A rebuild after a small change (a host fix, a rewriter tweak, a pull) takes almost as long as the first build, even though most of the inputs did not change.

The stage keys already skip extraction, the rewrite and the shaders when their inputs are the same. Two places still redo everything:

**1. Packing the IPA.** `dm/ios/tools/pack_ipa.py` reads, deflates and writes every file on every run, including a RomFS of many GB. On Breath of the Wild (16.4 GB IPA, Apple M4 Pro, USB SSD), repacking after a change to the executable alone took 105-163 s. Almost all of that is rewriting data that is already on disk.

**2. Rebuilding a game version the profile was not brought up on.** For a derived (or provisional) profile, the NSP script turns off reuse for the shader stages: `own = bool(provisional or derived)` reaches `split_shaders(..., provisional=True)`, which writes no reuse key. So every rebuild splits all the shaders again. A rebuild of Breath of the Wild 1.6.0 (profile registered for 1.9.0) with nothing changed took 884 s, and the shader split ran again for all 19,420 shaders.

Expected: a rebuild where only the host or the app changed should only redo the host, the app and the final pack, on iOS (IPA) and on the Mac (`--platform mac-app`).
title: Rebuilds redo work that did not change (IPA repack, derived-profile shader split)

Packing ToTK (1.4.3) as a Mac app after 4639c51 (#241, #260) fails at the new pipeline archive step. `metal-tt` refuses 11 of the 24,153 bases because the fragment function reads a `[[user(locnN)]]` input the vertex function does not write. One rejected pipeline fails the whole archive, so the build stops. All 11 pairs come from `pso_pairs.tsv` (agl BAHS program variations), which `vs_pad` does not read, so their vertex shaders are not padded.

### Environment

- nxnative 4639c51, shader chain `8393d85a4eae`
- MacBook Pro M4 Pro (`applegpu_g16s`), macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Xcode 26.3 (17C529)
- Metal toolchain 32023.864. The build warns that the tested toolchain is 32023.921 (`dmsh_chain.lock`). I have not checked whether 32023.921's `metal-tt` behaves differently.

### Reproducing

```
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NSP folder> -k <prod.keys> --platform mac-app
```

### Log output

```
✓ [5/7] Mac shaders (14:01): 28,667 of 28,669 shaders ready (0 from the cache); 2 failed, ...
✓ [6/7] Mac host (0:16): .../0100F2C0115B6000_build/tools/dmhost
✗ [7/8] Pipeline archive (5:00)
pso_offline: 24175 pairs: 24153 bases, 0 left to the device (function constants), left out as the host leaves them: reflection 0, stage inputs 0, library 0, layer 22, entry 0 (10.9 s)
pso_offline: applegpu_g16s: metal-tt, 24153 bases (minutes) ...
[RED] pso_offline: metal-tt failed for applegpu_g16s (exit 1): applegpu-nt: note: Fragment input(s) `user(locn1)` mismatching vertex shader output type(s) or not written by vertex shader
applegpu-nt: error: plugin '.../Metal.xctoolchain/usr/metal/32023/lib/wrapper-nt.dylib' cannot emit pipeline
(the note and error repeat 3 times)
air-tt: applegpu-nt command failed
air-tt: air-tt command failed
```

### The pairs

The notes do not name the pipelines. I compared every render pipeline descriptor in `pso/mac-work/bases.mtl4-json` against the MSL beside the libraries (`<key>_b.metal`). For each pipeline, I checked the `[[user(locnN)]]` fields of the vertex entry's return struct against the pixel shader's `[[stage_in]]` struct. 11 pairs have a fragment input with no matching vertex output. No pair had a type mismatch.

| vertex | entry | pixel | fragment input not written by the vertex shader |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0a91af5bef8578e2` | main0 | `3738395491f81ace` | locn1 (float4) |
| `0a91af5bef8578e2` | main0 | `42021637b83e615c` | locn1 (float4) |
| `0a91af5bef8578e2` | main0 | `68e9e237477fb7ca` | locn1 (float4) |
| `0a91af5bef8578e2` | main0 | `78c5b3edf2b0330f` | locn1 (float4) |
| `ed2c672cde57308b` | main0 | `68e9e237477fb7ca` | locn1 (float4) |
| `babbebb3901e5540` | main0 | `ab1edf029d475b9b` | locn6 (float4) |
| `babbebb3901e5540` | main0 | `dbdae732000612c3` | locn6 (float4) |
| `d8e0fdcd89a01a2b` | main0 | `92a245d0946376b4` | locn6 (float4) |
| `d8e0fdcd89a01a2b` | main0 | `96e3b74f94535e9d` | locn6 (float4) |
| `d8e0fdcd89a01a2b` | main0 | `a4d27d6f2a2935a5` | locn6 (float4) |
| `d8e0fdcd89a01a2b` | main0 | `eae6d9fb4abcabc0` | locn6 (float4) |

For example, `0a91af5bef8578e2_bp.metallib` and `_b.metallib` write only `user(locn0)`, while `3738395491f81ace_b.metallib` reads `user(locn0)` and `user(locn1)`. Every pair is in the build's `shader/pso_pairs.tsv` and none is in the profile's `shader_pairs.tsv`.


### Workaround atm 

`--gpu none` packs the app without the archive, and the app builds the pipeline bases on its first start. The iOS IPA is not affected: TotK's profile does not set `pso_mtl4`, so `PSO_GPUS` defaults to `none`.
title: pso_offline: metal-tt fails on ToTK's pso_pairs.tsv pairs whose pixel shader reads an output the vertex shader does not write

body:
This issue is fundamentally about how this project manages the deluge of changes that are landing in such a way so as fixes for one game don't break others. Please read the below @seedds! Cheers.

## What happened

c3a0880 (from #178, "Guard Metal image atomics") was validated thoroughly on Pokémon Legends: Z-A: all 28,603 shaders, GPU probes and a 240 s run. Even so, it broke at least two games outside that set:

- **SHIN MEGAMI TENSEI V** (#173): the host aborts with `FATAL [RED] image atomics: unsupported or overflowing IMG extent` at the first atomic on a buffer image. #263 fixes the reflection side.
- **Yoshi's Crafted World** (#218): the same abort about 6 s in, on compute shader `a94ca5c952ce0d72`. In addition, the translator now rejects 3 of its shaders (`572c1b843ca32afb`, `8dbd4ee9b3da30d4`, `f0b33a6b4f3cc64f`) because they use the value an image atomic returns, and it changes `a94ca5c952ce0d72` to read 0. Builds made with shaders from before c3a0880 run fine.

Neither failure is a mistake in the testing of #178. The project has one shader chain (`DMSH_CHAIN`) for every game, so each translator or host change affects all of the roughly 70 profiles. But it can only be checked on the games its author owns, and no contributor owns them all. CI can't help either, since it can't hold game files or run Metal 4 (#112).

## What the existing tests miss

- `dm/tools/tests/test_image_atomic_bounds.py` already builds synthetic Maxwell shaders from `InstTable.cs` and runs them through the translator, `spirv-val` and `spirv-cross`, with no game inputs. In CI, though, the translator cases are skipped: `DMSH_TEST_XLATE` is unset, and `spirv-cross` and `spirv-val` aren't installed.
- The same test asserts that an atomic whose result is used **must** be rejected (`require IGN with a discarded result`). That is the pattern Yoshi uses, so the regression was locked in as intended behaviour. Nothing told the author that shipping games depend on it.
- When shaders fail to translate, `dmsh_build.py` exits 0 and the NSP script packs the app anyway with "N of M shaders ready; K failed". The first sign is a crash at run time, often long after the change, once a rebuild picks up the new chain.

## Proposal

Every item works for any contributor and in CI. None needs game files, keys, Metal or a particular contributor owning a particular game.

1. **Run the translator fixture tests in CI.** Point `DMSH_TEST_XLATE` at the committed `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin`, and install the .NET runtime and `spirv-cross`/`spirv-val` in `tool-tests`. The Metal compile step (`DMSH_TEST_METAL`) stays local. This is small: about 15 lines of workflow.
2. **A synthetic fixture for each pattern a game turns up.** When a game hits a translator gap, the fix comes with a hand-encoded shader reproducing the instruction pattern, as `test_image_atomic_bounds.py` already does. For this case, that means a SUATOM/SURED with a used result, plus a buffer-image binding, replacing the assertion that requires rejection.
3. **Report shader regressions against the contributor's own previous build.** `dmsh_build.py` compares the new `_b_build.json` with the previous one in the same build folder. It prints the shaders that used to translate and now fail, with reasons, and the NSP script stops unless told to continue. Nothing is committed: every contributor gets the check for the games they own.
4. **A per-profile instruction census (for discussion).** `shader_split.py` already decodes every shader to make the profile's tables. It could also write per-shader counts of the instruction forms the translator treats specially (for example SUATOM with a used result, by clamp mode). Like `shader_facts.tsv`, it would hold only hashes and counts, no game code. The translator would declare the forms it rejects, and a CI test would list every profile whose census contains one. A PR that rejects a form used by a shipping game would then name those games, even when its author doesn't own them. Profiles without a census report "unknown" rather than pass, so it can be filled in gradually by people who own each game.

Ruled out: golden MSL outputs and committed per-game translation baselines. Both need the game to verify, and golden MSL is code derived from the game.

A smaller question: should the image-atomic admission skip the one dispatch with a `[RED]` line instead of aborting the app? I understand the abort is deliberate, since an unchecked atomic must never reach a dummy buffer. Skipping writes nothing, so it keeps that guarantee while a game keeps running.

## Offer

I'm happy to open PRs for items 1 to 3 now, as separate small PRs (2 together with the Yoshi translator fix). Item 4 changes what a profile holds, so I'd like your view first. Does the census sound acceptable, and would you prefer it in `shader_facts.tsv` or a separate table?

Related: #178, #263, #173, #218, #112.
title: Catch translator and host changes that break games nobody on the PR owns

body:
## Pokémon Violet: GPU BIF0 read page faults (wild VAs) freeze the game when the imgui text pipeline renders

**TL;DR** — Pokémon Violet freezes deterministically (~60 s) when UI text renders after loading a save. The GPU raises repeated BIF0 **read** page faults at wildly varying VAs, wedging the submission. Five independent runs all show the **same last-encoded draw**: the game's imgui text pipeline (`vs c77b47182ae6261f_b` + `fs da917a747d97908e_b`), yet that pipeline's MSL contains no out-of-bounds access. Every app-side hypothesis I could test has been ruled out (details below); I could not identify the faulting access and would appreciate help.

**环境 / Environment**: macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Pro (24 GB), Pokémon Violet `01008F6008C5E000` v720896, dm @ `main` (438f905 era; the fault predates every commit on my branch).

### Fault signature

From `gpuEvent-*` GPU reports across runs (all `is_read=true`, varying BIF0 requestors 1/17/33/49/97/113):

| VA | notes |
| --- | --- |
| `0x40` | 3 runs — reading a field at +0x40 through a NULL base |
| `0x2080`, `0xE000` | null base + offset |
| `0xC6003600` | 2 reports, same run, different requestors |
| `0x100C603xxxx`, `0x500ffdae200` | real-looking VAs (possibly in-pool / buffer-range) |

The wedge repeats every submission afterwards (`[RED] state of the failed submission fence=N: frame N-1; passes +119 …`), so the frozen picture never recovers.

### Correlation: the imgui text pipeline

I adapted the scenecap scene-capture tool (credit: oneincase/MacNativeGames `feat/scenecap-tool`) to this host and added a ring that records the last 48 drawn shader pairs, dumped on fault. **Five runs, five different play sessions: the last encoded draw is always** `vs c77b47182ae6261f_b + fs da917a747d97908e_b` (the `titanspecialimgui var0` text pipeline; the earlier opening-cutscene fault had `vs 5d42cbeb294d6f1c_b` + the same fragment).

But the MSL of that draw cannot fault on its own:
- the vertex stage reads **only** `spvDescriptorSet0.vp_c0._m0[100].x` (byte offset `0x640`, which dm fills with 0 — in bounds) and computes quad corners arithmetically; no other memory access;
- the fragment stage samples one texture (the glyph atlas; dummy fallback verified).

### What I ruled out (each with an experiment, commits on my branch)

| hypothesis | experiment | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| in-flight rewrite of host-lent command segments | fence-gate reuse + full no-reuse mode | gate caught 6 real in-flight recycles, **faults continued** |
| in-flight races in general | `DM_SYNC_SUBMIT=1`: CPU waits for GPU completion of every submission | **faults continued** at frame ~1200 |
| memory-pool residency | `DM_RES_ALL=1`: every pool wired at creation | faults continued |
| vertex stream / index / TFB bindings | probe dumping all bindings for 64 text-pipeline draws | all healthy, all resolve to valid GPU addresses |
| stale argument-block reuse | `ab_pass` guard audited (global monotonic serial) | sound |
| NULL/zero in the encoded descriptor | zero-slot scan of every encode of that pipeline | **never a zero entry**, always valid arena addresses |
| undefined argument-table entries | `initializeBindings = YES` on all tables | faults continued |
| the recorded command stream | two faulting-frame scene captures replayed offline (416–469 passes each) | **both replay fully clean**, pixel-exact exports |
| geometry path, encode-thread mode, the 60 fps timing patch | activity logs / `DM_PV_NO_PATCH` | no activity / already exonerated |

With full serialization, healthy bindings, valid descriptors and clean replays all confirmed, the faulting read is not explainable from app-observable state — it looks like either the MTL4 argument-table update-visibility semantics interacting with dm's shared `g_vt`/`g_ft` tables (per-draw capture vs live-object mutation), or something at the driver layer.

### Reproduce (~60 s, no gameplay needed)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/peachtaozhutou/nxnative && cd nxnative && git checkout scenecap-pv
# build the dm host for the Violet title id, then launch with the capture hooks and drive text:
echo 'A' >> $DM_CTL   # title → continue → in game; dialog text renders
# GPU faults appear within ~60 s of text rendering; the log then dumps
# "fault-keys" (last 48 shader pairs) and the residency ring at the fault.
```

The fault also fires on the title screen by itself in some runs (frame ~884–944).

### Attachments

- [save + fault evidence](https://github.com/peachtaozhutou/nxnative/tree/pv-hang-evidence) (`pv-save-hang.zip` = the save that freezes, `failed-submissions.txt`, `fault-keys-last48.txt`)
- probes & hardening commits: branch [`scenecap-pv`](https://github.com/peachtaozhutou/nxnative/tree/scenecap-pv) (11 commits: key ring, residency ring, crash-time capture flush, `DM_NVN_GPUTRACE`, `DM_SYNC_SUBMIT`, `DM_SEG_NOREUSE`, `DM_RES_ALL`, bind_vbufs/initializeBindings hardening)
- faulting-frame scene captures (`/tmp/pv-scene*.nvs`, 130–280 MB) available on request

### Ask

I'm out of app-side observable state to check. Any pointer on where to look next — especially anything about `MTL4ArgumentTable` update visibility semantics with shared tables across draws, or known BIF0 fault patterns with `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy` pools — would be very welcome. 更详细的中文复现说明可以看上面分支里的提交记录;存档在附件里,随时可以提供更多信息。
