body:
## What happens

FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE (`0100606026F12000`, update 1.0.1 / v65536), packed with `--platform mac-app`, boots to the title screen and plays the opening movie at 60 fps. Starting a **New Game** aborts the host every time (2 of 2 runs), about 17–21 s after launch, right after the opening movie stops:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] FATAL [RED] image atomics: unsupported or overflowing IMG extent (shader f3c5ced35cb619d0_b stage 5 slot 2 texture 2142)
[dm] CRASH sig=6 addr=__pthread_kill+0x8 ...
[dm] bt: abort+0x94 encode_args_+0x4e38 mtl_exec+0x47a4 h_nvnQueueSubmitCommands+0x180 dm_bigstack_enter+0x74 main+0x1443a2c ...
launcher: the host exited with 134
```

Just before the abort, the same run also logs a compute shader that wasn't built:

```
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] failed to load shader 41b20b5f09269ad8_b: cannot open .../Resources/msl/b-20fe3d62b9f6/41b20b5f09269ad8_b.metallib
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] shader 41b20b5f09269ad8 (compute) failed to load: build the shaders with dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py first
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] the dispatched program has no compute shader (or it is not mapped)
```

## Why I think it happens

This looks like a regression from **c3a0880**, "Guard Metal image atomics and reject unsupported bindings", 2026-10-25. Two symptoms point to it:

1. **Shader build: 850 failures instead of the game note's 11.** The Mac shader stage reported `72,646 of 73,496 shaders ready; 850 failed`, with these reasons:
   ```
   shaders 73496: ok 72646, translation failed 850
     [translation failed]   842  NotSupportedException: MSL 2.3 image atomics require IGN with a discarded result; TRAP/returning semantics are not implemented.
     [translation failed]     8  NotSupportedException: MSL 2.3 bounded image atomics support non-indexed 32-bit buffer/2D/2D-array images only.
   ```
   The game note (`dm/games/0100606026F12000/README.md`) lists only 11 unbuilt shaders: 3 geometry, plus 8 compute shaders with 3D image atomics.

2. **Runtime: the new guard aborts instead of degrading.** At c1b7eff, `imga_extent()` returns 0 for any texture that isn't a texture buffer, 2D or 2D array, and also for a texture type that doesn't match the binding (`t.textureType != b->dtt`). `encode_args` then calls `MDIE(...)`. The game note says this game uses 3D image atomics, and the build log shows a 3D-indexed atomic (`cp_i_cb2_4C_r32ui_atomic[int3(...)]`). So my guess is that the bound image is a 3D texture or doesn't match the binding's type, and the guard turns what used to be a skipped or approximate dispatch into a fatal abort. I haven't confirmed this with a probe.

## Proposed solution

- **Workaround (confirmed):** building from `c3a0880^` (4f29560) on the same machine and toolchain fixes it. The Mac shader stage builds **73,488 of 73,496 shaders, with 8 failures**: all `[metal failed]` 3D-indexed `cp_i_cb2_4C_r32ui_atomic[int3(...)]` compute shaders, which matches the game note. New Game then plays through the opening movies and autosaves into the field with no FATAL or abort: 60,000 frames (about 17 minutes), 9 save commits, launched from Finder with no custom env.
- **Related:** #263 fixes the same admission (`imga_extent` / `MDIE`) stopping SHIN MEGAMI TENSEI V, where a `texture_buffer` image was declared 2D. This looks like a sibling case: here the bound image is probably 3D, which `imga_extent` never admits.
- **Suggested fix:**
  - Treat an unsupported IMGA extent or type (3D, or a type mismatch) as non-fatal at run time: skip the dispatch, or send it to the scratch buffer, with a red line instead of `MDIE`.
  - Restore translation of returning (non-IGN) image atomics, or fall back to the pre-c3a0880 path for them, so the 842 shaders build again.
  - Possibly treat FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE as a regression test for the image-atomics guard, alongside Pokémon Legends: Z-A.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| nxnative source (crashing build) | `c1b7eff61fb3ca2d182320f12a9c6c30dc3c520e` (2026-10-26 07:28 +0800), which includes c3a0880 |
| Build date | 2026-10-25, 17:50–19:47 local time |
| Build command | `python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <folder> -k prod.keys --platform mac-app` (no other options) |
| Shader chain (in the app) | `msl/b-20fe3d62b9f6` |
| Game | FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE `0100606026F12000`, base v0 plus update v65536 (1.0.1), language en-US |
| Mac | Apple M2 Max, 64 GB RAM |
| macOS | 27.0.1 (26A434) |
| Xcode | 27.1 (27A9275); Metal 32023.921 (metalfe-32023.921.6) |
| Tools (Homebrew) | spirv-cross 1.4.363.0 (the build notes `8caa75a31452ae23`; the lock's tested revision is `d9dc197f061b42a5`), glslang 16.6.0, xcodegen 2.46.0, dotnet-sdk 10.0.402, Python 3.13.1 |
| Custom environment | **none**: no `env.txt` in Application Support or the bundle, no `DM_*` variables, launched from Finder |
| Controller | DualSense (Bluetooth) |

## Attachments

- `0100606026F12000.log`: the full runtime log of the last crash, from startup through the abort
- `0100606026F12000.prev.log`: the previous run, which crashed the same way
- `build_console_c1b7eff.txt`: the full console output of the build that made the crashing app. It includes the stage summary and the shader-chain or compiler note.

**Note about `dmsh_build.log`:** I started a rebuild from `c3a0880^` (the workaround) before I knew you'd want this log, and that rebuild overwrote it. The failure summary quoted above was copied from that log before it was replaced. I can regenerate the original by rebuilding from c1b7eff into a separate work folder if you need the whole file.

#  Add Support & Memory Cut for Pokémon Legends: Z-A v0 (1.0.0)

**Repository**: [`seedds/nxnative`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)  
**Target Title ID**: `0100F43008C44000` (Pokémon Legends: Z-A)  

---

### Issue Title
`[Feature/Fix] Add support & StandardAllocator cut for Pokémon Legends: Z-A v0 / 1.0.0 (0100F43008C44000)`

---

### Issue Body / Description

#### Summary
Currently, the profile for **Pokémon Legends: Z-A (`0100F43008C44000`)** only registers update **2.0.2 (`v393216`)**. 

When building from the base game alone (**`v0` / `1.0.0`**), `build_ipa_from_nsp.py` correctly identifies the title and derives a profile. However, because `DERIVED_SKIP` excludes `patches.py`—and `patches.py` only contained the address space cut for build `b1f12fd9...` at `0x1b3e3e4`—the rewritten `main` binary for `v0` does not receive the `StandardAllocator` 12 GB → 4 GB patch.

As a result, `nninitStartup` attempts to initialize the `StandardAllocator` with `0x300000000` (12 GB) inside the 4.25 GB alias region, causing an immediate abort on boot on Apple Silicon.

Adding the build row for `v0` and the corresponding cut for `main` at `0x19f84b4` allows `v0` to build and execute cleanly.

---

#### Binary Analysis (`v0` / `1.0.0`)
- **Base Title ID**: `0100F43008C44000`
- **Display Version**: `1.0.0`
- **`main` NSO Build ID**: `7222e13ecf6adb3249b5dd5c57fa40b1`
- **`sdk` NSO Build ID**: `df7a3960c74c3a4803f826c587153252` *(Identical to 2.0.2; existing `sdk_patches.py` node area cuts apply without modification)*

#### Disassembly & Patch Details
In `main` build `7222e13ecf6adb3249b5dd5c57fa40b1`:
```arm64
0x19f84a8: adrp x0, #0x3de5000
0x19f84ac: add  x0, x0, #0x4f8
0x19f84b0: mov  x1, xzr
0x19f84b4: mov  x2, #0x300000000     ; 6200c0d2 (12 GB address space request)
0x19f84b8: ldp  x29, x30, [sp], #0x20
0x19f84bc: b    #0x2fc5820           ; StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, size)
```

The cut changes `mov x2, #0x300000000` (`6200c0d2`) to `mov x2, #0x100000000` (`2200c0d2`), reducing address space reservation from 12 GB to 4 GB so the alias region (`mem_alias 0x110000000`) comfortably fits the 5 GB guest memory layout.

---

### Proposed Code Changes

#### 1. `dm/games/0100F43008C44000/patches.py`
```diff
--- a/dm/games/0100F43008C44000/patches.py
+++ b/dm/games/0100F43008C44000/patches.py
@@ -7,4 +7,8 @@ CUTS = {
   'b1f12fd919eae86ab8a978317677e64b': [
     (0x1b3e3e4, '6200c0d2', '2200c0d2', 'StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, size): address space mov x2,#0x300000000 → mov x2,#0x100000000 (12 GB → 4 GB)'),
   ],
+  # Pokémon Legends: Z-A 1.0.0 (v0) main
+  '7222e13ecf6adb3249b5dd5c57fa40b1': [
+    (0x19f84b4, '6200c0d2', '2200c0d2', 'StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, size): address space mov x2,#0x300000000 → mov x2,#0x100000000 (12 GB → 4 GB)'),
+  ],
 }
```

#### 2. `dm/games/0100F43008C44000/game.tsv`
```diff
--- a/dm/games/0100F43008C44000/game.tsv
+++ b/dm/games/0100F43008C44000/game.tsv
@@ -16,4 +16,5 @@ pad_layout	simple
 # ---- Versions ----
 build	v393216	2.0.2	main=b1f12fd919eae86ab8a978317677e64b	sdk=df7a3960c74c3a4803f826c587153252
+build	v0	1.0.0	main=7222e13ecf6adb3249b5dd5c57fa40b1	sdk=df7a3960c74c3a4803f826c587153252
 package	v393216
 shader_versions	v393216
```

---

### Verification & Test Results
- **Shader Pipeline**: Trinity Oodle decompressor split **23,209 shaders** from `v0`'s `arc/data.trpfs`. All 23,209 compiled successfully to Metal (`.metallib`).
- **Boot & Memory Stability**:
  ```text
  [dm] >>> nninitStartup
  [dm] [mem] alias region mapped up to +4.06 GB (alias region 4.25 GB)
  [dm] [mem] alias region mapped 3.15 GB (application pool 3.21 GB)
  [dm] [mem] MapPhysicalMemory +0x400000 refused: 3.15 GB mapped, the application pool is full (ResultLimitReached, the SDK frees cached pages and retries)
  [dm] [mem] alias region mapped 0.01 GB (application pool 3.21 GB)
  [dm] >>> nnMain
  ```
- **Runtime Performance**: Reached Lumiose City at steady 30 FPS (~33.3 ms frame times) on Apple Silicon (M1) at 1920×1080 resolution with Core Audio and controller input fully working.
title: Add Support & Memory Cut for Pokémon Legends: Z-A v0 (1.0.0)

Hi! Following up on #130: I built [NX Play](https://github.com/varyform/nx-native-wrapper), a SwiftUI Mac app that wraps `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` as it is, without reimplementing or forking it. It pulls nxnative before each run and rebuilds a game only when the update changes files.

How it differs from NX2Apple, which the README already links:
- a library of all your games in one window: extract, play on the Mac (`--platform mac`), rebuild;
- Install on Device through Xcode with the user's own team (`--prepare-xcode`), or an IPA to sideload;
- copying saves between the Mac and an iPhone/iPad, and freeing space by removing the NSPs of built games.

It doesn't ship, download or link to games or keys, and setup is one command (`bin/setup`: Homebrew tools, a uv venv for the Python packages, and a clone of nxnative). MIT licensed.

If you think it's useful, would you be open to a line in the README next to NX2Apple? Happy to send a PR, or leave it to you as with #130. Questions and bugs about NX Play go to its own repo, so it shouldn't add support load here. Thanks for nxnative!
title: NX Play: a Mac library app on top of build_ipa_from_nsp.py (no fork)

body:
I got **Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze** (`0100C1F0051B6000`, update 1.0.1 / v65536, SDK 4.4.0) running on an Apple silicon Mac with nxnative: boot, title, game select, the intro movie, and levels 1-1 and 1-2, at 60 fps with sound and correct graphics (including DK's fur). Along the way I hit several host bugs that look general rather than DKC-specific, so I'm reporting them here with the patches I used. Thanks for this project, it's great.

Nothing here is a polished PR — the diffs are what I ran locally against current `main`. Happy to adjust any of them.

## 1. Transform feedback: interleaved outputs in one buffer (`tf_layout`)

**Symptom:** DK's fur rendered as a flat brown slab most of the time, occasionally correct (whatever was left in the buffer). The build log had `[RED] <key>: transform feedback buffer 0 has a layout of unknown form (stride 24, enable 2, outputs [32, 33], components 771)` for 4 shaders.

**Cause:** DKC skins DK's fur mesh on the GPU and captures **two outputs into one feedback buffer**: position xyz and normal xyz, stride 24. In that layout `+0x6e8 + b` holds the output count (2, not 1) and the component word has one byte per output (`0x303`). `tf_layout` only accepted one output per buffer, so no `main0_tf` entry point was built.

**Fix:** accept 1–4 outputs per buffer, components one byte each, stride = 4 × sum; `vs_tf` stores each output at its word offset within the vertex record. The single-output form is unchanged.

<details><summary>dmsh_build.py</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py b/dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py
index 7c2100e..0e5b735 100644
--- a/dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py
+++ b/dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_build.py
@@ -374,10 +374,14 @@ def tf_layout(key, ctl):
     for b in range(4):
         if not strides[b]: out.append([]); continue
         locs = [x for x in ctl[0xdc + 0x80 * b:0x15c + 0x80 * b] if x]; n = struct.unpack_from('<I', ctl, 0x4dc + 0x80 * b)[0]
-        if ctl[0x6e8 + b] != 1 or len(locs) != 1 or not 0x20 <= locs[0] < 0x40 or not 1 <= n <= 4 or strides[b] != 4 * n:
+        # DKCTF: several outputs interleaved in one buffer. Then +0x6e8 + b holds the output count and the component word one byte per output
+        # (DK's fur skinning: outputs [0x20, 0x21], components 0x303 = position xyz + normal xyz, stride 24). One output keeps the measured form above
+        ns = [n] if len(locs) == 1 else [(n >> 8 * i) & 0xff for i in range(len(locs))]
+        if (ctl[0x6e8 + b] != len(locs) or not 1 <= len(locs) <= 4 or not all(0x20 <= x < 0x40 for x in locs) or not all(1 <= c <= 4 for c in ns)
+                or strides[b] != 4 * sum(ns)):
             print(f'[RED] {key}: transform feedback buffer {b} has a layout of unknown form (stride {strides[b]}, enable {ctl[0x6e8 + b]}, outputs {locs}, components {n}): no capture entry point; see tf_layout', flush=True)
             return None
-        out.append([locs[0] - 0x20, n, strides[b]])
+        out.append([[[x - 0x20, c] for x, c in zip(locs, ns)], None, strides[b]])
     return out
 
 def vs_tf(src, tf):
@@ -390,8 +394,14 @@ def vs_tf(src, tf):
     vm = re.search(r'uint\s+(\w+)\s*\[\[vertex_id\]\]', params); vid = vm.group(1) if vm else 'dm_vid'
     st = re.search(r'struct main0_out\s*\{(.*?)\};', src, re.S)
     names = {int(l): nm for nm, l in re.findall(r'float4 (\w+) \[\[user\(locn(\d+)\)\]\]', st.group(1) if st else '')}
-    stores = ''.join(f' dm_tf{b}[{vid} * {n} + {i}] = {f"as_type<uint>(out.{names[o]}.{c})" if o in names else "0u"};'
-                     for b, e in enumerate(tf) if e for o, n, _ in [e] for i, c in enumerate('xyzw'[:n]))
+    def outs(e):   # (output, components, word offset in the vertex's record); an older one-output entry is [output, components, stride]
+        if isinstance(e[0], list):
+            r, w = [], 0
+            for o, n in e[0]: r.append((o, n, w)); w += n
+            return r
+        return [(e[0], e[1], 0)]
+    stores = ''.join(f' dm_tf{b}[{vid} * {e[2] // 4} + {w + i}] = {f"as_type<uint>(out.{names[o]}.{c})" if o in names else "0u"};'
+                     for b, e in enumerate(tf) if e for o, n, w in outs(e) for i, c in enumerate('xyzw'[:n]))
     extra = ('' if vm else ', uint dm_vid [[vertex_id]]') + ''.join(f', device uint* dm_tf{b} [[buffer({TF_SLOT + b})]]' for b, e in enumerate(tf) if e)
     return f'\nvertex void main0_tf({params}{extra})\n{{' + body.replace('return out;', '{' + stores + ' return; }')
```
</details>

## 2. Transform feedback draws without rasterizer discard

**Symptom:** after fix 1 the capture entry point existed, but DK still looked wrong; the log never showed `transform feedback: first capture`. A pass dump showed `Y tf bind`, `Y tf begin` / `end` around the draw.

**Cause:** DKC's capture draw has feedback active, no fragment shader and colour writes off, but it never calls `SetRasterizerDiscard`. `tf_draw` only runs under rasterizer discard, so this draw went down the normal path and captured nothing.

**Fix:** also route to `tf_draw` when feedback is active, the vertex shader has a capture entry point and the program has no fragment stage.

<details><summary>nvn_mtl.m (draw dispatch part)</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m b/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m
index ade5e3a..636d0ca 100644
--- a/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m
+++ b/dm/gfx/nvn/nvn_mtl.m
@@ -2015,7 +2015,9 @@ static int mem_any(const uint8_t *p, uint64_t n) {   // whether any byte is non-
 static int tex_init_fill(const tex_t *t, id<MTLTexture> mt) {
     if (!t->mem || !t->pool || (t->pool->flags & NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_VIRTUAL) || t->has_layout) return 0;
     if (t->d.samples > 1 || (t->d.flags & NVN_TEXTURE_FLAGS_COMPRESSIBLE) || ((int)mt.pixelFormat >= 250 && (int)mt.pixelFormat <= 262)) return 0;   // 250..262: Depth16Unorm … X24_Stencil8 (some names are macOS-only)
-    int no_cpu = (t->pool->flags & NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_CPU_NO_ACCESS) != 0;
+    // CPU_UNCACHED pools need no flush, so their storage at first use is the content too (DKCTF loads its splash/title ASTC textures into a 0x22 pool before
+    // nvnTextureInitialize: the dirty-page tracking never saw a write, and the texture stayed zeros = magenta on most boots)
+    int no_cpu = (t->pool->flags & (NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_CPU_NO_ACCESS | NVN_MEMORY_POOL_FLAGS_CPU_UNCACHED)) != 0;
     static int flush_fill = -1; if (flush_fill < 0) { const char *e = getenv("DM_NVN_FLUSH_FILL"); flush_fill = !e || atoi(e) != 0; }
     if (!no_cpu && (!flush_fill || !nvn_flushed(t->mem, t->L.size))) return 0;
     if (!atomic_load(&g_sub_thread_set) || !on_sub_thread() || !mem_any(t->mem, t->L.size)) return 0;   // the upload batch belongs to the submit thread
@@ -7740,6 +7742,9 @@ static void draw(const p_draw *dw, const p_draw_idx *di) {
     __unsafe_unretained NvProg *pr = g_geo_program ? g_geo_program : prog_get(S.prog);
     draw_gs_check(pr);   // a geometry stage left with no function (see prog_fold_gs)
     if (S.rast_discard) { tf_draw(pr, dw, di); return; }   // the vertex stage only: transform feedback capture, or nothing (tf_draw)
+    // DKCTF: feedback active with a capture entry point and no fragment stage also captures. DK's fur skinning pass draws with feedback on, no fragment
+    // shader and colour writes off, but never sets rasterizer discard: as an ordinary draw it wrote nothing, and the fur read stale memory (a flat slab most of the time)
+    if (S.tf_on && pr && pr->sh[0] && pr->sh[0]->tf_fn && !pr->sh[1]) { tf_draw(pr, dw, di); return; }
     if (g_nubd && (g_enc || ubd_lazy()) && ubd_conflict(pr, dw, di)) { g_ubd_conflicts++; rp_end(); ubd_land(); }   // land the deferred inline updates before this draw (see ubd_conflict)
     if (zskip_can_draw(pr)) {   // Zero-source skip: the output is always 0, writing 0 over 0, so this draw changes no result (see zskip_can_draw)
         g_zskip_count++; { static int once; if (!once++) MLOG("zero-source skip: first case pass %llu", g_stat_pass + 1); }
```
</details>

## 3. Textures in `CPU_UNCACHED` pools stay zero (magenta) at random

**Symptom:** the splash and title textures (1280×720 ASTC, pool flags `0x22`) were magenta on roughly half of the boots. `DM_NVN_TEXINFO` showed the guest storage already held the data at first use (347,055 of 655,360 bytes non-zero), but the texture was not marked CPU-written. `tex_dirty_upload` did not help reliably.

**Cause:** DKC reads the texture data into the pool **before** `nvnTextureInitialize`, so the dirty-page tracking never sees a write, and `tex_init_fill` only fills from storage for `CPU_NO_ACCESS` pools or flushed ranges. Writes to an uncached pool need no flush, so there is never a flush either.

**Fix:** treat `CPU_UNCACHED` like `CPU_NO_ACCESS` in `tex_init_fill` (storage at first use is the content). This is the second hunk in the `nvn_mtl.m` diff above. After it, 4 of 4 boots showed the splash correctly.

## 4. Missing `nn::oe::GetUserInactivityDetectionTimeExtensionMode`

**Symptom:** `CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=sdk+0x15b73c` right as the intro cutscene starts (stack: `CCameraManager::StartCinematicCamera` → `CScreenDimmingUtil::DisableScreenDimming`).

**Cause:** `DisableScreenDimming` calls `GetUserInactivityDetectionTimeExtensionMode` before `SetUserInactivityDetectionTimeExtended`; the setter is already taken over, the getter is not, so it goes to `am` through a null proxy.

**Fix:** take it over and return 0.

<details><summary>hle_oe.c</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/dm/host/hle_oe.c b/dm/host/hle_oe.c
index c3a5780..49037a5 100644
--- a/dm/host/hle_oe.c
+++ b/dm/host/hle_oe.c
@@ -106,6 +106,8 @@ HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn2oe29BeginAutoSleepDisabledSectionEv", "open an auto-sleep disa
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn2oe27EndAutoSleepDisabledSectionEv", "close an auto-sleep disabled section (through am)", void, h_oe_NoSleepEnd, void) { if (g_nosleep > 0) g_nosleep--; }
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn2oe19IsAutoSleepDisabledEv", "whether an auto-sleep disabled section is open", unsigned, h_oe_NoSleepQ, void) { return g_nosleep > 0; }
 HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn2oe37IsUserInactivityDetectionTimeExtendedEv", "whether auto screen-off on inactivity is extended; the host does not turn the screen off, reports no", unsigned, h_oe_InactivityExtQ, void) { return 0; }
+// DKCTF: CScreenDimmingUtil::DisableScreenDimming asks for the mode before a cinematic (the intro); without a host answer it went to am and crashed at sdk+0x15b73c
+HLE_FORCE("_ZN2nn2oe43GetUserInactivityDetectionTimeExtensionModeEv", "auto screen-off extension mode; the host does not turn the screen off, reports none", int, h_oe_InactivityExtMode, void) { return 0; }
```

## 5. `SetHeapSize` above the heap region returns a result the SDK aborts on

**Symptom:** `SetHeapSize OOM: req 0x120000000 > cap 0xd0000000`, then `Break#1` in `nn::os` at boot.

**Cause:** DKC's `CMemory::InitHeap` binary-searches its heap size (it starts at 3 GB with an upper bound of 6 GB) and expects an out-of-memory result for sizes that don't fit. The host returns `0xD401` for a request above the region cap, which the SDK treats as fatal. I used `0x10801` (the same result as the app-pool check right below it), which the SDK passes back as `os::ResultOutOfMemory`; the search then converges. I'm not certain which exact kernel result Horizon returns here, so you may prefer a different one.

## 6. Same-core handoff can starve a low-priority worker indefinitely

**Symptom:** random hangs, on about one boot in four at the boot splash, and more often during level loads, with the loading screen still animating. The main thread spins (CPU 170 s in a 300 s run). DKC's priority-58 decompression job thread (`NJobSystem`, pinned to core 0) makes almost no progress.

**Cause:** in `dm_yield_to_core_peers`, a thread waits until every higher-priority thread pinned to its core is blocked. On core 0 DKC has several higher-priority threads that poll with short sleeps; `thr_runnable` counts them as runnable whenever they are between sleeps, so the worker waits in 50 µs steps until all of them happen to be asleep at once. On a busy load that can take minutes.

**Workaround (not a real fix):** an optional cap on that wait, `DM_CORE_YIELD_CAP_US` (unset = current behaviour). With 2000 µs, all my boots and level loads complete. A proper fix probably needs a better notion of "runnable" for polling threads, so I'm reporting this as an issue more than proposing the patch.

## 7. Audio: one-frame callbacks starve a second waiter on the renderer event

Probably worth knowing rather than fixing as-is:
- With the default 512-frame callbacks, DKC's audio crackles. The log shows 0 underruns but about 50 catch-up renders per second (`catch-up renders so far` grows steadily).
- `DM_DBG_AU_FRAMES=480` (two whole 5 ms frames per callback) sounds noticeably better to me. The catch-up rate stays about the same, so I don't fully understand why yet.
- `DM_DBG_AU_FRAMES=240` **freezes the game at boot**. `CAudioMemoryPool::Shutdown` on the main thread loops on `WaitSystemEvent(renderer event)` + `RequestUpdateAudioRenderer` until a pool detaches. At the same time, DKC's priority-29 audio thread (`CAxalSystem`) waits on the same event. With one render per callback, the higher-priority thread is woken for every signal and the main thread never is. With 480 or 512, renders come in pairs and the main thread gets the second signal.

## 8. Retro Studios shader containers (DKC support)

DKC's NVN programs are not in BNSH or GLSLC containers. Each is one zlib stream inside the `SNVN` chunk of an `RFRM`/`MTRL` form:
- `romfs/MaterialArchive.arc`, stored;
- the `MTRL` assets in the `.pak` files (`RFRM`/`PACK`, `ADIR` table: count × [fourcc, guid(16), u64 offset, u64 size], big endian). The body after the 0x20-byte form header is one zlib stream.

A decompressed program is the code areas of its stages back to back, then their control sections back to back (0x840 bytes each, SDK 4). Control `+0x704` gives each code area's length. 720 of the 1,374 programs in `MaterialArchive.arc` are VS+GS+PS.

With this reader the split finds 24,254 shaders (main 294, the rest from the archive and 374 unique pak `MTRL` assets), and gameplay has no `not in the shader map` lines. A few Scaleform shaders still differ from main's copies at control `+0x790` / `+0x7d0` at run time; I captured those with `DM_NVN_SHDUMP` and fed them in with a small `nvn_capture/` reader (included).

body:
### TotK (0100F2C0115B6000, 1.4.3) fails to boot on `9a56ecf` — black screen, packaged textures never upload; bisected, with a bounded-handoff workaround

**Commit bisected as first bad:** `9a56ecf` "Order same-core wake handoffs and remove Dread movie gates" (parent `9feac2f` boots fine; `main@c1b7eff` still broken for this title).

**Machine:** MacBook Pro M3 Pro 12-core, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), host built per docs/development.md "Build by hand (Mac)".

**Symptom:** after the boot logos the game renders a black screen at 60 fps forever (`frame p50 16.66 ms`, `84 functions 771 calls` — an empty scene). Input (A through a title menu) never gets past it. No CRASH, no red lines, shaders all load.

**Discriminators from the log:**
- `packaged textures: first uploads 0` for the whole session (a working boot shows 100+ within the first minute) — the game's texture pipeline never starts, so it waits forever on assets that never arrive.
- The wake-handoff path is the only thing that changed. The new `dm_yield_to_core_peers()` waits **without any bound** for every higher-priority same-core peer to leave `thr_runnable()`. TotK's `ModuleSystemWorker1/2` threads spin in guest code without taking a guest wait (the session's own power line shows them yielding ~150–200k times per 300 frames), so the signalling thread yields forever and boot serializes to a halt. The pre-`9a56ecf` code capped this wait at 5 ms, which is what kept the cycle broken.

**Workaround that restores boot on `main` (local patch, keeps the handoff semantics):** re-introduce a wall-clock bound in `dm_yield_to_core_peers()` — on cap hit log and return −1, like the old cutoff did. With a 5 ms default (env `DM_HANDOFF_CAP_US`, `0` = pure upstream) the game boots and enters the world: `first uploads 224`, `calls/frame 28k+` in the field, and the cap log fires during boot exactly where the unbounded wait used to spin. 400 s scripted arms on the bounded build: 30–31 frames over ~20 ms per 28,500 frames (vs 49–79 on `ab45d05`), so the handoff itself still appears to do its job when it can complete.

**Suggested upstream direction:** bound the handoff (per-call deadline, or a global budget), or treat a peer that has been runnable without a guest wait for N ms as "not making progress" and stop waiting for it. Happy to retest any candidate patch on this machine.
title: TotK (1.4.3) black screen at boot since 9a56ecf: unbounded same-core wake handoff never returns (bisected + bounded workaround)

body:
## Summary

A game that links OpenGL **directly from the SDK module** (no `eglGetProcAddress` loader) never reaches `dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m`: every GL call lands on the host's unimplemented stub, `glCreateShader` returns 0, and the game then dereferences a null shader handle.

Reproduced on Darkest Dungeon Complete (`01008F1008DA6000`, update `v327680`, SDK `nnSdk-3_6_0` / major 3, modules `main subsdk0 sdk`, OpenGL renderer). There is no profile for this title, so it runs from the provisional profile the NSP script writes.

## What happens

The Mac host boots the game to `nnMain`, records its first GL frame, then dies:

```
>>> nnosInitialize
>>> nninitInitializeSdkModule
>>> nninitStartup
>>> nnMain
[gl] frame 1: draws 0, passes 0, uploads 0 (0 by blit), command buffers 1, pipelines so far 0
CRASH sig=11 addr=0 pc=sdk+0x397510 lr=sdk+0x3bd9c4
bt: sdk+0x3bdb18 sdk+0x398450 sdk+0x3894e4 sdk+0x3bd36c sdk+0x3bc040 main+0x4623c main+0x1dca40 main+0x196c74 main+0x197dfc
```

`DM_GL_LOG=1 DM_GL_STUBS=1` shows where it comes from — every GL entry point is unimplemented, and the null flows straight into the game:

```
[gl] context current on a new thread
UNIMPL glClearColor …              UNIMPL glClear …
UNIMPL glCreateShader (x0=0x8b31 …)      → returns 0
UNIMPL glShaderSource  (x0=0)            ← null shader handle
UNIMPL glCompileShader (x0=0)
UNIMPL glGetShaderiv   (x0=0)
UNIMPL glGetShaderInfoLog (x0=0, x1=0x2, x2=0)   ← the game dereferences null here
```

## Why

`hle_gl.m` exposes GL through `eglGetProcAddress`: the comment at the top of the file describes the glad-style loader that Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth and Balatro use, and `eglGetProcAddress` is what returns entries from the layer's table. This engine instead takes its GL symbols from the SDK module's libGL and never calls `eglGetProcAddress`, so the host's table is never consulted and the calls fall through to the stub.

## Things I checked that are not the cause

- **`graphics gl` in the profile changes nothing.** `profile_guess.py` only guesses `gl` when `main` imports EGL *and* names `glShaderSource`; this build does not match, so the provisional profile said NVN. Adding `graphics gl` and regenerating `game_profile.h` produced the identical crash — the host does not read that key.
- **Shader table is not the first failure.** `gl_shaders.py` over the RomFS and `main` found 3 shaders, and `DM_GL_CAPTURE` wrote 0, because compilation never succeeds far enough to capture anything. The engine appears to build most shaders at run time, so a capture pass would be the right way to enumerate them once GL calls reach the layer.
- **Same provisional-profile route works elsewhere.** Darkest Dungeon II (`0100E5E01C098000`, SDK 19.3) from its own provisional profile boots and renders on both the Mac host (frame 3300, 1.97 GB resident) and iOS. So this is specific to the direct-GL path, not to provisional profiles in general.

## Suggestion

Either

1. hook the sdk module's GL exports into the same table `hle_gl.m` builds for `eglGetProcAddress` (so a game that imports libGL directly gets the layer too), or
2. detect the direct-import case in `profile_guess.py` / the survey and report it as unsupported, so the failure is a `[RED]` line at prepare time instead of a null dereference at boot.

Happy to attach the full `dmhost` trace (`DM_GL_LOG=1 DM_GL_STUBS=1`), the survey, or run any diagnostic you suggest. Environment: macOS, Xcode 27.1, nxnative at `9a56ecf`.
title: GL games that link libGL directly never reach dm/gfx/gl (Darkest Dungeon Complete, SDK 3.6.0)

## Result

Sifu builds and runs on an Apple M3 Mac using the automatically generated provisional profile. The tester reports that it “works great” after trying the app. This is a preliminary compatibility report, not a full-game completion or comprehensive graphics validation.

## Environment and game

- nxnative commit: `cbbb600866cef1ad6142f35d8273abca43ea06e4` (seedds/nxnative; working tree clean when checked).
- macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434.
- M3 iMac, 10-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory.
- Base title ID: `01007B5017A12000`.
- Update: `01007B5017A12800`, `v393216`.
- Deluxe Cosmetic Pack DLC: `01007B5017A13001`, `v0`, included in the build. DLC content was not separately verified in gameplay.
- The generated profile records display version `0.1`; the exact update and module build IDs below are the reliable reproduction identifiers.

## Reproduction

Put the base NSP, update NSP and DLC NSP together in one local folder. Using locally supplied keys, run from the nxnative checkout:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py /path/to/Sifu \
  -k /path/to/prod.keys --platform mac --app-name Sifu --progress lines
```

No existing Sifu profile was found. The script generated a provisional profile, extracted the update and DLC, rewrote `main`, `subsdk0` and `sdk`, and built the Mac host and Metal shaders. No nxnative source-code changes or manual game-code patches were made.

The initial automatic heap check hit `SetHeapSize OOM: req 0x600000 > cap 0`. It then changed `mem_alias` from `0x1008000000` to `0x1000000000`. The subsequent host passed initialization and reached the frame loop. The profile below contains that automatically corrected value.

The completed build was wrapped in a local macOS `.app`, using the generated host, rewritten modules, RomFS, shader libraries, profile, font and DLC. It launches with `DM_WINDOW=1`, `DM_AUDIO=1`, `DM_LANG=en-US` and `DM_METAL_HUD=0`; the data-directory variables point to the app resources and its own Application Support folder. No save migration was performed.

## Evidence and limits

- All 28,368 shaders reported `ok`; no shader compilation failures.
- Runtime samples report 30.0 fps. One 300-frame sample reports frame time p50 33.32 ms / p95 34.26 ms / max 73.20 ms and GPU p50 13.21 ms / p95 16.07 ms / max 17.15 ms. This is a log sample, not a controlled gameplay benchmark.
- No `CRASH` marker appeared in the runtime log inspected for this report.
- Automated screenshot verification was unavailable. The positive playability confirmation comes from the human tester.
- Gameplay duration, levels tested, save/reload, full-game progression and DLC functionality have not been documented.

Warnings worth retaining for follow-up:

- Left/right controller haptics: `Couldn’t communicate with a helper application. (NSCocoaErrorDomain 4097)`.
- Vertex attribute format `0x27` (8/16-bit integer) feeding a float input, with conversion on the CPU at replay.
- An earlier launch logged a display-link-silent/frozen-picture warning during an unsuccessful automated screen inspection. Its cause was not established, and the tester subsequently reported that the game works well. It is not being presented as a confirmed persistent gameplay defect.
- The shader analysis reports 3,414 shaders whose c1 accesses were not proven bounded, and queries using defaults. Compilation success should not be read as proof that all rendering paths are correct.

## Sanitised generated profile

```tsv

# Sifu, SDK 13; generated from the local game survey.

# ---- App ----
name	Sifu
ipa	Sifu.ipa

# ---- Versions ----
build	v393216	0.1	main=4a5d86da05a4e7bb7551ab8de5510177	subsdk0=a8cb97803f7f442a3b6cce1c7cd4ee4a	sdk=357efc198e728cb5d55265aff304f03c
package	v393216
shader_versions	v393216

# ---- Files ----
# every module main imports from
modules	main subsdk0 sdk
romfs_marker	Sifu/Content/Paks/pakchunk0-Switch.pak
zip_store	.mov:.mp4:.pak:.ttf:.metallib

# ---- Memory ----
# Unreal: nninitStartup reserves a 62 GB address region and its FMallocBinned3 takes 37 GB of it, so a 64 GB alias region for the bring-up on the Mac. An iPhone needs the allocator cut for the build and a capped region (game_args), as Octopath Traveler 0's profile (docs/reference/memory.md)
mem_reserve	0x1028000000
mem_stack	0x10000000
app_pool	0xCD500000
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
sys_resource	0x5000000

# ---- Shader split ----
# the decoded shader code archives: the engine's global shaders and the game's material shaders
shader_groups	ShaderArchive-Global-=global ShaderArchive-=game
shader_note	Sifu shaders (provisional profile)

# ---- Heap check on the Mac ----
# the game asked for a 0.01 GB heap: a 0.125 GB heap region
mem_alias	0x1000000000

# heap check: 2026-10-25, the heap request did not fit; set mem_alias
```

On a Mac whose region formats numbers with a decimal comma, the "extract" stage ends with
`0 files, 0.0 KB` although extraction succeeded.

nx_extract writes its summary with the current culture
(`dm/tools/nx_extract/Program.cs:192`, `{bytes / 1048576.0:F1}`), so the log says:

    .../ExeFS: 5 files 71,4 MB, 0 identical to the compare dir (cloned), 71,4 MB newly written

`extracted()` in `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py` parses it with `r'[:|] (\d+) files ([\d.]+) MB'`,
which does not match `71,4`, so it returns None. Besides the wrong summary, the next build's
extraction progress loses its exact total and falls back to the NSP-size estimate.
Any decimal-comma locale (de, fr, ru, tr, …) should be affected.

Possible fixes: format with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`, set
`<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>` in nx_extract.csproj, or accept `[\d.,]+`
and normalise the comma in the parser. Workaround: run the build with `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`.
title: Extraction summary reads "0 files, 0.0 KB" when the region uses a decimal comma

body:
## Setup
- nxnative `9116109`, macOS on an Apple M5 Pro, Xcode 26 with the Metal Toolchain
- Pokémon Violet base v0 + update 4.0.0 (v786432) + DLC 01008F6008C5F001, my own dumps
- SDK 13.3.13, modules `main` + `sdk`, Game Freak's Trinity engine (same as Pokémon Legends: Z-A)
- `build_ipa_from_nsp.py --platform mac`, provisional profile from the survey

With the three changes below the game runs from the boot through the intro, the name entry and the first scenes up to the first save point (9,300 frames, no GPU errors). I only tested on the Mac, not on iOS. Packed as a Mac app (the AppleGamingWiki step 8 bundle), it runs too, and a save from Ryujinx (`main`) loads and plays.

## 1. `StandardAllocator::Initialize` aborts in `nninitStartup`
**Symptom:** `Break#1 reason=0` right after `>>> nninitStartup`, bt `sdk+0x16b8e8 sdk+0x16ba48 sdk+0x3251a0 main+0x167d558 …`.
Same entry as Z-A in the symptom index ("StandardAllocators over 12 to 62 GB of address space"). The provisional profile gives the 5 GB block (`mem_reserve 0x140000000`, `mem_alias 0x118000000`).

**Workaround (Mac only):** the 64 GB layout from "Measuring address regions and commits":
```
mem_reserve	0x1030000000
mem_alias	0x1008000000
```
With it the game passes `nninitStartup`. The log shows `alias region mapped up to +13.25 GB` and `alias region mapped 3.17 GB (application pool 3.21 GB)`, so the allocator takes about 12 GB of address space, as on Z-A. For iOS this needs Z-A's cuts at Violet's offsets (a `main` cut for the allocator size and the node-area cut for this `sdk` build `bb560bdf…`, which is not in `sdk_patches.py` yet). I did not look for those offsets.

## 2. Abort in `nn::bluetooth::InitializeBle`
**Symptom:** `[RED] sf: the game connects to service bt itself, which the host does not serve`, then `Break#1`, bt `sdk+0x16b8e8 sdk+0x16ba48 sdk+0xaec1c sdk+0xb684c main+0xa0b030 …`.
`sdk+0xb684c` is `nn::bluetooth::InitializeBle()`, and `sdk+0xaec1c` is `nn::bluetooth::hal::user::InitializeBluetoothUserInterface()`. `main` imports 28 `nn::bluetooth` BLE/GATT functions (for the Pokémon GO Plus + accessory).

**Fix:** a new `dm/host/hle_bluetooth.c` (attached). It answers as a console with Bluetooth on and nothing in range: `InitializeBle` is a no-op, the five `AcquireBle*Event` are bound with `hle_bind_system_event` and never signalled, scan start and stop succeed, `GetBleScanResult` and `GetBleConnectionInfoList` return 0, `Register/UnregisterGattOperationNotification` succeed, and `ConnectToGattServer` and `DisconnectFromGattServer` fail. After this the game reaches its frame loop.

## 3. GPU page fault from image atomics past the scratch buffer (same shader as Z-A's #101)
**Symptom:** about 35 s in (the first scene after the name entry), `[RED] segment command buffer execution error … Caused GPU Address Fault Error (kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault)`. After that every submission is `Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)`, and the picture freezes while the game keeps running. With `MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1` the fault goes away, but text and some effects are missing.

The host log has `[RED] image atomics on a block-linear texture (texture ID 302 target 1): not followed, the atomics go to a scratch buffer` and `scratch buffer of 1 MB (texture 480x270, 1 layers)`.

GPU validation (`OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE=YES MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=1`): 121 × `Invalid store in 'device' or 'constant' address space` into that 1 MB buffer, all from one pipeline. The offsets range from 1.6 MB up to 2.1 GB past the end, plus offsets just under 2^34, which are negative indices (int → ×4 wrap, up to −560 MB).

**Shader:** fragment `318346b137ae3a33` (`ps_arc.bin#16116`), from `arc/system_resource/gfx2/shader/NX64/env_titan/special/imgui.trsha` var1. That is Violet's version of Z-A's `env_ikkaku` imgui shader `2bd5037003980716`. It reprojects a position and does `atomic_fetch_max` into an r32ui image at `int2(trunc(size * uv))`, with no clamp. The projected uv lands well outside [0,1] for some fragments. On NVN, image atomics outside the image are dropped. SPIRV-Cross's buffer emulation (`spvImage2DAtomicCoord`) indexes without a check, so a larger scratch buffer alone can't fix it.

**Workaround I used:** a bounds check in the generated MSL, then a recompile of that one metallib:
```metal
uint _468 = 0u;
if (_185 >= 0 && _189 >= 0 && uint(_185) < spvDescriptorSet0.fp_i_cb2_4A_r32ui.get_width() && uint(_189) < spvDescriptorSet0.fp_i_cb2_4A_r32ui.get_height())
    _468 = atomic_fetch_max_explicit((device atomic_uint*)&spvDescriptorSet0.fp_i_cb2_4A_r32ui_atomic[spvImage2DAtomicCoord(int2(_185, _189), spvDescriptorSet0.fp_i_cb2_4A_r32ui)], uint(_193), memory_order_relaxed);
```
After that: no GPU errors, and text and graphics are correct. The proper fix is probably for the translator to guard every emulated image atomic like this, since it's the NVN/Vulkan semantics. That would also cover Z-A's shader if its coordinates can leave the image.

## Other observations (not fixed)
- Under GPU validation, 3,519 × `Texture is not resident` for one texture (`gpuResourceID:136`) in two fragment pipelines (UIDs `5AEE1B6E…`, `44E9D797…`), from about 3 s in. It caused no visible problem without validation.
- During the intro some text boxes are drawn without their background. In normal play the text boxes look correct.
- `[RED] pipeline archive file …/run/pso_archive/000NN.mtl4a not usable (deployment target …)` on every start.

I can share full logs (host log and the validation log) and the provisional profile if useful.

[hle_bluetooth.c.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33932699/hle_bluetooth.c.txt)
title: Pokémon Violet (01008F6008C5E000) 4.0.0: boots and plays on the Mac with three fixes (memory layout, BLE stub, bounds check for image atomics)

[log-mario.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33932614/log-mario.txt)

[desassemblage.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33932620/desassemblage.txt)

Setup: Apple M1, macOS, nxnative built with --platform mac, game v0, no profile in dm/games
(provisional profile). Wonder runs fine with the same setup.

Symptom: the game crashes about 0.2 s after the shared fonts are served:
  CRASH sig=11 addr=0x38 pc=main+0x62d20  (x0=0, x1=0xe06b)
  bt: main+0x289ba8 main+0x40dee4 main+0x40dd80 ...

Analysis: main+0x62d20 is `ldrb w8,[x0,#0x38]` right after `bl main+0x66b00`, whose result
is not checked. That function loops over the loaded fonts calling
nn::fontll::ScalableFontEngine::CheckGlyphExist(U+E06B) (call at main+0x66bf0) and returns
NULL when no font has the glyph. So no font ever reports U+E06B.
This matches the "Shared font address: BFTTF header or bare TTF" note in docs/reference/services.md
(3D World: LoadFont 403 / SetFont 301 -> every lookup null -> crash at 0x38).

What I tried, same crash each time:
- shared_font bfttf (header) and automatic mode (bare TTF, "SDK 9, main imports Decode")
- nintendo_ext.ttf: original stand-in (46 code points), extended to U+E000-E153 with empty
  glyphs, with outlined glyphs, and a copy of Arial Unicode with U+E000-E153 added to its cmap
  (via DM_SHARED_FONT_EXT)
So the content of the Nintendo extension font does not seem to matter; I suspect
LoadFont/SetFont fails in the engine, or the font list is empty.

Not found: I could not locate LoadFont/SetFont/GetError call sites in main with sdis
(direct bl scan finds nothing, although main imports ScalableFontEngineHelper::Decode).

Attached: full dmhost log, disassembly around main+0x62d20 / 0x66bf4 / 0x289ba8.
Is there a recommended way to probe the engine's error code for this game (DM_PROBE address)?
title: Super Mario 3D All-Stars (010049900F546000, SDK 9.5): null deref at main+0x62d20 right after shared fonts load

body:
Reported downstream (NX2Apple issue #8, with permission to forward): `patch_nso.py` fails while rewriting a large NSO.

**Target**: EA Sports FC 27, title ID `0100C49025D3E000`, SDK 22, NSO compression ZBIC.
**Text size**: `0xb9780f0` = 185.47 MiB.
**Failure**: `AssertionError` in `nso_asm.py`, from `site_window -> emit(B(here(), t))`.
**Log**: `BIG_TEXT initial FRONT: -0x3990000`, then `DM_PATCH_FRONT retry: 0x6c0000` — the retry does not help.

The cause is the ARM64 branch range: `B`/`BL` reach ±128 MB, and a single front region cannot serve sites spread across 185 MB of text. The retry moves the front, but there is no placement that is within reach of every site at once.

What it seems to need is multi-region placement: emit trampolines in clusters near the sites that use them (each cluster within ±128 MB of its sites), and chain islands where one hop is not enough. The reporter suggests exactly that ("multi-region patch placement / branch islands for executables larger than 128 MiB").

Survey and extraction of this title succeed; only the rewrite fails, so the rest of the pipeline is not implicated. Not asking for a fix on my behalf — forwarding because the rewriter is shared and this looks like the first title to exceed the range, which suggests the limit will be hit again.
title: patch_nso.py: ARM64 branch range assertion on a 185 MB text (EA Sports FC 27) — multi-region patch placement

body:
## Context

The macOS frontend currently receives face-button events through Apple's `GCController` API, but the conversion in `dm/host/front_mac.m` assumes an Xbox-style physical arrangement for every controller.

This matters because `GCController` exposes standardized properties such as `buttonA`, `buttonB`, `buttonX`, and `buttonY`, while the physical positions and printed labels differ between controller families:

- On an Xbox-style controller, the printed B button is on the right.
- On a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, the printed B button is on the bottom.
- Both can still be reported through the `buttonB` property.

The previous conversion treated every `buttonB` event as the right-position input and converted it to the game's A input. As a result, pressing the printed B button on an NS Pro Controller triggered the game's A action. PR #180 adds an initial name-based distinction so Nintendo-style controllers preserve the reported labels while other controllers retain the existing positional conversion:

https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/pull/180

## Why name matching is not sufficient

The current PR checks `GCController.vendorName` for strings such as `Nintendo`, `Pro Controller`, and `Joy-Con`. This fixes the tested NS Pro Controller, but it is not a robust long-term classifier:

- Third-party controllers may use a Nintendo-style face-button layout without reporting a Nintendo-related name.
- Some third-party controllers may report a name containing `Pro Controller` even when their layout is different.
- Users or firmware may change the reported name.
- Unknown controllers need a deterministic fallback that does not break the existing Xbox-style behavior.

I would prefer an automatic solution rather than adding a user-facing layout setting for every controller.

## Candidate approaches

### 1. Apple GameController metadata

Continue using `GCController` for input and investigate whether its product/category information can provide a more reliable Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, or standard-controller classification than `vendorName` alone.

Advantages:

- No new third-party dependency.
- The classification and input events come from the same framework.
- Keeps the current macOS input and rumble path unchanged.

Limitation: it may still not distinguish all third-party Nintendo-layout devices.

### 2. HID vendor/product identification

Use IOKit HID vendor/product IDs as an automatic classifier for known devices, with a small table of confirmed VID/PID entries and the current positional mapping as the fallback for unknown devices.

Advantages:

- It does not depend on a user-editable display name.
- It can identify known first-party and common third-party devices consistently.
- It avoids changing the existing input path.

Limitation: a table must be maintained, and an unknown or newly released device still needs a fallback or a future entry.

### 3. SDL3 gamepad database

Use SDL3's gamepad database/type information to classify known Nintendo Switch Pro, Joy-Con, Xbox, PlayStation, and standard controllers, while keeping Apple's `GCController` responsible for actual input and rumble.

A metadata-only SDL3 integration could potentially provide broader coverage than a local VID/PID table, including third-party devices already covered by SDL's mappings. A local probe also suggests that SDL3's device identity (`DevSrvsID`) can be correlated with the corresponding IOKit registry entry, which may allow classification without replacing the existing `GCController` event path.

Advantages:

- SDL3 already maintains controller mappings and controller-type information.
- It may cover third-party devices without us maintaining every VID/PID ourselves.
- It can distinguish Nintendo, Xbox, and PlayStation layouts where its database has a mapping.

Questions/risks:

- Would adding and bundling SDL3 be acceptable for the standalone macOS app?
- Should SDL3 be used only as a metadata classifier, avoiding a second input/event path?
- What is the expected dependency and binary-size maintenance policy for the Mac host?
- How should devices missing from SDL3's database fall back?

## Request for guidance

Before extending the name-based heuristic further, I would appreciate the maintainer's recommendation:

1. Is SDL3 an acceptable dependency for the macOS host if it is used only for controller identification?
2. If yes, would you prefer SDL3's gamepad database/type classification over maintaining a local HID VID/PID table?
3. If no, should the implementation stay within Apple APIs and use `GCController` metadata plus a small known-device VID/PID table?
4. Is correlating SDL3 metadata with the existing `GCController` device identity a reasonable direction, or would the project prefer not to introduce a second controller discovery layer?

The intended behavior is to preserve the existing positional mapping for unknown devices, apply label-preserving mapping only when the controller type is identified as Nintendo-style, and leave shoulders, triggers, sticks, D-pad, player assignment, input delivery, and rumble unchanged.
title: Question: should macOS controller layout detection use SDL3 gamepad types or HID VID/PID?

body:
## Summary

Pokémon Legends: Z-A (`0100F43008C44000`, update 2.0.2 / v393216) on a **Mac host** now gets past the opening cinematic (that spot used to hang before `fd57159`), but freezes as soon as gameplay starts: moving the character for 2-3 seconds freezes the picture permanently. `dmhost` stays alive (does not exit), audio stops, and GPU utilisation drops to zero. No crash report is generated and jetsam never fires (resident footprint only ~2.0 GB).

This looks like a **second, distinct deadlock** from #149. On the iPhone the fault begins with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`; here there is no GPU fault in the log at all - the render thread simply blocks forever.

## Environment

- Host: Mac mini (Apple M4, 16 GB), macOS 27.0.1 (26A434)
- Repo: `fd57159` (Sync upstream 6a06877), which includes the `rec_publish()` deadlock fix from 569a415
- Build: `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <NSP dir> -k prod.keys --platform mac -l zh-Hans`
- Game: base 1.0.0 + update 2.0.2 (v393216), DLC `0100F43008C45002` attached as aoc index 2
- Run env: `DM_LANG=zh-Hans DM_WINDOW=1 DM_AUDIO=1 DM_FPS_TARGET=30 DM_OPMODE=0`
- Shader cache: all 28,603 Mac shaders precompiled from a clean cache

## Reproduction

1. Start the game and let the opening cinematic play through (this now completes; it used to freeze here).
2. As soon as control is handed to the player, move the character for 2-3 seconds.
3. The picture freezes. `dmhost` keeps running. GPU utilisation goes to 0.

100% reproducible in 3 runs. Saves are written to `run/save`, so the game state itself is fine.

## Evidence - stack sample of the hung process

`sample <pid> 1` of the frozen `dmhost`, 362 samples over 1 ms:

```
Thread_1500040: 0x1012 RenderWorker
  291  h_nvnWindowAcquireTexture  (hle_nvn.c:1267)
         -> mtl_link_wait_tick    (nvn_mtl.m:8641)        <- blocked here
   62  h_nvnQueueSubmitCommands   (hle_nvn.c:1149)
         -> mtl_exec              (nvn_mtl.m:7717)
                -> draw           (nvn_mtl.m:6900)
                       -> rp_begin_ex_ (nvn_mtl.m:2780)
```

The main thread is idle in `-[NSApplication run]`, so the AppKit loop is healthy. Only the render worker is stuck.

## Analysis

`mtl_link_wait_tick()` does have a timeout (`pthread_cond_timedwait` with `ETIMEDOUT` returns 0), so that call alone cannot block forever. The unbounded wait is one level up, in `h_nvnWindowAcquireTexture` in `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`:

```c
uint64_t tk = *idx < 4 ? o->ticket[*idx] : 0;
if (tk) { uint64_t w0 = now_ns(); mtl_present_wait(tk); g_pq_wait_ns += now_ns() - w0; }
```

and `mtl_present_wait()` (`nvn_mtl.m:8585`) waits on `g_pq_done < tk` with a bare `pthread_cond_wait` in the non-display-link path:

```c
if (!g_link_owns_layer) { pthread_cond_wait(&g_pq_cv, &g_pq_mu); continue; }   /* no timeout */
```

So if the present thread never advances `g_pq_done` to `tk`, this is a permanent hang with no escape: no stall detection, no `[RED]` log, and nothing printed to the log at the moment of the freeze (which matches "frozen picture, zero GPU, silence").

The `g_link_owns_layer` path does have `STALL_NS` handling (100 ms ticks, then a `[RED] display link silent ...` message). In this hang that message never appears, which suggests the code is in the non-display-link branch, or the display link is running but the present ticket is never completed.

## Questions

1. Is `g_pq_done` supposed to always be advanced by the encode/present thread even when the layer is not display-link owned? Is there a known path where a present ticket can be permanently lost (for example a dropped `g_present_discard`, or the `rec_publish()` ordering that 569a415 addressed, inside `mtl_present_flush()`)?
2. Would it be safe to give the non-display-link `pthread_cond_wait` the same `STALL_NS` bounded treatment (drop the queued frame, log it, let the game proceed on its own clock) so that a lost ticket degrades instead of deadlocking?
3. Z-A's `nn::nvn::Window::AcquireTexture` pacing (vsync blocking here rather than in present) is unusual. Is there a known interaction between that and the display-link pacing in `mtl_link_wait_tick`?

Happy to run any diagnostic build, `DM_NVN_TSV` instrumentation, or additional `sample` dumps - just tell me which env vars you want.

## Related

- #149 - Z-A freezes 40-60 s in on iPhone 16 Pro: the same "picture frozen, process alive, GPU idle" shape, but there the log opens with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorPageFault`. This report has no GPU fault and reproduces on a Mac host, so it may be a different trigger for the same deadlock family.
- #139 - Z-A hangs when entering the overworld from the station, audio keeps playing.
title: Pokémon Legends: Z-A (v393216) freezes on macOS after the opening: render thread blocks in mtl_present_wait (no timeout), GPU goes idle

body:
I tried and failed, but wanted to share my progress anyway.

## TL;DR

- Boots on the Mac through `nnMain`, NVN init, window creation, and 500+ successful texture / memory-pool / buffer allocations.
- Crashes on first-frame setup **in game code, not the host**: `pc=main+0x9c0d1c`, `x0=0`, `addr=0x8`, i.e. a null pointer passed in from the caller at `main+0x3e3b90` and dereferenced at offset 8.
- Deterministic: same PC, same backtrace, same register pattern across runs with and without `DM_NVN_LOG=1`.
- Getting to this point required three small local fixes that I believe are repo bugs independent of Astral Chain (details below). With them, the whole pipeline runs to `dmhost` from a fresh clone.

## Game

- Title ID `01007300020FA000`, update `01007300020FA800` (v65536 = 1.0.1)
- `main` build ID `4B159F0F7A360669738390EE8657B4F0`
- SDK `nnSdk-6_4_0-Releas`; NVN device API 53.313 (accepted by the host)
- 30 fps native (present interval 2); window is 1600×900, format 0x25
- Shaders: PlatinumGames **PKZ v0x10000** archives (`Text.pkz`, `shader.dat`, etc.). The header and 32-byte entries are byte-identical to v0x20000 (see "Build blockers" #3). Shader objects are `VSO` / `PSO` / `CSO` inside DAT archives, as in Bayonetta 3.

## What works

Pipeline with the three build fixes applied:

```
[dm] sdk: NintendoSDK nnSdk-6_4_0-Releas (major 6)
[dm] [nvn] device API 53.313 (SDK 6)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] depth mode: near=0, vertex shaders use the main0_z entry
[dm] [nvn] WindowInitialize swap chain 3 textures, interval 2, first 1600x900 format 0x25
[dm] [nvn] WindowCrop 0,0 1600x900
… 500+ Texture / MemoryPool / BufferInitialize lines, no [RED], no stub warnings …
```

Shader split: 1,348 shaders in 6 s. Mac shader libraries: 1,348 / 1,348 in 58 s.

## What fails

The last 32 calls before the crash are a batch of `0x100`-byte `BufferInitialize` at stride `0x200`, ending at `off=0xe0c400`. The last few:

```
[dm] [nvn] BufferInitialize … pool=0x7052c00000 off=0xe0be00 size=0x100
[dm] [nvn] BufferInitialize … pool=0x7052c00000 off=0xe0c000 size=0x100
[dm] [nvn] BufferInitialize … pool=0x7052c00000 off=0xe0c200 size=0x100
[dm] [nvn] BufferInitialize … pool=0x7052c00000 off=0xe0c400 size=0x100
[dm] CRASH sig=11 addr=0x8 pc=main+0x9c0d1c lr=main+0x3e3b90 sp=0x1711dae50
x0=0 x1=0x114bec188 x2=0 x3=0 x4=0 x5=0xe7
x6=0x30 x7=0 x8=0 x9=0 x10=0 x11=0x1
x12=0xa8 x13=0x7030204ff0 x14=0x7fffffff x15=0 x16=0x1187d5720 x17=0x117f4ee80
x18=0 x19=0x117bf62e0 x20=0x102f73f0c x21=0x1f4bf22c8 x22=0 x23=0x117bf6298
x24=0 x25=0 x26=0 x27=0 x28=0
[dm] *x1: 0 0 0 0 0 0
[dm] bt: main+0x3e3b90 main+0x9c26b8 main+0x3e3430 guest_main+0x1d0 guest_tramp+0x40 _pthread_start+0x88 thread_start+0x8
```

Other state at the crash:

- Threads created so far: 9. All secondary threads are blocked in `condvar` waits (SDK worker threads). The crash is on thread `0x1001` (`main thread`, priority 44, core 0).
- No `[RED]` lines before the crash. No NVN stub was called; every NVN function the game used is implemented.
- Handheld / docked: `WindowInitialize … 1600x900 format 0x25`, so the game chose handheld-ish scale. `hid supported controller ids 0x101`, `styles 0x7`.

## Analysis

- `pc=main+0x9c0d1c`, `lr=main+0x3e3b90`, `x0=0`, `addr=0x8` → `[null + 8]` dereference of a null pointer that was passed in, not created at the fault site. The immediate caller at `main+0x3e3b90` is where the null originates.
- `x1=0x114bec188` and `*x1` is six zeroed qwords → the caller passed a struct with zeroed fields. That reads like a resource that failed to be built upstream (something returned "not created" and its fields stayed at their zero init).
- `main+0x9c0d1c` (crashing PC) and `main+0x9c26b8` (the caller's caller, 6,624 bytes later) are close enough to plausibly be in the same source file — narrows the disassembly search.
- Both the verbose and non-verbose runs give the same PC and backtrace. The register differences (`x1`, `x6`) are ASLR artifact, not behavioural.

What the log does not show is which specific function returned null — that needs disassembly of `main.patched.bin` around `0x9c0cd0..0x9c0d60` and `0x3e3740..0x3e3bb0`. I stopped short of that (no Ghidra set up on this machine) rather than guess at it.

## Build blockers

All three appear to be repo bugs, not Astral-Chain-specific. A fresh clone on macOS 26 / Xcode 26 hits them in this order.

### 1. `shader_split.py`: PKZ v0x10000 rejected (`pkz_entries`, ~line 382)

```python
if ver != 0x20000: red(f'{path}: PKZ version {ver:#x}: only 0x20000 is known')
```

Fails on every PKZ in Astral Chain's RomFS:

```
[RED] …/Text/Text.pkz: PKZ version 0x10000: only 0x20000 is known
```

The header and 32-byte entries are byte-identical to v0x20000 (verified with `xxd -l 512 Text.pkz` and `xxd -s 0xB60 -l 0x40 Text.pkz`). The only differences:

- The version field (`0x10000` vs `0x20000`).
- Every entry's compression name offset is `0` — one compression for the archive, its name at the head of the name table (`ZStandard` for `Text.pkz`).

`pkz_entries` never reads the `alignment` field (`h[28:32]`); Astral Chain has `0` there, Bayonetta 3 has `0x1000`, so it doesn't matter either way.

```python
if ver not in (0x10000, 0x20000):
    red(f'{path}: PKZ version {ver:#x}: only 0x10000 and 0x20000 are known')
```

Verified: 1,348 shaders extracted from Astral Chain's archives; Bayonetta 3's v0x20000 archives still parse normally.

### 2. `dmsh_xlate` ships without an embedded source hash (`dmsh_chain.py:95`, `dmsh_build.py:18`)

A fresh clone fails at step 5:

```
[RED] the translator was not built from the in-repo source: embedded source  / in repo 16bbef6c762573ee (rebuild dmsh_xlate)
```

`--update-lock` does not help: it rewrites the lock from the source tree, and the source hash is already correct. The problem is that the shipped `dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate_bin/dmsh_xlate.dll` prints an empty string for `--source-sha`.

Rebuild fixes it:

```bash
cd dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_xlate
dotnet publish -c Release -r osx-arm64 -o ../dmsh_xlate_bin
cd ../../..
python3 dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.py --update-lock
```

After this, `dmsh_xlate --source-sha` prints `16bbef6c762573ee` (same as before the rebuild — the source didn't change) and the lock's three DLL hashes update. Suggest rebuilding in CI, or documenting the step in `docs/development.md`.

### 3. `nvn_mtl.m:2854` — `g_shmap` declared with the wrong value type

```c
static NSMutableDictionary<NSString *, NSArray *> *g_shmap;
```

Every store (line 2873: `g_shmap[c[3]] = c[2];`, where `c[2]` is an `NSString *`) and every load (line 3245: `NSString *stage = g_shmap[k];`) uses string values.

On Xcode 15+ / clang 15+ this is a hard error and refuses the host build:

```
nvn_mtl.m:3245:19: error: incompatible pointer types initializing 'NSString *' with an expression of type 'NSArray * _Nullable'
```

One-word fix:

```c
static NSMutableDictionary<NSString *, NSString *> *g_shmap;
```

On older clang this was only a warning, which is presumably why it slipped through.

## To reproduce

From a fresh clone, with `dotnet 10`, `spirv-cross`, `zstd`, `glslang`, and `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain` already applied:

1. Apply fixes #1, #2, #3 above.
2. `scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <nsp-folder> -k <prod.keys> --platform mac`
3. Run the `dmhost` command it prints.

The crash is at the same PC every time.

## Next steps

- Disassemble `main.patched.bin` around `0x9c0cd0..0x9c0d60` and `0x3e3740..0x3e3bb0` to find the null-returning function and its argument. If it turns out to be an SDK or NVN query that returns something the game treats as "not created", I can test a host-side fix immediately (launcher is in place, rebuild is one minute).
- If you want more data on the game's behaviour before that, run with `DM_PROBE=1`, `DM_FSLOG=1`, or `DM_NVN_SHDUMP=<dir>`.

## Environment

macOS 26, Xcode 26, Apple M2 Max, dotnet 10.0.x, Python 3.13, Homebrew `spirv-cross` / `zstd` / `glslang`, Metal Toolchain downloaded via `xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`.
title: Astral Chain (`01007300020FA000`, update v65536, SDK 6.4.0): boots through engine init, deterministically crashes at `main+0x9c0d1c` (`[null+8]`)

## Summary

FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE 1.0.1 has repeatable missing particle effects and flickering lighting/effects on an iPhone. The game otherwise boots and reaches gameplay. This report is based on my actual device tests.

## Environment

- Device: iPhone Air (iPhone18,4).
- iOS: 27.0.1.
- Game: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Hong Kong release, update 1.0.1.
- Installation: unsigned nxnative IPA imported into LiveContainer, with RomFS transferred separately.
- Frame-rate preference: original 30 fps, rather than the profile's 60 fps override.
- Built/tested around October 23–24, 2026. Multiple local diagnostic builds were used; the exact source commit and full build/runtime logs are unfortunately no longer retained.
- Relevant upstream profile: dm/games/0100606026F12000/README.md. I cannot provide a freshly verified regional title ID/build ID from the deleted build.

## Reproduction

1. Start a new game and watch the first story sequence.
2. Continue to the first ruined battlefield, where pixelated/sprite-like fires should burn along both sides of the path.
3. Observe the flames, smoke, illuminated surfaces, and combat effects in the opening scenes and first battles.

## Expected

- Bright, pixelated flames at several points along both sides of the ruined path.
- Smoke and stable illumination.
- The heroine's fireball has its fire texture, the blue spherical shield effect is visible, and soldiers' gunfire produces visible muzzle flashes.

## Actual

- The roadside pixel-style flames are absent and replaced by dark/black silhouettes or patches.
- These patches flicker; smoke and some illuminated parts of the scene also flicker.
- In the first story sequence, the heroine's fireball appears as a black block without its expected texture.
- The blue spherical shield effect is missing.
- Soldiers' muzzle flashes are missing.
- Some other scene elements appear absent, although I cannot yet distinguish missing geometry from a material/effect rendering problem.
- Skill activation also causes noticeable frame drops; no measured frame-time capture is available.

## Tests already made / limits of the evidence

- The visual defects recur across runs.
- A frame-rate change/test did not visibly resolve the rendering defects; 30 vs 60 fps should not be treated as a confirmed cause.
- A reversible runtime diagnostic setting did not change the result and was removed.
- A later local shader-precision diagnostic rebuild was installed, but I do not have a documented conclusive before/after result for it, so I am not claiming it fixed anything.
- I compared the actual iPhone view with normal reference footage of the same opening area: the reference clearly contains multiple bright pixelated fires where the iPhone view has black patches.
- I also noticed apparently absent flames in an upstream screenshot, but that is only a visual observation and not proof of the same underlying issue on macOS.
- The game has since been removed from the phone. There is no current runtime log, GPU capture, or shader hash tied to a failing draw.

## Relation to existing notes

The current game note already documents:
- tex_dyn_slots on for 2,077 particle vertex shaders;
- the integer fragment-output fact for c254eaa40e0c4f1e, fixing dark silhouettes from empty lighting channels;
- 11 unbuilt shaders (3 geometry and 8 compute shaders using 3D image atomics), described as not encountered so far.

Could the opening fire/smoke, fireball, shield, and muzzle-flash draws be checked against those paths? The visible symptoms may involve particle texture/sampler binding, lighting channels, or another shared rendering path, but **I do not have evidence that the 11 unbuilt shaders cause these defects**.

It would also be useful to know whether the same opening effects have been visually checked on the current main branch on an iPhone, and whether there is a recommended narrowly scoped diagnostic for identifying the failing draw/shader.

No game data, keys, account details, or saves are attached.
title: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE 1.0.1 / iPhone Air: missing fire, shield and muzzle-flash effects; black patches and flickering

## Summary

Tears of the Kingdom can hit Metal `Insufficient Memory` during ordinary play on a 16 GB M4 Mac. In the latest observed session, at about 76 seconds after launch, the upload-staging diagnostic reported **231 old blocks still alive / 7,392 MiB**, with **13,539 MiB of total GPU resource allocations**. Upload, render and display command buffers then reported out-of-memory errors; dropped uploads were marked unwritten and retried. Frame 1786 took **5,124.7 ms** with **zero new pipelines or shader libraries**.

Related to #147, but reported separately because this is a macOS transient staging spike and GPU allocation failure, rather than an established monotonic resident-memory leak or an iOS jetsam event. A common root cause has not been demonstrated.

## Environment

- Mac mini (Mac16,10), Apple M4, 16 GB unified memory.
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434).
- Official main source: `cdd56192266f0a3ef1a6589f85575b33c44c9cac`, no tracked source modifications.
- TOTK `0100F2C0115B6000`, update 1.4.3 (`v720896`), `zh-Hans`.
- Matching Mac shader cache, chain `dec5ee141a9f`.
- Native macOS windowed build; a small app entry sets runtime paths and calls the host's main function.
- `DM_FPS_TARGET=30`, `DM_WINDOW=1`, `DM_AUDIO=1`. `DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD` unset (macOS default off). No experimental graphics switches.
- Drawable changed from 2560x1440 / 2560x1504 to 3840x2160. Internal render resolution was not measured.
- First real windowed launch after this update. The Metal 4 pipeline archive started empty; the translated shader cache and existing pipeline prewarm list were retained.

## Observed sequence

1. Launch this build, continue an existing save, and resume normal play.
2. Around one minute into the observed run, a large group of texture re-uploads accumulated.
3. At frame 1786, Metal reported OOM in upload/render/display queues, followed by dropped-upload recovery and a multi-second hitch.
4. The process survived. Later staging dropped back to 96 MiB and total GPU allocations to around 2.3 GiB.

The exact location, input sequence and a minimal deterministic route have not been isolated. This is an actual player session, not a controlled idle/traversal A/B.

## Log excerpts

Memory fields labelled MB below use `>> 20`, i.e. MiB. Cumulative created/swapped totals are not live memory; the relevant values are **still alive now**.

```text
[dm] [nvn-mtl] pipeline prewarm done: shaders 3027 / render pipelines 5096 (specialized fragment skipped 0) / compute pipelines 65, background time 51156.3 ms; shader keys not in the shader map (another game version) 0

[dm] [nvn-mtl] upload staging blocks: 287 created in total, swapped within a batch 278 times (8740 MB of old blocks swapped out); swapped-out blocks still alive now 231, 7392 MB, still in the residency set 231; GPU allocated 13539 MB, residency set 3454 objects, deferred-release queue 956
```

Error excerpt (repeated nested NSError formatting and object addresses omitted):

```text
MTL4CommandQueueErrorDomain Code=3
Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
IOGPUCommandQueueErrorDomain Code=8

[dm] [nvn-mtl] upload command buffer dropped: the 1610 textures of this batch are marked unwritten and re-uploaded on next use (230 awaiting re-upload)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] upload command buffer dropped: the 7 textures of this batch are marked unwritten and re-uploaded on next use (231 awaiting re-upload)
[dm] [nvn-mtl] [RED] state of the failed submission fence=1789: frame 1786; since the last submission: passes +144, first texture uploads +0, re-uploads +231, serial table changes +307; deferred-release queue 960

[dm] [longframe] frame 1786 (75.95 s) whole frame 5124.7 ms, submit+present 5097.5 ms, GPU 1.7 ms; new pipelines 0 + shader libraries 0, 0.0 ms in all; texture uploads 0 first + 231 re-uploads, 3849.8 MB / 57.7 ms

[dm] [nvn-mtl] upload staging blocks (settled): 287 created in total, swapped within a batch 278 times (8740 MB of old blocks swapped out); swapped-out blocks still alive now 3, 96 MB, still in the residency set 3; GPU allocated 2359 MB, residency set 3009 objects, deferred-release queue 143
```

The periodic report at frame 1500 was only **4038 MiB resident / 2392 MiB GPU allocated**. Periodic resident-memory samples alone would miss this transient peak.

## Scope and interpretation

- A previous session on `156d3c2a18a362331aa52bc04c542792a5004586` showed the same class of failure: live staging up to 9,352 MiB and total GPU allocations 16,905 MiB. This is not established as a regression introduced by cdd5619 or pipeline archives.
- A separate first-use compilation hitch at frame 1204 took 1129.9 ms total, including 1066.4 ms of new pipelines/libraries. It should not be conflated with frame 1786's OOM event.
- The following frame lasted about 45 seconds, but focus changes occurred nearby; its full duration cannot confidently be attributed to the GPU error.
- `currentAllocatedSize` counts resource allocations, not unique physical resident RAM. These numbers do not prove that any particular larger RAM capacity fixes this.
- Upload batching, staging lifetime/retirement, re-upload amplification and backpressure seem worth investigating, but the root cause has not been isolated.

Could this path be instrumented or bounded so a large re-upload batch cannot accumulate several GiB of staging before retirement? Expected behavior is bounded transient upload memory and successful uploads without repeated Metal OOM recovery during normal play.
title: [TOTK/macOS M4 16GB] Upload staging spikes to 7.2 GiB with Metal OOM and multi-second stalls
